## v8.262.3 (2026-08-25) — Retail FX Positioning: Dukascopy fallback silently hid genuine 0% long/short readings

### Continuing industry-standard audit
Continued the module-by-module audit into Retail FX Positioning. CB Rate Expectations was audited first this session — clean, no changes (staleness guard, per-bank step sizes, and probability clamping all check out).

### Data integrity — assets/dashboard.js
- **`fetchSentiment()`'s SOURCE 2 (Dukascopy fallback) mapped `buy: Math.round(d.longVolume || d.buy || 50)` / `sell: Math.round(d.shortVolume || d.sell || 50)`.** `||` treats a genuine `0` as falsy — so an extreme, all-short (or all-long) retail crowding reading, exactly the kind of reading this panel exists to surface, would silently fall through to the 50% neutral default instead of displaying the real 0%. Same failure class already fixed once elsewhere in this project (`fetch_rates.py`'s `clean_rate()`, "Algunas tasas son 0% ... No debe descartarse").
- Fixed: switched both fields to `??` (nullish coalescing), which only falls through on `null`/`undefined`, preserving a real `0` reading through the fallback chain.
- `node --check` clean, `dashboard.test.js` 89/89 still passing.
- Cache-buster: `dashboard.js?v=8.262.2` → `?v=8.262.3`; `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION`/`STATIC_PRECACHE` synced to `gi-v8.262.3`.

## v8.262.2 (2026-08-25) — FX Pairs — Majors: 9 of 32 pairs (incl. EUR/NOK, EUR/SEK) were missing from the static spread floor, silently rendering a flat 0.5 pip fallback

### Continuing industry-standard audit
Continued the module-by-module audit into FX Pairs — Majors. `fetchReferenceSpreads()`'s live HV30+VIX+MOVE model only ever computes `LIVE_SPREADS` for the 7 USD majors (its own `ECN_FLOOR`/`VOL_COEF` maps are explicitly scoped to those 7) — every other pair in the 32-pair table depends entirely on the static `ECN_FLOOR_SPREADS` table as its permanent value, not a temporary fallback (the code comment saying "until first update" only describes the 7-pair case correctly). Cross-referencing `PAIRS`' full 32-id list against `ECN_FLOOR_SPREADS`'s keys found 9 pairs absent entirely: `eurnok`, `eursek`, `eurnzd`, `gbpaud`, `gbpnzd`, `audcad`, `cadchf`, `nzdcad`, `nzdchf`. `TYPICAL_SPREADS`'s Proxy `get()` falls back to a flat `0.5` for any key not present in either map — so all 9, including EUR/NOK and EUR/SEK (thinner crosses than USD/NOK, USD/SEK, which already carry a calibrated `2.0`), rendered the same 0.5 pip spread as EUR/USD in every render, understating their real cost of trading.

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- Added the 9 missing pairs to `ECN_FLOOR_SPREADS`: `eurnok`/`eursek` calibrated wider than `usdnok`/`usdsek` (a EUR-crossed-with-Scandies leg compounds two currencies' liquidity rather than one), the remaining 7 calibrated in line with the existing `gbpcad`/`audnzd`/`nzdjpy` tier they sit alongside in the table.
- `node --check` clean, `dashboard.test.js` 89/89 still passing (no existing test covers this table directly).
- Cache-buster: `dashboard.js?v=8.262.0` → `?v=8.262.2`; `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION`/`STATIC_PRECACHE` synced to `gi-v8.262.2`.

### GUIDELINES.md
Added one Data integrity rule (see footer) — a per-pair static calibration table needs to be checked against the panel's own full pair list on delivery, not just against the smaller model it was designed alongside; a Proxy/dict fallback with a generic default silently hides a coverage gap in exactly the way an explicit `undefined`/error would not.

## v8.262.0 (2026-08-25) — FX Fair Value's z-score was look-ahead-biased against its own regression window's endpoint — same mechanism as the v8.180.0 Correlations fix, never applied here

### Continuing industry-standard audit — panels not covered in the first pass
Session-start inventory found the first audit pass (Rates, COT, Correlations, Calendar, Dollar Smile, CB Rates, Risk Regime, ESI, Seasonality, Heatmap, Carry Rank, Economic Map) had left ~11 panels unaudited: Price Chart, FX Pairs — Majors, CB Rate Expectations, Cross-Asset tiles, Derivatives, Retail FX Positioning, Market Sessions, Alerts & Market Signals, FX Fair Value, DTCC FX, Watchlist. Starting with FX Fair Value as the highest-risk candidate (a regression-based signal, same class as the already-fixed Correlations pairs-trade signal).

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Real bug found:** `renderFairValue()`'s BEER-style regression fit `_fvRegress()` on `windowRows` — the most recent `FV_ROLLING_WINDOW` (60) usable rows — **including** `last` (the very row the resulting z-score is then computed against). `GUIDELINES.md`'s existing general rule, established fixing `fetch_correlations()`'s pairs-trade signal in v8.180.0, states this explicitly: *"any point-in-time statistical signal (z-score, percentile, threshold flag) must be evaluated against a reference distribution that does not include the point being evaluated"* — OLS pulls the fitted line toward its own endpoint, systematically damping exactly the z-score magnitude being read off it. That rule was never re-checked against Fair Value's own regression when it shipped (v8.197.0) or in any session since.
- **Live proof of mechanism:** a synthetic 60-row test (59 rows of noisy linear relationship + 1 deliberate outlier row as `last`) showed the in-sample z-score reading 7.3σ for the outlier, vs. its true magnitude once excluded from the fit — the old code's own residStd was inflated ~12x by including the outlier it was about to score, directly damping the z-score by the same factor. Real production data won't show swings this extreme, but the direction of the bias (any big move gets read as smaller than it is, right when the panel is supposed to flag it) is real and always active.
- **Fix:** walk-forward split, same pattern as `fetch_correlations()`'s v8.180.0 fix — `_fvRegress()` itself is unchanged (still a generic fit-and-residual-std function), but `renderFairValue()` now fits it on `windowRows.slice(0, -1)` (the training window, stopping one row before `last`) and scores `last` — which was never part of the fit — against that trained beta/residStd. Training window still comfortably clears `_fvRegress()`'s own `>= 2*k` singularity guard (59 rows vs. 10 required).
- Cache-buster: `dashboard.js?v=8.261.2` → `8.262.0` in `index.html`; `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION`/`STATIC_PRECACHE` synced to `gi-v8.262.0`.

### Gate run this session
`node --check` clean, 89/89 `dashboard.test.js` tests pass, synthetic before/after regression test run standalone (documented above).

### New rule
A look-ahead-bias fix landed for one panel (`fetch_correlations()`, v8.180.0) does not automatically cover a sibling panel using the same statistical pattern (point-in-time regression z-score) — even when the general rule was written down in `GUIDELINES.md` at the time. When a methodology rule is added, grep every other panel/script for the same statistical shape (here: "fit a model on a window, then score that window's own endpoint against it") before considering the rule fully applied, not just the one incident that prompted it.

## v8.166.3 (2026-08-19) — Mobile: huge empty gaps in the News tab (News/Research/Analysis sub-panels) fixed — desktop's equal-thirds CSS Grid had no real height to distribute on mobile

### Santiago flagged
Three screenshots on the News tab (mobile): a single headline followed by a large empty dark area before Research's header appeared; an empty area above Research's first note; an empty area above the Central Bank Rates table (the next section after News in the mobile stacking order, per v8.166.2's reorder). All three turned out to be different scroll positions through one continuous gap, not three separate bugs.

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.css
- **Root cause:** `#intel-scroll` (holds the News/Research/Analysis sub-panels inside `#section-news`) uses a CSS Grid on desktop — `grid-template-rows: auto minmax(0,1fr) auto auto minmax(0,1fr) auto minmax(0,1fr)` — giving the three feeds an exact equal-thirds split (see the existing v8.117.18 comment directly above the rule for the full history of that design). This only produces a *sensible* equal split because `#layout` is `display:grid` with a real, viewport-bound `calc(100vh - 92px)` height on desktop. On mobile, `#layout` switches to a flex column with `height:auto` (the "Layout: stack…" rule from v8.166.2 and earlier) — so `#main`/`#split-lower`/`#intel-scroll` have no definite height left to distribute, yet the grid's `minmax(0,1fr)` tracks and each feed's own `overflow-y:auto` still tried to enforce an equal one-third share of whatever near-zero height resulted — visually, any sub-panel with only a couple of items reserved a full third of the (effectively arbitrary) computed height, mostly empty below its actual content. Exactly the same class of bug as every other fixed/grid-height panel in this file that already gets a mobile auto-height override (Cross-Asset/Risk, News+Econ map widget, Sessions+Spreads, TV Calendar) — this one was simply missed because v8.117.18 was tested on desktop only.
- **Fix:** inside the existing `max-width: 900px` block, `#intel-scroll` drops the Grid entirely on mobile (`display:block; height:auto; flex:none; min-height:0; overflow:visible`), the three feed containers get `overflow-y:visible; max-height:none` (no more internal per-feed scroll box), and `.intel-sub-head` (the sticky sub-panel dividers) gets `position:static` since sticking to the viewport would otherwise compete with `#topbar` for the same `top:0` spot once the whole page — not `#intel-scroll` — is the scroll container. All three sub-panels now stack at their real natural content height and scroll as part of the normal mobile page flow, matching how every other panel on this page already behaves on mobile.
- Cache-buster: `assets/dashboard.css?v=8.23.18` → `?v=8.166.3` in `index.html`; `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION` `gi-v8.166.2` → `gi-v8.166.3`.

### Gate run this session
CSS-only change — brace balance checked programmatically (678 open / 678 close, matched). `node dashboard.test.js` re-run for safety since the same file ships together with `dashboard.js` — 85/85 passed, unchanged (no JS touched this session).

## v8.166.2 (2026-08-19) — Mobile: Overview stack reordered (narrative+chart first, sidebar panels last) and "+ Compare" chart overlay fixed (was fully non-functional on mobile)

### Santiago flagged
Two mobile-only issues via screenshots: (1) on load, the Overview tab showed the FX Liquidity / Crosses / Carry Trade Ranking / Watchlist sidebar stack *above* the narrative and price chart, forcing a scroll past all of it to reach the content that matters first; (2) the chart's "+ Compare" overlay button did nothing when tapped on mobile.

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.css
- **Mobile stacking order fixed:** `#layout`'s three children (`#sidebar`, `#main`, `#rightpanel`) are DOM-ordered sidebar → main → rightpanel for the desktop 3-column layout; on mobile, `#layout` collapses to `flex-direction: column` and previously just followed that DOM order, putting the sidebar stack first. Added `order: 1` (`#main`), `order: 2` (`#rightpanel`), `order: 3` (`#sidebar`) inside the existing `max-width: 900px` block — pure CSS `order`, no DOM/JS changes, so no ids moved and no event listeners needed re-binding. New visual order: narrative + chart (+ any other Overview-tab content in `#main`) → right panel data → sidebar panels, matching what Santiago asked for.

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **"+ Compare" button non-functional on mobile — root cause found and fixed:** `#lw-cmp-dropdown` was left as static HTML nested inside `#lw-range-bar`'s row-1 div, which has `overflow-x:auto` plus `-webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch` (needed for iOS momentum-scroll on that horizontally-scrollable toolbar). Switching the dropdown to `position:fixed` via JS on open is normally enough to escape an ancestor's overflow clipping — but `-webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch` is a documented WebKit/iOS exception: it forces the whole subtree, `position:fixed` descendants included, into the container's own scrolling compositor layer, so the dropdown stayed clipped to the toolbar row's bounds and was effectively invisible/untappable on iOS Safari and Chrome-iOS, while working normally on desktop (no touch/overflow quirk there). The codebase already had the correct pattern for this exact class of bug: the Indicators (`_lw-ind-dropdown`) and Draw (`_lw-draw-dropdown`) popups are `document.createElement`'d and `document.body.appendChild()`'d fresh on every open, so they're never a descendant of the scrollable toolbar row in the first place — confirmed by re-reading their code, which also already carries a "clamp into viewport" mobile fix of its own from a prior session. Applied the same body-reparent pattern to `#lw-cmp-dropdown` (idempotent — `appendChild` on an already-attached node just moves it, so it's safe to also re-run on every open as a safety net) and added the matching viewport-clamped positioning (horizontal 8px-margin clamp both edges, vertical flip-above-button when there isn't room below) — needed now that a body-level fixed dropdown can be opened from a button anywhere along the scrolled toolbar, not just one that happens to sit at the row's visible right edge.
- Cache-buster: `assets/dashboard.js?v=8.102.0` → `?v=8.166.2` in `index.html`.

### Engine — sw.js *(site repo, listed here per the single-CHANGELOG convention)*
- `CACHE_VERSION`: `gi-v8.154.3` → `gi-v8.166.2` (forces every client's Service Worker to fetch the new `dashboard.js`/`dashboard.css` rather than serve a stale cached copy — the cache had not been bumped since v8.154.3, several sessions behind the currently-shipped dashboard.js version even before today's change).

### Gate run this session
`node --check dashboard.js` (OK). `node dashboard.test.js` — 85/85 passed, unchanged.

### Not investigated this session
Whether the Indicators/Draw dropdowns' own "clamp into viewport" fix (referenced above, already in the codebase) fully covers every toolbar-button position on mobile, or whether the Compare dropdown's new clamp logic diverges from theirs in some edge case (e.g. extremely narrow viewports under ~320px) — both use the same 8px-margin approach but were written independently in this and a prior session; worth a side-by-side pass if either turns out to still misbehave live.

## v8.166.1 (2026-08-19) — AUD "Wage Price Index q/q" actual stuck at "—" 30+ min after release, fixed at the root cause (Myfxbook Low-impact filter), mirrored across both calendar parsers

### Santiago flagged
Live screenshots: AUD Wage Price Index q/q released at 22:30 GMT-3, still showing no Actual in the terminal's Economic Calendar panel more than 30 minutes later, while a second screenshot (MQL5's calendar, sourced from Myfxbook) showed the release had genuinely happened — Actual 0.8% = Consensus 0.8% = Previous 0.8%, tagged **LOW** impact.

### Root cause
Myfxbook RSS tags "Wage Price Index" **Low** impact (verified live against `myfxbook.com/forex-economic-calendar/australia/wage-price-index-qoq`), and it was missing from the `_IMPACT_UPGRADES` allow-list in **both** independent parsers of the feed — the exact same failure mode as the v3.43/v3.44 PPI, Retail Sales MoM, and Inflation Rate MoM fixes.

Traced why a row existed at all: `fetch_forexfactory_forward()` had forward-filled it from ForexFactory's own JSON export (FF classifies it medium, not low) while the event was still a future day — `vendor: "forexfactory"`, `forecast/previous` populated, `actual: null`. Once the event's date became "today," that forward-fill path stops touching it by design (its own docstring: *"today and earlier are Myfxbook's job — never overridden here"*), handing the actual update over exclusively to Myfxbook RSS — which then silently dropped it on every poll, fast Worker path and slow GitHub Actions cron alike, because of the missing upgrade entry. Confirmed live in the site repo's own `calendar-data/ff_calendar.json`: the entry sat at `"actual": null, "released": false` well past the release time.

### Fixed
- **`fetch_ff_calendar.py`** (scripts repo) v3.44 → v3.45 — added `"wage price index"` to `_IMPACT_UPGRADES`. Corpus-checked against the live 309-title `ff_calendar.json`: the only other "wage"-containing title, `"United States Employment Cost - Wages QoQ"`, does not contain the `"wage price index"` substring — zero collision.
- **`calendar-watcher.js`** (Cloudflare Worker, private `globalinvesting-scripts` repo) v5.33 → v5.33.1 — same entry added to its `IMPACT_UPGRADES` mirror, per the "two independent parsers of the same feed silently drift" rule. Build-version identifiers (`/` status endpoint's `version` field, poll-start log line) bumped to match; per-request `User-Agent` strings intentionally left at `5.33` (cosmetic, not functional — not touched to keep the diff reviewable).

### Gate run this session
`python3 -m py_compile fetch_ff_calendar.py` (OK). `node --check calendar-watcher.js` (OK).

### Flagged, not fixed this session
"Wage Price Index **y/y**" (AUD) has no entry anywhere in `ff_calendar.json` — only the q/q variant was ever forward-filled by ForexFactory's export. Unconfirmed whether FF's own JSON classifies the y/y variant below medium (excluding it from `fetch_forexfactory_forward()`) or whether this is a separate wiring gap — needs a live check against FF's raw JSON before any fix is attempted, per the "no equivalent source conclusions must be documented" rule. Today's `_IMPACT_UPGRADES` fix does **not** cover this, since forward-fill and Myfxbook-RSS title matching are independent code paths.

### Also flagged (pre-existing, unrelated to this fix)
`GUIDELINES.md`'s footer cites `v8.166.0` as current, but this `CHANGELOG.md`'s prior top entry was `v8.155.1` — an 11-version gap with no corresponding entries in this file. Per the existing "a CHANGELOG entry is not evidence a fix reached the repo" rule (v8.161.5), the reverse gap here means several GUIDELINES-only rule bumps (`v8.156.0`–`v8.166.0`) reference sessions whose CHANGELOG entries never made it into this file's export. Not investigated further this session — flagged for Santiago to reconcile from his own session history, since neither zip in this export contains the missing entries.

## v8.155.1 (2026-08-18) — Public workflow YAML no longer names data/infra vendors in comments — full setup detail moved to a new private ops runbook

### Santiago flagged
Pointed out that `globalinvesting.github.io`'s public `.github/workflows/*.yml` files reveal internal implementation detail — the `update-intraday-quotes.yml` shown as an example named Twelve Data, Alpha Vantage, and cron-job.org directly, with a full step-by-step PAT/cron-job.org setup runbook and specific rate-limit numbers, all sitting in a public repo. Asked how to resolve it.

### Constraint confirmed before making any change
GitHub Actions requires workflow files to live in the repo whose events trigger them — these can't simply move to a private repo, and moving them would also lose this project's unlimited free Actions minutes (the whole reason the public repo hosts them). So the `.yml` files themselves, their triggers, and their schedules must stay public; only the surrounding prose was in scope.

### Audit — all 7 public workflow files
| File | Vendor mentions before |
|---|---|
| `update-intraday-quotes.yml` | 17 (worst) |
| `forex-news.yml` | 11 |
| `update-ff-calendar.yml` | 6 |
| `update-fx-liquidity.yml` | 6 |
| `update-ohlc.yml` | 7 |
| `update-sitemap.yml` | 3 |
| `deploy-pages.yml` | 0 — no change needed |

### Fixed — 6 workflow files
Genericized every vendor/dispatch-service name in comments and step names: "cron-job.org" → "the external clock service" / "the external dispatcher"; "Twelve Data" → "the primary/fallback quote source"; "FRED" → "a credit-spread source"; "yfinance" → dropped from prose (kept only where functionally required, e.g. `pip install yfinance`). Removed the full PAT-creation + cron-job.org account-setup walkthrough and the internal "Bloomberg Terminal: <1 sec" competitive-benchmark aside from `update-ff-calendar.yml`'s latency comment. Version bumps: `update-intraday-quotes.yml` v1.6→v1.7, `update-fx-liquidity.yml` v2.0→v2.1, `update-ohlc.yml` v2.1→v2.2.

### New — `globalinvesting-engine/docs/ops-runbook.md` (private)
Holds everything stripped out of the public comments: the full cron-job.org setup steps, the active job table (workflow → event_type → frequency), and a per-workflow vendor/API breakdown. This is now the source of truth for "which vendor does what" — the public `.yml` comments only explain what a maintainer needs to safely edit the trigger/schedule.

### Explicitly NOT fixed this session (catalogued in the runbook's "Known residual leaks" section, not silently dropped)
- **`update-ff-calendar.yml`** — ForexFactory/Myfxbook names are baked in past comment level: the workflow's own name, step names, the committed public data filename (`calendar-data/ff_calendar.json`), and a `"vendor": "forexfactory"`/`"myfxbook"` field inside that publicly-served JSON itself. Fixing this needs a coordinated rename across this workflow, `fetch_ff_calendar.py` (private scripts repo), and every frontend consumer (`dashboard.js`, `econ-matrix.js`, `calendar-panel.js`) — too large a blast radius to fold into a comment-cleanup pass without its own dedicated session.

## v8.155.0 (2026-08-18) — narrative.json/signals.json/catalysts.json no longer reveal the AI vendor/model in public JSON — `_source`/`source_model` now use fixed aliases

### Santiago flagged
Pasted a live `narrative.json` and `signals.json` sample and pointed out `"_source": "gemini"` / `"_source": "gemini:gemini-3-flash-preview"` — these files are served as public static files on GitHub Pages, so the AI vendor and model name were directly visible to anyone fetching the raw JSON, not just in logs. Confirmed `catalysts.json`'s `source_model` field had the same issue ("gemini", plus "groq-internal-data" for the fallback tier — which also named the vendor). Requested: keep an internal alias for primary-vs-fallback distinction, but never reveal which vendor is which.

### Backend — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Root cause:** four independent write sites across two cascade functions each hardcoded a literal vendor string: `generate_narrative_via_gemini()` (`result["_source"] = "gemini"`), `generate_signals_via_gemini()` (`_sig["_source"] = f"gemini:{_sig_model}"` — this one leaked the specific model tier too, under a comment that incorrectly said it was "so logs show source model", when the field actually ships straight into the public `signals.json`), and the catalysts cascade's two branches (`source_model = "gemini"` / `"groq-internal-data"`). Groq's narrative/signals fallback path was already fine by omission — it never set `_source` at all — but that's incidental, not a designed convention, so it wasn't relied on.
- **Fixed:** added two module-level constants, `SOURCE_ALIAS_PRIMARY = "engine-ai-primary"` and `SOURCE_ALIAS_FALLBACK = "engine-ai-fallback"`, documented as the *only* place a vendor name may appear anywhere near the public-output path. All four write sites now use one of these instead of a literal string. Also fixed the one comparison depending on the old literal (`elif source_model == "gemini" and sources:` → `== SOURCE_ALIAS_PRIMARY`), which would have silently broken (always taking the `else: _ccy_sources = []` branch, dropping Gemini's own grounded-search sources whenever Tavily wasn't available) had it been missed.
- The actual vendor/model/key-index detail Santiago may still want for debugging stays exactly where it already was — `print()` lines in CI Actions logs, never published — so no diagnostic capability was lost, only the public-JSON leak.
- Confirmed via `grep` that no other write site in the file assigns `_source`/`source_model` outside these four (`ast.parse`/`py_compile` clean).
- Frontend audited: `assets/*.js`/`index.html` never reference either field — this was pure unused leakage, zero UI risk in changing it.
- Gate run this session: `python3 -m py_compile` + `ast.parse` on `generate_narrative_signals.py` (OK). `scripts/tests/test_all_scripts.py`'s only "source"-named test (`test_source_se_preserva_exacto`) covers an unrelated CB-rate-provenance field (`fetch_rates.make_result()`'s `source`, e.g. "RBA-HTML") — not touched, not affected.

## v8.154.3 (2026-08-17) — Frontend root cause found for "AUD/NOK/CAD 10Y still stale": econ-matrix.js was caching 10Y/CB Rate forever after first load, never re-fetching — backend data was already correct

### Investigated — "why haven't the AUD/NOK/CAD 10Y fixes from v8.154.2 shown up on the frontend"
- **Backend confirmed already fixed and fresh.** Diffed the new zip export's `extended-data/*.json` directly: AUD `bond10y: 5.05` (dated 2026-08-18), CAD `bond10y: 3.72` (2026-08-17), NOK `bond10y: 4.4` (2026-08-17) — all consistent with the v2.10.2 `fetch_bond_yields.py` fix and its live production run. This is not the bug.
- **Real root cause: `econ-matrix.js`'s own caching, unrelated to the backend fix.** v2.4.0 (2026-08-16, v8.163.0) fetches 10Y yield and CB Rate exactly once, on first scroll-into-view, then freezes them in `_y10Cache`/`_cbCache` for the rest of the page session — its periodic 3-min refresh only re-fetches `calendar.json`. The v2.4.0 rationale ("rates change far less often than calendar actuals") is wrong specifically for 10Y: `extended-data/{CCY}.json` bond10y is written **daily**. Any tab left open past a day's bond-yield run — or open at the moment the AUD/CAD orphaned-field fix landed — keeps showing the pre-fix value indefinitely, with no error and no visible staleness indicator, which exactly matches Santiago's screenshot (AUD 4.83%/CAD 3.59%/NOK 4.20%) against the already-fresh backend values above.

### Frontend — assets/econ-matrix.js (v2.4.0 → v2.5.0) / index.html / sw.js
- **Fixed:** the periodic refresh (`refreshCalendarOnly` renamed `refreshPanel`) now re-fetches `calendar.json` **and** 10Y (`Promise.all(CCY_ORDER.map(load10y))` — ten small JSON files, cheap) **and** recomputes CB Rate (`Promise.all(CCY_ORDER.map(getCBRate))` — no network cost, `getCBRate()` already reads the live `window._STATE_cbRates` that dashboard.js's own 5-min `health.json` sentinel poll keeps fresh; only the econ-matrix.js snapshot of it was stale) on every tick, replacing the fixed `_y10Cache`/`_cbCache` values. A failed re-fetch falls back to the last good snapshot rather than blanking the panel.
- `load10y()` also got `{cache:'no-store'}` (matching `loadCalendarData()`) so the browser/SW HTTP cache can't hand back a stale copy inside the 3-min window either.
- Cache-busters bumped: `index.html`, `sw.js` → `assets/econ-matrix.js?v=2.5.0`; `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION` → `gi-v8.154.3`.
- Gate run this session: `node --check` on `econ-matrix.js`/`sw.js` (OK), div-tag balance on `index.html` (OK, 383/383). ## v8.154.1 (2026-08-15) — Volatility Leaderboard "all GBP top 5" investigated: confirmed real market data + correct triangulation, not a bug — added a methodology-comparability caveat to the tooltip

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js (v8.101.0 → v8.101.1) / sw.js
- **Investigated Santiago's report** (screenshot: Volatility Leaderboard top 5 all GBP crosses — GBP/NZD, GBP/AUD, GBP/USD, GBP/CAD, GBP/JPY — "hace días que solo veo esos pares GBP") and whether Barchart should replace the CBOE/Saxo mix as the source for all currencies.
- **Root cause: not a bug.** Reproduced `fetchVolLeaderboard()`'s triangulation formula (`sqrt(ivA²+ivB²-2·ρ·ivA·ivB)`) by hand against the live `intraday-data/quotes.json` `fx_etf_iv` inputs (EUR 7.1, GBP 11.0, JPY 7.2, AUD 6.21, CHF 5.85, CAD 3.95, NZD 7.4) — all 5 screenshot values reproduce exactly (GBP/NZD 12.0, GBP/AUD 11.2, GBP/CAD 10.5, GBP/JPY 10.1, GBP/USD 11.0 direct). A control cross not involving GBP (EUR/JPY) computes to 6.8%, confirming the formula isn't systematically inflating GBP-family crosses — GBP dominates the top 5 purely because its own single-leg IV (11.0%, CBOE ^BPVIX) is genuinely ~50%+ higher than every other major fetched this run, and any cross containing the highest-vol leg will rank above crosses that don't.
- **Plausibility check:** GBP's persistently elevated vol lines up with the well-documented 2026 UK political/macro backdrop (Starmer's June 2026 resignation and succession, BoE holding but leaning hawkish against diverging Fed/ECB paths, residual US-Iran-war-driven repricing) — a genuine risk-premium story, not a one-day print or a stale-cache artifact (the `updated` timestamp on `quotes.json` was fresh at fetch time).
- **On Barchart-for-all-currencies:** recommended against. `_CBOE_FX_VOL_INDEX` (EUR/GBP/JPY) is a live, institutional-grade exchange-published index — the best available source for those three; Barchart's "aggregate" IV is explicitly documented in `fetch_intraday_quotes.py` as a last-resort fallback, currently used only for NZD because no CBOE/CME/Saxo alternative exists for it. Downgrading EUR/GBP/JPY to Barchart purely for cross-currency comparability would trade real data quality for the appearance of it — the opposite of this repo's usual verified-best-source-per-currency discipline.
- **What was fixed:** the panel's tooltip (`fx-tt-body`) didn't disclose that EUR/GBP/JPY are sourced from a CBOE/CME variance-swap-style vol index while AUD/CHF/CAD/NZD use a plain indicative ATM mid (Saxo/Barchart) — two different constructions that aren't strictly apples-to-apples. Added one sentence flagging this so a genuine GBP-vs-rest gap isn't read as a pure like-for-like market signal without that context.
- Cache-busters bumped: `index.html` → `assets/dashboard.js?v=8.101.1`; `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION` → `gi-v8.154.1`.
- Gate run this session: `node --check` on `dashboard.js`/`sw.js` (OK), 85/85 `dashboard.test.js` (OK, unaffected — tooltip string change only, no logic touched).

- **Root cause of the "0 / 10 FWD" / "10 on CPI proxy this run" tile Santiago flagged (screenshot).** The v14.1 preserve-from-disk fix for `inflationExpectations` only ever carried `data.inflationExpectations` + `dates.inflationExpectations` across this script's daily full-dict rewrite — it never carried `data.inflationExpectationsSource`, a sibling metadata field `fetch_inflation_expectations.py` v5.6 started writing to the same object *after* v14.1 shipped. ## v8.153.4 (2026-08-15) — CB Rate subtext showed "01 Aug" for every currency (monthly-series artifact, not a bug in the date formatter); Unemp column colored backwards (rising unemployment showed green)

### Frontend — assets/econ-matrix.js (v2.2.9 → v2.3.0)
- **CB Rate date fix.** Santiago flagged (screenshot) that every currency's CB RATE subtext showed the identical "Aug 01" — root cause traced to `getCBRate()` reading its date straight from `rates/{CCY}.json` observations[0].date, and that file is a FRED-style **monthly** series where every row is stamped to the 1st of its month by construction (confirmed directly: `rates/USD.json`'s latest three rows are 2026-08-01 / 07-01 / 06-01) — not a real per-currency decision date, and never was. `fmtDateShort()` itself was correct the whole time (proven by the 10Y column using the same helper with real per-currency dates). Fix: `getCBRate()` now also resolves the true last-meeting date from `meetings-data/meetings.json`'s per-currency `allMeetings` (real ISO decision dates) — the most recent entry not after today — and prefers that for the subtext, falling back to the old monthly-bucket date only if no meeting record exists for that currency. Verified against live `meetings-data/meetings.json`: USD 29 Jul, EUR 23 Jul, GBP 30 Jul, JPY 31 Jul, AUD 11 Aug, CHF 18 Jun, CAD 15 Jul, NZD 08 Jul, NOK 13 Aug, SEK 17 Jun — ten genuinely different dates, not one repeated placeholder.
- **Unemp column inverted-coloring fix.** `trendClass()` used the same generic "actual > previous → green (`up`)" logic for every column with no exception — meaning a *rising* unemployment rate rendered green, identical to rising GDP, exactly backwards. This app already has one audited, canonical keyword list for exactly this problem — `CAL_INVERSE_KW` in `calendar-panel.js` (mirrored as `INVERSE_KW` in `dashboard.js`, `_ESM_INVERSE_KW` in `econ-surprises-modal.js`): `['unemployment', 'unemployed', 'jobless', 'claims', 'deficit']` — but `econ-matrix.js` was built independently and never adopted it; this gap had never been audited against the canonical list before. Added the same list here (`MX_INVERSE_KW`) and `trendClass()` now takes the cell's event title, flipping up/down when it matches. Audited every other column's event titles against the list: GDP/CPI/CPI MoM/Core CPI/PPI/Ind Prod/Bus Cond/Rtl Sales/PCE — none match, correctly unaffected. Cur Acct/Trade Bal titles ("Current Account", "Trade Balance") also don't literally contain "deficit", so aren't auto-flagged — their sign is already baked into the printed value (a worsening balance already prints more negative, which the existing sign-aware `parseNum()` reads correctly), so no separate inversion was needed there. Only Unemp was actually affected in this file. Unit-verified: rising unemployment (3.5%→3.8%) → `down` (red); falling unemployment (3.8%→3.5%) → `up` (green); rising GDP unaffected (`up`); rising jobless claims → `down`.
- Cache-busters bumped: `index.html`, `sw.js` → `assets/econ-matrix.js?v=2.3.0`; `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION` → `gi-v8.153.4`.
- Gate run this session: `node --check` on `econ-matrix.js`/`sw.js` (OK), 85/85 `dashboard.test.js` (OK, unaffected).

### GUIDELINES.md
- Rule added: "A panel built independently from the calendar/dashboard/surprises stack must still be checked against the app's canonical inverse-indicator keyword list, not assumed exempt" (Data integrity section) — documenting the Unemp coloring gap above. Footer bumped to v8.153.4.

### Scripts — fetch_bond_yields.py (v2.10.0 → v2.10.1)
- **First live `update-bond-yields.yml` run since v2.10.0 shipped (Santiago pasted the full log): 10/10 currencies processed, 0 exceptions, 0 bad writes** — every TE miss fell through cleanly to each currency's existing fallback chain exactly as designed (e.g. CHF bond10y correctly landed on FRED-OECD-MEI, USD bond10y correctly fell to `ohlc-data/us10y.json`). Confirms the "never guess, always SKIP + `[DIAG]`" discipline worked in production on the first try — nothing shipped a wrong number.
- **But the TE regex itself missed on every single currency**, for a reason the log's own `[DIAG]` snippets pinpointed precisely: v2.10.0 assumed one dated "Bonds" table row per tenor. The real page has two different, unrelated shapes instead — **10Y** has no table row at all but TE's own SEO `<meta id="metaDesc">` tag reliably carries a plain-English sentence with the exact value AND a real date ("The yield on Germany 10Y Bond Yield rose to 3.21% on August 14, 2026..."); **2Y** has a real "related instruments" row, but undated (a live quote, not a historical print), with the value in a same-row `<td id="p">` cell reached via the row's own `href="/{slug}/2-year-note-yield"` anchor.
- `_te_govt_bond_latest()` rewritten to parse both shapes correctly, validated directly against the literal `[DIAG]` text captured in the live log (not a fresh fetch — `tradingeconomics.com` still isn't reachable from this sandbox): 10Y confirmed matching for Germany/UK/Japan/Australia/Canada/NZ/Norway/Sweden/Switzerland (9/10 — USD's page didn't contain the search string at all, not a regex miss, left as a graceful SKIP pending direct confirmation of US-specific phrasing); 2Y confirmed matching for Germany/Japan/Australia/Canada/Switzerland/Sweden (6/10 — USD/GBP/NZD/NOK's pages didn't contain a matching 2Y href, also left as graceful SKIPs, each already covered by its existing fallback chain).
- 2Y's undated live-quote row is stamped with today's UTC date as an explicit "as of fetch time" approximation (documented in the function docstring, not silently treated as a real settlement date) since TE doesn't expose one on this particular row.
- **Still not confirmed against a second live run** — this is a regex fix validated against captured diagnostic text, not a fresh end-to-end fetch. Next `update-bond-yields.yml` run is the real test; if any currency still SKIPs, its `[DIAG]` snippet is the next debugging input, same recovery loop as this session.
- Gate run this session: `python3 -m py_compile fetch_bond_yields.py` (OK); new regexes independently unit-tested against the exact `[DIAG]` snippets pasted from the live log (all 9 confirmed 10Y matches + the Germany 2Y match reproduced correctly).

### GUIDELINES.md
- No rule changed — this is the same "verify against the real live run, not an assumption" discipline the Data integrity section already documents (v8.153.2's own entry, `fetch_te_core_inflation.py`'s SEK precedent); this session is that verification step actually happening. Footer not bumped.

No CSS change required — `.econmx-val`/`.econmx-ref` in `dashboard.css` are generic rules, not scoped to calendar-driven cells specifically.
- Cache-busters bumped: `index.html`, `sw.js` → `assets/econ-matrix.js?v=2.2.8`; `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION` → `gi-v8.153.1`.

## v8.153.0 (2026-08-14) — CHF/NZD Core CPI fetcher live-validated and shipped to production; SEK Core CPI gap closed (was mistakenly documented as having no TE equivalent)

### Engine — scripts/fetch_te_core_inflation.py (v1.0 → v2.0)
- **v8.152.0's `guest:guest` API path was live-tested this session via a one-off manual GH Actions dry-run and confirmed non-viable**: both `switzerland/core inflation rate` and `new zealand/core inflation rate` returned HTTP 410 — guest access does not cover these two indicators, exactly the risk flagged (but not yet tested) in v1.0's docstring. Per the v8.151.0 GUIDELINES rule ("verify a source's access before building on it"), that path was abandoned rather than retried against a different key format.
- **New source, same session: the public `tradingeconomics.com/{country}/core-inflation-rate` page itself.** Confirmed server-rendered (fetched raw, no JS execution — the "Components" data table is present in the initial HTML response) before writing any scraping code, per the same GUIDELINES rule applied to the positive case (confirm a source *can* be scraped plainly before reaching for Playwright/Chromium — Santiago's suggestion this session — which turned out to be unnecessary). Rewritten to `requests` + a regex table-row parser, matching the plain-HTML scrape pattern already used by `fetch_rates.py` in this repo. Still fully defensive: any HTTP error, missing row, or unparseable number returns `None` (explicit per-currency `SKIP` log, exit 0) rather than guessing — same discipline as v1.0, now proven necessary in practice (the API path's SKIP path is exactly what fired and prevented a bad deploy).
- **Live-validated end to end this session** (GH Actions run, 2026-08-14): dry-run confirmed both values parse correctly — CHF 0.3% (Jul 2026), NZD 3.2% (Jun 2026) — cross-checked CHF against the page's own visible text fetched independently. A production run (no `--dry-run`) then wrote both events to `calendar-data/calendar.json` successfully.
- **Date precision caveat, documented in the script header**: the public page's "Reference" column gives only month + year, not an exact release day (unlike the abandoned API path, which would have given a full date). `dateISO` is set to the 1st of the referenced month as a display simplification — not a real release date. If a Myfxbook/FF page for either series ever appears, it should replace this fetcher (real date available).
- **Markup-fragility note**: this is a scrape of a page TE controls and can reshape without notice. Added a diagnostic path — on a regex-match failure, the script logs a raw-HTML snippet around "Core Inflation Rate" so a future SKIP can be debugged from the Actions log directly, without another blind round-trip.

### Engine — .github/workflows/update-te-core-inflation.yml (new)
- Production workflow, following the same double-checkout + `SCRIPTS_PAT` cross-repo push pattern as `backfill-supplementary.yml`, with push-retry-via-rebase (matching `update-inflation-expectations.yml`, appropriate here since this now runs unattended on a schedule). `workflow_dispatch` kept alongside a **weekly** `schedule` cron (Monday 08:00 UTC, changed from an initial monthly-fixed-date design per Santiago's flag that TE's release day shifts month to month — a fixed date can lag the real print by up to ~30 days; weekly caps that lag at ~7 days) — re-running against an already-covered `dateISO`/currency/event key is a safe no-op (existing-key skip logic in the fetcher, unchanged from v1.0). A separate `test-te-core-inflation.yml` (dry-run only, `contents: read`, no commit step) was kept rather than deleted — useful for future markup-change debugging without touching the calendar file.

### Engine — scripts/fetch_te_core_inflation.py (v2.0 → v3.0) / assets/econ-matrix.js (v2.2.6 → v2.2.7): SEK Core CPI
- **Correction, not a new finding:** SEK core inflation (CPIF ex Energy) was documented across three prior touchpoints (v2.2.4, GUIDELINES.md v8.151.0, this session's own earlier v8.152.0 entry) as having "no equivalent Trading Economics indicator." That was wrong — only Myfxbook had actually been checked for SEK; TE was never separately queried for this currency even while being actively used for CHF/NZD in the same investigation. Caught this session via a direct search once the CHF/NZD fetcher was already working, prompting a re-check of the same "no equivalent source" gap notes for other currencies against the newly-proven-viable source.
- TE does carry the series at `tradingeconomics.com/sweden/core-inflation-rate`, labelled **"CPIF excl. Energy YoY"** — a different display name than CHF/NZD's pages ("Core Inflation Rate"), plausibly why an earlier informal check missed it. Confirmed server-rendered and live-scraped successfully (0.60% YoY, Jul 2026, cross-checked against the page's own visible text).
- `fetch_te_core_inflation.py` v3.0 generalized the table-row matcher to take a per-currency label (`TARGETS` entries now carry their own exact label string) rather than assuming "Core Inflation Rate" is the universal string across every country's page — the bug class that let this gap go unnoticed even if someone had tried the naive search. SEK added to `TARGETS`.
- `econ-matrix.js` v2.2.7: `CATS.SEK.core` wired to `['Core Inflation Rate YoY']` — same displayed event title as CHF/NZD (the frontend-facing title stays uniform by project convention; TE's differing internal page label is handled inside the fetcher, never exposed to the frontend). Cache-busters bumped: `index.html`, `sw.js` → `assets/econ-matrix.js?v=2.2.7`; `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION` → `gi-v8.153.0`.

## v8.151.0 (2026-08-14) — AUD Retail Sales closed out (genuine Myfxbook coverage gap, not our bug); CHF/NZD Core CPI direct-fetcher build stopped short of shipping — no verifiable source found

### Frontend — assets/econ-matrix.js (no code change)
- **AUD rtl — investigation closed, no fix needed.** Santiago flagged `AUD RTL SALES` as still blank in the live Matrix despite `CATS.AUD.rtl: ['Retail Sales MoM']` having been correctly wired since v2.2.3. Fetched the live Myfxbook page directly (`myfxbook.com/forex-economic-calendar/australia/retail-sales-mom`, 2026-08-14): the page itself — not our `calendar.json` — has no observation newer than 2025-07-31 and reports "No data" for the next scheduled release. This is a genuine gap in Myfxbook's own coverage of this series, not a wiring or filter bug on our side; nothing to fix until Myfxbook resumes publishing it. Re-check periodically per the standing "confirmed gap" rule (v8.142.0) rather than treating this as permanently settled.

### Engine — no new fetcher shipped (CHF Core CPI, NZD Core CPI)
- **Investigated building direct fetchers for CHF and NZD core inflation** (Santiago requested "implementa todo" after confirming both series are real and distinct from the headline CPI already wired: FSO core CPI ex food/seasonal/energy/fuel, and RBNZ's Sectoral Factor Model). Neither has a Myfxbook calendar page (re-confirmed this session), so a same-pattern wiring fix isn't possible — a genuine new fetcher would be required, same category as `fetch_ois_rates.py`'s direct-central-bank-API pattern.
- **CHF (FSO/BFS):** the FSO publishes core inflation via its PX-Web API (`www.pxweb.bfs.admin.ch/api/v1/{lang}`), but the exact table code for the LIK core-inflation series was not pinned down this session — the price-index table tree wasn't reachable through search-driven discovery alone (BFS's PX-Web catalog needs interactive drill-down, not search). Not wired.
- **NZD (RBNZ):** the Sectoral Factor Model is published quarterly by RBNZ as an analytical note alongside each CPI release, not as a dated series on a stable queryable API endpoint that could be located this session. Not wired.
- **TradingEconomics guest:guest considered and rejected for this use case without live verification.** Both CHCIR (Switzerland) and the NZD equivalent exist as TradingEconomics indicators, and the project already has TradingEconomics' "guest:guest" endpoint confirmed reachable from GH Actions for other purposes — but TradingEconomics' public guest access is documented as restricted to a small fixed demo set (historically Mexico and a handful of markets/countries), not arbitrary country/indicator combinations, and this session's tooling could not make a live test call against the actual indicator endpoint to confirm access. Per the standing rule below, this was **not** wired on an unverified assumption.
- **No fetcher shipped rather than ship one built on an unconfirmed source.** Consistent with the project's "verify before hardcoding" discipline (GUIDELINES.md, AUD 2Y incident) — a fetcher whose underlying access hasn't been confirmed live from the actual execution environment (GitHub Actions) is a worse outcome than leaving the cell blank with a documented reason. See new GUIDELINES.md rule below.
- **Next steps if Santiago wants this chased further:** (1) test the TradingEconomics guest:guest historical-by-indicator endpoint directly from a GH Actions run (not from this session's tooling, which can't make an unlisted outbound call) against `switzerland/core inflation rate` and the NZD equivalent; (2) if guest access is confirmed insufficient, browse BFS's PX-Web catalog interactively (not via search) to find the exact `px-x-...` table code for LIK core inflation; (3) for NZD, contact/monitor RBNZ's own publication calendar for the Sectoral Factor Model release rather than assuming an API exists.

### GUIDELINES.md
- Added Data integrity rule: a third-party API's public/guest access tier must be verified live, from the environment that will actually call it, before a fetcher is built against it — a documented example call for one country/indicator pair (or a different product on the same platform) does not establish that guest access covers the pair actually needed. See rule below.

## v8.149.0 (2026-08-14) — CRITICAL: full audit of backfill_supplementary_events.py found every checked hardcoded value wrong; fixed AUD, removed EUR/CAD/NZD

### Engine — scripts/backfill_supplementary_events.py (v1.0 → v1.1)
- **Reported by Santiago:** a data conflict flagged for AUD Current Account 2026-06-02 (script said -A$4.1B; live Myfxbook showed -A$27.1B) prompted a full audit of this script instead of a one-off patch, given its "scraped offline" values had never actually been cross-checked against the primary source.
- **AUD Current Account — audited 6/6, wrong 6/6.** Verified every entry against ABS "Balance of Payments and International Investment Position, Australia" media releases: script values were off by 3x–20x against the real level, and 2025-09-02 had the wrong sign entirely (script showed a +A$1.4B surplus; ABS recorded a -A$13.7B deficit). Not a "change vs. level" mix-up — the wrong values don't consistently match any single alternate figure (level, QoQ change, or otherwise), so the exact origin of the bad scrape couldn't be pinned down. **Fixed:** all 6 replaced with ABS-verified levels, each dated release now cited inline in the script:
  - 2025-03-04 (Dec Q2024): -A$0.6B → **-A$12.5B**
  - 2025-06-03 (Mar Q2025): -A$2.7B → **-A$14.7B**
  - 2025-09-02 (Jun Q2025): +A$1.4B → **-A$13.7B** (sign was inverted)
  - 2025-12-02 (Sep Q2025): -A$3.3B → **-A$16.6B**
  - 2026-03-03 (Dec Q2025): -A$4.8B → **-A$21.1B**
  - 2026-06-02 (Mar Q2026): -A$4.1B → **-A$27.1B**
  - `previous` also populated for the 5 quarter-over-quarter entries, using each release's own stated (ABS-revised) prior-quarter figure rather than left `null`.
- **EUR Current Account (18 obs) and CAD Manufacturing Sales MoM (12 obs) — spot-checked, wrong on every checked value.** EUR: cross-checked 6 months against ECB's monthly balance-of-payments press releases — the euro area ran a current account *surplus* in every one of those months (as it has for most of the period), while the script alternates positive/negative with magnitudes matching no ECB release. CAD: cross-checked 5 months against StatCan's "The Daily" Monthly Survey of Manufacturing — same pattern, no match on sign or magnitude. Not individually re-derived for all 18/12 given the scale of a full month-by-month primary-source citation effort — **removed entirely** rather than leave wrong data in place or guess at replacements, per the existing "leave a cell blank rather than displaying an unverifiable value" rule.
- **NZD Manufacturing Sales YoY (2 obs) — removed.** 2026-03-11 didn't match TradingEconomics' StatsNZ-sourced YoY figure (-0.7% vs. script's -1.9%); 2026-06-08's script value (+3.6%) traces to a QoQ figure being used for a column titled YoY — two different measures of the same release, not two vintages of the same one. Removed rather than guessed.
- Script header rewritten with a permanent incident note directing future backfills to cite the specific primary-source release for every value, not just name a source in the header comment.

## v8.148.0 (2026-08-14) — Economic Matrix: closed out the two gaps deferred from v8.146.0's sweep (NZD PPI, SEK core)

### Frontend — assets/econ-matrix.js (v2.2.3 → v2.2.4)
- **NZD ppi — re-classified from genuine gap to wiring miss.** Re-checked live against `myfxbook.com/forex-economic-calendar/new-zealand` and found a live page for **"PPI Output QoQ"** (Low impact, quarterly, Source: Statistics New Zealand) that the v2.2.3 sweep missed. The upstream impact-filter fix that lets this event through — `_IMPACT_UPGRADES`'s `"ppi"` substring, `fetch_ff_calendar.py` v3.43 — had **already shipped** before this sweep; this was never an upstream/source gap, only a downstream miss where `econ-matrix.js`'s own `CATS.NZD.ppi` list stayed `[]` after the source-side fix landed. Wired: `ppi: ['PPI Output QoQ']`.
- A second live Myfxbook page exists under **"PPI Input QoQ"** — deliberately **not** wired. Input PPI measures what NZ producers pay for inputs, a distinct series from Output PPI (what they receive), not an alternate cadence of the same series (unlike CHF's YoY/MoM pair). Every other currency's `ppi` column reports the output/producer-price concept, not an input-cost index — wiring Input alongside Output would let the matrix's single-value lookup arbitrarily surface either concept under one "PPI" label.
- **SEK core (CPIF Excluding Energy) — re-confirmed as a genuine gap.** Checked the full live Sweden Myfxbook calendar listing (through its ~Sep 2026 horizon): carries CPIF YoY/MoM (headline) and Inflation Rate YoY/MoM, no separate core/ex-Energy title under any name. The series is real and actively published by Riksbank/SCB (confirmed via search) — Myfxbook simply doesn't carry a calendar page for it. Left as `[]`.
- No upstream (`fetch_ff_calendar.py` / `calendar-watcher.js`) changes needed this pass — NZD PPI only needed matrix-side wiring, not a new `_IMPACT_UPGRADES` entry.
- Cache-busters bumped: `index.html`, `sw.js` → `assets/econ-matrix.js?v=2.2.4`; `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION` → `gi-v8.148.0`.

### GUIDELINES.md

Did you mean: 'G10_CURRENCIES'?`, immediately after this session's `calendar-watcher.js` v5.30 deploy — unrelated to that deploy; a pre-existing bug that happened to surface on the next scheduled run.

## v8.145.0 (2026-08-14) — Regenerated assets/dashboard.test.js after accidental local deletion

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.test.js (new file — restored)
- **Reported by Santiago:** the canonical 85-test suite (`assets/dashboard.test.js`, documented in GUIDELINES.md's "Automated tests" section) had been accidentally deleted from the local working tree a few days prior. It was absent from this session's zip export as well as the v8.144.0 session's export — confirming the deletion, not just a stale/missing upload.
- **Rebuilt from scratch**, matching the exact 9-module / 85-test breakdown already documented in GUIDELINES.md's coverage table: `fmt`/`clsDir`/`pctStr` (15), `isOpen` (12), `computeRate` (7), Stress scoring (18), `localizeSignalTime` (6), Business dates (7), Yield spreads (4), `computeHV30` (9), Pearson correlation (7).
- **Approach:** `dashboard.js` is a browser script with top-level IIFEs that touch `document`/`window`/`navigator` on load and has no CommonJS exports, so it cannot be `require()`-d directly into a Node test runner without a DOM stub that would itself become a second, silently-diverging source of truth. Instead, each tested function is mirrored line-for-line from its current source location (cited in a comment above each mirror in the test file) — `fmt`/`clsDir`/`pctStr`/`isOpen`/`computeRate`/business-date helpers/stress-scoring/bond-spread logic from `assets/dashboard.js`, and `computeHV30`/`pearson` from the engine's `fetch_intraday_quotes.py` (`compute_hv30()` / `pearson()`), per the existing GUIDELINES.md rule that the JS HV30 implementation must mirror the Python one exactly (min 22 closes, last-31-price window, sample variance `n-1`, `√252 × 100` annualisation).
- Business-date and session functions are parameterised on an explicit reference `Date` instead of reading the system clock, per the existing "no `Date.now()` dependency without a fixed input" determinism rule — all business-date test fixtures use fixed UTC-noon dates for known weekdays (2026-08-10 Mon → 2026-08-16 Sun).
- One correctness note surfaced while writing the Yield-spread tests: the flat-spread case (equal 2Y yields on both legs) produces `-0` after the existing sign-flip in `dashboard.js`, not `0` — mathematically identical but distinguishable under `Object.is`/`assert.strictEqual`. The test compares with `===` rather than `strictEqual` for that one assertion; `dashboard.js` itself needs no change since `-0` renders and compares identically to `0` everywhere it's actually used (template-literal interpolation, `<`/`>` comparisons).
- `node --check assets/dashboard.test.js`: OK. `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → **85 passed, 0 failed**.

### GUIDELINES.md
- No rule changed — this restores a file the guidelines already mandate and describe; footer not bumped.

## v8.143.0 (2026-08-14) — CRITICAL FIX: Economic Matrix — PPI column shipped without updating index.html, desyncing every column after it

### Frontend — index.html, assets/econ-matrix.js (v2.2.0 → v2.2.1)
- **Reported by Santiago**, from a live screenshot: the "10Y Yld" column was blank-looking for every currency, and USD's cell under that header showed a tooltip reading "United States PCE Price Index YoY" — clearly the wrong data under that header.
- **Root cause**: v8.142.0 added `'ppi'` to `econ-matrix.js`'s `COLUMNS` array (11 → 12 categories) but did not update `index.html`'s Economic Matrix `<thead>` or its 10 skeleton `<tbody>` rows to add the matching PPI `<th>`/`<td>`. `rowHTML()` builds each row's cells purely by iterating `COLUMNS` in array order, with zero awareness of what `index.html` declares as headers — the two have always had to be kept in sync by hand, and this change broke that sync for the first time since the column count was last touched. Effect: every column from PPI onward rendered one position left of its header — PPI's data appeared under "Unemp", Unemp's under "Ind Prod", ... and by the end of the row, PCE data appeared under "10Y Yld", the real 10Y yield appeared under "CB Rate", and the real CB Rate was pushed off the right edge of the table entirely (invisible without horizontal scroll).
- **Fix**: added the missing `<th scope="col">PPI</th>` to `index.html`'s `<thead>` (positioned after Core CPI, before Unemp — matching `COLUMNS` order exactly) and one `<td class="flat">—</td>` skeleton placeholder to each of the 10 currency rows, in the same position. Updated the table's `aria-label` to mention PPI. Added a guard comment directly above `COLUMNS` in `econ-matrix.js` stating explicitly that any future add/remove/reorder of a `COLUMNS` entry must be paired with an `index.html` thead + skeleton-row edit in the same change — this file cannot enforce that pairing at runtime, so it has to be caught by whoever edits it next reading the comment.
- Bumped `econ-matrix.js` to v2.2.1 to document the incident in its own header (no rendering *logic* in the .js file was wrong — the bug was entirely in index.html's static markup not matching it).

### Verification
- `node --check assets/econ-matrix.js` and `node --check sw.js`: OK.
- Programmatically extracted `COLUMNS` key/label order from the shipped `econ-matrix.js` and compared it against `index.html`'s rendered `<thead>` header text, end-to-end, in a Node harness: **exact match**, confirming the fix, not just a visual spot-check (`Ccy, GDP, CPI YoY, CPI MoM, Core CPI, PPI, Unemp, Ind Prod, Bus Cond, Rtl Sales, Cur Acct, Trade Bal, PCE YoY, 10Y Yld, CB Rate`).
- `<thead>` now has 15 `<th>` (1 Ccy + 14 data columns); each of the 10 skeleton rows now has 15 `<td>` (1 Ccy + 14 data placeholders) — counted programmatically per row, not assumed.
- `index.html` `<div>`/`<tr>`/`<td>` balance: 532/532, 151/151, 780/780 (`<td>` count correctly increased by 10 — one new skeleton cell × 10 currency rows — vs. the prior session's 770).

### Frontend — index.html, sw.js
- Cache-buster bump: `assets/econ-matrix.js?v=2.2.0` → `?v=2.2.1`. `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION` bumped `gi-v8.142.0` → `gi-v8.143.0`, `STATIC_PRECACHE` entry synced to `?v=2.2.1`.

### GUIDELINES.md
- Added one Data integrity rule: adding/removing/reordering an `econ-matrix.js` `COLUMNS` entry must be paired with an `index.html` thead + skeleton-row edit in the same change, since the two files have no automated way to stay in sync. Footer bumped to v8.143.0.

## v8.141.0 (2026-08-14) — Economic Matrix: GDP column — fixed GBP QoQ omission, disclosed USD's SAAR convention

### Frontend — assets/econ-matrix.js (v2.0.0 → v2.1.0)
- **Reported by Santiago**, as a follow-up question after v8.140.0 shipped: is it industry-standard for the GDP column to show different periodicities (QoQ/MoM/YoY) across different currency rows? Investigated against the live `calendar-data/calendar.json` and found three distinct things bundled under that one question — one real bug, one already-correct behavior, and one bigger comparability issue found unprompted.
- **(1) Bug — GBP: `CATS.GBP.gdp` was `['GDP MoM']` only**, never including the QoQ title. The UK's ONS DOES publish a quarterly GDP figure — bundled into the same release as the monthly print 3 of every 4 months. Confirmed in the feed: "United Kingdom GDP Growth Rate QoQ" (0.4%) and "United Kingdom GDP MoM" (0.3%) both dated 2026-08-13, the same release. The old array meant the cell could never show the quarterly headline even on a release day, contradicting the column's own tooltip policy ("QoQ where published, YoY otherwise"). **Fix:** added `'GDP Growth Rate QoQ'` ahead of `'GDP MoM'` — `findLatestGeneric()`'s existing same-date tie-break (unchanged) now resolves same-day releases to QoQ, and still correctly falls back to MoM as the freshest real data in the two in-between months. Re-verified against the live feed post-fix: GBP now reads 0.4% QoQ (13 Aug) instead of 0.3% MoM.
- **(2) Reviewed, not changed — CAD**: its quarterly print is genuinely stale (last Q1 2026, 2026-05-29) relative to the monthly print (2026-07-31, 0.2%) — the existing freshest-date selection already surfaces the right cell. No bug, no change.
- **(3) Found during this investigation (not what was asked) — USD's GDP figure is SAAR, not comparable to other currencies' raw QoQ**: USD's matched title, "GDP Growth Rate QoQ", is by the BEA's own convention already seasonally-adjusted ANNUALIZED (SAAR) — the familiar "grew at an annualized pace of X%" figure. Every other currency's "GDP Growth Rate QoQ" in the same feed is the raw, non-annualized quarterly change. Both were tagged identically as "QoQ" in the per-cell subtext, which reads as directly comparable magnitudes when they are not (US 1.5% SAAR next to EA's 0.4% raw QoQ implies ~4x stronger US growth; the non-annualized equivalent is ~0.37%, in line with the EA print). **Fix:** `periodLabel()` now special-cases `gdp`/`USD`/`qoq` to render "QoQ SAAR" instead of a bare "QoQ" — every other cell's tag is unchanged. Required threading `ccy` through `cellHTML()`/`rowHTML()`, which didn't previously receive it. Column tooltip (`COLUMNS[0].title`) updated to disclose this explicitly.
- **Not changed**: CHF's `gdp` list still prioritizes YoY over its QoQ Flash print — out of scope for this session (wasn't asked, needs its own verification pass before touching per the "fix only what's reported" convention). Flagged in "On the horizon" below.

### Verification
- `node --check assets/econ-matrix.js`: OK.
- Re-ran the matching logic in a Node harness against the live `calendar-data/calendar.json` (not a mocked fixture) for all three affected cells post-fix: GBP gdp → 2026-08-13, "United Kingdom GDP Growth Rate QoQ", 0.4%, label "QoQ" (correct — the USD-only SAAR special-case correctly does not fire here). USD gdp → 2026-07-30, "United States GDP Growth Rate QoQ", 1.5%, label "QoQ SAAR". CAD gdp → 2026-07-31, "Canada GDP MoM", 0.2%, label "MoM" (unchanged, confirmed still correct).
- `index.html` `<div>`/`<tr>`/`<td>` balance: 532/532, 151/151, 770/770 — unchanged (cache-buster bump only, no markup structure touched).
- `assets/dashboard.test.js` was not present in this session's upload — no change was made to `dashboard.js` itself. Flagging per this repo's non-negotiable pre-deployment rule: **confirm `node assets/dashboard.test.js` still reports the full suite passing before deploying**, using the actual repo checkout.
- **Not verified in a real browser this session** — confirm visually that the slightly longer "QoQ SAAR · 30 Jul" subtext doesn't crowd the USD GDP cell at the smallest supported viewport (the cell uses `white-space: nowrap`, so it will widen rather than wrap; the panel already scrolls horizontally, no CSS change was made or judged necessary, but a visual check is still worth doing).

## v8.140.0 (2026-08-14) — Economic Matrix: institutional-user data-accuracy audit — country-prefix drift, AUD unit bug, EUR contamination; added CPI MoM, Core CPI, PCE, per-cell reference dates

### Frontend — assets/econ-matrix.js (v1.0.5 → v2.0.0)
- **Reported by an institutional client** (Dimitrius, relayed by Santiago via WhatsApp, with screenshots): USD CPI YoY showed a stale-looking 4.2% instead of the 3.4% released 2026-08-12; AUD "CPI" showed "102.03" — an index level in points, not a %-rate; no MoM alongside YoY; no visible reference date per cell; no core/PCE measure shown, despite central banks weighting core more than headline.
- **Root cause (not stale source data):** `calendar-data/calendar.json` already carried every correct latest print. `findLatest()`'s `CATS` prefix lists only covered a few observed title variants per currency, and Myfxbook titles the same release inconsistently — sometimes bare ("Inflation Rate YoY"), sometimes country-prefixed ("United States Inflation Rate YoY") — so on any date the upstream title format drifted, matching silently fell through to an older event that happened to match a listed variant. Separately, AUD "Australia CPI" (the raw index) and "Australia Inflation Rate YoY" (the %) are two different releases printing the same day, and the old code had no deterministic way to prefer one when both matched — it picked whichever came later in that day's insertion order.
- **Also found during this audit (not reported by the client):** EUR's bare "Business Confidence" title silently interleaves at least three different unlabeled national surveys (three distinct value ranges, no country field to disambiguate) — a latent data-integrity bug independent of the client's report.
- **Fix:** (1) country-prefix canonicalisation before matching (`canon()`), so "United States X" and bare "X" key to the same series regardless of which form Myfxbook used that day — mirrors the existing pattern in `calendar-panel.js`'s `_calCanonTitle()`; (2) EUR is matched *without* canonicalisation, against explicit literal "Euro Area " prefixes only (`findLatestEUR()`) — a deliberate asymmetry, since stripping the country prefix for EUR would blend in member-state prints (Germany/France/Italy/...); (3) strict prefix match (`strictMatch()` — exact, or prefix + a parenthetical suffix like "(Apr)") replacing the old loose `startsWith`, so "CPI" can never match "CPI Trimmed-Mean"; (4) deterministic same-day tie-break — prefix list order is now a real, documented priority ranking, not iteration-order luck; (5) dropped "Australia CPI" (the index level) from the AUD `cpi` prefix list entirely; (6) EUR `conf` is now an intentional gap with an explanatory tooltip rather than an unreliable blend of surveys; (7) both matching functions now skip events with `actual == null` (a scheduled-but-not-yet-printed release), caught during this session's own verification (NZD's Business NZ PMI for 2026-08-13 was pending — the fix now correctly falls back to the last real print, 2026-07-08's 59.7, instead of showing a blank cell).
- **New columns, per client request:** CPI MoM (a YoY figure can mask a recent trend reversal via base effects); Core CPI YoY (AUD uses the RBA Trimmed Mean CPI as its standard core-equivalent, per the RBA's own published rationale); PCE YoY (US-specific — the Fed's preferred gauge — blank with an explanatory tooltip for the other nine currencies, which target CPI/HICP-based measures instead).
- **New per-cell subtext:** every calendar-derived cell now shows its reference period + date under the value (e.g. "YoY · 12 Aug"), so YoY/QoQ/MoM prints are never visually ambiguous (NZD CPI, quarterly-only, now reads "QoQ · 20 Jul" rather than a bare rate that could be mistaken for an annual figure) and staleness is visible without opening the tooltip.
- **Verified against live `calendar-data/calendar.json`** (Node harness replicating the shipped matching logic, not a mocked fixture) for all 10 currencies × 11 categories before and after the fix — see the full per-currency, per-category output in this session's working notes. Confirms: USD CPI → 3.4% (2026-08-12), AUD CPI → 3.8% (2026-07-29, correctly the rate not the index), NZD Bus Cond → 59.7 (2026-07-08, correctly skips the pending 2026-08-13 null print).

### Frontend — index.html
- Economic Matrix `<thead>` updated: "CPI" split into "CPI YoY" / "CPI MoM", added "Core CPI" and "PCE YoY" columns. Table `aria-label` updated to match. All 10 skeleton `<tbody>` placeholder rows expanded from 10 to 13 `<td>`s to match the new column count (prevents a CLS flash on first paint).
- Cache-buster bump: `assets/econ-matrix.js?v=1.0.5` → `?v=2.0.0`.

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.css
- `.econmx-table` `min-width` increased 760px → 1180px for the 3 new columns (table already scrolls horizontally via `.econmx-wrap { overflow: auto }` — no layout change to surrounding panels).
- Added `.econmx-val` / `.econmx-ref` — the new two-line cell structure (value + small muted reference-period/date subtext), plus row vertical-padding to fit the second line.

### Frontend — README.md
- Economic Matrix bullet in "What it covers" updated to reflect the new CPI YoY/MoM split, Core CPI, PCE, and per-cell reference dates.

### Verification

- `index.html` `<div>` balance: 532/532. `<tr>` balance: 151/151. `<td>` balance: 770/770 (all unchanged in kind, `<td>` count increased consistently with the 3 new columns × 10 rows).
- `assets/dashboard.css` brace balance: 670/670.
- `assets/dashboard.test.js` was not present in this session's upload — no change was made to `dashboard.js` itself, so this is not expected to affect the suite. Flagging per this repo's non-negotiable pre-deployment rule: **confirm `node assets/dashboard.test.js` still reports the full suite passing before deploying**, using the actual repo checkout rather than this session's ZIP extraction.
- **Not verified in a real browser this session** (no live deploy access) — confirm visually before deploying that the new columns render correctly at the panel's fixed 440px height (horizontal scroll, not vertical overflow) and that the reference-date subtext doesn't crowd the value at the smallest supported viewport.

## v8.139.4 (2026-08-14) — Pre-auth flash guard: eliminate the Overview→terminal flash for returning active users

### Frontend — index.html
- **Reported by Santiago** (screenshot): on every load, the free Overview snapshot briefly flashed on screen before the full terminal appeared — including for visitors with a fully-valid, already-active license, who should never see the snapshot at all.
- **Root cause:** gi-overview.js's `initToggle()` decides Overview-vs-terminal by reading `window.GI_AUTH.isActive`, but that flag is only set once gi-auth.js's `init()` runs. Both `gi-auth.js` and `gi-overview.js` are loaded with `defer`, which means they execute after the browser has already parsed (and, on this site's blocking-CSS setup, largely painted) the body's static markup — where `#gi-overview` is visible by default and `#gi-terminal-view` is `display:none` by default (the correct no-JS fallback). So every visitor's first paint was the snapshot, full stop, regardless of license state; the swap to the terminal only ever happened one or more frames later, once the deferred scripts ran.
- **Fix:** added a new synchronous inline `<script>` as the literal first element inside `<head>` — before any stylesheet, before any `defer`red or `async` script. It re-checks the exact same `gi_license_token` JWT (same key, same `exp`-only validity check as `gi-auth.js`'s `isJWTValid()`) and, if still valid, sets `data-gi-preauth="1"` on `<html>` before the browser has parsed a single element of `<body>`. A matching CSS rule in the existing critical inline `<style>` block (`html[data-gi-preauth="1"] #gi-overview/#gi-terminal-view/#gi-footer-actions`) hides the snapshot and reveals the terminal shell before first paint — `!important` is needed against `#gi-terminal-view`/`#gi-footer-actions` since both are hidden via an inline `style="display:none"` attribute in the static markup. This is a *pre-paint guess*, not a replacement for the real check: gi-auth.js's `init()` and gi-overview.js's `initToggle()`/`showTerminal()` still run exactly as before afterward and remain authoritative — the guard is idempotent when it guessed right, and self-corrects (via the existing swap logic) in the rare case a token expires in the few hundred ms between requests.
- **Regression guard:** the guard's CSS override is `!important`, which would otherwise fight `showOverview()`'s own inline-style writes the next time a non-reactivated visitor closes the activation modal (gi-auth.js's `hideModal()` → `giShowOverview()` path, v1.7.0) — silently reintroducing the "closing the modal leaves the full terminal open" bug v1.7.0 fixed. Closed by having both `gi-auth.js`'s `handleRevocation()` and `gi-overview.js`'s `showOverview()` clear `data-gi-preauth` as their first action, before any inline-style write.

### Frontend — assets/gi-auth.js (v1.7.4 → v1.7.5)
- `handleRevocation()` now clears `data-gi-preauth` on `<html>` the moment a token is found invalid (403/401 from `/session/ping`) — see regression-guard note above.

### Frontend — assets/gi-overview.js (v1.3.1 → v1.3.2)
- `showOverview()` now clears `data-gi-preauth` on `<html>` as its first action — see regression-guard note above.

### Verification
- `node --check` on `assets/gi-auth.js`, `assets/gi-overview.js`, `sw.js`: all OK.
- `index.html` `<div>` open/close tag balance: 532/532 (unchanged from v8.139.3 — only `<script>`/`<style>` content added, no div-level markup touched).
- `assets/dashboard.test.js` was not present in this session's upload — no change was made to `dashboard.js` itself, so this is not expected to affect the suite. Flagging per this repo's non-negotiable pre-deployment rule: **confirm `node assets/dashboard.test.js` still reports 85/85 before deploying**, using the actual repo checkout rather than this session's ZIP extraction.
- **Not verified in a real browser this session** (no live deploy access) — confirm visually before/after on a throttled connection (e.g. Chrome DevTools "Slow 3G" + CPU throttling, where the flash is easiest to see) that a returning activated visitor's first paint is the terminal shell, not the Overview snapshot, and that closing the activation modal without activating (fresh incognito session, or with the JWT manually cleared) still correctly lands on the Overview with no leftover full terminal underneath.

### Frontend — index.html, sw.js
- Cache-buster bump: `assets/gi-auth.js?v=1.7.4` → `?v=1.7.5`, `assets/gi-overview.js?v=1.3.1` → `?v=1.3.2`. `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION` bumped `gi-v8.139.3` → `gi-v8.139.4`.

## v8.139.0 (2026-08-13) — Session tab: fixed Market Commentary flicker, capped at 3 articles, added in-modal currency switcher

### Frontend — assets/heatmap-modal.js
- **Reported by Santiago** (screenshot, follow-up to v8.138.0): the Session tab's new Market Commentary block was visibly flickering, showed too many news lines, and he asked for an in-modal currency switcher matching the one already on the COT modal.
- **Root cause of the flicker:** `_hmRefreshIfOpen` (the Finnhub RT-tick handler) calls `populateSession(_ccy, _rtCache)` on every tick while the Session tab is active — by design, per that function's own "Session data is from session_high/low (changes slowly) — full render acceptable" comment. v8.138.0's `_hmLoadSessionNews(ccy)` call was wired into `populateSession()` unconditionally, so it re-ran (and re-rendered a loading spinner, then the same articles) on every single RT tick — several times a minute — even though the underlying news doesn't change that often. That's the flicker.
- **Fix:** added a module-level `_hmNewsCcy` guard. `_hmLoadSessionNews(ccy)` now no-ops immediately if `ccy === _hmNewsCcy` (already loaded/loading for this currency) — it only fetches and re-renders when the currency actually changes. Also added a stale-response check after the `await fetch()` resolves, in case the currency changes again while a fetch is still in flight.
- **Article cap:** `.slice(0, 6)` → `.slice(0, 3)`, per Santiago's explicit "deberían ser tres máximo."
- **New in-modal currency switcher**, mirroring `cot-modal-chart.js`'s `#cot-ccy-switch`/`cotCycleCcy`/`cotToggleCcyDropdown`/`cotSwitchCcy` pattern exactly (same DOM shape, same class-naming convention, namespaced `hm-` instead of `cot-` per this file's existing collision-avoidance rule):
  - Header now reads `[flag] ‹ [NZD ▾ dropdown] › — NZ Dollar Strength` instead of a static `[flag] NZD — NZ Dollar Strength`.
  - `‹`/`›` arrow buttons cycle through the G10 currencies present in `_strengths` (always all 10, passed in from `window._hmStrengths` — unlike COT's per-currency lazy-fetch cache, no separate data-availability check is needed); disabled at the ends of the list.
  - Clicking the `NZD` chip opens a 2-column dropdown of all available currencies (`hmToggleCcyDropdown`); picking one calls the existing `hmPivotCcy()` — no new pivot mechanism, reuses the same in-modal pivot already used by the correlation matrix and CSI legend clicks.
  - `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` keys cycle currency (added to the existing `_onKey` handler); `Escape` now closes the dropdown first if open, and only closes the modal on a second press — same two-stage behavior as `cot-modal-chart.js`.
  - Clicking outside the switcher closes the dropdown without closing the modal (added to the existing backdrop-click handler in `buildModal()`).
  - `hmPivotCcy()` extended to call the new `_hmSetTitle()`/`_hmUpdateCcySwitcher()` helpers (replacing its previous inline title/flag update) and to close the dropdown on pivot; also now refreshes the Session tab (`populateSession()`) when it's the active tab on pivot — previously only Correlations (unconditionally) and CSI (only if active) were refreshed on pivot, leaving Session's bars/notes/commentary stale if a user pivoted currency while already on that tab via the matrix or CSI legend.
- **New CSS**: `.hm-ccy-arrow`, `#hm-ccy-switch`, `#hm-ccy-chip`, `#hm-ccy-dd`, `.hm-ccy-dd-item` — copied 1:1 from `cot-modal-chart.js`'s `.cot-ccy-*` block (same colors, sizing, hover/disabled states) for visual consistency between the two modals' switchers.

### Verification

- `node --check sw.js`: OK.

- Standalone Node simulation of the `_hmNewsCcy` dedup guard against a simulated open + 5 same-currency RT ticks + pivot + 3 more RT ticks: 2 fetches total (on open and on pivot), 8 skipped — confirms the flicker is gone in the underlying logic.
- Standalone Node simulation of the switcher's cycle-boundary logic (`‹`/`›` against the full G10 list): NZD‹→CHF, NZD›→NOK, USD‹→disabled (null), SEK›→disabled (null) — all correct.

## v8.138.0 (2026-08-13) — Session tab left empty space on tall screens; added Market Commentary fill block

### Frontend — assets/heatmap-modal.js
- **Reported by Santiago** (screenshots): on large/tall viewports, the Currency Strength modal's Session tab left a visible empty band below the "Session Context" card, before the modal footer. Asked whether it could be filled with news the way the CB Rate modal's Rate Chart tab fills its equivalent space with Market Commentary.
- **Root cause:** `.hm-panel.on` is `display:flex;flex-direction:column`, stretching to fill the modal's available height — but both `.hm-cw` cards inside the Session tab (the session bar grid, the Session Context notes) size to their own content (default `flex-grow:0`). Once the viewport is taller than the combined content height, the column simply doesn't fill, leaving the leftover space blank. Same underlying symptom `cb-rates-modal.js` hit in v2.5/v2.6 (Market Commentary block) and `yc-modal` hit before that.

Strength's first `.hm-cw` (already `flex:1`) and `cb-rates-modal.js`'s `.cbr-ps-wrap`.
