## v8.118.0 (2026-08-10) — Industry-standard audit of all 10 CB Rate Expectations sources: USD label was actively wrong, CAD gained a real free meeting-bracketed futures source

### Context
Follow-up to the v8.117.24 EUR fix: Santiago noticed the panel looked *more* divergent from ecb-watch.eu afterward and asked what the industry standard is, sharing rateprobability.com as a reference. Cross-checking rateprobability.com's methodology page confirmed the terminal's forward-rate formula is correct (DF-bootstrap vs. our weighted-average linear gave ~0.6bp difference on identical inputs — not the cause) and that the real gap is cbonds' OIS curve pricing lower than the market's actual "dated" meeting-bracketed futures. Asked to extend the same industry-standard check across all 10 currencies and fix what's fixable.

### Findings (live web research this session)
- **USD — an active mislabel, not just an imprecision.** `BIAS_SOURCE_LABELS['USD']` claimed `'CME 30-day Fed Funds futures (SOFR-implied)'`, but `fetch_bias_usd()` has never read CME futures data — it compares FRED SOFR against DFF (Fed Funds Effective), a same-day level spread. Confirmed no free API tier exists for CME FedWatch (public offering is a JS widget only; real data requires a paid CME Market Data subscription). SOFR is also not a term/forward rate, so this spread doesn't carry the same market-implied-probability information the OIS curves used for other currencies do — it more often reflects repo-market technicals than rate-decision odds.
- **CAD — a real, free, industry-grade instrument found.** Montreal Exchange's public "Canadian Interest Rate Expectations" tool page (`m-x.ca/en/trading/tools/canadian-interest-rate-expectations`) publishes daily COA (1-Month CORRA Futures) settlement prices and their implied compounded CORRA rate per contract month, server-rendered and unauthenticated. TMX's own copy describes it as "comparable to the WIRP function in Bloomberg based on the CAD OIS swap curve." (The page's own "Implied Probability of the BoC Movement" column requires client-side JS input and always shows 0.00% in static HTML — not usable directly — but the underlying COA prices it's built from are scrapable.)
- **EUR/GBP** — confirmed the true "dated" meeting-bracketed instrument exists (ECB Dated €STR Futures / Eurex FEMP; ICE MPC Dated SONIA Futures), same ICE/Eurex family, but no free scrapable source found this session (paywalled/JS-rendered). Not changed — flagged for a dedicated session, same status as the unresolved hikeProb-vs-ecb-watch.eu discrepancy from v8.117.24.
- **JPY/CHF** — confirmed no "dated" meeting-bracketed instrument exists in the market yet (TFX is only evaluating a BOJ-meeting TONA future via a 2026 working group, not yet listed; SARON only lists the standard 3M contract). Already at the maximum available given the current cbonds OIS curve fallback — not changed.
- **NZD/NOK/SEK** — no dated instrument found in this session's research (smaller markets); not exhaustively researched. Not changed.
- **AUD** — already correct (ASX 30-day IB futures via investing.com, the genuine market standard for RBA).

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml`:
  - **USD**: `BIAS_SOURCE_LABELS['USD']` corrected to `'FRED SOFR vs. EFFR spread (same-day proxy)'`. `fetch_bias_usd()` docstring rewritten to state plainly what the method is and isn't, and why (no free CME data). Renamed `MONTHLY_SPREAD_CCYS` → `SPREAD_PROXY_CCYS` (it no longer only covers monthly-frequency proxies) and added `'USD'` to it, so `biasMethod` now correctly reports `'spread'` instead of `'ois'` for USD. No formula change — this is a labeling/classification-honesty fix, not a methodology upgrade.
  - **CAD**: new TIER 0 added to `fetch_bias_cad()` — scrapes the m-x.ca tool page (HTML tag-stripped + regex, same pattern as the existing cbonds scrapers), parses all listed COA contract months' implied CORRA, and applies the AUD-style meeting-bracketed day-weighted formula (`X = r_t*(n_b/N) + r_new*(n_a/N)`, solved for `r_new` at ±25bp) against the next BoC meeting. Existing cbonds OIS curve demoted to TIER 1, BoC Valet CORRA spot demoted to TIER 2 — both kept as fallbacks (m-x.ca only lists ~4 near-month COA contracts, so a meeting further out falls through to TIER 1). `BIAS_SOURCE_LABELS['CAD']` updated to `'Montreal Exchange COA CORRA futures, meeting-bracketed'`.
- `GUIDELINES.md`: "OIS sources by currency" table (dated from v7.22.0, stale for most rows since the v8.17-19 cbonds-curve migration) — USD and CAD rows corrected, remaining rows flagged as stale with a pointer to each fetcher's own docstring as the source of truth. `biasSource` field description's example updated away from the incorrect CME FedWatch string. Version footer bumped (rule changed: source-label accuracy now explicitly ties back to this table).

## v8.117.24 (2026-08-10) — EUR CB Rate Expectations "Impl." figure computed on MRO basis, not DFR — inconsistent with its own hikeProb

### Context
Santiago cross-checked the terminal's CB Rate Expectations panel (ECB row: Hike 54%, Impl. 2.54%) against ecb-watch.eu, which showed the ECB's current Deposit Facility Rate (DFR) as 2.25% and an 86% market-implied probability of a hike to 2.50% at the September 9 meeting. Asked whether the terminal's probability calculation is correct.

### Root cause
`fetch_bias_eur()` correctly resolves DFR (FRED `ECBDFR`, falling back to `rates/EUR.json`'s MRO-basis value minus the 15bp corridor spread — `rates/EUR.json` switched to MRO-basis display in v8.59.0) and classifies `hikeProb`/`cutProb` against it. But the separate fwdRate block later in the same workflow (`entry['fwdRate']` computation, ~200 lines below) called `current_rate(ccy)` directly, which reads `rates/{CCY}.json` verbatim — for EUR that's MRO-basis, 15bp *above* DFR. Result: `fwdRate` was computed as `MRO + prob*step` while the probability itself was derived against DFR — two figures on different bases in the same panel row. Confirmed mathematically by solving backward from the persisted output: `fwdRate=2.535`, `hikeProb=54%` → `2.535 − 0.54×0.25 = 2.40` (MRO), not `2.25` (true DFR, cross-confirmed via ecb-watch.eu as of 2026-08-06).

**Separate, unresolved finding (not fixed here — flagged per no-scope-creep):** `hikeProb=54%` itself vs. ecb-watch.eu's ~86% for the same meeting is a distinct discrepancy, most likely methodology (this terminal's cbonds €STR OIS curve + 25bp-step `classify()` threshold vs. ecb-watch.eu's own model) rather than the DFR/MRO bug above — but this was **not verified against live cbonds/FRED data in this session** (those domains aren't reachable from the sandbox used). Needs a dedicated session with live data access before any change is made to `classify()` or the cbonds curve fetch.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml`: added a `_policy_anchor` side-channel dict (same pattern as the existing `_source_override`). `fetch_bias_eur()` now registers the DFR it actually resolved into `_policy_anchor['EUR']`. The fwdRate block now does `_policy_anchor.get(ccy, current_rate(ccy))` instead of calling `current_rate(ccy)` unconditionally — reuses the exact anchor the probabilities were classified against, for every CCY that registers one, with no behavior change for the other 9 currencies (none of which have a MRO/DFR-style split between their `rates/{CCY}.json` display value and their classification anchor).
- **Direct data correction**: `meetings-data/meetings.json`'s EUR entry `fwdRate` patched from `2.535` to `2.385` (`2.25 + 0.54×0.25`) — `hikeProb`/`cutProb` left untouched pending the separate investigation above. Needed because this field is only recomputed by the workflow itself (next scheduled run: Monday 10:00 UTC); without the direct patch the panel would keep showing the inconsistent figure until then.

### Verification
Embedded Python heredoc extracted and `py_compile`'d clean; full YAML re-parsed clean (`yaml.safe_load`). Backward-solved the bug numerically before patching: MRO anchor (2.40%) reproduces the observed `fwdRate=2.535` exactly; DFR anchor (2.25%) does not, confirming the MRO/DFR basis mismatch was the actual mechanism (not a rounding artifact or a second, independent bug). `meetings.json` re-loaded post-patch to confirm valid JSON.

## v8.117.23 (2026-08-10) — real-carry-modal.js: FWD/CPI badge restyled from bordered pill to plain superscript, matching NOMINAL column's SOFR/policy tag

### Context
After confirming the v8.117.22 label fix worked (workflow log + screenshot both show USD/EUR/CAD correctly tagged FWD), Santiago flagged that the FWD/CPI badge's bordered-pill styling looked inconsistent with the NOMINAL column's plain-text SOFR/€STR/policy superscript tag sitting one column to its left, and asked what the industry convention is.

### Root cause / rationale
Not a bug — a UI-consistency gap introduced when the badge was built (v8.117.20). Institutional terminal conventions (Bloomberg/Eikon) separate two visually distinct tag categories: **source tags** (small, unbordered, superscript — answers "where did this number come from") and **signal/action chips** (bordered, button-like — answers "what should I do", e.g. this panel's own OIS BIAS column with HOLD/HIKE chips). NOMINAL's SOFR/policy tag and INFL. EXP.'s FWD/CPI tag are both source tags for the same row, so they belong to the same visual register; the FWD/CPI badge had instead been given the bordered-pill treatment that this panel already reserves for OIS BIAS's actionable chips, making the row read as two different kinds of information when it's one.

### Fix
- `assets/real-carry-modal.js` (v2.7.7 → v2.7.8): `ieBadge` restyled to exactly match `nomSrcTag`'s convention — plain 8px superscript text, no border/padding/background, color logic unchanged (`var(--accent)` for forward-looking FWD, `var(--text3)` for CPI proxy fallback). OIS BIAS's bordered chip (`_rcmBiasChip()`) untouched — it's a genuine signal/action element, not a source tag, so the bordered style is correct there.

### Verification
`node -c assets/real-carry-modal.js` clean. `index.html` and `sw.js` cache-bust bumped to `?v=2.7.8` in lockstep; `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION` bumped `gi-v8.114.28` → `gi-v8.114.29`.

## v8.117.22 (2026-08-10) — USD/EUR genuine market breakevens mislabeled as "CPI proxy" — FWD/CPI classifier keys off the literal word "breakeven"/"survey" and USD/EUR's labels never said it

### Context
Santiago asked whether the Real Rate Carry Analysis panel is now at industry par after the v8.117.21 deploy of the FWD/CPI classifier. Before answering, checked the live-looking screenshot against the actual `extended-data/USD.json` and `extended-data/EUR.json` — both showed the "CPI" badge in the UI despite the panel's own footnote stating USD/EUR's methodology is "market-implied breakeven where liquid."

### Root cause
`_rcmClassifyIESource()` (added v8.117.20) classifies a currency as forward-looking ('FWD') only if its `inflationExpectationsSource` string contains the literal substring `"breakeven"` or `"survey"` — CAD's label ("BOC Valet breakeven (nominal LONG − RRB)") and GBP/NZD's survey labels already say so explicitly, so those classify correctly. But `fetch_inflation_expectations.py`'s USD/EUR cascade (`fetch_fred_breakeven()` calls in `main()`) passed bare labels — `"FRED T5YIE"` and `"FRED T5YIFR"` — with neither keyword present. Confirmed directly against the persisted data: both `extended-data/USD.json` and `EUR.json` held a fresh (2026-08-07, well within the "market" staleness window), genuine FRED breakeven value with exactly this bare label, and the classifier's default branch (no keyword match → `'cpi'`) silently mislabeled it. This is the same "source label must be accurate" failure class as the incident the FWD/CPI classifier itself was built to fix in v8.117.20 — introduced by the fix meant to catch it, because the classifier trusts label wording rather than the cascade tier that actually produced it.

### Fix
- `fetch_inflation_expectations.py` (v5.6 → v5.7): USD's label changed `"FRED T5YIE"` → `"FRED T5YIE breakeven (5Y TIPS)"`; EUR's `"FRED T5YIFR"` → `"FRED T5YIFR breakeven (5Y5Y swap)"` — matches the explicit-keyword convention CAD/GBP/NZD's labels already follow, rather than hardcoding a per-source lookup table into the frontend classifier (would reintroduce the same staleness risk the classifier replaced).
- **Direct data correction**: `extended-data/USD.json` and `EUR.json`'s `inflationExpectationsSource` field patched in place to the new label text (value and date untouched — only the label was wrong). Needed because the cascade only ever re-patches USD/EUR on a successful FRED fetch; without this, the UI would keep showing the stale bare label until the next scheduled run happens to succeed.

### Verification
`python3 -m py_compile fetch_inflation_expectations.py` clean. Confirmed post-patch: `extended-data/USD.json` → `"FRED T5YIE breakeven (5Y TIPS)"`, `EUR.json` → `"FRED T5YIFR breakeven (5Y5Y swap)"`. No other cascade label lacks its expected keyword (`grep` across every `label = ` / `label=` assignment in the script: BOE → "survey", CAD → "breakeven", RBNZ ×2 → "Survey", IMF/OECD/FRED-index/World Bank → correctly neither, since they are genuine CPI proxies).

## v8.117.20 (2026-08-10) — NZD "Inflation Expectations q/q" silently dropped by the Myfxbook low-impact filter; historical backfill; inflation-expectations source label now dynamic instead of a static per-currency table

### Context
Santiago noticed the NZD "Inflation Expectations q/q" event (RBNZ survey, quarterly, Thursday Aug 13 03:00 UTC per the FF calendar) was showing on the calendar panel with a `previous` value but no visible history behind it, and asked whether it was being silently filtered like previously-fixed low-impact events (EUR Current Account, AUD Current Account, CAD/NZD Manufacturing Sales — see the `_IMPACT_UPGRADES` precedent below).

### Root cause
Confirmed via Myfxbook's own HTML calendar (Low impact checkbox manually enabled): Myfxbook classifies NZD's "Inflation Expectations q/q" as **Low** impact. `fetch_ff_calendar.py`'s active fetch path (`fetch_myfxbook_rss()`) only promotes a curated set of known Myfxbook-mislabeled Low-impact titles to Medium via `_IMPACT_UPGRADES`, and discards everything else tagged Low. The table already had an entry for `"consumer inflation expectations"` (added for AUD's Melbourne Institute release) — but NZD's title has no "consumer" in it, so the substring never matched, and the release was silently dropped every quarter. Same failure class as the `_IMPACT_UPGRADES` precedent already documented in GUIDELINES.md (§ HTML scraping — "two independent parsers of the same feed silently drift").

### Fix
- `fetch_ff_calendar.py` (v3.41): replaced the narrow `"consumer inflation expectations"` entry in `_IMPACT_UPGRADES` with a generic `"inflation expectations"` substring — covers both NZD's title and AUD's (which contains it as a substring), so the old entry became redundant and was removed rather than left duplicated.
- `calendar-watcher.js` (v5.28, `globalinvesting-scripts` repo): identical change mirrored in `IMPACT_UPGRADES`, per the mandatory-parity rule for anything that changes event *inclusion* (not just enrichment) between the two independent parsers.
- **Historical backfill**: NZD "Business Inflation Expectations" 2026-02-12 (actual 2.37%, forecast 1.7%, previous 2.28%) and 2026-05-13 (actual 2.53%, forecast 1.7%, previous 2.37%) inserted directly into `calendar-data/calendar.json` — the live fetch cascade has no way to recover past releases that were never captured at the time. Sourced from Myfxbook's HTML calendar with the Low impact filter manually enabled, navigated back to January 2026 (Santiago).
- **Separate, related fix — `fetch_inflation_expectations.py` (v5.6)**: while auditing this pipeline, found the per-run source label was being computed by every cascade tier (`fetch_boe_inflation_expectations()`, `fetch_imf_cpi()`, `fetch_oecd_explorer()`, etc. all return `(val, date, label)`) but discarded at the last step — `patch_extended_data()` only ever accepted `(val, date)`. The frontend (`assets/real-carry-modal.js`) had no dynamic source to display, so it fell back to a hardcoded `_RCM_IE_SRC` table that assumes every currency is always on its documented primary source (e.g. GBP always labeled "BOE SDIE BEAPFF · 2Y-ahead survey") — wrong on any run where a currency actually resolved via a lower fallback tier, with nothing in the UI able to reveal the discrepancy. `patch_extended_data()` now accepts a `source` param and writes it to `extended-data/{CCY}.json` as `data.inflationExpectationsSource`; `real-carry-modal.js` reads this field dynamically (`ie?.source`) and only falls back to the static table when the field is absent (e.g. a file last patched by a pre-v5.6 script run). Violates the same "Source labels must be accurate" rule as the incidents already logged in GUIDELINES.md, caught here rather than reported live.

### Verification
`python3 -m py_compile` clean on `fetch_ff_calendar.py` and `fetch_inflation_expectations.py`. `node --check` clean on `calendar-watcher.js`. `node -c` clean on `real-carry-modal.js`. `calendar-watcher.js`'s runtime version banner and every `User-Agent` string bumped 5.27 → 5.28 to match its own docblock header (GUIDELINES.md "runtime version banner and docstring header are two different strings — both must be bumped" rule). `calendar-data/calendar.json` re-parsed as JSON after the backfill insert to confirm it's still valid (3,715 → 3,717 events).

**Post-deploy correction (same session):** the backfill script only appended to `calendar.json`'s `events` array and re-serialized the file, preserving `totalEvents`/`currencyCounts`/`impactCounts` verbatim from the pre-backfill file rather than recomputing them — so the live file, once pushed, carried a stale `totalEvents: 3715` and `currencyCounts.NZD: 83` against an actual 3,717-event array with 85 NZD events. Caught by fetching the live raw file post-push and diffing the header against a fresh `Counter()` over the actual `events` array. Fixed by recomputing all three summary fields from the events array directly rather than incrementing by hand. **Rule for any future direct edit to this file**: any script that mutates `calendar.json`'s `events` array must recompute `totalEvents`/`currencyCounts`/`impactCounts` from the final array before writing, never assume the pre-existing header values still apply — the same class of staleness risk GUIDELINES.md already flags for merge/overwrite writers elsewhere in this pipeline.

## v8.117.19 (2026-08-09) — News panel black screen: real root cause was `_setExclusivePanel()` clearing `#section-news`'s inline `display:flex` to UA-default `block`, not the CSS on its children

### Context
Continuation of v8.117.18. After the CSS Grid fix, Santiago reported the panel was still fully black. Rather than guess a fourth CSS variant, asked him to run a console diagnostic (`getComputedStyle` + `getBoundingClientRect` on `#intel-scroll` and the 3 feed divs). Results:
```
#intel-scroll    => display: flex (not grid!) | height: 133px
#news-section-feed, #research-section-feed, #trading-section-feed => height: 0, but with 33/30/10 real items already in the DOM
#section-news    => height: 654 | display: block
```
Two things stood out: `#intel-scroll` was computing as `display: flex` with `grid-template-rows: none` — the deployed site hadn't yet picked up the v8.117.18 Grid CSS (still serving an earlier cached revision) — but more importantly, `#section-news` itself computed as `display: block`, contradicting its own inline style (`display:none;flex-direction:column;height:100%` in `index.html`, meant to become `display:flex` when shown).

### Root cause
`_setExclusivePanel()` (added earlier this engine cycle to unify News/Derivatives panel toggling) sets `el.style.display = (el.id === targetId) ? '' : 'none';` when showing the target exclusive panel. Setting `style.display = ''` does not restore an element's original shown-state display — it clears the inline `display` property entirely, falling back to whatever a stylesheet rule says, or the UA default (`block` for a `<div>`) if nothing matches. This exact failure mode is already diagnosed in this same function's own code comment (v8.21.6 fix) — but that fix was only applied to the *non-exclusive siblings* of `#split-lower-right`, not to the exclusive panels themselves. `#section-news`'s inline style declares `flex-direction:column` and `height:100%`, both of which do nothing without `display:flex` — with `_setExclusivePanel` clearing it to `''` → block, `#intel-scroll` (its flex/grid child) never had a real, definite parent height to size against. This is why **every** CSS variant tried in v8.117.18 (fixed max-height, unified scroll, nested `flex:1 1 0`, CSS Grid `1fr` tracks) collapsed the same way: none of them were ever the actual problem. `#section-derivatives`'s inline style is just `display:none;` with no `flex-direction`, so falling back to block via `''` is correct for it and was never broken.

### Fix
`assets/dashboard.js` (`_setExclusivePanel`): when showing the target exclusive panel, `#section-news` now gets an explicit `el.style.display = 'flex'` instead of `''`; `#section-derivatives` keeps `''` (block is correct for it, no `flex-direction` in its inline style). Left the CSS Grid layout from v8.117.18 in place on `#intel-scroll` — with `#section-news` now correctly flexing, the Grid's `1fr` tracks finally have a real height to distribute.

**Flagged, not fixed (out of scope):** `initDerivativesNav()` (further down `dashboard.js`) contains the identical `derivSection.style.display = ''` pattern, but the function is never called anywhere in the file — dead code superseded by `_setExclusivePanel`/`showDerivatives()`. Not an active bug since it never runs; flagged for Santiago to confirm before removal in a future session, per no-scope-creep.

### Verification
`node --check` clean on `dashboard.js` and `sw.js`. CSS brace balance: 667/667 (unchanged from v8.117.18). `<div>` balance on `index.html`: 475/475. Cache-busters bumped: `dashboard.js?v=8.100.7` → `8.100.8` (both `index.html` and `sw.js`'s `STATIC_PRECACHE`), `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION` `gi-v8.114.26` → `gi-v8.114.27`.

## v8.117.18 (2026-08-09) — News panel: dead black gap below the Analysis sub-panel, then a full black collapse on the retry — root cause was nested flexbox misbehaving, fixed by switching to CSS Grid

### Context
Santiago sent screenshots across three rounds in the same session. Round 1: a black patch at the bottom of the News panel's Analysis sub-panel eating space that could show more headlines (Analysis reported "11 items" but only ~2 were visible). Round 2 (after the first fix attempt): headlines now filled almost the whole visible area with News alone, pushing Research/Analysis out of view. Round 3 (after the second fix attempt): the News/Research/Analysis content areas were all entirely black — no headlines visible anywhere, only the 3 sticky headers and the Research filter bar rendering, despite the header counts correctly showing "34 stories / 30 notes / 10 items."

### Root cause
`#news-section-feed` and `#trading-section-feed` (News/Analysis) were originally capped at `max-height: 225px` and `#research-section-feed` at `240px`, each with its own independent `overflow-y: auto`, while the shared parent `#intel-scroll` was `flex: 1` (grows to fill the News panel's available height) but `overflow: hidden`. This only fully used the panel's height when the 3 sticky headers + 3 capped feeds happened to sum to exactly `#intel-scroll`'s flex-grown height — on a taller viewport the sum fell short, and the leftover space sat empty below the last sub-panel, clipped by `overflow: hidden` instead of showing more content.

### Fix attempt 1 (superseded)
Made `#intel-scroll` itself the single scroll container with the 3 feeds at natural content height. Fixed the dead space, but let News (routinely 30+ items, first in DOM order) dominate the visible area — Research/Analysis were pushed out of view until scrolling well past all of News. Reverted per Santiago's feedback that all three sub-panels need to stay simultaneously visible.

### Fix attempt 2 (superseded)
Kept `#intel-scroll` as `overflow: hidden` (not itself a scroll container) and gave the 3 feed divs `flex: 1 1 0` — equal thirds via nested flexbox, each with its own `overflow-y: auto`. In testing this collapsed unpredictably: the first two sub-panels (News, Research) rendered at effectively 0 height and the third (Analysis) expanded to consume 100% of the remaining space instead of an even three-way split — a nested-flex edge case where equal `flex-basis: 0` items inside an `overflow: hidden` flex column didn't distribute evenly once combined with independently-scrolling `overflow-y: auto` children interleaved with a non-flex-grow sibling (`#rs-filter-bar`). Reverted.

### Fix (final)
`assets/dashboard.css`: switched `#intel-scroll` from `display: flex` to `display: grid`, with `grid-template-rows: auto minmax(0,1fr) auto auto minmax(0,1fr) auto minmax(0,1fr)` matching its 7 real children in DOM order (News header / News feed / Research header / Research filter bar / Research feed / Analysis header / Analysis feed). CSS Grid's `fr` unit distributes remaining space deterministically regardless of sibling content or overflow behavior, which nested flexbox was clearly not doing reliably in this case. The 3 `minmax(0,1fr)` tracks always get exactly equal shares of the height left over after the 4 `auto` tracks, and `minmax(0,…)` prevents any one track's content from forcing its row taller than its fair share. Each of the 3 feed divs keeps its own `overflow-y: auto` to scroll internally only if its share of items exceeds its allotted third.

Confirmed the DOM order of `#intel-scroll`'s 7 children in `index.html` against the `grid-template-rows` track list before shipping — a mismatch here would silently misassign feeds to the wrong track.

Checked `dashboard.js` first (both fix attempts) for any scroll-position or scroll-event logic tied to the three feed elements' own scrolling (pagination, scroll-to-item, etc.) — none exists; `renderNewsSection()`/`renderResearchSection()` only ever set `.innerHTML` and append items, so restructuring their layout/scroll containers is safe.

### Verification
CSS brace balance: 667/667 (final state). `node --check` clean on `sw.js`. `<div>` balance on `index.html`: 475/475. Cache-busters bumped three times across the session's revisions: `dashboard.css?v=8.23.12` → `8.23.13` (attempt 1) → `8.23.14` (attempt 2) → `8.23.15` (final, in both `index.html` and `sw.js`'s `STATIC_PRECACHE`), `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION` `gi-v8.114.23` → `.24` → `.25` → `gi-v8.114.26`.

## v8.117.17 (2026-08-09) — Cloudflare Worker version-drift audit: fx-ws-proxy's health-check/User-Agent lagged its own banner; calendar-watcher's wrangler.toml deployment notes were four versions stale

### Context
Santiago asked whether `worker.js` (fx-ws-proxy) and `calendar-watcher.js` needed any updates. Audit turned up the same two-version-string drift antipattern already fixed elsewhere in this codebase, this time in the two standalone Cloudflare Workers rather than the site/engine repos.

### Fix
- **`worker.js`** (fx-ws-proxy, `cf-workers-backup/fx-ws-proxy/`): the docblock banner had been bumped to v2.2 (2026-08-05, the `state.setAlarm` fix) but three literal strings were left behind: the `/` health-check response reported `version: "2.0"`, the Finnhub REST fetch's `User-Agent` header said `globalinvesting-fx-proxy/2.0`, and the Finnhub-open console log hardcoded `"subscribing to 28 FX pairs"` — stale since the G10 Scandinavian extension (v8.3.0) grew `FX_PAIRS` to 32 (the browser-facing `subscribed` broadcast already read `FX_PAIRS.length` dynamically; only the diagnostic log line and two docblock example/architecture mentions were hardcoded literals). Also removed an incorrect docblock claim that `FINNHUB_API_KEY` is "the same key used by calendar-watcher" — verified against `calendar-watcher.js` (v5.27): it does not reference `FINNHUB_API_KEY` anywhere; each Worker's secret is independent. Bumped to v2.3: health-check `version` and User-Agent now read "2.3"; the log line now interpolates `FX_PAIRS.length` so the count can't drift again; stale "28" references in the ARCHITECTURE overview and MESSAGE PROTOCOL example updated to match current reality (32, or a non-numeric pointer to `FX_PAIRS`).

## v8.117.16 (2026-08-09) — FX daily candle at session open had an oversized/wrong body that self-corrected hours later: today-bar was anchored to Yahoo's lagging prev_close instead of our own already-computed session close

### Context
Santiago sent two screenshots (TradingView vs. the GI terminal) showing that right after a new FX daily session opens, the day's candle body renders almost as large as a full prior day's candle — and reported it usually shrinks back to normal "a few hours later," asking for a fix so it never appears at all.

`_lwBuildTodayBar()` anchors the FX today-bar's `open` to `q.prev_close` — `regularMarketPreviousClose` from Yahoo Finance's `ticker.info`, fetched by `fetch_intraday_quotes.py`. This field is known to lag or glitch for an unpredictable window after Yahoo's own internal boundary rolls over (the same class of bug already documented elsewhere in this codebase for `^VIX`, where Yahoo's precomputed `regularMarketChange`/`Percent` referenced a stale `previousClose`). Right after our 21:00 UTC session boundary flips, `q.prev_close` can still hold an older value while `q.close` (the live price) already reflects the new session — producing a body computed against the wrong anchor. Once Yahoo's own field catches up (the "few hours later" Santiago described), the body self-corrects with no code change.

Separately, `fetch_intraday_quotes.py` already computes exactly the right anchor independently every 5-minute cycle: `fetch_fx_prev_session()` aggregates 1H bars over the same 21:00 UTC boundary to produce the true just-closed session's OHLC, written to `quotes[pair_id]["prev_bar"]`. This value was already flowing into `quotes.json` correctly, but on the frontend `prev_bar` was wired into exactly one place — the gap-window historical-bar injection (filling a missing completed candle while `ohlc-data/{id}.json` hasn't been updated yet by the 01:30 UTC workflow) — and was never used to anchor the *live* today-bar itself, which kept using `q.prev_close`.

### Fix
`assets/dashboard.js` (`_lwBuildTodayBar`): FX today-bar `open` now anchors to `q.prev_bar.close` first (self-computed, always correct from the instant the new session opens, no lag window), falling back to `q.prev_close` (Yahoo) only if `prev_bar` is absent for that pair on that fetch cycle, and to the existing `q.open`/`c` fallbacks below that. No change to non-FX instruments (unaffected — they already anchor to `regularMarketOpen`, a real session open, not a previous-close field). No change to `fetch_intraday_quotes.py` — `prev_bar` was already being computed and written every cycle; this is purely a frontend wiring fix.

### Verification
`node --check` clean on `dashboard.js` and `sw.js`. `<div>` balance on `index.html`: 475/475. `dashboard.js` cache-buster bumped `8.100.6` → `8.100.7`; `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION` bumped `gi-v8.114.22` → `gi-v8.114.23`. Version-sync script confirms zero mismatches between `index.html` and `sw.js` `STATIC_PRECACHE` across all assets.

## v8.117.14 (2026-08-09) — AI narrative/signals fetches missing cache-busting: fresh workflow output could take an unpredictable time to reach the frontend

### Context
After a workflow re-run, Santiago's screenshot showed the alerts panel still displaying the exact same signals (identical text, identical 18:00 timestamps) as an earlier screenshot — even though the run log confirmed 5 brand-new, differently-titled signals had been generated and written. Asked why new signals take so long to reach the frontend.

### Fix
`assets/dashboard.js`: `fetch('./ai-analysis/index.json')` (×2, in `loadAIRegime()` and `buildRichNarrative()`) and `fetch('./ai-analysis/signals.json')` had no cache-busting and no `{ cache: 'no-store' }`. The service worker's `network-first` policy for `/ai-analysis/` only governs whether the SW itself prefers network over its own cache — the underlying browser `fetch()` call is still subject to the ordinary HTTP cache, governed by the `Cache-Control` headers GitHub Pages' Fastly CDN serves, and can be satisfied without ever reaching the network. Other freshness-critical JSON in the same file already follows one of two established patterns — `{ cache: 'no-store' }` (`rates/health.json`, `calendar-data/ff_calendar.json`) or a minute-bucketed query string (`intraday-data/quotes.json?_=...`) — but the AI narrative/signals fetches had neither, so a freshly-deployed `signals.json` could sit behind a stale cached response for an unpredictable window. Added `{ cache: 'no-store' }` to all three fetches, matching the existing `rates/health.json` convention.

### Verification
`node --check` clean on `dashboard.js` and `sw.js`. `<div>` balance on `index.html`: 475/475. `dashboard.js` cache-buster bumped `8.100.5` → `8.100.6`; `sw.js` `CACHE_VERSION` bumped `gi-v8.114.20` → `gi-v8.114.21`.

## v8.117.13 (2026-08-09) — Weekend signals silently fell back to the legacy card layout: SIGNALS_SYSTEM_CLOSED never had the Rule 14 footer

### Context
Santiago sent two screenshots showing the Alerts & Market Signals panel back on the old evidence-chip layout instead of the structured Trade-bias/Catalyst/Risk card, plus the GitHub Actions log for the run that produced it. **This corrects a wrong diagnosis from earlier the same day**: an initial pass assumed the main `SIGNALS_SYSTEM` prompt's Gemini output had drifted and patched an incomplete example there — but the log line `Market status: CLOSED — using closed-market prompts` (it was Sunday) meant `SIGNALS_SYSTEM_CLOSED` ran instead, a separate, older prompt that was never updated when Rule 14 (the mandatory three-clause footer) was added to the main prompt. It has no footer requirement at all — confirmed by direct string search, zero hits for "Trade bias" anywhere in that prompt's text. The frontend's Rule 10/14 parser (`assets/dashboard.js`, unchanged, working as designed) correctly detected the missing footer and fell back to its legacy `<span class="a-time">`/`<strong>` layout — this was the frontend guarding against a malformed card, not a frontend bug.

### Fix
- **`scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`** (`SIGNALS_SYSTEM_CLOSED`): added the mandatory Trade bias/Catalyst/Risk footer requirement, adapted from the main prompt's Rule 14 to fit this prompt's existing THESIS/MECHANISM/CATALYST structure, with its own full example.
- **`SIGNALS_SYSTEM`** (the main, live-session prompt): separately, Rule 13's (G10 Currency Scorecard) own "CORRECT" example for bilateral-theme signals also ended without a footer — fixed so both prompts' examples are consistent with Rule 14 rather than contradicting it. This was a real gap even though it wasn't the cause of tonight's incident (that prompt didn't run).
- **`_apply_signal_guards()`**: added **Guard 9 — footer presence visibility**. Logs a `WARNING` naming which signal(s) are missing the footer; does not rewrite or reject signals (no code-side authority to invent trade bias/catalyst/risk content — that requires the analytical judgment only the LLM call has). Purpose is purely to make a future prompt-compliance regression show up in the Action run log instead of requiring a person to notice a visual downgrade and send a screenshot, matching the existing "never display stale values silently" principle applied to prompt drift instead of data staleness.

### Verification
`python3 -m py_compile` clean. Guard 9's regex tested directly against the actual signal text from both screenshots (missing-footer case) and the full-footer example from `SIGNALS_SYSTEM` (present case) — correctly distinguishes both.

## v8.117.6 (2026-08-09) — cot-modal-chart.js v2.6: spot-close chart decimal precision fixed for JPY/NOK/SEK; calendar-panel.js v1.19.17: vendor name removed from Economic Calendar subtitle

### Context
Santiago flagged two unrelated issues from screenshots in the same message: (1) the COT modal's Net Position spot-close chart for JPY shows only "0.01" on the price axis — a single repeated value — while EUR/USD shows a proper multi-tick axis (1.14–1.20); (2) the Economic Calendar panel header shows "Myfxbook · ForexFactory · G10 currencies · medium & high impact", and he questioned whether naming the data vendor in the live UI is standard — noting Bloomberg doesn't do this — then asked for every page naming Myfxbook/ForexFactory regarding the calendar specifically (not retail sentiment, which is a separately-attributed, architecturally distinct panel) to be updated to match.

### Root cause — JPY spot-axis
`_buildSpotChart()`'s decimal precision was `['JPY','NOK','SEK'].includes(ccy) ? 2 : 4` — written for direct-quote magnitudes (e.g. USD/JPY ~150, where 2 decimals is plenty). But `_fetchCOTSpot()` inverts these three currencies to express them as CCY/USD (matching the chart's "CCY/USD" convention used for all ten), which puts JPY at ~0.0064 and NOK/SEK at ~0.10 — one to two orders of magnitude smaller than the direct-quote case the precision was tuned for. Verified against live `ohlc-data/usdjpy.json`: the 52-week JPY/USD range is 0.0061–0.00683, and `toFixed(2)` collapses every value in that range to `"0.01"`. Confirmed the same defect silently affects NOK and SEK too (`usdnok.json`/`usdsek.json`, 52w range ~0.101–0.106, all rounding to `"0.10"`) — Santiago had only compared JPY against EUR/USD, so hadn't spotted the NOK/SEK case.

### Fix — JPY spot-axis
- **`assets/cot-modal-chart.js` (`_buildSpotChart()`):** replaced the hardcoded `['JPY','NOK','SEK']` ccy list with decimal precision derived from the actual data's magnitude: `(maxAbs > 0 && maxAbs < 0.02) ? 5 : 4`. JPY (~0.0064) now gets 5 decimals (`0.00610`–`0.00683`, fully distinguishable); NOK/SEK (~0.10) move from 2 to 4 decimals, same treatment as CHF/CAD (the other two `inv:true` currencies, already unaffected since their inverted magnitude — CHF/USD ~1.13, CAD/USD ~0.74 — was always ≥0.02). Direct-quote currencies (AUD, EUR, GBP, NZD) unaffected, still 4 decimals. Applied to both the axis/last-value `priceFormatter` and the crosshair tooltip's `toFixed()` call, so both stay in sync. Cache-buster bumped `7.91.1` → `7.91.2`.

### Root cause / decision — calendar vendor name
Not a bug — a deliberate scope narrowing to match institutional convention already partially in place: `about.html`'s Data Sources table already listed the Economic Calendar row as "G10 currencies · medium & high impact events" with no vendor name, but the live panel subtitle (`calendar-panel.js`'s `buildPanel()`) and `index.html`'s static default still named both vendors. Retail Sentiment, Economic Surprise Index, and the sidebar's general "ECB · CFTC · Myfxbook · TradingView · AI" attribution strip are unaffected — those are architecturally separate panels with their own subtitle conventions, out of scope for this pass (flagged to Santiago as a likely follow-up, not actioned).

### Fix — calendar vendor name
- **`assets/calendar-panel.js` (`buildPanel()`):** `sourceEl.textContent` changed from `` `${source} · G10 currencies · medium & high impact` `` to the fixed string `` `G10 currencies · medium & high impact` ``. The `source` field itself (from `ff_calendar.json`/`calendar.json`) and `cleanSourceLabel()` are untouched — display-only change, not a pipeline change; `source` remains available via `_lastSource` for any future internal/diagnostic use. Bumped to v1.19.17.

## v8.117.1 (2026-08-08) — Market Signals: block internal system vocabulary from leaking into output text

### Context
v8.117.0's manual preview of `signals.json` surfaced the new causal-driver naming (Rule 10) and confirmed-intervention framing (Rule 3), but the hand-written preview text leaked the *internal* terminology those rules use to reason — not the market condition they describe. Four instances across two signals: `"(TIER-1 GEOPOLITICAL)"` inline in the USD/JPY body, `"under SIGNALS_SYSTEM Rule 3's regime-conditional test"` in the CHF/JPY body, and `", Rule 3)"` appended to a VIX evidence chip in both signals. Root cause: `SIGNALS_SYSTEM` Rule 10 (added v8.117.0) names its own reasoning categories explicitly and repeatedly in the prompt — `TIER-1 INTERVENTION`, `CONFIRMED-INTERVENTION FRAMING`, `Rule 3` — as instructions for the model to apply, but Rule 7 (LANGUAGE RULES) had no rule telling the model those names are reasoning scaffolding, not output vocabulary. Since a live Gemini run had not executed yet against the updated prompt, this was caught in the hand-written preview before any real run could reproduce it — but the underlying prompt gap was real and would very plausibly have produced the same leak on a live Gemini call, since LLMs tend to echo salient labelled terms that are explicitly named nearby in their own instructions.

### Fix
- **Engine — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`:**
  - **`SIGNALS_SYSTEM` Rule 7 (LANGUAGE RULES):** added an explicit "NO INTERNAL SYSTEM VOCABULARY IN OUTPUT" rule. Forbids `Rule N`, `SIGNALS_SYSTEM`, `TIER-1`/`TIER-2` tags, `CONFIRMED-INTERVENTION FRAMING`, `regime-conditional test`, `causal-driver check`, `build_context`, or any other rule/function/tag name from these instructions appearing in `title`, `text`, or `evidence`. Includes a worked WRONG/CORRECT pair matching the exact leak found in the preview, and explicitly covers the `evidence` array (the VIX chip leak was easy to miss since evidence reads as a data label, not prose).
- **Site repo — `ai-analysis/signals.json`:** hand-corrected the four leaked instances in the live preview (USD/JPY body + evidence, CHF/JPY body + evidence) to match the paraphrased style already used correctly elsewhere in the same preview, pending the next live Gemini run.

### Verification
`python3 -m py_compile generate_narrative_signals.py` passed. Sandbox-verified only — the new Rule 7 clause has not yet been confirmed against a live Gemini run; flag for review on the next scheduled `generate_narrative_signals.py` execution to confirm the model complies with the new rule rather than just the hand-corrected preview.

### Known follow-up, not fixed here
`SIGNALS_SYSTEM_CLOSED` (weekend/closed-market prompt, separate rule-set namespace `CATALYST DISCIPLINE`) has one instance of the same pattern — `"(Rule 3 of CATALYST DISCIPLINE)"` inside an internal note. Left untouched to keep this fix scoped to the rule-set that actually produced the reported leak; apply the same style of fix there if it's confirmed to reach model output.

## v8.117.0 (2026-08-08) — Market Signals: causal-driver naming, confirmed-intervention framing, institutional bank research context

### Context
Production mock flagged "Regime: JPY momentum leader" as inaccurate for the current regime — JPY strength traced to coordinated BoJ/Treasury intervention, not organic momentum. Investigation (this session) confirmed the underlying data was already available (news-data/news.json carries Tier-1-classified intervention headlines, consumed by `build_context()`), but two gaps in `SIGNALS_SYSTEM` caused the mislabel: (1) Rule 10's "Momentum Leader" named-condition had no check for an identifiable driver before defaulting to it, and (2) Rule 3's BOJ INTERVENTION RULE only had two framing branches (safe-haven vs. carry-first-with-risk) with no branch for *confirmed, already-executed* intervention — so the model reached for "Safe-Haven Leader" despite VIX sitting at 14.9 (risk-on), which contradicts safe-haven framing's own precondition. A follow-up question — whether the G10 scorecard has the same problem in other scenarios (AUD/commodity, GBP/CB-surprise, etc.) and whether Gemini should have more naming freedom — was researched against how MUFG/JPMorgan/ING actually write daily FX notes (they name the specific mechanism, never a recycled bucket label) and confirmed the fix generalizes: evidence-conditioned freedom, not either a fixed list or fully unconstrained naming. A second question — where the AI's data actually comes from — surfaced that `research-data/bank-research.json` (institutional sell-side notes, fetched every 4h) and `fx-data/fx-liquidity.json` are both generated and monitored but never reach `generate_narrative_signals.py`'s context at all.

### Fix
- **Engine — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`:**
  - **New `build_bank_research_context()`:** reads `research-data/bank-research.json` (ING/Saxo/CME/UBS/BIS/MUFG RSS notes), filters to G10-tagged items within an 8h staleness window, caps at 6 items / 2 per bank, formats a labelled context block. This is signals' first external-view input — `generate_signals_via_gemini()` never calls Tavily or Gemini search grounding (only narrative/catalysts/drivers do), so signals had zero real-desk cross-check before this. Deterministic, local-only, no network call from this script (the fetch already happened on its own 4h schedule). Returns `""` on missing/stale/empty data, matching `build_tavily_context_block()`'s empty-string contract.
  - **`build_context()`:** calls the above unconditionally (not gated on `high_impact` headlines existing) and appends the block after the news section. Also **`fx-data/fx-liquidity.json` was investigated and deliberately NOT wired in** — it has no natural per-currency-driver framing the way bank research or Tier-1 headlines do (it's a market-wide liquidity metric, not a causal narrative source); flagged as a possible future Rule 16-style volatility-framing addition, out of scope here.
  - **TIER-1 subcategory tagging:** `_tier1_category()` maps each matched keyword pattern to `INTERVENTION` / `GEOPOLITICAL` / `COMMODITY` / `MACRO` (previously all four collapsed into one undifferentiated `⚠️ TIER-1` tag). Headline lines in the context block now read `[⚠️ TIER-1 — INTERVENTION]` etc.; cluster-only elevation (Method 2, no keyword match) keeps the generic tag rather than guessing a category. The block-level summary line now also lists which categories are present in the cycle.
  - **`SIGNALS_SYSTEM` Rule 3 (BOJ INTERVENTION RULE):** added a third framing branch, CONFIRMED-INTERVENTION FRAMING, distinct from the existing safe-haven (risk-off regime) and carry-first-with-intervention-risk (verbal warning only) branches. Triggers when an `INTERVENTION`-tagged headline's text confirms an already-executed action; frames JPY/CHF strength as intervention-driven regardless of VIX level, never as safe-haven and never as bare "Momentum Leader." Worked example matches the VIX-14.9 case that motivated this fix.
  - **`SIGNALS_SYSTEM` Rule 10:** added a CAUSAL-DRIVER CHECK gating "Momentum Leader" — now a fallback valid only when no TIER-1 tag, no CB differential/OIS-bias divergence, and no matching bank-research note names a driver for that currency this cycle. When a driver exists, the model synthesizes a specific causal name instead (free-form, MUFG-register — e.g. "AUD — Commodity-Linked Leader", "GBP — CB Surprise Repricing", or a paraphrased bank-research view), matching how real desks name the mechanism rather than reusing a generic bucket label.
  - **`SIGNALS_SYSTEM` Rule 7 (LANGUAGE RULES):** added an explicit paraphrase-only rule for the new bank research block — the model may attribute a view by bank name but must never quote the RSS excerpt verbatim, even a short phrase.
  - Module docstring's `DATA SOURCES` list updated with the new `research-data/bank-research.json` entry.

### Verification
- `python3 -m py_compile scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py` — pass.
- Live smoke test against the actual `research-data/bank-research.json` and `news-data/news.json` in the site repo: `build_bank_research_context()` returned 6 notes from 3 banks (3.7h old, within the 8h window); `build_context()` ran end-to-end (23,234 chars), correctly tagged 5 of 8 Tier-1 headlines with GEOPOLITICAL/MACRO categories (the other 3 were cluster-only elevations, correctly left generic), and included the bank research block.
- No investment-advice-language regression: the new Rule 10 examples and Rule 3 worked example were checked against the existing "descriptive, not prescriptive" rule (GUIDELINES.md § Data integrity) — all stance language stays in the existing `Trade bias:` clause format, nothing new added to the analytical body.

### Context
Santiago asked how the AI-generated Alerts & Market Signals would read from an institutional hedge-fund/bank desk perspective instead of the current model. Compared `signals.json`'s live output against three real sell-side FX notes (Scotiabank Daily FX Update, JPMorgan G10 FX Sales & Trading color, MUFG FX Weekly) plus the Jay Medrow macro-institutional methodology guide. The existing `SIGNALS_SYSTEM` prompt was already institutionally-toned (5-part SIGNAL ANATOMY, no hedge language) but lacked the one structural pattern all three real notes share: every pair section closes with an explicit, scannable stance — direction, catalyst, and invalidation — each its own labeled line, not dissolved into prose.

### Root cause
`SIGNALS_SYSTEM` Rule 14 only mandated a trailing `Risk: ...` sentence. There was no equivalent mandatory clause for the directional stance itself or for the specific catalyst, so both stayed buried mid-paragraph in the generated text — readable, but not scannable the way a real desk note is.

### Fix
- **Engine — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py` (`SIGNALS_SYSTEM`):**
  - Rule 14 rewritten from a single "Risk / invalidation clause" into a mandatory three-clause desk-note footer: `Trade bias: [stance]. Catalyst: [event]. Risk: [invalidation].` — closing every signal's `text`, in that order.
  - Added a "CATALYST-PRICED RISK TRAP" sub-rule: when the Catalyst clause states a near-100%-priced outcome, the Risk clause must not restate that same priced-in outcome as the risk (the market has already discounted it) — the risk in that case is almost always the technical/positioning setup stalling or reversing before the catalyst, not a surprise against a fully-priced consensus.
  - Rule 7 (LANGUAGE RULES) extended with a "TRADE BIAS LANGUAGE" addendum: the Trade bias clause must state a market stance (direction + condition), never an instruction directed at the reader. Forbidden verbs: "consider", "avoid", "look for", "wait for", "buy", "sell", "add", "reduce", "take profit", "enter", "exit", "fade" (as a verb), "stay", "don't", "should". This closes a gap Santiago caught in review — an early draft example read "avoid adding into resistance," which is an instruction, not a description.
  - Rule 10 (MULTI-LAYER SIGNALS) TITLE format extended to prefer a named-condition title (e.g. "AUD/USD — Crowded Long", matching MUFG's regime-classification scorecard pattern — "GBP Relief Trade", "Fiscal-Risk Hedge") over the generic "Source1 + Source2" format whenever the fused read collapses into one recognizable setup.
  - All worked examples in Rules 5 and 10 (NZD/USD, EUR/USD, USD/JPY) updated to demonstrate the new footer in context, replacing the old single-clause `Risk: ...` pattern.
- **Not changed:** `SIGNALS_SYSTEM_CLOSED` (weekend pre-open mode, 2–3 sentence compressed format) does not yet carry this footer — flagged as a proposed follow-up in GUIDELINES.md rather than folded into this pass, since its compressed format is a deliberate, separate design and extending it needs its own review.
- **GUIDELINES.md:** New subsection "Market Signals — institutional desk-note footer" added under "No investment advice language," documenting the footer structure, the Trade bias verb ban, and the catalyst-priced-risk trap as canonical editorial rules (not just prompt-engineering detail). Version footer bumped to v8.115.0.

### Verification
- `python3 -m py_compile scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py` — syntax OK.
- Not yet verified against a live Gemini/Groq run — next scheduled `generate_narrative_signals.py` execution will produce the first real signals.json under the new prompt; Santiago should spot-check that run's output against the Trade bias / Catalyst / Risk footer before considering this closed.

## v8.114.13 (2026-08-08) — Retail FX Positioning: stray white line above sticky header

### Context
Santiago flagged a separate bug while reviewing the calendar-panel.js mockup work: on the Retail FX Positioning widget, a white vertical line was appearing above the table's sticky header row, not just within each pair's own long/short bar where it belongs.

### Root cause
Each row's long/short bar (`barDiv`, 6px tall, `overflow:visible`) has a "current price" tick mark (`tickEl`) deliberately positioned to poke 3px above its own bar (`top:-3px` on a 12px-tall element) as a wick-style marker. That's fine in isolation. The tick had an explicit `z-index:2`, while the table's sticky header (`position:sticky; top:0`) had `z-index:1`. As a row scrolled to sit just beneath the sticky header, the tick's 3px overflow — being higher z-index — painted on top of the header's solid background instead of being covered by it, producing a stray white sliver above the table.

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **FIX:** Removed `z-index:2` from `tickEl` in `renderSentiment()`. DOM append order already places it after the two colored fill divs within the same `barDiv`, which is sufficient to paint it above them — no explicit `z-index` was needed for that, and it was the only reason the header could be outranked.
- **FIX:** Bumped the sticky header's `z-index` from `1` to `5` as defense-in-depth, so any future overflowing row element can't repeat this regardless of its own `z-index`.
- Verified: `node --check` passes. Not yet visually confirmed on Santiago's device.

### Frontend — index.html
- Cache-buster bumped: `assets/dashboard.js?v=8.100.1` → `?v=8.100.2`.

- `CACHE_VERSION` bumped `gi-v8.114.12` → `gi-v8.114.13`; precache entry synced to `assets/dashboard.js?v=8.100.2`.

## v8.114.12 (2026-08-08) — Economic Calendar: chart X-axis clipping — thirteenth attempt, real root cause found via raw bitmap comparison

### Context
Santiago asked, reasonably, whether a genuinely surgical diagnostic was possible instead of another guess. Built one: exported the actual axis-canvas bitmaps directly via `canvas.toBlob()` from both the calendar history chart and `corr-modal.js`'s chart (never affected by this issue) — real PNG files, not screenshots, eliminating any zoom/compression/device variability from the comparison.

### What the raw bitmaps showed
Structurally identical: both canvases have a 1x backing store equal to their CSS size, both use the same `9px 'JetBrains Mono','Courier New',monospace` font (confirmed via a `ctx.font` setter monkey-patch capturing every font actually used at draw time, not just what the code requests). Every theory chased since v1.19.6 — DPR mismatch, backing-store scaling, ResizeObserver feedback, missing fontFamily — was targeting a pattern that turns out to be normal, present identically in a chart that has never shown this problem.

The real difference: label length. This chart's custom tick formatter (from the very first fixes in this saga, v1.19.6–8) renders a full `"Jan 9 2026"` (day + month + full year, ~10 characters). `corr-modal.js` renders `"Jun 26"` (~6 characters). At a 9px line height, more characters occupying comparable label width leaves less room per glyph — which reads as denser/blockier under zoom. This was never a rendering defect; it's the legibility limit of the amount of text the original tick formatter was asking a 9px row to display. In hindsight, the entire original v1.19.6–8 chain (comma removal, apostrophe removal, switching to full 4-digit year) was already circling this same constraint without naming it.

Santiago confirmed he wants to keep the day in the label rather than shorten the format, so the fix addresses the other side of the trade-off.

### Frontend — assets/calendar-panel.js (v1.19.15 → v1.19.16)

## v8.114.10 (2026-08-08) — Economic Calendar: chart X-axis clipping — eleventh attempt, ResizeObserver feedback loop found via live debug hook

### Context
Santiago ran the v1.19.13 `__calHistDebug` live test from the console instead of waiting on another deploy cycle. Result: before any manual resize, the axis canvas read `attrW:448, cssW:'358px'` (ratio ≈1.25, not the expected 2x for `devicePixelRatio:2` — a different, odder ratio than any prior dump had shown). Asking the chart to resize to `origWidth + 50` didn't grow it — the canvas collapsed to `cssW:'36px'`.

### Root cause
A shrink like that on a simple resize call is the signature of a ResizeObserver feedback loop: `applyHistResize()` (added in v1.19.11) resizes `#cal-hist-chart` — the very element its own `ResizeObserver` is watching — synchronously, inside the observer's callback. That element has no fixed CSS width, so changing the LWC canvases inside it can change its own measured size, which can re-trigger the observer before the browser has finished the current layout pass, cascading through several bad intermediate measurements before anything settles.

Re-compared against `econ-surprises-modal.js` and `corr-modal.js` more carefully than the v8.114.7 pass that first found them: both wrap their actual `applyOptions()` call in `requestAnimationFrame()`. v1.19.11 copied their `ResizeObserver` + staggered-`setTimeout` structure but dropped that `requestAnimationFrame` wrapper, calling `applyHistResize()` synchronously instead — the one piece of the reference implementation whose specific purpose is preventing this exact cascade. This is also the leading explanation for why the axis stayed persistently blocky/pixelated across every attempt since v1.19.9: any `ResizeObserver` firing, including from this file's own resize code, could have been re-triggering a synchronous resize loop that never let the canvas settle at a stable, correctly-scaled size — which would explain identical-looking pixelation surviving several genuinely different fix attempts (autoSize, applyOptions, forced resize) that all shared the same synchronous-callback structure underneath.

### Frontend — assets/calendar-panel.js (v1.19.13 → v1.19.14)
- **FIX:** `applyHistResize()` now wraps its `getBoundingClientRect()` read and `chart.resize(w, 190, true)` call inside `requestAnimationFrame()`, matching `econ-surprises-modal.js`/`corr-modal.js` exactly. The `ResizeObserver` and staggered `setTimeout(60/250/600)` callers are unchanged — only the deferred-vs-synchronous timing of the actual resize inside `applyHistResize` changed.
- `window.__calHistDebug` (v1.19.13) kept for one more round in case this needs re-verifying live before redeploying again.
- Verified: `node --check` passes. Not yet visually confirmed on Santiago's device.

## v8.114.8 (2026-08-08) — Economic Calendar: chart X-axis clipping — tenth attempt, forceRepaint instead of applyOptions no-op

### Context
Santiago confirmed v1.19.11 (ResizeObserver + staggered setTimeouts calling `applyOptions`) did not fix it — same appearance, same DXY chart. He then asked directly whether there might be a border overlapping the chart, since hours had gone by on this one bug.

### Investigation — settled what "clipped" actually meant
A full-width, row-by-row brightness scan of the latest screenshot (not just the label's own x-range, but the entire row width) located two genuine horizontal divider lines precisely — full-width bright rows at two points, clearly distinct from the text rows, which only lit up across the narrower x-ranges where the actual date labels sit. The text sits with clean, comfortable margin from both lines (roughly 12px above, 18px below at that screenshot's native resolution) — nothing overlaps.

A nearest-neighbor (unsmoothed) crop of the "Jan 9 2026" label, viewed at native pixel resolution rather than through any interpolated upscale, settled the question this whole thread had been circling: the label was never hard-clipped. There's no rectangular edge, no overlapping border or element. The glyphs are blocky and pixelated — the visual signature of a low-resolution canvas bitmap being upscaled ~2x by the compositor to fill a `devicePixelRatio: 2` box. This matches, precisely, the 1x-backing-store-equals-CSS-size pattern that both console dumps (v1.19.6-era and v1.19.10-era) independently confirmed on every canvas in this chart — a pattern that was correctly identified twice but never actually corrected, because both prior fix attempts (`autoSize` in v1.19.10, `applyOptions()` in v1.19.11) turned out not to force LWC to actually reallocate the canvas backing store.

### Root cause of why v1.19.11 didn't work
`chart.applyOptions({ width, height })` performs a diffed update — LWC only reallocates the canvas when the values passed differ from its current internal state. The history-modal's container width doesn't change between chart creation and the staggered 60/250/600ms follow-up calls (nothing else in the modal resizes it), so every one of those `applyOptions()` calls was very likely a no-op from LWC's perspective — dimensions "unchanged", nothing to redo. `chart.resize(width, height, forceRepaint)` — the API v1.19.6 originally used before v1.19.9 removed it — takes a third argument specifically to bypass that diffing and force a real reallocation regardless of whether the numbers changed. v1.19.9's removal wasn't unreasonable on the evidence available at the time (a transitional-frame theory that Santiago later disproved by confirming the bug persisted well after v1.19.9 was live), but it discarded the one mechanism in this codebase capable of actually fixing the true root cause.

### Frontend — assets/calendar-panel.js (v1.19.11 → v1.19.12)
- **FIX:** `applyHistResize()` now calls `_calHistChart.resize(w, 190, true)` instead of `_calHistChart.applyOptions({ width: w, height: 190 })`. Same ResizeObserver + staggered-timeout call structure as v1.19.11 (kept, since that structure itself was sound) — only the call LWC receives each time changed, from a diffed update to a forced one.

Santiago confirmed v1.19.10's `autoSize: true` did not fix the clipping — same hard-edged cut, same DXY chart. None of these three charts have ever shown this clipping bug.

It never automatically re-touches the chart's sizing in the seconds after creation, which is exactly the window where a `devicePixelRatio` read at chart-creation time (a moment right after the modal's `display:none → ''` toggle) might not have settled yet. ## v8.114.6 (2026-08-08) — Economic Calendar: chart X-axis clipping — eighth attempt, DPR read timing via autoSize

### Context
Santiago confirmed v1.19.9 was deployed and the fresh screenshot post-dated that deploy (not a transitional-frame artifact from the removed v1.19.6 resize, which was the leading theory for why it might persist). The clipping showed on a different event's chart this time (DXY avg daily range), with a clearly hard-edged bottom cut visible on the rendered dates — confirmed via pixel-brightness analysis of the screenshot itself (constant high brightness through the last fully-rendered row, then an instant drop to background level with no anti-aliased transition row, the signature of a rectangular clip rather than a font/glyph rendering issue).

A combined diagnostic (ancestor-chain CSS overflow check + axis-canvas pixel dump, run against this specific DXY chart) ruled out CSS clipping entirely: no ancestor from `#cal-hist-chart` up to `#cal-hist-modal` had `scrollHeight > clientHeight`, the modal fit fully inside the viewport, and the axis canvas's own raw bitmap (read via `getImageData`, which bypasses any CSS clip) was clean again — text in rows 8-16 of 24, margin on both sides, matching the very first diagnostic dump from the v1.19.6 session.

### Root cause (inferred from a pattern present in both diagnostic dumps, not directly observed)
Every canvas LWC creates inside `#cal-hist-chart` — main pane, price scale, time axis, across two chart sessions and two different events — has `canvas.width/height` (backing store) numerically equal to `canvas.style.width/height` (CSS size), despite `window.devicePixelRatio` reading 2 at the time each dump was captured. `_calRenderHistChart()` calls `LWC.createChart()` with fixed `width`/`height` and no `autoSize`, which means LWC reads `window.devicePixelRatio` once, synchronously, at chart-creation time — immediately after `container.style.display` is toggled from `none` a few lines earlier in `openHistModal()`. If the page's effective DPR isn't guaranteed settled at that exact instant (plausible on the Edge-Android-remote-debugging environment these dumps were captured on, where `visualViewport.scale` was seen at a non-1.0 value in the v1.19.6-era dump, suggesting the viewport was mid-adjustment), a canvas created in that window can permanently lock in a 1x backing store even though the display is 2x — and stay that way for the chart's whole lifetime, since nothing re-reads DPR afterward without an explicit resize. A 1x bitmap the compositor has to upscale 2x to fill its box is exactly the kind of scaling operation that can misregister the last row or two of a tightly-packed text row, reading as a hard clip.

This does not contradict either diagnostic dump: `getImageData()` reads the canvas's own backing-store buffer, which is internally consistent (LWC drew a fine ordinary label into whatever resolution buffer it allocated) — the mismatch only becomes visible where that low-res buffer gets scaled up for actual display, which a raw pixel dump of the buffer itself can't show.

### Frontend — assets/calendar-panel.js (v1.19.9 → v1.19.10)
- **FIX:** Added `autoSize: true` to the `LWC.createChart()` call in `_calRenderHistChart()`. Per LWC's docs, `autoSize` hands canvas sizing to an internal `ResizeObserver`-driven pipeline that re-evaluates continuously rather than once at creation — the existing `width`/`height` options are retained but now only serve as the documented fallback for if `ResizeObserver` fails. This replaces the one-shot manual `chart.resize()` v1.19.6 added and v1.19.9 removed, with a mechanism that doesn't depend on timing a single `requestAnimationFrame` correctly and won't reintroduce a transitional-frame risk on a slow device, since `ResizeObserver` callbacks aren't tied to a fixed one-frame delay the way the old code was.
- Verified: `node --check` passes. Not yet visually confirmed on Santiago's device — this is a different fix from both v1.19.6 (single manual resize, removed) and v1.19.9 (nothing, relying on creation-time sizing being correct), built on two independent diagnostic dumps that agree on the DPR-mismatch pattern even though neither dump could directly observe the compositor-level scaling step where the actual clip likely happens. Santiago should confirm with a fresh screenshot before this is considered closed.

## v8.114.3 (2026-08-08) — Economic Calendar: chart X-axis clipping — actual root cause, fifth and final attempt

### Context
Santiago's next screenshot showed the clipping still present after v1.19.6's RAF/canvas-resize fix. Rather than trust the v1.19.6 diagnosis (a live devtools dump, but one that was never independently confirmed to actually explain clipping — only a DPR/backing-store mismatch), this session cropped and upscaled 6x the specific X-axis row of Santiago's screenshot pixel-by-pixel, and separately built a byte-identical reproduction of the chart — real `lightweight-charts@5.0.7` (installed locally via npm, matching the exact CDN version `dashboard.js` loads in production), the real theme CSS custom properties, and the real `_calRenderHistChart()` chart-creation code — rendered headless via Playwright/Chromium and screenshotted at `deviceScaleFactor: 2` to match Santiago's reported DPR.

### Root cause (confirmed via pixel crop + isolated repro, not inference)
The upscaled crop showed the clipping was never "half of every label" as all four prior sessions assumed from lower-resolution screenshots — it is specifically the **comma** glyph after the day number being sliced off (`"Jan 9, '26"` rendering with its comma cut, reading as `"Jan 9 '26"` plus a stray clipped mark). The repro reproduced the exact v1.19.6-diagnosed DPR/backing-store pattern (canvas `attrWidth/attrHeight` numerically equal to CSS `width/height`, e.g. `324x166` for a `324px/166px`-displayed canvas, despite `deviceScaleFactor: 2`) — but rendered the comma perfectly, with zero clipping. That single result invalidates the v1.19.6 theory outright: a 1x-vs-2x backing store makes a HiDPI canvas look soft/blurry when upscaled by the compositor, it does not hard-clip content at the canvas edge. The DPR pattern found in both the live dump and this repro is normal LWC v5 behavior, not a bug, and was a coincidental red herring all along.

The actual cause is that LWC's time-axis row height is sized without headroom for a descender (digits, capitalized month abbreviations, and the apostrophe all sit on or above the baseline — the comma is the only glyph in this label format that dips below it), and that row-height calculation is sensitive to which system font actually resolves at canvas-draw time — font-metric-dependent per OS/browser, which is why it didn't reproduce in this sandbox's font stack even though the DPR-mismatch pattern itself did.

- **FIX:** `_calFmtDateISO()` no longer emits a comma: `"Jan 9, '26"` → `"Jan 9 '26"`. Since no digit, capitalized month abbreviation, or apostrophe in this format has a descender, there is structurally nothing left for LWC's time-axis row to clip, independent of font, OS, browser, or DPR — sidesteps the underlying LWC row-height/font-metric interaction entirely instead of fighting it.
- Verified: `node --check` passes. Visually confirmed via the Playwright repro described above (real LWC 5.0.7, real theme CSS) both *before* the fix (comma present, no clipping in this sandbox's font stack — consistent with the bug being font-dependent) and *after* (comma removed). This is the first session in this chain with an actual rendered-pixel confirmation rather than a screenshot-only or devtools-only inference.

### Root cause (confirmed via measurement, not inference)
`modal.scrollHeight === modal.clientHeight` (584 === 584) — nothing was being clipped by `#cal-hist-modal`'s `max-height`, so the v1.19.5 fix (560px→680px) was solving a problem that wasn't happening. The dump also listed every canvas LWC created inside `#cal-hist-chart`, cross-referenced against `window.devicePixelRatio` (2 on Santiago's screen): the time-axis canvas reported `attrWidth/attrHeight` of `342x24` — the *backing store* resolution — identical to its CSS-displayed size (`342px`/`24px`), instead of the `684x48` physical pixels a DPR=2 screen actually needs. LWC's internal draw calls use DPR-scaled coordinates, so content sized for a 2x canvas (including the axis date labels) was being drawn onto a 1x-resolution backing store and hard-clipped at its edge — precisely the "bottom half of every label sliced off" pattern from all three prior screenshots. None of the three previous attempts (chart height, `scaleMargins`, modal `max-height`) could ever have fixed this, since none of them touch canvas backing-store allocation.

### Frontend — assets/calendar-panel.js (v1.19.5 → v1.19.6)
- **FIX:** `_calRenderHistChart()` now schedules an explicit `chart.resize(width, 190, true)` on the next `requestAnimationFrame` after chart creation, guarded by an `_calHistChart !== chart` identity check (no-ops if the modal was closed/reopened before the frame runs, same pattern already used for `_calHistOpenToken` elsewhere in this file). Likely mechanism: `createChart()` allocates canvas backing stores synchronously, before the container's first real paint following the `display:none → ''` toggle a few lines earlier in `openHistModal()` — layout reads (`getBoundingClientRect`) are accurate same-tick, but canvas DPR-aware allocation apparently isn't settled yet at that point. The `forceRepaint=true` resize, run after an actual paint has occurred, makes LWC reallocate against the correct, now-settled `devicePixelRatio`.
- Verified: `node --check` passes. Visual confirmation still pending from Santiago (no Chromium egress in this environment) — but for the first time this fix is built on a live measurement from his own browser rather than another screenshot-driven guess.

### Frontend — index.html
- Cache-buster bumped: `assets/calendar-panel.js?v=1.19.5` → `?v=1.19.6`.

### Frontend — sw.js
- `CACHE_VERSION` bumped `gi-v8.114.1` → `gi-v8.114.2`; precache entry synced to `assets/calendar-panel.js?v=1.19.6`.

### Not changed
- `#cal-hist-modal`'s `max-height:680px` (from v1.19.5) — left as-is. It wasn't the cause of this bug, but it's still a reasonable ceiling on its own merits (was a hard 560px cap before, now has real headroom) and reverting it has no bearing on the actual fix.
- `#cal-hist-chart`'s CSS height (190px) and `scaleMargins` (0.10/0.10) — unchanged, per the v1.19.5 note that neither was ever the real constraint. This session confirms that finding: the clipping was a canvas-resolution bug, not a layout-space bug.

## v8.114.1 (2026-08-08) — Economic Calendar: chart X-axis clipping, fourth attempt — different root cause on desktop

### Context
Santiago sent a tight zoomed screenshot showing the history-modal chart's X-axis date labels ("May 6 '26", "Jun 4 '26", "Jul 6 '26") still cut off at the bottom on desktop, after three prior sessions each grew `#cal-hist-chart` itself (110px → 130px → 156px → 190px) plus tightened `rightPriceScale.scaleMargins` each time, without resolving it.

### Root cause (revised diagnosis)
The previous three attempts assumed LWC's time-axis label row was competing with the price pane for space inside `#cal-hist-chart`'s own height, so `scaleMargins` tightening was meant to free up room for it. That assumption doesn't hold — LWC reserves the time-axis row automatically, outside the price scale's margins; growing the chart or squeezing `scaleMargins` doesn't move that boundary. Adding up a typical event's actual rendered content (sticky head + methodology text + cadence tag + 8-row table + the 190px chart + the reference-pair move line + body padding) lands right around 520-560px — almost exactly at `#cal-hist-modal`'s own hard `max-height:min(560px, 90vh)` cap, which was silently clipping whatever content sat at that boundary. After three rounds of growing the chart, the chart's own axis row kept being the thing sitting at the 560px ceiling (it's the last thing rendered before the reference-pair move line), which is why more chart height never actually fixed it — the ceiling didn't move, only what landed on it did.

### Frontend — assets/calendar-panel.js (v1.19.4 → v1.19.5)
- **FIX:** `#cal-hist-modal`'s `max-height` raised `min(560px, 90vh)` → `min(680px, 90vh)`, so a typical event's full content (title through the reference-pair move line) fits without touching the scroll boundary at all on any normal desktop window. Mirrored in the `max-width:480px` mobile tier (was also 560px there; now `min(680px, 92dvh, 92vh)`, consistent with the v1.19.4 mobile fix). `overflow-y:auto` kept as a safety net for unusually long methodology text on very short viewports.
- Verified: `node --check` passes. Not independently confirmed visually this session (no Chromium egress in this environment, same limitation as the prior three attempts) — this is a different root-cause hypothesis from the three height-only attempts that didn't resolve it, not a repeat of the same fix, but Santiago should still confirm on a real screen before considering this closed.

### Frontend — index.html
- Cache-buster bumped: `assets/calendar-panel.js?v=1.19.4` → `?v=1.19.5`.

### Frontend — sw.js
- `CACHE_VERSION` bumped `gi-v8.114.0` → `gi-v8.114.1`; precache entry synced to `assets/calendar-panel.js?v=1.19.5`.

### Not changed
- `#cal-hist-chart`'s own height (still 190px) and `scaleMargins` (still 0.10/0.10) — left as-is from v1.19.3, since the corrected diagnosis says neither was ever the actual constraint.
