## v8.114.0 (2026-08-08) — Economic Calendar: history modal broken on mobile (global CSS leak)

### Context
Santiago reported the calendar history modal (`#cal-hist-modal`) was broken on mobile and sent a screenshot (United States Unemployment Rate) showing the title, table headers ("Previous" reduced to a sliver), and general layout looking cut off / squeezed on a phone-width viewport, despite the modal rendering correctly on desktop.

### Root cause
Not in `calendar-panel.js`. `assets/dashboard.css`'s mobile block (`@media (max-width: 900px)`) carries an unscoped `table { min-width: 480px; }` rule, added to force the FX pairs table to scroll horizontally instead of squeezing on small screens. Because the selector is a bare `table` with no scoping, it also applied to `#cal-hist-modal table` on every viewport ≤900px — effectively every phone. The modal itself is capped at `width:min(420px, 100%)` and never grew to match, so the 480px-wide table physically overflowed the dialog's border. That read as clipped/truncated text in the screenshot; it wasn't a text-clipping bug, the table was simply wider than the box containing it. The same media block already carries a precedent for exactly this kind of exclusion (`#rightpanel table { min-width: unset !important; ... }`, added for the same reason in an earlier session) — `#cal-hist-modal` was the one dialog that hadn't been added to that exclusion list.

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.css
- **FIX:** `#cal-hist-modal table { min-width: unset !important; width: 100% !important; }` added directly below the existing `#rightpanel table` exclusion in the `max-width: 900px` block, so the calendar history table sizes to its own modal instead of inheriting the FX-table's 480px floor.
- Cache-buster bumped: `assets/dashboard.css?v=8.23.10` → `?v=8.23.11`.

### Frontend — assets/calendar-panel.js (v1.19.3 → v1.19.4)
- **HARDENING (defense in depth, independent of the dashboard.css fix):** `#cal-hist-modal .ch-body { overflow-x:auto }` and `#cal-hist-modal table { min-width:0 }` added to this file's own injected `<style>` block, so the table can never again overflow the dialog silently even if a future unrelated global rule leaks in the same way — this file no longer depends on dashboard.css getting the scoping right.
- **IMPROVEMENT — small-phone tier (`max-width: 480px`):** overlay padding 16px→8px (more usable width on narrow phones); table cell padding/font trimmed a notch (`3px 3px` / `9px`) so all four columns (Date/Actual/Forecast/Previous) sit comfortably without wrapping; `max-height` now prefers `92dvh` (falls back to `92vh`) so the modal sizes against the real visible viewport rather than the layout viewport some mobile browsers report before the address bar collapses/expands.
- Verified: `node --check` passes. `dashboard.test.js` was not present in this session's zip export, so the 90/90 suite could not be re-run this session — worth confirming it's still green next session before further calendar-panel.js changes.

### Frontend — index.html
- Cache-busters bumped: `assets/dashboard.css?v=8.23.10` → `?v=8.23.11`; `assets/calendar-panel.js?v=1.19.2` → `?v=1.19.4` (index.html had fallen behind the file's own `v1.19.3` header from the previous session — synced while here).

### Frontend — sw.js
- `CACHE_VERSION` bumped `gi-v8.104.11` → `gi-v8.114.0` (had also fallen well behind the site version — this forces every client to discard its stale precache rather than continue serving old `dashboard.css`/`calendar-panel.js`).
- Precache list entries corrected to match: `assets/dashboard.css?v=8.23.11`, `assets/calendar-panel.js?v=1.19.4` (was still listing `v=1.12.0`, five minor versions stale).

### Not changed
- `#cal-hist-modal` table row content (the CHF Consumer Confidence duplicate-date row, flagged in the v1.19.3 entry) — left as-is; that's a documented, deliberate "show the raw source data" decision, not part of this mobile-layout fix.
- No other `table` consumers were audited for the same `min-width:480px` leak in this session — `#rightpanel` and `#cal-hist-modal` are the two known exclusions; a fuller audit of every dialog/table on the site is worth doing separately if more of these turn up.

## v8.109.0 (2026-08-08) — Economic Calendar sandbox: impact filter, week navigation, FOMC voter tag, historical drill-down modal

### Context
Follow-up to v8.108.0. Santiago asked to implement all viable items from the v8.108.0 idea list ("industry-standard" pass), directing anything too cramped for per-row space into a new click-through modal instead of another inline badge.

### Frontend (sandbox) — assets/calendar-panel-test.js (v1.15-TEST → v1.16-TEST), index-test.html
- **NEW — High-impact-only filter:** second, independent toggle (`#cal-impact-filter` / `passesImpactFilter()`) alongside the existing currency isolate, narrowing the already G8+medium/high-filtered dataset down to just high-impact events. Persisted via `localStorage` the same way as the currency filter.
- **NEW — Week navigation:** Prev/This week/Next controls (`#cal-week-nav`, `_calWeekOffsetDays`) shift the whole -3d/+14d display window by ±7 days per click. Not persisted — resets to the real current window on reload, matching how a Bloomberg/Refinitiv calendar pages without "remembering" position. The live-countdown highlight and the empty-window ForexFactory-outage fallback are now scoped to only apply at offset 0 — neither is meaningful once paged into a different week.
- **NEW — Full-year series index:** `fetchEconomicCalendar()` now also feeds the already-fetched `calendar.json` payload (previously used only for its ≤2-past-day truncation-guard backfill) into `_lastFullHistory` / `_seriesIndex` (`buildSeriesIndex()`), keyed by `currency/canonicalized-title`. Independent of `ff_calendar.json`'s ~21-day window used for the main row list — needed by the two features below, which require up to a year of prior prints.
- **NEW — Cadence tag:** "Weekly"/"Monthly"/"Quarterly"/etc., inferred from the actual variance between a series' own past release-date gaps (`inferCadence()`) rather than a maintained keyword list, per this codebase's already-documented keyword-list drift risk. Needs ≥3 prior releases and low gap variance, otherwise shows nothing rather than guessing.
- **NEW — FOMC voting-member tag:** small "V" (voting, green) / "nv" (non-voting, muted) superscript next to Fed speaker names only (`_fomcVoterTag()`, `FOMC_VOTERS_2026`). Scoped to the Fed because it's the only G10 central bank in this calendar with a structural voting/non-voting split (7 Governors + NY Fed always vote; 4 of 11 other regional presidents rotate onto a vote each year) — the ECB, BoE, BoC, RBA, SNB, RBNZ, Norges Bank and Riksbank all vote as a full body every meeting, so no tag is shown for those speakers. Dated snapshot sourced from federalreserve.gov (page's own "Last Update: July 29, 2026"); documented inline with a re-verify-every-January note since the rotation changes annually.

## v8.106.0 (2026-08-08) — Economic Calendar currency-filter sandbox (round 3) + production display-restoration bug fix

### Context
Continuing the sandboxed Economic Calendar enhancements (`calendar-panel-test.js` / `index-test.html` / `inline-index-styles.css` — none of this section shipped to production `calendar-panel.js`/`index.html` yet), Santiago caught a real misalignment in the v1.13.2-TEST screenshot: Actual/Forecast/Previous no longer sat directly above their own data columns once the currency-filter button group was added to the header. Separately, he asked that a bug found while building this feature — clobbered `display:grid` on `#cal-static-col-header` — be back-ported into production `calendar-panel.js` now rather than waiting for the sandbox feature itself to ship, since it's an isolated, already-verified one-line fix unrelated to the unreleased filter work.

### Frontend (sandbox) — index-test.html, assets/calendar-panel-test.js
- **Header column-order fix (v1.13.3-TEST):** `index-test.html`'s `#cal-static-col-header` grid-template-columns changed from `52px 52px 18px 1fr 58px 58px 58px auto` to `52px 52px 18px 1fr auto 58px 58px 58px` — the currency-filter button group's `auto` track now sits between Event and Actual instead of after Previous. Root cause of the misalignment: grid tracks are per-row, and the data rows below (`.cal-event-row`, unchanged, still the original 7-column grid) have no button track to subtract from their own 1fr — so the header's Event track was computing a different width than the data rows' Event track, shifting the header's fixed 58px Actual/Forecast/Previous columns left by the button group's width relative to the data underneath. Fixed-width tracks are pixel-locked to the right edge regardless of where 1fr lands, so moving the button track to sit before them (not after) restores alignment.
- **`buildPanel()`'s relocation logic updated to match:** when moving `#cal-ccy-filter` back from `#cal-panel-head-actions` (wide-fullscreen split mode) into `#cal-static-col-header`, it now `insertBefore()`s at the Actual span's position (index 4) instead of `appendChild()`-ing at the end, keeping the same column order the static markup already has.
- Verified with a jsdom + local static-server smoke test (docked / narrow-fullscreen / wide-fullscreen-split / isolate-filter-collapsing-to-one-column, all re-checked) and Chromium (Playwright) screenshots confirming Actual/Forecast/Previous now sit directly above their data columns in all three layout states, with the filter still relocating correctly and no duplicate `#cal-ccy-filter` ids.

### Frontend — assets/calendar-panel.js (v1.12 → v1.12.1)
- **BUG FIX — `#cal-static-col-header` display-restoration:** `staticHdr.style.display = splitCols ? 'none' : ''` cleared the inline `display` longhand instead of restoring it. This element has no stylesheet rule of its own — only the one-time inline `display:grid` written in `index.html`'s raw markup — so once JS ran this line (on the very first `buildPanel()` after each page load), the property fell through to the `<div>` UA default (`block`), silently degrading the docked/narrow-fullscreen column header from a grid to plain inline text flow, permanently, for the rest of that page session. Changed to explicitly restore `'grid'` instead of clearing to `''`. Isolated one-line fix — no other logic touched.
- Found while building the sandboxed currency-filter header enhancement above (adding an 8th grid column made the pre-existing bug immediately obvious; on the narrow 180px docked panel with only 7 short text labels, degraded block-flow and an intact narrow grid look similar enough at a glance that it had gone unnoticed).
- Verified: `node --check assets/calendar-panel.js` clean, `node --check assets/dashboard.js` clean, `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 90/90 passed (no dashboard.test.js coverage of calendar-panel.js directly; the fix itself was confirmed via the same jsdom smoke test used for the sandbox files, since the two files share the identical logic on this line).

### Not changed
- `calendar-data/ff_calendar.json`, `fetch_ff_calendar.py` — no data/pipeline changes.
- Production `index.html` / `calendar-panel.js` currency-filter, revision-marker, and surprise-magnitude-tiering features — still sandboxed only, not shipped. This session's production change is limited to the single `display` line above.

## v8.105.0 (2026-08-07) — Saxo ATM IV term structure + Barchart consolidation; removes live per-5-min Barchart scrape

### Context
Following up on the Saxo OTC options-data work earlier this session: rather than a new standalone low-frequency script/workflow, Santiago asked to extend the existing `fetch_saxo_rr.py` (which already renders Saxo's `otc.html` once/weekday via Playwright, but only parsed the RR table, leaving the ATM VOLATILITIES table on the same page unused). Santiago asked that any pair sourced from Barchart move into the new low-frequency script specifically to eliminate that exposure, not just the new nzdusd addition.

### Engine — scripts/fetch_saxo_rr.py (v2.1 → v2.2)
- **Added `find_atm_table()` / `parse_atm_table()`** — parses the ATM VOLATILITIES table (first table on the page; RR is the second) using the same dual-column-layout detection already proven for the RR table. Zero additional requests to Saxo — same Playwright render as before.

Written via `write_iv()`, with independent preserve-on-failure per block (a Barchart outage doesn't block writing fresh Saxo data and vice versa) — see the function's own docstring.
- **Verified offline** against a synthetic fixture reproducing Saxo's real column layout (both ATM and RR tables, standard + cross-pair rows) — `find_atm_table()`'s heading-text match correctly picks table 1 while `find_rr_table()` picks table 2 from the same page; parsed values match the live screenshot Santiago provided exactly (EURUSD 1M ATM = 5.0%, EURGBP 1M ATM = 3.18%). Not yet verified against the real live HTML this session (no fresh `otc.html` sample was uploaded) — recommend a `workflow_dispatch` run and an Actions-log check before relying on it in production.

### Engine — .github/workflows/update-saxo-rr.yml
- **Schedule moved 08:30 UTC → 13:00 UTC** (`30 8 * * 1-5` → `0 13 * * 1-5`). Santiago noticed Saxo's own page footer ("Change from ... 12:30 to ... 12:30 UTC") implies a once-daily refresh around 12:30 UTC — the old 08:30 UTC run was capturing the *previous* day's snapshot every time. Inferred from a single observed page load, not confirmed across multiple days; documented as an assumption in the workflow file, re-verify if the refresh time turns out to drift.

- **Removed the live Barchart scrape entirely** — `_barchart_aggregate_iv()` and `_BARCHART_CME_SYMBOL` deleted from this file. This is a full removal, not a second parallel fetcher on a different schedule — `fetch_saxo_rr.py` is now the sole fetcher/writer of Barchart-derived IV, per the single-writer-per-field discipline already established elsewhere in this repo (see the `inflationExpectations`/`bond2y` incidents in GUIDELINES.md).

## scripts: fetch_ohlc.py v1.10 → v1.11 (2026-08-07) — Silver routed to CME 1H session aggregation (was on the native-1D path with the pre-fix Gold bug)

### Context
Santiago compared the live Silver Futures chart against TradingView's SI1! reference and flagged it looked visibly off — shape/timing mismatch versus the reference chart. Investigated the routing logic in `fetch_ohlc.py` before touching anything.

### Root cause
`CME_SYMBOLS = {'gold', 'wti', 'dxy'}` never included `'silver'`. Silver (`SI=F`) fell through to the generic native-1D `yfinance` path used for the 7 true non-FX/non-CME instruments (BTC, ETH, US10Y, SPX, Nasdaq, VIX, and the equity-1H pair). That path uses a UTC-midnight cutoff — exactly the bug documented and fixed for Gold across v7.50.2–v7.50.4 (session-open-date mislabeling, H/L missing the session's first hour, `open ≈ prev_close` artifacts from Yahoo's settlement-tick construction). Silver is CME COMEX metals, same exchange family and **identical session calendar to Gold** (Sun 18:00 ET–Fri 17:00 ET, same 17:00–18:00 ET maintenance break, same genuine electronic session open) — it should have been swept into the Gold fix at the time but wasn't.

### Fix
- **`CME_SYMBOLS`** extended to `{'gold', 'silver', 'wti', 'dxy'}`.
- **`fetch_gold_ohlc_from_1h()` renamed to `fetch_metals_ohlc_from_1h()`** and now serves both Gold and Silver. ## site: dashboard.js/dashboard.css v8.100.0 → v8.100.1 (2026-08-07) — Compact News mode: fix title-wrap gap

### Context
Santiago tested the new Expanded/Compact toggle live and flagged that some news items left a visible gap where the item's line should be, with the headline appearing below it instead — screenshots showed items like the ForexLive Americas market-news-wrap headline rendering as an empty meta-only line followed by the full title on its own line beneath.

### Root cause
The compact-mode CSS (`#section-news.ns-compact .ns-article/.rs-article`) used `display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap` with the meta row and the title `<div>` as two separate flex items. For any headline too long to fit next to the meta row on one line, flexbox wrapped the **entire title element** down to a new flex line rather than wrapping the text within it — meta occupied its own row, the title occupied a second row below, and because row heights varied per item (1 line for short headlines, 2 for long ones), the layout looked like some items had a blank gap followed by a dropped-down headline. This wasn't a rare edge case: any headline too long for the available width (a majority in a 620px-wide panel) triggered it.

### Fix — `assets/dashboard.css`
- `flex-wrap: wrap` → `flex-wrap: nowrap` on the compact-mode article row, with `overflow: hidden`.
- `.ns-art-title`/`.rs-art-title` set to `flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis` — long headlines now truncate with an ellipsis on the same single line as the meta row, instead of wrapping to a second line. Same ellipsis handling added for the `<a>` child (clickable headlines) since an inline anchor doesn't inherit block-level text-overflow from its parent.
- `.ns-art-meta`/`.rs-art-meta` given `flex-shrink: 0` so the meta row (source · time · currency) never gets compressed to make room for the title — only the title truncates.
- Net result: every compact-mode row is now a fixed single line height, regardless of headline length — matches the intended TOP<GO>-style dense scan list.

### Fix — `assets/dashboard.js`
- Added `title` attribute (native browser tooltip, full untruncated headline) to the title element in both `_buildNsItem()` (News/Analysis) and the Research inline article builder — so truncated headlines in compact mode remain fully readable on hover, and screen readers/tooltips still expose the complete text. Harmless no-op visually in Expanded mode.
- `node --check` clean. `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 90 passed, 0 failed (unaffected — CSS layout + a `title` attribute, no logic touched).

### site — `index.html` / `sw.js`
- Cache-bust bumped `dashboard.js?v=8.100.0` → `?v=8.100.1`, `dashboard.css?v=8.23.9` → `?v=8.23.10`. `CACHE_VERSION` bumped `gi-v8.104.10` → `gi-v8.104.11`.

## site: heatmap-modal.js v2.3.3 → v2.3.4 (2026-08-07) — CSI: normalize by actual per-date pair coverage, not a fixed pair count

### Context
Santiago asked whether the EURUSD coverage-gap issue flagged (but deferred) in the v2.3.2 entry could be fixed. Investigated the root cause on the data side first.

### Root cause (data side — not a bug, no fix applied there)
`scripts/fetch_ohlc.py`'s `build_intraday_ohlc()` drops any H1 bar where `open == high == low == close` (line ~1336) — a pre-existing, deliberate data-integrity guard used identically elsewhere in the same file, rejecting degenerate/flat bars that yfinance occasionally returns for a symbol's still-in-progress current hour. `eurusd.json`'s most recent bar being one hour behind the other 31 CSI pairs is this guard correctly doing its job on an occasional flat tick from yfinance for that one symbol — not a pipeline defect, and the next fetch cycle picks it back up. Editing that guard to accept flat bars would violate GUIDELINES.md's no-fabricated/no-degenerate-data rule, so it was left untouched.

### site — `assets/heatmap-modal.js` v2.3.3 → v2.3.4 (CSI coverage-aware normalization)
- **What was actually fixable:** `_loadCSIData()` divided each currency's summed daily log-return by a **fixed** pair count (`pairsForCcy`, e.g. 9 for USD) regardless of how many of those pairs actually had a bar for that specific date. On any date with a legitimately missing pair (the EURUSD case above, or any future occurrence of the same guard on any other symbol), this **systematically understated** — not just added noise to — that currency's return for that one bar: an 8-pair sum divided by 9 undercounts by design, biased toward zero rather than toward the true average.
- **Fix:** track `ccyDailyCov[ccy][date]` (how many pairs actually contributed) alongside the existing `ccyDailyRet[ccy][date]` sum, and normalize by `sum / cov` instead of `sum / pairsForCcy`. This is the unbiased per-pair average estimator — dividing by however many pairs actually reported gives the correct average currency move for that bar instead of diluting it by pairs that didn't report. `cov` is guaranteed ≥1 whenever `sum` is non-null (both are only ever set together in the accumulation loop), so no divide-by-zero risk.
- **Verified a no-op on full-coverage history:** on any date where all of a currency's pairs reported (the overwhelming majority — confirmed against real `ohlc-data/h1/*.json`, e.g. USD 7/7, EUR 4/4 on a date 50 bars before the tail), `cov === pairsForCcy` and the new formula produces a bit-identical result to the old one. The only behavior change is on partial-coverage bars, where it now produces the statistically correct value instead of a biased-toward-zero one. Verified numerically on the real current gap: USD's last H1 bar (8/9 coverage) moves from −0.0004% (old, biased) to −0.0005% (new, correct); EUR's from −0.0105% to −0.0119%.
- `node --check` clean. `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 90 passed, 0 failed (unaffected — isolated to `_loadCSIData()`'s normalization step, not covered by the existing suite; verified manually against real OHLC data as shown above, both for the partial-coverage tail bar and for confirming no change on fully-covered history).

### site — `sw.js`

## site: heatmap-modal.js v2.3.4 → v2.4.0 (2026-08-07) — CSI: single industry-standard range selector, chart-width fitContent() fix

### Context
Santiago pushed back on the two-row Interval+Range control added earlier this session: "Antes era solo el rango... la idea era agregar más rangos a partir de una hora y que solo se eligiera ese rango. No es estándar de industria eso?" Also flagged that chart width doesn't consistently fill the screen across timeframes. Researched before implementing (this is an architecture reversal, not a bug fix) — confirmed against TradingView's own Time-Scale docs: "When users switch a time frame... The chart resolution changes. The bars scale horizontally to cover the entire requested date/time range" — a single range control with auto-resolution underneath, never two independent controls. CSM-specific tools (FXSSI, MarketMilk/DailyFX) follow the same one-control pattern. Presented the finding plus a concrete 7-range proposal via ask_user_input_v0; Santiago confirmed "Apliquemos el estándar de industria."

### site — `assets/heatmap-modal.js` v2.3.4 → v2.4.0

**1. Single range selector, replacing the two-row Interval+Range control:**
- Removed `_CSI_TF_PERIODS`, `_CSI_TF_DEFAULT_DAYS`, `csiSetTf()`, `csiPeriod()`, `_renderCSIPeriodBtns()`, and the `#hm-csi-tf`/`#hm-csi-period`/`.hm-csi-group`/`.hm-csi-sep` markup and CSS added in the v2.3.1–v2.3.3 entries above.
- Added `_CSI_RANGE_CONFIG`: an ordered list of 7 ranges (1D, 1W, 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, All), each mapping to BOTH a lookback (`days`) and an auto-selected OHLC resolution (`tf`), chosen so every range renders a readable bar count (verified against real data): 1D/1W→H1 (~25/~119 bars), 1M→H4 (~137 bars), 3M/6M/1Y→D1 (~66/~131/~262 bars), All→W1 (~155 resampled weekly points over full history).
- New `window.csiSetRange(btn, rangeKey)` replaces the old pair of handlers. Only triggers a real `_loadCSIData()` fetch when the resolution actually changes between two ranges (e.g. 1W→1M changes H1→H4); switching within the same resolution (e.g. 3M↔6M↔1Y, all D1) just re-slices and re-renders already-loaded data — no unnecessary network round-trip.
- `_csiTf`/`_csiPeriodDays` remain as internal derived state (still read by `_csiCutoffDate`, `_renderCSIChart`, `_renderCSIStats`, `_updateCSILiveBar` — none of that logic changed) but are no longer independently user-settable; both are now set as a unit from one `_CSI_RANGE_CONFIG` entry.
- `_renderCSIStats()`'s period-label lookup simplified: it used to search `_CSI_TF_PERIODS[_csiTf]` for a matching `days` value; now `_csiRange` (the range key itself, e.g. `'3M'`) IS the label.

**2. Chart width not filling consistently across ranges (separate bug, same investigation):**
- `_renderCSIChart()` never called `chart.timeScale().fitContent()` after loading series data — confirmed by grep, no occurrences anywhere in the file. Without it, Lightweight Charts uses a fixed default bar-spacing (~6px) rather than stretching the loaded range to fill the container, so a range with few bars (e.g. old "1D" on H1, ~24 bars) left visible empty space instead of spanning the chart's full width, while wider-bar-count ranges filled differently — inconsistent width behavior across timeframes, matching what Santiago described.
- Fix: added `_csiChart.timeScale().fitContent();` right after all 10 currency series get `setData()`. Bar spacing now always scales to fill the available width regardless of how many bars are loaded for the selected range.

**Validation:** `node --check` clean. `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 90 passed, 0 failed (unaffected — this change is DOM/LWC-instance logic, no test harness for it; verified the range→resolution bar-count mapping numerically against real `ohlc-data/*.json` / `ohlc-data/h1/*.json` / `ohlc-data/h4/*.json`, shown above). Grepped the full file for any remaining references to the removed `csiSetTf`/`csiPeriod`/`_renderCSIPeriodBtns`/`_CSI_TF_PERIODS`/`_CSI_TF_DEFAULT_DAYS`/`#hm-csi-tf`/`#hm-csi-period`/`.hm-csi-group`/`.hm-csi-sep` — none found outside an explanatory comment.

## site: heatmap-modal.js v2.3.1 → v2.3.2 (2026-08-07) — CSI lines jumping/converging at the chart's right edge on live updates

### Context
Santiago reported that the CSI chart's lines all converged/dropped together near the most recent bar (see screenshot, H1 TF / 1W period). This was a regression introduced by, and missed in, the same day's earlier v2.3.1 session.

### site — `assets/heatmap-modal.js` v2.3.1 → v2.3.2 (CSI live-update baseline bug)
- **Root cause:** v2.3.1 migrated the CSI period cutoff from a bar-count offset to a real calendar-day cutoff (`_csiCutoffDate()`) in `_renderCSIChart()` and `_renderCSIStats()`, but missed a third place that used the exact same old bar-count pattern: `_updateCSILiveBar()`, the function that pushes a live point onto each already-rendered series on every RT tick (`_hmRefreshIfOpen`, called from `dashboard.js`'s `populateHeatmap()`). It still computed `startIdx = allDates.length - _csiPeriodDays` and rebased the live point against `allDates[startIdx]` — treating `_csiPeriodDays` (a day count, e.g. `7` for H1's "1W" preset) as a bar-index offset, i.e. only 7 *bars* (7 hours on H1) back, instead of 7 *calendar days* (~120 H1 bars) back. Meanwhile every other point already on the chart was rebased by `_renderCSIChart()` against the correct 7-calendar-day-back baseline. Verified numerically: for the real H1 series (last bar 2026-08-07 04:00 UTC), the old code's baseline was 2026-08-06 21:00 UTC (7 bars back) vs. the correct 2026-07-31 04:00 UTC (7 calendar days back) — a ~6.3-day gap in cumulative CSI movement between the baseline the live point used and the baseline every other point on screen used. Since `_updateCSILiveBar()` re-pushes a point for all 10 currencies on every tick, this showed up as every CSI line snapping to a value on a completely different footing at the chart's most recent bar simultaneously — the "lines all converge/drop together at the end" Santiago described.
- **Fix:** `_updateCSILiveBar()` now computes its cutoff with the exact same `_csiCutoffDate(lastDate, _csiPeriodDays)` call `_renderCSIChart()` uses, so the live-updated point stays on the same baseline as the rest of the series regardless of TF or period.
- Also confirmed (not a rendering bug, no fix applied — flagging for Santiago): `_loadCSIData()`'s per-currency normalizer divides by a **fixed** pair count (`pairsForCcy`, e.g. 9 for USD) rather than the **actual number of pairs that reported a bar for that specific date** (`cov`). In the current H1 data, `eurusd.json` is one bar (1 hour) behind the other 31 pairs' files — at the very last unioned date, EUR and USD's coverage is 8/9 instead of 9/9, so that single bar's return is understated for those two currencies by roughly 1/9th of a normal bar's magnitude. Small (~0.01 CSI points) and not the cause of the reported bug, but worth a decision: normalize by actual `cov` instead of fixed `pairsForCcy`, or leave as-is and rely on the next fetch cycle to backfill the missing bar. Deferred pending Santiago's call — this is a data-normalization design choice, not a clear-cut bug.
- `node --check` clean. `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 90 passed, 0 failed (unaffected — this fix is isolated to the RT live-update path, which has no DOM/WebSocket harness in the existing suite). Verified numerically against the real `ohlc-data/h1/*.json` files (see root-cause paragraph above) rather than by running the live chart, since RT ticks aren't reproducible in this environment.

- Cache-bust bumped `assets/heatmap-modal.js?v=2.3.1` → `?v=2.3.2`.

## site: heatmap-modal.js v2.3.0 → v2.3.1 + dashboard.js (2026-08-07) — CSI TF/period control bar fixes: single row, uniform sizing, cross-contamination with the main chart's TF selector, and a period-start drift bug on H1/H4/W1

### Context
Santiago reported three follow-up bugs after the previous session's CSI H1/H4/1D/1W timeframe work: (1) the TF row (H1/H4/1D/1W) and the period row (1M/3M/6M/1Y/All) sat stacked on separate lines with visibly different button sizes instead of one row; (2) switching timeframe on the shorter ones was changing the button content/highlight on the longer-timeframe buttons; (3) the chart's start point for short timeframes didn't match the period button actually selected — it would show a span unrelated to what was clicked.

### site — `assets/heatmap-modal.js` v2.3.0 → v2.3.1 (CSI control bar)
- **Bug 1 — stacked rows, mismatched sizes:** `#hm-csi-tf` and `#hm-csi-period` were two separate `display:flex` blocks, and the TF buttons used the main chart's `.lw-tf-btn` class (`font-size:9px`, sans-serif) while the period buttons used `.hm-csi-pbtn` (`font-size:10px`, monospace) — visibly different button chrome stacked on two lines. **Fix:** both rows now live inside a single `#hm-csi-controls` flex container (`flex-wrap:wrap` for narrow viewports) separated by a thin `.hm-csi-sep` divider, and both button groups share one new `.hm-csi-btn` class, so every button in the row renders identically sized.
- **Bug 2 — TF switch corrupting the other row's buttons — root cause:** this was **not** a bug in the CSI code's own state management (`_csiTf`/`_renderCSIPeriodBtns` were already correctly scoped and rebuilt fresh on every switch). The actual cause was a **cross-contamination with the main price chart**: CSI's TF buttons reused the main chart's `.lw-tf-btn` CSS class for free styling, but `dashboard.js`'s TF click handler toggles the `sel` state with an **unscoped** `document.querySelectorAll('.lw-tf-btn')` — matching *every* element with that class in the document, not just the main chart's own row. Once the CSI modal had been built once (it's built lazily on first open and left in the DOM, `display:none`, thereafter — see `buildModal()`'s `if (document.getElementById('hm-bd')) return;` guard), switching the *main chart's* timeframe would silently re-highlight the CSI panel's TF buttons underneath it too, completely out of sync with the CSI panel's actual `_csiTf` variable — which is what Santiago was seeing as "changing the shorter TF changes the longer TF's buttons." **Fix:** CSI's TF buttons no longer use `.lw-tf-btn` at all — they use the new `.hm-csi-btn` class exclusively, so there is no shared class name left for `dashboard.js`'s selector to accidentally match. `csiSetTf()`'s own toggle is scoped to `#hm-csi-tf .hm-csi-btn`.
- **Bug 2 defense-in-depth — `assets/dashboard.js`:** also scoped the main chart's own TF-button selector from `document.querySelectorAll('.lw-tf-btn')` to `document.querySelectorAll('#lw-range-bar .lw-tf-btn')`, so this class of bug can't recur even if a future panel reuses `.lw-tf-btn` for its own styling.
- **Bug 2 side-effect fix:** since the TF row and period row now share one `.hm-csi-btn` class, `csiPeriod()`'s own "on" toggle had to be scoped to `#hm-csi-period .hm-csi-btn` (was `document.querySelectorAll('.hm-csi-pbtn')`) — otherwise clicking a period button would also strip the `on` highlight off the currently-selected TF button, since they're now the same class.
- **Bug 3 — start point ignoring the selected period — root cause:** the period presets (`_CSI_TF_PERIODS`) were a fixed **bar count** (e.g. H1 "1W" = 85 bars), derived from an assumed bars-per-calendar-day ratio (17/day for H1, 4.25/day for H4 — the same ratio `dashboard.js`'s `_lwSetRange` uses for the main chart). That ratio is a reasonable *approximation* for the main chart, because `_lwSetRange` only ever scrolls the viewport (`setVisibleLogicalRange`) over one already-fully-loaded instrument's own bar sequence — being a little off just means a slightly-off zoom level, not wrong data. The CSI series is architecturally different: `_loadCSIData()` builds it from the **union of bar timestamps across all 32 pairs**, and — critically — FX trading has a real ~48h weekly gap (closed weekends), so the *actual* bar density in the last N bars varies depending on whether that trailing window happens to straddle a weekend or not. Verified numerically against the real `ohlc-data/h1/*.json` / `h4/*.json` files: the old H1 "1W" preset (n=85) rendered only a **3.5-calendar-day** window, not 7 — the bar-count assumption silently drifted depending on exactly when the chart was opened, which is what Santiago was seeing as "the start point isn't the one I chose."
- **Fix:** period presets are now literal **calendar days**, resolved via a new `_csiCutoffDate(lastDate, days)` helper that does real date-math from the series' own last date (`lastDate - days*86400` for H1/H4's unix-second timestamps, `Date.setUTCDate()` arithmetic for D1/W1's `'YYYY-MM-DD'` strings) — the same range-selection model Bloomberg/TradingView use, and exact regardless of local bar density or weekend placement. Verified against the real data files: H1 "1W" (now `days:7`) renders exactly a 7.00-calendar-day window every time; same exactness confirmed for all H1/H4/D1 presets (1D/1W/2W/1M/3M/6M/1Y).
- `_CSI_TF_PERIODS` values renamed `n` → `days` throughout (button data attributes, `_renderCSIPeriodBtns`, the `_periodPreset` lookup in `_renderCSIStats`); `_CSI_TF_DEFAULT_N` renamed `_CSI_TF_DEFAULT_DAYS` with new day-based defaults (H1:7, H4:30, D1:91, W1:365). `_csiPeriodDays`'s own doc-comment, previously "not literal calendar days (name kept for backward compat)", is now accurate — it *is* literal calendar days.

## site: dashboard.js (Fibonacci Retracement 0%/100% inverted) + heatmap-modal.js v2.2.4 → v2.3.0 (2026-08-07) — Fib Retracement had 61.8%/78.6% at the wrong end of the swing; added H1/H4/1D/1W timeframes to the CSI chart

### Context
Two requests from Santiago after reviewing the live chart: (1) a screenshot of a USD/CHF H4 Fibonacci Retracement showed 61.8%/78.6% sitting near the TOP of an up-swing instead of near the bottom, where the "golden pocket" is expected; (2) could the CSI panel (currently daily-only) get H1/H4/1D/1W timeframes, matching the main chart's own TF selector.

### site — `assets/dashboard.js` (Fibonacci Retracement fix)
- **Root cause:** the `fib`/`fibext` render and hit-test code anchored 0% at the point the user dragged FROM and 100% at the point dragged TO. Verified against TradingView's documented behavior (and MT5's convention it's meant to mirror): it's the opposite — dragging from the swing low to the swing high, 0% lands at the high (the point dragged TO, the most recent extreme) and 100% at the low (dragged FROM). The previous formula had this backwards, which is what put 61.8%/78.6% near the top of an up-swing instead of the bottom.
- **Fix:** for `type === 'fib'` only, level price is now `p2.price + lv * (p1.price - p2.price)` (0%→p2/dragged-TO, 100%→p1/dragged-FROM), applied identically in both `_svgForDrawing` (render) and `_hitTestDrawing` (click/select), so a level line stays clickable after the fix.
- **`fibext` (Fibonacci Extension) deliberately left unchanged** — it's a distinct convention (0% at the FROM point, 100% at the TO point, continuation targets beyond 100% projecting further outward past the TO point in the swing's direction). Flipping it to the retracement convention would have sent extension targets backward past the FROM point instead of forward — not what an extension tool is for.
- Verified numerically against Santiago's screenshot values (USD/CHF H4, swing low 0.80351 → swing high 0.82062): with the fix, 61.8% now falls at 0.81005 and 78.6% at 0.80717, both below the 50% midpoint — i.e. near the bottom of the swing, as expected.
- `node --check` clean; `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 90 passed, 0 failed (test suite doesn't cover the SVG drawing layer, which has no DOM/canvas harness in this repo — verification here was manual numeric substitution against the real screenshot values, documented above).

### site — `assets/heatmap-modal.js` v2.2.4 → v2.3.0 (CSI timeframe selector)
- **New H1 / H4 / 1D / 1W timeframe buttons** on the CSI tab, styled with the same `.lw-tf-btn`/`.sel` classes the main chart's own TF selector already uses (no new CSS).
- **H1/H4** reuse the exact intraday OHLC files the main price chart already fetches for those timeframes (`ohlc-data/h1/{pair}.json`, `ohlc-data/h4/{pair}.json` — unix-second bar times) — no new data pipeline needed. All 32 CSI `PAIR_DEFS` pairs confirmed present in both directories.
- **1W has no separate source file.** `_resampleCSIWeekly()` downsamples the daily cumulative series to one point per ISO week (keyed by that week's Monday, keeping the week's last daily value). This is mathematically exact, not an approximation: the CSI series is a running sum of daily log-returns, and a sum telescopes — the cumulative value on a week's last day already equals the sum of every return up to and including that week, identical to what you'd get computing returns from weekly closes directly.
- **New `_CSI_TF_PERIODS`** — each TF gets its own period-button preset set (bar-count based, not calendar days, since the CSI chart is a cumulative line series, not candles), derived from the same bars-per-calendar-day ratios (`H1≈17/day`, `H4≈4.25/day`, `W1=1/7 days`) `dashboard.js`'s own TF range-button system already uses, so "1W", "1M", etc. mean the same thing here as they do on the main chart.
- **`_loadCSIData(tf)`** now branches its fetch base path by TF and sorts dates with an explicit comparator (`a<b?-1:a>b?1:0`) instead of the default `.sort()`, which stringifies — coincidentally correct for same-length unix-second numbers but not guaranteed, so this is now correct by construction for both the D1/W1 string dates and the H1/H4 numeric ones.
- **`_computeCSILiveView()` scope boundary:** the live in-progress-session point (STOOQ_RT_CACHE-based, 21:00-UTC daily-session-boundary rule) is skipped for any TF other than D1 — it has no equivalent for intraday bars or the resampled weekly series. H1/H4/W1 still show fully current data as of the last completed bar; they just don't get the extra "session still open" point D1 gets. A live intraday point would need its own resolution-aware boundary logic — flagged as a possible follow-up, not attempted here.
- **Tooltip fix:** the crosshair tooltip previously concatenated `param.time` directly into the DOM, which would have rendered a raw unix-second number (e.g. `1786068000`) for H1/H4 points. New `_csiFormatTooltipTime()` handles the number case (→ `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC`) and the BusinessDay-object case some LWC versions return for whole-date strings, falling back to the original string behavior for anything else — no change for existing D1/W1 output.
- Chart's `timeScale.timeVisible` now turns on for H1/H4 only, so intraday points show hour granularity on the axis instead of repeating the same date label across several bars.
- Period-label logic in `_renderCSIStats` (was a hardcoded `21/63/126/252` ternary chain) and the stats-panel footer text ("Daily OHLC history…") are now both driven off `_CSI_TF_PERIODS`/`_CSI_TF_TITLE` so they stay correct across all four TFs instead of only ever saying "Daily".
- Isolated Node test of the new `_resampleCSIWeekly` logic and the sort comparator (8 cases: week-boundary keying, weekday-only-week edge case, string-date sort, numeric-unix-second sort) — 8/8 passed. No existing automated test harness covers `heatmap-modal.js` (only `dashboard.test.js` exists, unaffected by this change; 90/90 still passing).
- `node --check` clean on `heatmap-modal.js`.

### site — `index.html`
- Cache-bust bumped `assets/dashboard.js?v=8.99.3` → `?v=8.99.4`, `assets/heatmap-modal.js?v=2.2.4` → `?v=2.3.0`.

- No live/in-progress-session point for H1/H4/W1 CSI views (see `_computeCSILiveView` note above) — daily-only feature for now.

### Context
Santiago's screenshots (post v1.11 restore, calendar showing history again) showed Canada/US/Australia Balance of Trade and US Imports/Exports rendering with no green/red on the Actual column, despite clear beats/misses (e.g. Canada Balance of Trade C$3.86B actual vs C$3.0B forecast — should be green, rendered plain). Asked whether it could also be affecting the ESI.

### Root cause
`buildPanel()`'s local `stripNum(s)` only stripped `%`, commas, `K`/`M`/`B`/`T` suffix letters, and whitespace — it left leading currency symbols (`$`, `C$`, `A$`, `€`, `¥`, etc.) untouched. `parseFloat("C$3.86B")` → after strip: `"C$3.86"` → `parseFloat` returns `NaN` immediately because the string doesn't start with a digit/sign. The `!isNaN(actualN) && !isNaN(forecastN)` guard then failed silently (no thrown error, no console warning) and `cls` stayed `''` — every Trade Balance / Imports / Exports / Current Account row lost its coloring, for every currency, every time.

**Confirmed the ESI is unaffected.** `dashboard.js`'s `_parseNum()` and `fetch_economic_calendar.py`'s `_parse_num()` — the actual ESI scorers — already carry a documented fix for this exact bug class (strip-to-digits-and-restore-sign, not pattern-exclude-known-suffixes), and `econ-surprises-modal.js` uses the same correct pattern. `calendar-panel.js`'s `stripNum` was a separate, cruder, display-only implementation that never received the same fix — this was purely cosmetic, isolated to this one panel's Actual-column color.

### site — `assets/calendar-panel.js` (v1.11 → v1.12)
- **New module-scope `_calParseNum()`**: ports the exact strip-to-digits/restore-sign strategy already proven in `dashboard.js`/`fetch_economic_calendar.py`. Replaces the old `stripNum`+`parseFloat` pair at the Actual-coloring call site.
- Verified against the failing cases from Santiago's screenshots: `C$3.86B → 3.86`, `$-73.3B → -73.3`, `A$1.929B → 1.929`, `A$-1.1B → -1.1`, `€17.4B → 17.4` — all now parse correctly, alongside the previously-working `15.0K → 15`, `0.4% → 0.4`.
- `node --check` clean; `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 90 passed, 0 failed.

### site — `index.html`
- Cache-bust bumped `assets/calendar-panel.js?v=1.11.0` → `?v=1.12.0`.

### site — `sw.js`
- `CACHE_VERSION` bumped `gi-v8.104.2` → `gi-v8.104.3`.

## site: calendar-panel.js v1.10 → v1.11 (2026-08-07) — Duplicate GMT label + calendar still missing historical events after the v5.27/v1.10 fixes

### Context
Santiago reported two things after the v5.27/v1.10 fixes landed: (1) "GMT-3" appeared twice on the panel — once at the end of the subtitle, once again in the column-header row directly below — and (2) previous days' events were still not showing, and asked whether it was a watcher problem.

It was not a watcher problem — the watcher fix (v5.27) and the label fix (v1.10) were both correct, but two more things had gone wrong on top of them:

1. **`fetchEconomicCalendar()`'s fallback never actually falls back.** It loops `[ff_calendar.json, calendar.json]` and takes the first file with `events.length > 0`, then `break`s. ff_calendar.json was still sitting in its truncated (single-day, 24-event) post-incident state — non-empty, so it always won the race, and calendar.json's full history was never reached. This bug has existed since the fallback was written; the 2026-08-06/07 incident just exposed it for the first time.
2. **Data itself was in the wrong file.** Tracing the real commit history (`git log -p` equivalent via the GitHub API) showed that the 272-event restore snapshot built in the prior session — meant for `calendar-data/ff_calendar.json` — was instead committed to `calendar-data/calendar.json` (commit `c2318cb6`, "Update calendar.json", direct GitHub-UI edit). That commit landed **after** and clobbered a good, complete `fetch_ff_calendar.py`/`fetch_economic_calendar.py` pipeline run (commit `79bca176`, 00:56 UTC) that had already regenerated `calendar.json` correctly — 3,698 events, full 2025-08-07→2026-08-07 range, 265-series `surpriseStats`. That pipeline-generated calendar.json is the file the ESI panel and modal depend on for beat/miss z-scores (`n≥5` history per series); the 272-event overwrite would have silently starved those calculations of a year of history down to 17 days, on top of the calendar panel showing only today.

### site — `assets/calendar-panel.js` (v1.10 → v1.11)
- **Duplicate timezone label removed**: the subtitle no longer appends `tzLabel()` — the column-header time cell (`#cal-th-time`) already shows it directly above the time values it labels, which is the correct single place for it (Bloomberg/Refinitiv convention: label the column, not the panel twice).
- **Coverage-guarded fallback**: `fetchEconomicCalendar()` now fetches `ff_calendar.json` and `calendar.json` in parallel rather than racing a first-match loop. If `ff_calendar.json`'s events don't reach back at least 2 distinct days before today, it's treated as truncated and `calendar.json`'s older events are merged in (deduped by `currency|dateISO|timeUTC|title`) instead of being dropped. This is a defense-in-depth fix, independent of the data restore below — it means a future truncation of ff_calendar.json degrades gracefully instead of silently hiding history again.
- **Event field normalization**: calendar.json's native schema (from `fetch_economic_calendar.py`) uses `.event`, not `.title`. The dedup filters already guarded against this (`ev.title || ev.event`) but `buildPanel()`'s row renderer read `ev.title` unguarded — a calendar.json fallback would have rendered blank event names even with the coverage-guard fix. Events are now normalized once at fetch time so every downstream consumer can rely on `.title` always being set.
- `node --check` clean.

### site — `index.html`
- Cache-bust bumped `assets/calendar-panel.js?v=1.10.0` → `?v=1.11.0`.

### site — `sw.js`
- `CACHE_VERSION` bumped `gi-v8.104.1` → `gi-v8.104.2`.
- `STATIC_PRECACHE` entry for `calendar-panel.js` was still pinned at the stale `?v=1.9.0` (missed in both the v1.9 and v1.10 bumps) — corrected to `?v=1.11.0`.

### Immediate data fix (not a code change) — `calendar-data/ff_calendar.json` and `calendar-data/calendar.json`
- **`calendar-data/calendar.json`**: restored to the good pipeline-generated snapshot from commit `79bca176` (3,698 events, 2025-08-07→2026-08-07, 265-series `surpriseStats`) — recovered from GitHub commit history, since the live copy had been overwritten by the misfiled restore.
- **`calendar-data/ff_calendar.json`**: populated with the 272-event/17-day restore snapshot that was previously misfiled into calendar.json (same content, correct destination this time), with `source` updated to describe the recovery so this doesn't get mistaken for a normal pipeline run's output later.
- Both changes fetched/regenerated locally and validated (event counts, date ranges, schema) before writing — not a blind re-upload.
- The next scheduled `update-ff-calendar.yml`/`update-economic-calendar.yml` Actions runs will continue populating both files normally from here; this restore only repairs the gap left by the incident.

### Verification
- `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 90 passed, 0 failed.

## scripts: calendar-watcher.js v5.26 → v5.27 (2026-08-07) — Direct-commit fallback was overwriting ff_calendar.json's history on every run

### Context
Santiago reported the economic calendar panel had stopped showing previous days' events for the first time, and asked whether it was connected to the 2026-08-06 GitHub Actions/Pages incident. It was: `calendar-data/ff_calendar.json` (fetched from the live repo) showed `generated_at: 2026-08-07T00:46:06Z`, `source: "...CF Worker direct-commit fallback — GitHub Actions unavailable"`, and exactly 24 events — all `dateISO: 2026-08-07`. `calendar-data/calendar.json` (the separate, longer-lived history file) still had the full ~1-year backfill intact, confirming the loss was isolated to `ff_calendar.json` and specifically to the Worker's fallback write.

### Root cause
`commitFallbackToGitHub()` (calendar-watcher.js, added v5.14) fires when `repository_dispatch` didn't get picked up by Actions in time — it commits `calendar-data/ff_calendar.json` directly via the Contents API so the panel doesn't go stale during an Actions outage. It built the file's `events` array from nothing but the current Myfxbook RSS batch (`KV_PAYLOAD`, near-term days only) and wrote that as the **entire** file — no merge with what was already there. `fetch_ff_calendar.py`'s normal path has a Step 2 historical merge for exactly this reason (RSS/FF JSON only cover the current window; the file's ~21-day rolling history is preserved run over run by merging in `prev_events`), but the Worker's fallback path never had an equivalent — it was written as a one-off patch for a missed run, not as a second writer of the same accumulating file. The 2026-08-06 incident triggered enough fallback commits to fully collapse the file down to a single day.

### scripts — `cf-workers-backup/calendar-watcher/calendar-watcher.js` (v5.26 → v5.27)
- **`commitFallbackToGitHub()` now merges instead of overwriting**: decodes the current file's content (already fetched for its `sha`) and ports `fetch_ff_calendar.py`'s Step 2 merge — same key (`currency, dateISO, timeUTC, title`), same ghost-title guard (a same-slot prior title with `actual: null` and no match in the fresh batch is dropped as stale, not carried forward), same 21-day lookback window.
- **New constant `CALENDAR_LOOKBACK_DAYS = 21`**, mirroring `LOOKBACK_DAYS` in `fetch_ff_calendar.py`.
- **Fail loud, not quiet**: if decoding/merging the existing file throws, the fallback now aborts the commit entirely (re-throws) instead of falling through to the old overwrite behavior — a merge failure must never silently reproduce this same truncation bug.
- **Scope check**: audited every other direct-commit path in this file (intraday quotes, FX liquidity, Myfxbook sentiment, Frankfurter) — each of those merges into a keyed object (`existing.quotes[id] = ...`, etc.) rather than replacing an array, so none of them were exposed to this bug. Calendar was the only array-replacing writer.
- `holidays: []` in the fallback payload is unchanged — pre-existing, already-documented limitation (Myfxbook RSS/HTML carry no holiday rows), not part of this fix.
- Merge logic unit-tested in isolation (same-day dedup, cross-day preservation, ghost-title drop, 21-day cutoff drop) — all four cases verified against expected output. `node --check` clean on the full file.
- Version banner bumped in all locations: header comment, root-endpoint JSON `version` field, poll-start log line, and every outgoing `User-Agent` header (v5.26 → v5.27).

### GUIDELINES.md
- **New incident entry** under Data integrity: "Direct-commit fallback writers must merge, not overwrite" — documents the root cause and generalizes the rule to any future Worker fallback writing an accumulating-history file.
- Version footer bumped v8.101.6 → v8.101.7; `calendar-watcher.js` reference updated v5.26 → v5.27.

### Immediate data fix (not a code change)
`calendar-data/ff_calendar.json` on the live site is still in the truncated (single-day) state from before this fix — the code fix prevents recurrence but doesn't retroactively restore what was overwritten. Next scheduled `update-ff-calendar.yml` Actions run will repopulate history via its own Step 2 merge against `calendar-data/calendar.json` and Myfxbook, once Actions is confirmed healthy again.

## scripts: fetch_intraday_quotes.py v3.13 → v3.14 (2026-08-07) — usdcad ATM IV: Yahoo doesn't expose CME futures-options at all; added Barchart aggregate as Source 3.5

### Context
Direct follow-up to v3.13. That fix worked — the near-strike window found a bid where before it would have given up — but usdcad's ATM IV still showed `—`. Different root cause from usdchf: the resolved IV (11.3%) correctly failed the HV-relative gate (3.2x vs. max 2.5x), and Santiago's screenshot of Yahoo's FXC options page confirmed why — every near-ATM strike (calls at 70/71/75/80, puts at 62/66/68) had `bid=0.00`. The gate was doing exactly what it should on a genuinely thin ETF options market.

Santiago then asked whether the PHLX (`^XDC`) or CME (`6C=F`) legs of the cascade had anything left to give. `^XDC` was already tried and already dead (only 1 strike fell inside the 3% tolerance window, no bid). `6C=F` was more interesting: fetching the live Yahoo quote page directly showed no "Options" tab in the nav at all — confirming `6C=F`/`6CU26`/`6CZ26`'s "no options listed"/"no price history" isn't a symbol-format bug, it's Yahoo's `v7/finance/options` endpoint not covering CME futures-options chains, period.

Santiago then linked Barchart's page for the same CME contract (`D6*0` — Barchart's naming for CME 6C front month) and it told a completely different story: **17,417 calls + 6,051 puts open interest**, real premium totals ($149K calls / $226K puts), and a page-level aggregate **Implied Volatility: 4.10%** — 1.17x usdcad's HV30 (3.5%), comfortably inside the plausibility gate. The underlying market was never thin — Yahoo's API just doesn't serve this contract type for any symbol, for any of the 6 CME-backed pairs.

### Root cause
Not a liquidity problem, not a strike-selection problem (both already fixed/ruled out) — a **provider coverage gap**. Yahoo's options endpoint returns empty for CME futures-options regardless of symbol tried; the market itself is real and liquid, confirmed independently via Barchart.

### scripts — `fetch_intraday_quotes.py` (v3.13 → v3.14)
- **New function `_barchart_aggregate_iv(barchart_symbol, label, hv30=None)`**: scrapes Barchart's server-rendered page-level "Implied Volatility: X.XX%" figure via `requests` + regex (`Implied Volatility:.{0,100}?([\d.]+)\s*%`, tolerant of markup between the label and the number without risking a false match elsewhere on the page). Also extracts days-to-expiration/expiry date for logging. Explicitly an aggregate read, not a single-strike ATM lookup — Barchart's per-strike chain table is rendered client-side via JS and isn't reachable by a plain HTTP fetch, only the top-of-page summary figures are server-rendered. Same absolute `[_IV_MIN,_IV_MAX]` and HV-relative `_IV_HV_RATIO_MAX` plausibility gates as every other source apply before returning a result.
- **New dict `_BARCHART_CME_SYMBOL`**: maps pair_id → Barchart root symbol. **Only `usdcad` → `"D6*0"` is populated** — verified live against `barchart.com/futures/quotes/D6*0/options` on 2026-08-07. The other 5 CME-backed pairs (EUR/GBP/JPY/AUD/CHF) likely have equivalent Barchart pages (E6/B6/J6/A6/S6 roots) but are unverified; deliberately not added without checking each one first (see new GUIDELINES.md incident entry — this exact "unverified assumption" mistake is what caused the original problem, in reverse).
- **Cascade updated in `fetch_fx_etf_iv()`**: added as Source 3.5, firing only when Sources 0/0.5/1-3 have all failed AND the pair has a verified `_BARCHART_CME_SYMBOL` entry. Docstring and inline comments updated to note Sources 1/2 (CME via yfinance) are now understood to be structurally dead for all 6 pairs, not just failing intermittently — kept in the cascade as fast-failing candidates rather than removed, in case Yahoo's coverage changes.
- **Verified**: regex tested offline against a reconstructed HTML fragment matching the real page's markup shape (`<strong>4.10%</strong>` style bold-wrapped figures) — correctly extracts `4.1`, passes both plausibility gates against usdcad's real HV30 (3.5%, ratio 1.17x). Live end-to-end fetch not run in this session (this environment's network egress is allowlisted to package registries/GitHub only, no arbitrary web access) — needs confirmation on the next real GitHub Actions run.
- `python3 -m py_compile fetch_intraday_quotes.py` passes.
- Runtime-banner version bumped in both the docstring header and the `main()` print banner (v3.13 → v3.14 in both spots — same recurring checklist item flagged in the v3.13 and earlier entries).

### GUIDELINES.md
- "Estimated data must be labeled" → ATM IV row updated to mention the new Barchart aggregate fallback (usdcad only) and its distinct label format (`"Barchart {symbol} options (aggregate)"`).
- **New incident entry** under Data integrity: "Yahoo's options endpoint does not expose CME futures-options chains — confirm against a second source before concluding 'no market exists'" — documents the root cause, fix pattern, and the deliberately narrow scope (usdcad only, not extended to unverified pairs).
- Version footer bumped v8.101.5 → v8.101.6; `fetch_intraday_quotes.py` reference updated v3.13 → v3.14.

## scripts: fetch_intraday_quotes.py v3.12 → v3.13 (2026-08-06, same-day follow-up) — Root cause found: single-strike ATM selection, not a missing source

### Context
Direct follow-up to the v3.12 entry below. Santiago linked Yahoo's live FXF options page and attached a screenshot instead of running the extended multi-expiry probe that had been proposed. The screenshot alone was enough to find the actual root cause.

### Root cause
Screenshot: FXF spot=108.45, Aug 21 2026 expiry. The **exact-ATM strike, K=108** (|Δ|=0.45, genuinely the closest to spot) has **bid=0.00**, IV=27.10% — a stale-price artifact, correctly rejected by the existing has-bid gate. But **K=110** (|Δ|=1.55, only 1.4% from spot) has a **real bid=0.10**, IV=11.18% — a highly plausible quote (1.7x usdchf's own HV30 of 6.62%, well inside the 2.5x gate, right in line with every other major's IV/HV ratio). `_atm_iv_from_ticker()` computed `atm_strike = min(strikes, key=lambda s: abs(s - spot))` — a single strike, no fallback — and gave up entirely when that one strike had no bid. It never looked at K=110 even though a perfectly good market existed one row away in the exact same chain. This is not a coverage gap (no source exists) or an illiquidity dead-end (nothing trades) — it's a selection bug: real, live, plausible liquidity was sitting in the data the whole time and the code never checked for it.

This reframes the v3.12 conclusion: the "PHLX WCO confirmed illiquid" finding for `^XDS`/`^XDC` (both showed bid=0 at their single nearest strike in the earlier probe) is now suspect for the same reason — those tickers were never checked for a nearby-strike market either, and may well have one.

### scripts — `fetch_intraday_quotes.py` (v3.12 → v3.13)
- **New constants**: `_IV_STRIKE_CANDIDATES = 5`, `_IV_STRIKE_MAX_PCT = 0.03`.
- **`_atm_iv_from_ticker()` rewritten**: instead of a single `min(strikes, key=...)` lookup, sorts all strikes by distance to spot, filters to those within `_IV_STRIKE_MAX_PCT` (3%) of spot, takes the nearest `_IV_STRIKE_CANDIDATES` (5), and tries each — call then put, same has-bid gate as before — in closest-to-spot order until one resolves. The 3% cap exists because moving further from spot picks up real vol skew (OTM/ITM options don't share ATM's implied vol), so a "near-ATM" fallback strike needs a tight leash to stay a legitimate ATM proxy rather than smuggling in skew as if it were the level.
- **Output transparency**: when the resolved strike isn't the true closest one, `source` becomes `"{label} options (near-ATM)"` (was `"{label} options"`), and the console log appends `(near-ATM, X.X% from spot — exact-ATM strike had no bid)`. No schema change — still a plain string, `dashboard.js` only ever displays it as free text in a tooltip (confirmed no substring-matching logic depends on the old exact string).
- **Verified offline** (no network access in this environment) by reconstructing the exact screenshot data (spot=108.45, the 7 visible strikes with their real bid/IV values) as a pandas DataFrame and running it through the new selection logic directly: correctly skips K=108 and K=109 (bid=0), resolves K=110 → IV=11.18%, ratio 1.69x HV30 → passes the plausibility gate cleanly. Matches the manual read of the screenshot exactly.
- Applies to the entire cascade — PHLX (0.5), CME (1-2), ETF (3) all route through this same function — not just FXF/usdchf. Doesn't guarantee usdchf/usdcad resolve on every run (still depends on live liquidity existing *somewhere* near spot), but removes a confirmed false-negative rather than papering over it with a new source.
- `python3 -m py_compile fetch_intraday_quotes.py` passes.
- Fixed the runtime-banner version drift again while bumping (v3.12 → v3.13 in both the docstring header and the `main()` print banner) — same class of oversight flagged in the v3.12 entry and in GUIDELINES.md's 2026-08-02 incident note; will keep needing to check both spots each version bump until/unless the banner is made to read the docstring version programmatically instead of duplicating the literal.

### GUIDELINES.md
- "Estimated data must be labeled" → ATM IV row updated: liquidity gate now described as tried "across up to 5 near-spot strikes within 3% of spot," and the resolved-quote label note (`"... options (near-ATM)"`) added. Removed the now-outdated "CHF/CAD confirmed illiquid" claim from the v3.12 entry — superseded by this fix; whether they resolve is now a live-data question again, not a closed one.
- **New incident entry** under Data integrity: "The exact-ATM strike is not always the most liquid one — try nearby strikes before giving up" — documents the root cause and fix pattern for future option-chain-derived metrics in this project.
- Version footer bumped v8.101.4 → v8.101.5; `fetch_intraday_quotes.py` reference updated v3.12 → v3.13.

## scripts: fetch_intraday_quotes.py v3.11 → v3.12 (2026-08-06, same-day follow-up) — Investigated usdchf/usdcad null ATM IV; PHLX WCO tested and found illiquid, not a fix but a documented, harmless addition

It wasn't confused with anything real: FIX-30/31c (earlier 2026-08-06 sessions) fixed the *quality* of what showed up when the cascade did resolve — rejecting a stale/zero-bid FXF quote at 22.9% (vs. usdchf's own HV30 of 6.62%, a 3.5x ratio) and an FXC quote at 11.0% (vs. usdcad's HV30 of 3.52%, 3.1x) — but never added a source that actually covers these two pairs. AUD and NZD both escaped an equivalent gap earlier by using the Nasdaq PHLX World Currency Options index (`^XDA`, `^XDZ`) instead of the illiquid ETF fallback. Same "technically-live but economically stale/no-market" pattern FIX-30's has-bid gate was built to catch on FXF — not a new failure mode, and the existing gate already handles it correctly.

### scripts — `fetch_intraday_quotes.py` (v3.11 → v3.12)

## engine: calendar-watcher.js v5.25 → v5.26 (2026-08-06, same-day follow-up) — Manual force-trigger route for the Myfxbook Sentiment fallback

### Context
After deploying v5.25 (the credential `.trim()` fix), the natural way to verify it — waiting for the fallback's own gates to let it fire again — wasn't practical: `wrangler tail` from the prior session showed the fallback had *already* committed successfully once at 00:07 UTC (still on v5.23, before the fix existed), which reset `sentiment-data/myfxbook.json`'s staleness clock. With the 2h staleness threshold and a fresh 00:07 commit, the fallback wouldn't naturally re-fire until ~02:07 UTC — too long a wait just to confirm a one-line fix.

Also worth flagging for its own sake: that 00:07 success, on the *unfixed* v5.23 code, is inconsistent with "the credentials always have stray whitespace" — if the whitespace were static and deterministic, every attempt with the same secret value should have failed identically. The intermittent failure pattern (fail at 23:43, 23:52, 23:57, then succeed at 00:07) leaves open a real possibility that the root cause was something transient on Myfxbook's side (e.g. login rate-limiting after repeated failed attempts producing a generic "wrong password" response) rather than — or in addition to — whitespace corruption in the secret. The v5.25 `.trim()` fix stands regardless (it's a correct hardening either way, matching the Python original's tolerance), but it should not be treated as a confirmed root-cause fix until directly re-tested.

### calendar-watcher.js (v5.25 → v5.26)
- **New: `GET /myfxbook-sentiment-direct-commit-force`** — calls `commitMyfxbookSentimentDirectFallback()` directly, bypassing both gates `checkMyfxbookSentimentDirectCommitFallback()` applies on the cron path (30min failure cooldown, 2h staleness vs. real GitHub commit history). Manual-only: the cron tick handler never calls this route, only a human hitting it via `curl` does. Writes the same `KV_MYFXBOOK_SENTIMENT_DIRECT_COMMIT_LAST` bookkeeping the gated path does, so it doesn't desync `/myfxbook-sentiment-direct-commit-status`'s view of the last run. Returns `{"status":"done"}` or `{"status":"failed","error":...}` directly in the HTTP response — no need for `wrangler tail` to see the outcome.
- Added to the root `/` endpoints list.
- `node --check calendar-watcher.js` passes.

## engine: calendar-watcher.js v5.24 → v5.25 (2026-08-06, same-day follow-up) — Fix: Myfxbook Sentiment direct-commit login failing with correct credentials

### Context
Right after deploying v5.24 and setting the two new `MYFXBOOK_EMAIL`/`MYFXBOOK_PASSWORD` Worker secrets (via `wrangler secret put`, interactive stdin prompt on Windows CMD), `wrangler tail` showed the Myfxbook Sentiment Phase 2 direct-commit fallback repeatedly failing: `myfxbook-sentiment direct-commit failed: Myfxbook login failed: Wrong email/password.` — on every tick where it fired (staleness threshold kept re-triggering it since it never succeeded).

### Root cause
`fetch_myfxbook_sentiment.py` (the GitHub Actions script already using the same credentials successfully) reads them as `os.environ.get("MYFXBOOK_EMAIL", "").strip()` / `.strip()` on the password too — Python silently tolerates any stray leading/trailing whitespace in the secret value. `commitMyfxbookSentimentDirectFallback()` in `calendar-watcher.js` read `env.MYFXBOOK_EMAIL`/`env.MYFXBOOK_PASSWORD` raw, with no trim. An interactive terminal prompt (`wrangler secret put`'s `Enter a secret value: ...`) picking up a trailing space or `\r` from how the value was typed/pasted would silently corrupt only the Worker's copy of the credential — invisible in the masked `***` echo, and invisible in `wrangler secret list` (values aren't shown) — producing exactly this symptom: "wrong password" against otherwise-correct credentials that work fine everywhere else.

### calendar-watcher.js (v5.24 → v5.25)
- `commitMyfxbookSentimentDirectFallback()` now does `(env.MYFXBOOK_EMAIL || "").trim()` / `(env.MYFXBOOK_PASSWORD || "").trim()` before the not-set check and before use in the `login.json` call — matches the Python original's tolerance exactly.
- No other call sites reference these two env vars.
- `node --check calendar-watcher.js` passes.

### Verification note
This fix can't be confirmed live from a session transcript alone — it removes a *plausible* whitespace corruption but doesn't rule out a genuine credential mismatch. See the v5.26 entry above for the manual force-trigger route added specifically to test this without waiting out the staleness window.

## engine: calendar-watcher.js v5.23 → v5.24 (2026-08-06, same-day follow-up) — Closes the fx-liquidity outlier-guard gap in the Cloudflare Worker fallback

### Context
Direct follow-up to the `fetch_fx_liquidity.py` v1.1 entry below. That session flagged an explicit "Known gap": `calendar-watcher.js`'s `fetchYahooHourlyHL()` (the fx-liquidity Phase 2 direct-commit fallback) is a faithful JS port of the same `build_hourly_profile()` methodology and has the identical single-sample-per-hour exposure, but couldn't be patched that session because the only copy of `calendar-watcher.js` available was a stale pre-session backup (v5.22) rather than the live deployed v5.23 file. Santiago re-uploaded the live file this session.

### calendar-watcher.js (v5.23 → v5.24)
- **New: `FX_LIQUIDITY_OUTLIER_MULTIPLIER = 6`** and a two-pass rewrite of `fetchYahooHourlyHL()` — pass 1 walks every valid H-L range candle across the full 35d fetch window to compute `refMedian` (JS equivalent of `pair_reference_median()`, same JPY-close normalization, not scoped to `n_days`); pass 2 buckets candles by UTC hour into `p30`/`pToday`, discarding any candle whose range exceeds `refMedian × 6` before it's pushed into either bucket. Logs a `console.warn` with the discard count and ceiling, mirroring the Python `[WARN]` line, so a real recurring glitch stays visible in `wrangler tail` output.
- Behaviour now matches `fetch_fx_liquidity.py` v1.1 exactly: whichever implementation happens to be the one writing `fx-data/fx-liquidity.json` for a given run (GitHub Actions normally; this Worker's Phase 2 direct-commit only when Actions has gone stale) applies the identical protection, closing the "rule added to one implementation doesn't propagate to its sibling" risk this incident originally surfaced.
- Verified with a synthetic reproduction of the same failure mode (20x spike candle at the current UTC hour, `today` slice, single pair) ported to Node: without the guard the spike passes through unchanged; with it, the hour falls back to `0` (which `commitFxLiquidityDirectFallback()`'s existing per-hour handling already treats the same as any other zero — no downstream change needed). Neighboring normal-range hours unaffected. `node --check calendar-watcher.js` passes.
- No output schema change — `direct_commit_partial` and the rest of the payload shape are untouched.
- Version bumped in the header comment, the `version` field in the root JSON response, the startup poll log line, and every `User-Agent` header sent to GitHub's Contents API (15 occurrences) — no other in-code version references were current-version markers (the rest are historical "introduced in v5.23" labels on the two standalone Phase 2 fallbacks added that version, left as-is since those features weren't touched this pass).

### GUIDELINES.md
"Single-sample metrics are vulnerable to source glitches" entry's "Known gap" note updated to "Closed" with a pointer to this entry. Version footer bumped v8.101.1 → v8.101.2 and the `calendar-watcher.js` reference in the footer's version list updated v5.23 → v5.24.

## scripts: fetch_fx_liquidity.py v1.1 (2026-08-06) — Outlier guard: single corrupted yfinance candle was reaching the FX Liquidity Canvas undiluted, wrecking the chart's Y-axis scale

### Context
Santiago flagged the FX Liquidity Canvas rendering as a flat/compressed shape with an abrupt spike near the end of the day, instead of the normal session-by-session wave (Tokyo/London/NY overlaps). Traced to `fx-data/fx-liquidity.json`: the `today` array had one hour (21:00 UTC) at `1018.4`, ~10x every other hour that day and ~10x the `baseline_30d` peak (100.0, by construction).

### Root cause
`dashboard.js`'s `drawLiquidityChart()` scales its Y-axis with `maxV = Math.max(...hours, ...baseline, 10)`. A single absurd value anywhere in `today` forces `maxV` up to that value, compressing the entire rest of the day's real curve toward the floor — visually indistinguishable from a flat line — with a "spike" appearing only where the chart reaches the contaminated hour.

Traced further into `fetch_fx_liquidity.py`: `today`'s per-hour value is a **median across whichever of the 5 pairs have a candle for that hour, computed from a single day of data** (unlike `baseline_30d`, which medians ~30 days per pair and is naturally robust to one bad print). With only 1 pair reporting for hour 21 — common for a still-forming or thin hour — that "median" is just that one pair's raw H-L range for that single candle. A known yfinance intraday-data glitch (a stale/corrupted High or Low print) reaches the output completely undiluted.

### Scripts — `fetch_fx_liquidity.py` (globalinvesting-scripts repo, v1.0 → v1.1)
- **New: `pair_reference_median()`** — computes each pair's own long-run median H-L range across the full 35d fetch window (same JPY-close-normalization as the existing hourly logic), independent of whichever `n_days` slice (`30` for baseline, `1` for today) is being built from it.
- **`build_hourly_profile()` now accepts `ref_median`** — any individual candle whose `hl_range` exceeds `ref_median × OUTLIER_MULTIPLIER` (new constant, `6`) is discarded before the per-hour median is taken, same treatment as a candle with no data (`<= 0`). Logs a `[WARN]` line with the count discarded and the ceiling used, so a real recurring data-quality problem stays visible in workflow run logs rather than silently vanishing.
- `main()` now computes `ref_median` once per pair (from the full 35d `df`, before slicing to `n_days`) and passes it into both the `n_days=30` and `n_days=1` calls for that pair — the reference stays stable and sample-size-independent regardless of which profile is being built, specifically so the low-sample "today" profile (the one that broke) gets the same protection as the well-diluted 30d baseline.
- 6x multiplier chosen as: well above normal session-to-session H-L range variance (London/NY overlap peaks run ~2-3x the quietest Tokyo-only hours in the 30d baseline), well below the magnitude the observed glitch produced (~20x that pair's own median).
- Verified with a synthetic reproduction of the exact failure mode (1 pair, 1 corrupted candle at one hour, ~20x the pair's normal range, no other pair reporting that hour to dilute it): guard discards the candle, hour falls back to `0.0` (which `dashboard.js`'s existing `fetchLiquidityData()` already treats as "no real data for this hour" and substitutes `baseline_30d[h]` — no code change needed there). Confirmed neighboring normal-range hours are untouched by the guard.
- No output schema change — `fx-data/fx-liquidity.json`'s shape (`updated`, `today`, `baseline_30d`, `hours_complete`, `source`, `fallback`) is unchanged, so `dashboard.js` needs no update.

### Known gap — Cloudflare Worker fallback not yet updated
`calendar-watcher.js`'s `fetchYahooHourlyHL()` (the fx-liquidity Phase 2 direct-commit fallback, v5.22) explicitly ports this same `build_hourly_profile()` methodology using Yahoo's chart API in place of yfinance — same 5 pairs, same median-per-hour logic, same failure mode possible (single corrupted candle, low-sample "today" profile, no cross-pair dilution). This session's outlier guard was **not** ported there yet: the copy available in this session's `globalinvesting-scripts` zip (`cf-workers-backup/calendar-watcher/calendar-watcher.js`) is a stale pre-session backup (v5.22), not the actual v5.23 file Santiago deployed live earlier this same session — patching the stale backup would not affect production and would create a second, wrong "current" copy. Needs the live `calendar-watcher.js` re-uploaded to apply the equivalent guard to `fetchYahooHourlyHL()` and keep both implementations consistent, per the exact "a rule added to one implementation doesn't propagate to a sibling implementation automatically" risk already documented in GUIDELINES.md's calendar-panel.js section.

### GUIDELINES.md — new Data integrity rule
Added **"Single-sample metrics are vulnerable to source glitches"** under Data integrity — non-negotiable rules, same style as the existing "Single writer per field" incident entry. Codifies the general pattern (not just this one script): a metric computed as "median across whichever sources reported this period" degrades to "that one source's raw value, no dilution" whenever only one source actually reported, so any such metric needs its own per-source outlier guard rather than relying on cross-source dilution. Flags the still-open `fetchYahooHourlyHL()` gap above as a known exposure under this same rule. Version footer bumped v8.101.0 → v8.101.1 and the stale `calendar-watcher.js v5.13` reference in the footer's version list corrected to `v5.23` (already deployed live this session, footer just hadn't been touched since) while in there.
