## v8.96.0 (2026-08-04) — Fix: CHF bond10y/bond2y — SNB source now has a staleness guard

### Root cause
A live GH Actions run pasted by Santiago showed CHF `bond10y` and `bond2y` both pinned at `2025-07-31` across two consecutive runs — exactly one year stale — with no warning or notice anywhere in the log. `_snb_latest()` (the SNB rendoblid-cube fetcher used as CHF's primary source for both fields) only checked that its query returned a non-empty row after sorting by date; it never checked whether that last row's date was actually recent. This is the identical failure class FIX-26 already fixed for `_ohlc_latest()` in this same file: a feed that keeps echoing (or silently degrades to) the same old observation is read as a fully valid, "fresh" success indefinitely. `fetch_chf()` only range-checks the returned *value* (`-2 < val < 10`), not its date, so the year-old figure kept being written to `CHF.json` every run looking exactly like a live update — no `req_failures`/`opt_failures` entry, no `::warning::`, nothing visibly wrong in the dashboard beyond the number itself being wrong.

### Scripts — `fetch_bond_yields.py` (globalinvesting-scripts repo, v2.9.6 → v2.9.7)
- **`_snb_latest()` staleness guard (FIX-35).** Added a `max_stale_days` parameter (default 7 — a normal weekend plus a one-day CH bank holiday, slightly more slack than FIX-26's 5 for OHLC since SNB publishes once daily rather than intraday). Once the last observation's date exceeds this threshold, the function now logs a `::warning::` and returns `(None, None)` — a miss — instead of returning the stale row as if it were current.
- **Effect on `fetch_chf()` (no changes needed there):** bond10y already has a live fallback (ECB FM `CHF10YT_RR`, monthly) that will now correctly trigger the next time SNB gets stuck, instead of never firing. bond2y has no fallback source (documented as OPTIONAL, unchanged) — a stuck SNB feed will now correctly show up as `CHF.bond2y` in `opt_failures` with a notice, rather than silently repeating an old value forever.
- Version bumped to v2.9.7 in file header, docstring, and `main()`'s startup print.

### Verification
- `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(...)"` clean on the edited file.
- Both `_snb_latest()` call sites (`fetch_chf()`, dims `10J0` and `2J`) confirmed to use the new default `max_stale_days=7` — no call site overrides it.
- **Not yet confirmed against a live GitHub Actions run.** Santiago should check the next `update-bond-yields.yml` run: either SNB itself has recovered and both fields show a genuinely fresh date, or (if SNB is still stuck) bond10y should now visibly fall through to `ECB-FM-CHF-monthly fallback` in the log instead of silently repeating `2025-07-31` a third time, and bond2y should show up in the `opt_failures` / notice output. If bond10y/bond2y still show the exact same stale date with no warning logged after this ships, that means the underlying SNB query itself is returning a *plausible current-looking* date that just isn't updating in value — a different bug — and needs re-diagnosis, not a re-trigger of this same guard.

A live fetch of this ZIP this session succeeded with no challenge. FRED `IRLTST01GBM156N` kept in the bond2y cascade despite being confirmed discontinued — harmless (fails fast) and free insurance if FRED ever republishes a successor series under a new ID.

## v8.93.0 (2026-08-03) — Docs: NZD/NOK bond2y source investigation (Norges Bank 2Y corroborated, NZD alternates ruled out)

### Scripts — `fetch_bond_yields.py` (globalinvesting-scripts repo, v2.9.3 → v2.9.4)
- **Requested by Santiago:** find a way to get NZD and NOK 2Y yield data — indagar a fondo todas las fuentes posibles. Both fields already have live cascades in production (NOK: Norges Bank GOVT_ZEROCOUPON primary / FRED fallback, shipped v2.9.3; NZD: RBNZ B2 xlsx primary / FRED fallback, shipped v2.9). This session's work was source verification and a fresh alternative-source search, not a new implementation.
- **NOK bond2y (DOC-4):** v2.9.3's "2Y" tenor code for the Norges Bank API was an inference, confirmed only for "12M". Corroborated this session via Norges Bank's own public query-builder (`query.norges-bank.no/no/GOVT_ZEROCOUPON`), which lists a live, near-daily "2 år" series (248 observations in its trailing 12-month window) alongside 12 måneder/3 år/…/10 år. This confirms a 2-year point genuinely exists and is actively published — it does not, by itself, prove the API's tenor string is exactly `"2Y"` (a live API pull kept returning only 12M rows this session regardless of the `TENOR` filter used). Left a one-line `curl` command in the code docstring for Santiago to run and settle this outright. No functional code change — the existing fully-defensive fallback already degrades cleanly to FRED if the tenor code is ever wrong.
- **NZD bond2y (DOC-5):** exhaustive fresh search for alternatives to the confirmed-blocked RBNZ B2 xlsx (403 from GitHub Actions IPs, documented since v2.9.2). Checked and ruled out:
  - **data.govt.nz** (NZ government's own open-data catalogue, a different domain from `rbnz.govt.nz`) — its "Wholesale interest rates" dataset resource entries turned out to be plain CKAN links pointing straight back at the same `rbnz.govt.nz/-/media/.../hb2-daily.xlsx` file, not an independent mirror. The catalogue page itself also returned an Incapsula bot-challenge on a routine fetch, so it carries its own block risk on top of not being independent.
  - **DBnomics** — confirmed to mirror RBA (already used for AUD bond2y) but has no RBNZ/NZ government-bond series in its catalogue.
  - **NZ Debt Management / Treasury** (`debtmanagement.treasury.govt.nz`) — publishes primary-issuance data (tenders, syndications, securities on issue) only; no daily secondary-market yield curve.

## v8.91.0 (2026-08-03) — Feat: Fibonacci Extension drawing tool; Fix: RSS popover off-screen on mobile; Fix: "weekend tape" replaced with authentic phrasing in AI narrative prompt

### Site — assets/dashboard.js (Fibonacci Extension)
- **New drawing tool: Fibonacci Extension** (`fibext`), added to the Draw dropdown alongside Trend Line, Fibonacci Retracement, and Rectangle. 2-point tool (drag swing start → swing end), projecting continuation targets beyond the swing at 127.2/161.8/200/261.8% — the standard extension levels quoted in institutional FX research, matching TradingView's "Fib Extension" tool convention.
- Implementation shares all rendering/hit-test/selection/move/resize/copy-paste machinery with the existing `fib` type (both type-branches merged into one `d.type === 'fib' || d.type === 'fibext'` check in `_svgForDrawing` and `_hitTestDrawing`, switching only the level array — `FIB_LEVELS` vs new `FIB_EXT_LEVELS`). No new interaction code needed since the existing p1/p2 drag model already generalizes.
- **Scope note:** this is the 2-point variant. The rigorous "trend-based" 3-point Fibonacci Extension (swing start → swing end → retracement end, matching Bloomberg/MT5's native `Fibonacci Expansion` object) is a materially bigger feature — a third handle, extended selection/resize/serialization across the whole drawing-tools subsystem — and was deliberately not attempted in this pass. Flagged as a candidate for a dedicated session if full parity is wanted.
- New color: teal `rgba(0,191,165,0.9)` for `fibext`, distinct from Retracement's amber, so both tools stay visually distinguishable when overlaid on the same swing.

### Site — assets/feed.js (RSS popover mobile fix)
- **Bug (reported, screenshot-confirmed):** on mobile, the RSS subscribe popover (`rss-popover`) rendered partially off-screen to the left, with the cut-off portion unreachable (no scroll). Root cause: `positionPopover()` computed a `right:` CSS offset purely from `rss-btn`'s position (`window.innerWidth - rect.right`) with no clamp — on mobile the button sits near the left edge of a narrow status bar, so the 260px-wide popover's *left* edge landed off-screen (negative x) with nothing constraining it back into view.
- **Fix:** `positionPopover()` now computes the popover's actual rendered width (mirroring the existing `max-width:calc(100vw - 16px)` CSS rule, computed rather than measured via `offsetWidth` since this function also runs while the popover is still `display:none`, where `offsetWidth` reads 0) and clamps `right` so the popover's left edge never sits closer than 8px to the viewport edge, regardless of where the button is. Desktop behavior is unchanged (the clamp is a no-op when there's ample room).

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py (weekend narrative wording)
- **Editorial fix, reported by Santiago:** the AI-generated weekend narrative repeatedly used the phrase "the weekend tape" — checked against real desk-note usage and found no support for it as institutional phrasing; "tape" specifically denotes the live Time & Sales / ticker-print feed, which by definition doesn't exist while the market the note is describing is closed for the weekend, making the phrase mildly incongruous rather than authentic. The root cause was structural, not a one-off LLM slip: "weekend tape" was hardcoded into `NARRATIVE_SYSTEM_CLOSED`'s few-shot style example and its VERB RULES illustration, so the model reliably reproduced it verbatim nearly every week.
- Replaced both instances with "the weekend headlines" (preserves the exact grammatical role the prompt needs — a noun that can "dominate" without implying an active/live market, satisfying the VERB RULES constraint — while reading as something a real desk note would actually say). Updated the adjacent explanatory code comment for consistency; no functional/regex changes needed since no sanitizer pattern referenced the literal word "tape."

### Verification
- `node --check` clean on `dashboard.js` and `feed.js`.
- `_svgForDrawing`/`_hitTestDrawing` fibext branch verified against the same code path already exercised by `fib` — no new untested logic, just a second entry in an existing generic branch.
- RSS popover clamp math verified with a Node simulation: mobile viewport (390px) + button near left edge → popover left edge clamped to 8px (previously would have gone negative); desktop viewport (1440px) + button near right edge → unchanged from prior behavior.
- `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(...)"` clean on `generate_narrative_signals.py`.
- **Not verified live** — the Fibonacci Extension tool and RSS popover fix need a visual check in a real (ideally mobile) browser session before considering this fully closed; the narrative wording fix will only be visible in the next weekend narrative generation run.

Wired into both `_rba_xlsx_2y_latest()` and `_rbnz_2y_latest()`, replacing their bare `try: import openpyxl / except ImportError: return None, None` guards.

## v8.90.22 (2026-08-02) — Fix: only DE showed a 2Y in Sovereign Spreads — a second, unmerged writer wiped bond10y/bond2y/bond5y for most currencies daily

### Root cause
Santiago reported that the Sovereign 10Y Spreads panel only showed a 2Y yield for DE (EUR); every other country showed "–". Two independent scripts write `extended-data/{CCY}.json`: `fetch_bond_yields.py` (globalinvesting-scripts repo, `update-bond-yields.yml`, daily 23:00 UTC — a real multi-source cascade per currency: FRED daily / ECB SDMX / BOE SDIE / BoC Valet / SNB rendoblid / Treasury XML / FiscalData, confirmed accurate against official sources in the previous audit) and `update_extended_data.py` (this repo, `update-extended-data.yml`, daily **06:00 UTC — seven hours later**). The second script built a brand-new, non-merged dict every run (`all_data = {c: {} for c in CURRENCIES}`) and unconditionally `json.dump()`'d it over the whole file. Its own bond10y/2y/5y fetch logic had no 2Y coverage at all for JPY/AUD/CHF/NZD/NOK/SEK, and an inferior/frequently-broken FRED-monthly fallback for GBP/CAD — so every morning at 06:00 UTC it silently erased whatever correct data `fetch_bond_yields.py` had written the night before, for every currency except EUR (the one case where both scripts' sources happened to be healthy on the same day). Same underlying failure class as the v14.1 `inflationExpectations` incident (documented in `update_extended_data.py`'s own changelog) — that fix was never extended to bond10y/bond2y/bond5y at the time.

### Engine — scripts/update_extended_data.py (v14.2 → v14.3)
- Removed `fetch_bonds()` and all of its exclusive helpers (`BOND_FRED_FALLBACK`, `BOND_PRIMARY_FETCHERS`, `_bond_eur/_gbp/_jpy/_aud/_cad/_chf/_nzd`, `_jgb_auction_from_calendar`) — ~350 lines of now-dead, redundant, and less-capable bond-yield fetching.
- The MAIN section now **preserves** `bond10y` / `bond2y` / `bond5y` (data + dates) by reading the existing `extended-data/{CCY}.json` before writing, exactly mirroring the existing `inflationExpectations` preservation pattern from v14.1 — no more blank-dict overwrite of fields this script doesn't own.
- Simplified the "expected keys" / missing-field warning logic: removed the hardcoded `_BOND2Y_CCYS = {"USD","EUR","GBP","CAD"}` / `_BOND5Y_CCYS = {"USD"}` currency sets, since actual per-currency bond2y/5y coverage is now entirely owned by (and can evolve independently in) `fetch_bond_yields.py` in the other repo — duplicating that coverage list here was itself a source of drift.
- `vix`, `hyOas`, `igOas` fetching (USD-only, genuinely owned by this script) is unaffected.

### Data hygiene note (no functional impact, flagged for cleanup)
While investigating, found a stray, stale copy of `fetch_bond_yields.py` (labeled v2.6 in its own header) committed inside `globalinvesting-scripts/.github/workflows/fetch_bond_yields.py`. Confirmed this is dead weight, not a second execution path: `update-bond-yields.yml` checks out the whole `globalinvesting-scripts` repo into a `private-scripts/` directory and runs `private-scripts/fetch_bond_yields.py`, which resolves to the real root-level script (currently v2.8) — GitHub Actions does not auto-execute `.py` files sitting inside `.github/workflows/`. Recommend Santiago delete `globalinvesting-scripts/.github/workflows/fetch_bond_yields.py` next time he's in that repo, purely to avoid future confusion (e.g. someone editing the wrong copy). Not fixed in this session — no working file was uploaded for it and it carries zero runtime risk as-is.

- Inline harness: simulated `update_extended_data.py`'s new MAIN-section logic against a fixture `extended-data/GBP.json` with `bond2y=5.0051` already on disk — confirmed the field survives a simulated run unchanged (previously it would have been wiped to `null`/absent).

This caused a real support confusion: Santiago's Action logs showed "v2.4"/"v3.6" and reasonably read that as "the FIX-29 files weren't deployed," when in fact the FIX-29 *logic* was running correctly (confirmed by the `prev X% (date)` line appearing in the log output, which only exists in the new code) — only the cosmetic banner string was stale.

- **New rule added to GUIDELINES.md** (see below) to prevent recurrence: any script with both a docstring version header AND a separate runtime print banner must have both bumped together — grep for the old version string as part of every version bump, not just the docstring.

### Confirmed — one-time bond2y_prev race, not a logic bug
In the Action logs Santiago shared, `fetch_bond_yields.py` (07:02 UTC run) correctly computed and wrote `bond2y_prev = 4.22 (2026-07-29)` to `extended-data/USD.json`. `fetch_intraday_quotes.py` ran essentially the same minute (07:02:28Z) and read a copy of `extended-data/USD.json` that did not yet have `bond2y_prev` populated — because this was the very first run of the updated `fetch_bond_yields.py` since FIX-29 was deployed, so no prior run had ever written that field for `fetch_intraday_quotes.py` to pick up. The FIX-29 fallback path in `fetch_intraday_quotes.py` fired exactly as designed: it did not crash and did not fabricate a number, it kept the pre-existing (stale, `^IRX`-derived) `prev_close` — which is why both of Santiago's dashboard screenshots still showed the 2Y's day-over-day change frozen at the old value even though the *level* (4.23%) was already correct. This is expected to self-resolve on the next `fetch_intraday_quotes.py` run once `bond2y_prev` is present in the checked-out repo state — not a logic bug, and no code change made for this specific finding. Flagged for Santiago to re-check the next Action run's log for a `prev X% (2026-07-29)` line (not `n/a`) to confirm.

### GUIDELINES.md
- New rule under versioning conventions: scripts with a docstring version header AND a separate runtime print banner (`fetch_bond_yields.py`, `fetch_intraday_quotes.py` — pattern may exist elsewhere, not yet audited) must have both updated on every version bump. Grep the old version string (not just increment a counter) before considering a version bump complete. Footer bumped to `v8.90.21`.

### Verification
- `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(...)"` clean on both modified files.
- `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 85/85 passed (no frontend logic touched).
- Audit performed via live web search against FRED/FRED-sourced third-party sites, not from training-data memory (dates are after this environment's reliable knowledge cutoff).

## v8.90.20 (2026-08-02) — Fix: US 2Y day-over-day change frozen forever, AND corrected data never actually reached the deployed site

### Context
Two compounding bugs on top of v8.90.19's FIX-28. FIX-28 corrected the *level* (`bond2y`) but not the *change* — `chg`/`prev_close` for `us2y` kept recycling a stale value indefinitely. Separately, even a fully-correct `intraday-data/quotes.json` commit was never actually being published: the workflow that writes it pushes with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which per GitHub's own loop-prevention rule does **not** trigger other `on: push` workflows — so `deploy-pages.yml` silently never fired for it. The dashboard could show the same stale numbers indefinitely regardless of how correct the underlying JSON was.

### Engine — scripts/fetch_bond_yields.py (globalinvesting-scripts repo, v2.7 → v2.8)
- **FIX-29 — `bond2y_prev` now persisted:** added `_fred_csv_rows()` (fetches the full FRED DGS2 CSV series) and `_fred_csv_latest_and_prev()` (returns both the latest and second-to-last observation). The `bond2y` block now writes `data["bond2y_prev"]` / `dates["bond2y_prev"]` to `extended-data/USD.json` alongside `bond2y`, whenever the primary FRED DGS2 path succeeds. The Treasury XML / FiscalData fallback paths do not attempt to populate `bond2y_prev` (no reliable prior-observation semantics from those APIs) — in that case the field simply keeps its last known value rather than being overwritten with something wrong.

### Engine — scripts/fetch_intraday_quotes.py (globalinvesting-scripts repo, v3.7 → v3.8)
- **FIX-29 — stopped recycling `prev_close`/`chg` forever:** PASO 4 (`us2y` replacement) previously did `existing_us2y.get("prev_close", ...)`, i.e. carried forward whatever `prev_close`/`chg` already existed in `quotes.json` — which itself never came from a real 2Y in the first place (it inherited from the `^IRX` 3M proxy fetched in PASO 1-3). Once `bond2y`'s level was corrected by FIX-28, `chg` stayed frozen at the old contaminated value permanently, because nothing ever supplied a new "yesterday." Now reads `bond2y_prev` / `bond2y_prev_date` from `extended-data/USD.json` (written by `fetch_bond_yields.py` FIX-29, same run) and computes `chg = bond2y - bond2y_prev`, `pct` from that pair — both from real numbers, not inherited ones. Falls back to keeping the existing `chg`/`prev_close` (not fabricating one) if `bond2y_prev` isn't present yet, so this doesn't break if the two files are deployed slightly out of order.

### Data — site repo — `.github/workflows/*.yml` (6 files: `forex-news.yml`, `update-ff-calendar.yml`, `update-fx-liquidity.yml`, `update-intraday-quotes.yml`, `update-ohlc.yml`, `update-sitemap.yml`)
- **Root cause confirmed via GitHub Actions run history:** `update-extended-data.yml` (engine repo, cross-repo push via `PAT_TOKEN`) reliably triggers `deploy-pages.yml`. None of the 6 site-repo-native data workflows above ever did — they push to their own repo using the ambient `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and GitHub explicitly does not cascade `on: push` workflow runs from `GITHUB_TOKEN`-authored commits, to prevent infinite trigger loops. This is by design, not a bug in `deploy-pages.yml`'s trigger config.
- **Fix — explicit dispatch instead of relying on the push event:** each workflow's commit/push step now has `id: push` and writes `pushed=true`/`pushed=false` to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` at every one of its existing exit points (no-op/no-changes, successful push, retries exhausted — behavior of the retry loop itself is unchanged). A new final step, `Trigger Pages deploy`, runs `gh workflow run deploy-pages.yml --ref main` (authenticated via the workflow's own `github.token`) conditioned on `steps.push.outputs.pushed == 'true'`, so a deploy is dispatched if and only if that run actually committed new data. Requires `actions: write` added to each workflow's `permissions:` block (already present in `update-ff-calendar.yml` for its existing cross-repo dispatch step; added fresh to the other 5).
- **`update-ff-calendar.yml` specifics:** the new "Trigger Pages deploy" step is additionally gated on `steps.gate.outputs.run == 'true'` (the existing release-window gate), and inserted before the pre-existing "Dispatch cb-rate-decision" step so both post-push actions run independently off the same `steps.push` output.
- **Not changed:** `deploy-pages.yml` itself, and `update-extended-data.yml` (engine repo) — both already work correctly; this fix only closes the gap for the 6 site-native workflows.

### GUIDELINES.md
- New rule under "Data integrity" / workflow section: pushes authored with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` never cascade into other `on: push`-triggered workflows in the same repo — any workflow whose job is to get its own commit published (not just committed) needs an explicit `gh workflow run <target>.yml` dispatch step, gated on whether that run actually pushed. Cross-referenced against the existing `repository_dispatch` / `github.repository` incident note (2026-07-08) — same underlying class of "the push looked successful but nothing downstream happened," different mechanism. Footer bumped to `v8.90.20`.

### Verification
- `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(...)"` clean on both `fetch_bond_yields.py` and `fetch_intraday_quotes.py`.
- All 6 modified workflow YAML files re-parsed clean with `yaml.safe_load`.
- `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 85/85 passed (no frontend logic touched this session, run per standing convention before packaging).
- Inline Python harness confirmed `chg`/`pct` derive from a real `(bond2y, bond2y_prev)` pair rather than a carried-over constant.
- **Not verified live:** the actual GitHub Actions dispatch (`gh workflow run deploy-pages.yml`) — this sandbox has no network access to the GitHub API's `workflow_dispatch` endpoint under Santiago's repo permissions. Watch the Actions tab after the next scheduled run of any of the 6 workflows for a `Trigger Pages deploy` step firing a new `deploy-pages.yml` run.

## v8.90.19 (2026-08-02) — Fix: US 2Y Treasury yield silently equaled the 3M T-Bill yield for ~2 months (ohlc-data/us2y.json mislabeled ^IRX as 2Y)

### Engine — scripts/fetch_ohlc.py (globalinvesting-scripts repo, v1.9 → v1.10)
- **Removed the `"us2y": "^IRX"` ticker mapping entirely.** `^IRX` is the CBOE 13-week T-Bill (3M) index — yfinance/CBOE has no native 2Y Treasury index, so this was never a valid "proxy," despite the inline comment claiming otherwise (added by `FIX-24`, 2026-06-08). Also removed the now-dead `us2y` entries from `DECIMALS`, `GUARDS`, and `NON_FX_SYMBOLS`. Confirmed via grep that `assets/dashboard.js` never reads `ohlc-data/us2y.json` directly — it isn't a chartable symbol in the main terminal (no entry in `_TV_TO_OHLC`/`_OHLC_LABELS`), so removing the file has no frontend impact.

### Engine — scripts/fetch_bond_yields.py (globalinvesting-scripts repo, v2.5 → v2.7)
- **FIX-28 — USD bond2y cascade fixed:** `bond2y` was checking `ohlc-data/us2y.json` first (added as PRIMARY by `FIX-24`). Because that file always returned a fresh value, the correct FRED DGS2 → Treasury XML → FiscalData fallback beneath it never ran — `bond2y` silently mirrored `bond3m` (both ultimately traced back to `^IRX`) on every run since 2026-06-08. Live-verified via web search on 2026-08-02: dashboard showed US 2Y = 3.68% (== 3M) the same week real FRED:DGS2 traded ~4.3–4.4%. New cascade: FRED DGS2 → Treasury XML `BC_2YEAR` → FiscalData API → 14d cache (no OHLC leg). `bond5y` (`^FVX`) is unaffected — that's a genuine CBOE 5-Year Treasury index, correctly labeled.
- **Note:** this file's own changelog jumps v2.5 → v2.7. `CHANGELOG.md`'s previous top entry (v8.90.18) documents a v2.6 (JPY/SEK/NZD bond2y sources) that is **not present** in the copy of `fetch_bond_yields.py` uploaded this session — flagged for Santiago to check whether that work was actually committed.

### Data — site repo
- **Deleted `ohlc-data/us2y.json`** (the mislabeled 3M-as-2Y file) from the public site repo. It will not be regenerated by `fetch_ohlc.py` going forward.
- **Not manually corrected in this session:** `extended-data/USD.json` `bond2y` and `intraday-data/quotes.json` `us2y` still hold the pre-fix contaminated value. This sandbox has no network access to FRED/Treasury, so rather than hand-write an approximate figure into a pipeline-owned data file, the fix is left to the next scheduled `update-bond-yields.yml` run (daily 23:00 UTC) or a manual/`cron-job.org` trigger for an immediate correction.

### GUIDELINES.md
- Added an incident note under the existing "Yield data — 2Y must come from FRED DGS2" rule: that rule already existed and was scoped to `update_extended_data.py`, but `fetch_ohlc.py` (a different script, different repo) violated it via an unrelated-looking OHLC ticker map entry that fed into `fetch_bond_yields.py` as a trusted primary. Rule reinforced: check any new ticker/symbol map addition against every Data integrity rule in this document by **instrument**, not just by field name or script name. Footer bumped to `v8.90.19`.

### Flagged, not fixed this session
- **Duplicate/out-of-sync workflow files:** `update-bond-yields.yml` exists both at the `globalinvesting-scripts` repo root and under `.github/workflows/`, with different content (the root copy has `openpyxl` + `GI_RIKSBANK_API_KEY`; the one GitHub Actions actually runs, under `.github/workflows/`, has neither). Needs reconciliation — see repo hygiene debt.

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Root cause:** two independent functions render pair detail from different entry points — `updatePairDetail()` (floating popover, opened via the ⓘ button / double-click) and `buildInlineDetail()` (inline expansion in the FX Pairs table and sidebar crosses, opened via single-click). v8.90.16 only edited `updatePairDetail()`. `buildInlineDetail()` was never touched, so its "Price" section kept the old 4-cell layout with no spread — exactly what the user's screenshot showed, and exactly why re-uploading `dashboard.js` and hard-refreshing did not change anything: the deployed file already matched what was sent, the second render path just didn't have the feature yet.
- **Fix — `buildInlineDetail()` now computes the same sovereign bond spread as `updatePairDetail()`, byte-for-byte identical logic:** reads `bondBase`/`bondQuote` from the existing `BOND_YIELD_CACHE`, prefers 2Y, falls back to 10Y with an explicit `{tenor} Spread` label when either leg lacks 2Y coverage (JPY/NZD/NOK/SEK), and applies the same `invert`/`cross` sign convention already used for the Carry cell. No new cache, no new fetch — reuses `BOND_YIELD_CACHE` populated once at boot.
- **UI:** renamed the inline "Price" group label to "Price & Spreads" and added the `{tenor} Spread` cell (same tooltip copy as the popover version) to `.pd-inline-metrics`. Confirmed `.pd-inline-metrics` is `display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap` (not a fixed-column grid), so the 5th cell wraps cleanly — same pattern already used by the 5-cell Volatility group in the same function.
- **Verification:** `node --check assets/dashboard.js` clean, `node assets/dashboard.test.js` 85/85.
- Cache-buster bumped `?v=8.90.16` → `?v=8.90.17` in `index.html`.

## v8.90.15 (2026-08-02) — Fix: Sovereign Spreads table showed CHF at 31.00%/+2626bp and wrong curve-slope bp for all rows; CHF.json never committed

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Root cause of the CH row showing `31.00%` / `+2626 bp` vs US:** `renderSovereignSpreads()` had a `norm()` heuristic — `v < 1 ? v * 100 : v` — meant to handle yields stored as a fraction (e.g. `0.04`) vs already as percent (e.g. `4.0`). CHF genuinely trades under 1% (`bond10y: 0.31` in `extended-data/CHF.json`), so the heuristic misread it as a fraction and multiplied by 100. Removed `norm()` entirely — `extended-data/*.json` always stores true percent values, confirmed across USD/EUR/GBP/etc., so no conversion belongs here at all. CH now reads `0.31` → displays `0.31%`.
- **Second bug, same function — curve-slope column silently missing a ×100 conversion:** the 2Y–10Y slope was computed as `n10 - n2` (a raw percentage-point difference, e.g. `0.07`) and rendered with a `bp` suffix, so GB showed `+0 bp` and CA showed `+1 bp` instead of the correct `+7 bp` / `+73 bp`. Fixed to `(n10 - n2) * 100`, matching the same pct-pts→bp conversion the "vs US" spread column already did correctly.
- **Verification:** `node --check assets/dashboard.js` clean, `node assets/dashboard.test.js` 85/85.

### Engine — scripts/fetch_bond_yields.py workflow (globalinvesting-scripts repo, `.github/workflows/update-bond-yields.yml`)
- **Root cause of CHF.json never updating in production (still `0.31`, no `bond2y`) despite v2.5 shipping a working SNB fetch:** the "Commit and push" step's `git add` list enumerated 9 currency files and omitted `extended-data/CHF.json`. On a run where CHF was the only file that changed, `git diff --quiet` saw the unstaged CHF diff and did *not* take the "no changes" early exit, but nothing was staged for `git commit` to actually commit — the step failed with exit code 1 (`no changes added to commit`) before ever pushing. Added `extended-data/CHF.json` to the `git add` list; also added `CH10Y/2Y` to the commit message.
- **Verification:** workflow YAML re-parsed clean with `yaml.safe_load`.

## v8.90.7 (2026-08-01) — Fix: Parabolic SAR rendered as solid line, CB meeting markers not appearing on W1/MN, OBV/CMF/MFI/VWAP selectable on no-volume symbols

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Parabolic SAR rendering as a continuous line instead of dots (Santiago, screenshot):** `case 'psar'` in `_calcIndData` already flagged its series with `markers:true`, and `_buildIndicatorPane`'s markers branch tried to hide the connecting line via `lineWidth: 0`. That doesn't work — Lightweight Charts' `LineWidth` type is a union clamped to `1|2|3|4`, so `0` silently falls back to a visible 1px stroke instead of hiding the line, which is exactly the solid red curve in the screenshot. Fixed by using the actual dots-only API: `lineVisible: false` + `pointMarkersVisible: true` (with `pointMarkersRadius: 2`) on the `LineSeries` options, per Lightweight Charts v5's `LineStyleOptions`.
- **CB Meeting markers never appearing on W1/MN timeframes (Santiago, reported after toggling CB on and seeing nothing):** `_applyMarkers`'s date-matching only tried an exact string match against `barDates`, or the following calendar day (a weekend/holiday shift meant for D1 trading-day gaps). W1/MN bars are aggregated and keyed by the period's *start* date (ISO Monday for W1, first-of-month for MN — see the W1/MN aggregation notes earlier in this file), so an FOMC/BoE/ECB meeting date almost never lands on that key even when it's well within the visible range — `dateMap` ended up empty and no line/label ever drew, regardless of the CB toggle state. Fixed by falling back to the last bar whose date is `<=` the meeting date (i.e. the bar for the period that actually contains it) when neither the exact-date nor next-day match succeeds. D1 behavior (exact match, or +1 day for weekend meetings) is unchanged.
- **Verification (CB fix):** re-simulated the exact old vs. new date-matching logic standalone against the real `ohlc-data/gbpusd.json` aggregated to W1 and the real `meetings-data/meetings.json` BoE dates. Old logic: 0 of 4 in-range meetings matched any bar (matches the reported "nothing shows"). New logic: all 4 matched their containing week's bar.
- **OBV/CMF/MFI/VWAP selectable on symbols without volume data (Santiago):** these four indicators all fall back to `b.volume || 0` per-bar, so on a no-volume symbol (gold, indices without volume in the feed, etc.) they silently rendered a flat or degenerate line instead of being unavailable. Added `volRequired:true` to their `_IND_CATALOGUE` entries; the Indicators dropdown row-disabling logic (previously only used for timeframe-blocked Pivot Points) now also disables these rows — same greyed-out/`not-allowed` treatment, with a "this symbol has no volume data" tooltip — when the active symbol's `hasVolume` is false. `_calcIndData` also now returns `[]` early for `volRequired` indicators on no-volume symbols, so a symbol switch away from a volume-having pair can't leave a stale flat pane on screen if the indicator was already toggled on.
- **Verification:** `node --check assets/dashboard.js` clean, `node assets/dashboard.test.js` 85/85.
- Cache-buster bumped `assets/dashboard.js?v=8.90.6` → `?v=8.90.7` in `index.html`.

### Frontend — sw.js
- **`CACHE_VERSION`:** bumped `'gi-v8.90.6'` → `'gi-v8.90.7'` and `STATIC_PRECACHE`'s `dashboard.js` entry updated to `?v=8.90.7`, to stay in sync with the cache-buster bump above.

## v8.90.6 (2026-08-01) — Fix: Supertrend channel bug (real root cause, not caching); Pivot labels reduced to one per line

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Context (Santiago, after confirming via DevTools Network that the v8.90.5 Service Worker fix WAS deployed and `dashboard.js?v=8.90.4` was loading fresh — yet NZD/USD still rendered Supertrend as a solid two-band channel): this ruled out caching entirely and pointed back at the renderer.**
- **Actual root cause: Lightweight Charts' line series does not visually break on "whitespace" data.** The `supertrend` case built two series (up/down) sharing time coverage via a single time-only whitespace point dropped at each flip, expecting it to create a gap the way whitespace does for candlestick series. It doesn't, for line series — per the library's own maintainer (GitHub issue tradingview/lightweight-charts#700): "Whitespace doesn't mean gap actually right now. It means there is no value for a series." The renderer still draws a straight stroke between the nearest two REAL points either side of any whitespace, regardless of how many whitespace entries or how many weeks sit between them. Every inactive stretch (up to 184 bars long, in one measured case) was therefore silently bridged, and stacked across ~20+ flips per symbol that reads as a continuous filled channel — exactly the reported symptom. The underlying trend-gated calculation itself was correct the whole time (confirmed again this session: zero real-value overlap in the raw NZD/USD output).
- **`case 'supertrend'`:** rewritten to build ONE independent `LineSeries` instance per contiguous trend run instead of two whitespace-gapped series. Separate series objects cannot bridge each other — this is the only mechanism Lightweight Charts actually supports for a true visual gap (per the same GitHub thread). For a typical D1 history this is ~20-25 series instead of 2; well within what the library handles for an overlay pane.
- **`lastValueVisible`:** each segment now carries an explicit flag; only the most recent (current) run shows the right-axis value tag, matching Bloomberg/TradingView convention, instead of every historical run.
- **`_buildIndicatorPane`:** the `LineSeries` options now respect an explicit `s.lastValueVisible` on the series descriptor when present, falling back to the previous `si === 0` default for every other overlay indicator (EMA, Bollinger, Keltner, etc.) — unchanged behavior for all of those.
- **Pivot Points inline labels (`_calcPivotSeries`):** reduced from one tag per historical segment (shipped in v8.90.4, matching TradingView's literal per-segment convention) to a single tag per level, on the current/most recent period only. With 7 levels (R1-R3/PP/S1-S3) × many periods visible on a typical chart, per-segment tagging read as clutter rather than signal — Santiago asked for one current-value label per line instead.
- **Verification:** `node --check assets/dashboard.js` clean, `node assets/dashboard.test.js` 85/85. Re-simulated the new segment logic standalone against real NZD/USD D1 data (767 bars): 23 clean segments, every bar assigned to exactly one segment, zero time collisions — structurally impossible for two segments to bridge each other now.
- Cache-buster bumped `assets/dashboard.js?v=8.90.4` → `?v=8.90.6` in `index.html`.

### Frontend — sw.js
- **`CACHE_VERSION`:** bumped `'gi-v8.90.5'` → `'gi-v8.90.6'` and `STATIC_PRECACHE`'s `dashboard.js` entry updated to `?v=8.90.6`, to stay in sync with the cache-buster bump above (per the KEEP IN SYNC note added in v8.90.5).

## v8.90.5 (2026-08-01) — Fix: stale Service Worker cache serving months-old dashboard.js

### Frontend — sw.js
- **Context (Santiago, reported Supertrend rendering as a solid channel instead of a single flipping line): DevTools Network tab showed `dashboard.js?v=8.90.4` loading with `Status 200` from the page itself, but `sw.js` was separately fetching `dashboard.js?v=8.21.0` and `dashboard-v2.css?v=8.21.0` (404 — that filename no longer exists) in the background.**
- **Root cause: `CACHE_VERSION` was stuck at `'gi-v8.21.0'` across many releases, and `STATIC_PRECACHE` was never kept in sync with `index.html`'s asset list.** Because `cache.addAll()` is all-or-nothing, the 404 on the renamed `dashboard-v2.css` silently failed the *entire* `install()` step on every deploy since. And because `CACHE_VERSION` never changed, `activate()` never had a version bump to trigger deleting whatever static cache *had* successfully installed the last time `install()` last succeeded — so a returning client could still be served an old cached `dashboard.js` (from before the Supertrend trend-gating logic existed) indefinitely, regardless of what shipped on `main`.
- **`CACHE_VERSION`:** bumped `'gi-v8.21.0'` → `'gi-v8.90.4'` so every client drops old caches on next activation.
- **`STATIC_PRECACHE`:** rebuilt from scratch against the current `index.html` asset list (`dashboard.css?v=8.23.1`, `dashboard.js?v=8.90.4`, `gi-auth.js`, `fx-websocket.js`, `cot-modal-chart.js`, `cb-rates-modal.js`, `real-carry-modal.js`, `corr-modal.js`, `yc-modal.js`, `heatmap-modal.js`, `econ-surprises-modal.js`, `onboarding.js`, `layout-resizer.js`, `feed.js`, `share.js`, `inline-panel.js`, `calendar-panel.js`, `econ-matrix.js`, plus `gdpr.js`, `sw-register.js`, favicons, `manifest.json`). Removed the stale, renamed `dashboard-v2.css` and out-of-date `yc-modal.js?v=7.74.41` entries.
- **Verification:** `node --check sw.js` clean, `node assets/dashboard.test.js` 85/85. Confirmed the underlying `supertrend` calculation was never wrong — re-audited against real AUD/CHF and USD/JPY multi-year data with a single active line and zero band overlap; the "channel" only ever appeared when a client's Service Worker was still serving a pre-trend-gating build of `dashboard.js`.

## v8.90.4 (2026-08-01) — Pivot Points labels: replace price-axis tag with TradingView-standard per-segment inline placement

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Context (Santiago, side-by-side comparison against TradingView's Pivots Traditional): v8.90.3's fix put each pivot level's `title` on Lightweight Charts' native series `title`/`lastValueVisible` option, which surfaces exactly one tag, pinned to the series' current last value, on the right-hand price axis. That only ever identifies the CURRENT segment — every historical segment on screen stays unlabeled — and doesn't match the reference screenshots, where TradingView tags every period's own segment individually, positioned at the START of that segment inside the plot area itself.**
- **`_calcPivotSeries`:** now computes a `segStartsByField` entry per level — the first real (non-whitespace) point of every isolated flat run, i.e. the point immediately following each period's whitespace break (or the very first output point). This is what lets the new overlay place one tag per historical segment instead of one tag at the latest value.
- **New inline label overlay (`_pivotLabelOverlay` / `_drawPivotLabels` / `_ensurePivotLabelOverlay` / `_setPivotLabels`):** a transparent, `pointer-events:none` SVG layered over `chartDiv`, following the same pattern already in use for the CB-meeting-date overlay (`_cbOverlay`/`_drawCbLines`) — redrawn from `timeToCoordinate`/`priceToCoordinate` on every `subscribeVisibleTimeRangeChange`. Registered/cleared per indicator id from `_buildIndicatorPane`/`_destroyIndicatorPane`, including the empty-array case so a period pivot blocked by `_pivotTfOk` on the current timeframe doesn't leave stale labels from a prior timeframe.

## v8.90.3 (2026-08-01) — Fix: Pivot Points still zigzagging on same-or-coarser timeframes; add missing R1-R3/PP/S1-S3 axis labels

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Context (Santiago, two follow-up screenshots after v8.90.2 shipped): (1) on an AUD/USD D1 chart with Daily Pivot on, the lines still connected every bar into one continuous diagonal instead of showing isolated flat segments; (2) asked whether the pivot lines shouldn't carry R1/R2/S1/etc. labels — with 7 similarly-toned lines stacked on the price pane, there was no way to tell which line was which.**
- **Root cause 1 (the zigzag): a structural gap in v8.90.2's own fix, not a regression.** `_calcPivotSeries`'s whitespace-break logic only fires `when the incoming period has more than one bar` (`countByKey[key] > 1`) — a deliberate data-loss guard from v8.90.2. But Daily Pivot viewed on a D1 chart is the one case where that condition is *never* true: on a Daily chart, one bar always equals one full Daily-Pivot period, so every single bar is its own period and the guard blocks the gap on literally every transition — producing a screen-wide diagonal instead of the "minor one-bar-wide diagonal" the v8.90.2 comment expected as the rare edge case. There is no time slot available between two adjacent Daily bars to place a break without arithmetic on `bar.time` (the exact type hazard fixed in v8.90.2), so this case cannot be fixed by adjusting the gap logic — it has to be recognized as structurally unplottable and not rendered at all, which matches the standard MT5/TradingView convention of only exposing a period pivot on timeframes strictly *below* that period (Daily Pivot on H1/H4 only; Weekly Pivot up to D1; Monthly Pivot up to W1).
- **`_pivotTfOk(unit)` (new):** checks the active chart timeframe (`_lwActiveTf`) against the minimum-granularity rule above. `_calcPivotSeries` now returns `[]` immediately when the check fails, instead of attempting to plot a period pivot the current timeframe structurally cannot support.
- **Indicators menu:** the Pivot Points (Daily/Weekly/Monthly) rows are now visually disabled (dimmed, `not-allowed` cursor, explanatory `title` tooltip — matching the existing disabled-button convention already used for chart-type buttons on daily-print-only series) and un-clickable whenever the current timeframe doesn't support them, so the user can't turn on an indicator that would render nothing (or, before this fix, the corrupted zigzag). Re-evaluated fresh each time the dropdown opens, so switching timeframes updates availability without a page reload.
- **Root cause 2 (missing labels): `_buildIndicatorPane`'s per-series axis label (`lastValueVisible`) was hardcoded to only the first series (`si === 0`) for every overlay indicator, and the pane-corner legend built from each series' `label` field (`_addPaneLegend`) was only ever wired up for oscillator sub-panes (`if (!isOverlay ...)`) — overlay indicators with more than one line (Pivot Points chief among them, at 7 lines) had no in-chart way to identify which line was which.**
- **Fix:** `_calcPivotSeries` now sets a compact `title` field per series (`DR3`, `DPP`, `DS1`, etc. — unit-prefixed so Daily/Weekly/Monthly pivots stay distinguishable from each other if shown together). `_buildIndicatorPane`'s line-series branch passes that `title` straight into Lightweight Charts' native series option of the same name and forces `lastValueVisible: true` whenever a `title` is present — this surfaces each pivot level as its own always-on tag directly on the price axis (the standard TradingView/MT5 treatment for overlapping pivot lines), rather than adding a custom DOM legend box that would risk colliding with the existing OHLC/watermark overlay already occupying the main pane's top-left corner. Other overlay indicators that don't set `title` are unaffected and keep the prior `si === 0` behavior.
- **Supertrend re-verified, not re-changed:** re-extracted the exact shipped `supertrend` case and `_iTR`/`_iRMA` from the file (not a hand-copied approximation) and ran it standalone against a synthetic 70-bar series with two trend flips — exactly one whitespace point per flip in each of the up/down series, both strictly ascending and unique, no channel-forming connect-the-dots behavior. The code itself has no remaining defect; a multi-band "channel" appearance in a screenshot with several overlays active (MAs, Bollinger, Keltner, etc. all stacked) is not attributable to Supertrend's own data structure, which can only ever hold one active (non-whitespace) line at a time. If the channel look persists with *only* Supertrend enabled, that would point to a stale cached `dashboard.js` in the browser rather than a code defect — worth a hard refresh against `?v=8.90.3` to confirm.
- **Verification:** `node --check assets/dashboard.js` clean, `node assets/dashboard.test.js` 85/85, no regression. Re-extracted the real, patched `_calcPivotSeries`/`_pivotTfOk`/`_iAggregatePeriods`/`_iPivotPeriodKey`/`_timeToEpoch` from the file and ran standalone: Daily Pivot on a D1 chart → correctly returns empty (blocked) instead of the zigzag; Daily Pivot on synthetic H1 bars → 7 titled series (`DR3`…`DS3`), distinct daily levels, all times strictly ascending/unique; Weekly Pivot on D1 and Monthly Pivot on W1 → both correctly allowed and returning 7 series each; Monthly Pivot on an MN chart → correctly blocked.
- Cache-buster bumped `assets/dashboard.js?v=8.90.2` → `?v=8.90.3` in `index.html`.

## v8.90.2 (2026-08-01) — Fix: Supertrend and Pivot Points invisible/corrupted on Daily/Weekly/Monthly timeframes

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Context (Santiago, screenshot right after v8.90.1 shipped): on a D1 chart, Supertrend showed as a thick filled block instead of a line and Pivot Points didn't render meaningfully at all. Root cause: v8.90.1's whitespace-gap fix computed a synthetic midpoint time (`bars[i-1].time + (bars[i].time - bars[i-1].time)/2`) to place the break — but `bar.time` is a `'YYYY-MM-DD'` business-day string on D1/W1/MN timeframes (confirmed against the existing "Universal drawing-point time" convention already documented in this file for the drawing-tools code) and a plain unix-seconds number only on H1/H4. `string + number` in JS silently concatenates instead of throwing (e.g. `"2026-08-01" + 1` → `"2026-08-011"`), so every timestamp downstream of the first gap was garbage, corrupting both indicators' render on any D1/W1/MN chart.**
- **A second, independent bug in the same area, present since v8.90.0 (not introduced by v8.90.1): `_iPivotPeriodKey()` did `new Date(t * 1000)` directly on `bar.time` without normalizing it first — `string * 1000` is `NaN` in JS, so every D1/W1/MN bar produced the same `NaN` period key, collapsing the entire chart into one giant "period" and explaining the original "pivot lines span the whole screen" bug report on its own, independent of the connect-the-dots gap issue v8.90.1 addressed.**
- **`_iPivotPeriodKey`:** now runs `bar.time` through the existing `_timeToEpoch()` helper (already used elsewhere in this file for exactly this D1/W1/MN-string vs. H1/H4-number distinction) before any date math.
- **Both `_calcPivotSeries` and the `supertrend` case:** replaced the synthetic-midpoint-time gap with a whitespace point placed on an *existing* bar's own time slot — no arithmetic on `bar.time` at all, so it's correct regardless of whether the active timeframe uses string or numeric time.
- **Pivot data-loss guard:** placing a gap this way means sacrificing that bar's real value, which is fine when a period spans many bars (the usual case) but would silently drop every value on a period made of exactly one bar (e.g. Daily Pivots viewed ON a Daily chart, where every bar is its own period). `_iAggregatePeriods` now also tracks a bar `count` per period, and `_calcPivotSeries` only takes the gap-and-sacrifice path when the incoming period has more than one bar; single-bar periods stay directly connected (a minor one-bar-wide diagonal at the transition, not the original whole-chart-spanning flat line, which was the `NaN`-key bug above, already fixed independently of this).
- **Verification:** `node --check assets/dashboard.js` clean, `node assets/dashboard.test.js` 85/85. Re-extracted the exact shipped `_calcPivotSeries`/`_iAggregatePeriods`/`_iPivotPeriodKey`/`_timeToEpoch` functions from the file (not a hand-copied approximation) and ran them standalone against three scenarios: Daily Pivot on Daily (`'YYYY-MM-DD'` string) bars — 14/14 bars retained a value, zero data loss; Weekly Pivot on the same Daily bars — correctly zero-gap on this particular short dataset since only one week boundary had more than one bar to spare; Daily Pivot on Hourly (numeric epoch) bars — 336 points, 13 gaps, 14 distinct daily levels, all output times strictly ascending and unique as required by Lightweight Charts' `setData()`.

## v8.90.1 (2026-08-01) — Fix: Supertrend rendering as a filled channel, Pivot Points rendering as one continuous line

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Context (Santiago, visual bug report with screenshot right after v8.90.0 shipped): Supertrend was rendering as a wide filled channel instead of a single line that flips color on trend change, and Pivot Points were rendering as flat horizontal lines running the full width of the chart instead of a distinct segment per day/week/month. Root cause for both: `_calcIndData` fed Lightweight Charts `LineSeries.setData()` arrays that skip time entries whenever a bar doesn't belong to that series (Supertrend's inactive trend leg) or whenever a bar's level hasn't changed (irrelevant here, but the same connect-the-dots behavior applies to pivot period boundaries) — Lightweight Charts does not infer a break from a time gap on its own; it draws a plain connecting line between whatever two points are adjacent in the array, however far apart in time.**
- **`supertrend`:** on every trend flip, a whitespace point (`{time}`, no `value`) is now inserted into the series that just went inactive, at the midpoint between the flip bar and the prior bar. Previously the up-band and down-band series would each keep their last pre-flip point and next post-re-flip point directly adjacent in the array, so Lightweight Charts bridged the entire flipped-away stretch with a straight line — since both bands sit only a couple ATRs from price, that bridge read visually as a filled channel rather than a color-flipping single line.
- **`_calcPivotSeries` (`pivotd`/`pivotw`/`pivotm`):** same whitespace-gap technique applied at every period boundary (day/week/month), so each period's PP/R1-R3/S1-S3 levels now render as their own isolated flat segment — matching the standard TradingView/MT5 pivot display — instead of one polyline threading every period's level into the next across the whole chart.
- **Verification:** `node --check assets/dashboard.js` clean. `node assets/dashboard.test.js` — 85/85 passing, no regression (these two indicators aren't independently importable from this file's chart-closure functions, so as with the original v8.90.0 session, verification was done via a standalone extraction of the two functions run against synthetic bar data outside the DOM). Pivot fix checked against 10 synthetic days of hourly bars: 9 distinct daily PP levels (day 1 has no prior day to derive from), 8 whitespace gap points separating them, all output times strictly ascending and unique (required by `setData()`). Supertrend fix checked against a synthetic 60-bar series with an uptrend, a sharp reversal into a downtrend, and a reversal back up: exactly 2 trend flips produced exactly 1 gap point in each of the up/down series, both series' times strictly ascending and unique.

## v8.90.0 (2026-08-01) — Price Chart: Supertrend and Pivot Points (Daily/Weekly/Monthly) indicators

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js · Guides — guide-dashboard.html
- **Context (Santiago, follow-up to the Jay Medrow institutional-methodology gap analysis): flagged that Supertrend and daily/weekly/monthly Pivot Points were both missing from the Indicators menu.** Both slot cleanly into the existing indicator plug-in architecture (`_IND_CATALOGUE` entry + a `case` in `_calcIndData`) — unlike Volume Profile (Nivel 3 of the same gap analysis), which needs its own renderer and is deferred to a separate session.
- **`supertrend` (new, `type:'overlay'`, group `Overlays`, params: ATR Period default 10, Multiplier default 3):** standard ATR-ratchet-band algorithm — two candidate bands (support/resistance) are computed each bar from `hl2 ± mult×ATR` and can only move in the current trend's favor; the trend flips when price closes through the *opposite* band's prior value. Rendered as two separate line series (up-trend / down-trend) so the color flips visually at each trend change, following the same two-series-per-flip pattern already used elsewhere in this file for anything that needs a hard color change (e.g. MACD's histogram sign coloring) rather than adding unsupported per-point coloring to a plain line series. Reuses the existing `_iTR()`/`_iRMA(tr,n)` ATR pipeline already shared by Keltner Channel — `_iRMA` returns an array 1:1 index-aligned with `bars`, so no offset math was needed (confirmed by tracing Keltner's existing usage before writing this).
- **`pivotd` / `pivotw` / `pivotm` (new, `type:'overlay'`, group `Overlays`, no params):** classic floor-trader pivot formula (PP, R1-R3, S1-S3) computed from the **prior** period's aggregate H/L/C — daily uses a UTC calendar-day boundary (matches the existing VWAP session-reset convention in this same file), weekly uses proper ISO-8601 week numbering (Mon-Sun, correctly handles year boundaries including 53-week years like 2020), monthly uses UTC calendar month. New shared helpers: `_iPivotPeriodKey()`, `_iAggregatePeriods()`, `_iPivotLevels()`, `_calcPivotSeries()` — one aggregation/lookup path reused by all three period variants instead of three separate implementations.
- **Verification:** `node --check assets/dashboard.js` clean. `node assets/dashboard.test.js` — 85/85 passing (no shared-code regression). Standalone numerical validation (outside the DOM-bound chart closure, since this file's indicator functions aren't independently importable): ISO week boundary logic checked against 7 known reference dates including the 2020/2021 year-boundary edge case (53-week year) — all correct. Classic pivot formula checked against a hand-computed example (H=110/L=100/C=105 → PP=105, R1=110, S1=100, R2=115, S2=95, R3=120, S3=90) — exact match. Supertrend flip logic checked against a synthetic 40-bar series (steady uptrend → sharp 3-unit-per-bar reversal → steady downtrend): correctly held the up-trend band through the calm uptrend and flipped exactly on the first reversal bar, with no further false flips through the downtrend.
- **`guide-dashboard.html`:** indicator count/list sentence updated from "25 overlays and oscillators" to "29", with Supertrend and Pivot Points Daily/Weekly/Monthly added to the Overlays group list. No other guide page repeats this count.
- Cache-buster bumped `assets/dashboard.js?v=8.87.0` → `?v=8.90.0` in `index.html` (jumped past 8.88.0/8.89.0, already used by the prior CSI/calendar sessions logged above).

## v8.89.0 (2026-08-01) — Economic Calendar fullscreen: two-column layout on wide monitors

### Frontend — assets/calendar-panel.js · Site — index.html
- **Context (Santiago): after capping the fullscreen calendar table to a readable max-width (v8.88.x session), asked whether the recovered dead space on ultra-wide monitors should instead be used to show more information, matching the philosophy of Bloomberg Terminal / Refinitiv Eikon (every pixel shows data, not blank margin). Approved implementing a two-column split.**
- **Note:** this feature was designed and unit/integration-tested (jsdom, 85/85 `dashboard.test.js`) in the prior session, but the corresponding `index.html` CSS/markup and the updated `assets/calendar-panel.js` were never actually committed — a fresh export of the repo confirmed only the single-column, width-capped fullscreen (v8.88.x state) was live. This entry lands that work for real.
- **`calendar-panel.js`:** `buildPanel()`'s date/event loop now builds per-date groups (`{dateISO, html, rowCount}`) instead of one flat HTML string. `shouldSplitCalColumns()` gates the split to fullscreen + viewport ≥1400px; `groups.length > 1` guard prevents splitting a single date group. `relayoutCalendar()` re-renders from a cached last fetch (`_lastEvents`/`_lastSource`/`_lastHolidays`) on fullscreen open/close and on a debounced `resize` listener, so the layout adapts live without waiting for the next 2-min poll.
- **Column balancing:** the split point is chosen by comparing the row-count sum immediately before vs. after crossing the midpoint and picking whichever side is closer to 50/50 — not simply the first group that crosses it, which produced badly lopsided columns on heavy days (e.g. an FOMC day would otherwise pack 42 rows into column 1 and 6 into column 2; the fix balances this to ~22/26).
- **Scroll handling generalized** for two independent scroll containers (one per `.cal-col-wrap`) instead of one: capture/restore scroll position as an array, and `scrollRootFor()` resolves the correct container (a `.cal-col-wrap` or the outer `cal-events-body`) for the "Next event" jump button and first-render smart-scroll logic in either layout mode.
- **`index.html`:** added `id="cal-static-col-header"` to the docked column-header row so JS can hide it when the 2-column layout is active (each column renders its own sticky `.cal-col-header` instead). New CSS: `.cal-events-cols` (flex row), `.cal-col-wrap` (independent scroll container per column, divider border between them), `.cal-col-header`/`.cal-th-num` (per-column sticky header, mirrors the docked header's inline styles). `#section-tvcalendar.cal-fs-split` widens the fullscreen max-width from 1180px to 2200px so two columns have room; single-column fullscreen keeps the narrower 1180px cap.
- **Verification:** `node --check assets/calendar-panel.js` clean. `node assets/dashboard.test.js` — 85/85 passing. No duplicate IDs (`cal-static-col-header` and all fullscreen-related IDs confirmed unique). jsdom integration test against the actual shipped `index.html` + `calendar-panel.js` (not a standalone harness) confirmed: docked view stays single-column; opening fullscreen at 1920px produces exactly 2 `.cal-col-wrap` columns, hides the static header, and adds `.cal-fs-split`; closing fullscreen reverts to 0 columns and restores the static header; a narrow (900px) fullscreen viewport stays single-column (below the 1400px breakpoint); live resize while fullscreen stays open does not close the overlay and correctly toggles columns on/off crossing the breakpoint.
- Cache-buster: `assets/calendar-panel.js?v=1.7.0` in `index.html` (unchanged version number — this entry lands the v1.7 work that should have shipped already, not a new file version).

## v3.39 (2026-08-01) — `fetch_ff_calendar.py` (scripts repo): manual workflow_dispatch bypasses the :00/:30 forward-fetch gate

### Scripts — `fetch_ff_calendar.py` (scripts repo) · Site — `.github/workflows/update-ff-calendar.yml`
- **Context (Santiago): ran a manual `workflow_dispatch` right after v3.38 shipped to verify the hybrid fetch. The run's log showed `ForexFactory JSON: off-gate tick — skipping forward fetch this run` — 0 forward events, despite the feature being correctly implemented. Confirmed with Santiago: "es que ese log es de una corrida manual."**
- **Root cause: not a bug in v3.38 — a UX gap in the gate design.** `FF_FORWARD_MINUTE_TOLERANCE`'s :00/:30 tick gate exists to protect ForexFactory's community-documented ~2req/5min rate limit against the workflow's dense `*/5` production cron. A manual `workflow_dispatch` is a human actively testing or debugging, not a cron tick — it will happen at most a few times a day and should always exercise the full hybrid fetch, not silently skip depending on which minute the person happened to click "Run workflow."
- **Fix:** `on_gate_tick` now also evaluates true when `os.environ.get("GITHUB_EVENT_NAME") == "workflow_dispatch"`. `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` is one of GitHub Actions' default per-step environment variables (documented, always present — no workflow YAML change was needed to expose it, unlike a custom secret/env). Scheduled and CF-Worker-dispatched (`repository_dispatch`) runs are unaffected — the :00/:30 tick gate still applies to them exactly as in v3.38.
- **Companion diagnostic fix — `update-ff-calendar.yml`'s "Display summary" step:** previously only showed today's high-impact events and a flat total. Now also prints a per-vendor breakdown (`myfxbook` vs `forexfactory` counts) and a forward-vs-today split, so any run's log — manual or scheduled — confirms at a glance whether the ForexFactory forward fetch actually populated events, without needing to inspect the raw JSON. Pre-v3.38 carried-forward events have no `vendor` field yet; the summary script defaults those to `"myfxbook"` (the sole source before v3.38) rather than miscounting them as unattributed.
- **Verification:** `python3 -m py_compile fetch_ff_calendar.py` clean. Unit-tested the gate expression in isolation across four cases: off-tick minute + `schedule` event → gate closed (unchanged behavior); off-tick minute + `workflow_dispatch` → gate open (new); on-tick minute + `schedule` → gate open (unchanged); on-tick-with-tolerance minute + `repository_dispatch` → gate open (unchanged). `python3 -c` YAML-parsed the updated workflow file to confirm no syntax break from the summary-step edit. `node assets/dashboard.test.js` — 85/85 passing (no frontend/shared-code touched).

## v3.38 (2026-08-01) — `fetch_ff_calendar.py` (scripts repo): hybrid source architecture — Myfxbook actuals + ForexFactory forward calendar

### Scripts — `fetch_ff_calendar.py` (scripts repo) · Site — `.github/workflows/update-ff-calendar.yml`
- **Context (Santiago): "el calendario económico de la terminal solo muestra el día de calendario actual... el estándar de industria es que el calendario muestra la o las semanas siguientes... agregamos el calendario de forex factory para los días siguientes a hoy y dejamos que el de hoy sea myfxbook" — approved "implementar esto a la par de la industria."**
- **Root cause: a documentation/code drift, not a new gap.** This file's own module docstring (SOURCE / OUTPUT SCHEMA / FETCH WINDOW sections) still described the pre-v3.23 architecture — ForexFactory JSON, "this week + next week" — but the pipeline has been Myfxbook-only since the v3.23 migration (2026-06-10), and Myfxbook RSS's own docstring documents a rolling ~24h window. Nothing beyond ~today+1 could ever populate `ff_calendar.json`, even though `calendar-panel.js`'s display window (v1.5, `[-3, +14]` days) had room to show it. `GUIDELINES.md`'s `calendar-data/` table row repeated the same stale claim and has been corrected as part of this change.
- **Fix — hybrid source, not a full reversion.** Myfxbook RSS remains the sole source for today and all past days — its fast-actuals path (CF Worker KV overlay, carry-forward, dedup) is untouched, and the v3.23 rationale for moving off ForexFactory JSON (10h+ actual lag) still holds for that use case. ForexFactory's public weekly JSON export (`nfs.faireconomy.media/ff_calendar_thisweek.json` + `_nextweek.json` — the same endpoint used pre-v3.23, still live/public/unauthenticated, confirmed 2026-08-01) is reintroduced strictly for `dateISO > today`, populating forecast/previous/impact only — no `actual` field is ever read from it.
- **New:** `fetch_forexfactory_forward()` parses the FF export into `ff_calendar.json` event dicts, filtered to G10 currencies + medium/high impact, keeping only forward-looking days. Events are tagged `vendor: "forexfactory"` (Myfxbook-origin events now tagged `vendor: "myfxbook"` too) so downstream logic can distinguish the two without guessing from field shape.
- **New:** `_drop_superseded_ff_placeholders()` — once a forward day becomes today (or Myfxbook's own ~24h window reaches into it), Myfxbook's differently-titled, differently-timed row for the same real-world event must not persist as a duplicate alongside the FF placeholder. Reuses the existing `_title_keywords()` cross-vendor title normaliser (already built for FF's slash notation vs Myfxbook's spelled-out MoM/YoY) plus a tolerant ±90min same-day time match, since the two vendors are never guaranteed to agree to the minute.
- **Rate-limit safety:** ForexFactory's weekly export endpoints are community-documented (not an official SLA) to reject more than ~2 requests/5min combined across formats. `update-ff-calendar.yml` runs every 5 min in release windows — the forward fetch is gated internally (`FF_FORWARD_MINUTE_TOLERANCE`) to only the workflow's existing :00/:30 ticks, reusing the current cron schedule instead of adding a new one. A rate-limited or failed forward fetch degrades gracefully (skip this run, keep prior forward events via the existing Step 2 historical merge) and never blocks the Myfxbook actuals path.
- `source` field in `ff_calendar.json` is now computed dynamically after all merges: `"Myfxbook · ForexFactory"` once any ForexFactory-vendor event survives into the write, `"Myfxbook RSS"` otherwise — matches this project's data-integrity rule against hardcoded/inaccurate source labels (see the earlier `guide-economic-surprises.html`-adjacent audit that flagged the same class of stale label).
- **Docs corrected to match:** module docstring's SOURCE / OUTPUT SCHEMA / FETCH WINDOW / SCHEDULE sections rewritten for the v3.38 hybrid architecture (previously unchanged since v3.7). `GUIDELINES.md`'s `calendar-data/` table row corrected in the same pass.
- Workflow step in `update-ff-calendar.yml` renamed and commented to describe the hybrid fetch instead of the old "(ForexFactory)"-only label, which was itself stale (the step has run Myfxbook, not ForexFactory, since v3.23).
- **Verification:** `python3 -m py_compile fetch_ff_calendar.py` clean. Unit-tested `fetch_forexfactory_forward()` and `_drop_superseded_ff_placeholders()` in isolation against synthetic payloads: non-G10 currency, low-impact, today-or-past, and unparseable-date events correctly filtered out of the forward set; a Myfxbook-origin event correctly supersedes/drops its FF-origin placeholder for the same (currency, dateISO) with overlapping title keywords, while an unrelated FF-origin event for a different date is correctly kept. `node assets/dashboard.test.js` — 85/85 passing (no frontend/shared-code touched by this change).
- **Manual follow-up for Santiago:** after this deploys and runs through at least one full day/night cycle, confirm in the live `calendar-data/ff_calendar.json` that (a) forward days beyond today are populated with ForexFactory-origin events, and (b) yesterday's forward placeholders were cleanly superseded once Myfxbook's own actuals landed for those events — no duplicate rows for the same release.

### Frontend — assets/heatmap-modal.js
- **Context (Santiago, follow-up to v8.87.1's cache-buster fix): asked to close the remaining architectural gap where the CSI chart lags the EA's live line even after the cache-buster fix — approved implementing "opción 2" (today-bar injection reusing `STOOQ_RT_CACHE`, matching `_lwBuildTodayBar()`'s pattern in `dashboard.js`) "siguiendo los estándares de industria."**
- **Root cause (diagnosed in the same session, before this fix): a structural gap, not a caching bug.** `ohlc-data/{pair}.json` is written by `fetch_ohlc.py`, which by design strips the in-progress today-bar before writing so a candle with truncated H/L wicks never persists on disk (see that script's own header comment and `update-ohlc.yml`'s 01:30 UTC session-finalization rationale). `_loadCSIData()` only ever reads from these files, so the CSI chart's last point structurally cannot reflect the session currently in progress until the OHLC workflow's next close-out run (~21:00-22:30 UTC) — no cache-buster value fixes this, since the file itself doesn't contain today's data yet. The main price chart already solved the equivalent problem for candlesticks via `_lwBuildTodayBar()` / `_lwUpdateTodayBar()`, sourced live from `STOOQ_RT_CACHE`; the CSI chart had no analog.
- **Fix — added a CSI-specific live-point layer, `_computeCSILiveView()` / `_csiLiveDateStr()` / `_updateCSILiveBar()`:**
  - `_csiLiveDateStr()` mirrors `_lwBuildTodayBar()`'s FX session-open date convention (21:00 UTC boundary — a bar forming at/after 21:00 UTC belongs to the session `fetch_ohlc.py` will date tomorrow).
  - `_computeCSILiveView()` derives one extra point per currency for the in-progress session using the **exact same per-pair sign convention and log-return math already in `_loadCSIData()`** (`Math.log(close/prevClose) * sign`, averaged across each currency's participating pairs) sourced from `STOOQ_RT_CACHE`'s `close`/`prev_close` fields — the same fields `_lwBuildTodayBar()` reads — so the live point is numerically consistent with, not just visually appended to, the historical series. Returns the plain historical `_csiData` unchanged (no-op) during the FX weekend (reuses this file's existing `isMarketWeekend()` guard), when `STOOQ_RT_CACHE` isn't populated yet, or when the OHLC workflow has already closed out today's session and the historical series already contains it — avoiding a double-counted day.
  - `_updateCSILiveBar()` is the RT-tick handler, wired into `_hmRefreshIfOpen()`'s existing per-tab dispatch (previously a no-op comment: *"CSI tab uses historical OHLC data only — no RT refresh needed"*). It pushes the live point onto each already-rendered LWC series via `.update()` — flash-free, no chart teardown/rebuild — matching the same in-place-update intent `_updateBreakdownRT()`/`_updateCorrelationsRT()` already use for their tabs, and the same "push to existing series" intent as `_lwUpdateTodayBar()` on the main chart.
  - `populateCSI()` and `csiPeriod()` (period-toggle) now compute `_csiDataLive` before each full `_renderCSIChart()`/`_renderCSIStats()` call, so opening the CSI tab or switching 1M/3M/6M/1Y/All always renders with the freshest live point, not just RT ticks while already open.
  - Legend (`_updateCSILegend`) and the stats table (`_renderCSIStats`) both read from `_csiDataLive` (falling back to `_csiData`) so the live point is reflected everywhere on the tab consistently, not just the chart lines.
- **Scope boundary:** this only affects the CSI tab's own rendering functions in `heatmap-modal.js`. `_loadCSIData()` itself, the OHLC JSON files, and `fetch_ohlc.py`/`update-ohlc.yml` are untouched — the fix is purely a client-side live overlay, matching how the main price chart's today-bar is also a client-side overlay on top of unmodified closed-session JSON.
- **Verification:** `node assets/heatmap-modal.js` (via `node --check`) — syntax clean. Live-return sign convention validated in isolation against a synthetic JPY-rally scenario (USDJPY 163.37→159.52, EURJPY equivalent move): JPY live return correctly resolves positive, USD/EUR counterparties correctly resolve negative, matching the existing `_loadCSIData()` base/quote sign rule. `node assets/dashboard.test.js` — 85/85 passing (no shared-code regression).
- Cache-buster bumped `assets/heatmap-modal.js?v=2.2.2` → `?v=2.2.3` in `index.html`.
- **Manual follow-up for Santiago:** verify visually in a live session — open a currency's CSI tab mid-week during active FX hours and confirm the rightmost point of the line moves as `STOOQ_RT_CACHE` ticks update, without the chart flashing/rebuilding on each tick.

## v8.87.0 (2026-07-30) — Confidence shrinkage for thin-sample ESI readings (parallel fix to MT5 EA v3.347)

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Context (Santiago, after the MT5 EA's SURPRISE INDEX panel fix): "esto cambio a la par de la industria también se aplica en la terminal web?"** — audited `renderEconSurprises()`'s bar/index math against the same two issues found and fixed in the EA's `ComputeESI()` (v3.347).
- **Bar-scaling bug: not present here.** The EA's bug was scaling bar width against the locally-observed max `|score|` among the 10 currencies currently on screen. This panel already scales `halfPct` against the fixed `idx100` range (`[-100, +100]`, per the Citi CESI convention comment above it) — a currency's bar length was already comparable across sessions/screenshots. No change needed for this half of the issue.
- **Confidence shrinkage: was missing, now added.** `idx100` previously had no penalty for thin sample support — a currency with `N=1` that happened to beat consensus could render `idx100=+100` (a full-width half-bar), visually identical to a reading backed by dozens of independent releases. Added a `confidence = Math.min(1, s.total / CONFIDENCE_MIN_N)` multiplier (`CONFIDENCE_MIN_N = 15`, reusing the `s.total` counter already computed for the N column, and matching the existing `lowConf = s.total < 15` threshold this same function already uses to dim the N column) applied to `idx100` before the bar and tooltip are built.
- **Threshold note:** the EA's equivalent (`CONFIDENCE_MIN_EVENTS = 6`) counts *distinct event_ids* (unique indicator series, e.g. "GDP q/q" counted once regardless of how many monthly prints occur in-window); the web terminal's `s.total` counts *raw scored releases* (each monthly print counted separately, matching what's already displayed in the N column). The two thresholds are not directly comparable because the underlying counters measure different things — flagging as a known cross-repo methodology difference, not a bug, but a candidate for a future harmonization pass if Santiago wants the EA and web terminal to converge on one counting convention.
- `node assets/dashboard.test.js` — 85/85 passing.

## v8.86.11 (2026-07-30) — Root-cause fix: W1/MN drawings resolved to x=0 because `logicalToCoordinate()` silently rejects fractional indices in this library version

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Diagnostic path (v8.86.8–v8.86.10):** since the v8.86.6/8.86.9 fixes still left rectangles invisible on W1/MN with no thrown exception and no null coordinate, a temporary `window._lwDebugDraw` flag was added to `_svgForDrawing()`/`_renderDrawings()` to log real coordinate values without flooding the console on every price tick (throttled to fire only on timeframe change or value change). Browser console output confirmed `x1: 0, x2: 0` exactly on both W1 and MN, while `y1`/`y2` varied normally — isolating the failure to the x-axis interpolation path specifically, not price scale or clip-path.
- **Root cause, confirmed via `lightweight-charts@5.0.7` source (`TimeScale.qt`) and live browser output:** `_epochToXInterpolated()` (v8.86.6/8.86.9) assumed `logicalToCoordinate()` is defined continuously between bars, per its own doc comment — but this library version guards internally on `Number.isInteger()` and returns a bare `0` (not `null`, no error) for any fractional logical index. A D1-drawn shape read back on W1/MN almost never lands on an integer bar position, so every fractional fallback call was silently coerced to zero, producing `x1 = x2 = 0` on both timeframes.
- **Fix:** `_epochToXInterpolated()` no longer passes fractional indices to `logicalToCoordinate()` at all. It now calls `logicalToCoordinate()` only on the two integer bar indices bracketing the target epoch (`_logicalToX()`), then linearly interpolates between their two resulting *pixel* coordinates (`_interpX()`) — mathematically equivalent given uniform bar spacing in pixel space between adjacent bars, and correct for both the interior binary-search case and the two boundary-extrapolation cases (before the first bar / after the last bar).
- `node assets/dashboard.test.js` — 85/85 passing.
- Cache-buster bumped `assets/dashboard.js?v=8.86.10` → `?v=8.86.11` in `index.html`.
