## v8.86.7 (2026-07-30) — Fix: drawing overlay bleeds into oscillator sub-panes; rectangles vanish entirely on coarse timeframes (W1/MN)

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Bug 1, confirmed via code review (Santiago, H1/H4 screenshots after v8.86.6: "tiene el bug de que queda por arriba de la ventana del oscilador. Eso no puede pasar"):** `_renderDrawings()`'s clip-path only ever excluded the right price-scale ribbon and the bottom time-axis strip from the *whole* `chartDiv` — which, once an oscillator (RSI, Stochastic, MACD, etc.) is active, spans pane 0 (the main price pane, the only pane any drawing is ever anchored to) *plus* every sub-pane stacked below it. A shape whose price fell outside pane 0's own autoscaled range (now a real possibility since v8.86.5/8.86.6 let a shape be viewed on any timeframe/zoom, not just the one it was drawn on) kept extending straight past pane 0's bottom edge into whichever sub-pane sat underneath — exactly the "spills into the oscillator's window" screenshots.
  - **Fix:** when `_lwChart.panes().length > 1`, the clip-path's bottom inset is now `max(time-axis height, chartDiv height − pane 0's own HTMLElement height)`, so the overlay stops exactly at the bottom of the main price pane whenever a sub-pane exists below it, and falls back to the old time-axis-only clip when there's just the one pane (no behavior change for the common no-indicator case).
- **Bug 2 (Santiago: "En W1 y MN no aparece aún"):** root-caused as a rendering, not a coordinate-resolution, failure — verified by replaying the real aggregation + interpolation logic against production `ohlc-data/eurusd.json`, which confirmed `_epochToXInterpolated()` (v8.86.6) resolves finite, distinct logical positions for both W1 and MN, never `null`. The real problem: per SVG spec, a `<rect>` with a *computed* width or height of `0` is not rendered **at all** — not even its stroke. A shape drawn on D1 spanning roughly 9 days is only a fraction of a single W1 bar (~7 days) or MN bar (~30 days) wide, so its rendered width on those timeframes can round to effectively nothing, and the whole rectangle silently disappears exactly the way Santiago described — this is a general risk for *any* rectangle viewed on a coarser timeframe than it was drawn on, not specific to this one shape.
  - **Fix — industry-standard minimum visible size (TradingView/MT5 never let a drawn object vanish this way):** `_svgForDrawing()`'s `rect` branch now clamps both width and height to a 2px floor, expanding outward from the shape's own center so it stays anchored at the same real-world midpoint instead of snapping to one edge.
- `node assets/dashboard.test.js` — 85/85 passing.
- Cache-buster bumped `assets/dashboard.js?v=8.86.6` → `?v=8.86.7` in `index.html`.

## v8.86.6 (2026-07-30) — Fix: drawn objects still invisible on W1/H4 after v8.86.5's universal-epoch storage fix

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Root cause (Santiago, with screenshots: rectangle visible on D1, absent on H4 and W1 — "Sigue sin reflejarse el objeto en distintas temporalidades"):** v8.86.5 correctly stores every drawing point as a universal unix-epoch second, but `_xForPoint()` still read it back with a single `ts.timeToCoordinate(_epochToActiveTime(pt.time))` call. `timeToCoordinate()` only resolves a Time that exactly matches an existing bar on the *active* series — it silently returns `null` (no error, no console warning) for anything else. A D1-drawn epoch only ever lands on an exact bar time when the active series is also D1: W1 bars are stamped on one specific weekday per week, H4 bars every 4 hours, so a D1 date essentially never coincides with a W1 or H4 bar's exact time. The object was never actually being drawn on those timeframes; it just looked like it was "not there."
- **Fix — industry-standard interpolated anchoring:** added `_epochToXInterpolated()`, which still tries the direct exact-match `timeToCoordinate()` call first (covers the common same-timeframe case with zero added cost), then falls back to binary-searching the active series' own bars (converted to epoch via the existing `_timeToEpoch()`, so it works whether the active series uses `'YYYY-MM-DD'` strings or unix seconds) for the two bars bracketing the target epoch, and uses `logicalToCoordinate()` — which, unlike `timeToCoordinate()`, is defined continuously between and beyond bars — on the fractional logical index between them. This is the same technique TradingView/Bloomberg-class terminals use to keep a drawn object anchored to real time independent of the active chart's bar spacing.
- `_xForPoint()` now calls `_epochToXInterpolated()` instead of the raw `timeToCoordinate()` call; the `futureIndex` same-timeframe fallback for points drawn past the last real bar is unchanged.
- **Verified** with a standalone reproduction of the interpolation math against synthetic D1/W1/H4 bar arrays: a rectangle's D1 corner dates (2026-07-20, 2026-07-29) resolve to exact integer bar positions on D1 (as before), fractional-but-finite logical positions on W1 (7 and 8.29 — previously `null` on both, since neither date is a Monday), and exact integer positions on H4 (both dates fall on 4-hour boundaries).
- `node assets/dashboard.test.js` — 85/85 passing.
- Cache-buster bumped `assets/dashboard.js?v=8.86.5` → `?v=8.86.6` in `index.html`.

## v8.86.5 (2026-07-30) — Drawn objects now project to the same real-world time/price on EVERY timeframe, including H1/H4

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Context (Santiago, after v8.86.4's timeframe-group fix): "debería tener la misma ubicación en cada temporalidad el objeto incluyendo H1 y H4"** — the screenshots showed a rectangle at a completely different position/width between MN, W1, and D1. v8.86.4 only solved *disappearing* by grouping D1/W1/MN together and H1/H4 together (both groups still isolated from each other) — it did not make one object appear at the same coordinates across every group, and the screenshots predate that fix reaching the browser regardless (each rectangle shown was actually a separately hand-drawn object under the old per-exact-timeframe storage, not the same object misplaced).
- **Real fix:** drawing points are no longer stored in whatever raw time format the timeframe active at draw-time happened to produce (`'YYYY-MM-DD'` string for D1/W1/MN, unix seconds for H1/H4). Added `_timeToEpoch()` / `_epochToActiveTime()` — every point is now stored as universal unix-epoch seconds (UTC) and converted to whichever format the *currently active* timeframe's series needs only at render/hit-test time, inside `_xForPoint()` (the single read path used by every drawing/handle/hit-test routine) and `_resolveTimeAt()` (the single write path used by every create/move/resize/paste routine).
- **Storage key simplified from `${ohlcId}_${timeframe-group}` (v8.86.4) to just `${ohlcId}`** — with points now timeframe-independent, there's no longer a reason to split storage at all; one array per symbol covers all five timeframes.
- **Known, documented limitation:** a point drawn into the empty space *past* the last real bar (dragging beyond "now") still carries a `futureIndex` (a logical bar-count position) as a same-timeframe rendering fallback for the rare case `timeToCoordinate()` can't yet resolve a real-world future time. `futureIndex` is inherently timeframe-relative (bar density differs enormously between D1 and H1), so that specific fallback only applies on the timeframe the point was created on — a future-space point won't render on a different timeframe until enough real bars arrive to fill in behind it on that timeframe too. This does not affect any point anchored to real chart history (the normal case, including everything in Santiago's screenshots).
- Cache-buster bumped `assets/dashboard.js?v=8.86.4` → `?v=8.86.5` in `index.html`.

## v8.86.4 (2026-07-30) — Fix: drawn objects (trend line, Fib, rectangle) disappear when switching chart timeframe

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Root cause (reported by Santiago: a trend line drawn on EUR/USD D1 wasn't there after switching to W1):** drawings were persisted (in-memory `window._lwDrawings` + `localStorage['gi_drawings']`) under a key of `${ohlcId}_${_lwActiveTf}` — the *exact* timeframe, e.g. `eurusd_D1` vs `eurusd_W1` as two completely separate buckets. TradingView/MT5 convention is that an object drawn on a chart stays there when you change the interval; this codebase was scoping storage one level too narrow.
- **Fix:** re-keyed drawing storage to `${ohlcId}_${timeframe-group}` instead of the exact timeframe. D1/W1/MN form one group — they already share the same `'YYYY-MM-DD'` business-day bar format (see the `_jsonPath` resolution in `_renderLWChart`), so `lightweightCharts`' `timeToCoordinate()` can correctly project a D1-drawn shape's `{time, price}` points onto the W1/MN time axis. H1/H4 form a second group, since they use unix-timestamp bars instead — a different time type that D1/W1/MN's date strings can't be projected onto, so those two are intentionally kept separate rather than silently failing to render (`timeToCoordinate()` returns `null` for a mismatched time type, which would just make the shape invisible with no error).
- **Known limitation, accepted rather than solved here:** a shape drawn on H1/H4 will not appear on D1/W1/MN or vice versa — reconciling that would require converting between the two time representations (unix seconds ↔ date string) at draw-time and re-deriving each chart's coordinate mapping, which is a larger change than this fix's scope. Flagging in case Santiago wants that as a follow-up.
- **Not a data-loss concern:** old drawings saved under the previous per-exact-timeframe keys (e.g. `eurusd_D1`, `eurusd_W1` as separate entries) are simply orphaned under the old key strings in `localStorage['gi_drawings']` — they don't reappear under the new group key, but nothing is deleted; a "Clear all" per symbol will still only clear the active group's array.
- Cache-buster bumped `assets/dashboard.js?v=8.86.3` → `?v=8.86.4` in `index.html`.

## v8.86.3 (2026-07-30) — Force Area chart type for single-daily-print series (HY OAS, IG OAS, US10Y) in the local Lightweight Charts renderer

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Context (Santiago asked whether Candle or Area is the industry-standard chart type for VIX/MOVE and, by extension, the credit-spread OAS series):** confirmed VIX and MOVE both carry genuine intraday range — VIX is recalculated continuously from live SPX option prices, and MOVE was upgraded by ICE from end-of-day to near-intraday publication in 2020 (both are pulled via yfinance's native daily OHLC in `fetch_ohlc.py`, real bars, not synthetic) — so Candlestick default is correct and already matches Bloomberg/Barchart/TradingView convention for those two.
- **HY OAS / IG OAS / US10Y are different:** sourced from FRED, which publishes exactly one value per business day — no real intraday range exists, so any "candle" is a synthetic flat-body construction (`open` = prior close, `high`/`low` = `min`/`max(open, close)`), as already documented in the v8.86.0 entry above. The codebase already encoded this distinction for the TradingView-fallback path (`_LINE_STYLE_SYMS` in `_loadTVWidgetFallback`, forcing TradingView style `3`/Area for `FRED:DGS10`, `FRED:BAMLH0A0HYM2`, `FRED:BAMLC0A0CM`) — but the local `_renderLWChart` path, now primary since v8.86.0, had no equivalent and would render whatever `window._lwChartType` was last globally selected, including a misleading synthetic candle.
- **Fix:** added `_AREA_ONLY_IDS` (`us10y`, `hyoas`, `igoas`) and an `_effectiveChartType(ohlcId)` helper. Every read of the chart-type state inside `_renderLWChart`, `_updateLWHeader`, and the live-tick update paths (`_lwUpdateTodayBar`) now goes through this helper instead of reading `window._lwChartType` directly, so Area is forced whenever one of these three symbols is active — regardless of what type is globally selected for FX pairs/other instruments. The global selection itself is left untouched, so switching back to a normal symbol still respects the user's last Candle/Bar/Line/Area choice.
- **Candle/Bar buttons disabled (not just ignored)** while one of these three symbols is active, with a tooltip explaining why, so the toolbar doesn't offer a choice that would silently produce a fake candle. Re-enabled automatically on every render for all other symbols.
- Added `.lw-tb-btn:disabled` style (`assets/dashboard.css`-equivalent inline block in `index.html`) — dimmed, `cursor:not-allowed`, `pointer-events:none`.

## v8.86.2 (2026-07-30) — Fix: chart header shows "undefined" after switching chart type on HY/IG OAS (and MOVE, NOK/SEK pairs)

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Root cause (reported by Santiago: switching chart type on the HY OAS tile left the header reading "undefined · D1"):** `_updateLWHeader()` resolves the header symbol name as `_OHLC_FULL_NAMES[ohlcId] || label`. `label` is only supplied on the *first* render of a symbol (`_renderLWChart(ohlcId, label)` called from `loadTVChart()`); every subsequent re-render — chart-type switch, timeframe switch, PC/Vol/CB toggle, compare-overlay refresh — calls `_renderLWChart(_lwActiveOhlcId)` with no second argument, relying entirely on `_OHLC_FULL_NAMES` to supply the name. `hyoas` and `igoas` (added in v8.86.0) were never added to that map, so on any re-render both `_OHLC_FULL_NAMES[ohlcId]` and `label` were `undefined`, producing the literal string "undefined" in the header.
- **Same gap found for five other symbols already live on the site** (`move`, `usdnok`, `usdsek`, `eurnok`, `eursek`) — all missing from `_OHLC_FULL_NAMES`, all exhibiting the identical bug on re-render, just not yet reported.
- **Fix:** added all six missing entries to `_OHLC_FULL_NAMES` (`hyoas`, `igoas`, `move`, `usdnok`, `usdsek`, `eurnok`, `eursek`), verified by diffing every value in `_TV_TO_OHLC` against the keys of `_OHLC_FULL_NAMES` — zero symbols now fall through to the `label` fallback on re-render.
- **Process note:** any future symbol added to `_TV_TO_OHLC`/`_OHLC_LABELS` must be added to `_OHLC_FULL_NAMES` in the same change — the `label` parameter is a first-load-only convenience, not a durable name source.
- Cache-buster bumped `assets/dashboard.js?v=8.86.0` → `?v=8.86.2` in `index.html`.

## v8.86.1 (2026-07-30) — Fix: dashboard.js cache-buster stuck at v8.80.0, blocking the v8.85.0/v8.86.0 HY/IG OAS changes from reaching browsers

### Frontend — index.html

- **Root cause (reported by Santiago: HY/IG OAS tiles still not opening local charts after v8.86.0 was deployed and `ohlc-data/hyoas.json`/`igoas.json` confirmed live):** `assets/dashboard.js?v=8.80.0` — the cache-busting query string — was never bumped through v8.85.0 (tile content/click parity) or v8.86.0 (local OHLC), even though the file changed materially in both. Every other asset (`dashboard.css`, `cot-modal-chart.js`, `heatmap-modal.js`, etc.) has its own independently-bumped `?v=`; `dashboard.js`'s was stuck. Since GitHub Pages/its CDN cache static assets by exact URL, a browser or edge cache that had fetched `dashboard.js?v=8.80.0` before either deploy could keep serving that stale cached copy indefinitely under the same URL, even though the file's content on `main` was already correct — verified by diffing the committed file (has `_TV_TO_OHLC['FRED:BAMLH0A0HYM2']` etc.) against what a `?v=8.80.0`-keyed cache would still be holding.
- **Fix:** bumped to `assets/dashboard.js?v=8.86.0`, forcing every client to fetch the current file on next load.
- **Process gap:** the "Version management" convention (cache-busting query strings bumped alongside every JS change) was not followed in v8.85.0 or the v8.86.0 session that added credit-spread OHLC. Going forward, bumping `dashboard.js`'s `?v=` is part of the output checklist for any session that edits `assets/dashboard.js`, not an optional cleanup step.

## v8.86.0 (2026-07-30) — US HY OAS / US IG OAS charts: local Lightweight Charts history instead of TradingView fallback

### Scripts repo — `fetch_credit_spreads.py` (new, in `globalinvesting-scripts`)

- **New script**, following the same conventions as `fetch_ohlc.py` and `fetch_bond_yields.py`: a pure data-prep script that lives in `globalinvesting-scripts` and gets checked out (read-only, via `SCRIPTS_PAT`) into a step of `update-ohlc.yml` in the public repo.
- Fetches `BAMLH0A0HYM2` (US HY OAS) and `BAMLC0A0CM` (US IG OAS) from FRED and builds synthetic daily OHLC bars: `open` = prior day's close, `high`/`low` = `max`/`min(open, close)`, `close` = today's reading. FRED publishes one value per business day for these series — there is no real intraday range, so this is a thin/flat-bodied candle by construction, not a fabricated range.
- Values converted from FRED's native percentage points (e.g. `2.81`) to whole basis points (`281`), matching how HY/IG OAS are already read elsewhere on the site (`hyOasDelta20d`/`igOasDelta20d`, tile subtext `-14bp`).
- Output: `ohlc-data/hyoas.json`, `ohlc-data/igoas.json` — identical bar shape to every yfinance-sourced D1 file, so `_renderLWChart()` reads them through the same code path with no source-specific branching.
- **Not a new symbol inside `fetch_ohlc.py` itself**, because these two come from FRED (requires `FRED_API_KEY`), not yfinance — kept as a self-contained script rather than adding a second data-source branch to the yfinance-only script.
- **Full replace on every run, no incremental merge.** An earlier design (prototyped directly in `update_extended_data.py`, never merged) bootstrapped a deep 3-year FRED pull once and merged incrementally afterward, to avoid re-downloading history on every run. That concern doesn't apply here: a full FRED history pull is free/unmetered, and every other D1 symbol in `fetch_ohlc.py` already rebuilds its full file from scratch on every run rather than merging — this script matches that existing convention instead of introducing a second, more complex pattern.

### Site repo — `.github/workflows/update-ohlc.yml` (v2.0 → v2.1)

- New step "Fetch credit spread OHLC — FRED HY/IG OAS", calling `fetch_credit_spreads.py`, added right after the main "Fetch OHLC data" step.
- **Gated to the D1 finalization run only** (`30 1 * * 2-6`, or manual dispatch) — same `if` condition already used by the `calculate_technical_levels.py` step. FRED updates these two series once per business day with a lag, so running the fetch on the intraday 30-min ticks would repeat an identical request with no new data.
- `FRED_API_KEY` passed as an env var to this step only. The secret was already present in this (public site) repo, so no new secret needed to be added.

### Frontend — `assets/dashboard.js`

- `_TV_TO_OHLC`: added `'FRED:BAMLH0A0HYM2': 'hyoas'` and `'FRED:BAMLC0A0CM': 'igoas'` — `loadTVChart()` now resolves both to the local Lightweight Charts renderer instead of falling straight to the TradingView widget (v8.85.0's behavior, kept as the automatic fallback if `_renderLWChart` fails for any reason — e.g. before the first D1 run has populated the files).
- `_OHLC_LABELS`: added `hyoas: 'BAMLH0A0HYM2'`, `igoas: 'BAMLC0A0CM'` for the chart source footer.
- Decimal-precision map (both copies — the live-tick injector at `_lwUpdateTodayBar()` and the chart-open renderer): added `hyoas:0, igoas:0` (whole basis points, no decimals).
- `_LINE_STYLE_SYMS` in the TradingView-fallback path (`FRED:DGS10`, `FRED:BAMLH0A0HYM2`, `FRED:BAMLC0A0CM`) was **left unchanged** — it only affects the widget's chart style when `_renderLWChart` isn't used, and a line style is still the correct rendering for a single-fixing series in that fallback path.

### Testing

- `python3 -m py_compile fetch_credit_spreads.py` — clean.
- Simulated `build_ohlc()` against synthetic FRED-shaped input: verified the open/close chain, `high >= max(open, close)`, `low <= min(open, close)` for every bar, and correct oldest→newest ordering.
- `node -c assets/dashboard.js` — clean.
- `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` on `update-ohlc.yml` — clean.
- `node assets/dashboard.test.js` — 85/85 passed, no regressions.

## v8.84.1 (2026-07-30) — update_extended_data.py: per-currency expected-fields, fixing false "Missing" noise on every run

### Engine — scripts/update_extended_data.py

- **`EXPECTED_KEYS` was a single blanket list (`bond10y, bond2y, bond5y, vix, hyOas, igOas, inflationExpectations`) applied to all 8 currencies, but `bond2y`/`bond5y`/`vix`/`hyOas`/`igOas` are only ever fetched for a subset by design** (`bond2y`: USD/EUR/GBP/CAD; `bond5y`/`vix`/`hyOas`/`igOas`: USD only — see `fetch_bonds()` and the credit-spread/VIX blocks). Every run logged `⚠️ JPY/AUD/CHF/NZD: Missing: bond2y, bond5y, vix, hyOas, igOas` even though those currencies never had those fields — 7 of 8 currencies showed a false warning on every single run, burying any genuine miss (e.g. a real GBP/CAD 2Y fetch failure) in noise that looked identical every day.
- **Fix:** replaced the blanket list with `_expected_keys_for(curr)`, built from the same per-currency scoping the fetchers already use (`_BOND2Y_CCYS = {USD, EUR, GBP, CAD}`, `_BOND5Y_CCYS = {USD}`, `_USD_ONLY_KEYS = [vix, hyOas, igOas]`). Verified against the exact field-availability from the 2026-07-30 19:5x UTC production run pasted by Santiago: JPY/AUD/CHF/NZD now report ✅ clean; GBP/CAD correctly still report `⚠️ Missing: bond2y` for the run where their 2Y fetch genuinely failed.
- **Not touched:** `monitor_data_health.py`'s own health checks (`check_bond_yields`) were already correctly scoped to USD-only for `bond2y`/`bond5y`/`vix` — this was purely a log-message issue local to `update_extended_data.py`'s own per-run summary, not a real data-health gap.

## v8.84.0 (2026-07-30) — Fix: update_extended_data.py was overwriting inflationExpectations daily, breaking Real Rate Carry Analysis for 6/10 G10 currencies

### Engine — scripts/update_extended_data.py (v14.0 → v14.1)

- **Root cause:** reactivating `update-extended-data.yml` in v14.0 (2026-07-28, for the new Credit Spreads panel) also silently reactivated this script's own internal `fetch_inflation_expectations()` — a second, inferior writer for a field (`inflationExpectations`) that already had an authoritative owner: `update-inflation-expectations.yml` (weekly, `globalinvesting-scripts` repo, full G10 via IMF SDMX/OECD/BOE/RBNZ/FRED). Both scripts do a full-file overwrite of `extended-data/{CCY}.json`, so the daily job clobbered the weekly job's correct data every morning at 06:00 UTC.
- **User-visible effect (caught by Santiago via the Real Rate Carry Analysis modal, JPY showing `—`):** JPY inflation expectation was `null` (this script's own World Bank fallback has no JPY series; FRED's JPY CPI series ended in 2021). GBP, AUD, CAD, CHF, NZD were silently replaced with World Bank annual figures up to 18 months stale — several with a **fabricated placeholder date** (`wb_latest()` returned `"{year}-06-15"`, not the real observation date) — flipping the sign of the real-rate calculation for AUD (-1.15% shown vs. +0.39% correct) and GBP (-0.15% shown vs. +0.91% correct), among others. NOK/SEK were unaffected (not in this script's `CURRENCIES` list); USD/EUR were roughly correct (both scripts independently hit the same FRED series).
- **Fix — single writer, not a smarter merge:** removed `fetch_inflation_expectations()`, `_index_to_yoy()`, `wb_latest()`, `WB_BASE`, and the entire calendar-extractor block that only existed to enrich this field (`CALENDAR_INFLEXP_PATTERNS`, `_calendar_extract()`, `_load_calendar()`, `_parse_cal_value()`, `fetch_calendar_supplements()` — all dead code once their sole consumer was gone). `_jgb_auction_from_calendar()` (JPY bond10y fallback, a genuinely live consumer of `calendar-data/calendar.json`) was updated to read the calendar file directly instead of delegating to the now-removed `_load_calendar()`. The script now **preserves** `data.inflationExpectations`/`dates.inflationExpectations` from the existing file on disk when it rewrites each `extended-data/{CCY}.json`, instead of recomputing them. `update-extended-data.yml`'s header comment and commit message were updated to describe the field as preserved, not fetched.
- **Verification:** `py_compile` clean. Simulated the preserve-block standalone against a present value (NOK), a present-but-null value (JPY), and a missing file (synthetic ccy) — all three behave correctly (kept, kept-as-null, defaulted-to-null-with-today's-date respectively).

### GUIDELINES.md

- **New rule: "Single writer per field — cross-workflow overwrite"** (§ Data integrity), documenting this incident and the general principle: before adding, duplicating, or reactivating any fetch step in any of the three repos, grep all three repos for existing writers of the same JSON key. A field with an established owner gets either preserved (if the second script's write pattern is full-file overwrite) or transferred outright — never run two live fetchers for the same field in parallel.

### Testing

- `python3 -m py_compile scripts/update_extended_data.py` — clean.
- Confirmed no remaining references to removed names (`wb_latest`, `_index_to_yoy`, `fetch_inflation_expectations`, `_load_calendar`, `_calendar_extract`, `_parse_cal_value`, `CALENDAR_INFLEXP_PATTERNS`, `fetch_calendar_supplements`) outside of docstring/comment notes.
- `CURRENCIES`, `EXPECTED_KEYS`, and the missing-field warning logic left unchanged — `inflationExpectations` is still an expected key, just no longer computed here.

## v8.80.0 (2026-07-29) — Drawings no longer render over the price-scale ribbon

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js

- **Trend lines/rectangles/Fib guides painted on top of the right-side price-scale labels when dragged into that area:** `_drawOverlay` (the SVG that renders every drawing) is a plain `position:absolute` sibling spanning the full `chartDiv` at `z-index:3`, on top of Lightweight Charts' own price-scale and time-scale widgets by construction — there's no native way to tell LWC to paint the scale above arbitrary DOM content. Fixed by clipping the overlay to the chart's actual plotting area via CSS `clip-path: inset()`, computed fresh on every `_renderDrawings()` call from `chart.priceScale('right').width()` and `chart.timeScale().height()` — both queried live rather than hardcoded, since the price scale's width isn't fixed (it grows with the digit count of the active symbol's price format, e.g. USDJPY vs EURUSD) and the time-axis height can shift slightly with font metrics. Matches TradingView/MT5/Bloomberg, where drawings always tuck under the scale rather than over it.

### Testing

- `node assets/dashboard.test.js` — 85/85 pass.

## v8.79.0 (2026-07-29) — Fixed chart layout/drawing distortion after exiting fullscreen

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js

- **Chart came back from fullscreen with the oscillator strip squashed and drawings sitting off their anchored candles:** two independent effects compounded into the reported "todo desproporcionado y corrido." (1) Oscillator sub-panes (RSI, MACD, Stochastic, etc.) get a fixed pixel height via `pane.setHeight(80` or `90)` when built (`_buildIndicatorPane`), but Lightweight Charts does not treat that as a hard floor across `chart.resize()` — a large total-height swing (leaving fullscreen: ~900px tall → ~290px) proportionally rescales every pane, including ones with an explicit `setHeight()`. This is a known library limitation (`tradingview/lightweight-charts#1847`), not something fixable via chart options. (2) The drawing overlay (`_renderDrawings`) only re-projects on `timeScale().subscribeVisibleTimeRangeChange` — i.e. pan/zoom — but a `resize()` changes the main pane's price-scale pixel mapping without necessarily firing that event (the visible *time* range is unchanged), so every trend line, rectangle, and Fib guide stayed rendered at its pre-resize pixel position, reading as "shifted" relative to the candles it was anchored to.
- **Fix:** new `_lwReapplyPaneHeights()` re-applies `setHeight(80/90)` to every active oscillator pane, and new `_lwReprojectDrawings()` re-runs the drawing overlay's coordinate projection (via the already-exposed `window._lwRenderDrawings`). Both now run immediately after every `_lwChart.resize()` call in the file: the fullscreen open/close handlers, the responsive `ResizeObserver`, and the exclusive-panel-closed repaint (`_repaintAfterExclusivePanelClosed`) — so the fix also covers window resizes and split-layout panel toggles, not just fullscreen, on the same root cause. The fullscreen open/close resize calls additionally pass `forceRepaint:true` to `chart.resize()` so the corrected layout paints on the same frame instead of one frame after the old (wrong) proportions would otherwise have been visible.
- **Also exposed:** `window._indPaneIndex` (previously a closure-local variable inside `_renderLWChart`, inaccessible from the top-level fullscreen handlers) so `_lwReapplyPaneHeights()` can look up which pane index belongs to which active oscillator.

### Testing

- `node assets/dashboard.test.js` — 85/85 pass.

## v8.78.0 (2026-07-29) — Drawing tools: Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V copy-paste, and free drawing/moving past the last candle

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js

- **Couldn't draw or move an object past the last real candle (or a few bars into the rightOffset margin):** every drawing-tool coordinate conversion went through Lightweight Charts' `timeScale().coordinateToTime()`/`timeToCoordinate()`, which only resolve pixel positions that map onto an actual bar's timestamp — plus a short internally-extrapolated stretch inside the chart's `rightOffset` margin, and nothing beyond that. Any drag past that point silently returned `null` and was ignored, so a trend line, rectangle, or Fibonacci guide couldn't be drawn (or moved) into the empty space to the right of "now" — unlike TradingView, MT5, or Bloomberg, which all allow drawing freely into the future. Fixed with a new fallback pair, `_resolveTimeAt()`/`_xForPoint()`: when the native time lookup comes back `null`, they fall back to `coordinateToLogical()`/`logicalToCoordinate()` — LWC APIs that are defined *continuously*, with no data-range limit — and derive a synthetic bar time from the logical index (`_extrapolateTimeForIndex()`: whole-interval steps for H1/H4's numeric timestamps; real calendar-day arithmetic, skipping Sat/Sun, for D1's date-string bars; +7 days for W1; +1 month for MN). The absolute logical index is kept on the point (`futureIndex`) so a drawing anchored in the future stays pinned to that exact slot even as new real bars arrive and fill in behind it — it doesn't drift. All 8 render/hit-test/toolbar-positioning call sites, plus drag-move and the initial-drag distance check, now go through this pair instead of calling the native APIs directly.
- **New: Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V copies and pastes the selected drawing** — same clipboard convention as MT5's chart objects (and any other on-screen element). Ctrl+C stores a deep clone of the selected object on `window._lwDrawClipboard`; Ctrl+V pastes a duplicate offset by a fixed 24px down-right (so it doesn't land exactly on top of the original and look like nothing happened — same convention as pasting a duplicate shape in PowerPoint/Illustrator), auto-selects the new copy, and persists it via the existing `_saveDrawings()` path. The paste offset itself goes through the same future-space fallback above, so copy-pasting a shape that's already near the right edge works correctly. Works with Cmd+C/Cmd+V on Mac. The Draw ▾ dropdown's footer hint now mentions the shortcut.

### Testing

- `node assets/dashboard.test.js` — 85/85 pass.

## v8.77.0 (2026-07-29) — Oscillator reference levels now edge-to-edge and user-editable (industry standard)

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js

- **Reference levels (RSI 30/50/70, Stoch 20/50/80, CCI ±100, etc.) weren't reliably reaching the right edge of the pane:** `_addRefLines()` previously drew each level as its own trailing `LineSeries`, plotting one flat data point per historical bar and slicing to a trailing window (`s.data.length + 10` bars). That's a data-bound approach — correct in the common case, but fragile: any mismatch between the closure's `bars` snapshot and what's actually rendered (stale re-render, timeframe edge cases) leaves the ref line's last data point short of the chart's true last bar. Replaced with Lightweight Charts' native `series.createPriceLine()` API, called on the oscillator's own value series. Native price lines are computed from the price scale, not from a bounded array of per-bar points, so they always span the full width of the pane by construction — this is also how TradingView, MT5, and Bloomberg draw overbought/oversold/zero lines. Removing an indicator now calls `series.removePriceLine()` on each tracked line instead of `chart.removeSeries()`.
- **New: editable levels.** Every oscillator that has reference levels (RSI, Stochastic, CCI, Williams %R, MFI, Ultimate Oscillator, Choppiness, MACD/ROC/Momentum/AO/TRIX/DPO/CMF zero-lines, ADX, Aroon — 16 series across the catalogue) now exposes one small numeric input per level in its expanded row in the Indicators ▾ dropdown, right next to the existing period/smoothing params — matching TradingView/MT5's "Levels" tab convention. Edits persist to `localStorage` (`gi_ind_levels`, mirroring the existing `gi_ind_params` pattern) and survive symbol/timeframe switches and page reloads. A default-values lookup (`_IND_LEVEL_DEFAULTS`) is the single source of truth for both the level lines' defaults and the edit UI; user overrides are only honored when the saved array length still matches the current defaults, so a future addition/removal of a level for some indicator can't silently misalign with stale localStorage.

### Testing

- `node assets/dashboard.test.js` — 85/85 pass.

## v8.76.1 (2026-07-29) — Draw ▾ dropdown was expanding to near full viewport width on mobile

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js

- **Root cause:** the Draw ▾ panel (`_openDrawDropdown`) declared `min-width:210px` but no `max-width`. Its footer hint ("Click a drawing to select it. Drag its body to move, drag an endpoint to resize...") is a single long sentence with no forced line break. For a `position:fixed`, auto-width block, the browser's shrink-to-fit algorithm sizes the box to `min(available width, preferred one-line width)` — since the preferred one-line width of that sentence vastly exceeds a phone's available width, the panel was sized to essentially the full viewport instead of wrapping the text within a normal dropdown column. Fixed by adding `max-width:260px`, which forces the footer (and option descriptions) to wrap normally like any other text, matching the panel's intended TradingView-style dropdown proportions on both desktop and mobile.

## v8.76.0 (2026-07-29) — Mobile fixes: drawing tools now commit live via touch, dropdown toggles actually close, narrative text collapses

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js, index.html

- **Mobile drawing tools weren't rendering live, only after leaving the chart:** root cause was that `chartDiv` (our wrapper around Lightweight Charts' own canvas) never declared `touch-action`, so on touch devices the browser's native gesture recognizer could claim a finger-drag as a page-scroll before our pointer handlers ever saw continuous movement. `_setChartPannable(false)` on `pointerdown` disables LWC's *internal* pan handling but doesn't touch the browser's touch-action decision, and calling `preventDefault()` inside the pointerdown listener doesn't reliably stop a scroll gesture that's already been granted to the browser at touch-start. Net effect: `pointermove` was suppressed for the whole gesture (no live preview), and the shape only committed on `pointerup` — wherever the finger happened to lift, typically outside the chart bounds after the page had scrolled. Fix: `touch-action:none` added directly to `chartDiv`'s inline style at creation. Since CSS `touch-action` is the *intersection* of an element and its ancestors, this restricts the whole subtree (including LWC's own canvas) regardless of what LWC declares on it, forcing the entire gesture to be handled via JS pointer events from the start — which is what both LWC's own panning and our drawing tools already do internally, so nothing else changes.
- **Indicators ▾ and Draw ▾ dropdowns couldn't be closed by tapping the toggle button again:** both use the same pattern — a `document`-level `mousedown` listener (added via `setTimeout(…, 0)` right after opening) closes the popup on any outside interaction. The bug: that listener didn't exclude the toggle button itself, and `mousedown` fires *before* `click`. So tapping the button while the dropdown was open would (1) close it via the `mousedown` listener, then (2) immediately reopen it via the button's own `click` handler (`_open…Dropdown()`, which is a toggle) — the dropdown could visually never be closed from the button, only by tapping elsewhere. Fixed by having the outside-close handler check `btn.contains(e.target)` and bail out when the mousedown originated on the toggle button, leaving that case entirely to the button's own click-toggle.
- **Narrative paragraph too long on mobile:** the AI narrative (now 5-7 sentences at institutional density, see v8.62.0) was rendering unclamped in the `#narrative` panel at the top of every page, pushing the chart and everything below it far down the screen on a phone. `#narrative-text` is now CSS-clamped to 3 lines (`-webkit-line-clamp:3`) inside the existing `@media(max-width:900px)` block only — desktop is unaffected. A new `#narr-more-btn` ("Show more"/"Show less") sits below the text; it's hidden by default and only revealed via `_syncNarrativeClamp()` (called after every narrative update and, debounced, on resize/orientation-change) when the rendered text actually overflows the 3-line clamp, so short narratives never show a pointless toggle. Clicking it toggles a `.narr-expanded` class that lifts the clamp.

### Testing

- `node assets/dashboard.test.js` — 85/85 pass (unchanged; these are UI/mobile fixes with no coverage in the deterministic-math suite, verified manually against the reported repro instead).

## v8.75.0 (2026-07-29) — Drawing tools: select/move/resize instead of click-to-delete, per-object color picker

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js

- **Click no longer deletes:** replaced click-to-delete with the TradingView/MT5/Bloomberg convention — a plain click on a drawing now **selects** it (shown with a soft outline highlight plus two square grab handles at its endpoints) and leaves it untouched. Clicking empty chart space deselects; deletion moved entirely into the new floating toolbar (see below) and the Delete/Backspace key.
- **Move:** dragging the body of a selected object (anywhere along a trend line, inside a rectangle, or on the Fibonacci swing guide) translates the whole shape. Implemented via pixel-space delta translation (capture start/current pointer position in screen pixels, apply the delta to both endpoints' on-screen coordinates, then convert back through `coordinateToTime`/`coordinateToPrice`) rather than arithmetic on the stored time/price values directly — this sidesteps `BusinessDay` objects on D1/W1/MN timeframes, which aren't numeric and can't be added to like an intraday `UTCTimestamp` can.
- **Resize:** the two square handles at p1/p2 are independently draggable (8px hit-radius, checked before body/move hit-testing so a handle grab always wins over a move). Dragging a handle sets that endpoint directly to the cursor's chart position — for Fibonacci this live-recalculates all 7 levels against the new swing range, exactly like drag-to-create.
- **New floating toolbar:** appears above the selection (flips below if there's no room above the visible chart area) with six preset color swatches, a native color-picker swatch for any exact custom shade, and a trash-icon delete button (inline SVG, not an emoji — see GUIDELINES.md "No emojis"). Swatches show an outline ring on the object's current color. The toolbar is a `position:fixed` DOM node repositioned every render while a selection is active, following the object through pan/zoom/move/resize/live-tick updates the same way `_lwRenderDrawings` already re-projects the shapes themselves.
- **Delete/Backspace key** removes the selected object as a keyboard-accessible equivalent to the toolbar's trash button (ignored while focus is on an `input`/`textarea`/contenteditable element elsewhere on the page). Esc now does double duty: cancels an armed-but-not-yet-drawn tool (unchanged from v8.74.0), or deselects the current selection if no tool is armed.
- Arming a new tool (Trend Line/Fibonacci/Rectangle from the Draw ▾ menu) or using "Clear All Drawings" now clears any existing selection and hides the toolbar first, so a stale toolbar can never point at an object that's mid-recreation or gone.
- Added a short usage hint to the bottom of the Draw ▾ dropdown ("Click a drawing to select it. Drag its body to move, drag an endpoint to resize...") since the interaction model changed from the previous click-to-delete convention.
- A leftover toolbar DOM node from a prior render pass (symbol/timeframe switch) is swept on every rebuild of the drawing-tools block, since selection state — and therefore the code path that would otherwise hide it — resets to "nothing selected" on each rebuild.

## v8.74.1 (2026-07-29) — Drawing drag was collapsing to a single point (root cause of Rectangle drawing nothing)

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js

- **Root cause:** v8.74.0's drag tracking sourced its live coordinates from `subscribeCrosshairMove`, but Lightweight Charts' own pan-handling latches onto a pressed-mouse-move gesture the instant `pointerdown` reaches its *internal* (target-phase) listener on the canvas — which fires before our `chartDiv`-level (bubble-phase) listener could disable panning. Once that internal pan/drag state activates, `crosshairMove` stops firing for the rest of the gesture. The practical effect: the anchor point and every subsequent "live" point were read from the same single crosshair snapshot taken just before the drag started, so every drawing committed with `p1 === p2` — a zero-length drag. Visually this showed up differently per tool: Trend Line collapsed to a single overlapping dot (the two endpoint circles drawn on top of each other), Fibonacci showed all 7 levels stacked unreadably at the same price (since `priceHigh === priceLow` gives a zero range), and Rectangle rendered a literal 0×0 box — invisible, i.e. "no dibuja nada." It only ever appeared to "work" after leaving and re-entering the chart because that generates a fresh, unambiguous `crosshairMove` call once the stuck internal pan state let go.
- **Fix:** replaced the crosshair-sourced coordinates with direct conversion from the pointer event's own `clientX`/`clientY` against `chartDiv`'s bounding rect (`timeScale().coordinateToTime()` / `series.coordinateToPrice()`), so the drag no longer depends on `crosshairMove` firing at all. `pointerdown` is now registered on the **capture phase** (`{capture: true}`) so panning is disabled *before* Lightweight Charts' own handler ever sees the event, preventing the internal pan latch in the first place. A new document-level `pointermove` listener (de-duplicated the same way as the existing `pointerup` listener, so repeated symbol/timeframe switches don't accumulate stale listeners) drives the live preview continuously and independently of the chart's own crosshair state.
- Verified: all three tools (Trend Line, Fibonacci, Rectangle) now track the full drag distance and commit the actual dragged shape rather than a collapsed point.

## v8.74.0 (2026-07-29) — Drawing tools: click-and-drag, Rectangle tool, bounded Fibonacci width

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js

- **Fibonacci no longer spans the full chart width:** v8.73.1 fixed the axis-label collision by switching Fibonacci levels to `series.createPriceLine()`, but that API always draws a line across the *entire* chart — it has no way to bound a line's horizontal extent, which is exactly what produced the "Fibonacci occupies the whole chart" report. Reverted to hand-drawn SVG lines, this time correctly bounded between the two x-coordinates the user actually drags (`xLeft`..`xRight`) — the width is now literally whatever the user defines by dragging, matching the request ("un ancho definible"). Level labels sit just past the box's right edge instead of at the chart's axis, so they no longer collide with the price scale or the live price tag.
- **Click-and-drag replaces click-two-points:** all three tools now use the industry-standard press-drag-release gesture (TradingView/Bloomberg/MT5) instead of click-then-click. Implemented via `subscribeCrosshairMove` for live, chart-native coordinates plus a `pointerdown`/`pointerup` pair to detect the press and release; chart panning/zooming (`handleScroll`/`handleScale`) is temporarily disabled for the duration of the drag so a press-drag on the canvas draws instead of panning the chart, then restored on release. A drag under 8px is treated as an accidental tap and discarded (the tool stays armed to retry) rather than committing a zero-size shape.
- **Real-time preview while dragging:** the shape being drawn (including all 7 Fibonacci level lines/labels, recalculated live) now follows the cursor and updates on every `crosshairMove` event during the drag, rendered with a dashed preview style until release commits it — directly addresses "la línea o fibo se dibujen en tiempo real."
- **New: Rectangle tool** — drag to mark a price/time zone, rendered as a semi-transparent filled box with a solid border; same persistence, live-tick redraw, and click-to-delete (clicking anywhere inside the box, not just its border) as the other two tools.
- **Esc cancels** an armed or mid-drag tool without drawing anything, restoring normal chart panning immediately (previously the only way out of an armed tool was to complete a drawing).
- `window._lwDrawDocPointerUp` / `window._lwDrawEscHandler` are stored on `window` and de-duplicated (old listener removed before a new one is attached) on every chart re-render, so switching symbol/timeframe repeatedly doesn't accumulate stale `document`-level listeners — the previous click-based version only needed a chart-scoped `subscribeClick`, which doesn't leak this way, so this is new since drag detection needs a `document`-level `pointerup` to catch releases outside the chart.

### Frontend — index.html

- "Rectangle" entry added to the Draw ▾ menu alongside Trend Line and Fibonacci Retracement (menu-only change; `#lw-draw-btn` markup unchanged from v8.73.0).

## v8.73.1 (2026-07-29) — Drawing tools: native Fibonacci price lines, real-time redraw

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js

- **Fibonacci levels no longer overlap the price axis or the live price tag:** the v8.73.0 implementation hand-drew each Fibonacci level as an absolutely-positioned `<line>` + `<text>` spanning the full chart width, recomputed from scratch on every pan/zoom. The text sat wherever the math placed it, with no awareness of the native price-scale labels or the live price tag next to it — on screens with several levels close together (e.g. 50%/61.8%/78.6% near the current price) the hand-drawn labels visually collided with the axis labels and with each other, exactly as flagged with screenshots. Replaced with Lightweight Charts' native `series.createPriceLine()`: each Fibonacci level is now a real price line, rendered and labeled by the library in the same lane as every other axis label, which is the same mechanism TradingView/Bloomberg use to avoid this collision. `_syncFibPriceLines()` creates/removes price lines to stay in sync with `_curDrawings()` (add, click-to-delete, Clear All); the diagonal swing line itself (the line connecting the two clicked points) still renders on the lightweight SVG overlay, now dashed to visually distinguish it from the solid/dotted Fibonacci level lines.
- **Real-time redraw was wired but never invoked:** `window._lwRenderDrawings` was exposed in v8.73.0 for exactly this purpose but no caller was added before the prior session ended, so the Trend Line diagonal only re-projected on pan/zoom (`subscribeVisibleTimeRangeChange`), not on a live tick that widens the autoscaled price range without changing the visible time range. Added a call to `window._lwRenderDrawings()` at the end of both live-bar paths in `_lwUpdateTodayBar()` (H1/H4 partial-bar block and the D1/W1/MN today-bar block), so an open Trend Line stays correctly projected as new ticks arrive — matching the "se dibujen en tiempo real" request. The Fibonacci levels didn't need this call: native price lines already track the axis on every live tick with zero polling from us.
- **Efficiency:** the native price-line approach removes the per-pan/zoom re-computation and re-stringify-to-SVG of up to 7 level lines + labels per Fibonacci drawing; the library only needs to reposition an existing line object, and the SVG overlay itself now only carries the diagonal swing lines (Trend Line + Fibonacci swing), not the levels.

## v8.73.0 (2026-07-29) — Live-bar header desync fix; new Trend Line / Fibonacci drawing tools

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js

- **Root-caused the "incorrect rendering" reported with screenshots:** on H1/H4 charts, `_lwCandleSeries.update(_liveBar)` runs unconditionally on every RT tick, but the O/H/L/C header text only refreshed when `_rt.pct != null`. Any tick that delivered a valid `close` without a `pct` value (a momentary gap in that field, not a stale connection) left the header frozen at its last value while the plotted candle kept growing — exactly the mismatch in the screenshots, where the live candle visibly spiked well above the header's stale High. Decoupled the two: the header now always refreshes from the live bar on every tick; only the %/change override passed to it is conditional on `_rt.pct` being present. `_updateLWHeader()` already had a working fallback path for computing %/chg without an override (via `_prevCloseMap`), so no other behavior changes.
- **New: Drawing Tools (Trend Line, Fibonacci Retracement)** — industry-standard click-two-points UX (TradingView/Bloomberg/MT5 convention): pick a tool from the new "Draw" toolbar menu, click the first anchor, click the second, the drawing commits. Fibonacci Retracement renders the standard ratio set (0, 23.6, 38.2, 50, 61.8, 78.6, 100%) with the 0% level anchored to whichever point was clicked first (matches TradingView/MT5 convention), each level labeled with its price. Drawings persist per symbol+timeframe in `localStorage` (`gi_drawings`) — a line on EUR/USD H1 doesn't appear on GBP/USD or the Daily chart. Rendered as an SVG overlay synced to `timeToCoordinate`/`priceToCoordinate` on every pan/zoom, the same pattern already used for the CB meeting-markers overlay. Click-to-delete: clicking directly on an existing line or Fibonacci level (when no tool is armed) removes it — avoids building a separate selection/handle UI. "Clear All Drawings" is available in the same menu when the active chart has any.
- **New toolbar button:** `#lw-draw-btn` ("Draw ▾") added next to the Indicators button, same markup/behavior pattern (dropdown menu, `aria-expanded`, clone-to-clear-listeners on re-render).

### Frontend — index.html

- Added `#lw-draw-btn` to the chart toolbar, positioned immediately after `#lw-ind-btn`. No new DOM element added inside `#tv-chart-wrap` (its `innerHTML` is wiped on every `_renderLWChart()` call) — the SVG drawing overlay is instead created dynamically in `dashboard.js` on each render, same as the existing CB-markers overlay.

## v8.72.5 (2026-07-29) — Price Chart / Indicators panel bugfix batch

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js

- **Oscillator default colors:** RSI, Williams %R, TRIX, DPO, Ultimate Oscillator, ATR, Choppiness, and OBV were each assigned a distinct color (purple, orange, purple, orange, green, orange, blue-gray, indigo) from `_IND_CATALOGUE`. Changed all eight to light blue (`#64b5f6`) per request. ADX's own line (index 0 of its 3-color set) changed from red (`#f44336`) to light blue as well, while `+DI`/`-DI` (`#26a69a`/`#ef5350`) are unchanged, so ADX stays visually distinct from its own DI lines rather than because of a color clash with the other oscillators.
- **Oscillator level-line color:** the reference bands (overbought/oversold thresholds — RSI 30/70, Stochastic 20/80, Williams %R -20/-80, CCI ±100, ADX 25, Aroon, etc.) used `rgba(239,83,80,0.3)` (red) for every threshold line across 8 indicators. Changed to `rgba(158,161,170,0.35)` (light gray) on all 8 occurrences. The Ichimoku Cloud's own red span fill (a different visual element, not an oscillator threshold) was left untouched.
- **VWAP reset bug:** `_calcIndData('vwap', ...)` accumulated `cumTPV`/`cumV` across the entire loaded `bars` array with no reset, so on any timeframe holding more than one session (i.e., every timeframe except a single intraday day) the running average degenerated into what looked like an extremely long-period moving average instead of a daily VWAP — worse on H1 because more bars accumulate before the average can move. Fixed by resetting both cumulative sums at every UTC calendar-day boundary (`Math.floor(bar.time / 86400)`), matching the indicator's own catalogue description ("VWAP · daily sessions"). `bar.time` is already a unix timestamp for both the daily and H1/H4 loaders.
- **Pane divider too white:** the horizontal line separating the price pane from an oscillator pane (RSI, MACD, ADX, etc.) was rendered by Lightweight Charts' own default `layout.panes.separatorColor`, which was never set — so it fell back to the library's default, a near-white color that stood out sharply against the dark theme. Added `panes: { separatorColor: _themeColorAlpha('--border', 0.6), separatorHoverColor: _themeColorAlpha('--text2', 0.25), enableResize: true }` to the chart's `layout` config so the divider matches the theme's border color instead.
- **Indicators dropdown scroll jump on click:** `_openIndDropdown()` is called at 3 sites to fully rebuild the dropdown after a state change (indicator on/off toggle, `+ Add MA`, remove MA) — each site did `pop.remove(); _openIndDropdown();`, which recreates the panel `<div>` from scratch and always mounts it at `scrollTop: 0`. Clicking any indicator checkbox therefore snapped the whole list back to the top instead of staying where the user was. Added an optional `preserveScrollTop` parameter to `_openIndDropdown()`, captured as `pop.scrollTop` immediately before each of the 3 `pop.remove()` calls and restored on the rebuilt panel right after it's appended to `document.body`.
- **Moving Averages line-width `<select>` too narrow:** the per-MA line-width dropdown (`widthSelect`, values like "1px", "2px") was fixed at `width:36px`, too narrow to fit its own selected text next to the browser's native dropdown arrow — the text visibly clipped/overlapped the arrow. Widened to `width:50px`.
- **Indicators dropdown clipped on mobile:** horizontal positioning only enforced an 8px left-edge margin (`pop.style.left = Math.max(8, rect.left)`), with no check against the right edge. On mobile, where the "Indicators" button sits near the right side of the toolbar, the panel's `min-width:300px` pushed its right side past the viewport with no way to reach it — the fixed-position panel doesn't scroll horizontally. Added a right-edge clamp using `pop.offsetWidth` so the panel is pulled back in from the right with the same 8px margin whenever it would otherwise overflow.

## v8.72.4 (2026-07-29) — Root-caused why entity corruption survived the v8.72.3 fix: rolling carry-forward re-propagates pre-fix values

### Bugfix — `fetch_ff_calendar.py` (scripts repo)

- **Investigation trigger:** verifying the v8.72.3 fix live, `ff_calendar.json` generated 2026-07-29T18:29 (well after v3.36 shipped) still contained 48 fields with raw HTML entities (`&#163;`, `&#8364;`), all on events dated on or before 2026-07-16.
- **Root cause:** v3.36 decoded entities only at the point of *extraction* (RSS/HTML parsers). This file also keeps a rolling `LOOKBACK_DAYS` accumulation across runs — every run reloads its own previous output (`prev_events`) and re-appends any event not covered by the current fetch window (Step 2 historical merge, Step 2a actual carry-forward, Step 1b Worker KV inject). Events written before v3.36 already had undecoded entities baked into `actual`/`forecast`/`previous`; the merge/carry-forward code copied those dicts through verbatim on every subsequent run, with no re-decode. The corruption wasn't stale data waiting to age out — it was being actively re-written into every fresh `ff_calendar.json`.
- **Fix:** added `_redecode_entities()` (wraps `html.unescape()`, a no-op on already-clean strings) and applied it at all three points a value can enter `fresh` from a non-fresh-extraction source: the Step 2 historical merge, the Step 2a actual carry-forward, and the Step 1b Worker KV payload (`kv_map` construction — the Worker's own KV can still hold actuals cached before `calendar-watcher.js` v5.11's fix). This self-heals the rolling history over the next run(s) instead of requiring a separate one-off backfill script.
- **Companion fix:** `main()`'s startup print still read `v3.34` despite the module header reading `v3.36` — the same version-sync-drift class v3.36 itself flagged and fixed in the header two entries ago; the runtime `print()` literal a few hundred lines down was missed. Bumped to v3.37, both locations now match.
- **Verification:** unit-tested `_redecode_entities()` against the exact corrupted production event (`Germany Balance of Trade`, `&#8364;19.1B` → `€19.1B`). `python3 -m py_compile` and `ast.parse` clean.

### Bugfix — `fetch_economic_calendar.py` (scripts repo)

- **Root cause (same class, second location):** this script's own Step 3 historical merge (`load_previous_calendar()` → `fresh.append(ev)`) has the identical carry-forward-without-re-decode pattern, independently of `fetch_ff_calendar.py`. Confirmed live: production `calendar.json` (generated 2026-07-29T15:27) held 99 corrupted fields across dates back to 2026-06-12 — most from event types (`Goods Trade Balance`, `Balance of Trade`, `BoE Consumer Credit`, `Mortgage Lending`) that are recent releases, not aged-out history.
- **Second, related finding from the same audit:** `calendar.json`'s `events` array was found to mix two schemas — the legacy schema (`currency`/`event`/`dateISO`/`hourUTC`/`actual`/`forecast`/`previous`/`impact`/`importance`/`source`) predating the v3.0 rewrite (pre-2026-05-23 investing.com/direct-Myfxbook-HTML scraper), and `ff_to_cal_event()`'s current output (`date`/`dateISO`/`timeUTC`/`country`/`currency`/`flag`/`event`/`impact`/`actual`/`forecast`/`previous`). **Correction to this entry's first draft:** the legacy `hourUTC` schema is the *majority* (3196 of 3716 events in the audited production file), not a minority — the current pipeline has only been live ~2 months (since 2026-05-23) against `MAX_HISTORY_DAYS=365` of retained history, so older investing.com-era rows still dominate by volume even though they're no longer being freshly written. `assets/dashboard.js`'s calendar fingerprint (~line 9717) reads `ev.timeUTC` only, so all 3196 legacy-schema rows currently in production display a blank time until they age out.
- **Third finding — surpriseStats was also corrupted, not just display values:** `_parse_num()` in this script uses the identical "strip everything except digits" strategy as `dashboard.js`'s `_parseNum()` (by design, documented in its own docstring as required to stay in sync). `compute_surprise_stats()` runs `_parse_num()` over the same `actual`/`forecast` strings used for display, so the entity corruption fed directly into the z-score baseline. Confirmed by recomputing `surpriseStats` against the repaired events: `EUR/balance of trade` mean surprise corrected from -16730.29 to -2.29, `JPY/current account` from -550298.11 to -848.11, `GBP/goods trade balance non-eu` from -3670.06 to -2.56 — all three had means inflated by roughly the same 3-4 order-of-magnitude pattern as the display-side bug (entity digits splicing into the real number), meaning any z-score the Economic Surprises panel showed for these series was wrong, not just the raw actual/forecast text.
- **Manual repair pass applied to production files directly (this session), rather than waiting on the next scheduled run:** ran `_normalise_carried_event()` over all 3716 events in the current `calendar-data/calendar.json` (97 corrupted fields fixed, 3196 `hourUTC`→`timeUTC` renames) and recomputed `surpriseStats` from the cleaned events; ran `_redecode_entities()` over all 217 events in the current `calendar-data/ff_calendar.json` (48 corrupted fields fixed). Both delivered alongside the script fixes below — commit these two JSON files as-is rather than relying solely on the next `update-ff-calendar`/`update-economic-calendar` run to self-heal, since a partial/interrupted run before the next full cycle could otherwise leave the site showing corrupted values a while longer.
- **Fix:** added `_normalise_carried_event()`, applied at the Step 3 merge point, which (1) re-decodes `actual`/`forecast`/`previous` via `html.unescape()` (no-op if already clean) and (2) renames `hourUTC` → `timeUTC` on any prev_event still carrying the legacy field name. Both self-heal on the next run rather than requiring a backfill script or waiting out the full history window.
- **Companion fix:** `main()`'s startup print read `v3.3` while the module header read `v3.6` — same version-sync-drift class as above. Bumped to v3.7, both locations now match. Added `import html`.
- **Verification:** unit-tested `_normalise_carried_event()` against the exact corrupted production event (`United Kingdom Goods Trade Balance`, `&#163;-26.05B` → `£-26.05B`, plus `hourUTC` → `timeUTC` rename). `python3 -m py_compile` and `ast.parse` clean. No existing pytest coverage exists for either script (`scripts/tests/` in this repo and `globalinvesting-scripts` do not exercise them) — verification was manual, against real corrupted production values pulled from the live `calendar-data/` files.
- **Not yet done:** these fixes make the rolling history self-heal going forward (every surviving historical event gets re-decoded/renamed the next time it's merged), but that's gated on the event still having an `actual` and being within the lookback window each script enforces. Any corrupted event that ages out or gets purged before its next merge pass simply drops out of history rather than getting fixed — acceptable here since the affected fields are 90-day-lookback beat/miss inputs, not permanent records, but noted in case Santiago wants a true one-off backfill pass instead of/in addition to relying on the next few scheduled runs.

## v8.72.3 (2026-07-29) — Root-caused ESI numeric corruption to undecoded HTML entities in the calendar pipeline

### Bugfix — `fetch_ff_calendar.py` (scripts repo)

- **Investigation trigger:** Santiago flagged a disproportionately high SEK score on the MT5 EA's Economic Surprise Index. That reading was confirmed *not* a bug (SEK's own-history GDP beat on 2026-07-29, amplified by thin ~10-event coverage over 2 years — documented behavior). Comparing the same panel on the web terminal surfaced a second, unrelated issue: EUR "Jobseekers Total" showing a surprise of +3,118,418 and JPY Current Account/Trade Balance events showing swings in the thousands — both economically implausible.
- **Root cause:** `fetch_myfxbook_rss()`'s entity decoding replaced only a fixed allowlist (`&#60;`/`&#62;`/`&#39;`/`&lt;`/`&gt;`/`&amp;`) — enough to unescape the RSS description's own `<td>` table markup, but missing currency-symbol entities (`&#163;`=£, `&#8364;`=€, `&#165;`=¥) that Myfxbook sometimes emits inside actual/forecast/previous cell text for GBP/EUR/JPY events. The HTML-scrape fast-actuals path (`fetch_myfxbook_html_actuals()`) had **no** entity decoding at all. `dashboard.js`'s `_parseNum()` recovers the number by stripping every non-digit character — so a leftover `"&#163;-13.05B"` string parses to `-16313.05` (the entity code's own digits `163` splice onto the real number) instead of `-13.05`. Reproduced and confirmed via `html.unescape()` round-trip: `&#163;-13.05B` → `£-13.05B` (correct), `&#8364;5.2B` → `€5.2B`, `&#165;3907B` → `¥3907B`.
- **Fix:** replaced the hand-rolled allowlist with stdlib `html.unescape()` (generic named + numeric entity decoder) in both the RSS parser and the HTML-scrape parser (`previous`/`forecast`/`actual` extraction). Also fixed a version-header drift in the same file — the module docstring still read v3.34 though a v3.35 fix (Myfxbook Sentiment pseudo-event exclusion) had already shipped and was referenced from `fetch_economic_calendar.py`'s comments. Header now correctly reads v3.36.
- **Companion fix — `calendar-watcher.js` (scripts repo, Cloudflare Worker, `cf-workers-backup/calendar-watcher/`):** same bug class, confirmed present since this Worker's `/payload` output is pulled into `fetch_ff_calendar.py` (Step 1b) and can carry the same undecoded entities. Replaced its fixed allowlist with a new `decodeHtmlEntities()` generic decoder (named + numeric + hex entity forms) and applied it to both the RSS description decode and the HTML-scrape actual-value extraction (`parseMyfxbookHTMLActuals()` and the `/test-html` diagnostic endpoint), neither of which decoded entities at all before this fix. Bumped v5.10 → v5.11, all four version-string call sites kept in sync (module header, `/` root response, cron log line, GitHub dispatch User-Agent).
- **Scope note:** this affects the web terminal's Economic Surprises panel and ESI, fed by the Myfxbook RSS/HTML → `ff_calendar.json` → `calendar.json` pipeline only. The MT5 EA's own ESI (`ComputeESI()` in the .mq5 source) reads MetaTrader's native broker calendar via `CalendarValueHistory()` — a completely separate data source untouched by this fix. Confirmed via the EA source: no `NOISE_KW`-equivalent filter exists there either (separate, already-flagged gap — not addressed in this entry).
- **Verification:** `python3 -m py_compile fetch_ff_calendar.py` clean; `node --check calendar-watcher.js` clean; `html.unescape()` manually verified against the three problem entities above.
- **Not yet done:** cannot confirm live whether `calendar.json` in production currently holds already-corrupted historical rows from before this fix — this only prevents new corruption going forward. A backfill/repair pass over existing `calendar.json` history is a separate follow-up if Santiago wants it.

## v8.72.0 (2026-07-28) — HY OAS 20d widening added as a canonical stress-score factor (industry-standard credit inclusion)

### GUIDELINES.md — Stress scoring canonical table

- **Rule change:** added a 7th binary factor to the canonical stress-scoring table — HY OAS 20-day change > +15bp (widening) → +1 point. Maximum possible score raised from 9 to 10 (VIX×3 + 7 binary factors). Regime mapping thresholds (0→RISK-ON, 1→MIXED, 2–3→CAUTION, ≥4→RISK-OFF) left unchanged — adding one more possible point doesn't change what counts as "elevated" vs "crisis" severity.
- **Rationale (industry standard, confirmed via web search, not assumed from training data):** credit spreads are a standard leg of institutional cross-asset risk-regime composites, not a niche addition — the Kansas City Fed's RORO Index explicitly combines credit spreads, equity vol, funding conditions, and FX/gold into one score; Gilchrist & Zakrajšek (2012, *American Economic Review*) and the KC Fed's own RORO paper find credit spreads drive the vast majority of capital-flow effects and are often more predictive of EM FX flows than VIX alone; CBOE/S&P's "credit VIX" indices formalize credit vol as its own dimension distinct from equity vol.
- **Why direction (Δ20d) and not level:** OAS updates daily (not intraday, unlike the rest of the score's inputs), and can sit in a historically tight zone while still actively widening — the pattern practitioners call the "silent killer" (VIX/equities calm, credit quietly deteriorating), which historically preceded 2007-style credit events. The level alone would miss this; the 20-day direction catches it. Threshold (+15bp) matches the existing Widening/Narrowing/Stable classification already shown in the Risk Indicators table (v8.71.13), so the same number now means the same thing in both places.
- **Explicitly scoped smaller than a full industry replica:** did not adopt a weighted composite (e.g. the ~20–25% credit weighting seen in some public multi-asset risk-appetite indices) — the existing score is unweighted/additive across binary factors, and changing that would be a bigger architectural decision. This session applied the standard in the form that fits the existing scoring mechanism: one more binary factor, consistent with how AUD/JPY and the USD/JPY+AUD/JPY combo were added previously.

### Frontend — `assets/dashboard.js`

- `renderRiskData()`: `stressScore` now adds +1 when `byId.hyOasDelta20d > 15`. Comment block documents the "silent killer" rationale and industry precedent inline, matching the style of the existing AUD/JPY/USD-JPY factor comments.
- Regime cell tooltip (`attachRiskMonitorTooltips()`) updated to list HY OAS 20d change among the composite's factors, and the MIXED example now mentions credit-only stress as a possible trigger. HY OAS 20d Δ row tooltip updated to note it now feeds the Regime score above.

### `assets/dashboard.test.js`

- Added `hyOasDelta20d` (default 0) to the standalone `computeStressScore()` test helper, with `> 15` triggering +1, mirroring the production threshold exactly.
- New tests: boundary at exactly +15bp (no score), +15.01bp (scores), narrowing at −30bp (no score — only widening counts), and +40bp alone with calm VIX/equities → MIXED (score 1) — the "silent killer" scenario in isolation. Updated the existing "all factors max" test to include `hyOasDelta20d: 40`, bumping its expected score from 7 to 8.
- Stress-scoring section: 14 → 18 tests. Total suite: 81 → 85 tests, all passing.

### GUIDELINES.md — housekeeping

- Updated both hardcoded "81 tests" references (pre-deployment checklist rule, repo-inventory table) to 85 to match the new total. Version footer bumped to v8.72.0 (rule change, per the skill's own instructions).

**Verification:** `node -c assets/dashboard.js` clean; `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 85/85 passed; `index.html` tag-balance check (`div`/`a`/`table`/`tr`/`td`/`th`/`tbody`) all balanced (index.html itself untouched this entry — only `dashboard.js`/`dashboard.test.js`/`GUIDELINES.md` changed).

**Note found, not fixed this session:** `scripts/CHANGELOG.md` (inside the engine repo's `scripts/` directory) appears to be a stray duplicate of the root `CHANGELOG.md` at an older point in time — same pattern as the stray-file regressions documented earlier in this same file (see the v8.8.x-era entries on duplicate `dashboard.js`/`dashboard.test.js` files). Flagged for Santiago to confirm before deletion; not touched here since it wasn't part of what was asked this session and deleting repo files without explicit confirmation is out of scope.

## v8.71.14 (2026-07-28) — Fix: HY/IG OAS unit mismatch (percent vs basis points) in Risk Monitor

### Frontend — `assets/dashboard.js`

- **Root cause:** the first live `workflow_dispatch` of the reactivated `update-extended-data.yml` (2026-07-28) surfaced a units bug: `update_extended_data.py` stores `hyOas`/`igOas`/`hyOasDelta20d` in **percentage points** (log output: `HY OAS: 2.81%`, `IG OAS: 0.81%` — confirmed in the script's own source comment, `% pts`), but the v8.71.13 frontend integration treated `byId.hyOas.close` as already being in basis points, feeding raw values like `2.81` straight into `Math.round(hy) + ' bp'` and into the `>500`/`>350` bp thresholds. Result: the panel would have rendered "3 bp" instead of "281 bp", and every reading would have permanently scored "Tight" regardless of actual stress level.
- **Fix:** `fetchRiskData()` STEP 1 now multiplies `d.hyOas`, `d.igOas`, and `d.hyOasDelta20d` by 100 at ingestion (percent → bp) before storing into `byId`, so `renderRiskData()`'s bp-denominated thresholds and display logic downstream are unaffected and correct as originally written.
- **Verification:** re-ran `node assets/dashboard.test.js` (81/81 passed) and `node -c assets/dashboard.js` (clean). Manually recomputed the threshold/label logic against the real 2026-07-28 run values (HY 2.81% → 281bp → "Tight"; IG 0.81% → 81bp → "Tight") — both match the live "post-2009 tight range" read confirmed via web search when the thresholds were first set (v8.71.13), so no threshold values needed changing, only the unit conversion.
- **Scope boundary:** `bond10y`/`bond2y`/`bond5y` fields are unaffected — those are genuinely displayed as percent (`toFixed(2) + '%'`) elsewhere in `renderRiskData()`, so no conversion was ever needed for them. This bug was specific to the two new bp-denominated fields.

### Frontend — `assets/gi-auth.js` (v1.2.1)

**Root cause:** The activation modal's TMGM line ("Opened a verified TMGM account instead? Contact us
to receive your access link — no MT5 key required.") correctly presented the EA-rental and TMGM-account
paths as two independent, alternative ways to unlock the terminal — that framing was never ambiguous.
What it never addressed is a separate question: *who Santiago is relative to TMGM*. A prospective user
messaged Santiago directly asking "you're a broker at TMGM?" before asking anything about how to access
the terminal — i.e. the confusion was about identity/affiliation, not about the two access mechanics,
which `access.html`'s existing FAQ (line ~944) already disambiguates clearly for anyone who reaches it.

**Fix:** Added a short clause to the same line — "As our referral partner, TMGM account holders get full
web terminal access too" — so the disclaimer is visible at the first touchpoint (the modal) rather than
only on `access.html`, and scopes the claim explicitly to *web terminal* access (not the native MT5 EA
overlay, which TMGM account holders do not get). Wording chosen to stay inside the bounds of the TMGM
Introducing Broker Agreement §2.c (must never claim to be more than a referrer, or an authorised/recognised
party of the Principal) — "referral partner" describes the actual IB relationship without overclaiming it.

**Verification:** Manual review only (single-string HTML copy change inside an existing template literal;
no logic, selectors, or gating behavior touched). Confirmed the edit doesn't affect line count parity of
surrounding `<p class="gi-auth-sub">` blocks or the `-10px`/`-8px` `margin-top` spacing hacks between them.

**Scope boundary:** `access.html`'s TMGM sub-card copy and the compact gate-overlay message ("Premium —
included with EA rental or verified TMGM account") were reviewed and left unchanged — both are either
already unambiguous (`access.html` FAQ) or too space-constrained for a disclaimer to fit without breaking
layout (gate overlay). No i18n system exists for `gi-auth.js` — any localized (e.g. Portuguese) rendering
seen in-browser is a browser-level auto-translation of this English source, not a maintained translation
file, so this fix propagates to it automatically.

## v8.71.10 (2026-07-27) — Myfxbook "Sentiment" pseudo-events purged from economic calendar and ESI

### Scripts repo — `fetch_ff_calendar.py` (v3.35), `fetch_economic_calendar.py` (v3.6) · Site repo — `assets/calendar-panel.js`, `calendar-data/ff_calendar.json`, `calendar-data/calendar.json`

**Root cause:** Myfxbook's RSS and HTML economic-calendar sources (the same feeds `fetch_ff_calendar.py`
uses for real macro data) also carry Myfxbook's own retail-positioning product, published as calendar rows
like `"European Union Myfxbook EURUSD Sentiment"`. These are not official economic releases — there is no
real consensus forecast; Myfxbook backfills a `concensus` value from last week's own reading. They are
tagged `impact="medium"`, so they passed the low-impact filter cleanly and were fetched, stored, and
displayed like any other event.

The ESI/Economic-Surprises z-score baseline was already partially protected: v3.5 (2026-07-11) added a
`'myfxbook'` keyword to `NOISE_KW`/`_ESM_NOISE_KW` (`dashboard.js`/`econ-surprises-modal.js`) and to
`compute_surprise_stats()` in `fetch_economic_calendar.py`, so these pseudo-events couldn't fabricate a
beat/miss z-score. But that only closed the *scoring* gap — nothing stopped them from being **fetched** into
`ff_calendar.json`, **converted** into `calendar.json`, or **displayed** in the raw Economic Calendar panel
(`calendar-panel.js` had no title filter at all), which is what the user was actually seeing.

**Fix, root cause first:**
- `fetch_ff_calendar.py` v3.35: new `_is_myfxbook_sentiment(title)` helper, applied in both
  `fetch_myfxbook_rss()` and `fetch_myfxbook_calendar()` (HTML) before the impact filter — Myfxbook
  Sentiment pseudo-events are now dropped at the point of ingestion and never written to
  `ff_calendar.json`. (The disused `_normalise_worker_events()` CF-Worker path was left as-is — it is not
  called from `main()`, confirmed via the v3.26 CHANGELOG entry removing that call.)
- `fetch_economic_calendar.py` v3.6: `ff_to_cal_event()` now also excludes `myfxbook`-titled events when
  converting `ff_calendar.json` → `calendar.json`, closing the gap where they still reached the Economic
  Surprises panel and the Economic Matrix's latest-actual lookups even though `compute_surprise_stats()`

  defense-in-depth stop for any pseudo-events still sitting in `ff_calendar.json`'s 21-day history or
  `calendar.json`'s longer history from before these fixes take effect on the next pipeline run.
