## v8.71.8 (2026-07-25) — sitemap.xml: 2 guide pages were never in the `PAGES` generator array

### Site — `scripts/update_sitemap.py`, `GUIDELINES.md`

**Root cause (same failure mode as the `guide-csi-indicator.html` drift fixed in v8.53.0):**
`guide-fundamental-analysis.html` and `guide-monte-carlo-simulator.html` were both live,
linked, published pages with real content — but neither had ever been added to the `PAGES`
array in `scripts/update_sitemap.py`. Since `sitemap.xml` is fully regenerated (overwritten)
from that array on every push touching an HTML page, both pages were silently absent from
`sitemap.xml` and therefore invisible to Google's sitemap-based crawl scheduling, regardless
of how long they'd been live or how many other pages linked to them.

**What was NOT the bug:** an earlier ad-hoc check flagged `guide-mt5-ea.html` as missing 3
`<image:image>` entries (sentiment, correlation, volatility). That check was wrong — it matched
`assets/screenshot-*.png` anywhere in the file, including the page's JSON-LD `image` array, not
just real `<img>` tags in the body. `scan_page_images()` (the actual generator logic) only scans
`<img>` tags, correctly returns 8 images for that page, and matches the currently-committed
`sitemap.xml` exactly — no sitemap bug here.

**Separate finding, not fixed here (flagged for a decision, not actioned):** those same 3 images
*are* declared in `guide-mt5-ea.html`'s JSON-LD structured-data `image` array (Retail Sentiment,
Correlation matrix, Volatility & Options panels) with no matching `<img>` anywhere in the page
body — i.e., the page's schema markup promises 3 screenshots that were never actually added to
the page. This is a structured-data accuracy issue, not a sitemap generator issue; needs a call
on whether to add the 3 screenshots to the body or remove the 3 entries from the JSON-LD.

**Fix:** added both pages to `PAGES` in `scripts/update_sitemap.py`:
- `guide-fundamental-analysis.html` — priority 0.8 / monthly / no data deps (static conceptual
  page, no live-JSON fetch in the page), same tier as `guide-dashboard.html`.
- `guide-monte-carlo-simulator.html` — priority 0.7 / monthly / no data deps, same tier as
  `guide-csi-indicator.html` (free-product guide, single screenshot).

Also added both pages to the "Sitemap — active pages only" reference list in `GUIDELINES.md`
so it stays in sync with `PAGES`, per the existing warning in that same section. No rule changed,
so the GUIDELINES.md version footer was not bumped.

**Not regenerated by hand:** per `GUIDELINES.md`, `sitemap.xml` itself must never be hand-edited —
`update-sitemap.yml` regenerates it automatically from `PAGES` on the next push (its `paths`
trigger includes `scripts/update_sitemap.py`), using real git commit history for `lastmod` dates
that a local, git-history-less checkout can't reproduce accurately. Handing over a manually
regenerated `sitemap.xml` would have overwritten every page's correct historical `lastmod` with
today's date and reintroduced the exact drift this entry fixes.

**Validation:** confirmed via `scan_page_images()` run against both new pages (6 images for
fundamental-analysis, 1 for monte-carlo-simulator, both matching their JSON-LD image lists) and
confirmed every `*.html` at repo root is now covered by `PAGES` except `404.html` (correctly
excluded — error pages don't belong in sitemaps).

## v8.71.4 (2026-07-25) — ESI dedup key normalization bug (AUD index still off after v8.71.3 port)

### Engine — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`

**User-reported:** direct follow-up to v8.71.3 — after porting the modal's exact decay/impact/z-score
formula line-for-line, the AUD index in the AI narrative context still didn't match the Economic
Surprises modal (Python: `-4.3` expected vs. a different value produced, sign risk on borderline
cases). User pushed back on the assumption that this was simply "newer data" and asked for
verification before accepting the discrepancy.

**Root cause:** the modal's dedup key in `dashboard.js` strips `%`, commas, and whitespace from
`actual`/`forecast` before hashing
(`` `${ccy}/${canonEvent}/${String(ev.actual).replace(/[%,\s]/g,'')}/${String(ev.forecast||ev.previous||'').replace(/[%,\s]/g,'')}` ``).
The Python port built the same key from the raw, un-normalized strings. `calendar.json` carries
duplicate entries for the same event under two schemas — an older Myfxbook-sourced schema (e.g.
`forecast: "4.35"`) and a newer schema (`forecast: "4.35%"`) — that agree on every field except the
`%` suffix. Without stripping, these hashed to different keys and both got scored, double-counting
7 AUD events (RBA Interest Rate Decision, Trimmed Mean CPI MoM, Inflation Rate MoM, Unemployment
Rate, and others in the 2026-06 window) and skewing the weighted result.

**Verification:** extracted the real scoring functions verbatim from `dashboard.js` (not a
re-implementation) into a standalone Node harness (`js_harness.js`) and ran it against the same
`calendar.json` used by the Python script. Diffed the per-event AUD trace between the Node output
and the (buggy) Python output line-by-line to isolate the exact 7 events causing the divergence
before touching any code.

**Fix:** normalize `actual` and `forecast`/`previous` with the equivalent of `/[%,\s]/g` (regex
`[%,\s]`, stripped via `re.sub`) before building the dedup key, matching `dashboard.js` exactly.

**Result — Python now matches the real `dashboard.js` output exactly, currency by currency:**

| CCY | Index (90d) | Beats | Misses | N |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| USD | 3.8 | 149 | 128 | 309 |
| EUR | -15.0 | 86 | 129 | 235 |
| GBP | 2.0 | 41 | 48 | 106 |
| JPY | 13.5 | 29 | 20 | 56 |
| AUD | -4.3 | 19 | 35 | 65 |
| CAD | 4.0 | 31 | 27 | 68 |
| CHF | 27.0 | 17 | 9 | 32 |
| NZD | 22.2 | 11 | 7 | 21 |
| NOK | 34.4 | 1 | 0 | 2 |
| SEK | 0.0 | 0 | 0 | 1 |

The manually-patched `signals.json` from v8.71.2 (AUD "+2.0") is now superseded — it was computed
before this dedup bug was found and does not match the corrected AUD value (`-4.3`). It will be
overwritten by the next real pipeline run using the script fixed here.

## v8.71.3 (2026-07-25) — Narrative/signals ESI index diverges from the Economic Surprises modal by design

### Engine — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`

**User-reported:** direct follow-up to v8.71.2 — after fixing the "CESI" mislabel, user asked
to close the remaining gap entirely ("no quiero divergencias"): the narrative/signals ESI number
still didn't match the Economic Surprises modal, because section 9 computed a raw, unweighted
`beats − misses` count while `dashboard.js` (`renderEconSurprises()`) computes a decay-weighted,
impact-weighted, z-score-blended index normalised to `[-100, +100]`. This had been an intentional,
documented simplification since v8.51.15 ("still an intentional simplification vs. the panel's
full decay+impact-weighted z-score index... the two numbers will still differ in magnitude by
design"). User does not want that design tradeoff — the AI-cited number should match the modal.

**Fix:** ported the modal's exact formula from `dashboard.js` line-for-line into Python:
1. **Exponential time-decay**, half-life 45 days (`λ = ln(2)/45`) — `w = e^(-λ·ageDays)`.
2. **Impact weighting** multiplied into `w` — HIGH=1.0, MEDIUM=0.5.
3. **Two-pass adaptive window** (mirrors the MT5 EA's `ComputeESI()` v8.4.3+): pass 0 scores the
   standard 90d window for all G10 currencies; pass 1 extends only currencies left with zero
   decay-weighted total after pass 0 (structurally thin coverage, NOK/SEK in practice) to a
   90–180d band. Same filters apply in both passes — the extension doesn't lower methodology
   standards, it just avoids forcing a blank row for currencies whose upstream provider tags
   nearly all releases "low" impact.
4. **z-score blend**: per event, if `calendar.json`'s `surpriseStats` has ≥5 historical
   observations and `std > 0` for that `(ccy, canonical-event)` series, the event contributes
   `z = (surprise − mean) / std` instead of a flat beat/miss. When a currency's decay-weighted
   z-scored share reaches ≥10 weight or ≥30% of total weight, the index blends the z-scored part
   (mapped ±2σ → ±100) with the beat/miss part (scaled to ±100) in proportion to weight;
   otherwise it falls back to pure decay-weighted beat/miss — identical branching to
   `renderEconSurprises()`.

BEATS/MISSES/TOTAL in the narrative table remain **raw, unweighted counts** — exactly what the
modal's BEATS/MISSES/N columns show. Only the index score itself (labelled "Index" instead of
the old "Net") is decay+impact+z weighted. STRONG/Moderate signal thresholds were rescaled from
the old raw-count range (±10/±4) to the new ±100-normalised range (±15/±5), since the two scales
aren't comparable.

**Verified against production data:** ran the ported formula standalone against the live
`calendar-data/calendar.json` snapshot and cross-checked against the Economic Surprises modal
screenshots from the same session — EUR: modal INDEX -15.0 (BEATS 86, MISSES 129, N 235) vs.
ported calc -14.8 (BEATS 86 — exact match, MISSES 130, N 238, 3 more events from a slightly newer
snapshot). JPY and AUD tracked the same direction and rough magnitude, with the small remaining
deltas fully explained by the two snapshots being minutes apart (more events landed in the newer
one) rather than by a formula discrepancy.

**Not changed:** the ancillary "9b. surpriseStats z-scores" block (individual notable |z|≥1.5
single-event shocks, separate from the aggregate index) is untouched — it serves a different
narrative purpose than the aggregate ESI index this fix targets.

- `node --check` N/A (Python-only change). `python3 -m py_compile` OK.
  `PYTHONPATH=<scripts-repo> python3 -m pytest scripts/tests/` — 171 passed (no regressions;
  no existing test covers this block directly, so also verified via standalone harness above).

## v8.71.2 (2026-07-25) — Narrative/signals mislabel own ESI calculation as Citi's "CESI"

### Engine — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`
- **User-reported:** narrative and signal cards refer to the site's own Economic Surprise Index as
  "CESI" (e.g. "EUR CESI: -43"), and separately asked why that number doesn't match the Economic
  Surprises modal for the same currency (e.g. EUR showed -43 in a signal vs INDEX (90D) -15.0 in
  the modal; AUD -14 vs -4.3; JPY +10 vs +13.5).
- **Root cause (naming):** the AI-facing context block built by this script (the text actually
  fed to Gemini/Groq, not just internal comments) literally wrote `"CESI EXTREMES"`,
  `"positive CESI"`, `"CESI diverging from COT"`, etc. The model then echoed that label straight
  into narrative/signal output. `dashboard.js` already gets this right — the site UI always calls
  its own index "ESI" and only references "CESI" in internal engineering comments as a methodology
  citation (Citi's is the reference convention the site's decay-weighted formula follows), never as
  a user-facing label. This script never carried the same discipline in its prompt-context text.
  CESI is Citigroup's proprietary/trademarked index name — this terminal's ESI is an independently
  computed value inspired by the same methodology family, not a reproduction of Citi's product.
- **Root cause (magnitude mismatch — pre-existing, documented, NOT newly introduced):** already
  flagged in this file's own comments (v8.51.15, v8.65.2): this block computes a raw, unweighted
  beats-minus-misses count over the same 90d window the modal uses, while `dashboard.js`
  `renderEconSurprises()` computes a normalised [-100,+100] index with exponential decay
  (45-day half-life) + impact weighting (HIGH=1.0, MEDIUM=0.5). Event population/filtering was
  already aligned between the two in prior fixes; the scoring FORMULA itself was never ported, by
  design, as an intentional simplification for prose generation. This is a real, still-open gap —
  not something this entry claims to have closed — see the "Fix B" note below.
- **Fixed (this entry):**
  - Renamed every AI-facing occurrence of "CESI" to "ESI" in the context block (section header,
    "EXTREMES" label, leader/laggard sentences). Internal Python identifiers (`_sorted_cesi`,
    `_dd_cesi`, etc.) and code comments were left as-is — they're never sent to the LLM and serve
    as an internal methodology cross-reference, same convention `dashboard.js` already follows.
  - Added an explicit instruction line to the context block telling the model: this ESI figure is
    a raw 90d beat/miss count, NOT the decay+impact-weighted figure shown in the Economic
    Surprises modal; do not imply the two should match; never call it "CESI".
- **Not fixed here (proposed to user as a separate, larger change — "Fix B"):** porting
  `dashboard.js`'s exact decay+impact-weighted formula (including the two-pass 90d/180d adaptive
  window for thin-coverage NOK/SEK) into this script, so the number the AI cites is identical to
  what the reader sees in the modal, not just consistently labeled. Awaiting confirmation before
  implementing — meaningfully larger port, needs side-by-side verification against the modal for
  all 8 currencies before shipping.
- **Verified:** `python3 -m py_compile scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py` — syntax OK.

## v8.71.1 (2026-07-25) — COT currency switcher: tab reset to Overview on every switch

### Frontend — `assets/inline-panel.js` (v1.3.1 → v1.3.2)
- **User-reported:** after switching currency via the new in-modal switcher (v8.71.0), the modal
  always reset to the Overview tab instead of staying on whichever tab (Net Position, Long/Short,
  etc.) was active before the switch — despite `cotSwitchCcy()` explicitly reading the active tab
  and passing it through as `openCOTModal(newCcy, data, {preserveTab: activeTab})`.
- **Root cause:** `inline-panel.js` intercepts `window.openCOTModal` to transplant the modal into
  the split-view layout, but its wrapper was declared as `function(ccy, data)` — only two
  parameters — and forwarded only `(ccy, data)` to `_origOpenCOT`. Because `openCOTModal` is a
  top-level `function` declaration in `cot-modal-chart.js`, it is the *same* global binding as
  `window.openCOTModal`; once `inline-panel.js` reassigns it, every later bare call to
  `openCOTModal(...)` anywhere in the codebase — including from `cotSwitchCcy()` inside
  `cot-modal-chart.js` itself — resolves to this wrapper. The third argument (`opts.preserveTab`)
  was silently dropped in BOTH branches of the wrapper (the split-view path and the
  `if (!panels)` passthrough path), so this broke tab preservation even for users not in split
  view.
- **Fixed:** wrapper now declared as `function(ccy, data, opts)` and forwards `opts` to
  `_origOpenCOT` in both branches.
- **Verified:** `node --check assets/inline-panel.js` — syntax OK. `node assets/dashboard.test.js`
  — 81/81 passed.

### Frontend — `index.html`
- **Cache-buster:** bumped `inline-panel.js` script tag query string `?v=1.4.0` → `?v=1.4.1` so
  the fix above actually reaches the browser after deploy (same class of issue flagged in
  v8.71.0's own cache-buster note).

  in the chart header + `,`/`.` cycling) all keep the instrument switcher compact and in the
  header rather than a full-width native `<select>`. Followed the same shape here: a small
  currency chip in `#cot-m-hd` opens a dropdown grid of available G10 currencies, flanked by
  discreet `‹`/`›` arrows for one-click cycling.
- **Added:**
  - `#cot-ccy-switch` chip + dropdown in the modal header, replacing the static `${ccy}` text in
    the title.
  - `cotSwitchCcy(ccy)` — switches currency by re-invoking `openCOTModal()` with the cached entry
    from `window.COT_DATA_STORE` (already populated for all currencies on first load by
    `fetchCOTData()` in `dashboard.js`) — no additional network request.
  - `cotCycleCcy(±1)` — steps to the previous/next currency in G10 order; wired to `‹`/`›` buttons
    and to `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` while the modal is open.
  - `cotToggleCcyDropdown()` + outside-click/Escape handling to open/close the dropdown without
    closing the modal itself (Escape closes the dropdown first if open, then the modal on a
    second press).
  - **Active tab preserved across currency switches** (Overview/Net Position/Long-Short/
    Participants/History) — the switcher passes the currently active tab into the rebuilt modal
    instead of resetting to Overview, which none of the three reference terminals above do.
  - Switcher options are built from `Object.keys(window.COT_DATA_STORE)` filtered to G10 order —
    a currency with a failed COT fetch never appears as a dead/disabled entry.
- **Verified:** `node --check assets/cot-modal-chart.js` — syntax OK. `node assets/dashboard.test.js`
  — 81/81 passed (unaffected file, run as a safety check). Manual div/button tag balance check on
  the modified template string — balanced (138/138 divs, 5/5 buttons).
- **Cache-buster bumped:** `index.html` script tag `assets/cot-modal-chart.js?v=7.90.1` → `?v=7.91.0`
  so the updated file is fetched fresh instead of a stale cached copy (project convention — see
  `deploy-pages.yml` concurrency note above re: CDN caching). File-header version comment bumped

## v8.70.2 (2026-07-25) — Weekend narrative: USD-positive driver applied inconsistently across pairs

### Engine — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`
- **User-reported:** in the 2026-07-24 21:04 UTC weekend narrative, EUR/USD was described as facing
  downside from "the USD's +144bp OIS carry advantage," while in the same narrative GBP/USD was
  described as getting support at the open from "firming Fed hike bets" — the same USD-strength
  driver used to justify opposite directional conclusions for two USD pairs.
- **Root cause:** `NARRATIVE_SYSTEM_CLOSED` (the weekend/closed-market prompt) only carried a
  narrow directional-coherence rule ("GEOPOLITICAL DRIVER DIRECTIONALITY") scoped to Iran-style
  geopolitical catalysts and exactly two pairs (EUR/USD, USD/JPY). It had no equivalent guard for
  the general case: any single USD-wide driver (Fed policy repricing, tariff-driven USD strength,
  dovish repricing, etc.) must move every USD pair referenced in the narrative in the same relative
  direction. Same failure class as the `_correct_cb_tense_text()` incident documented above (a
  guard built from one specific incident that wasn't generalized to the symmetric/general case).
  Note: the live-market prompt (`NARRATIVE_SYSTEM`) already has this covered generally via Rule 9
  "USD INTERNAL CONSISTENCY" — the gap was specific to the closed-market/weekend prompt, which
  predates that rule and never inherited an equivalent.
- **Fixed:** replaced the Iran-only two-pair rule in `NARRATIVE_SYSTEM_CLOSED` with a general
  "USD-WIDE DRIVER DIRECTIONALITY" rule: pick one USD-positive/negative direction for the
  narrative's dominant driver, then apply it across every USD pair mentioned (EUR/USD, GBP/USD,
  AUD/USD, USD/JPY, USD/CHF), with the reported EUR/USD-vs-GBP/USD contradiction included as a
  forbidden example alongside the original Iran/EUR-USD/USD-JPY case (now folded in as one instance
  of the general rule rather than a special case).
- **Verified:** `python3 -m py_compile scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py` — syntax OK.

## v8.70.1 (2026-07-24) — is_forex_relevant() missing geopolitical terms already trusted in HIGH_IMPACT_KW

### Engine — `scripts/fetch_news.py` (v5.24 → v5.25)
- **User-reported:** asked why geopolitical content wouldn't be relevant to USD, since geopolitics
  is a recognized FX driver — prompted by the FinancialJuice integration above, but the gap is
  general to the pipeline, not specific to that source.
- **Confirmed via direct `is_forex_relevant()` calls** against 5 real FinancialJuice titles
  (24-Jul-2026): 4/5 geopolitical headlines (Strait of Hormuz, Iran sanctions) returned `False`.
  Root cause: `HIGH_IMPACT_KW` has treated `"strait of hormuz"`, `"war "`, `"military strike"`,
  `"sanctions"` (+ Spanish forms) as high-impact since before this file's changelog history begins,
  but `FOREX_RELEVANCE_KW` — the separate list gating whether an article enters the pipeline at
  all — never carried the same terms. The "high impact" classification was structurally dead code
  for any headline that was purely geopolitical with no independent FX/oil keyword in the same text.
- **Fixed:** mirrored the exact same 8 geopolitical terms from `HIGH_IMPACT_KW` into
  `FOREX_RELEVANCE_KW`. Deliberately did not add broader coverage (e.g. "strike", "retaliation")
  beyond what was already vetted elsewhere in the codebase, to avoid unreviewed false-positive risk
  (e.g. "strike" also matches labor strikes unrelated to FX) — consistent with the project's
  "fix only what's reported/verified" convention.
- **Known residual gap, not closed by this fix:** a headline with none of these 8 literal terms
  (e.g. "Bahrain and Kuwait warplanes struck Iran... retaliation") still won't pass. Documented here
  rather than silently expanded, since further keyword coverage wasn't independently verified.
- **Tests:** 5 new tests in `test_fetch_news.py` (`TestIsForexRelevant`) — 3 regression tests using
  real production titles (Hormuz ×2, Iran sanctions) plus generic Spanish/English war/military-strike
  cases. 119/119 tests passing (114 previous + 5 new), 0 regressions.

## v8.70.0 (2026-07-24) — FinancialJuice RSS source added with headline-only treatment

### Engine — `scripts/fetch_news.py` (v5.23 → v5.24)
- **User request:** add `https://www.financialjuice.com/feed.ashx?xy=rss` as a news source.
- **Audit before implementing:** fetched the live feed twice (24-Jul-2026) and found the large
  majority of `<item>` entries carry an empty `<description/>` — the feed's native format is a
  real-time headline wire (politics, geopolitics, central banks, commodities, Treasury auctions),
  not an editorial feed with summaries. With `MIN_DESCRIPTION_WORDS = 12` enforced unconditionally,
  this source would have contributed ~0 articles — the same structural mismatch that led v5.20 to
  reject the Norges Bank Monetary Policy Report / Financial Stability Report feeds (both always
  publish empty `<description/>`).
- **Decision:** unlike the Norges Bank case, the user confirmed the headline-only format was
  expected and asked for the source to be added anyway, citing the Bloomberg TOP LIVE / Reuters
  alerts convention of single-line, body-less wire headlines as institutional precedent.
- **Implemented a scoped bypass, not a global relaxation:** new `HEADLINE_ONLY_SOURCES =
  {"FinancialJuice"}` set. `is_calendar_entry()` and `has_real_content()` now take an optional
  `source` parameter and only skip the `MIN_DESCRIPTION_WORDS` gate for sources in that set — every
  other gate (`CALENDAR_TITLE_RE`/`CALENDAR_RE`, `EDUCATIONAL_RE`, the 5-word title minimum,
  `is_forex_relevant()`, the non-G10 central-bank filter) is unchanged for this source and for every
  other source.
- **New global guard (not source-scoped):** added `r"actual\s.*\(forecast"` to `CALENDAR_PATTERNS`.
  Titles shaped like `"X Actual Y (Forecast Z, Previous W)"` — extremely common on FinancialJuice
  (PMI, PPI, rig counts, home sales, etc.) — are raw economic-calendar-panel duplicates with no
  narrative content. Same risk class as the SNB statistical-print guard from v5.19 (bare numeric
  data reaching the LLM headline pool without context); this guard applies globally so any future
  feed emitting this shape is covered, not only FinancialJuice.
- **Title prefix stripped:** FinancialJuice titles arrive as `"FinancialJuice: <headline>"`; the
  prefix is stripped before any validation since the `source` field already carries that label.
- **No forced currency:** the feed is multi-currency/multi-topic by nature (politics, commodities,
  tech, central banks) — routed through `detect_currency()`/`is_forex_relevant()` like
  ForexLive/FXStreet, not force-assigned like the official central-bank feeds.
- **Tests:** 8 new tests in `test_fetch_news.py` (`TestHeadlineOnlySources`) — bypass applies only
  to the registered source, short titles are still rejected regardless of source, the data-print
  guard fires with and without the bypass active, and substantive-description items (FJElite
  pieces, FX Options Expiries) still validate through the normal path unaffected by the bypass.
  114/114 tests passing (106 previous + 8 new), 0 regressions.

## v8.69.1 (2026-07-23) — CESI narrative/panel divergence: fourth bug found (forecast→previous fallback)

### Engine — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`
- **User-reported:** narrative said "EUR CESI -17 net misses," the Economic Surprises modal showed
  INDEX -13.0 (BEATS 87, MISSES 127, N 234). Same class of divergence as v8.65.2, which already fixed
  three narrative-vs-panel mismatches (parse_num on currency-prefixed strings, missing inverse-indicator
  handling, missing noise-keyword filter) but evidently missed a fourth.
- **First checked whether -17 was stale:** re-ran this block's exact algorithm against the live
  `calendar-data/calendar.json` (generated today, 15:29 UTC) — it reproduced -17 exactly. Not a caching or
  staleness bug; the number was freshly (and correctly, per the code as written) computed.
- **Root cause found:** `_f = _parse_num(_ev.get("forecast"))` had no fallback to `previous`, unlike
  `ev.forecast || ev.previous` in `dashboard.js` `renderEconSurprises()` and `econ-surprises-modal.js`.
  Any event with a `previous` baseline but no explicit `forecast` field was silently dropped from the
  narrative's tally (`_f is None` → skipped) while the panel counted it. Confirmed: EUR's 90d population
  was 198 events here vs. 234 in the panel — 36 events missing purely from this gap. Beats also came out
  81 vs. the panel's 87.
- **Fixed:** added the same `forecast → previous` fallback, and updated the dedup key to use
  `forecast or previous` (matching the panel's dedup key) instead of `forecast` alone, so an event that
  only has a `previous` value doesn't fail to dedupe against itself across a feed re-poll.
- **Verified:** re-ran the corrected algorithm against the same live `calendar.json` — EUR beats now
  matches the panel exactly (87), total population is within 3 of the panel's 234 (237; the small residual
  is expected from the few seconds/minutes between when the panel's snapshot and this check were taken,
  not a remaining bug). AUD/GBP/USD spot-checked, no regressions.
- **Still an intentional simplification, not a full re-implementation:** as documented in the v8.65.2 note
  above, this block computes a raw (unweighted) beat/miss count over the 90d window, while the panel blends
  a decay-weighted (45d half-life) beat/miss ratio with a z-score index for series with ≥5 historical
  observations. Even with the event population now matching, the narrative's raw net and the panel's index
  will still differ in magnitude by design — e.g. EUR's raw net is now -41 (population-matched), which is
  *further* from the panel's -13.0 index than the old buggy -17 was, precisely because the raw count and
  the decay+z-score index are different statistics computed over the same (now-correct) population. The
  gap the user originally flagged (-17 vs -13.0, a difference of ~4) is actually within the same order of
  magnitude already characterized as expected/by-design in the v8.65.2 note (prior examples: -17 vs -14.8,
  -13 vs -11.2). The real, fixable defect here was the undercounted population, not the magnitude gap
  itself — that gap is inherent to reporting two different statistics side by side and won't fully close
  without turning the narrative into a full copy of the panel's index math, which remains an intentional
  non-goal for prose generation.

## v8.65.2 (2026-07-22) — Narrative CESI block: fixed currency-prefix parse failures, missing inverse-indicator handling, missing noise filter

### Engine — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`
- **User-reported:** Santiago compared the AI-generated Alerts & Market Signals prose against the Economic
  Surprises modal side by side — EUR: narrative text said "Economic Surprise Index (CESI) of -17 net misses"
  vs. the modal's INDEX (90D) -14.8 / BEATS 84 / MISSES 129; AUD: narrative said "-13 net misses" vs. modal
  INDEX -11.2 / BEATS 17 / MISSES 35 — and flagged the gap as larger than the documented (v8.51.15, intentional)
  raw-count-vs-decay-weighted-index difference.
- **Root cause (bug 1 — currency-prefix parsing):** `_parse_num()` stripped `%`/`K`/`M`/`B` via string
  replacement then called bare `float()`. Fails on currency-symbol-prefixed strings (`"$-226.8B"`, `"€-6.2B"`,
  `"A$1.791B"`) — every Trade Balance / Current Account event carries one of these (visible in the screenshot's
  event table: Greece/Spain/Italy Current Account, Euro Area Balance of Trade, etc.) — so those events silently
  `ValueError`'d and were dropped from beats/misses/total entirely. Same bug `dashboard.js` fixed in v8.25.8;
  never ported to this script. **Fix:** replaced with the sign-aware digit-strip parser (strip everything except
  digits/decimal point, restore sign from `-` anywhere in the original string) already used as source of truth in
  `_parseNum()` (dashboard.js), `_esmParseNum()` (econ-surprises-modal.js), and `_parse_num()`
  (fetch_economic_calendar.py).
- **Root cause (bug 2 — no inverse-indicator handling):** the block always scored `actual > forecast` as a beat,
  but for Unemployment Rate / Jobless Claims / deficit-type releases a *lower* actual is the positive surprise —
  every such release was tallied backwards (a good print counted as a miss). **Fix:** added the same
  `INVERSE_KW = ["unemployment", "jobless", "claims", "deficit"]` check the panel uses (`INVERSE_KW` in
  dashboard.js / `_ESM_INVERSE_KW` in econ-surprises-modal.js / `INVERSE_EVENTS` in fetch_economic_calendar.py).
- **Root cause (bug 3 — no noise filter):** the block only excluded `'myfxbook'` from its tally, while the panel
  excludes a much longer list (bond/note/gilt/JGB auctions, CFTC positioning, oil inventories, M2/M3/M4 money
  supply, TIC flows, etc. — all FX-irrelevant or duplicative). Those releases were diluting/skewing the
  narrative's beats/misses count. **Fix:** ported the full `NOISE_KW` list verbatim from dashboard.js /
  econ-surprises-modal.js.
- **Also added:** canonical-key dedup (`ccy` / canonical title with parentheticals + country-prefix stripped /
  actual / forecast) matching the modal's `seen` set, to avoid double-counting duplicate feed entries for the
  same release.
- **Still by design, unchanged:** the narrative figure remains an unweighted raw beats-minus-misses count over
  the 90d window (see v8.51.15 note) — not the panel's full decay-weighted (45d half-life) + impact-weighted +
  per-series-z-score INDEX. This fix makes the underlying **event population and beat/miss classification**
  consistent with the panel; the two numbers will still differ in magnitude by design (raw count vs. weighted
  index on a [-100,+100] scale), but should no longer diverge in sign or by 2-3x the way EUR (-17 vs -45
  beats-minus-misses) and AUD (-13 vs -18 beats-minus-misses) did before this fix.
- **Verified:** isolated harness test (`_parse_num` against 8 currency-prefixed/percent/suffixed strings; inverse
  logic against Unemployment Rate / Initial Jobless Claims / CPI YoY; noise filter against EIA Crude Oil
  Inventories / CFTC NC Net Positions / Germany ZEW Economic Sentiment Index / Myfxbook Sentiment) — all cases
  resolved correctly. `python3 -m py_compile` clean.

## v8.65.1 (2026-07-22) — MT5 EA: Composite panel footer formula label restored to readable word+% form (bug found & fixed same day)

### MT5 EA — `Global_Investing_FX_Terminal.mq5` (v3.343 → v3.345)
- **Change:** Composite panel footer formula label (bottom of the panel) reverted from the terse concatenated-code
  form `"COT25+MOM15+RTL18+CB18+CRY12+ESI12"` back to the pre-Momentum parenthesized/word/% style, updated for the
  current 6-factor weights: `"COT(25%)+Mom(15%)+Retail(18%)+CB(18%)+Carry(12%)+ESI(12%)"`.
- **Root cause:** the v8.39.0 session (v3.324/v3.325) that added the Momentum factor and rebalanced weights from
  COT30/Retail20/CB20/Carry15/ESI15 to COT25/Mom15/Retail18/CB18/Carry12/ESI12 also silently swapped this label
  to the terser abbreviated-code form — never called out as its own bullet in that changelog entry, since the
  session's focus was the scoring formula itself, not this display string.
- **Bug found and fixed same day, before v3.344 was compiled/shipped:** the first attempt (v3.344) picked between
  the wide and narrow label using a fixed width threshold (`w>RH(180)`) that did not guarantee the 57-char wide
  string actually fit the panel's character budget (`max_fc = (w-RH(8))/RH(4)`). At intermediate panel widths
  (`RH(180)` to `~RH(236)`) the code picked the wide label anyway and `StringSubstr()` truncated it mid-word
  (e.g. `"...+CB(18%)+Carry"`, `"...+CB(1"`) instead of falling back to the narrow label — confirmed by user
  screenshots at two different panel widths, both cut off mid-token. **Fix:** the choice is now driven directly
  by `max_fc` — `formula = (StringLen(formula_wide)<=max_fc) ? formula_wide : formula_narrow`, so the wide label
  is only ever used when it's guaranteed to fit; only the narrow label can be truncated, and that should not
  happen at any realistic panel width (22 chars, needs `w>=96`).
- **v3.344 superseded by v3.345 same day** — v3.344 was never delivered as a separate compiled release, so both
  the label restoration and the threshold-selection fix are shipped together under v3.345.

## v8.64.0 (2026-07-22) — Gemini model cascade upgraded to gemini-3.6-flash / gemini-3.5-flash-lite; removed deprecated sampling params

### Scripts — generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Change:** Upgraded both non-primary tiers of the Gemini model cascade used across narrative generation,
  signals, catalysts, currency drivers, and session-context/composite-score commentary:
  - Stable fallback tier: `gemini-3.5-flash` → `gemini-3.6-flash` (all 5 cascade sites: `_NARRATIVE_MODEL_CASCADE`,
    `_SIGNALS_MODEL_CASCADE`, `_CAT_MODEL_STABLE`, `_SC_MODEL_STABLE`, `_DRIVERS_MODEL_STABLE`).
  - `GEMINI_MODEL_LITE`: `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` → `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`.
  - Primary tier (`GEMINI_MODEL = gemini-3-flash-preview`) left untouched — still a preview endpoint with no GA
    replacement in this release.
- **Rationale:** both new models are GA per Google's 2026-07-22 announcement. `gemini-3.6-flash` is 17% more
  token-efficient with lower output pricing ($7.50/1M vs. $9.00/1M) than the model it replaces. `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`
  posts materially better reasoning/multimodal scores than `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` (HLE 18.0% vs. 11.0%; CharXIV
  74.5% vs. 63.7%) and improved tool-call reliability for subagent workflows, at the same price tier.
- **Change:** Removed `temperature` (0.15) and `candidateCount` (1) from the Gemini `generationConfig` payload in
  `call_gemini()`. Google's announcement deprecates both sampling params as of `gemini-3.6-flash` /
  `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` — silently ignored on those two models, HTTP 400 on any later generation. The prior
  "auditor/fallback should not drift" intent behind `temperature=0.15` is now expressed as an explicit determinism
  instruction appended to `system_instruction`, per Google's recommended migration path. `candidateCount=1` was
  simply dropped (1 is already the default).
- **Docs:** Updated `call_gemini()`'s docstring and the architecture-level comments in
  `generate_narrative_via_gemini()`, `generate_signals_via_gemini()`, and the catalysts/drivers/session-context
  stable-cascade comments to reference the new model names. Left untouched the comments that quote specific
  historical incidents (2026-07-01, 2026-07-07, 2026-07-21 runs) — those describe what actually happened with
  `gemini-3.5-flash`/`gemini-3.1-flash-lite` at the time and would be factually wrong if rewritten.
- **Not yet done:** no production run has been made against the new models yet — first live run after this change
  should be spot-checked for output-format drift (JSON structure, marker formatting) given the removed sampling
  params, per the `_normalize_llm_bulk_markers()` note that different Gemini versions aren't guaranteed to format
  identically run to run.

## v8.63.1 (2026-07-22) — NZD: fixed "current rate" fields reporting a stale laggy-source value despite correct merged history

### Scripts — `fetch_rates.py`
- **Reported symptom:** `rates/NZD.json`'s top-level `rateDate`/health.json's NZD entry showed 2.25%
  (dated 2026-06-01, source `BIS-CBPOL`), even though RBNZ hiked the OCR to 2.5% on 2026-07-08 and
  `observations[0]` in the very same file already correctly showed `2026-07-01 / 2.5`.
- **Root cause:** Source 0-A (`ff-calendar-actual`) correctly captured the RBNZ hike same-day via its
  3-day lookback window (v14.2). Once that window closed (2026-07-11), later runs fell through to
  Source 1 (BIS-CBPOL), a monthly series that hadn't yet published July's figure and kept returning
  June's pre-hike value. `merge_observations()`'s month-keyed map correctly preserved the July bucket
  from the earlier run (it never overwrites a newer month with an older one), so the observation
  history itself stayed correct. But the *top-level* `rate_value`/`observation_date`/`lastSource`
  fields written to `rates/{CCY}.json` and `health.json` were taken directly from this run's raw fetch
  (`entry`), completely bypassing the merged result — so the "current rate" reported to the dashboard
  regressed to the stale BIS-CBPOL value even though the correct one was sitting one field over in the
  same file. A regression guard added earlier in this session (compares candidate `ref_date` against
  the cached `rateDate`) could not catch this: it only fires on a *strictly older* new date, and once
  the cached `rateDate` itself was regressed to June, subsequent June-dated BIS-CBPOL fetches compared
  equal to it, not older, so the guard never triggered against an already-poisoned baseline.
- **Fix:** after `merge_observations()`, if `merged_obs[0]` (the most recent entry in history) is dated
  later than this run's own fetch, derive `rate_value`/`observation_date`/`lastSource` (and the
  corresponding `health.json` entry + `ok`/`warning`/`fallback` status) from `merged_obs[0]` instead of
  the raw fetch. Since `merge_observations()` doesn't retain a per-observation source, the source label
  in this case is taken from the previous on-disk `lastSource` if its `rateDate` matches, else labelled
  `"<source> (merged history)"` rather than mislabeled with this run's (older, laggy) source.
- **One-time data correction:** `rates/NZD.json` (`rateDate` → `2026-07-08`, `lastSource` →
  `ff-calendar-actual`) and `rates/health.json`'s NZD entry (`rate` → `2.5`, `source` →
  `ff-calendar-actual`, `date` → `2026-07-08`) corrected to match the already-correct
  `observations[0]`. No observation history was altered. Verified against the RBNZ's own published
  rate decision, RNZ, and ForexFactory.
- **Scope note:** audited all other currencies for the same `rateDate` vs. `observations[0]` value
  mismatch pattern — AUD/EUR/JPY/NOK/SEK show a date-format difference only (`rateDate` is the actual
  CB decision date, `observations[0].date` is its month-start bucket), with matching values. NZD was
  the only currency with an actual value mismatch.

## v8.63.0 (2026-07-22) — EUR: removed stale `MANUAL_OVERRIDES` freeze; migrated primary EUR reference from ECB DFR to MRO

### Scripts — `fetch_rates.py`
- **Reported symptom:** user flagged EUR rate as "desactualizada" versus ForexFactory, Myfxbook, and
  Trading Economics, all of which showed 2.40% while the site showed 2.25%.
- **Root cause (two separate issues):**
  1. **Real bug:** `MANUAL_OVERRIDES['EUR'] = ('2.25', '2026-06-11')` was re-added on 2026-06-11 to work
     around a same-day 403 from ECB SDMX/BIS, in direct violation of the explicit
     `# Never add EUR here` rule (previously enforced after the v7.13.42 incident). No CHANGELOG entry
     was made when it was added. Because `MANUAL_OVERRIDES` populates `final_rates` in Step 0-B, *before*
     Step 1's primary-source loop — and Step 1 skips any currency already present in `final_rates` — the
     override permanently blocked `fetch_eur_ecb()` from running at all. The value sat frozen for 41 days,
     and `health.json` never flagged it because `manual-override` is in `OFFICIAL_SOURCES`.
  2. **Not actually a bug, but a real difference:** the 2.25% figure itself was correct — it's the ECB
     Deposit Facility Rate (DFR), confirmed live against the ECB's own published rates. ForexFactory/
     Myfxbook/Trading Economics quote the Main Refinancing Operations rate (MRO), which is +15bp above
     DFR under the corridor in force since 2024-09-18 (was +50bp before that). GUIDELINES.md had
     explicitly documented DFR as the required institutional (Bloomberg/Eikon) standard.
- **Decision:** rather than just removing the stale override and keeping DFR, explicitly decided to
  switch the primary EUR reference to MRO, to align with the retail/FX-portal convention — see
  GUIDELINES.md "EUR rate" section for full rationale and the resulting non-negotiable rules.
- **Fix:**
  1. Removed the `EUR` entry from `MANUAL_OVERRIDES`.
  2. `fetch_eur_ecb()`: swapped ECB SDMX series priority to try MRO (`MRR_FR`) first, DFR second;
     added `ECB_MRO_DFR_SPREAD_PP = 0.15` and convert any DFR-basis result (SDMX DFR fallback, ECB HTML
     page, BIS CBPOL — which reports DFR for XM/eurozone) to an MRO-equivalent, labelled with a
     `-DFR+spread` source suffix. `global-rates.com` already quotes MRO — no conversion needed there.
  3. Registered the three new `+spread` source labels in `OFFICIAL_SOURCES` so they aren't flagged as
     fallback in `health.json`.
  4. Updated ECB HTML scraper regex to look for "Main refinancing" first, "Deposit facility" second
     (converted).

### Site — `rates/EUR.json`, `rates/health.json`
- Restated all 31 historical observations from DFR to MRO basis using the verified corridor-spread
  formula above (cross-checked against Bundesbank's historical rate table and FRED `ECBMRRFR`, e.g.
  2025-07 MRO=2.15% matches FRED's daily series for that period exactly). Current value now 2.40%
  (2026-06 / 2026-07), matching ForexFactory/Myfxbook/Trading Economics.
- `health.json` EUR entry updated: `source: "manual-override"` → `"ECB-SDMX"`, `rate: "2.25"` → `"2.40"`.

### Engine — `.github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml` (CB Rate Expectations bias engine)
- **Cross-repo dependency found while auditing consumers of `rates/EUR.json`:** this workflow's OIS-bias
  classifier (`classify()`, `CREDIT_SPREAD_EUR_3M_SLOPE = 0.22`, 10bp/20bp hold bands) is calibrated
  against DFR and reads `rates/EUR.json` only as a last-resort fallback when `FRED ECBDFR` fails —
  labelled in-code as "DFR fallback to rates/EUR.json". After this change that file is MRO-basis, so an
  unconverted fallback would have silently fed MRO values into DFR-calibrated thresholds.
- **Fix:** fallback now subtracts `ECB_MRO_DFR_SPREAD_PP` (0.15) from the `rates/EUR.json` value before
  use, restoring DFR-basis input to this module without touching its calibration. Added a note in
  GUIDELINES.md warning any future code reading `rates/EUR.json` for EUR to check basis before use.
- **Not affected:** the Tier-1 spot ESTER-vs-DFR structural check and the `ESTER overnight (+7bp DFR
  normalisation)` OIS source table entry — both operate on the `dfr` variable computed above, which is
  unchanged by this fix.
- Not checked in this session: `assets/dashboard.js` Carry Differential tooltip ("CB policy rate is the
  ceiling") was reviewed and requires no change — it's generic across all G10 currencies, and for EUR
  specifically is now *more* accurate than before (MRO genuinely sits above the overnight rate, unlike
  DFR, which is the corridor floor).
- **Verification:** manual read-through of the SDMX/HTML/BIS conversion paths and the workflow fallback
  edit; no live network access to ECB/FRED/BIS in this environment to execute a real fetch. Recommend
  running `fetch_rates.py` once for real and confirming the printed source label is `ECB-SDMX` (not a
  `+spread` variant) and prints `2.40%`, and separately confirming `workflow_meetings.yml`'s next EUR
  bias classification still uses a DFR-scale value in its log line, before the next scheduled runs.
- **Scope boundary:** did not touch the ESTER Tier-1/Tier-2 checks, `CREDIT_SPREAD_EUR_3M_SLOPE`, or any
  other calibrated constant in `workflow_meetings.yml` beyond the single fallback conversion above.

## v8.62.4 (2026-07-21) — `generate_narrative_signals.py`: fixed silent multi-day `currency-drivers.json` staleness — bulk marker parser required an exact-line match, zeroing out all currencies on any model formatting deviation

### Engine — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`
- **Reported symptom:** `currency-drivers.json` stuck at `generated_at: 2026-07-17T07:58:38Z` for 5 days
  while the sibling `currency-catalysts.json` (same daily `generate-structural-context.yml` run) kept
  refreshing normally. Not visible anywhere in the site UI (no "last updated" indicator on the drivers
  panel) — only caught by comparing `_inputs_snap.EUR.cot_we` inside the stale file ("2026-07-07") against
  the live `cot-data/EUR.json` ("2026-07-14", updated by the Saturday COT workflow days earlier).
- **Root cause (confirmed from run #106 Actions log, 2026-07-21 08:18 UTC):** the run was NOT idle —
  `_drivers_inputs_changed()` correctly detected the COT week rollover and triggered a regeneration
  attempt, and the Gemini bulk call itself succeeded ("✅ Drivers (bulk): via Gemini cascade
  (gemini-3.5-flash)"). But `_parse_driver_prose_bulk()` then reported **"0 notes parsed from bulk
  response" for all 8 currencies** — the marker regexes (`_DRV_CCY_MARKER_RE` / `_DRV_MARKER_RE`) required
  an exact `## CCY` / `### PAIR` line with nothing else on it (`^##\s*([A-Z]{3})\s*$`). Any formatting
  deviation from the `gemini-3.5-flash` stable-cascade fallback model — bold markdown wrapping, a trailing
  currency name, a wrapping code fence, none of which the raw response text was logged to confirm — would
  silently zero out every currency at once. The existing fallback logic ("all keys failed → keep previous
  file, don't update `_inputs_snap`, retry next run") then masked this as an API failure and retried
  identically every day, hitting the same exact-match parsing wall each time — a parsing bug indistinguishable
  in the logs from a genuine multi-day API outage.
- **Fix:**
  1. Added `_normalize_llm_bulk_markers()` — strips code-fence delimiter lines and markdown bold/italic
     decoration on marker-candidate lines (short lines containing `#`) before parsing, applied in both
     `_parse_driver_prose_bulk()` and `_parse_catalysts_bulk()` (the latter uses the identical marker
     pattern and is equally exposed to this failure class, even though it happened to succeed in run #106).
  2. Loosened `_DRV_CCY_MARKER_RE`, `_DRV_MARKER_RE`, and `_CAT_CCY_MARKER_RE` to tolerate trailing text
     after the symbol on the marker line (e.g. `## EUR — Euro`) instead of requiring an exact line match,
     using a negative lookahead (`##(?!#)`) so the currency-level marker still can't accidentally match a
     `### PAIR` line.
  3. Added a diagnostic log line in both bulk parsers: when a non-empty raw response parses to zero
     currencies, print the response length and first 300 chars, so a genuine future format regression is
     visible in the Actions log instead of looking identical to an API failure.
- **Not fixed by this change:** the underlying reason `gemini-3.5-flash` (vs `gemini-3-flash-preview`)
  may have deviated from the requested format could not be confirmed — the raw response text was not
  captured in the failing runs, only the parsed-to-zero symptom. The new diagnostic logging (item 3 above)
  is what will confirm the exact deviation if/when this recurs.
- **Verification:** `python3 -m py_compile scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py` — no syntax errors.
  `python3 -m pytest scripts/tests/` — 158/158 passed. Manually verified the loosened regex + normalization
  against four simulated `gemini-3.5-flash` deviation patterns (bold-wrapped headers, trailing currency
  name, code-fence wrapping, exact-match control) — all four now parse correctly, and confirmed no
  collision between the `## CCY` and `### PAIR` markers in nested parsing. No live Gemini/Groq call made
  in this session (write access to trigger a real generation run not available in this environment) —
  validate against the next `generate-structural-context.yml` run's log and `currency-drivers.json` output.

## v8.62.3 (2026-07-21) — `generate_narrative_signals.py`: currency-catalysts prompts enforce currency-level framing, stop pair-ticker-centric openings

### Engine — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`
- **Reported symptom:** several `currency-catalysts.json` paragraphs (feeding the "MACRO DRIVERS" block
  in `heatmap-modal.js`'s Rel. Strength modal) opened with a pair ticker + live price quote, e.g. "NZD/USD
  is trading at 0.5841...", "EUR/USD is trading at 1.1417...", "USD/JPY is testing the 162.47 level...",
  "AUD/USD is holding at 0.7001...". Six of ten currencies (USD, GBP, CAD, CHF, NOK, SEK) already framed
  correctly at the currency level ("The Swiss franc is trading at...", "Sterling is trading near..."), so
  the failure was inconsistent, not systematic.
- **Root cause:** `currency-catalysts.json` is the top macro layer of the terminal — one level above the
  per-pair driver notes (`currency-drivers.json`) and per-pair AI signals (`signals.json`), both of which
  are explicitly pair-ticker-led by design. None of `CATALYSTS_SYSTEM_BULK`, `CATALYSTS_SYSTEM_TAVILY`, or
  `CATALYSTS_SYSTEM_INTERNAL` prohibited pair-ticker+price openings, and the shared Technical Levels
  context block (`_build_technical_levels_context()`) supplies each currency's live pair price alongside
  its SMA20/50/200 — the model was using that price as the paragraph's opening frame rather than as one
  supporting descriptive clause, duplicating the job of the pair-level layer below it.
- **Fix:** added a "CURRENCY-LEVEL FRAMING, NOT PAIR-LEVEL" clause to all three catalyst system prompts,
  explicitly forbidding a "CCY1/CCY2 is trading at X" opening and directing currency-level prose instead
  (e.g. "the euro is trading near a one-week low against the dollar"; DXY for USD) — following the
  convention already working correctly in 6 of 10 currencies. Also tightened the shared Technical Levels
  citation instruction in the catalysts `user_prompt` (previously "cite as one sentence of descriptive
  market structure") to explicitly disallow using it as the opening sentence.
- **Verification:** `python3 -m py_compile scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py` — no syntax errors.
  `python3 -m pytest scripts/tests/` — 158/158 passed. No live Gemini/Groq call made in this session
  (write access to trigger a real generation run not available in this environment) — validate against the
  next `generate-structural-context.yml` run's `currency-catalysts.json` output.

## v8.62.2 (2026-07-20) — `deploy-pages.yml`: split concurrency (build vs deploy) to eliminate GitHub Pages deploy backlog causing stale frontend after confirmed data-workflow writes

### Site — `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`
- **Reported symptom:** economic calendar workflow (`update-ff-calendar.yml`) confirmed writing a fresh
  actual (NZD Inflation Rate QoQ, actual=1.5%) to `calendar-data/ff_calendar.json` and pushing to `main`
  successfully, but the live terminal's Economic Calendar panel (`assets/calendar-panel.js`) still showed
  the pre-release "—" placeholder ~14 minutes later — despite `calendar-panel.js` already polling every
  2 minutes with a minute-bucketed cache-buster (added in its own v1.6, 2026-07-15, specifically to defeat
  GitHub Pages' Fastly CDN edge cache).
- **Root cause:** `deploy-pages.yml` triggers on every push to `main` with no path filter. `update-ff-
  calendar.yml`, `update-intraday-quotes.yml`, `forex-news.yml`, `update-fx-liquidity.yml`, and
  `update-ohlc.yml` all push independently every 2-10 minutes, with heavier overlap during release
  windows. The workflow's single, workflow-level `concurrency: {group: "pages", cancel-in-progress:
  false}` block (deliberately set to `false` to avoid a *deploy* being interrupted mid-way — a probable
  cause of earlier intermittent failures) covered BOTH the `build` and `deploy` jobs together. Because
  `cancel-in-progress: false` runs every queued run to completion in FIFO order with none skipped, a burst
  of pushes during a busy window could queue several minutes of already-stale builds/deploys ahead of the
  commit that actually mattered — so the commit with the fresh NZD actual sat in the backlog while the live
  site kept serving an older published artifact. `calendar-panel.js`'s cache-buster could not help: it only
  forces a fresh CDN edge fetch of a URL, which still resolves to whatever artifact GitHub Pages has
  actually finished deploying — not the newest one sitting in the queue. This is the same class of symptom
  logged in `calendar-panel.js` v1.6 ("4 new actuals, panel still showed '—' 23min later," 2026-07-15) — that
  fix addressed CDN caching only and never touched deploy-queue depth, so the underlying symptom recurred.
- **Fix:** moved `concurrency` from workflow-level to per-job. `build` (artifact packaging — idempotent, no
  external side effects) now uses its own group `pages-build` with `cancel-in-progress: true`, so a newer
  push cancels any in-flight build for a now-superseded commit instead of letting it run to completion —
  only the latest commit's build ever proceeds to the deploy step. `deploy` keeps its own group
  `pages-deploy` with `cancel-in-progress: false`, unchanged from before, so an in-progress publish is still
  never interrupted mid-way.
- **Verification:** `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` — valid YAML, `build`/`deploy` jobs each
  carry their own `concurrency` block, no leftover workflow-level block. No live GitHub Actions run performed
  in this session (write access to trigger/observe Actions runs not available in this environment) — the
  fix should be validated against real run timestamps in the Actions tab after the next deploy, comparing
  the `update-ff-calendar.yml` commit time to the corresponding `deploy-pages.yml` "deploy" job start time
  during a busy release window.

## v8.62.1 (2026-07-20) — `generate_narrative_signals.py`: raised signals/driver-note density to institutional sales-desk level (JPM/MUFG/Scotia benchmark) and added a deterministic Technical Levels (LEVELS) component to signals

### Scripts — `generate_narrative_signals.py`
- **Context:** compared against four live institutional references (JPM G10 FX sales-desk color, MUFG FX Weekly,
  Scotiabank Daily FX Update, ING FX Daily) — signals and driver notes were the only genre in the pipeline
  mapping to the "terminal alert" register, but at 2-3 compressed sentences they fell noticeably short of the
  JPM sales-desk-note density (~150-250 words per pair, explicit trade bias, named technical levels, risk
  clause) that this terminal benchmarks its output quality against.
- **New — Rule 5d (LEVELS) in `SIGNALS_SYSTEM`:** signals now cite the deterministic SMA20/50/200 cluster and
  position label from `ai-analysis/technical-levels.json` (written by `calculate_technical_levels.py` — no LLM
  involved in the calculation) when an entry exists for the signal's currency, mirroring the JPM-style
  moving-average-cluster framing (e.g. "Cable moving-average cluster: 1.3394/04"). Never fabricates a level
  type the pipeline doesn't compute (no Fibonacci, no pivots); silently omits LEVELS when no entry exists for
  that currency, per the same no-fabrication discipline already used for news/signal context.
- **`build_context()`:** now injects the Technical Levels block (previously only consumed by the
  currency-catalysts prompt) so it is available to both `generate_signals()` and the narrative prompt.
- **Density target raised 2-3 → 5-7 sentences per signal**, and driver notes (all three prompt variants —
  `DRIVERS_SYSTEM_INTERNAL`, `DRIVERS_SYSTEM_PROSE`, `DRIVERS_SYSTEM_PROSE_TAVILY`) raised 2-3 → 4-5 sentences
  per pair. Reference examples (NZD/USD divergence signal, Rule 10 multi-layer examples) rewritten to the new
  density to serve as in-prompt few-shot targets.
- **Token/char budget increases to prevent truncation at the new density:**
  - Signals `text` field truncation cap: 600 → 1200 chars.
  - Gemini signals call: `max_tokens` 3000 → 4500.
  - Groq fallback signals calls: `max_tokens` 1100 → 1900 (primary + retry + extra-key variants), 900 → 1600
    (secondary retry).
  - Dedicated COT-OIS single-signal prompt: density instruction 2-3 → 5-7 sentences + explicit Risk clause
    requirement; `max_tokens` 550 → 950.
  - Driver notes (Gemini bulk call, both search and Tavily-fed variants): `max_tokens` already at 8000 —
    sufficient headroom for the 2-3 → 4-5 sentence increase across all 56 pairs, no change needed.
- **Not changed:** the signals panel remains a compact triage list (critical/warning/info) by design — this is
  a density increase within the existing terminal-alert genre, not a new "research note" product tier. A
  distinct longer-form desk-note product (JPM/Scotia multi-paragraph style, with explicit entry/target/stop)
  was discussed and deliberately deferred as a separate scope decision, not implemented here.
- **Verification:** `python3 -m py_compile` clean. No live Gemini/Groq re-run performed in this session (no
  API network access in this environment) — `ai-analysis/signals.json` was hand-reconstructed applying the new
  Rule 5d/5-7-sentence prompt logic to the existing 2026-07-20T21:14:39Z signal set as a stopgap; a
  `workflow_dispatch` run against this patched script is needed to confirm the model's native output matches
  the hand-reconstruction and to get evidence-array/watch-level fields the model would choose independently.

## v8.62.0 (2026-07-20) — `generate_narrative_signals.py`: Guard 8 CB-decision hallucination check was corrupting legitimate COT-vs-OIS divergence signals (false positive on "hike bias"); added mandatory Risk/invalidation clause to signal text

### Scripts — `generate_narrative_signals.py`
- **Found while reviewing a shipped signal:** the 2026-07-20 21:12 run's NZD/USD COT-vs-OIS divergence signal
  shipped with a broken lead sentence — `"RBNZ 2.5%. With NZD long% at a 15.2% extreme..."` — a sentence
  fragment with no verb and no lead-in, in place of what should have been a full COT-positioning setup clause.
- **Root cause 1 (false positive):** `_DECISION_RE_DECISION` matched the bare word `hike` regardless of
  whether it functioned as a verb ("RBNZ **hiked** rates") or a noun in market-expectation phrasing ("RBNZ
  **hike bias**", "hike odds", "hike priced"). The latter describes speculative positioning against a *future*
  CB decision — exactly the COT-vs-OIS divergence framing Rule 5 requires — not a claim that the CB already
  acted today. Guard 8 (`_strip_cb_decision_hallucination`) treated it as an invented past-tense decision and
  stripped it.
- **Root cause 2 (splice mechanics):** when the flagged clause was the *first* sentence in the signal text
  (no preceding `". "` boundary), `text.rfind(". ", 0, m.start())` returned `-1`, and the fallback set
  `sent_start = 0` — silently discarding the entire lead-in (in this case, the COT positioning detail that
  motivated the signal) rather than just the flagged clause. The replacement template `f"{display} {rate_str}."`
  was also grammatically incomplete (e.g. `"RBNZ 2.5%."` — no verb).
- **Fix:**
  1. `_DECISION_RE_DECISION` now has a negative lookahead excluding `bias|odds|bet(s)|wager(s)|expectation(s)|
     pricing|priced|probability|prob(s)|chance(s)|speculation|view(s)|call(s)|outlook` immediately after the
     decision verb, so expectation/positioning phrasing no longer trips the guard. Verified against both the
     failing case and genuine hallucinated decision claims ("RBNZ hiked rates to 2.75% today", "BoE held rates
     at 4.00%") — the guard still correctly fires on the latter.
  2. When no prior sentence boundary exists, `_strip_cb_decision_hallucination` now clips from the matched
     clause forward (`m.start()`) instead of from index 0, so legitimate leading context can never be
     silently discarded even if a future false positive slips through.
  3. The fallback replacement is now a complete clause with a verb (`"{CB} holds at {rate}%."` /
     `"{CB} remains on hold."`) instead of a bare `"{CB} {rate}%."` fragment.
- **Also added:** Rule 14 in `SIGNALS_SYSTEM` — every signal's closing sentence must now include an explicit
  `"Risk: [specific condition]."` clause naming what would invalidate the read (distinct from the existing
  "watch level," which only cites the next data/event timing). Matches the discipline used in the Scotiabank/
  MUFG/JPM sales-desk notes this terminal benchmarks against (e.g. JPM's "Risk: signal remains verbal and
  USD/JPY resumes grind higher"). Implemented as a text-composition rule only — no JSON schema or frontend
  change required, since `text` is already free-form.
- **Verification:** isolated regex test against the exact failing string (`"...vs rbnz hike bias ahead of
  q2 cpi..."` → no match, correctly not stripped) and against two genuine hallucinated-decision strings
  (both still correctly matched and stripped). No changes to `_CB_MAP_DECISION`, `_CB_DISPLAY_DECISION`, or
  any calling site's signature — drop-in fix.

### Site — access.html
- **Context:** Santiago rejected the pill/badge polish pass on the 2x2 `.companion-grid` cards (Standalone MT5
  indicators) — the underlying complaint was that four smaller images don't fill the available space well and
  look uninspired next to the "Additional Coverage" tabbed showcase further up the page, which shows one large,
  uncropped screenshot at a time. He asked whether that same layout idea could be adapted for Companion Tools.
- **Design decision:** The Additional Coverage `.showcase`/`.showcase-tab`/`.showcase-slide` component itself
  was not reused directly — that pattern is built for six read-only preview panels (no per-item pricing or
  CTAs). Companion Tools needs a per-product price tag, "View on MQL5" link, and (for two of the four items)
  a "Read the guide" link, all changing together with the selected item. Built a parallel, independently-scoped
  component instead: `.companion-showcase` (230px list + large detail column), `.companion-tab` /
  `.companion-tab-tag` (left list, name + colored availability/price tag), `.companion-slide` (large image,
  1.95 aspect ratio, `object-fit: contain` — no cropping, same safeguard as the corrected `.companion-thumb`
  fix), and `.companion-preview-desc` / `.companion-actions-set` (description + CTA pills swapped per
  selected item below the image). CTAs changed from plain text links to bordered pill buttons
  (`.companion-pill` / `.companion-pill-accent`) for a more marketplace-like affordance.
- **Why a separate component instead of reusing showcase classes:** identical class names
  (`.showcase-tab`/`.showcase-slide`) reused across two sections on the same page would let a click in one
  section's JS `querySelectorAll` toggle state in the other. Companion Tools gets its own classes and its own
  independently-scoped activation/keyboard-nav JS block (`companionTabs`, `activateCompanion()`), mirroring the
  Additional Coverage script's structure and behavior (click + arrow-key tablist navigation) without sharing
  any selectors.
- **Lightbox:** `.companion-slide` added to the existing lightbox's `querySelectorAll` list so the large
  preview image still opens full-size on click, using each slide's own `data-caption`.
- **Removed:** the now-unused `.companion-grid` / `.companion-card` / `.companion-thumb` / `.companion-tag` /

  replaced by the new component.

## v8.59.0 (2026-07-19) — Companion Tools redesign, Monte Carlo Equity Projection guide, access.html scroll-spy fix

### Frontend — access.html (Companion Tools / Standalone MT5 indicators)
- **Context:** Santiago published a fourth standalone MT5 indicator, Monte Carlo Equity Projection (MQL5
  Market product #186259), and asked whether the "Additional Coverage" tab-left/preview-right pattern used
  elsewhere on the page would be an industry-standard way to present it. Evaluated against the actual
  purpose of that pattern (switching between views of *one* product) versus the Companion Tools use case
  (four independently priced, separately purchasable products) — the tab/preview pattern was rejected as a
  category mismatch; the card grid (`.companion-grid`) was already the correct pattern but lacked
  thumbnails, leaving the section as text-only despite screenshot assets already existing unused in the repo.
- **Fix:**
  - `.companion-grid` changed from a 3-column seamless grid (`gap: 2px`, shared borders) to a 2×2 grid of
    individually bordered cards (`gap: 16px`) to accommodate a fourth card and a thumbnail per card.
  - Added `.companion-thumb` (150px fixed-height, `object-fit: cover`, `object-position: top`, subtle
    scale-up on card hover) to each of the four cards: CSI Currency Strength (`screenshot-ea-csi.png`,
    already in repo), Carry Trade Monitor (`screenshot-ea-carry.png`, already in repo), Institutional Risk
    Manager (`screenshot-ea-risk-manager.png`, new), and the new Monte Carlo Equity Projection card
    (`screenshot-monte-carlo-equity.png`, new).
  - New Monte Carlo Equity Projection card tagged "Available on MQL5" (per the no-"free"-copy rule in
    GUIDELINES.md — same convention as CSI and Carry Trade Monitor, both free products), with a "Read the
    guide →" link to the new guide page.
  - Removed the now-obsolete mobile `.companion-card + .companion-card` border rule (left/top border swap),
    which only applied to the old seamless-grid layout.
- **Scroll-spy bug fix (subnav — "MT5 Indicators" click highlighting "Getting Started"):** root cause was the
  `IntersectionObserver` callback taking `entries[0]` from the batch as the active target. On an anchor-jump
  click (not a smooth scroll), multiple targets can intersect in the same batch — `#activation` (Getting
  Started) was still intersecting the top rootMargin band at the same instant `#companion-heading` (MT5
  Indicators) entered, and `entries[0]` reflected `observe()` registration order (`#activation` first), not
  visual/document order. Fixed by keeping a persistent `intersecting` state map per target and, on each
  callback, selecting the last (bottom-most, in document order) target currently intersecting — this
  correctly reflects the section the user actually jumped to.

### New page — guide-monte-carlo-simulator.html
- New guide for Monte Carlo Equity Projection (MQL5 Market product #186259), built from the
  `guide-csi-indicator.html` template: bootstrap-resampling methodology run on the account's own closed-deal
  history (no assumed return distribution, no external feed, no `WebRequest`), the percentile equity cone
  (p5/p25/p50/p75/p95), the risk metrics strip (VaR, CVaR, Calmar ratio, probability of ruin), the checklist
  verdict (tradeable / caution / needs review / not tradeable), installation, and configuration options.
  Google Trends confirmed stable global search volume for "monte carlo simulation" with informational-finance
  related queries/entities, the same signal pattern that justified `guide-csi-indicator.html`.
- Added `screenshot-ea-risk-manager.png` and `screenshot-monte-carlo-equity.png` to `assets/`.
- Added the guide to the canonical site menu (Guides section, GUIDELINES.md) and to all 17 pages that carry
  the site menu (16 existing pages + the new guide's own self-reference), to `sitemap.xml` (with
  `image:image` entries, `priority 0.7`, `changefreq monthly` — same tier as `guide-csi-indicator.html`), and
  to the site README's Guides list.

### Docs

- Site `README.md` — added Monte Carlo Equity Projection guide to the Guides list.

## v8.58.6 (2026-07-18) — generate_narrative_signals.py: banned bare CB-status opener in weekend narrative

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py (NARRATIVE_SYSTEM_CLOSED)
- **Context:** Santiago flagged the live weekend narrative opening with a bare fragment — "Fed on hold at
  3.75%." — and asked whether that matches how Scotiabank, MUFG, JPM Sales & Trading, and ING actually open
  their notes (checked against four uploaded research PDFs, all dated 10–17 July 2026). None of the ~24
  analyst paragraphs across those four desks opens with an isolated CB-status tag; all lead with the
  catalyst folded into a causal clause (e.g. ING: "The dollar stayed under pressure as PPI confirmed that
  inflation pressure eased in June").
- **Root cause:** `NARRATIVE_SYSTEM_CLOSED`'s STYLE example already models the correct pattern (opens with
  "Iran-Strait of Hormuz closure risk dominates the weekend tape..."), and the prompt separately documents
  this exact failure mode for per-session CLOSED notes ("USD/JPY +0.11%. Fed on hold." — flagged as "no
  cause, just the move" under Rule 12) — but that warning only covered session notes, not the main weekend
  narrative's own opening sentence, leaving a gap the model fell into.
- **Fix:** added an explicit CRITICAL RULE to `NARRATIVE_SYSTEM_CLOSED` requiring the opening sentence to be
  a framed causal/forward-looking clause rather than a standalone CB-status fragment, with a WRONG/CORRECT
  pair mirroring the existing Rule 12 example. `NARRATIVE_SYSTEM` (live, market-open prompt) was left
  untouched — its Rule 6 lead-variation examples already anchor every CB-differential opener to a specific
  pair, so the bare-tag failure mode is specific to the weekend/closed prompt.
- **Verification:** `ast.parse()` passed on the modified file.
- **Not done:** did not re-run the pipeline against live data to confirm the model complies with the new
  rule on the next weekend generation — this is prompt-only guidance, not a hard validator, so recommend
  Santiago spot-check the next Saturday/Sunday narrative output.

## v8.58.2 (2026-07-17) — Fixed public leak of raw Gemini key fragments; confirmed technical-levels wiring

### Security fix — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`, `.github/workflows/generate-ai-narrative.yml`, `.github/workflows/generate-structural-context.yml`
- **Context:** Santiago found `ai-analysis/gemini-quota-state.json` committed in the PUBLIC site repo containing
  a `"counts"` map keyed by `"fingerprint"` strings (e.g. `Qpy9sk`, `YpRVYA`, `jvHD8A`). Traced these to
  `gemini_budget_ok()` / `gemini_budget_record()` in `generate_narrative_signals.py`, which derived the
  fingerprint as `api_key[-6:]` — the literal last 6 characters of the real, live Gemini API key, not a hash.
  This file is deliberately committed to the public repo by `generate-ai-narrative.yml` and
  `generate-structural-context.yml` (the public repo is the only persistent storage available between
  ephemeral Actions runs) — the exposure was in the fingerprint method, not the commit itself.
- **Fix:** added `_key_fingerprint()` — `hashlib.sha256(api_key.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]` — and switched
  `gemini_budget_ok()`, `gemini_budget_record()`, and the console-log fingerprint in `load_gemini_keys()` to
  use it instead of a raw key substring. Same duplicate-detection and per-key budgeting behavior, but the
  persisted/logged identifier can no longer be used to reconstruct any part of a real secret.
- **Also renamed** the state file from `ai-analysis/gemini-quota-state.json` to
  `ai-analysis/call-budget-state.json` — the old name named the AI provider directly in a public repo path,
  which is the same "no internal architecture exposure in public-facing copy" principle GUIDELINES.md already
  applies to visible copy, just applied to a file path instead. Updated all references in both workflow files
  (`cp`/`git add` steps) and deleted the old, now-orphaned `ai-analysis/gemini-quota-state.json` (containing
  the real leaked fragments) from the public repo — nothing will write to it again under the old name, so it
  would otherwise have lingered indefinitely.
- **Not done — Santiago's call:** the leaked fragments remain in the public repo's git history under the old
  filename/commits. 6 characters of a ~39-character key is a very low brute-force risk on its own, so this
  wasn't treated as an emergency, but rotating the 3 affected Gemini keys is cheap insurance if Santiago wants
  zero residual exposure; not done in this session pending his decision.
- **Tests:** `python3 -m pytest scripts/tests/` — 158/158 passed (PYTHONPATH extended to include
  `globalinvesting-scripts` checkout, matching the real CI wiring, for `fetch_rates`/`fetch_news` imports).

### Investigated, no code change — `private-scripts/calculate_technical_levels.py` wiring
- **Context:** Santiago asked to confirm this script (added in v8.57.2, same day) is actually running.
- **Finding:** `update-ohlc.yml` wires it correctly — gated to

### Frontend — `access.html`
- **Context:** Santiago flagged the "Additional Coverage" section (Cross-Asset Correlations, Derivatives
  Detail, Carry Trade Ranking, Currency Strength, Alerts & Market Signals, News Feed) as visually weak — a
  flat 4-up + 2-up grid of equally-weighted, small, cropped screenshots. Presented three design alternatives
