- **Change:** Replaced the two `.feat-card-grid` blocks with a new `.showcase` component: a vertical list of
  6 tabs on the left (title always visible, description expands only for the active tab) and a single large
  preview frame on the right that swaps between 6 stacked, absolutely-positioned `.showcase-slide` elements
  via `active`-class toggling (no `src` swapping, so no network/decode hitch on tab switch and no CLS risk).
  All 6 screenshots keep their original alt text, dimensions, and `loading` attributes (first eager, rest
  lazy) — only the container/layout changed, not the assets or copy content per panel.
- **Accessibility:** Tabs use `role="tablist"` / `role="tab"` / `aria-selected`, the preview frame is
  `role="tabpanel"` with `aria-labelledby` tracking the active tab, and the tab list supports Arrow-Up/Down
  keyboard navigation (roving `tabindex`) per standard ARIA tablist authoring practice — matching the
  existing chart-tab convention already required elsewhere in the terminal (see GUIDELINES.md Accessibility
  section).
- **Lightbox integration:** `.showcase-slide` was added to the existing lightbox click-target selector
  list (`.scr-hero, .scr-item, .feat-card-thumb, .showcase-slide`). Each slide carries its own
  `data-caption` attribute (title + description) so the lightbox caption doesn't depend on a sibling
  `.feat-card-body` element that no longer exists in this section — the lightbox `openLb()` helper now
  checks `el.dataset.caption` first, before falling back to the existing `.scr-meta`/`.feat-card-body`
  sibling lookup used by the other screenshot galleries on the page (`guide-*.html` conventions unaffected).
- **CSS cleanup:** Removed the now-unused `.feat-card*` rule block and its two responsive overrides (900px,
  680px breakpoints) after confirming via repo-wide grep that no other HTML/CSS/JS file references those
  classes. Added `.showcase*` rules in their place, reusing existing CSS variables only (`--bg2`, `--bg3`,
  `--border`, `--border2`, `--blue`, `--text2`, `--text3`, `--font-ui`, `--font-mono`) — no new colors or
  fonts introduced.
- **Copy:** Minor rewording of the section intro paragraph ("Six more panels — ... Select one to preview it
  at full size.") to reflect the new interactive behavior; panel titles and descriptions themselves are
  unchanged from the prior grid.
- **Not done in this session:** No automated CWV re-verification run (PageSpeed Insights) — the change is
  scoped to `access.html` (a satellite page, not `index.html`), and CLS risk is low since the preview frame
  has a fixed height (420px desktop / 320px ≤900px / 260px ≤680px) regardless of which slide is active, but
  this should still be spot-checked before the next deploy per the Core Web Vitals checklist.
- **Fourth follow-up, same session:** removed the `01 / 06` index counter badge — with the tabs pattern
  (all 6 panels always listed, active one highlighted), the counter was redundant wayfinding left over from
  the original carousel-style thinking. Removed `.showcase-index` CSS, its markup, and the now-dead
  `indexEl` JS reference in the tab-activation handler.
- **Third follow-up, same session:** Santiago found the floating-window version (fixed 420px frame,
  `object-fit: contain`) unconvincing — forcing 6 differently-proportioned screenshots into one fixed box
  left uneven empty space per tab regardless of frame color. Removed the fixed-height frame entirely:
  `.showcase-preview-frame` no longer sets `height`/`background`/`border` — each `.showcase-slide` is now
  toggled via `display: none/flex` (not absolute-position + opacity crossfade), so the container's height
  matches whichever screenshot is active, at its natural aspect ratio, capped only by `max-width: 100%`.
  The border + shadow on the image itself (`var(--border2)`, same shadow curve as `.scr-item-frame`) are
  unchanged — only the surrounding fixed box was removed. Also removed the now-obsolete
  `.showcase-preview-frame { height: ... }` overrides at the 900px/680px breakpoints, and moved the
  `01 / 06` index counter out of absolute positioning into normal flow (`.showcase-preview` is now a column
  flex wrapper with the counter right-aligned below the image) since the frame no longer has a fixed box
  to anchor it to.
- **Second follow-up, same session:** measured actual edge-pixel colors of the 6 screenshots directly —
  they range from `#131722` to `#4f7fff` (each is a crop of a different terminal panel, so each carries a
  different internal border/background) — confirming that no single frame background color can blend
  seamlessly with all 6 without per-image color-matching, which would be fragile and break on the next
  screenshot update. Replaced the color-matching approach with a "floating window" pattern (Stripe/Linear
  convention): `.showcase-preview-frame` background reverted to `var(--bg)` (matches the rest of the page,
  so the frame reads as page background rather than a nested box) with `overflow: visible`; each
  `.showcase-slide img` now carries its own `border: 1px solid var(--border2)`, `border-radius: 4px`, and
  `box-shadow: 0 14px 32px -10px rgba(0,0,0,.65)` (brightens slightly on hover), capped at `92%`/`88%` of
  the frame so there's breathing room for the shadow. This mirrors the existing `.scr-item-frame` treatment
  used by the screenshot gallery earlier on the same page (same shadow curve, same border variable) — no
  new colors, shadows, or variables introduced. The screenshot's own internal border color no longer needs
  to match anything; the image is now an intentionally separate floating object rather than an attempt at
  full-bleed blending.
- **Follow-up fix, same session:** the initial `.showcase-preview-frame` used `var(--bg3)` (satellite-page
  palette, `#1a1e2e`) plus 14px padding around each `object-fit: contain` slide. Since the screenshots
  themselves are captured from the live terminal's own dark background (`--bg: #131722` in the terminal
  palette — a different, closer-to-black tone than the satellite page's `--bg3`), the mismatch showed up as
  a visible gray rectangle around every image wherever the aspect ratio caused letterboxing. Fixed by
  dropping the frame background to `var(--bg)` (the satellite page's own darkest tone, `#0b0e14`, closest
  match to the screenshots' own near-black background) and removing the 14px padding entirely — the letterbox
  now reads as a clean dark mat instead of a mismatched border.

## v8.57.2 (2026-07-17) — Deterministic moving-average levels feed the Currency Catalysts narrative

### Scripts repo — `calculate_technical_levels.py` (new, in `globalinvesting-scripts`, NOT the engine)
- **Context:** Following up on v8.57.1 — Santiago asked whether the technical-levels gap identified vs.
  Scotiabank/JPMorgan/MUFG could be closed via RSS. It can't (RSS is text/news, not a price series), but
  no new data source was actually needed: `fetch_ohlc.py` (also in `globalinvesting-scripts`) already
  fetches 3 years of daily OHLC bars via yfinance into `ohlc-data/{pair}.json` for the Lightweight Charts
  panel — this is a downstream calculation on data the engine already has, not new architecture.
- **Repo placement — corrected mid-session:** first drafted this inside `globalinvesting-engine/scripts/`,
  which was wrong. This script needs no API keys/secrets and performs no cross-repo write of its own — it
  reads `ohlc-data/*.json` and writes `ai-analysis/technical-levels.json`, both in the public site repo.
  That's exactly the shape of `fetch_ohlc.py` and `fetch_bond_yields.py`: pure data-prep scripts that live
  in `globalinvesting-scripts` and get checked out (read-only, via `SCRIPTS_PAT`) into a workflow that runs
  in the public site repo, matching `update-ohlc.yml`'s pattern. The engine repo is for scripts that need
  the Gemini/Groq API keys and AI-orchestration prompt IP (`generate_narrative_signals.py`) — this isn't
  that. Moved to `globalinvesting-scripts/calculate_technical_levels.py`.
- **What it computes:** SMA20/50/200 on daily close, one primary pair per G10 currency (DXY for USD,
  bilateral pairs for the other nine — same pair convention as `PAIR_KEYS` in `build_context()`). Writes
  `ai-analysis/technical-levels.json`: `{ccy: {pair, close, sma20, sma50, sma200, position, asof}}`.
  `position` is a deterministic string (e.g. `above_sma20_below_sma50_above_sma200`) — descriptive only.
- **Why moving averages only, not Fibonacci/support-resistance:** SMA on close is a fixed formula — same
  yfinance closes the desks use, directly comparable output (validated: our computed DXY 100.75/SMA20 101.06
  and USD/JPY 162.35 land right where Scotiabank's July 17 note put DXY "around the 100.5 point" and
  USD/JPY at 162.40). Fibonacci retracements require choosing a swing high/low reference, which is an
  analyst judgment call, not a deterministic calculation — Scotiabank and JPMorgan can legitimately anchor
  to different swings for the same pair. Computing a Fib level here would mean fabricating that same
  subjective call, which conflicts with GUIDELINES.md's data-integrity rules. Left for a v2 only if
  Santiago wants to define an explicit, documented swing-selection rule.
- **No network call, deterministic, reproducible** — reads already-fetched files, no `Math.random()`,
  no LLM involved in the calculation. Currencies with missing/short OHLC history are omitted rather than
  estimated (validated against all 10 G10 currencies with the uploaded OHLC data — 10/10 computed cleanly).

### Engine — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`
- **`_build_technical_levels_context()` (new):** reads `technical-levels.json` and formats a labelled
  context block, or returns an empty string if the file is absent — same no-fabrication pattern as the
  existing news/signal context builder.
- Wired into all three catalyst-generation paths (`CATALYSTS_SYSTEM_TAVILY`, `CATALYSTS_SYSTEM_BULK`,
  `CATALYSTS_SYSTEM_INTERNAL`/Groq fallback) with an explicit instruction: the model may cite the
  SMA20/50/200 position as one descriptive sentence of market structure ("holding above its 50-day moving
  average") — never as a buy/sell signal, and never inventing a level not present in the block. This is
  the same descriptive-only constraint added to the catalyst prompts in v8.57.1, now extended to cover
  the new technical-levels input.

### GUIDELINES.md
- Added `technical-levels.json` to the "Estimated data must be labeled" table (label:
  `SMA20/50/200 · yfinance daily closes · computed, not LLM-estimated`) and bumped the version footer
  to v8.57.2 — a new labeling rule, not just content.

### Deployment note (not yet wired into a workflow — flagged for Santiago, not done silently)
- `calculate_technical_levels.py` needs to run after `fetch_ohlc.py` (22:30 UTC) and before the catalysts
  job, so `ohlc-data/*.json` is fresh when it reads. This wiring (new workflow step or a `needs:` dependent
  job) was **not added** in this change — scope was the calculation script and its prompt integration only;
  workflow scheduling is a separate, reviewable change per the propose-before-implementing rule.

## v8.57.1 (2026-07-17) — Currency catalysts prompt: raised precision bar to match sell-side desk notes

### Engine — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`
- **Context:** Santiago benchmarked the Macro Drivers narrative and Alerts & Market Signals panel against
  same-day desk notes from Scotiabank, MUFG, JPMorgan, and ING. Verdict: the quantitative layer (Alerts —
  COT LF net, VRP, CESI, correlation z-scores) is genuinely comparable to what these desks publish.
  The narrative layer is weaker on two specific points these notes hit consistently: named catalysts with
  exact figures/dates/short quotes (e.g. Scotiabank quoting FinMin Katayama by name and date; MUFG citing
  exact swap-rate moves in bps), and explicit "trade bias" framing with entry/target/stop-loss levels.
- **Trade bias — explicitly declined, not a gap:** GUIDELINES.md ("No investment advice language") already
  prohibits prescriptive direction/action language in Alerts & Market Signals and AI narrative — the same
  rule that separates a Bloomberg-style analytics terminal from a broker-dealer's regulated sales & trading
  commentary. Sell-side notes carry that language because the issuing bank is a regulated broker-dealer with
  the corresponding disclosure/certification apparatus (visible in every one of the four notes reviewed);
  GlobalInvesting is a retail MQL5 Market product with no such registration. Added an explicit
  "STRICTLY DESCRIPTIVE, NEVER PRESCRIPTIVE" clause directly into `CATALYSTS_SYSTEM_TAVILY` and
  `CATALYSTS_SYSTEM_BULK` (previously this constraint only lived in `_apply_signal_guards()` downstream —
  it now also holds at generation time, defense in depth).
- **Catalyst precision — addressed:** both catalyst-generation prompts previously said "name people,
  institutions, and dates explicitly" with no worked example of what that means in practice, so output
  quality depended entirely on how literally the model interpreted "explicitly." Added a "PRECISION BAR"
  block to both prompts: prefer an exact figure over a description when the search data supports one,
  reuse an official's exact title, quote a short (<12-word, copyright-safe) verbatim phrase when directly
  supported by source text, and cite the next scheduled catalyst by date. Includes one CORRECT/WEAK example
  pair to anchor the standard. Explicitly reiterates the existing no-fabrication rule so the precision push
  doesn't create an incentive to invent specificity.
- **Deferred, requires separate approval:** classic technical levels (Fibonacci retracements, moving-average
  clusters, support/resistance) — the other clear gap versus the desk notes — need a historical-price
  pipeline the engine does not currently have; this is an architecture change (new data source/script), not
  a prompt edit, and was intentionally left out of this change pending Santiago's sign-off.
- **No frontend or data-schema changes** — `currency-catalysts.json` output shape (`{"catalyst": "...",
  "sources": [...]}` per currency) is unchanged; only the generation prompt changed. No changes needed to
  `heatmap-modal.js` or the 81-test suite.

## v8.57.0 (2026-07-17) — Macro Drivers relocated out of the Rel. Strength tab into a persistent block

### Frontend — `assets/heatmap-modal.js`
- **Context:** Santiago asked whether nesting the Macro Drivers narrative (AI-written, per-currency "why is this moving" paragraph) inside the "Rel. Strength" tab — sharing that tab with a 10×10 strength-differential matrix and a "top 3 pairs by contribution" box — was the industry-standard placement.
- **Mandatory compliance check (GUIDELINES.md):** verified against Bloomberg's actual `WCRS` (World Currency Ranker) function rather than assuming from the existing layout. `WCRS` is purely quantitative (spot/interest/total return, carry, historical ranking); Bloomberg keeps narrative context in a structurally separate function (`NI`, searchable by topic — `NI ECB`, `NI FED`, `NI TOP`) rather than nesting it inside a ranking screen. The prior layout blurred that separation, and — because "Pair Breakdown" is the default tab on open — most users never saw the Macro Drivers text at all unless they specifically clicked into "Rel. Strength."
- **Change:** moved the `MACRO DRIVERS` block (`#hm-catalyst-title` / `#hm-catalyst`) out of `#hm-p-correlations` into a new persistent `#hm-macro` block, positioned between `#hm-metrics` and `#hm-tabs`. It now renders immediately when the modal opens and stays visible regardless of which tab is active — matching Bloomberg's model of narrative-as-a-distinct-always-reachable-layer rather than one more tab of the quant drill-down.
- **Implementation:**
  - Extracted the catalyst-rendering logic out of `populateCorrelations()` into its own `populateMacroDrivers(ccy)`, called directly from `openHeatmapModal()` (right after `populateMetrics()`) and from `hmPivotCcy()` (so pivoting the modal's focal currency updates the persistent block too, not just whichever tab is active).
  - `fetchCatalysts()` now calls `populateMacroDrivers(_ccy)` again once `currency-catalysts.json` resolves, in case the fetch completes after the initial synchronous render (previously this only mattered for the "Rel. Strength" tab, which usually wasn't open yet; now it's visible from the first frame, so the re-render on arrival actually matters).
  - `populateCorrelations()` unchanged otherwise — the strength-differential matrix and "Strength Drivers · Top 3 Pairs" box stay in the Rel. Strength tab, since those are genuine quantitative drill-down (Bloomberg-equivalent: still `WCRS`-style), not narrative.
- **Not touched:** `STRENGTH DRIVERS · TOP 3 PAIRS BY CONTRIBUTION` box — pair-level, quantitative, correctly stays tab-gated.

## v8.56.0 (2026-07-17) — Retail Sentiment panel was silently missing 9 of 37 available G10 pairs

### Engine — `scripts/fetch_myfxbook_sentiment.py`
- **Context:** Santiago noticed several symbols visible on Myfxbook's own Community Outlook page (e.g. NZD/CHF, CAD/CHF, NOK/JPY) never appear in the EA/terminal's retail sentiment panel, despite Myfxbook clearly publishing data for them.
- **Root cause:** `renderSentiment()`/`fetchSentiment()` in `dashboard.js` render whatever pairs are present in `sentiment-data/myfxbook.json` — there is no frontend-side pair filter. The gap was entirely upstream: `TRACKED_PAIRS` in `fetch_myfxbook_sentiment.py` was last revised for the v8.3.4 Scandi rollout (which only added USD/NOK, USD/SEK, EUR/NOK, EUR/SEK) and was never revisited for the rest of the G10 cross matrix, so the script silently dropped every pair not on that list — even though `get-community-outlook.json` returns them on every run.
- **Verification:** Confirmed against Myfxbook's live symbol list (myfxbook.com's own toolbar widget) rather than assuming from pipeline logic. Of the 45 mathematically possible G10 (USD/EUR/GBP/JPY/AUD/CAD/CHF/NZD/NOK/SEK) crosses, Myfxbook publishes 37; the other 8 (AUD/NOK, AUD/SEK, NZD/NOK, NZD/SEK, CAD/NOK, CAD/SEK, CHF/NOK, CHF/SEK) do not exist under any symbol name on Myfxbook at all — a genuine upstream data gap, not fixable from this side.
- **Fix:** expanded `TRACKED_PAIRS` from 28 to all 37 available pairs — added NZD/CAD, NZD/JPY, NZD/CHF, CAD/CHF, GBP/NOK, GBP/SEK, NOK/JPY, SEK/JPY, NOK/SEK. No other logic changed: the existing `raw_lookup` slash-insertion (`name[:3] + "/" + name[3:]`) already handles arbitrary 6-character Myfxbook symbol codes generically, so no parsing changes were needed.
- **Cross-check against the EA:** `Global_Investing_FX_Terminal.mq5`'s own `RETAIL_MFX`/`RETAIL_MFX_X` arrays were not affected by this bug — the EA fetches Myfxbook sentiment independently (per-symbol `WebRequest`, gated on Market Watch presence) and already carried NZD/CAD, NZD/JPY, NZD/CHF, CAD/CHF in its base 28, plus GBP/NOK, GBP/SEK, NOK/JPY, SEK/JPY, NOK/SEK in its 17-pair extension — this is what made it possible to confirm the correct 37-pair universe against a second, independent implementation. The EA's extension list also includes the 8 pairs Myfxbook doesn't publish (AUD/NOK, AUD/SEK, CAD/NOK, CAD/SEK, CHF/NOK, CHF/SEK, NZD/NOK, NZD/SEK), gated only on broker symbol availability, not Myfxbook data availability — those rows will show no data if the broker lists the pair, which is a separate pre-existing EA behavior, left untouched here.
- **Not in scope:** XAU/USD and XAG/USD (gold/silver) also appear on Myfxbook's sentiment page but are commodities, not G10 FX pairs — outside this script's tracked universe. Gold already has its own live-price/stress-scoring presence via the intraday cross-asset panel (`quotes.json`); it has no retail-sentiment row anywhere in the terminal today. Flagging this as a scope question for Santiago rather than adding it unilaterally: would a Gold (and optionally Silver) row belong in the Retail Sentiment panel, or is that panel intentionally FX-only?

## v8.55.1 (2026-07-17) — Fixed: site menu dropdown closes when moving the mouse down into it

### Frontend — `assets/dashboard.css`
- **Root cause:** `.site-menu` (the wrapper div around the "Menu" button and its dropdown panel) had no `position` set, so it defaulted to `static`. `.site-menu-panel` and the `.site-menu::after` hover-bridge (added specifically to prevent this class of bug — see its own comment) are both `position: absolute`, which means without a positioned `.site-menu`, both fell back to positioning against `.topbar-right` — the next ancestor up that actually has `position: relative`. `.topbar-right` is a taller row (it also holds the session label and clock), so the bridge ended up computed against the wrong box height and didn't reliably cover the real gap between the button and the panel. Moving the mouse down from the button into the dropdown crossed that uncovered gap, `:hover` was lost, and the panel closed before the pointer arrived.
- **Corroborating evidence:** `guide-dashboard.html`'s own inline mirror of this CSS (`/* mirrored from dashboard.css */`) already has `.site-menu { position: relative; ... }` — the guide's copy was correct; production `dashboard.css` had silently drifted from it.
- **Fix:** added `position: relative;` to `.site-menu` in `assets/dashboard.css`. This gives `.site-menu-panel` and `.site-menu::after` the correct containing block (the button's own wrapper), so `top: 100%` and the 8px bridge now align with the button's actual bottom edge instead of the taller sibling row.
- **Not touched:** `guide-dashboard.html` (already correct, used as the reference), `dashboard.js` (no JS involved), `dashboard.test.js` (no test in the 81-suite covers this CSS rule; nothing there to break).

### Frontend — `index.html`
- Cache-bust bump: `assets/dashboard.css?v=8.23.0` → `?v=8.23.1`.

## v8.54.2 (2026-07-16) — calendar-watcher.js v5.10: experimental header fix for a new Myfxbook HTML 403/400 block (unverified — needs Santiago's /test-html confirmation)

### Context
While confirming the v8.54.1 deploy live, `GET /test-html` showed the Myfxbook HTML secondary source failing: anon attempt → 403 Forbidden, cookie attempt → 400 Bad Request. Reproduced identically twice, >1 minute apart — ruled out a transient rate-limit from the testing burst (deploy + reset + trigger + payload check all happened within ~90 seconds beforehand).

### Engine — `cf-workers-backup/calendar-watcher/calendar-watcher.js` (v5.9 → v5.10)
- **Found:** the HTML fetch's header set declared a Chrome 124 `User-Agent` but sent none of the `sec-ch-ua`/`sec-fetch-*`/`upgrade-insecure-requests` client-hint headers a real Chrome browser always sends — a bot signal to modern WAFs on its own, independent of any IP-based blocking.
- **Fix (experimental):** added `htmlFetchHeaders(cookie)`, a shared header builder now used by both `fetchMyfxbookHTMLActuals()` and `handleTestHTML()` (previously each had its own inline copy of the same header object — fixed the duplication while touching this code), with a full `sec-ch-ua`/`sec-fetch-dest`/`sec-fetch-mode`/`sec-fetch-site`/`sec-fetch-user`/`upgrade-insecure-requests` set added to the existing headers.
- **Explicitly NOT claimed as a confirmed fix:** if Myfxbook is blocking by source IP/ASN — plausible, since Cloudflare Workers egress ranges are widely fingerprinted, and this exact pattern (ForexFactory blocking these same IPs) is already in this file's own v3.1 history — no header set changes that. Needs Santiago to redeploy and check `GET /test-html`.
- **Verification done here:** `node --check` passes; extracted `htmlFetchHeaders()` into an isolated harness and confirmed it produces the expected header object for both the anon and cookie cases, including the `Cookie` header only being added when a cookie is passed. Could not verify against the live Myfxbook endpoint from this environment (no network access) — this is genuinely unverified until tested in production.
- **Realistic fallback if this doesn't resolve it:** RSS-only remains a working, non-fatal path (confirmed live via `wrangler tail` — `HTML fetch failed (non-fatal, RSS fallback active)` already logs and falls through correctly). No user-facing outage either way; only the ~2-5 min HTML speed boost is at stake.

### Not in scope
- Did not attempt an IP-rotation, proxy, or alternate-egress workaround — that's a materially bigger architecture change (cost + complexity) and shouldn't be pursued speculatively before confirming headers alone don't already fix it.
- Did not touch `MFB_SESSION_COOKIE`'s actual value — the 400-vs-403 discrepancy between the anon and cookie attempts could also indicate a stale/malformed cookie specifically, independent of the header fix; worth a separate look if the header fix doesn't resolve the cookie attempt's 400.

## v8.54.1 (2026-07-16) — Calendar latency audit: calendar-watcher.js v5.9 fixes a 7-event-type asymmetry that bypassed the fast dispatch path

### Context
Santiago reported that Economic Calendar events don't always update right away after their release (screenshots + two production `update-ff-calendar.yml` run logs, ~3 min apart, showing US Retail Sales YoY as `pending` in the first run and filled in the second). Audited the full pipeline (`calendar-watcher.js` Cloudflare Worker → `repository_dispatch` → `fetch_ff_calendar.py` → `ff_calendar.json`).

### Investigation — ruled out
- **KV→RSS merge logic (`fetch_ff_calendar.py` Step 2a-ii):** built a synthetic harness reproducing the exact key composition (`currency, dateISO, timeUTC, title`) used to match the Worker's `/payload` KV events against Python's own RSS-parsed events. Confirmed the merge correctly injects a KV-sourced actual when the underlying data is genuinely present on both sides — this code path is not broken.
- **The specific incident reported (US Retail Sales YoY):** already "high" impact directly from Myfxbook, so not affected by the bug found below. Concluded this was normal multi-provider publish staggering — 8 USD events released simultaneously at 12:30 UTC don't all appear in Myfxbook's own backend atomically; each newly-appearing actual re-triggers the Worker's fingerprint check and fires a fresh dispatch, which is the architecture working as designed (~2-6 min observed, within its stated ~2-3 min best case plus GitHub Actions queue/checkout overhead).

### Bug found and fixed — Engine — `cf-workers-backup/calendar-watcher/calendar-watcher.js` (v5.8 → v5.9)
- **Root cause:** `fetch_ff_calendar.py` has an `_IMPACT_UPGRADES` table promoting 7 Myfxbook-"low"-tagged event types (producer price index, machine tool orders, building approvals, private house approvals, consumer inflation expectations, current account, manufacturing sales) to "medium" so its own low-impact filter doesn't drop them. `calendar-watcher.js`'s `parseMyfxbookRSS()` had no equivalent table — it discarded these 7 event types via `impact === "low"` *before* they ever reached `buildFingerprint()`. Since the Worker's fingerprint is the sole trigger for the fast `repository_dispatch` path, a released actual for any of these 7 types was structurally invisible to Tier 1 (~2-3 min) and could only reach `ff_calendar.json` via the Tier 2 GitHub Actions cron fallback (up to 30 min off-peak) — silently, since the cron eventually fills it in with no visible error.
- **Fix:** added an `IMPACT_UPGRADES` array (mirrors the Python set) and applied it in `parseMyfxbookRSS()` before the low-impact `continue`, promoting a match to `"medium"` instead of dropping the event.
- **Verification:** extracted `parseMyfxbookRSS()` + `IMPACT_UPGRADES` into an isolated Node harness (mirrors the "targeted harness simulating real production log patterns" convention used for Python scripts). Confirmed (1) a synthetic low-impact CAD "Manufacturing Sales MoM" event is now promoted to `medium` and kept in the fingerprinted event set, and (2) a genuinely low-impact, non-upgraded event is still correctly filtered (no false positives introduced). `node --check` passes.
- **Deployment note:** this is a Cloudflare Worker — the fix in this repo is a source-of-truth copy (`cf-workers-backup/`). Not live until Santiago runs `npx wrangler deploy` from his local `calendar-watcher/` folder.

### Engine — `cf-workers-backup/calendar-watcher/wrangler.toml`
- **Found:** deployment notes still described a defunct v3.1 "FCS API" architecture and a `FCS_API_KEY` secret that doesn't exist anywhere in the current v5.9 code (confirmed via grep — zero references). Real secrets in current code: `GITHUB_PAT`/`GITHUB_OWNER`/`GITHUB_REPO` (required, used to fire the dispatch) and `PAYLOAD_TOKEN` (optional, gates `POST /inject-actuals` only).
- **Also found:** `GET /payload` is not actually gated by `PAYLOAD_TOKEN` in the current code — it's public/unauthenticated. `fetch_ff_calendar.py` sends a bearer token anyway (harmless, just not checked).
- **Fix:** rewrote the deployment notes to describe the actual current architecture and secrets; removed the stale FCS API references.

### Scripts (`globalinvesting-scripts`) — `fetch_ff_calendar.py` (v3.33 → v3.34, docs only)
- **Fixed stale docstring** in `fetch_worker_payload()`: claimed the Worker polls Myfxbook RSS "every 30min" (actually every 1 minute since v5.2 — confirmed against `calendar-watcher.js`'s header and `wrangler.toml`'s `crons = ["* * * * *"]`), and described the HTML/KV relationship backwards. Also documented the `/payload` auth finding above. No functional/behavioral change.

### `GUIDELINES.md`
- **New "HTML scraping" lesson:** "Two independent parsers of the same feed silently drift" — documents that `fetch_ff_calendar.py` and `calendar-watcher.js` parse the same RSS feed independently and are not auto-synced; a filter change to one that affects event *inclusion* (not just formatting/enrichment) must be evaluated for the other, since it changes the Worker's fingerprint surface and therefore its dispatch behavior.
- Version footer bumped v8.54.0 → v8.54.1 (new rule added).

### Not in scope
- Did not port `_force_high_if_rate_decision()` to the Worker — confirmed `impact` is not part of `buildFingerprint()`'s hash, so it has no effect on dispatch behavior; only affects downstream consumers of `ff_calendar.json`'s `impact` field, which is Python-only territory.
- Did not change the CF Worker's cron interval, GitHub Actions time-gate windows, or the 2-minute cache-busting bucket in `calendar-panel.js` (v8.53.8) — none were implicated by this audit.

## v8.54.0 (2026-07-16) — License worker: append-only visit history, durable error visibility, sendBeacon-on-unload

### Context
Santiago asked whether `gi-admin-dashboard.html` guarantees visibility into every user access to the web terminal. Audit found it does not: `access_log` only records activations (a returning user with a still-valid JWT never touches it again), and `active_sessions` is presence-only — upserted on every `/session/ping` with no history retained. This entry closes the gaps that are actually closable and documents the one that structurally isn't (a client that never talks to the Worker cannot be forced to report itself).

### Engine — `gi-license-worker` (`globalinvesting-scripts/cf-workers-backup/gi-license-worker/worker.js`)
- **Added `session_events` table (append-only visit history):** one row per *detected visit* — first-ever ping for a `session_id`, or a ping arriving after a `NEW_VISIT_GAP_MS` (30 min) gap since that session's last recorded activity — not one row per ping. Logging every 3-minute ping would have grown this table by ~20-40 rows/hour of open-terminal-time per user for no analytical benefit; visit-level granularity answers "how many times / when did account X open the terminal" without that blowup. `active_sessions`'s existing presence/upsert behavior is unchanged.
- **New endpoint `GET /admin/sessions/history`:** `[X-Admin-Key] ?limit=&account=&server=&session_id=&since=` — paginated, filterable query over `session_events`.
- **Added `worker_errors` table + `logWorkerError()` helper:** `logAccess()` and the three D1 writes inside `/session/ping` (prior-row lookup, `session_events` insert, `active_sessions` upsert) are intentionally best-effort — a telemetry failure must never block real validation or presence tracking — but their catch blocks previously only wrote to `console.error`, visible solely via an active `wrangler tail` session. They now also durably log to `worker_errors`. The write to `worker_errors` is itself wrapped in try/catch with a `console.error`-only fallback, so an error-logging failure can never cascade into a second unhandled failure.
- **New endpoint `GET /admin/health`:** `[X-Admin-Key] ?hours=` — recent `worker_errors` count + rows.
- **`handleSessionPing()` now accepts `?token=&session_id=` query params as a fallback** alongside the existing `Authorization`/`X-Session-Id` headers, to support `sendBeacon()` calls (see below), which cannot set custom request headers.
- **Header docblock rewritten** to document all endpoints (including the two new ones) and the three-table data model (`access_log` / `active_sessions` / `session_events`).

### Engine — `schema.sql`, new `migration-2026-07-16-session-history.sql`
- **`schema.sql`:** added `session_events` and `worker_errors` table + index definitions, for fresh-database setup.
- **New migration file:** additive-only `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` for both new tables against the live, already-deployed database — does not touch `access_log` or `active_sessions`.

### Site — `assets/gi-auth.js` (v1.1.1 → v1.2.0)
- **Added `navigator.sendBeacon()` ping on `pagehide`/`visibilitychange`:** the existing 3-minute periodic ping can leave a session's `last_seen` up to 3 minutes stale at the moment a user actually closes the tab. `sendBeacon()` is designed to reliably complete even as the page unloads, which a plain `fetch()` call from the same event handler is not guaranteed to do. Since `sendBeacon()` cannot set custom headers, token and session id are passed as query params on this call only.

### Engine — `tools/gi-admin-dashboard.html`
- **Added two tabs:** "Visit History" (queries `/admin/sessions/history`, filterable by account/server/session_id/since) and "Health" (queries `/admin/health`, shows a pass/fail badge plus the raw error rows).
- Both wired into the existing tab-switch, auto-refresh, and connect/disconnect flow unchanged; reused existing `callAdmin()`/`renderEmpty()`/`renderError()`/`escapeHtml()`/`timeAgo()`/`formatLocation()` helpers rather than duplicating them.

### `GUIDELINES.md`
- **New section "License worker — audit trail & error visibility":** documents the three-table data model (`access_log` / `active_sessions` / `session_events`), the error-visibility pattern (`worker_errors` + `logWorkerError()`), and explicitly records the structural limit that none of this can guarantee visibility into a client that never contacts the Worker at all — future sessions should not present `session_events` as a guaranteed-complete access log.

### Verification
- `worker.js`: syntax-checked (`node --check`).
- `gi-auth.js`: syntax-checked (`node --check`).
- `gi-admin-dashboard.html`: inline `<script>` block extracted and syntax-checked (`node --check`); tab-button count (5) matches panel-section count (5).
- `assets/dashboard.test.js` (unrelated frontend suite, not touched by this change) re-run as a regression check since `gi-auth.js` lives in the same repo — 81/81 passed, 0 failures.

### Not in scope
- Did not reduce the 35-day JWT expiry — that remains an intentional trade-off aligned to monthly billing, not a bug; shortening it would force more frequent `access_log`-visible re-activations but was explicitly decided against previously.
- Did not attempt to solve the case of a client that blocks the Worker's domain entirely or runs a fully offline-cached build — no server-side or client-side change can force telemetry from a client that never sends a request. This is documented as a known limit in `GUIDELINES.md`, not treated as an open bug.

## v8.53.11 (2026-07-15) — fetch_news.py v5.23: non-G10 currency headlines (Mexican Peso, Thai Baht, Singapore Dollar) leaking into the G10 news feed

### Scripts (`globalinvesting-scripts`) — `fetch_news.py`
- **Bug reported and fixed:** Santiago flagged non-G10 currency headlines appearing in the G10-only news feed. Confirmed in production `news.json` (2026-07-15T23:31 UTC) — 3 articles tagged `USD`: "Mexican Peso surges as inflation data weighs on the USD", "Thai Baht: Limited gains as Oil stays elevated – OCBC", "Singapore Dollar: Consolidation bias holds within tight band against US Dollar – UOB".
- **Root cause:** `EMERGING_MARKET_TITLE_RE` only ever had the Spanish-language forms (`peso mexicano`, `real brasileiro`, `lira turca`) and had no entry at all — in either language — for Thai Baht or Singapore Dollar. All three real headlines are in English (FXStreet/OCBC/UOB sourcing), so none matched the filter, and each article's incidental "USD"/"US Dollar" mention scored exactly `CURRENCY_MIN_SCORE=5` in `CURRENCY_KEYWORDS_WEIGHTED["USD"]`, so `detect_currency()` tagged them `USD` despite the actual subject being a non-G10 currency. Same failure shape as the State Bank of Vietnam incident (v8.43.17): a G10-currency mention incidental to a non-G10-subject article slipping past the pre-filter.
- **Fix:** added English-language forms `mexican peso`, `thai baht`, `\bbaht\b`, `singapore dollar` to `EMERGING_MARKET_TITLE_RE`, alongside the existing Spanish forms. Scoped to the 3 currencies actually observed in production — did not preemptively add unreported ASEAN/Asian currencies (INR, CNY, KRW, IDR, MYR, PHP, VND, HKD, TWD), per the established fix-what's-reported convention.
- **Verification:** added 4 targeted tests to `scripts/tests/test_fetch_news.py` using the exact production article titles, plus one regression test confirming the existing Spanish form still works. Ran the full suite against a temporary sibling copy (`fetch_news.py`/`fx_config.py`/`test_fetch_news.py`, same orphaned-suite caveat as prior entries) — 106/106 passed (102 previous + 4 new), 0 regressions.
- **Not in scope:** did not add a general non-G10-currency-name filter or expand beyond the 3 reported currencies.

## v8.53.8 (2026-07-15) — `calendar-panel.js` v1.6: cache-bust the ff_calendar.json fetch — GitHub Pages CDN was serving stale data for minutes after each workflow commit

### Site — `assets/calendar-panel.js` / `index.html`
- **Found live (2026-07-15):** `update-ff-calendar.yml` (workflow run #2908) committed 4 new actuals (NY Empire State Manufacturing, Canada Manufacturing Sales, PPI MoM, Core PPI MoM) to `calendar-data/ff_calendar.json`. 23 minutes later the Economic Calendar panel still showed "—" for all four.
- **Root cause:** `fetchEconomicCalendar()` fetches `./calendar-data/ff_calendar.json` with `cache: 'no-store'` on a static URL, polled every 2 min. `cache: 'no-store'` is a browser-local-cache directive only — it has no effect on GitHub Pages' CDN (Fastly), which can continue serving an edge-cached copy of that exact URL for several minutes after the underlying file changes, independent of what the client's request asks for. Every poll hit the same URL, so every poll could keep getting the same stale edge copy until the CDN's own TTL expired — unrelated to and longer than the panel's 2-min poll interval.
- **Fix:** `fetchEconomicCalendar()` now appends a minute-bucketed cache-busting query string (`?_=<Math.floor(Date.now()/120000)>`) to both `ff_calendar.json` and `calendar.json` fetch URLs, so each 2-min poll cycle requests a URL the CDN hasn't served before. Mirrors the existing pattern already used for `./intraday-data/quotes.json` in `dashboard.js`. `index.html`'s script tag bumped to `calendar-panel.js?v=1.6.0` so browsers pick up the fixed script itself.
- **Verified:** `node --check` passes on the modified file. Behavior of the panel's own dedup/window-filter logic is unchanged — only the fetch URL changed.
- **Scope note:** this is a different failure mode from v8.53.7 (calendar-watcher.js title-matching bug) — that one was actuals never reaching `ff_calendar.json` at all; this one is `ff_calendar.json` having the correct data but the browser not seeing it promptly. Both can present as "actual not showing on the site."

### Engine — `cf-workers-backup/calendar-watcher/calendar-watcher.js` (Cloudflare Worker, deployed by Santiago via `wrangler deploy`)
- **Found live (2026-07-14):** JPY Machinery Orders MoM/YoY (release 20:50 GMT-3) showed its actual on myfxbook.com (-12.4% / -1.9%) while the GI Terminal's own economic calendar still showed the event unreleased. Root cause: Myfxbook's RSS feed titles this event `"Japan Machinery Orders MoM"` (country name included) while its HTML calendar page's event-link text reads `"Machinery Orders MoM (May)"` (no country name, trailing period parenthetical instead). `mergeHTMLActuals()` matches an HTML-sourced actual onto its RSS-sourced event via `normTitle(title)` as part of the `(currency, dateISO, timeUTC, normTitle(title))` key — since `normTitle()` only lowercased and trimmed whitespace, these two representations of the same event never matched, so the HTML source's actual (visible within minutes of release) was silently discarded and the event fell back to the slow ~1h RSS path. This affected every G10 event whose RSS title carries a country prefix — i.e. every currency except USD, since Myfxbook's RSS never prefixes "United States".
- **Fix:** `normTitle()` now also strips a trailing `"(month/quarter)"` parenthetical and a leading country-name prefix (list mirrors `SLUG_TO_CCY`'s own country coverage) before the two title representations are compared. Matching stays scoped to `(currency, dateISO, timeUTC)`, so this cannot merge two genuinely different events that happen to release in the same minute. Also updates `handleInjectActuals()`'s title match, which calls the same `normTitle()`. Output schema unchanged — `ev.title` still stores the original (unstripped) RSS title; normalization is match-key-only.
- **Verified:** unit-tested the new `normTitle()` against the live RSS/HTML title pairs captured from this incident (JPY Machinery Orders MoM/YoY, USD Fed Cook Speech, EUR Industrial Production MoM) — all four pairs collapse to the same key. `node --check` passes on the full file.
- **Not fixed here, separate failure mode:** the historical "Core Machinery Orders m/m" → "Machinery Orders MoM" title change observed in `fetch_ff_calendar.py`'s Step 2 history (2026-05-20, ~48.7h to self-heal via the existing ghost-title guard) is Myfxbook renaming the *same RSS feed's* title over an event's own lifecycle (drops "Core", switches slash notation to MoM/YoY) — a different mismatch than the RSS-vs-HTML one fixed here, and not addressed by this change. Left alone deliberately: stripping "Core" in a shared normalizer risks collapsing genuinely distinct series (e.g. "Core CPI" vs "CPI") if a future event pair happened to share a release minute.
- **Deployment note:** this is a Cloudflare Worker — the fix in this repo is a source-of-truth copy (`cf-workers-backup/`). Santiago deploys via `wrangler deploy` from `calendar-watcher/` locally; this change is not live until deployed.

## v8.53.6 (2026-07-14) — `fetch_inflation_expectations.py` v5.5: removed the Chromium tier — live test confirmed RBNZ's block is IP/ASN-level, not client fingerprint

### Scripts — `fetch_inflation_expectations.py` / `update-inflation-expectations.yml`
- **Found via a real workflow run (2026-07-14):** the v5.4 Chromium fetch also returned HTTP 403 on the M14 XLSX, and the RBNZ stats-page navigation itself timed out on "networkidle" before that. A real headless browser failing exactly like plain `requests` did rules out a TLS/client-fingerprint WAF — it confirms an IP/ASN-level block on GitHub Actions' runner ranges, which no HTTP client can get past while egressing from that same IP range, however browser-like it is.
- **Removed `fetch_nzd_rbnz_chromium()`** and its step in the NZD cascade, plus the `playwright` pip install and `playwright install --with-deps chromium` step from the workflow — real CI time (browser download + launch) for a path now known to always fail from this environment. Restored `timeout-minutes` to 15.
- **Kept** the `_parse_rbnz_m14_xlsx()` helper extracted in v5.4 — still used by `fetch_nzd_rbnz_survey()`, and cleaner than the pre-refactor duplicated version regardless of Chromium's removal.
- **Current NZD cascade:** XLSX via requests → insights PDF (v5.3) → IMF CPI YoY → OECD → FRED → World Bank. NZD's practical ceiling from GitHub Actions is the OECD/IMF CPI YoY fallback already in place (currently serving 2026-03-01 OECD data). Further escalation (residential proxy, self-hosted runner with a non-blocked IP) is a materially different kind of change and isn't planned without an explicit decision to pursue it.
- Verified: `python3 -m py_compile` passes; YAML parses correctly (`timeout-minutes: 15` confirmed); grepped for any remaining executable `playwright`/`chromium` references — none found outside historical docstring notes.

## v8.53.5 (2026-07-14) — `fetch_inflation_expectations.py` v5.4: NZD RBNZ fetch escalated to headless Chromium after the v5.3 PDF fallback also 403'd on an unrelated URL path

### Scripts — `fetch_inflation_expectations.py` / `update-inflation-expectations.yml`
- **Found via a real workflow run (2026-07-14):** v5.3's insights-PDF fallback returned HTTP 403 on all 4 candidate URLs — a completely different RBNZ URL path (`/insights/...`) than the XLSX (`/hm14.xlsx`), failing identically. Two unrelated paths blocked the same way rules out a per-file protection rule; it points to either a domain-wide TLS/JS-challenge WAF or an IP/ASN-level block on GitHub Actions' runner ranges.
- **Added `fetch_nzd_rbnz_chromium()`:** fetches the same M14 XLSX through a real headless Chromium browser (Playwright) instead of `requests` — visits the RBNZ stats page first (session/cookies, as a real user's browser would), then requests the XLSX through the browser context's own network/TLS stack (`context.request.get`, not a separate plain HTTP client). This can get past a genuine TLS/JS-challenge WAF; it explicitly **cannot** get past an IP/ASN-level block, since Chromium still egresses from the same GitHub Actions IP range as `requests` did.
- **Refactored:** extracted the RBNZ M14 XLSX-bytes parsing logic (column/date detection, staleness check, ~90 lines) out of `fetch_nzd_rbnz_survey()` into a shared `_parse_rbnz_m14_xlsx()` helper, so the requests-based and Chromium-based fetch paths parse identically instead of duplicating that logic.
- **New NZD cascade order:** XLSX via requests → **XLSX via Chromium (new, v5.4)** → insights PDF → IMF CPI YoY → OECD → FRED → World Bank.
- **Workflow changes:** added `playwright` to the pip install step and a new step (`python -m playwright install --with-deps chromium`) to install the browser binary + system libs on the bare `ubuntu-latest` runner. Raised `timeout-minutes` from 15 to 20 to account for the added install/launch time — this job goes from a few-second pure-`requests` run to one that downloads and launches a real browser.
- **Explicitly scoped:** if Chromium also 403s, that's strong evidence for the IP/ASN-block hypothesis, at which point NZD's practical ceiling from GitHub Actions is the OECD/IMF CPI YoY fallback already in place. No further escalation (e.g. residential proxies) is planned without an explicit decision to do so — that would trade clean architecture for evading a block in a materially grayer way than header/browser spoofing.
- Verified: `python3 -m py_compile` passes; YAML parses correctly (`timeout-minutes: 20` confirmed); `playwright` package imports correctly and exposes the API surface used (`sync_playwright`, `chromium.launch`, `new_context`, `context.request.get`). **Not verified against the live RBNZ WAF** — `rbnz.govt.nz` isn't reachable from the review environment, and the Chromium binary itself isn't installed there either (no network path to download it). Needs a `workflow_dispatch` run to know whether this clears the 403 or confirms the IP/ASN-block hypothesis.

## v8.53.4 (2026-07-14) — `fetch_inflation_expectations.py` v5.3: NZD gets a second RBNZ source after the M14 XLSX's 403 survived v5.2's User-Agent fix; also fixed `openpyxl` never being installed by the workflow

### Scripts — `fetch_inflation_expectations.py` / `update-inflation-expectations.yml`
- **Found via a real workflow run (2026-07-14):** v5.2's browser User-Agent header did not clear the RBNZ M14 XLSX's HTTP 403 — confirmed via `workflow_dispatch`, same 403 on both URL variants. Header-level spoofing was the wrong tool for this: the block is very likely at the TLS/client-fingerprint level (WAF bot management), which no `requests` header change can get past.
- **Added a new SECONDARY source tier for NZD, `fetch_nzd_rbnz_insights_pdf()`:** RBNZ separately publishes a quarterly narrative PDF ("STATS INSIGHT") at a different URL path (`/insights/{year}/survey-of-expectations-{month}-{year}.pdf`) than the blocked XLSX. Confirmed via web search that Google has crawled and indexed this PDF's text directly — inferred (not confirmed against the live WAF from a runner) to sit outside the XLSX endpoint's bot-management tier. Parses the "Two-year-ahead inflation expectations ... to X%" sentence via regex from PDF text (`pypdf`); regex tested locally against all five real sentence variants found across RBNZ's Feb/May/Aug/Nov 2025–2026 releases (increase/decrease/unchanged phrasing) — all extract the correct post-change value, not the starting one.
- **New cascade order for NZD:** RBNZ M14 XLSX (primary) → **RBNZ insights PDF (new, v5.3)** → IMF CPI YoY → OECD → FRED → World Bank.
- **Also fixed, found while reviewing the workflow file:** `update-inflation-expectations.yml` only ever ran `pip install requests` — `openpyxl` was never installed, meaning the RBNZ XLSX parser would have failed with "openpyxl not available" the instant the 403 was ever cleared, independent of this session's fix. Added `openpyxl` and the new `pypdf` dependency to the same install step.
- **Corrected a stray docstring inconsistency found in the same file:** the top-of-file source cascade summary claimed NZD's primary source was "RBNZ Inflation Expectations 2Y-ahead survey (DBnomics)", while the actual implementation's own comment states DBnomics doesn't index this series and fetches directly from RBNZ instead — the two statements contradicted each other. Corrected the summary to match what the code does. Also fixed a stale hardcoded `(v5.1)` in the runtime console banner (cosmetic only, didn't affect any fetch logic — caused a false alarm in this same debugging session where a v5.2 run was mistaken for the old version).
- **Not yet verified live:** same limitation as v5.2 — `rbnz.govt.nz` isn't reachable from the review environment. Needs a `workflow_dispatch` run to confirm the insights-PDF path actually resolves and parses. If it also fails, the documented next escalation (not implemented here, deliberately) is a headless-browser fetch via Chromium/Playwright, which can solve genuine TLS/JS-challenge WAFs that header spoofing cannot — held off since it adds a heavy CI dependency (browser binary download, added job time) not yet justified by a live failure of this cheaper path.
- Verified: `python3 -m py_compile` passes; new regex tested locally against all 5 real RBNZ sentence phrasings pulled from search results (all extract the correct value).

## v8.53.3 (2026-07-13) — `fetch_inflation_expectations.py` v5.2: RBNZ M14 survey fetch fixed User-Agent to clear a 403 (was silently falling back to OECD, 134d stale)

### Scripts — `fetch_inflation_expectations.py`
- **Found while investigating a `monitor_data_health.py` warning:** NZD `inflationExpectations` was 134d old (threshold 95d), well past what the weekly `update-inflation-expectations.yml` cadence should allow. Production run log (2026-07-08) showed the cause: the RBNZ M14 XLSX request (primary NZD source, 2Y-ahead survey) failed with `HTTP 403` on both URL variants, cascading past a 0-observation IMF response down to OECD CPI YoY — a structurally laggier fallback than the RBNZ survey it's meant to be a last resort for.
- **Root cause:** an earlier fix had already added `Referer`/`Accept`/`Accept-Language` headers to the RBNZ request specifically to get past bot-blocking, but the request was still sending `BASE_HEADERS`' bot-identifying User-Agent (`GlobalInvesting-FX-Terminal/4.3 ...`) since `_RBNZ_HEADERS` never overrode it. `.govt.nz` sites commonly WAF-fingerprint on User-Agent independent of Referer, so the earlier fix was incomplete.
- **Fixed:** `_RBNZ_HEADERS` now includes a browser User-Agent override, scoped to only the RBNZ request — `BASE_HEADERS` and every other currency's fetch (FRED, BOE, IMF, OECD, FRED, WB) are untouched.
- **Not yet verified live:** `rbnz.govt.nz` isn't reachable from the review environment used to write this fix. Needs a `workflow_dispatch` run of `update-inflation-expectations.yml` to confirm the 403 clears and the M14 parser actually reaches a 2Y-ahead value — flagged in-code (v5.2 docstring) as unverified pending that run.
- CHF's separate 103d-stale warning from the same health-check batch was reviewed and left alone: it fetches successfully from IMF on every run with no error, it's just that IMF hadn't published a newer monthly CPI print yet as of the 2026-07-08 run — a source-publication lag, not a fetch bug, so no code change was made for CHF.

## v8.53.2 (2026-07-13) — LICENSE rewritten as proprietary; AdSense fully removed (was abandoned in practice, still live in code and copy on every page)

### Repo — `LICENSE`
- **Found on review:** `LICENSE` was a full MIT License — granting anyone permission to "use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and/or **sell** copies of the Software... free of charge" — while `terms.html` Section 7 (now Section 6) states the opposite: *"You may not reproduce, redistribute, or commercialize any part of this Terminal without prior written permission."* The README's own badge already read `License-Proprietary`, not MIT. Two files in the same repo made contradictory legal claims about the same codebase, and the EA is simultaneously sold as a paid rental on the MQL5 Marketplace — a permissive MIT grant sitting alongside that is a real business risk, not just an inconsistency.
- **Fixed, per Santiago's direction:** rewritten as an All Rights Reserved proprietary license, consistent with the README badge and `terms.html`. Clarifies that using the hosted terminal or a licensed EA copy grants no rights to this repository's source.
- **Also found and removed:** the DATA ATTRIBUTION block listed "Trading Economics — scraped from public pages; commercial use requires license." Confirmed via full-repo search that Trading Economics is not referenced by any current script in the site, engine, or private scripts repo — same class of staleness as the `economic-data/` fetch disabled in v7.24.1, just sitting in `LICENSE` instead of a data file. Removed; the remaining six attributions (FRED, CFTC, Frankfurter, OECD, World Bank, ONS) were individually confirmed still in active use before being kept.

### Site — AdSense removed sitewide
- **Found while reviewing `terms.html` for the AdSense mention Santiago flagged:** the mention wasn't isolated to that one file. AdSense touched the whole site: a `google-adsense-account` meta tag on all 16 pages, a matching consent-banner sentence on all 16 pages, a full "Google AdSense" section in both `terms.html` and `privacy.html`, live script-loading code in `assets/gdpr.js` (`pagead2.googlesyndication.com/adsbygoogle.js`, fired on cookie-accept), ad-network domains in the CSP of `GUIDELINES.md`, `netlify.toml`, and `_headers`, and `ad_storage`/`ad_user_data`/`ad_personalization` consent-mode signals in `index.html`'s inline gtag config.
- **Confirmed genuinely abandoned, not just stale copy:** no `<ins class="adsbygoogle">` ad-unit element exists on any page. The script in `gdpr.js` was still loading and pushing a config on every cookie-accept, but with no ad slot to render into — functionally dead, not visibly dead.
- **`assets/gdpr.js`:** removed `loadAdSense()`/`loadAdSenseNonPersonalized()` entirely and their call sites. `applyConsent()`/`init()` now only manage `analytics_storage` for GA4 consent mode.
- **`index.html`:** inline `gtag('consent','default', ...)` simplified to `analytics_storage` only; comment updated to state plainly that no ad-serving network is used.
- **All 16 pages** (`index`, `access`, `about`, `contact`, `privacy`, `terms`, all 8 guides): removed the `google-adsense-account` meta tag; rewrote the cookie-consent banner sentence from *"We use first- and third-party cookies (Google AdSense) to display relevant advertising"* to *"We use first-party cookies for analytics to understand how the Terminal is used."* `index.html`'s stale `<!-- Google Verification & AdSense account -->` comment header corrected to `<!-- Google Search Console verification -->` (the `google-site-verification` tag itself is unrelated to AdSense and was kept).
- **`terms.html`:** removed Section 6 "Advertising" outright; renumbered Sections 7–10 down to 6–9. `Last updated` bumped March 2026 → July 2026.
- **`privacy.html`:** Section 4 "Google AdSense" rewritten in place as "Google Analytics" (describing GA4 consent-mode gating, and stating plainly that no ad network is used) — kept the section slot rather than deleting it, since the consent banner itself is now about analytics and the policy needs a section that matches. **Also fixed a real accuracy bug found in the same section:** Section 5 (TradingView) previously said TradingView widgets "load regardless of your AdSense consent" while Section 3 claimed TradingView cookies were "only loaded after your explicit consent" — self-contradictory, and TradingView in fact always loads unconditionally. Section 3's sentence corrected to state that only Google Analytics is consent-gated; TradingView is not. Section 8's "withdraw your AdSense cookie consent" corrected to "analytics cookie consent." Meta description and `og:description` changed from "cookies, advertising data, and third-party integrations" to "cookies, analytics, and third-party integrations." `Last updated` bumped to July 2026.
- **Not touched, flagged for a future session:** `privacy.html` doesn't actually disclose Google Analytics usage anywhere prior to this fix, and even now the new Section 4 is the only GA4 disclosure on the site — worth a dedicated review of whether GA4's own data practices (IP handling, retention) need more detail here, separate from the AdSense cleanup this session was about.
- **`GUIDELINES.md`:** CSP allowed-origins list no longer includes `pagead2.googlesyndication.com`; note added explaining the removal and confirming the ad-domain CSP entries were dropped for the same reason across `netlify.toml`/`_headers` below.
- **`netlify.toml` / `_headers`:** both already documented as inert on GitHub Pages (v8.52.6) — cleaned anyway, since leaving ad-serving domains (`pagead2.googlesyndication.com`, `partner.googleadservices.com`, `tpc.googlesyndication.com`, `googleads.g.doubleclick.net`) in a file kept as "documentation of intent" would misrepresent that intent going forward.
- Verified: all 16 pages checked for `<div>`/`<h2>`/`<p>` tag balance post-edit (all matched); JSON-LD blocks on `index.html` re-validated as parseable JSON; `assets/gdpr.js` re-checked with `node --check`; full-repo grep for `adsense|pagead|googlesyndication|googleadservices|doubleclick` returns zero remaining matches.

## v8.53.0 (2026-07-13) — Crawl policy: robots.txt blocks raw data directories; sitemap generator auto-derives image blocks and stops dropping `guide-csi-indicator.html`

### Engine — `scripts/update_sitemap.py`
- **Root cause found:** `guide-csi-indicator.html` was confirmed missing from both the `PAGES` list and the live `sitemap.xml` — the second time this exact drift has happened (first caught and "fixed" in v8.43.5, referenced again as still-missing in v8.52.4). Both prior fixes edited `sitemap.xml` directly instead of the generator script; since `update-sitemap.yml` fully regenerates `sitemap.xml` from `PAGES` on every push touching an HTML page, any hand-edit to the XML file is silently reverted on the next automated run. **Fixed at the actual source this time:** `guide-csi-indicator.html` added to `PAGES` (priority 0.7, monthly — matches its sibling standalone-indicator guide).
- **Added image sitemap support:** `urlset` now declares `xmlns:image`. New `scan_page_images()` scans each page's own HTML for `<img>` tags whose `src` matches the `assets/screenshot-*` naming convention (favicons/icons never match this pattern, so they're excluded with no extra logic) and emits an `<image:image>` block per distinct screenshot, with `<image:caption>` from the image's own `alt` text. This replaces what would otherwise be a hand-maintained image list — the same class of drift that hit `guide-csi-indicator.html` twice for URLs — with a value derived from the live page content, so a screenshot can never be present on a page but absent from its sitemap entry.
- Regenerated `sitemap.xml` this session: 16 `<url>` entries (was 15), 61 `<image:image>` blocks across the 8 pages that have real content screenshots (`access.html` 14, `guide-dashboard.html` 26, `guide-mt5-ea.html` 8, `guide-cot.html` 5, `guide-rates-yield-curve.html` 3, `guide-economic-surprises.html` 2, `guide-csi-indicator.html` 2, `guide-gbpjpy-cot.html` 1). `index.html`, `guide-cross-asset-risk.html`, `guide-market-sentiment.html`, `guide-fx-liquidity.html`, and the four legal/about/contact pages correctly have zero, matching their actual `<img>` content. `lastmod` dates preserved from the currently published sitemap for this hand-assembled snapshot, since this local checkout has no git history to derive them from — the next push will let `update-sitemap.yml` recompute `lastmod` from `git log` as normal; this session's regeneration only needed to add the missing page and the image blocks.
- Validated: `python3 -m py_compile` passes; output XML parses as well-formed via `xml.etree.ElementTree`.

### Site — `robots.txt`
- **Found via Search Console review:** no `Disallow` rule existed for any of the 15 raw data directories (`ai-analysis/`, `calendar-data/`, `cot-data/`, `dtcc-data/`, `economic-data/`, `extended-data/`, `fx-data/`, `intraday-data/`, `meetings-data/`, `news-data/`, `ohlc-data/`, `ois-rates/`, `rates/`, `research-data/`, `rr-data/`, `sentiment-data/`) or `scripts/`, meaning Google was free to crawl and index raw JSON/CSV files directly instead of only the HTML pages that render them.
- **Fixed:** added a `Disallow` line for each of those directories, plus `scripts/` (Python source, no reader value). `assets/` deliberately left fully crawlable — it holds the screenshots the new image sitemap depends on.
- **Second, previously-invisible bug fixed in the same pass:** the file had separate `Googlebot`, `Bingbot`, and `Slurp` user-agent groups. The `Bingbot` and `Slurp` groups contained only `Allow: /` with no `Disallow` lines — per the robots.txt spec, a bot's own named group fully overrides the wildcard group for that bot, so Bing and Yahoo/Slurp were never actually subject to *any* of the wildcard block's disallow rules (this predates today's change; it applied to the old `news.html`/`en.html`/etc. lines too, they just happened to be moot since those files don't exist). Consolidated everything into a single `User-agent: *` block — no bot-specific behavior is needed here, and this removes the gap by construction instead of just patching it for the new rules.
- Existing `Disallow` lines for `news.html`, `en.html`, `guia-cot.html`, `tecnico-vs-fundamental.html` kept unchanged (documented in v8.52.6 as harmless legacy — those files don't exist, so the lines are inert either way).

### GUIDELINES.md
- New "Crawl policy — robots.txt" subsection under Hosting & deployment documenting the data-directory block list and the single-user-agent-group rationale.
- "Sitemap — active pages only" section rewritten: documents the two-time `guide-csi-indicator.html` drift and states plainly that `sitemap.xml` must never be hand-edited — only `scripts/update_sitemap.py`'s `PAGES` list, since the file is fully regenerated on every relevant push. Image sitemap paragraph rewritten to describe the new auto-scan behavior instead of a manual-add-in-the-same-session rule.
- Version footer bumped v8.52.6 → v8.53.0.

## v8.52.6 (2026-07-12) — Auditoría SEO (Search Console): `netlify.toml`/`_headers` inertes en producción, `.nojekyll` añadido

### Repo hygiene — hosting reality vs. dead config
- **Encontrado analizando el export de Google Search Console:** la home aparece fragmentada en tres URLs distintas con posiciones muy dispares (`/` pos. 19.08, `/index.html` pos. 24.73, `/index` pos. 7.92 sobre 28 días) — síntoma de canonicalización incompleta.
- **Causa raíz identificada:** `netlify.toml` y `_headers` definen redirects 301 (`/index.html → /`, `/news.html → /`, `/en.html → /`, `/guia-cot.html → /guide-cot.html`, `/tecnico-vs-fundamental.html → /guide-dashboard.html`) y cabeceras `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, pero **ninguno de los dos archivos se lee nunca en producción**: `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` despliega vía `actions/deploy-pages` (GitHub Pages puro, sin CNAME), que no procesa `netlify.toml` ni `_headers`. Esos redirects y cabeceras llevan tiempo dando una falsa sensación de estar resueltos.
- **Fixed:** añadido `.nojekyll` en la raíz del repo de sitio — Jekyll estaba activo por defecto (sin este archivo) y generaba la variante de permalink limpio `/index` además de `/` y `/index.html`, siendo la tercera fuente de fragmentación. Esto también evita el paso (no usado) de build de Jekyll en cada deploy.
- **No se puede arreglar con redirect real:** `/index.html` es el archivo físico que GitHub Pages sirve en `/`; no puede 301-earse a sí mismo sin servidor propio. La única defensa activa es el `rel="canonical"` ya presente en `index.html` (correcto, sin cambios) — se deja que Google termine de consolidar con el tiempo.
- **Confirmado inofensivo:** `en.html`, `guia-cot.html`, `tecnico-vs-fundamental.html`, `news.html` ya no existen como archivos (404 real) — los `Disallow` de `robots.txt` para esas rutas y los bloques `X-Robots-Tag` de `_headers` son restos sin efecto, no un problema activo.
- **Documented, not deleted:** ambos archivos ahora llevan una cabecera de advertencia explicando que están inertes mientras el deploy siga siendo GitHub Pages puro, y se preservan por si el proyecto migra a Netlify/Cloudflare Pages en el futuro.
- **GUIDELINES.md:** nueva sección "Hosting & deployment" bajo Architecture documentando este hallazgo para que no se repita el error de asumir que esas reglas están activas.
- **Otros hallazgos del mismo audit, sin acción de código (ver respuesta al usuario):** `guide-cot.html` tiene 2378 impresiones con solo 0.29% CTR pese a posición media ~10.4 — título/descripción candidatos a test A/B, no tocados en esta sesión por ser una decisión editorial de Santiago, no un bug. Varias queries larguísimas en Consultas.csv (estilo instrucción de agente IA) generan impresiones sin clics — consistentes con crawlers de motores de respuesta IA (Perplexity/ChatGPT/SGE), no un error a corregir.

## v8.52.3 (2026-07-12) — Admin dashboard: geolocation + time-remaining across all three tabs

### Infra — `gi-license-worker/worker.js` (Cloudflare Worker, manual deploy)
- **Completed the geolocation work started (and cut short mid-session) previously:** `handleSessionPing()` now captures `request.cf.country`/`request.cf.city` the same way `logAccess()` already did, and additionally stores the JWT's own `exp` claim (unix seconds) on every ping. `exp` is the authoritative expiry for that specific session token — it's already verified server-side by `verifyJWT()`, so storing it is free and avoids re-deriving expiry from `access_log` for the sessions view.
- **`/admin/sessions`** now returns `country`, `city`, `exp` per row (`active_sessions` table).
- **`/admin/logs/summary`** now returns `last_days`, `last_country`, `last_city` per group, via a correlated subquery against the single most recent `access_log` row for that `account`+`server`+`source` — not an aggregate. These describe the latest event only (a failed attempt as the latest row leaves them `null`, since `logAccess()` only records `days` on success). This lets "time remaining" and "last known location" show on the Summary tab without misrepresenting an aggregated window as one location/expiry.
- **`/admin/logs`** already had `country`/`city` in the previous session; no further change needed there — a "time remaining" column is computed client-side from the existing `ts` + `days` columns, no new backend field required.
- **Required D1 migration (not yet applied — run manually before deploying):**
  ```
  npx wrangler d1 execute gi-access-log --remote --command "ALTER TABLE access_log ADD COLUMN country TEXT"
  npx wrangler d1 execute gi-access-log --remote --command "ALTER TABLE access_log ADD COLUMN city TEXT"
  npx wrangler d1 execute gi-access-log --remote --command "ALTER TABLE active_sessions ADD COLUMN country TEXT"
  npx wrangler d1 execute gi-access-log --remote --command "ALTER TABLE active_sessions ADD COLUMN city TEXT"
  npx wrangler d1 execute gi-access-log --remote --command "ALTER TABLE active_sessions ADD COLUMN exp INTEGER"
  ```
  Existing rows get `NULL` for these columns until the next write — expected, same pattern as the historical gap already documented for `yt-founder-01-v2`.

### Tools — `tools/gi-admin-dashboard.html`
- **Active Sessions:** added `Location` (`city, COUNTRY`) and `Time left` columns, the latter from the session's stored `exp`.
- **Activation Log:** added `Time left` (computed client-side from `ts` + `days`, blank when the row wasn't a successful key/grant event) and `Location` columns.
- **Summary:** added `Time left` and `Last location` columns, both sourced from `last_days`/`last_country`/`last_city` (the most recent event in the group) — the `Last location` cell carries a title tooltip clarifying it reflects only the latest event, since the row itself is aggregated across possibly many IPs/sessions.
- New `.time-left` styling: default gray, orange under 3 days (`.soon`), red once past expiry (`.expired`).
- No new dependency — location/time-left formatting done with two small helper functions (`formatLocation()`, `timeRemaining()`), consistent with the file's existing zero-dependency, single-file pattern.

## v8.52.1 (2026-07-12) — License worker: /admin/* CORS opened for a standalone local admin dashboard

### Infra — `gi-license-worker/worker.js` (Cloudflare Worker, manual deploy)
- **Problem:** after v8.52.0 shipped `/admin/sessions`, Santiago confirmed the endpoint works via `curl` (`{"count":1,"sessions":[{"account":"yt-founder-01-v2","server":"promo",...}]}`) and asked for an HTML dashboard instead of running curl by hand. The worker's single `CORS_HEADERS` constant hardcoded `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://globalinvesting.github.io` for every route, so a dashboard opened from a local file or any other origin would have its `/admin/*` fetch calls blocked by the browser even with a correct `X-Admin-Key`.
- **Fix:** split into two header sets. `CORS_HEADERS` (unchanged, origin-locked to `https://globalinvesting.github.io`) still applies to `/validate`, `/session/ping`, and `/ping` — these are called from the public terminal's own browser JS and have no reason to be reachable elsewhere. A new `ADMIN_CORS_HEADERS` (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`) applies to every `/admin/*` route. `corsHeadersFor(pathname)` picks the right set for the OPTIONS preflight; `json()`/`err()` now take an optional `headers` argument so each admin handler (`handleAdminGrant`, `handleAdminLogs`, `handleAdminLogsSummary`, `handleAdminSessions`) passes `ADMIN_CORS_HEADERS` explicitly on every response, including error paths.
- **Why this doesn't weaken security:** every `/admin/*` handler already gates on `X-Admin-Key` via `timingSafeEqual()` before touching D1 — CORS only controls which browser origins can *read* the response, not whether the request reaches the Worker or succeeds. An unauthenticated caller from any origin still gets 401. Opening the origin restriction removes a redundant, incidental restriction (this endpoint was never meant to be origin-gated for security — it predates the admin-key check) without changing the actual access-control boundary.
- **Not changed:** `/validate` and `/session/ping` keep the origin lock — no reason yet to call these from outside the public site, and loosening them would let any page make license-key guesses or forge session pings against real accounts more conveniently (still infeasible without the HMAC seed/JWT secret, but no reason to widen the surface).

### Docs/backup — `cf-workers-backup/gi-license-worker/worker.js`, `cf-workers-backup/README.md`
- **Found stale while touching this file:** the `globalinvesting-scripts` repo's backup copy of `worker.js` predated `/admin/grant`'s D1 `logAccess()` integration (v8.40.0) and all of `/admin/logs`, `/admin/logs/summary`, `/session/ping`, `/admin/sessions` (v8.51.x–v8.52.0) — it only had the original `/validate` + `/ping` + bare `/admin/grant`. Replaced with the current production `worker.js` (including this session's CORS split) so the backup is a true mirror again. This drift wasn't caught earlier because `worker.js` deploys are manual (`wrangler deploy`) and don't touch this repo automatically — flagging for future sessions: **the backup copy needs a manual re-sync check any time `worker.js` changes**, there's no automated way to catch this drift.
- **README row updated** (see Infra section above) to describe the new per-route CORS split instead of the old single-origin description.

### New file — `gi-admin-dashboard.html` (not committed to any repo)
- **New standalone HTML/JS admin dashboard** for `/admin/sessions`, `/admin/logs`, and `/admin/logs/summary` — three tabs (Active Sessions, Activation Log, Summary), worker URL + admin key entered in the browser (key optionally cached in this file's own `localStorage` via a "Remember on this device" checkbox, never sent anywhere but the worker URL typed in), auto-refresh (30s) on the active tab, relative "time ago" formatting, and per-row badges distinguishing `key` vs `grant` activations and success/fail outcomes.
- **Deliberately kept out of both site repos:** this is an operator tool with no purpose for terminal users, and keeping it off `globalinvesting.github.io` avoids any chance of the admin surface being indexed or linked from the public site. Delivered as a standalone file for Santiago to keep locally and open directly (`file://`) or host privately.
- Styled with the same CSS custom properties (`--bg`, `--bg2`, `--blue`, `--font-mono`, etc.) as `assets/dashboard.css`'s default theme, for visual consistency with the rest of the terminal tooling.

## v8.52.0 (2026-07-12) — gi-auth.js: periodic session ping for real-time "who has the terminal open" visibility

### Frontend — assets/gi-auth.js
- **Santiago requested a way to see which activated accounts currently have the terminal open**, complementing the existing `/admin/logs` (activation history) and `/admin/logs/summary` (per-account activation counts) endpoints added on the license worker (`worker.js`, out of scope for this repo). Those only capture the moment of activation, not ongoing usage.
- **Fix:** `gi-auth.js` now calls the license worker's new `POST /session/ping` endpoint (Authorization: Bearer `<jwt>`) once immediately after activation succeeds, and again every 3 minutes (`SESSION_PING_INTERVAL_MS`) for as long as the tab stays open. Also fires on page load when a previously stored token is still valid (covers both key-activated sessions and one-click `?grant=` promo links).
- Ping calls are wrapped in a bare `.catch(() => {})` — a failed or unreachable ping never surfaces an error to the user or blocks any terminal functionality.
- Module version bumped to v1.1.0 (docstring header) to reflect the new capability.
- No new user-facing UI; this is a silent background call, so no accessibility or copy review was needed.

This now renders `Myfxbook RSS · actual vs consensus · 90d rolling` (or `90d/180d rolling` when the window auto-widens), matching the guide text corrected in v8.51.22 and the real `source` field in both JSON files.

## v8.51.17 (2026-07-11) — index.html: fixed mobile site-menu dropdown right-edge misalignment

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.css
- **Follow-up to v8.51.16.** After switching `.site-menu-panel` to `right: 0`, Santiago noticed the panel still didn't line up like on `access.html`: it opened flush against `.site-menu`'s own right edge rather than the true right edge of the header, leaving a strip of the CROSSES table's quote values visible past the panel's edge instead of being covered.
- **Root cause:** on `access.html`, `.site-menu` is the *last* child of `.topbar-right`, so its right edge already coincides with the header's true right edge — `right: 0` just works. On `index.html`, `.site-menu` is followed by `#session-label` and the clock inside `.topbar-right`, so `.site-menu`'s own right edge (the containing block `right: 0` resolves against) sits short of the header's actual edge.
- **Fix:** moved the positioning context up one level — added `position: relative` to `.topbar-right` and removed it from `.site-menu`. The panel's nearest positioned ancestor is now `.topbar-right`, so `right: 0` anchors to the header's true right edge (matching `access.html`'s behavior) without reordering any visible header elements. The `.site-menu::after` hover-bridge inherits the same new containing block — still functions, just spans the full `.topbar-right` width instead of only `.site-menu`'s width, which is harmless.
- Verified: `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 81 passed, 0 failed (CSS-only change).
