## v8.51.15 (2026-07-11) — ESI/CESI: fixed narrative-vs-panel divergence, excluded Myfxbook Sentiment noise

### generate_narrative_signals.py — Economic Surprise Index block
- **Root cause of narrative numbers disagreeing with the Economic Surprises panel (e.g. AI narrative said "GBP CESI net: +22 beats" while the panel showed GBP index -9.0 / 39% beat rate).** The narrative's CESI tally scanned the *entire* calendar.json history (up to `MAX_HISTORY_DAYS`=365d in `fetch_economic_calendar.py`), unweighted, while `dashboard.js` `renderEconSurprises()` scores only a 90d rolling window with exponential decay (45d half-life) + impact weighting (HIGH=1.0, MEDIUM=0.5). Reproduced exactly: GBP net=+22 came from 415 events over ~365d (beats 157, misses 135); the panel's 90d window has n≈122. Different populations, sometimes opposite sign.
- **Fix:** added a `ROLLING_WINDOW_DAYS = 90` cutoff (matches `LOOKBACK_DAYS` in `fetch_economic_calendar.py`) to the narrative CESI tally, so it describes the same event population the panel shows. Still an unweighted raw beat/miss count by design (narrative prose doesn't need the full decay/z-score blend) — but the *window* now matches, which was the dominant source of divergence. Verified post-fix: GBP net -3 (n=107), JPY net +12 (n=52) — both now directionally consistent with the panel instead of contradicting it.
- Prompt label updated to read "90d rolling window" explicitly so Gemini doesn't imply a different window than what the reader sees on the panel.

### Myfxbook "Sentiment" events excluded from all ESI/CESI scoring
- **Santiago flagged that "Japan Myfxbook USDJPY Sentiment" and similar events were being scored as economic releases in the Economic Surprises detail table.** These are Myfxbook's retail-positioning percentages, not official economic data — they carry no real consensus forecast. `calendar.json` was backfilling their missing `forecast` field from `previous` (last week's sentiment %), which fabricated a beat/miss against last week's reading rather than an actual survey estimate. Confirmed in production data: 287 Myfxbook Sentiment events in calendar.json; in one 90d window sample, 15/123 (~12%) of scored GBP events and a comparably large share of JPY events were this noise, inflating N and skewing beat rate / index.
- Added `'myfxbook'` to `NOISE_KW` (`dashboard.js`) and `_ESM_NOISE_KW` (`econ-surprises-modal.js`) — the keyword is `'myfxbook'` specifically, not `'sentiment'`, so legitimate sentiment surveys (Michigan Consumer Sentiment, ZEW Economic Sentiment, IFO, GfK Consumer Confidence) remain scored.
- `fetch_economic_calendar.py` v3.5: `compute_surprise_stats()` now also excludes Myfxbook titles from the surpriseStats z-score baseline, keeping the mean/std series clean even though downstream lookups were already unreachable for noise-filtered events.
- `generate_narrative_signals.py`'s CESI block gets the same exclusion for defense-in-depth (it currently drops these naturally via the forecast-only lookup, but previous-fallback could be added later).

## v8.51.10 (2026-07-11) — guide-rates-yield-curve.html: full content audit — 2Y tenor's true update cadence and fallback source corrected

### Guides — guide-rates-yield-curve.html
- **Overstated "updates every 5 minutes" claim applied uniformly to all five tenors (critical — data accuracy).** Traced the intraday quotes pipeline (`fetch_intraday_quotes.py`): 3M, 5Y, 10Y, and 30Y genuinely refresh every ~5 minutes during US market hours via yfinance tickers (`^IRX`, `^FVX`, `^TNX`, `^TYX`). The 2Y tenor does not — `^IRX` is the 13-week T-Bill, not a 2Y yield, so PASO 4 of the script always overwrites `quotes.us2y.close` with the daily FRED `DGS2` value read from `extended-data/USD.json`. That value only changes once per day, on whatever cadence the engine's `update_extended_data.py` FRED fetch runs, regardless of US market hours. Rewrote both the "What It Shows" paragraph and the detail-view "Data source" callout to state this explicitly rather than implying uniform 5-minute freshness across all five tenors.
- **Fallback claim named only DGS2, omitting DGS10 and DGS5 (or, in the detail view, omitted DGS5 entirely).** Verified against `fetchRiskData()`'s repo-fallback block: when the intraday feed is unavailable, `byId.us10y`, `byId.us2y`, and `byId.us5y` all fall back to `extended-data/USD.json` (FRED DGS10, DGS2, and DGS5 respectively) — not DGS2 alone. Also confirmed `update_extended_data.py` never populates `bond3m` or `bond30y` in that file, so the 3M and 30Y tenors have **no repo fallback** and render a dash if the intraday fetch fails, unlike what the original text implied. Rewrote both passages to name all three fallback series and call out the two tenors with no fallback.
- **Panel subtitle logic note added.** The "Live ~5min delay" vs. "FRED DGS2 · daily batch" subtitle (`yield-panel-sub`) is gated entirely on `byId.us2y.fromRepo` — i.e., the label that describes the whole five-tenor panel is driven by the one tenor that is never actually a live 5-minute tick. Documented this in the detail-view callout so the label's behavior isn't misread as reflecting all five tenors' individual freshness.
- Verified accurate, no changes needed: five-tenor set (3M/2Y/5Y/10Y/30Y) and their descriptions, 2Y–10Y spread table signals and thresholds, US–DE and US–JP 10Y spread signal logic (`US Premium`/`DE Premium`/`JP Premium`, matching `ys-usde-sig`/`ys-usjp-sig`), the Spreads tab's nine-economy scope, the detail-view Market Commentary sourcing description, and the Playbook section's four scenario descriptions.
- Verified via balance/anchor checks: `div` 105/105, `table` 2/2, `tr` 10/10, `td` 24/24, `th` 6/6, `ul` 1/1, `li` 5/5; all TOC anchors resolve to a matching `id`. `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 81 passed, 0 failed (no dashboard.js changes this session — guide-only fix).

  - **28 pairs / 8 currencies:** confirmed via the default `CurrencyPairs` input (28 comma-separated pairs, `SymbolGroups` = AUD/CAD/CHF/EUR/GBP/JPY/NZD/USD — 8 currencies, no NOK/SEK).

  - **Multi-lookback weighted z-score model, Asness/Moskowitz/Pedersen (2013):** confirmed — the indicator computes independent log-returns over 3 horizons, normalises each into a cross-sectional z-score (mean/SD across the pair universe at that horizon, not across history), then combines via `(W_s·z_s + W_m·z_m + W_l·z_l) / (W_s+W_m+W_l)` — matches the guide's description of the methodology and its cliff-edge-avoidance rationale exactly. Both the code's own header comments and `#property description` strings cite the same Asness et al. (2013) paper the guide cites.
- No corrections required — this entry closes out the open verification item from v8.51.5.

## v8.49.3 (2026-07-10) — access.html + guide-dashboard.html: removed the container border around framed mobile screenshots

### Reported by Santiago
After v8.49.2 removed the opaque black corner/margin fill from the mobile screenshot PNGs, a separate rectangular border was still visible around each phone mockup on both `access.html` and `guide-dashboard.html` (the 3-across grid).

### Root cause
Not an image problem this time — it's CSS. `.scr-hero` (the container `<div>` wrapping every screenshot on both pages) carries `border: 1px solid var(--border)`, intended for plain rectangular panel screenshots that have no frame of their own. The three mobile mockups already have a device outline baked into the PNG itself, so the container's own border was drawing a second, rectangular frame around the phone's rounded silhouette — the exact seam Santiago flagged.

### Fix
Added a `.scr-hero-frameless` modifier (`border: none; border-radius: 0;`, and clears the hover border-color) in both files' `<style>` blocks, and applied it alongside `scr-hero-contain` on all 4 mobile-mockup instances: the one in `access.html`'s `mobile-feature-row`, and the three in `guide-dashboard.html`'s `mobile-shots-grid`. Every other `.scr-hero` usage (plain panel screenshots, Derivatives Detail, etc.) is untouched — they still get their border.
- Verified: `access.html` div 198/198, `<section>` 6/6, `<p>` 18/18; `guide-dashboard.html` div 117/117, `<p>` 83/83; `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 81 passed, 0 failed.

## v8.49.2 (2026-07-10) — assets: removed opaque black corner/margin fill from framed mobile screenshots

### Reported by Santiago
The three framed mobile screenshots (`screenshot-mobile-*-framed.png`, used on `access.html` and `guide-dashboard.html`) had visible black square corners around the rounded phone-frame silhouette, creating a hard-edged contrast seam against the page's dark (but not pure-black) background.

### Root cause
All three PNGs were already RGBA, but the margin surrounding the phone mockup — not just the four corners, the full border on all sides — was filled with near-black RGB (~0–10) at full opacity (alpha=255), instead of being transparent. The phone bezel itself sits inset from the canvas edge (light-grey frame, RGB ~44–173, clearly distinguishable from the margin), so the mockups were originally composited onto/exported with an opaque black canvas rather than a transparent one.

### Fix
For each of the three assets: built a near-black mask (max(R,G,B) < 25), ran connected-component labeling (`scipy.ndimage.label`, 8-connectivity), and set alpha to 0 only for components touching the image border — i.e. the margin/corner fill connected to the outer edge. Verified zero affected pixels in the central 60% of each canvas (no leakage into the phone's actual screen content, which has its own legitimately dark — but not pure-black — background). Dimensions and color mode (RGBA) unchanged; only the alpha channel of the border-connected black region was modified. `assets/screenshot-mobile-cross-asset-risk-framed.png` (720×1440), `screenshot-mobile-narrative-chart-framed.png` (720×1441), `screenshot-mobile-overview-top-framed.png` (720×1440) — all replaced in place, filenames unchanged, no HTML edits needed.
- Verified: `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 81 passed, 0 failed.

## v8.49.0 (2026-07-10) — access.html: promoted Risk Monitor to flagship panel row, demoted Carry Trade Ranking to reference grid, retired FX Liquidity Canvas thumbnail

### Reported by Santiago
Asked whether Risk Monitor would be more relevant than one of the two panels then occupying prime real estate on `access.html`: Carry Trade Ranking (flagship `panel-feature-row`) and FX Liquidity Canvas (compact `feat-card-grid`). Before acting on a hunch, pulled the Search Console export (`Performance on Search`, last 16 months) to check actual query demand rather than guessing.

### Search Console evidence
- **Cross-asset / VIX / risk-sentiment cluster has real, sustained demand**: queries like "cross-asset flow relationships risk rates fx commodities crypto" (113 impressions, pos. 5.87), "eurusd cross market equities bonds vix gold correlation" (27–34 impressions, pos. ~7–9), "cross-asset risk analysis" (51 impressions), "gbp/usd vix correlation risk sentiment", plus `guide-cross-asset-risk.html` already carrying 1,277 impressions — demand exists and is only partially captured today.

## v8.48.0 (2026-07-09) — access.html: added sticky in-page section nav (scroll-spy)

### Reported by Santiago
Asked whether `access.html` should have a jump-to-section menu like the tab bar on Bloomberg Professional Services' product pages ("Overview / Key Features / Get the App"), so a visitor could reach any section (Pricing, Getting Started, etc.) without scrolling manually. First pass placed the nav between `#topbar` and the hero — flagged as looking like an unwanted extension of the fixed topbar rather than a page component, and in the wrong position relative to the hero. Relocated and restyled in the same session.

### Frontend — access.html
- **New `<nav class="subnav">`**: sits at the divider between the hero (`Institutional FX intelligence...`) and the first content section (`Interface — What you get`) — i.e. in normal document flow after the hero, not pinned above it. Lists all 6 page sections as anchor links — Overview, What You Get, Features, Pricing, Getting Started, MT5 Indicators — pointing at the existing heading/section ids (`#hero-heading`, `#iface-heading`, `#coverage-heading`, `#sub-heading`, `#activation`, `#companion-heading`). No new ids were needed; `#activation` was already the target of the existing "How to activate" hero button.
- **Sticky-on-scroll, not sticky-on-load**: `position: sticky; top: 36px` (36px = height of `#topbar`, itself sticky at `top: 0`). Because the nav is now positioned after the hero in the DOM, it only starts pinning once the user has scrolled it up to that offset — it does not appear docked to the topbar on initial page load.
- **Redesigned visual treatment (2nd pass — simplified further)**: first restyle (moved off `var(--head-bg)` onto `var(--bg2)` with mono uppercase tabs) still read as "off" — different font family from the rest of the page's body copy, plus a visible background band that didn't match the plain, no-chrome look of the Bloomberg reference tabs. Replaced with: `background: var(--bg)` (blends into the page instead of forming a band), `var(--font-ui)` (Inter, same as body/nav — not `var(--font-mono)`, which is reserved elsewhere for labels/data), sentence case at 13px/500 weight for inactive tabs, 700 weight + bright `#e8edf8` + `var(--blue)` underline for the active tab.
- **Redesigned visual treatment (3rd pass — contained-width divider)**: the bottom hairline was still on `.subnav` (full viewport width), so it stretched edge-to-edge unlike every other divider on the page — `.ac-section` borders sit inside `.page-body`'s `max-width: 1040px` column. Moved the `1px solid var(--border)` rule from `.subnav` to `.subnav-inner` (which already has that same `max-width: 1040px` centering), so the line under the tabs now matches the width and feel of the section dividers further down the page instead of spanning the full screen.
- **Redesigned visual treatment (4th pass — removed hero's own full-width border)**: even after the 3rd pass, a full-width line still showed *above* the tabs — this was `.hero`'s pre-existing `border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule)`, which used to be the hero's natural boundary before the subnav existed. With the subnav now sitting directly below the hero, that border read as a second, mismatched divider stacked right above the tabs' own contained one. Removed `border-bottom` from `.hero` entirely — the subnav's contained-width bottom border is now the only divider between the hero and the rest of the page.
- **Redesigned visual treatment (5th pass — divider reverted to full width; chrome vs. content distinction)**: on review, the contained-width divider (3rd pass) was the wrong call. The subnav is navigation chrome sitting directly under `#topbar` (itself full-width) — institutional-platform convention (and the Bloomberg reference) treats nav/tab bars as full-width interface chrome, while contained-width dividers are reserved for separating *content* sections (`.ac-section` boundaries further down the page). Moved the `1px solid var(--border)` rule back to `.subnav` (full width), matching `#topbar` directly above it, while `.subnav-inner`'s `max-width: 1040px` still keeps the tab text aligned to the same content column as the rest of the page.
- **Scroll offset fix (6th pass)**: clicking a tab was landing with the target heading partially cut off behind the sticky bars — `scroll-margin-top: 78px` undershot the actual combined sticky height (`#topbar` 36px + `.subnav` ~49px ≈ 85px), leaving no breathing room. Increased to `scroll-margin-top: 104px` on `#hero-heading`, `.section-title`, and `#activation` so the heading clears both sticky bars with visible margin instead of sitting flush against them.
- **Scroll-spy**: a small `IntersectionObserver` (vanilla JS, no library) highlights the active link as the user scrolls. Degrades gracefully (no active-state styling, but links still work) if `IntersectionObserver` is unsupported.
- **`scroll-margin-top: 84px`** on `#hero-heading`, `.section-title`, and `#activation` — accounts for topbar (36px) + subnav (~48px) both being pinned when a link is clicked mid-scroll, so anchor jumps don't hide the heading behind them.
- **Mobile**: `.subnav-inner` added to the existing 700px-breakpoint padding rule (alongside `.hero-inner`, `.page-body`) and scrolls horizontally (`overflow-x: auto`, scrollbar hidden) rather than wrapping, since 6 labels don't fit a narrow viewport in one row.
- No existing section, id, or button behavior changed — this is additive only.
- Verified after edit: `access.html` div count 198/198, `<section>` count 6/6 (nav is not a `<section>`), `<p>` count 18/18, `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 81 passed, 0 failed.

## v8.47.13 (2026-07-09) — access.html: fixed two `panel-feature-row` bugs (font mismatch, broken border-suppression selector) + missed gallery-break transition

### Reported by Santiago
Flagged three things after v8.47.12: (1) the Carry Trade Ranking / Panel Views body copy reads in a visibly different font from the rest of the page, (2) "Any Device" now shows a divider both above and below the label, and (3) whether the "Screenshots" section needs work to cohere with everything redesigned around it. All three traced to concrete causes, not design ambiguity.

### Frontend — access.html
- **Root cause 1 — font mismatch**: `.panel-feature-desc` (added in v8.47.11) only declared `max-width`, with no `font-size`/`color`/`line-height`/`strong` rules — so it fell back to the page's default `<p>` styling (15px, bright `var(--text)`, 1.6 line-height) instead of the intended editorial-row treatment. Added the same declarations `.mobile-feature-desc` already uses (13.5px, `var(--text2)`, 1.8 line-height, `strong` in `var(--text)`), so Panel Views and Any Device copy now render identically.
- **Root cause 2 — double divider**: `.mobile-feature-row:first-of-type` and `.panel-feature-row:first-of-type` used `:first-of-type`, which matches by **tag** (`div`), not class — since other `<div>`s (labels, grids) now precede these rows in the DOM, the selector never matched, so each row's own `border-top` rendered *in addition to* the new `.gallery-break` divider above the label. Replaced both with `.scr-gallery-label + .mobile-feature-row` / `.scr-gallery-label + .panel-feature-row` (adjacent-sibling on the actual preceding element), which is correct regardless of what else is in the container. Fixed the same latent bug on the first Panel Views row, not just Any Device.
- **Missed transition — Screenshots → Panel Views**: this is a grid→editorial density transition exactly like the other two already fixed in v8.47.12, but its label (`Panel Views`) still had the old plain `margin-top:28px`. Applied `.gallery-break` here too, so all three density transitions in this cluster (Screenshots→Panel Views, Panel Views→Additional Coverage, Additional Coverage→Any Device) now use the same rule consistently.
- **Screenshots section — no change needed**: confirmed it already shares the same reference-grid typographic grammar as Additional Coverage (`.scr-item-meta` and `.feat-card-desc` are both `var(--font-mono)`, both `var(--text3)`, both ~10px) — the size difference (2-col hero-scale vs 4-col compact) is the intentional flagship-vs-supplementary hierarchy, not a mismatch. The two-mode system (mono-caption reference grids vs sans editorial rows) is now applied consistently page-wide.
- Verified after edit: `access.html` div count 197/197, `<section>` count 6/6, `<p>` count 18/18, `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 81 passed, 0 failed.

## v8.47.3 (2026-07-09) — CORRECTION to v8.47.2: the RBNZ hike was real, not a hallucination — Guard 7's same-day-only window was overwriting true CB decisions with false "on hold" claims

### Correction — Santiago caught this, I was wrong in v8.47.2
Santiago flagged that the RBNZ actually did raise the OCR 25bp to 2.50% on **8 July 2026** — confirmed directly against rbnz.govt.nz ("The Monetary Policy Committee agreed to increase the official cash rate to 2.5% on Wednesday 8 July") plus Bloomberg, FXStreet, and ActionForex coverage. Next scheduled decision: 2 September 2026. **This was never a hallucination.** The NZD/JPY CRIT signal ("RBNZ delivers a hawkish rate hike to 2.5%") was correct. The narrative ("RBNZ on hold at 2.5%") was the one that was wrong — and Guard 7 is what made it wrong, by overwriting a true claim with a fabricated one.

### Real root cause
`Guard 7` (`_apply_narrative_guards`) and the shared `_released_rate_decision_ccys_today()` (used by drivers/catalysts, and now Guard 8 in signals per v8.47.2) both required the calendar event's `dateISO` to match **exactly today's UTC date**. The run that produced this narrative executed at `2026-07-09T17:00:29Z` — one calendar day *after* the RBNZ's release on `2026-07-08`. The strict same-day check excluded NZD from "confirmed decisions," so Guard 7 treated a real, 24-hour-old rate hike as if it had never happened, stripped the narrative's (correct) reference to it, and replaced it with a generic "RBNZ on hold at 2.5%" fallback — actively converting true information into false information. My v8.47.2 fix (Guard 8 for signals) reused this exact same shared function, so it would have made the identical mistake to signals on any future run one day after a real decision — same bug, just not yet triggered in that run's log.

### Fix — widened the date window, same shared source, three call sites at once
- `_apply_narrative_guards()` Guard 7 (inline calendar check): `dateISO == today` → `dateISO in (today, yesterday)` (UTC).
- `_released_rate_decision_ccys_today()` (shared function backing drivers, catalysts, and the new signals Guard 8): same widening, in one place, so all three call sites move together and can't drift.
- Verified safe against the original bug Guard 7 was built for (v8.1.0, SNB case documented at CHANGELOG line ~2411): that was a decision *fabricated 2 days before* the real meeting date — a different failure mode, unaffected by widening the trailing/backward window to include yesterday.
- Re-verified against this exact incident: with the fix, `dateISO="2026-07-08"` now falls inside `{today="2026-07-09", yesterday="2026-07-08"}` → NZD correctly included in confirmed-decision currencies → the real hike is preserved instead of stripped.
- `python3 -m py_compile` clean.

### Residual, not fixed this pass (flagging, not scope-creeping)
Widening to "yesterday" only patches the specific 24–48h window; it does not address CB decisions older than that still occasionally appearing in incorrect present tense (e.g. "RBNZ delivers a hike" three days later, when it should read "RBNZ, which raised rates last week..."). A separate tense-correction pass already exists for driver notes (`_correct_cb_tense_text`, used via `_sanitize_cb_action_tense_drivers`) but nothing analogous runs on narrative or signals. Worth a dedicated session if stale-tense CB references recur beyond the 2-day window.

## v8.47.2 (2026-07-09) — generate_narrative_signals.py: fixed a real CB-decision hallucination that shipped in a CRIT signal — Guard 7 protected the narrative, signals had no equivalent guard

### Bug found and fixed — Engine, `_apply_signal_guards()`
**Reported by Santiago** as a "narrative quality" complaint on the 2026-07-09T17:00 intraday run; investigation found something more serious than quality — a factual contradiction between two Gemini outputs from the same run:
- The narrative call hallucinated *"New Zealand Dollar jumps to a three-week high after a hawkish RBNZ rate hike"* — caught and stripped by `_apply_narrative_guards()` Guard 7, which confirmed via `ff_calendar.json` that **no currency had a released rate decision that day** (log: `Guard 7: currencies with released rate decision today: none`). Final narrative correctly read "RBNZ on hold at 2.5%."
- The **signals call**, run separately ~20s later in the same workflow execution, hallucinated the identical false claim — `[CRIT] NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + RBNZ Hawkish Hike: "NZD/JPY surges as the RBNZ delivers a hawkish rate hike to 2.5% (HIKING)..."` — and it shipped to `signals.json` uncorrected, as a CRIT-severity alert.

**Root cause:** Guard 7's CB-decision hallucination check (added v8.1.0, generalized into `_strip_cb_decision_hallucination()` / `_released_rate_decision_ccys_today()` and wired into driver notes and catalysts) was never wired into `_apply_signal_guards()`. `_apply_signal_guards()`'s own docstring enumerated exactly 6 guards (stale date, modal verb, filler, CB rate stale-training, OIS injection, squeeze direction) plus an unnamed 7th (carry cross-pair mismatch) already in the code — none of them check for an invented CB decision. Two independent Gemini calls (narrative, signals) can hallucinate the same false central-bank action in the same run; only one of the two outputs had a guard against it.

**Fix — Guard 8, `_apply_signal_guards()`:**
- Reuses the exact same truth source and functions already trusted for narrative/drivers/catalysts (`_released_rate_decision_ccys_today()`, `_strip_cb_decision_hallucination()`) — no new detection logic, no risk of the three call sites drifting out of sync.
- **Body (`text`):** same sentence-level replacement already used for driver notes — invented decision sentence replaced with a generic `"{CB} {actual_rate}%."` fallback sourced from `rates/*.json`.
- **Title:** signals have no sentence structure to fall back on, so the hallucinated clause and its `+`/`—`/`-` connector are excised instead of inventing title prose (`"NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + RBNZ Hawkish Hike"` → `"NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme"`).
- Verified against the exact strings from this run's log (title + body regex match, correct clause excised, correct currency identified) before wiring into the guard pipeline; `python3 -m py_compile` clean.

### Also verified this run (not bugs, explains the "poorer quality" complaint)
- All three Gemini calls in this run (narrative, signals, session context) exhausted the primary model `gemini-3-flash-preview` across all 3 keys (503 "model overloaded" + at least one real daily-quota exhaustion — self-tracked tally 14/17 — confirmed genuine, not just transient) and fell back to the weaker `gemini-3.5-flash`. Session context fell through even that to the Groq pool (`llama-3.3-70b-versatile`, auto-selected over the known-broken `gpt-oss-120b` via the existing TPM-aware model cascade). This is the fallback cascade working as designed under sustained upstream Gemini degradation, not a pipeline defect — but it explains why today's narrative prose reads thinner than usual. No action taken; same known `gpt-oss-120b` 413 regression from prior sessions remains open separately.

### Still open (unchanged from prior sessions)
- `gpt-oss-120b` 413 TPM regression on Groq session-context calls (only avoided here because the cascade routed around it to `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`, not because it's fixed).
- `sitemap.xml` missing `xmlns:image` namespace / `<image:image>` blocks.

## v8.46.4 (2026-07-08) — access.html: fixed screenshot grid uniformity regression (reported by Santiago via screenshot)

### Root cause
`.scr-item-frame`'s base rule uses a fixed `aspect-ratio: 1.95` with `object-fit: contain` precisely so all four screenshots in the grid render at a uniform frame size regardless of each source image's native proportions (this is why MT5 EA, Web Terminal, Derivatives, and CFTC Positioning all look consistent). The v8.46.2/v8.46.3 sessions added inline `style="aspect-ratio: ..."` overrides using each new image's *native* ratio (406/364, then 407/336) to guard against CLS — this defeated the uniform-frame system and made the CB Rate Expectations / Economic Surprise Index row render visibly taller/more square than the row above it.

### Frontend — access.html
- **Fix:** Removed the inline `aspect-ratio` overrides on both `.scr-item-frame` divs (CB Rate Expectations, Economic Surprise Index), restoring the shared `1.95` base rule. CLS is unaffected — the frame's box size is fixed by CSS independent of image dimensions, so this is actually more CLS-safe than the per-image override, not less.
- `width`/`height` attributes on the `<img>` tags and the JSON-LD `ImageObject` entries are left untouched (accurate intrinsic/metadata dimensions; they don't drive frame layout).

## v8.46.1 (2026-07-08) — SEO: shortened title tags and meta descriptions on guide-cot.html and guide-gbpjpy-cot.html to fix truncation-driven CTR loss

### Reported by Santiago
Google Search Console (last 3 months) showed both pages ranking well but converting almost none of that visibility into clicks: `guide-cot.html` — 8,919 impressions, position 8.28, CTR 0.16%; `guide-gbpjpy-cot.html` — 3,222 impressions, position 4.88, CTR 0.03% (1 click). A position under 5 with a CTR near zero is not a ranking problem — it is a SERP snippet problem.

### Root cause
Both pages' `<title>` tags were 90–99 characters and meta descriptions were 246–263 characters — well past Google's effective SERP display budget (~60 chars for title before pixel-width truncation, ~155–160 chars for description). Truncation was cutting the brand suffix off the title and ending the description mid-sentence, producing an incomplete-looking snippet despite strong rankings.

### Fix — `guide-cot.html`, `guide-gbpjpy-cot.html`
- Rewrote `<title>`, `<meta name="description">`, `og:title`, and `twitter:title` on both pages to industry-standard lengths (titles 48–54 chars, meta description 143–150 chars), front-loading the primary keyword and keeping the most information-dense clause before the truncation point.
- Left `og:description`, `twitter:description`, and the JSON-LD `headline`/`description` fields unchanged — these are not subject to the same SERP truncation and the existing longer copy is appropriate for social-preview and structured-data contexts (JSON-LD headline on `guide-gbpjpy-cot.html` is 80 chars, already under Google's 110-char Article rich-result cap).
- Validated both files' JSON-LD blocks still parse correctly post-edit (`re.findall` + `json.loads`, 3 blocks in `guide-cot.html`, 4 in `guide-gbpjpy-cot.html`, all OK).

### Verification
- No leftover references to the old title/description strings anywhere else in the site (checked `.html`/`.xml`).
- Manual char-count check confirms new title/description lengths are within the safe SERP display range on both desktop and mobile.

### Follow-up (manual, not done in this session)
- Monitor Search Console CTR for both pages over the next 2–4 weeks to confirm the snippet change moves CTR toward the 3–8% range typical for positions in the 5–8 band, rather than assuming the fix worked from ranking alone.

## v8.46.0 (2026-07-08) — Fix: "next meeting" and OIS forward calcs ignored already-resolved same-day meetings

### Reported by Santiago
After the PAT_TOKEN sync was fixed and `workflow_meetings.yml` run #119 executed successfully, its own log confirmed a second, independent bug (predicted before the run, then observed live): NZD's next meeting stayed pinned at "8 Jul" — a meeting that had already happened and already been decided (RBNZ hike 2.25%→2.5%) — instead of advancing to "2 Sep". The log also showed the NZD cbonds OIS curve fetched 19 tenors successfully but never reached the forward-rate calculation step, falling through silently to the weaker NZFBF/IR3TIB fallback chain.

### Root cause — `.github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml` (engine)
Every per-currency "next meeting" filter (`_future_mtgs_<ccy> = [d for d in _mtg_list_<ccy> if d >= today]`, repeated for EUR/GBP/JPY/CAD/CHF/NZD/NOK/SEK, plus AUD's own `_aud_next_meeting_date()`, plus the main output loop's `nextMeeting` calc) only checked whether the calendar date had passed — never whether the decision had actually been released. When a meeting's date is today, `days_to_T1` computes to `0`, and each fetcher's own OIS forward-rate guard (`if T1_days > 0`) treats `0` as falsy and skips the real curve calculation entirely, with no error or warning logged. This is exactly why NZD's `bias=hold` in run #119 was correct by coincidence (via the weak IR3TIB fallback) rather than by the intended cbonds OIS forward path that was fetched but never used.

### Fix — `workflow_meetings.yml` (engine)
- Added a shared `_meeting_resolved(ccy, meeting_date)` helper that cross-references `calendar-data/ff_calendar.json` (already checked out from the site repo in this workflow) — a meeting counts as resolved only if a same-day, same-currency "Rate Decision" event is marked `released: true` with a non-empty `actual` value. Fails safe (treats as unresolved) if the calendar file or matching event is unavailable.
- Added `_next_unresolved_meetings(ccy, meetings, today)`, replacing the plain `d >= today` filter in all 8 cbonds-curve fetchers (EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, CHF, NZD, NOK, SEK).
- Applied the same resolved-check to AUD's `_aud_next_meeting_date()` and to the main output loop that produces `nextMeeting` for all 10 currencies (USD included, for display consistency).
- Relaxed each fetcher's `T1_days > 0` guard to `T1_days >= 0`, so a meeting dated today that has *not yet* been decided (calendar hasn't caught up, or the decision genuinely hasn't happened yet at run time) still uses the real OIS curve — bracketing the forward calc at the nearest available tenor — instead of silently falling back to a weaker source tier.
- Bumped the workflow's internal log banner from the stale `v8.7.0` label to `v8.46.0`.
- Verified against the live `calendar-data/ff_calendar.json` snapshot: NZD's meeting list now correctly resolves to `2026-09-02` as the next meeting instead of the already-decided `2026-07-08`.

## v8.45.0 (2026-07-08) — Fix: CB Rate Expectations showed stale pre-hike RBNZ forecast after Central Bank Rates already updated

### Reported by Santiago
After the RBNZ 2026-07-08 hike (2.25%→2.5%), Central Bank Rates correctly showed 2.50%, but CB Rate Expectations kept showing the pre-decision forecast for the meeting that had just happened ("Hike 82% · 2.46%") instead of anything reflecting the post-hike state.

### Root cause #1 — `.github/workflows/update-ff-calendar.yml` (site) — the "Dispatch cb-rate-decision" step has never actually worked
`meetings-data/meetings.json` (CB Rate Expectations' data source) is written by `workflow_meetings.yml` in `globalinvesting-engine`, which only had a Monday 10:00 UTC cron. The v5.2 fast-path was supposed to close this gap for `rates/*.json` via a same-repo dispatch to `update-rates.yml`, but that dispatch itself was broken: it POSTed to `https://api.github.com/repos/${{ github.repository }}/dispatches` using `GITHUB_TOKEN`. `github.repository` always resolves to the repo the *workflow file* lives in — `globalinvesting.github.io` — never the listener's repo. `update-rates.yml`'s `repository_dispatch: types: [cb-rate-decision]` trigger lives in **`globalinvesting-scripts`**, a different repository — `repository_dispatch` events only fire workflows within the exact repo the event was POSTed to. The dispatch has therefore been a silent no-op since it was introduced: no workflow in `globalinvesting.github.io` listens for `cb-rate-decision`, and `GITHUB_TOKEN` couldn't have authenticated a cross-repo call regardless. This is why today's RBNZ correction to `rates/NZD.json` needed a manual `workflow_dispatch` of `update-rates.yml` instead of updating on its own.

Separately, even a working dispatch to `update-rates.yml` would only have fixed `rates/NZD.json` (Central Bank Rates) — it never touched `meetings.json` (CB Rate Expectations) at all, which explains the second half of the symptom: the rate panel corrected itself (once triggered manually) while the expectations panel had no same-day refresh path whatsoever, only the Monday cron.

### Fix — `update-ff-calendar.yml` (site — v5.3)
- Rewrote the "Dispatch cb-rate-decision" step to explicitly target `GlobalInvesting/globalinvesting-scripts` (not `${{ github.repository }}`), authenticated with `SCRIPTS_PAT` — already documented in GUIDELINES.md as having `Contents: Read and write` on both `globalinvesting.github.io` and `globalinvesting-scripts`.
- **Added a second dispatch**, to `GlobalInvesting/globalinvesting-engine`, authenticated with `PAT_TOKEN` (the same secret the engine repo's own workflows already use to write back to this public repo), so `workflow_meetings.yml` recalculates the OIS-implied bias for the next meeting same-day instead of waiting up to a week.
- Both calls now check the HTTP status code (`204` = accepted) and print a warning with the response body on failure, instead of assuming success silently — the entire class of bug fixed here was a dispatch that "succeeded" (curl returned 0) while doing nothing, so future failures should be loud, not silent.

### Fix — `workflow_meetings.yml` (engine — v8.19.1)
- Added `repository_dispatch: types: [cb-rate-decision]` to the `on:` block so this workflow can be triggered immediately by the dispatch above, alongside its existing Monday-only cron.

### Manual interim data correction — `meetings-data/meetings.json` (site)
Per the existing GUIDELINES.md rule ("If a CB makes an emergency inter-meeting decision and the OIS source has not yet updated, manually set `bias` and `biasUpdated` in `meetings.json` and commit directly"), patched the `NZD` entry by hand as a stop-gap until the fixed dispatch (or the next Monday cron) recalculates it live:
- `nextMeeting`/`nextMeetingISO` advanced from the just-occurred `8 Jul` meeting to the genuinely upcoming `2 Sep` meeting (the entry was still describing the meeting that already happened).
- `bias` reset to `hold` (`cutProb`/`hikeProb` = 0, `fwdRate` = 2.50 = current policy rate) rather than fabricating a new hike/cut probability for the Sep 2 meeting — this environment has no network access to cbonds.com to compute a genuine post-hike forward, so a neutral placeholder was used instead of an invented number. `biasMethod` set to `heuristic` and `biasSource` annotated as an interim placeholder so this is auditable as non-live data until the automated pipeline overwrites it.

### Not verified live
No network access to `api.github.com`'s dispatch endpoint, `cbonds.com`, or GitHub Actions from this environment. `python3 -m py_compile`/YAML-parse validation passes for all three changed files. Recommend confirming in production: (1) that `SCRIPTS_PAT` and `PAT_TOKEN` are both configured as repo secrets in `globalinvesting.github.io` (this fix assumes they are, per existing usage elsewhere in this same workflow file and across the engine repo); (2) trigger `update-ff-calendar.yml` (or wait for the next genuine rate-decision actual) and confirm both dispatch calls return HTTP 204 in the Actions log; (3) confirm `meetings.json`'s `NZD` entry gets overwritten with a live OIS-derived read shortly after.

## v8.44.4 (2026-07-08) — Fix: narrative kept saying "Watch the RBNZ rate decision at 02:00 UTC tomorrow" a full day after the decision already happened

### Reported by Santiago
The AI narrative referenced the RBNZ rate decision as still upcoming ("Watch the RBNZ rate decision at 02:00 UTC tomorrow") in a narrative generated well after the decision had already been released — same incident day as v8.44.3 above, different symptom.

### Root cause — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`, Guard 6 ("Watch-clause calendar validation", v8.4.8)
This guard already existed specifically to catch the LLM inventing rate-decision times from training memory: it extracts the CB name from any "Watch [Bank] rate decision at HH:MM UTC" clause and checks whether that bank has a genuinely upcoming (unreleased, within 48h) calendar event before allowing the clause through.
The check was too coarse: it added the **bare currency code** to the "validated" set for **any** upcoming event of that currency, not specifically rate-decision events. NZD had an unrelated, genuinely upcoming "New Zealand Business NZ PMI" within the 48h window (visible in Santiago's earlier calendar screenshot) — that alone was enough to make the guard treat "Watch the RBNZ rate decision" as validated, even though the *specific* rate-decision event for NZD had already been released hours/a day earlier.

### Fix
Guard 6 now only adds a currency to the validation set when the calendar event's own title matches a rate-decision keyword (`interest rate decision`, `rate decision`, `monetary policy decision`, `monetary policy statement`, `cash rate decision`, `cash rate target` — the same keyword class introduced in `fetch_ff_calendar.py` v3.33 / `fetch_rates.py` v14.2 earlier today, kept in sync manually since this is a separate repo). An unrelated upcoming release (PMI, GDP, etc.) for the same currency no longer falsely validates a rate-decision claim.
Verified with two isolated tests: (1) reproducing the exact incident (RBNZ released + upcoming unrelated NZD PMI) — the claim is now correctly identified as unvalidated and gets stripped to "Watch the next RBNZ meeting"; (2) a regression check with a genuinely upcoming rate decision (CAD) — still correctly validated, no false negatives introduced.

### Related
See the "Never gate critical logic on an upstream source's own subjective classification..." principle added to `GUIDELINES.md` today (v8.44.3) — this is the same underlying pattern (a coarse proxy signal standing in for a more specific one) surfacing in a second, independent place the same day.

---



### Reported by Santiago
The 2026-07-08 RBNZ decision (2.25%→2.5%) appeared in the Economic Calendar within the normal pipeline latency, but never updated the Central Bank Rates panel or the Economic Matrix CB RATE column — both stayed at 2.25% for hours afterward.

### Root cause
Two fast-path mechanisms exist specifically to get same-day CB rate decisions into `rates/*.json` without waiting on the slow BIS/RBNZ-scraping fallback chain (introduced in v8.1.0):
1. `.github/workflows/update-ff-calendar.yml` — "Dispatch cb-rate-decision" step, fires `repository_dispatch` → `update-rates.yml` when a released high-impact rate-decision actual is detected.
2. `scripts/fetch_rates.py` (site repo) — Step 0-A, reads `ff_calendar.json` actuals as the highest-priority source on every run (dispatched or scheduled).

Both hard-filter on `event["impact"] == "high"`. Myfxbook's RSS feed tagged "New Zealand RBNZ Interest Rate Decision" as `impact="medium"` — Fed/ECB/BoE decisions are consistently tagged `"high"` by Myfxbook, but smaller G10 central banks are not guaranteed to be. Both fast-path mechanisms silently no-op'd on this event; confirmed via the workflow's own "Display summary" step, which only listed `high`-impact events for the day (FOMC Minutes) — the RBNZ decision, though released with `actual=2.5%`, wasn't in that list. The calendar panel itself doesn't filter on impact when rendering actuals, so it displayed correctly — only the two fast-path CB-rate consumers were blind to it. Without the fast path, `rates/NZD.json` was left to the normal Step 1 fallback chain (BIS WS_CBPOL — monthly frequency, real lag of days; RBNZ's own site returns 403 to all scraping), so the correction would not have arrived same-day at all.

### Fix — `scripts/fetch_ff_calendar.py` (site — v3.33)
- **New shared helper `_force_high_if_rate_decision(title, impact)`:** forces any event whose title matches a rate-decision keyword (`interest rate decision`, `rate decision`, `monetary policy decision`, `monetary policy statement`, `cash rate decision`, `cash rate target`) to `impact="high"`, regardless of the upstream source's own tag. Applied in all three parsers — `fetch_myfxbook_rss()` (the live production path), `fetch_myfxbook_calendar()` (HTML fallback), and `_normalise_worker_events()` (currently dead code, CF Worker `/myfxbook` endpoint is blocked from GH Actions — fixed anyway in case it's revived).
- Fixing at the classification source means the calendar UI itself (impact-dot color, any impact-based filtering) is correct going forward.
- **Caveat found after writing this fix:** re-running `update-ff-calendar.yml` does NOT retroactively repair an already-recorded event. The commit/dispatch gate (`data_changed`) fingerprints on `(title, currency, dateISO, actual, forecast)` — it does not include `impact` — so a run that only reclassifies an already-seen actual computes `data_changed=False`, skips the git commit, and the "Dispatch cb-rate-decision" step never even runs its check. This fix therefore protects *future* decisions (first time an actual is seen, the corrected impact is part of the initial fingerprinted write) but does nothing for the NZD backlog already sitting in `ff_calendar.json` with `impact="medium"`.

### Fix — `scripts/fetch_rates.py` (site — v14.2) — the fix that actually unblocks NZD right now
Confirmed via Santiago's `update-rates.yml #36` production log: Step 0-A ran and printed `No released high-impact rate-decision actuals in 3-day window` — the RBNZ actual was sitting right there in `ff_calendar.json` (`actual="2.5%"`, `released=true`, today's date) but `impact="medium"` on the persisted file (the `fetch_ff_calendar.py` fix above hasn't run again yet, and per the caveat, won't retroactively fix this record even once deployed). NZD fell through to SOURCE 1 → BIS CBPOL/M.NZ, monthly frequency, returning a rate dated **2026-05-01** — over two months stale, independent of today's hike.
- **Removed the `if _ev.get('impact') not in ('high',): continue` gate from Step 0-A entirely.** The very next check already does a title-keyword match against `_RATE_DEC_KW` (`interest rate decision`, `cash rate target`, etc.) — a signal at least as reliable as Myfxbook's impact tag, and one this pipeline fully controls. Step 0-A no longer depends on any upstream source's impact classification at all.
- Verified with an isolated harness reproducing the exact production event (title="New Zealand RBNZ Interest Rate Decision", impact="medium", actual="2.5%", released=true) — Step 0-A now correctly resolves NZD to 2.5% from that record alone.
- **Practical effect:** no need to re-run `update-ff-calendar.yml` to fix the current NZD staleness — the already-committed `ff_calendar.json` has everything Step 0-A needs. Deploying this fix and triggering `update-rates.yml` directly (workflow_dispatch, or its next scheduled cron) resolves it immediately.
- This is also the more durable fix of the two: even if a future upstream source misclassifies impact for some other G10 bank the same way, `fetch_rates.py` no longer cares — it decides for itself from the title.


### Not fixed here (separate, non-bug topic — also asked by Santiago)
- **"Why does the calendar itself take several minutes to update?"** This is expected pipeline latency, not a bug: CF Worker detection (~2–3 min) → workflow run (~10s once triggered) → git commit/push → `deploy-pages.yml` triggers on push → GitHub Pages build/deploy (~1–2 min) → CDN edge propagation/browser cache. Several minutes end-to-end is consistent with the documented "Normal (CF Worker active): ~2–3 min" latency in `update-ff-calendar.yml`'s header plus the deploy chain on top of it — Bloomberg-style sub-second latency isn't achievable on free REST APIs + static hosting regardless of architecture.

### Not verified live
No network access to Myfxbook or GitHub Actions from this environment. `python3 -m py_compile` passes for both changed files. `fetch_ff_calendar.py`'s three call sites were traced against the exact production log Santiago supplied. `fetch_rates.py`'s Step 0-A was verified with an isolated harness reproducing the exact production event byte-for-byte (title, impact="medium", actual="2.5%", released=true) — confirmed it now resolves NZD to 2.5% from that record alone. Recommend confirming in production: (1) trigger `update-rates.yml` now and confirm `rates/NZD.json` shows 2.5% dated today with `source="ff-calendar-actual"`; (2) watch the next fresh (not-yet-seen) rate decision from any G10 bank to confirm the full same-day pipeline end-to-end.

## v8.44.1 (2026-07-07) — Session context Groq fallback 413'd immediately after the v8.44.0 model swap; added a TPM-aware model cascade for this call site only

### Engine — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`
- **Reported by Santiago:** the next scheduled run after v8.44.0 shipped showed `generate_session_context()` failing with `GROQ_HTTP_413: Request too large for model openai/gpt-oss-120b ... TPM: Limit 8000, Requested 11368` — a direct regression from the v8.44.0 Groq model swap (`llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct` → `openai/gpt-oss-120b`).
- **Root cause:** `generate_session_context()` makes ONE call covering all 10 G10 currencies × 4 sessions (session status + OIS bias + calendar + news + live-market-context blocks combined) — a fundamentally larger prompt than the narrative/signals calls the v8.44.0 swap was validated against. Confirmed via Groq's published on-demand-tier rate limits (console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits, cross-checked against third-party trackers, 2026-07-07): `openai/gpt-oss-120b` is capped at 8,000 TPM on this tier, while `llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct` (the model it replaced) was capped at 30,000 TPM — a 3.75x reduction that the v8.44.0 session showed no evidence of having been checked against this specific call site's ~9.7–11.4K-token prompt. This is a genuine regression, not intermittent bad luck: at 8K TPM the call was going to 413 every time it reached Groq, not occasionally.
- **Fix — TPM-aware model cascade, scoped to this call site only:** added `SESSION_CONTEXT_GROQ_CASCADE` (`gpt-oss-120b` → `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` [Production, 12K TPM] → `llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct` [Preview, 30K TPM]). The Groq fallback loop in `generate_session_context()` now catches `GROQ_HTTP_413` specifically and retries the *same key* on the next model in the cascade before rotating keys (a 413 is a per-model ceiling, not a per-key fault — rotating keys alone would just reproduce the same 413). `llama-4-scout` is only reached if both production-tier models 413, which is a deliberate, scoped exception to the v8.44.0 Preview-tier avoidance: it accepts that narrow deprecation risk only for this one oversized call, in exchange for a TPM ceiling large enough to actually succeed.
- **Not touched:** `MODEL` (`openai/gpt-oss-120b`) stays the default everywhere else (narrative, signals) — those prompts are far smaller and were not implicated in this failure.
- **Not verified live:** same sandbox limitation as v8.44.0 — no network access to `groq.com` from this environment. `python3 -m py_compile` passes; the cascade logic was traced by hand against the exact 413 response body from Santiago's run log. Recommend watching the next few scheduled runs to confirm `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` clears the TPM ceiling for this prompt in practice (estimated ~11K total request tokens against its 12K cap — workable but not roomy; if calendar/news content grows, it's plausible this also 413s and falls through to `llama-4-scout`, which is intentional, not a bug).

---

## v8.44.0 (2026-07-07) — Gemini/Groq narrative-fallback reliability and quality: 503 retry, 3rd model tier, search grounding, Groq model swap off a Preview-tier model

### Engine — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`
- **Reported by Santiago:** the 2026-07-07 21:26 UTC run showed noticeably weaker narrative quality after Gemini's entire 2-tier cascade (`gemini-3-flash-preview` → `gemini-3.5-flash`) failed on all 3 keys (mix of 503 "model overloaded" and one daily-limited key) and fell through to the Groq fallback. Asked to (1) reduce future Gemini failures and (2) improve fallback quality when it does happen.
- **Fix 1 — short retry on Gemini 503 (`call_gemini`):** a 503 now gets one short retry (6s) on the *same* key before the key is abandoned and the cascade rotates on. 503 is a capacity signal, not a per-key fault, so retrying the same key is valid (unlike `DAILY_LIMIT`, which is genuinely exhausted). Previously every 503 immediately burned the key and moved to the next one/model with no chance for a transient overload to clear.
- **Fix 2 — 3rd Gemini model tier (`generate_narrative_via_gemini`, `generate_signals_via_gemini`):** added `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` (already defined as `GEMINI_MODEL_LITE` but never wired into either cascade) as a third fallback tier after `gemini-3.5-flash`. Root cause of the reported run: `gemini-3-flash-preview` AND `gemini-3.5-flash` both returned 503 on the same run — a correlated outage across two same-generation Gemini-3-series models that the 2-tier cascade had no way to route around. `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` is a separate stable GA model, giving the cascade a real chance to avoid Groq entirely on days when only the Gemini-3 series is degraded.
- **Fix 3 — search grounding for the Groq narrative fallback (`generate_narrative`):** both the closed-market and open-market Groq narrative calls now pass `use_search=True`, routing through `groq/compound` (Tavily-backed web search, already used as the last-resort path for catalysts/drivers). Previously the Groq fallback reasoned only from the static context block with no live web grounding — this call only fires once the entire Gemini cascade (now 3 tiers) has already failed, so it is unambiguously the last-resort path and should have the same grounding advantage the other last-resort paths already have.
- **Fix 4 — Groq model swap off a Preview-tier model (`MODEL` constant, `call_groq`):** `meta-llama/llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct` has moved to Groq's **Preview** tier (confirmed at console.groq.com/docs/models, 2026-07-07) — Groq's own guidance states Preview models "should not be used in production environments as they may be discontinued at short notice." This was a reliability risk on top of the quality complaint. Replaced with **`openai/gpt-oss-120b`** (Production tier, 120B reasoning model, similar price, 8x the completion-token ceiling: 65,536 vs 8,192).
  - **Companion fix in `call_groq`:** switched the request payload from the deprecated `max_tokens` key to the current `max_completion_tokens` key (per Groq's docs, used uniformly across all model families). Added a `reasoning_effort="low"` flag plus a +400 token safety margin whenever the resolved model is a GPT-OSS model — GPT-OSS is a reasoning model that spends part of the completion-token budget on hidden reasoning tokens before writing `message.content` (Groq returns reasoning in a separate `message.reasoning` field, but it still counts against the same budget). Our existing `max_tokens` values were tuned for a non-reasoning model; without this guard a reasoning model could exhaust the budget on reasoning and return truncated/empty content.
- **Not verified live:** this sandbox has no network access to `groq.com` or `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, so none of the above could be exercised against the real APIs. `python3 -m py_compile` passes and the control flow was traced by hand, but the next few scheduled runs should be watched (especially for `openai/gpt-oss-120b` output — confirm `message.content` is well-formed JSON with `reasoning_effort="low"` before trusting it unattended).
- **Not in scope:** did not extend `use_search=True` to the Groq signals path (`generate_signals`) — signals succeeded via Gemini in the reported run and the signals path has its own token-budget tracking (`_signals_tokens_used` / `_SIGNALS_TOKEN_BUDGET`) that would need separate validation against `groq/compound`'s cost/latency profile before enabling.

## v8.43.17 (2026-07-07) — COT panel column layout breaks when #rightpanel is resized narrow; non-G10 central bank news slipping past the currency filter

### Frontend — `assets/dashboard.css`
- **Bug reported and fixed:** Santiago flagged the COT Positioning panel (`CFTC Disaggregated TFF · Leveraged Funds`) rendering with the Long/Short bar squeezed to near-zero width and the last column (OI) clipped, at typical `#rightpanel` widths.
- **Root cause:** `.cot-header`/`.cot-row` use an 8-column grid (`36px 1fr 42px 64px 52px 14px 46px 68px`). The 7 fixed columns + gaps total **378px minimum**, but `#rightpanel` is user-resizable via `assets/layout-resizer.js` down to `MIN_RIGHT=150px`, with **`DEFAULT_RIGHT=220px`** — narrower than the grid needs even at its default width. `.cot-bar-outer` (the `1fr` track) has no intrinsic content (its fill bars are `position:absolute`), so its automatic minimum is 0 — the grid collapses the bar first, and the row still overflows the remaining space with no scroll mechanism at desktop widths (`.cot-scroll-wrap` only had an `overflow-x` rule inside the `≤900px` mobile media query; `#main` has `overflow-x:hidden`), so the tail of the row is silently clipped instead of reachable.
- **Fix:** matched institutional dense-grid convention (Bloomberg/FactSet side panels scroll horizontally within the widget rather than compressing a bar chart to unreadable width or hiding data with no way to reach it):
  - `.cot-scroll-wrap { overflow-x: auto; }` (plus thin `::-webkit-scrollbar` styling matching `#rightpanel`'s) now applies at all widths, not just mobile.
  - `.cot-bar-outer { min-width: 36px; }` gives the bar a floor — this also sets the grid's automatic minimum for the `1fr` track, so the row's intrinsic min-width becomes ~414px (322px fixed cols + 56px gaps + 36px bar).
  - `.cot-header, .cot-row { min-width: 414px; }` reinforced explicitly for clarity/robustness.
  - The existing `≤900px` mobile media query already overrides both to `min-width: 0` with its own compact column set — no change needed there, cascade verified.
- **Verification:** `node assets/dashboard.test.js` → 81 passed, 0 failed (CSS-only change, no logic touched).

### Scripts (`globalinvesting-scripts`) — `fetch_news.py`
- **Bug reported and fixed:** Santiago flagged a Vietnam-focused article (State Bank of Vietnam policy stance, via FXStreet) appearing in the G10-only news feed.
- **Root cause:** the article's summary compares the Vietnamese Dong to the "US Dollar" — that phrase scores `5` in `CURRENCY_KEYWORDS_WEIGHTED["USD"]`, exactly meeting `CURRENCY_MIN_SCORE=5`, so `detect_currency()` tagged the article `"USD"` even though its actual subject is a non-G10 central bank. The existing `NON_G10_CB_RE` blocklist (which correctly excludes RBI, PBOC, Banxico, SARB, CBRT, Bank of Russia, etc. before the currency scorer ever runs) had never been extended to cover the State Bank of Vietnam — a gap in blocklist coverage, not a scoring-logic defect.
- **Fix:** added `state bank of vietnam|\bsbv\b` to `NON_G10_CB_RE`, following the exact existing pattern for other non-G10 central banks. `is_forex_relevant()` now returns `False` for this article before `detect_currency()` is reached (verified directly against the real article text — see Verification).
- **Not in scope:** did not touch `detect_currency()`'s scoring logic or add a general non-G10-country filter — this is a targeted blocklist addition matching the established pattern for this exact failure mode (a G10-currency comparison mention inside a non-G10-subject article). Other non-G10 central banks not yet in the blocklist may exist and would need to be added the same way if/when reported.
- **Verification:** ran the 102-test `scripts/tests/test_fetch_news.py` suite (note: currently orphaned in the engine repo — expects `fetch_news.py`/`fx_config.py` as siblings under `scripts/`, but both now live in `globalinvesting-scripts` per the v8.22.0 script-placement migration; verified by running the suite against a temporary copy, not committed anywhere) — 102 passed, 0 failed. Also directly confirmed `is_forex_relevant()` returns `False` for the real reported article text.

## v8.43.15 (2026-07-05) — Guard 7 (CB-decision hallucination) stripped forward-looking language and produced a broken fallback sentence

### Engine — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py` — `_apply_narrative_guards()` Guard 7
- **Bug reported and fixed:** Santiago flagged a poor-quality narrative from the `generate` workflow (run #797): `"RBNZ 2.25%. USD/JPY holds at 161.27 despite soft NFP data..."` — a dangling fragment that also dropped the day's dominant theme (NZD/USD leading G10 on RBNZ hike bias, confirmed by the run's own `[CRIT]` signal).
- **Root cause (two independent bugs):**
  1. `_DEC_VERBS7`'s decision-verb pattern includes bare `hike[s]?` to catch past-tense claims like "SNB hiked rates," but the same token also matches present-tense/noun-phrase forward-looking usage — "rate **hike** expectations," "**hike** bias," "**hike** bets." Guard 7's own header comment states it should only strip past-tense completed-decision claims and leave forward-looking language to Guard 6 (Watch-clause), but the regex enforced no such distinction — it matched and stripped the sentence carrying the day's actual dominant theme, an entirely legitimate forward-looking claim (RBNZ meets July 8; market prices a hike to 2.50%).
  2. The replacement fallback (`_rate_str7`) dropped the word "on hold" whenever the current rate was known (`_rt7 is not None`), producing `"RBNZ 2.25%."` instead of a complete sentence. The unknown-rate branch (`"on hold"` with no number) was correctly worded; only the known-rate branch was broken.
- **Fix:**
  1. Added a forward-looking exclusion check: if the matched span contains any of a set of prospective markers (`expectation`, `bets`, `bias`, `odds`, `probability`, `speculation`, `pricing`, `consensus`, `forecast`, etc.), Guard 7 now skips it (`continue`) and leaves the sentence untouched. Checked against the full regex match span rather than only the text after it, since the regex's greedy `(?:\s+\w+){0,4}` trailing window typically swallows the forward-looking noun into the same match.
  2. Fixed the known-rate fallback to `f"on hold at {_rt7}%"` instead of `f"{_rt7}%"`, so both branches now produce a complete, grammatical sentence.
- **Verification:** isolated behavioral test (regex + exclusion logic run standalone against the exact failing sentence from run #797's log) confirms the forward-looking sentence is now spared, while a genuine past-tense hallucination ("SNB kept rates unchanged at its meeting today") is still correctly detected and would still be stripped — the guard's original purpose is intact. `py_compile` clean. Full suite: 154/154 engine tests passing.
- **Not in scope:** did not touch Guard 6 (Watch-clause) or the calendar-check logic that determines `_rate_decision_ccys7` — both were verified working correctly in the same log (Guard 6 correctly stripped an invented meeting-time detail earlier in the same run).

## v3.330 (2026-07-05) — EA: Market Sessions panel falsely reporting "WEEKEND / Markets closed" after Sunday reopen

### EA — `Global_Investing_FX_Terminal.mq5` — `DrawSessions()`
- **Bug reported and fixed:** Santiago reported the Market Sessions panel showing all four sessions CLSD and the footer reading "WEEKEND · Markets closed" on a Sunday evening in Montevideo (UTC-3) — well after the true 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen (confirmed ~2h16m post-reopen from the reported screenshot timestamps).
- **Root cause (two compounding bugs) in the `is_weekend` check:**
  1. The check ORed in a raw `TimeToStruct(TimeCurrent(), bdt)` read (broker/server time) alongside the UTC read as a "safety net." `TimeCurrent()` freezes at the last received tick and does not advance while no ticks arrive — precisely what happens across the Friday-close → Sunday-reopen gap. This file already documents and defends against that exact failure mode in `GetReliableUTCOffsetSec()` ("frozen clock mid-session," with a full cache/fallback layer built specifically to avoid trusting a raw `TimeCurrent()` read) — but this block used a raw read anyway, letting a broker whose wall-clock day still read Saturday/Sunday (relative to UTC) force `is_weekend=true` well past the genuine UTC reopen.
  2. Independent of bug #1: `wdt.day_of_week==0` (Sunday) closed the market for the full 24 hours of Sunday, with no hour boundary — but FX reopens Sunday 22:00 UTC (Sydney). Only the Friday side of the check (`day_of_week==5 && hour>=22`) had a correct hour boundary; Sunday needed the mirror-image `day_of_week==0 && hour<22`.
- **Fix:** dropped the `TimeCurrent()`/`bdt` component entirely — `TimeGMT()` (via the local PC clock, not tick-dependent) is the reliable source, and it's already what `BuildSession()` itself uses for all open/close math, so this now uses the same source everywhere. Added the missing Sunday hour boundary. New logic: Saturday closed all day; Sunday closed only before 22:00 UTC; Friday closed only from 22:00 UTC — a straightforward, tick-independent restatement of the standard Fri-22:00-UTC → Sun-22:00-UTC FX trading week.
- **Verification:** code-only (comment-stripped) paren/brace balance confirmed unchanged around the edit; `bdt`/`TimeCurrent()` had no other callers in `DrawSessions()`, confirmed via full-file grep, so removing it has no other side effects.
- **Version:** header comment and `#property version` were drifted (header said v3.329, property tag said "3.326") — synced both to v3.330 with this fix.

## v8.43.11 (2026-07-05) — access.html: cropped Carry Ranking screenshot to fix row-density mismatch vs CB Rates

### Guides — `access.html`
- **Problem:** `screenshot-cb-rates.png` (387×245, ratio 1.579) and `screenshot-carry-ranking.png` (572×371, ratio 1.542) had nearly identical box aspect ratios, so the two `.scr-item-frame` boxes rendered at almost the same height. But CB Rates packs 8 compact table rows into its box (row pitch ≈ 6.25% of image width) while Carry Ranking only fit 7 taller ranking-bar rows into a same-size box (row pitch ≈ 8% of image width) — so Carry's rows read as noticeably larger/"zoomed in" next to CB's tighter table, an inconsistency versus the compact-table conventions of Bloomberg/Eikon-style panels.
- **Root cause:** matching the outer box aspect ratio doesn't fix per-row visual scale — cropping/resizing the whole image proportionally doesn't change row-pitch-to-width, since the browser just scales the image uniformly to fill the box. The only way to shrink the box without stretching or introducing artificial padding is to remove rows from the source screenshot.
- **Fix:** cropped `assets/screenshot-carry-ranking.png` from 7 rows to 6 (removed the lowest-ranked pair, GBP/NZD), taking it from 572×371 (ratio 1.542) to 572×325 (ratio 1.76). This shortens the Carry Ranking box relative to CB Rates, bringing the two panels closer to a consistent row-density feel instead of matching on raw image aspect ratio alone. Updated the `<img>` `width`/`height`, the inline `aspect-ratio` style on `.scr-item-frame`, and the JSON-LD `ImageObject` `height` (mirrored in three places) to 325.
- **Rejected approach:** artificial background-color padding (tried and reverted in an earlier session) — left a visible seam/franja that didn't read as native to the screenshot. Cropping rows is the only fix that doesn't introduce synthetic content.

## v8.43.8 (2026-07-05) — CSI guide caption font-size specificity fix

### Guides — `guide-csi-indicator.html`
- **Bug found and fixed:** the screenshot caption (`<p class="scr-meta">`) was rendering at 15.4px — the same size as ordinary body paragraphs — instead of its intended 10px caption size. Root cause: `.guide-section p` (specificity 0,1,1, one class + one element) sets `font-size: 15.4px` for all paragraphs inside a `.guide-section`, which beats the single-class selector `.scr-meta` (specificity 0,1,0) regardless of source order, since the caption `<p>` sits inside a `.guide-section` div. This is why the caption looked oversized compared to `access.html`'s identical `.scr-meta` captions, which aren't nested inside any conflicting `.guide-section p` rule and so rendered correctly at 10px.
- **Fix:** changed the selector to `.guide-section p.scr-meta` (specificity 0,2,1 — two classes + one element), which now deterministically beats `.guide-section p` regardless of CSS source order. No properties or values changed, only the selector's specificity.
- **Scope check:** confirmed this pattern (a `.scr-meta`/`.scr-hero-wrap` screenshot caption nested inside a `.guide-section p` rule) is unique to `guide-csi-indicator.html` among all guide pages — `guide-mt5-ea.html`'s screenshot was removed in v8.43.3, and `access.html` has no competing `.guide-section p` rule at all. No other page needed this fix.

## v8.43.6 (2026-07-05) — CSI methodology accuracy fix + EA guide missing panel sections

### Guides — `guide-csi-indicator.html`
- **Bug found and fixed:** the Methodology section, the MT5-indicator intro paragraph, and the "How is the CSI calculated?" FAQ answer all described the standalone MT5 indicator's normalization as a single z-score over "a configurable lookback." Verified against `CSI_Currency_Strength.mq5`: the actual model computes the return independently across three separate horizons (`Lookback_Short`/`Lookback_Mid`/`Lookback_Long`, default 1/3/12), normalises each into its own cross-sectional z-score, then blends the three with configurable weights (`Weight_Short`/`Weight_Mid`/`Weight_Long`, default 25%/35%/40%) — a multi-lookback weighted z-score model explicitly based on Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen (2013), designed to avoid the cliff-edge artifact a single fixed lookback produces (per the indicator's own `#property description` and inline methodology comments). All three passages rewritten to describe the three-horizon weighted blend and cite the academic basis, rather than a generic single-lookback z-score.
- **Not changed:** the on-chart footer label in the indicator itself (`"ML Z-SCORE · 1/3/12"`) still displays the raw lookback values with no unit, which reads as months (matching the Asness convention and the input comments' "on a monthly timeframe" framing) but is actually days under the indicator's default `PERIOD_D1` timeframe. This is a `.mq5` source-level ambiguity, not a guide content issue — flagged separately, pending confirmation of the intended fix (unit suffix on the label vs. changing the default timeframe) before touching the EA source.

### Guides — `guide-mt5-ea.html`
- **Gap found and fixed:** of the EA's 13 rendered data panels, three had no dedicated description in the Panel-by-Panel Overview walkthrough — Composite Score (mentioned only in passing, twice, with no explanation of what it shows), Economic Surprise Index, and Market Sessions (neither mentioned at all). Added three new subsections, verified against `Global_Investing_FX_Terminal.mq5`:
  - **Composite Score:** documented the actual six-factor weighting (`GetCompositeScoreFromInputs()`: COT 25%, momentum 15%, retail 18%, CB bias 18%, carry 12%, ESI 12%) and the NOK/SEK pro-rata weight redistribution when no CFTC data is available.
  - **Economic Surprise Index:** documented the Citi-methodology construction, the 10-currency coverage, and the adaptive 90D/180D window (`ComputeESI()` / `g_esi_window_days`).
  - **Market Sessions:** documented the four-session (Sydney/Tokyo/London/New York) open/closed display, the DST-aware boundary calculation per zone, and the overlap/weekend footer logic (`DrawSessions()`).
- **New TOC entries:** `#composite-panel`, `#esi-panel`, `#sessions-panel` added between "Economic Calendar" and "Sentiment, CSI, Correlation, Volatility".
- **Confirmed accurate (no change needed):** product #180326, AI narrative + push notification claims, native MT5 calendar integration (`CalendarValueHistory`/`CalendarEventById`), and the Volatility & Options panel's RR-skew claim — all verified directly against the EA source in this session.

## v8.42.0 (2026-07-04) — Audit follow-up: EA session DST parity, symmetric CB-tense guard, live-region hygiene

### MT5 EA — `Global_Investing_FX_Terminal.mq5` (v3.325 → v3.326)
- **Bug (recurring DST class, EA-side — audit item "not yet verified" from v8.41.0's report, now confirmed and fixed):** `DrawSessions()` hardcoded the same fixed-UTC-hour pattern already found and fixed on the web side (`SYDNEY 22-7, TOKYO 0-9, LONDON 7-16, NEW YORK 12-21`). Confirmed the EA's table mixed DST assumptions inconsistently across zones — London/New York were tuned to their DST (summer) offsets while Sydney was tuned to its standard (winter) offset — meaning no single calendar date could have had all four correct simultaneously, only the (northern-summer/southern-winter) period the values happened to match.
- **Fix:** added `NthSundayOfMonth()`, `GetLondonUTCOffset()`, `GetNewYorkUTCOffset()`, `GetSydneyUTCOffset()` — MQL5 has no `Intl`-equivalent timezone database, so EU/US/Australia DST transition dates (2nd-Sunday-March/1st-Sunday-November for US, last-Sunday-March/last-Sunday-October for EU, 1st-Sunday-October/1st-Sunday-April for Australia, wrapping year-end) are computed directly from first principles. `DrawSessions()` now converts each zone's nominal local hours (Sydney/London/New York 08:00–17:00, Tokyo 09:00–18:00 — Tokyo has no DST, unchanged) to today's UTC boundary dynamically, mirroring the web terminal's `updateSessions()` fix (v8.41.0) exactly.
- **Verified:** cross-checked the `NthSundayOfMonth()` transition dates against the actual 2026 DST calendar (US Mar 8/Nov 1, EU Mar 29/Oct 25, Australia Oct 4/Apr 5 — all correct) and confirmed the resulting UTC session boundaries for both a January and a July date match the already-verified web-side values exactly.
- **Version bump:** all 4 required locations (header comment, `#property version`, topbar title string in `DrawTopBar()`, footer `ver` string in `DrawNews()`) updated 3.325 → 3.326. Note: the topbar title string (a literal embedded mid-string, not matched by a naive `"v3\.` search) was missed by the narrower version-consistency grep used in the prior audit session — it was not actually drifted (already read 3.325 correctly), but the check itself had a blind spot, now closed by searching for the version number directly rather than only the quote-prefixed pattern.

### Engine — `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py`
- **Bug (asymmetric guard coverage — audit item "temporal contradiction handling for BoJ/rate-decision catalysts"):** the prior audit's search for this item used the term "temporal contradiction" and found nothing, because the actual implementation (`_correct_cb_tense_text`, built from exactly this BoJ scenario: a completed June 16 hike rendered as "poised to raise" in catalysts) uses "tense," not "temporal," terminology — a search-term miss, not a genuine gap. However, re-reading the implementation surfaced a real, related gap: the guard only ever detected a completed **hike** mischaracterized as pending ("poised to raise", "about to raise", etc.) — there was no symmetric check for a completed **cut** mischaracterized the same way ("poised to cut", "expected to lower rates").
- **Fix:** generalized `_correct_cb_tense_text()`'s regex and replacement logic to detect both directions (`raise` → hike, `cut`/`lower` → cut) and compare against the correct OIS bias field (`hike` vs `cut`) for whichever direction matched, instead of hardcoding the hike case. `_sanitize_cb_action_tense_drivers()`/`_catalysts()` (unchanged — they already just delegate to `_correct_cb_tense_text()`) now get the cut-direction coverage for free.
- **Verified:** re-ran the original BoJ hike scenario (unchanged output) plus a new synthetic Fed cut scenario ("expected to lower rates" when the Fed already cut and bias is not further-cut) through `_correct_cb_tense_text()` directly — both corrected as expected; a control case (bias matches the claimed direction) confirmed left untouched.

### Frontend — `index.html`
- **Bug (undocumented live-region deviations — audit item "full accessibility sweep," ARIA-live under live updates):** two elements had `aria-live` attributes not present in GUIDELINES.md's canonical live-region table (`#narrative`, `#risk-regime`, `#alerts-container`, `#sr-announce` only):
  - `.risk-grid` (parent of the documented `#risk-regime` live region) had its own `aria-live="polite"` — a **nested live region**, which has unpredictable cross-browser/AT behavior and is explicitly discouraged by ARIA authoring practices. Removed; `#risk-regime`'s own `assertive` live region is unaffected.
  - `#lw-chart-header` (chart OHLC legend) had `aria-live="polite"` despite being rewritten on every `subscribeCrosshairMove` callback — dozens of times per second while a sighted user drags across the chart. This would have flooded screen-reader users with announcements. Removed.
- **Also verified (false alarm from the prior audit's own tooling):** the "17 missing `<th scope>`" figure reported in the 2026-07-04 audit report was a regex false-positive — the check's `<th[^>]*>` pattern also matched `<thead>`. Re-run with a corrected pattern (`<th(?:\s[^>]*)?>`, requiring a boundary after "th"): all 91 `<th>` elements across all 17 tables already have `scope` set correctly. No fix needed; audit report finding retracted.
- **Cache-bust:** no change (dashboard.js content unchanged this entry; index.html itself isn't query-versioned).

### GUIDELINES.md
- **New rule:** live-region hygiene — no nesting, and no `aria-live` on elements that update on high-frequency events (crosshair/mouse-move/tick streams) — added directly under the canonical live-region table, with both fixes above as documented examples.
- **Updated rule:** the DST-aware session-hours rule (v8.41.0) now documents the EA-side reference pattern alongside the existing web-side one.
- **Updated rule:** the narrative-guard-coverage rule now documents the directional-symmetry principle (check both directions of a guard built from one specific incident).
- Version footer bumped to v8.42.0.
