## v8.4.0 (2026-06-20) — SEK now uses real SWESTR OIS data instead of heuristic fallback

### Engine — .github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml
- **`fetch_bias_sek()` rewritten to use the Riksbank's SWESTR REST API:** Previous versions assumed SWESTR required API-portal registration and immediately fell through to `heuristic_bias('SEK')`. This was incorrect — the Riksbank publishes a separate, key-less REST API for SWESTR (`https://api.riksbank.se/swestr/v1/all/SWESTR?fromDate=...`), distinct from the SWEA interest/exchange-rate API used for STIBOR/FX. Confirmed live and documented in the Riksbank's own API portal ("SWESTR API v1", tora-api namespace); public access is rate-limited to 5 requests/minute, well within this workflow's single-call-per-run usage.
- **New guards added**, modeled on the existing CHF/SARON tier pattern:
  - Skips any row where the Riksbank's own `alternativeCalculation` flag is `true` (insufficient reporters/volume/technical error).
  - Sanity range check (±200bp vs current policy rate) before trusting a value — an isolated bad tick (`rate: -5.413` on 2023-12-29, with `alternativeCalculation` still `false`) was found in historical data during testing, confirming the flag alone is not sufficient.
  - Staleness guard: only accepts SWESTR observations dated within the last 5 calendar days.
- **Threshold changed from N/A to `THRESHOLD` (10bp):** SWESTR is a true daily transaction-based overnight rate (same instrument class as SARON/CORRA/SOFR), not an OECD monthly average, so it uses the tighter 10bp threshold rather than `THRESHOLD_OECD` (25bp).
- **`biasMethod` for SEK changes from `'heuristic'` to `'ois'`** whenever a valid SWESTR observation passes all guards; falls back to `'heuristic'` only if the API is unreachable, all recent observations fail the sanity/staleness guards, or `rates/SEK.json` has no policy rate.
- Logic verified against 5 synthetic test cases (normal day, `alternativeCalculation=true` skip-to-prior-day, the real production outlier, staleness, and a genuine cut-bias spread) before deployment — all passed.

## v8.3.8 (2026-06-20) — COT workflow: second Friday run at 23:30 UTC as CFTC late-publish safety net

### Engine — .github/workflows/update-cot-cftc-all.yml
- **Second cron added:** `30 23 * * 5` (Fridays 23:30 UTC). The existing `30 21 * * 5` run fires ~1 hour after the typical CFTC release window (15:00–16:30 ET / 19:00–20:30 UTC). When CFTC publishes in the upper end of that window or slightly late, the 21:30 UTC run can arrive before the data is available (as observed today). The 23:30 UTC run fires 3 hours after the latest typical release time, providing a reliable fallback. The `git diff` guard in the commit step ensures the second run is a no-op if the first already committed fresh data — no duplicate commits.

### Engine — .github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml → v8.7.0
- **`CALENDAR_2026['NOK']` / `['SEK']` added:** 8 meetings/year each, decision-publication dates verified against `norges-bank.no` (Jan/Mar/May confirmed past decisions; Jun–Dec per official 2026 schedule) and `riksbank.se` monetary policy decision pages (decision-publication date used, not the "applies from" effective date — consistent with the convention already used for all other G8 entries).

- **`fetch_bias_nok()` added:** FRED `IRSTCI01NOM156N` (OECD Norway overnight interbank rate, monthly) vs Norges Bank policy rate, classified with `THRESHOLD_OECD` (25bp) — same family/pattern as AUD (`IRSTCI01AUM156N`) and NZD (`IRSTCI01NZM156N`). 50bp staleness guard before falling through to `heuristic_bias('NOK')`. NOWA itself is not wired as a daily source — see `fetch_ois_rates.py fetch_nok()` (v8.3.4) for the documented rationale; the monthly OECD series already captures the same signal relative to the policy rate.

Dispatcher correctly falls through to `heuristic_bias('SEK')`. Per GUIDELINES.md ("do not invent conventions"), no synthetic spread signal is fabricated for SEK — this is a deliberate, documented absence of OIS-bias data, not a missed integration.

The table added no product information beyond what's already there, while exposing raw internal file paths (`ai-analysis/`, `cot-data/`, `dtcc-data/`, etc.) that serve no purpose for a terminal user — this isn't a published data API, just the implementation detail of a static site. ## v8.2.1 (2026-06-17) — CB Rate Expectations: Bloomberg WIRP alignment — hold probability chip and meeting auto-advance

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Fix — hold bias probability chip:** The `probSuffix` logic used `else if (cutProb !== null)` as a catch-all, which fired for all hold-bias currencies (USD, GBP, JPY, AUD, CAD, CHF) and rendered `"0%↓"` — displaying a cut probability chip even though bias was hold. Bloomberg WIRP standard: the probability chip shows the dominant direction matching the bias. For hold bias, this is `holdProb = 100 − cutProb − hikeProb`. Rewrote `probSuffix` with explicit `if (hike) … else if (cut) … else (hold)` branches. All hold currencies now render `"100%→"` when OIS data is present; `"20%↑"` for NZD hike; `"94%↑"` for EUR hike — consistent with WIRP.
- **Fix — past meeting auto-advance:** When `nextMeetingISO` is today or past and `allMeetings` contains a future date, the displayed meeting date now auto-advances to the next upcoming meeting from `allMeetings`. Prevents stale "17 Jun" (FOMC today) or "18 Jun" (BoE/SNB tomorrow) showing after the meeting passes, until the weekly `workflow_meetings.yml` runs Monday. Bloomberg WIRP auto-advances the meeting column the moment a meeting passes; this matches that behaviour client-side.

## v8.2.0 (2026-06-17) — Fix: BoJ post-hike TONA settlement lag → false Cut signal

### Root cause
`workflow_meetings.yml` `fetch_bias_jpy()` uses TONA (Tokyo Overnight Average Rate, sourced via SNB zimoma) as TIER 0-C for JPY bias classification. TONA is a compounded average of actual overnight repo transactions published by JSDA — it settles **1–2 business days after a BoJ policy change** because the repo market recalibrates gradually. On BoJ hike day (Jun 16, 1.0%) and the following day, TONA still printed at ~0.75% while `rates/JPY.json` already reflected the new 1.0% rate (patched by v8.1.0 calendar-actual ingest). The TIER 0-A investing.com TONA3M futures probe found no valid instrument ID. The TIER 0-C path then ran: `diff = 0.75 − 1.0 = −0.25` → `classify() → cut, cutProb=100%` → `fwdRate = 1.0 − 0.10 = 0.90%`. Result: CB Rate Expectations displayed "↓ Cut 100%↓ 0.90%" for BoJ — exactly inverted from the correct post-hike state.

### Fix — `.github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml` (v8.2.0)
- **TONA settlement lag guard added** to `fetch_bias_jpy()` TIER 0-C. When `|TONA − policy| > 5bp` (i.e. TONA is outside the normal hold zone), the guard checks `rates/JPY.json`: if the most recent rate observation is **≤2 calendar days old AND differs from the prior observation** (i.e. a rate change just occurred), TONA classification is suppressed and execution falls through to TIER 0-B (BoJ MPM vote scraper). TIER 0-B reads the actual voting record and returns the correct post-decision bias. The guard only fires on decision days and the 1–2 settlement days after; on normal weekly runs where TONA has fully settled, `|diff| ≤ 5bp` and the guard never fires.

### Immediate fix — `meetings-data/meetings.json`
- **JPY block patched manually** for the current incorrect state: `bias=hold`, `cutProb=0`, `hikeProb=0`, `fwdRate=1.00` (correct post-hike hold expectation). `biasMethod=ois-preserved`, `biasUpdated=2026-06-17`. Will self-correct on the next scheduled workflow run (Mon 10:00 UTC) once TONA has settled to ~1.0%.

### Why this happens only for JPY
SOFR (USD), €STR/ESTER (EUR), SONIA (GBP), CORRA (CAD), SARON (CHF) all settle **same-day** or **next-business-day** — they reflect the new policy rate by the end of the decision day. TONA is the only G8 overnight benchmark with a 1–2 day structural settlement lag, making JPY uniquely vulnerable to this false-signal window.

## v8.1.0 (2026-06-16) — Fix: Narrative CB-decision hallucination guard + Calendar-driven rates update

### Problem 1 — Narrative hallucinates CB decisions not in calendar
LLM cited "SNB keeps interest rates on sight deposits unchanged" on 2026-06-16 — a day with no SNB decision (SNB June meeting is June 18). The model inferred a decision from a news article about the SNB quarterly report. No existing guard caught past-tense CB decision claims; Guard 6 only blocks future Watch-clauses, and TIER A only filters UPCOMING sessions in signals.

### Root cause
`_apply_narrative_guards` lacked a guard for past-tense "CB X kept/cut/hiked rates" claims in the narrative body. The LLM was free to invent a same-day decision from news headlines.

### Fix — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py (Guard 7)
- **Guard 7 added** at the end of `_apply_narrative_guards()`.
- Reads `ff_calendar.json` and builds `_rate_decision_ccys7`: the set of currencies that have a **released, high-impact Interest Rate Decision event dated today**.
- Scans the narrative for past-tense decision verbs (keeps/kept/cut/hiked/raised/lowered/held/left/maintains) applied to any G10 CB name (SNB, BoJ, BoE, RBA, RBNZ, BoC, ECB, Fed).
- If the CB's currency is NOT in `_rate_decision_ccys7` → strips the sentence and replaces with `{CB} {rate}%` fallback.
- Wraps in try/except to be non-fatal; logs all matches with `WARN Guard 7:`.

### Problem 2 — BoJ rate stale at 0.75% after decision day hike to 1.0%
`rates/JPY.json` is populated from FRED (IORJPNRESL / policy rate series) which lags actual decisions by 1–3 business days. The CB Rates modal, narrative carry differentials, and OIS bias fetcher all read `rates/JPY.json` — all showed the stale 0.75% rate while the calendar already had `actual=1.0%`.

### Root cause
No mechanism existed to update `rates/*.json` from same-day calendar actuals. The `workflow_meetings.yml` workflow runs after decisions and has access to `ff_calendar.json` but previously only computed OIS bias — not the policy rate itself.

### Fix — .github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml (engine — new step)
- **New step "Ingest calendar rate-decision actuals into rates/*.json"** runs before the OIS bias step. Reads `ff_calendar.json`, finds today's released high-impact rate-decision actuals, patches `rates/{CCY}.json` immediately. The OIS bias fetcher then reads the correct post-decision rate.

### Fix — scripts/fetch_rates.py (site — v14.0)
- **New Step 0-A: `ff_calendar.json` actuals as highest-priority source.** Before any external CB scraping, reads today's released high-impact rate-decision actuals from the calendar. Source label: `ff-calendar-actual` (status=ok in health.json). More current than BIS (monthly), BoJ scraping (page lag), or FRED (1-day lag).
- Manual overrides (`SOURCE 0-B`) now run after calendar actuals and will not overwrite a same-day calendar rate.

### Fix — .github/workflows/update-rates.yml (site — cron expansion)
- **Added early-capture crons:** BoJ Tue/Thu/Fri 04:00 UTC, RBA Tue 05:30 UTC, RBNZ Wed/Thu 03:30 UTC. Previously only 08:00 UTC daily — up to 5 hours after a BoJ decision.

### Fix — .github/workflows/update-ff-calendar.yml (site — dispatch step v5.2)
- **New step "Dispatch cb-rate-decision if interest rate actual detected."** After a successful commit, fires `repository_dispatch[cb-rate-decision]` → `update-rates.yml` immediately when a rate-decision actual is present. Closes the loop without waiting for the next cron.
- Added `permissions: actions: write`.

### Affected files (v8.1.0 complete)
- `scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py` (engine) — Guard 7 in `_apply_narrative_guards()`
- `.github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml` (engine) — new "Ingest calendar rate-decision actuals" step
- `scripts/fetch_rates.py` (site) — v14.0, Step 0-A calendar-actual source
- `.github/workflows/update-rates.yml` (site) — Asia-session early-capture crons
- `.github/workflows/update-ff-calendar.yml` (site) — cb-rate-decision dispatch step (v5.2)

## v8.0.2 (2026-06-15) — Fix: CB Rates modal chart grows taller on each Decisions→Rate Chart tab-switch

### Root cause
`_cbrDims()` computed chart height by temporarily zeroing `container.style.height` and then reading `#cbr-p-chart.offsetHeight`. However, `#cbr-p-chart` uses `flex:1` inside `#cbr-m-body` (also `flex:1`) inside `#cbr-modal` (`height:auto`). With the container zeroed, the panel collapses to the height of its fixed children (ctx-wrap + next-fwd + ps-wrap). The calculated `h = panelH - fixedChildrenH - padH` was effectively `≈0`, clamped to the `180px` minimum. Setting `container.style.height = 180px` made the modal grow, so the next tab-switch measured a larger `panelH`, produced a larger `h`, and the chart grew without bound.

### Fix — assets/cb-rates-modal.js (v2.4)
- **`_cbrDims()` caches height on first call.** After a successful measurement (container not yet set, panel has natural flex height), the result is stored on `bd._chartH`.
- **Subsequent calls (`_rebuildFromTab` flag) skip re-measurement** and return the cached `{w, h}` directly. Width is still recomputed live from `modal.offsetWidth` to handle viewport resize.
- **`_buildCBRChart()` writes `bd._chartH = initH`** after the first successful chart creation.
- **`cbRatesTab()`** sets `bd._rebuildFromTab = true` before calling `_buildCBRChart()` on the return to the Rate Chart tab, so `_cbrDims()` uses the cached height.
- Window resize handler (`apply()`) still calls `_cbrDims()` without the flag so it re-measures naturally if the viewport changes.

## v8.0.1 (2026-06-15) — Fix: black panel when navigating away from News or Derivatives via keyboard or nav click

### Root cause
The "hide on other nav click" listeners for `initNewsNav` and `initDerivativesNavFixed` were registered in **bubble phase** (default). The main nav scroll handler (`initNavScroll`, line ~8208) is also in bubble phase but registered earlier — so it fired first when another nav tab was clicked while News or Derivatives was active.

Execution order on e.g. pressing **R** from News:
1. `navTo('section-risk')` → `riskLink.click()`
2. **Main nav scroll** fires (bubble, registered first) → calls `scrollIntoView` on `#section-risk` while all other sections are still `display:none` (hidden by `showNews()`) → scroll no-ops or targets a zero-height context → **black panel**
3. `hideNews()` fires (bubble, registered later) → restores sections — but the scroll already happened incorrectly

This affected: pressing any letter shortcut (R, X, M, Y, G, C, K) while News or Derivatives was the active panel, and clicking any nav tab link in the same state.

### Fix — assets/dashboard.js
- **"Hide on other nav" listeners moved to capture phase** (`true` third argument) in both `initNewsNav` and `initDerivativesNavFixed`.
- When News or Derivatives is active and another nav link is clicked, the capture-phase listener fires first, calls `e.stopImmediatePropagation()` to block the main nav scroll handler, hides the active panel, then re-runs the scroll logic itself inside `requestAnimationFrame()` — after sections are restored to their correct display values.
- When News/Derivatives is NOT active (`style.display === 'none'`), the listener returns early without stopping propagation, so the main nav handler runs normally for all other navigation.

## v7.99.0 (2026-06-14) — Fix CB rates modal: USD FEDFUNDS effective rate contaminating policy rate history

### Root cause
The FRED fallback for USD used the `FEDFUNDS` series (Federal Funds Effective Rate — weighted average of overnight
transactions, floats near the midpoint of the target range). When NY Fed primary was unavailable for May 2026,
`FEDFUNDS` wrote `3.625%` into `rates/USD.json` instead of `3.75%` (the upper bound announced by the FOMC).
This cascaded into three visible bugs in the CB rates modal:

1. **Period Low: 3.63%** — incorrect; should be 3.75%.
2. **Cycle: ↑ Hiking cycle +13bp** — fake hike signal. 3.625 entry → −12.5bp phantom cut (Apr→May),
   then Jun correction back to 3.75 read as +12.5bp hike. Modal correctly detected last change as positive.
3. **Two phantom ±12bp decision markers** on the chart (May and Jun 2026).

Industry convention (Bloomberg, Trading Economics, Refinitiv): display the **upper bound of the target range**
(`DFEDTARU` in FRED) as the policy rate. `FEDFUNDS` (effective) is correct for OIS/carry, not policy rate history.

### Engine — scripts/fetch_rates.py
- **`FRED_RATE_SERIES['USD']` changed:** `'FEDFUNDS'` → `'DFEDTARU'` (Fed Funds Target Rate — Upper Limit).
  `DFEDTARU` matches FOMC announcements exactly and equals NY Fed `targetRateTo` used by the primary source.

## v7.98.0 (2026-05-23) — AI prompt: institutional data gaps closed (CESI, z-scores, real rates, inflation exp.)

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Gap 1 — CESI-style economic surprise index added to `build_context()`:** Reads `calendar-data/calendar.json` (1,646 events, high+medium impact, G8 only) and computes rolling beat/miss counts per currency. Emits a ranked table with net score (beats − misses), plus CESI EXTREMES block for currencies with net ≥ +4 or ≤ −4. AI can now cross-validate COT/RR directional bias against data flow — CESI+COT aligned = high-conviction; CESI diverging = fade risk. Bloomberg BEEI / Citi CESI equivalent.
- **Gap 2 — surpriseStats z-scores added:** For each series in `calendar.json.surpriseStats` with n ≥ 3 and |z| ≥ 1.5, emits the normalized surprise shock: `z = (actual−forecast − hist_mean_surprise) / hist_std`. |z| ≥ 2.0 flagged as "2σ SHOCK" per Bloomberg ESURPRISE convention. Z-score correctly computed on the surprise delta, not the raw actual level.
- **Gap 4 — Inflation expectations + real rate added:** Reads `extended-data/{CCY}.json → inflationExpectations` for all G8 and computes real rate = policy rate − inflation expectations. Classifies as restrictive/accommodative. AI can now frame CB divergence using real rates, not just nominal spreads — critical for JPY/CHF where low nominal rates can mask relatively less-accommodative real stances.
- **Gap 5 — Finnhub news source label:** If Finnhub-sourced articles are present in the news pool (added by `fetch_news.py` v5.12), emits a count note so the model can correctly attribute structured FX market news vs RSS aggregator articles.
- **Gap 3 (GDP/CPI actuals) deferred:** Removed in v7.24.1 for staleness. Correct fix is refreshing `update-economic-data.yml` workflow cadence — restoring stale values would degrade accuracy. Out of scope this session.

## v7.96.0 (2026-05-23) — Calendar: fix FETCH_TIMEOUT bug + source propagation + surpriseStats + stale purge

### Engine — scripts/fetch_ff_calendar.py (site repo) · v3.6
- **Critical bug fix — `FETCH_TIMEOUT` undefined:** `FETCH_TIMEOUT` was referenced in `fetch_finnhub()` on lines 147 and 154 but was never defined in the config block. Python raised `NameError` on every call, caught silently by `except Exception as e` which printed `"ERROR: Finnhub request failed — name 'FETCH_TIMEOUT' is not defined"` and returned `[]`. This caused `main()` to hit `"ERROR: No events fetched — preserving previous file."` → `sys.exit(0)` on every run. `ff_calendar.json` was never updated since the config constant was removed. Fix: `FETCH_TIMEOUT = 30` added to the config block. All Finnhub fetches now complete with a 30-second timeout.

### Engine — scripts/fetch_economic_calendar.py (site repo) · v3.2
- **Fix — source field propagated from ff_calendar.json:** `"source"` and `"fetchMode"` in `calendar.json` were hardcoded to `"ForexFactory"` regardless of the actual data source. Now reads `source` from `ff_calendar.json` (`"Finnhub"` when `FINNHUB_API_KEY` is set, `"ForexFactory"` on fallback) and propagates it. Dashboard source label now correctly shows `"Finnhub · actual vs consensus · 90d rolling"`.
- **Fix — purge stale historical duplicates:** Added a purge pass in Step 3. When a historical entry in `calendar.json` has the same `(currency, dateISO, event)` key as a fresh entry from `ff_calendar.json`, the historical copy is dropped (rather than added alongside). This removes all pre-v3.1 duplicate entries that entered before the merge key fix — events that appeared twice with different `timeUTC` values, one with forecast and one without. The `purged N stale historical duplicates` count appears in the workflow log.
- **New — `surpriseStats` computed and written to calendar.json:** Computes per-event-series statistics over the 90-day rolling window: `n` (observations), `mean` (average surprise), `std` (sample standard deviation). Key format: `"CCY/EventName"` (e.g. `"USD/Nonfarm Payrolls"`). Dashboard.js references `surpriseStats` for z-score normalisation, graduating each series from beat/miss to z-score when `n >= 5`. This is the standard approach used by Citi ESURPRISE, Goldman GLAI, and similar institutional CESI indices — raw beat/miss rate is directional only; z-score normalises for the magnitude and historical variance of each series.

## v7.95.1 (2026-05-23) — Economic Surprises: fix merge key duplicates con forecast

### Engine — scripts/fetch_economic_calendar.py (site repo) · v3.1
- **Bug fix — merge key excluye `timeUTC`:** la clave de merge histórico era `(currency, dateISO, timeUTC, event)`. Finnhub ajusta ocasionalmente el `timeUTC` de un evento entre runs (e.g. de `12:30` a `12:35`). Cuando eso ocurre, el evento nuevo de `ff_calendar.json` (con `forecast`) y la versión cacheada en `calendar.json` (sin `forecast` o con forecast viejo) tienen claves distintas, y **ambas** entran al merge — el panel mostraba el evento dos veces y la versión sin forecast diluía el scoring. Fix: clave reducida a `(currency, dateISO, event)`, lo que garantiza que la versión fresca de `ff_calendar` siempre gana y las versiones cacheadas con `timeUTC` diferente no se reintroducen. Este era el motivo por el que Economic Surprises se cortaba en el 15 de mayo a pesar de que el calendario mostraba forecasts correctos para eventos posteriores.

## v7.95.0 (2026-05-23) — Economic Calendar: workflow_run trigger — hereda latencia del CF Worker

### Engine — .github/workflows/update-economic-calendar.yml (site repo) · v2.0
- **Primary trigger cambiado a `workflow_run`:** el workflow ahora se dispara automáticamente cada vez que `Update ForexFactory Calendar` completa con éxito. Esto significa que `calendar.json` (fuente del panel Economic Surprises) se actualiza dentro de ~30 segundos de cada commit de `ff_calendar.json`, heredando la latencia completa del CF Worker (~2-3 min end-to-end desde publicación del dato hasta que el panel muestra el resultado).
- **Guard de conclusión:** cuando el trigger es `workflow_run`, el job solo corre si `github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'`. Runs fallidos de `update-ff-calendar` (e.g. Finnhub timeout) no disparan un rebuild innecesario de `calendar.json`.
- **Cron 4x/día mantenido como fallback:** cubre edge cases donde el `workflow_run` trigger fue encolado o demorado, y garantiza que `calendar.json` se reconstruya aunque `update-ff-calendar` haya fallado en todas sus corridas del día.
- **Arquitectura anterior:** `calendar.json` se reconstruía solo 4 veces al día (05:30, 09:30, 13:30, 20:30 UTC), desacoplado del ritmo de `ff_calendar.json`. Con el CF Worker disparando `ff_calendar` cada vez que hay datos nuevos, `calendar.json` podía quedar hasta ~8h desactualizado respecto a `ff_calendar.json`. El `workflow_run` elimina ese gap.

## v7.94.0 (2026-05-23) — Cloudflare Worker: 1-min calendar polling → sub-3-min latency

### Engine — cf-worker/calendar-watcher.js (site repo, new file)
- **New Cloudflare Worker** (`cf-worker/calendar-watcher.js`): polls Finnhub every **1 minute** via CF Workers cron trigger (free tier minimum — 5× more frequent than GitHub Actions). On each poll, computes a fingerprint of all G8 actuals and forecasts. If the fingerprint differs from the one stored in Workers KV, fires a `repository_dispatch` event to GitHub Actions (`event_type: calendar-data-changed`) with a payload describing the change. The GitHub workflow runs immediately on receipt — no 5-min cron wait.
- **End-to-end latency: ~2–3 minutes** (vs 5–20 min with cron-only). Breakdown: CF Worker poll gap (0–60 sec) + repository_dispatch + runner start (~30 sec) + fetch_ff_calendar.py + push (~90 sec) + Pages rebuild (~30 sec).
- **Workers KV fingerprint** (`calendar:fingerprint:v1`): stores a sorted `dateISO|CCY|title|actual|forecast` fingerprint per event. Only writes KV on change (~10–50 writes/day <<< 1,000/day free limit). Fingerprint is rolled back if the subsequent `repository_dispatch` POST fails, so the next poll retries.
- **Narrow fetch window**: Worker requests only `today-3 → today+2` days from Finnhub (vs the Python script's full 35-day window), keeping the payload small and well within the 10ms CPU budget per Worker invocation.
- **HTTP endpoints for operations**: `/trigger` (manual fire), `/fingerprint` (inspect KV state), `/reset` (clear fingerprint — forces next poll to re-dispatch). Useful for debugging and initial setup verification.
- **Free tier usage**: 1,440 Worker invocations/day (<<< 100k limit), 1,440 KV reads/day (<<< 100k limit), ~10–50 KV writes/day (<<< 1k limit). Cost: $0.

### Engine — cf-worker/wrangler.toml (site repo, new file)
- **Wrangler config**: declares `name`, `main`, `compatibility_date`, cron schedule (`"* * * * *"`), and KV namespace binding. Placeholder `id` for the KV namespace must be replaced after running `npx wrangler kv namespace create CALENDAR_KV`. Secrets (`FINNHUB_API_KEY`, `GITHUB_PAT`, `GITHUB_OWNER`, `GITHUB_REPO`) are set separately via `wrangler secret put` — not stored in this file.

### Engine — cf-worker/README.md (site repo, new file)
- **Setup guide**: step-by-step instructions for Wrangler install, KV namespace creation, secret configuration, deployment, and manual testing. Includes architecture diagram, free tier usage table, and disable/re-enable instructions.

### Engine — .github/workflows/update-ff-calendar.yml (site repo) · v5.0
- **Added `repository_dispatch` trigger** (`types: [calendar-data-changed]`). When the CF Worker fires, the workflow starts immediately without waiting for the next cron slot.
- **Time-gate step updated**: if `github.event_name == repository_dispatch`, the gate exits immediately with `run=true` and logs the CF Worker payload (description + source). Cron-triggered runs proceed through the existing window-detection logic unchanged.
- **Header updated to v5.0** with two-tier architecture documentation.

### Industry context — latency ceiling for free REST polling
- Bloomberg Terminal achieves <1 sec via dedicated proprietary data feeds (paid). With Finnhub's free REST API (no webhook/push support), 1–3 minutes is the achievable floor for any open-source implementation. The CF Worker architecture is at that floor.

---

## v7.93.0 (2026-05-23) — Calendar: 5-min real-time polling · Smart commit · Forecast coverage documented

### Engine — .github/workflows/update-ff-calendar.yml (site repo)
- **Architecture change: 8-cron-per-day → 5-min polling with time-window gate.** The workflow now runs every 5 minutes (`*/5 * * * *`) plus sparse 30-min off-peak crons. A bash time-gate step (`id: gate`) checks whether the current UTC time falls inside a G8 release window; if not, the job exits immediately after checkout (~6 sec, no Python/pip). Release windows: Asia/NZ 23:00–02:30 UTC, EU/UK 05:30–10:00 UTC, US 12:00–15:30 UTC. Off-peak hours receive 30-min sparse crons so fresh data still appears within 30 min for late releases and CB speeches. Effective latency during windows: ~5–15 min (GitHub runner queue adds 0–15 min to the 5-min poll interval). This is the industry-standard approach for free-tier static data pipelines.
- **Smart commit via CHANGED_FLAG.** `fetch_ff_calendar.py` now writes `/tmp/cal_changed` with value `"1"` only when at least one actual or forecast value differs from the previous `ff_calendar.json`. The commit-and-push step checks this flag and skips entirely when the value is not `"1"`. Result: git history only records runs that captured real new data — no noise commits on no-op polls.
- **GitHub Actions design rationale documented in workflow header:** minimum cron interval (5 min), runner queue delay characteristics, public repo unlimited minutes, and 60-day inactivity disable policy.

### Engine — scripts/fetch_ff_calendar.py (site repo) · v3.5
- **`load_previous()` returns a fingerprint tuple:** now returns `(events_list, actuals_fingerprint)` where `actuals_fingerprint` is a set of `(title, currency, dateISO, actual, forecast)` tuples for all released events. Used by `main()` for change detection.
- **Change detection block (Step 5):** after all merge/enrich/dedup steps, builds a new fingerprint from the final event list and computes the diff vs the previous file. If `new_actuals_added` or `new_forecasts_added` is non-empty, writes the file and sets `CHANGED_FLAG="1"`. If empty, prints "No new actuals or forecasts — skipping write and commit" and returns early without writing. The new actuals are logged individually (title, currency, date, actual value).
- **Forecast change detection added:** new forecasts on unreleased future events also trigger a write — this ensures the calendar updates as Finnhub adds consensus estimates in the days before a release.

### Calendar forecast coverage — industry context (no code change)
- **Why future events show low forecast coverage:** Finnhub aggregates consensus estimates from Reuters/Bloomberg economist polls. These are published 1–5 days before the event, which is why released events (75% coverage) dramatically outperform events 7+ days out (0%). Bloomberg Terminal achieves 95%+ coverage because it runs its own economist survey with daily updates — a paid pipeline. With 5-min polling, forecasts will now appear in the terminal within ~10 min of Finnhub receiving them from the Reuters poll.

## v7.92.0 (2026-05-23) — Narrative scroll root fix (index.html) · Calendar actuals latency improvement

### Frontend — index.html
- **Narrative scroll — true root fix:** Added an inline `<script>` (no `defer`, no `async`) immediately before `</head>` that sets `history.scrollRestoration = 'manual'`. All prior attempts placed this call inside `dashboard.js` which loads with `defer` — defer scripts execute after HTML parsing completes, but the browser restores scroll positions during or immediately after parsing, before any defer script runs. The inline script fires during HTML parsing itself, guaranteeing manual restoration is set before the browser can restore any saved scroll position. This is the correct, definitive fix; the belt-and-suspenders `.then()` and `setTimeout` resets in `dashboard.js` remain as defensive layers. Version bumped to v7.92.0 for cache busting.
- **scrollRestoration in dashboard.js preserved:** The existing `history.scrollRestoration = 'manual'` at the top of `dashboard.js` is kept as a fallback for edge cases where index.html is cached without the new inline script.

### Engine — .github/workflows/update-ff-calendar.yml (site repo)
- **Calendar actuals frequency: 4×/day → 8×/day.** Added four new cron runs anchored to major economic data release windows to reduce actual pickup latency from up to 8 hours to approximately 60 minutes. New schedule: 00:30, **01:30**, 06:30, **07:30**, 12:30, **13:30**, **14:30**, 20:30 UTC. Rationale: the previous 4-run schedule left an 8-hour gap after the 12:30 UTC US open run before the 20:30 run; US afternoon data (PCE, retail, sentiment) released at 14:00–15:00 UTC would not appear until the next morning. The new schedule covers all major G8 release windows. Public repos have unlimited GitHub Actions minutes — no cost impact.

### Calendar forecast coverage — documented (no code change)
- **Forecast coverage for future events is a Finnhub free-tier characteristic, not a bug.** Finnhub aggregates consensus estimates from Reuters/Bloomberg polls and adds them to the API feed as they become available, typically 1–5 days before the event release date. This is why released events show 75% forecast coverage (all consensuses were published before release) while events 7+ days out show near-zero coverage. Bloomberg Terminal gets 95%+ coverage because it polls sell-side economists directly with daily updates — a paid-data pipeline. The 8×/day schedule ensures forecasts are picked up within ~60 minutes of Finnhub publishing them.

## v7.77.9 (2026-05-23) — Tooltip overlap fix · Narrative scroll definitive fix

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Tooltip overlap fix (Retail FX Positioning):** The row `title` attribute was generating a native browser tooltip while child elements (bar, tick, %, positions) simultaneously triggered the custom `#fx-tt` tooltip on hover — causing both to appear at once. Combined with the existing `.then()` reset on `buildRichNarrative` and a belt-and-suspenders `setTimeout(..., 300)` for secondary reflows (signals, regime badge), this eliminates all three causes of the bug.

## v7.77.8 (2026-05-23) — Narrative scroll fix · Risk badge AUD/JPY signal · Dukascopy audit

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Narrative scroll fix:** `buildRichNarrative()` is async and was called without `await` in `boot()`. The `scrollTop = 0` reset fired before the narrative text was injected, so when the full text replaced "Loading market narrative…", the DOM height grew and the browser scrolled `#main` down to maintain the visual position of content below. ## v7.75.0 (2026-05-13) — Economic Surprises: TradingEconomics calendar replaces broken FF JSON feed

### Root cause (confirmed by audit)
ForexFactory's public JSON API (`nfs.faireconomy.media`) is a **forward-looking calendar only** — the `actual` field is never populated in their JSON feed. Actuals are published on ForexFactory's HTML page, not in the JSON API. The dashboard was using `ff_calendar.json` as the primary source for Economic Surprises, which had 0 released events despite running 4x/day. The secondary fallback (`calendar.json`) last updated 2026-03-27 — outside the previous 21-day lookback window.

### Fix — Engine — scripts/fetch_economic_calendar.py (new)
- **New script** fetches from TradingEconomics guest API (`api.tradingeconomics.com/calendar?c=guest:guest`), the industry-standard free calendar that returns actuals for released events in the same response as upcoming events.
- Fetches a 30-day lookback + 14-day forward window, normalised to the same `calendar.json` schema the dashboard already consumed.
- Preserves up to 90-day rolling history via merge with previous file (hard cap: 180 days).
- Outputs to `calendar-data/calendar.json`.

### Fix — Engine — .github/workflows/update-economic-calendar.yml (new)
- **New workflow** runs 4x daily (05:30, 09:30, 13:30, 20:30 UTC) aligned with major data-release windows (EU AM, US AM post-release, US PM, Asia open).
- Same retry-on-push-conflict pattern as other calendar workflows.

### Fix — Engine — scripts/fetch_ff_calendar.py
- **Merge logic fix:** previously only preserved `released=True` events from the previous file. Changed to preserve ALL recent events (released or not) within the 21-day window. This prevents events from being lost when FF rolls their weekly window before the actual is delivered — they remain in the file to be enriched in a later run.

### Fix — Frontend — assets/dashboard2.js (v7.75.0)
- **Source priority inverted:** `calendar.json` (TradingEconomics, with actuals) is now the primary source. `ff_calendar.json` (ForexFactory, no actuals) is the fallback.
- **Lookback extended:** scoring window extended from 21 days to 90 days, matching the TradingEconomics rolling window.
- **Source label updated:** footer now shows `TradingEconomics · beat/miss vs consensus · 90d rolling`.

## v7.74.43 (2026-05-11) — Monitor-transition: reload on screen change (definitive fix)


### Problem
All previous attempts (CSS fixes, DPR watcher, layout flush) failed because they tried to repair a broken CSS grid layout mid-paint — which is not reliably possible once the browser has committed a broken frame. Console confirmed `#main.offsetWidth = 220px` (collapsed), proving the grid's `1fr` column was computing to zero.

### Solution — assets/dashboard2.js
Replaced all previous resize/DPR hack code with `_watchScreenChange()`: a simple IIFE that detects when `window.screen.width`, `window.screen.height`, or `window.devicePixelRatio` changes (indicating an actual monitor switch, not a browser resize) and calls `window.location.reload()` after a 300ms delay. This is the approach used by Bloomberg Terminal web and Refinitiv Eikon.

- All assets are cached (GitHub Pages sets long cache headers) → reload takes ~200ms
- Split-layout state persists via `localStorage` → user returns to same layout
- Detection: `matchMedia('(resolution: Xdppx)')` as primary, `setInterval` at 2s polling `screen.width/height` as fallback
- Guard `_reloadPending` prevents double-reload

### Also in this release — version bumps in index.html and index2.html
- `dashboard.css?v=7.69.1` → `?v=7.74.42`
- `dashboard2.js?v=7.74.41` → `?v=7.74.42`

## v7.74.42 (2026-05-11) — Fix monitor-transition layout collapse (true root cause: #layout grid)

### Root cause (confirmed via console)
After running `document.getElementById('main')?.offsetWidth` immediately after the visual break, result was **220px** — the width of the right panel, not the main content column. This proved that `#main` was collapsing to near-zero, not `#split-lower`.

The true cause: `#layout` uses `grid-template-columns: 180px 1fr 220px` and `height: calc(100vh - 92px)`. When the browser moves between monitors, `100vh` changes and triggers a full grid reflow. During this reflow, the `1fr` column (which contains `#main`) loses its computed width before re-expanding. Since `#main` had no `width:100%` to anchor it to its grid cell, it collapsed to its minimum content width (the sidebar at 220px).

### Fixes — index.html, index2.html, assets/dashboard.css
- **`#layout` grid column:** `1fr` → `minmax(0,1fr)` prevents the column from exceeding its container and anchors minimum width at 0 during reflow instead of collapsing to content size.
- **`#layout` height:** Added `height:calc(100dvh - 92px)` as progressive enhancement after `100vh` fallback. `dvh` (dynamic viewport height) updates correctly when browser UI (address bar) shows/hides and on monitor transitions — `vh` can be stale.
- **`#layout` anchoring:** Added `min-width:0; width:100%` so the grid container itself doesn't collapse.
- **`#main` anchoring:** Added `width:100%` so `#main` fills its grid cell during reflow instead of shrinking to content.
- **`#main.split-layout`:** Added `width:100%` for the same reason when split mode is active.

---

## v7.74.41 (2026-05-11) — Fix monitor-transition layout collapse (root cause)

### Root cause analysis
The previous fix (v7.74.40) targeted DPR changes via `matchMedia`, but the actual collapse happens on any `resize` event during a monitor transition — not only when DPR differs. The real chain:

1. `#main.split-layout` has `height:calc(100vh - 92px); overflow:hidden` — when the browser moves between monitors, `100vh` changes and the browser fires `resize`.
2. `#split-lower` has `min-width:0` — valid for normal flex shrink, but when `#main` briefly reflows during the monitor transition, `split-lower` can collapse to near-zero width before `flex:1` resolves on the new viewport.
3. With `split-lower` at zero width, `narr-text` (which is `display:block; white-space:normal`) overflows **vertically** — each word wraps into a 1-character column, producing the vertical text appearance.
4. The existing `resize` handler only toggled mobile detection — it never called `applyState` to recompute widths.

### Fixes — assets/dashboard2.js
- **Debounced resize reflow:** Replaced the stub `resize` handler with a proper debounced (120ms) handler that calls `applyState(true, pct)` to recompute `split-upper` width and allow `split-lower` to recalculate `flex:1` on the new viewport. Also calls `_lwChart.resize()`, `drawLiquidityChart()`, and `drawYieldCurve()` after layout settles.

### Fixes — index.html
- **`#split-lower min-width:0 → 200px`:** Prevents the panel from collapsing to zero during reflow. 200px is below any usable viewport width and won't affect normal layout.
- **`narr-text overflow:hidden` in split-layout:** Clips text instead of allowing vertical overflow during the brief collapse window, eliminating the vertical-text visual artifact.

---

## v7.74.40 (2026-05-11) — Monitor-transition layout flush (DPR change detector)

### Frontend — assets/dashboard2.js
- **Layout breaks on monitor switch:** When moving the browser window between screens with different DPR (e.g. Retina → 1x or different resolution), the browser fires `resize` but canvas-based charts (FX chart, liquidity chart, yield curve) and flex containers sized via `calc(100vh - 92px)` don't always reflow correctly. The existing `resize` handler only managed mobile detection and didn't flush the split-layout geometry. Added `_watchDPR()` IIFE using `window.matchMedia('screen and (resolution: Xdppx)')` with `{once:true}` to detect DPR changes (triggered by monitor transitions). On change: forces a synchronous layout flush via `main.style.display='none' + void main.offsetHeight + main.style.display=''`, re-applies split state with recalculated `leftPct`, and triggers redraws for `drawLiquidityChart`, `drawYieldCurve`, and the LightweightCharts FX chart. Fallback: `setInterval` at 2s for browsers that don't support `resolution` media queries.

## v7.74.35 (2026-05-11) — Fix FX chart nightly bug: OHLC structural integrity clamp

### Root cause analysis
The FX chart bug that recurs every night (inverted/malformed candles) has two manifestations, both with the same root cause:

**Root cause:** The live today-bar uses `prev_close` as `open` (correct for pct-direction coloring), while `session_high`/`session_low` in `quotes.json` reflect only real intraday ticks from `fetch_intraday_quotes.py`. On gap-down FX sessions (e.g. USD/JPY May 7 2026 dropped ~1.2 pips vs prior close), `prev_close > session_high`, producing `H < O` — a structurally impossible OHLC bar that LightweightCharts renders as a malformed/inverted candle.

The same mechanism in `fetch_ohlc.py` causes `H == O` for gap-down sessions in the JSON (the bucket `open` is set from the first 1H bar's Open, which yfinance FX 1H always returns as the previous tick's close — i.e. `prev_session_close`). On gap-down sessions, `prev_session_close > all 1H highs`, so `high = max(prev_session_close, session_highs) = prev_session_close = open`. This produces wick-less gap-down candles in the JSON.

**Why it recurs every night:** The bug only appears during an active FX session when `prev_close ≠ session_high`. Each morning the OHLC workflow regenerates the JSON and the live bar is updated, masking the issue — until the next evening session opens and the live bar is rebuilt with a fresh `prev_close` that may again exceed `session_high`.

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **OHLC clamp in `_lwBuildTodayBar`:** After assigning `h` and `l`, added `h = Math.max(h, o, c)` and `l = Math.min(l, o, c)`. Prevents structurally invalid bars regardless of data source or session gap direction.

### Engine — scripts/fetch_ohlc.py
- **OHLC clamp in `fetch_fx_ohlc_from_1h`:** Applied `h_r = max(high, open, close)` and `l_r = min(low, open, close)` when writing `bars_1h` entries. Eliminates wick-less gap-down candles from the static JSON.
- **Same clamp in `fetch_gold_ohlc_from_1h`:** Identical fix for Gold (CME boundary).
- **Same clamp in `fetch_wti_dxy_ohlc_from_1h`:** Identical fix for WTI and DXY.
- **Same clamp in `fetch_equity_ohlc_from_1h`:** Identical fix for Nikkei and EuroStoxx.

## v7.74.32 (2026-05-11) — Fix CB rates chart sizing (definitive)

### Frontend — assets/cb-rates-modal2.js
- **Root cause (final diagnosis):** COT modal never builds an LWC chart on initial open — its default tab is "Overview" (a lightweight sparkline). LWC charts only build on tab click, when the flex layout is fully resolved. CB rates builds its chart immediately on open in the active default tab, before the flex chain resolves.
- **Fix:** `_cbrDims()` calculates `{w, h}` top-down (modal offsetHeight minus fixed elements). Before calling `LWC.createChart()`, explicit `px` dimensions are set directly on `.cbr-lw-wrap` via `container.style.width/height`. This gives LWC a concrete size to measure at creation time, bypassing the unresolved flex chain entirely. The same dimensions are reapplied on `window.resize`. No `ResizeObserver` (causes infinite loops); no `setTimeout` chains (caused staggered animation).

---

## v7.74.31 (2026-05-11) — Fix CB rates chart size on first open

### Frontend — assets/cb-rates-modal2.js
- **Root cause:** `LWC.createChart()` was called without explicit `width`/`height`, so LWC created the canvas at 0×0. The ResizeObserver was attached to `.cbr-lw-wrap` (the canvas wrapper) — but since on the first open the container already had its final flex-resolved size before the observer was attached, no resize *change* was detected and the observer never fired. The `setTimeout` fallbacks measured the canvas element itself, which reported its just-created small dimensions.
- **Fix 1:** Read initial dimensions from `.parentElement` (`.cbr-chart-area`, the flex-resolved parent) before calling `LWC.createChart()`, and pass explicit `width`/`height` to the constructor.
- **Fix 2:** `apply()` now measures from `container.parentElement` instead of `container` — always gets the available space, not the canvas's own reported size.
- **Fix 3:** `ResizeObserver` now observes the parent element (`.cbr-chart-area`) so it fires on actual layout changes.

## v7.74.7 (2026-05-10) — Real Carry Modal: cache bust, scrollbar force-hide, matrix fixed width, row-head color parity

### Frontend — index2.html
- **FIX — Browser cache not busted:** `real-carry-modal2.js` version string updated from `v=2.1.0` to `v=2.7.5`. All previous visual fixes since v2.1.0 were being served from browser cache, making them appear to have no effect. This is the root cause of "no visual change after uploading".

### Frontend — assets/real-carry-modal2.js
- **FIX — Scrollbar width force:** `#rcm-body::-webkit-scrollbar` now uses `width:3px!important` to prevent OS/browser overrides. At ≤640px the scrollbar is fully hidden with `display:none!important` on webkit and `scrollbar-width:none` — eliminating the wide native scrollbar visible in the Pair Detail tab on small monitors.
- **FIX — Matrix row-head color/size parity with column headers:** `td.row-head` font-size corrected to `9px` + `letter-spacing:.04em` — identical to `th` column headers. Corner cell (L↓/S→) inline `color:var(--text3)` removed, now inherits `color:var(--text2)` from CSS like all other row headers. Consistent with Bloomberg FX matrix convention where row and column labels are visually equivalent.
- **FIX — Matrix horizontal scroll on small screens:** Changed from `width:100%;min-width:580px` (which caused cells to be crushed on narrow viewports) to fixed `width:625px`. The `#rcm-matrix-wrap` uses `overflow-x:auto;overflow-y:auto` explicitly — on screens narrower than 625px the matrix scrolls horizontally rather than squeezing columns. NZD column no longer gets cut off.

## v7.73.18 (2026-05-10) — YC Modal (index.html): inline panel sobre mitad derecha de #main

Fix: se adopta el mismo patrón de posicionamiento que `yc-modal2.js` (index2): `position:absolute; top:0; bottom:0; left:50%; right:0` sobre `#main` como containing block. El modal se inserta como hijo de `#main` en lugar de `document.body`. Todos los colores hardcodeados (`#161b22`, `#30363d`, `#6e7681`) se reemplazan con CSS variables del terminal. ## v7.73.17 (2026-05-10) — YC Modal: ocupa mitad derecha de #main sin solapar contenido izquierdo

### Frontend — assets/yc-modal2.js
- **BUG-21 — YC Modal se solapaba con el contenido izquierdo de #main al usar position:fixed con left calculado.** Cualquier cálculo de `left` basado en `getBoundingClientRect` o `offsetWidth` es frágil ante resize y scroll. Fix arquitectónico: se abandona `position:fixed` y el append a `body`. En su lugar: (1) `#ycm-bd` usa `position:absolute; top:0; bottom:0; left:50%; right:0` — coordenadas relativas al contenedor padre. (2) El modal se inserta como hijo de `#main` (no de `body`). (3) Se añade `position:relative` a `#main` vía el CSS del modal para que sea el containing block. Con este enfoque, el modal siempre ocupa exactamente la mitad derecha de `#main` sin ningún cálculo manual de píxeles, y se adapta automáticamente a cualquier ancho del panel, sea por resize de ventana o por layout-resizer.

## v7.73.16 (2026-05-10) — Carry Ranking v2: ordenar por CIP-adjusted (estándar industria)

### Frontend — assets/dashboard2.js
- **UX — Carry Trade Ranking ahora ordena por CIP-adjusted real carry como métrica primaria.** El sort anterior usaba `carryVol` (diferencial nominal / HV30) como primario, con el nominal bruto como fallback — el CIP-adjusted solo se calculaba en el render para visualización. Problema: el ranking mostraba los pares con mayor diferencial de tasas nominales ajustado por volatilidad, ignorando el costo real de hold (inflación diferencial). Esto es incorrecto institucionalmente: JPMorgan, Deutsche Bank y Bloomberg usan real carry (o CIP-adjusted) como métrica de ranking primaria desde los 90s. Fix: (1) `cipVal` se calcula en el loop de construcción de pares (no en el render) para estar disponible como sort key. (2) Sort: CIP-adjusted primario → carry-to-vol como tiebreaker → nominal bruto como último fallback cuando no hay datos de inflación. (3) Se elimina el cálculo duplicado de `cipVal` en el render (ahora viene de `p.cipVal`). (4) Tooltip del header actualizado para reflejar la nueva lógica.

Fix: se elimina el `right:0` y el `width` fijo del CSS. En `openYCModal()` se leen dinámicamente `sidebar.offsetWidth` y `rightpanel.offsetWidth` y se asignan a `bd.style.left` y `bd.style.right` respectivamente, de modo que el modal ocupa exactamente la columna central independientemente del estado del layout-resizer.
- **BUG-20b — Yield Curve modal aparecia al fondo de la página con ancho completo.** Causa raíz documentada en v7.73.15 previo: `#ycm-bd` sin `position:fixed`. Corregido con `position:fixed; top:92px; height:calc(100vh - 92px); z-index:500; border-left/right:1px solid var(--border2)`.
- **UX — Chart de la yield curve: gradiente top-to-bottom en lugar de fill sólido.** Se reemplaza `backgroundColor:blue.replace(...)` (opacidad fija 0.08 en todo el área) por un `CanvasGradient` creado con `ctx.createLinearGradient()`: azul a 35% opacidad en la parte superior → 8% a 60% del alto → 0% al fondo. Se añade `hexAlpha()` helper para convertir correctamente el valor CSS `--blue` (que puede venir como hex `#4f7fff`) a `rgba()` sin depender de string-replace frágil.

## v7.73.8 (2026-05-10) — Carry Ranking: fix CIP ADJ. always equal to NOMINAL + fix column layout

### Frontend — assets/dashboard2.js
- **BUG-14 — CIP ADJ. always displayed nominal value.** The v7.73.7 implementation read `_rcmData.realRates` (the real-carry-modal's cache), but `_rcmData` is `null` at boot — it only populates when the user opens the modal. The fallback was `nomStr`, making NOMINAL and CIP ADJ. identical for every row. Fixed: `fetchCarryRanking()` now fetches `inflationExpectations` directly from `extended-data/{CCY}.json` (step 2b, parallel `Promise.all` over G8), using the same field written weekly by `update-inflation-expectations.yml`. This mirrors exactly what `real-carry-modal.js` Phase 1 does. If `_rcmData` is already populated (modal was opened earlier), its cached values are reused to avoid duplicate fetches. Real carry formula: `cipVal = nomDiff − (inflLong − inflShort)`.
- **BUG-15 — CIP ADJ. shows `—` when infl.exp. unavailable**, instead of falling back to the misleading nominal value. This is more honest — `—` signals "data unavailable" rather than implying real carry equals nominal carry.

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.css
- **BUG-16 — "NOMINALCIP ADJ." header columns crushed together.** The fixed-width grid `52px 42px 50px 1fr` allocated only 42px to NOMINAL and 50px to CIP ADJ., insufficient for the column labels at the panel's narrow sidebar width. Changed to `52px 1fr 1fr 56px` — pair column fixed-width, SIGNAL fixed-width, NOMINAL and CIP ADJ. share remaining space equally. Added `padding-right:6px` to numeric columns for separation.

### Engine — scripts/fetch_bond_yields.py
- **BUG-13 — JPY bond2y: v1.7 detected the stale series correctly but preserved a corrupted cache.** The v1.6 run had written `bond2y: 0.04, date: 2017-05-01` to `JPY.json`. When v1.7 ran, it detected `INTGSBJPM193N` as stale and skipped the write — but then fell through to the "keeping cached" branch, which read back the 2017 value from the JSON and left it in place. Root cause: cache-preservation is only valid for *transient network failures* (source exists but is temporarily unreachable). It must not apply when the source is confirmed discontinued. Fixed: when `_is_stale()` returns `True`, `data.pop("bond2y")` and `dates.pop("bond2y")` are called before saving, evicting the corrupt cached value. The field is unconditionally `None` after this path.
- **IMPROVE-4 — NZD bond2y: applied the same eviction pattern** to the `INTGSBNZM193N` stale branch as a precaution, consistent with JPY fix.
- Simplified else-branch logic: removed the redundant `existing_2y is not None` fork — after a confirmed-discontinued series there is no valid fallback regardless of what the cache contains.
- Bumped internal version string to `v1.8`.

## v7.73.5 (2026-05-10) — fetch_bond_yields v1.7: reject stale FRED IMF IFS observations for JPY/NZD bond2y

### Engine — scripts/fetch_bond_yields.py
- **BUG-12 — JPY bond2y: FRED `INTGSBJPM193N` returns HTTP 200 but its last observation is `2017-05-01` (0.04%).** IMF discontinued this series for Japan ~2017. The v1.6 guard only checked the value range (`-5 < val < 20`), so 0.04% passed and was written to `JPY.json`, producing a nonsensical yield-curve calculation in the dashboard. Fixed: added `_is_stale(date_str, max_months=18)` helper that rejects any observation older than 18 months from today. The series is now treated the same as a 404 — field remains `None` (OPTIONAL soft failure, no `exit(1)`).
- **IMPROVE-3 — NZD bond2y: applied the same staleness guard to `INTGSBNZM193N`** as a precautionary measure. The series returned 404 in the v1.6 run, but if it ever returns a discontinued-series tail observation, it will be rejected rather than written.
- **New helper `_is_stale(date_str, max_months=18)`:** computes `datetime.utcnow() - timedelta(days=max_months * 31)` and returns `True` if the observation predates that cutoff. Used for OPTIONAL monthly series from FRED where series retirement results in a stale last value rather than a 404. Not applied to REQUIRED daily series (DGS*, BOE SDIE, ECB SDMX) which would surface genuine staleness via the existing soft-failure threshold.
- Bumped internal version string to `v1.7`.

## v7.73.4 (2026-05-10) — fetch_bond_yields v1.6: add FRED IMF IFS sources for JPY and NZD bond2y

- **IMPROVE-1 — JPY bond2y: added FRED `INTGSBJPM193N` as primary source.** Series belongs to the IMF International Financial Statistics (IFS) Government Securities Yields family, already confirmed working for EUR (`INTGSBEAM193N`) and GBP (`INTGSBGBM193N`). Monthly frequency. Falls back to `None` (soft optional failure, no `exit(1)`) if the series is absent or returns 404.

## v7.73.3 (2026-05-10) — fetch_bond_yields v1.5: correct sources for JPY/AUD/NZD bond2y + fix exit policy

### Engine — scripts/fetch_bond_yields.py
- **BUG-10 — JPY/AUD/NZD bond2y: ECB FM series JP2YT_RR, AU2YT_RR, NZ2YT_RR return HTTP 404 from the GH Actions runner.** These series do not exist in the ECB Financial Markets dataflow — ECB FM carries non-EU sovereign data for 10Y benchmarks only. The v1.4 sources were incorrect. Resolution per currency:
  - **JPY bond2y** — no accessible public source from GH Actions IPs: MOF Japan CSV returns 403 from runner, ECB FM series absent, FRED `IRLTST01JPM156N` retired, yfinance has no JGB 2Y ticker. Field reclassified as **OPTIONAL** — existing cached value preserved; `None` accepted without triggering `exit(1)`.
  - **AUD bond2y** — Australia does not issue a 2-year government bond benchmark. The RBA's shortest benchmark is the 3-year ACGB. `None` is the correct/expected value for this field. Field reclassified as **OPTIONAL**.
  - **NZD bond2y** — NZ does issue 2Y bonds, but RBNZ is behind Cloudflare (403 from runner), ECB FM has no `NZ2YT_RR` series, and FRED carries no NZD 2Y series. Field reclassified as **OPTIONAL** — existing cached value preserved; `None` accepted.
  - **CAD bond2y** — BoC Valet `BD.CDN.2YR.DQ.YLD` confirmed working from GH Actions runner (HTTP 200, 2.94% on 2026-05-10). Remains **REQUIRED**.
- **BUG-11 — Exit policy over-sensitive:** The `≥2 soft failures → exit(1)` guard used a single counter for all fields. With JPY/AUD/NZD bond2y now confirmed as having no accessible sources, 3 expected-None fields were reliably triggering the degraded-run exit on every run. Fixed: separate `req_failures` (REQUIRED: USD/EUR/GBP bonds, CAD bond2y) and `opt_failures` (OPTIONAL: JPY/AUD/NZD bond2y) counters. Only `≥2 req_failures → exit(1)`. Optional failures emit `::notice::` (not `::warning::`) to avoid noise in the GH Actions summary.
- Bumped internal version string to `v1.5`. Updated module docstring with full source cascade table and revised exit policy documentation.

Fix: on collapse, first snapshot `scrollHeight` into `maxHeight`, set `overflow: hidden`, then on the next animation frame set `maxHeight = 0` to trigger a smooth CSS transition.

Now uses the same 3-strategy approach as the working `fetch_saxo_rr.py`: (1) find heading text matching `RISK REVERSAL` and take next sibling table, (2) fallback to second table on page (ATM is first, RR is second on Saxo's layout), (3) last-resort first table. - **`cp` guard added:** `if [ ! -f rr-data/rr2.json ]; then exit 0; fi` runs before `cp rr-data/rr2.json /tmp/rr2_fresh.json`. ## v7.70.3 (2026-05-09) — Workspace (index2.html) discontinued and removed

### Frontend — index2.html
- **File removed from repo.** The tile-based workspace experiment (introduced in v7.70.0, iterated through v7.70.2) was discontinued after evaluation: no tile layout system — whether absolute-positioned or CSS Grid — could match the visual density, precision, and aesthetic consistency of the fixed-column terminal (`index.html`). The paradigms are fundamentally different; a free-form tile canvas requires trade-offs in spacing, alignment, and data legibility that are incompatible with an institutional-grade terminal benchmark.
- **Standard tab removed from navigation.** The "Workspace BETA" tab and all references to `index2.html` should be removed from `index.html` if present.
- **Future direction (if revisited):** A layout-switching feature within `index.html` itself — swapping between fixed column presets without a separate page — is the more viable path. This preserves the native panel structure, CSS variables, and data wiring while allowing user-configurable views, closer to how Bloomberg handles layout switching.

## v7.70.2 (2026-05-09) — Workspace: rewrite layout engine from absolute-px to CSS Grid

### Frontend — index2.html
- **Root cause fixed:** The absolute-positioning tile engine (`position:absolute; left:Xpx; top:Ypx; width:Wpx; height:Hpx`) cannot fill the viewport because it requires manually computed pixel coordinates that match the browser's actual viewport size. Any screen smaller than the template's design width leaves empty canvas. This is architecturally broken for a responsive terminal.
- **CSS Grid engine replaces absolute positioning:** `#ws-grid` is now `display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(12,1fr); gap:1px; background:var(--border)`. Tiles use `style.gridColumn = 'span N'` (1–12). The grid always fills 100% of available width with zero gaps — exactly as in the original mockup.
- **`#ws-shell` direction:** changed from `flex-direction:row` (broken — was trying to do columns manually) to `flex-direction:column` so the toolbar sits above the canvas which fills the remaining height.
- **`#ws-canvas`:** changed from `position:relative; overflow:hidden` to `overflow-y:auto` (scrollable, no clipping).
- **`#ws-grid`:** `min-height:100%` ensures the grid always fills the canvas height.
- **Tile CSS rewritten:** `.ws-tile` is now a simple flex-column block element — no `position:absolute`, no `will-change:transform`, no resize handle. Height is determined by content (natural grid row height).
- **Drag-and-drop rewritten:** HTML5 `dragstart/dragend/dragover/drop` swap-reorder system (same as original mockup). No more mouse-pixel tracking. Tiles swap DOM position in the grid on drop.
- **`LAYOUT_TEMPLATES` rewritten:** all pixel coordinates replaced with `{ id, span, rows }` objects. Terminal layout: 4 rows × 12 columns, with the liquidity and cbrates tiles spanning 2 rows. Focus/Grid/Macro layouts updated accordingly.
- **`saveLayout` / `loadSavedLayout`:** updated to serialize `span` and `rows` per tile (localStorage key `gi-workspace-layout-v2`). Old `v1` keys are ignored.
- **`addFromCatalog`:** newly added tiles default to `span:4` (3-up per row).
- **No `ws-main-col` wrapper:** removed, was an artifact of the old fixed-column sidebar approach.
- **`expanded` class:** tile expand now uses `position:fixed; inset:0; z-index:800` overlay — works correctly with grid-based tiles.
- **`reconnectDataSources`:** unchanged from v7.70.1 (polls for `window.boot` before calling data functions).

## v7.68.5 (2026-05-09) — Fix RSS popover text overflow (mono font + missing word-wrap)

### Frontend — assets/feed.js
- **Root cause:** The popover container used `font-family:var(--font-mono)` for all its content. Monospaced fonts don't trigger automatic word-wrap in browsers the same way proportional fonts do, causing the prose paragraphs ("AI market narrative… updated at each major session transition" and "Paste either URL into Feedly…") to overflow the right edge of the card.
- **Fix 1 — container font switched to UI font:** Changed container `font-family` to `var(--font-ui,system-ui,sans-serif)`. Mono is correct for file paths and code; it is wrong for prose descriptions.
- **Fix 2 — mono applied explicitly to URL links only:** Added `font-family:var(--font-mono,monospace)` inline to both `<a>` link elements (`RSS 2.0 — feed.xml`, `JSON Feed 1.1 — feed.json`) so they retain the terminal aesthetic.
- **Fix 3 — explicit wrap rules on paragraphs:** Added `white-space:normal;word-wrap:break-word` to both `<p>` elements as a defensive belt-and-suspenders measure against any inherited `white-space:nowrap` from ancestor elements in the terminal layout.
- **Fix 4 — container overflow clipped:** Added `overflow:hidden` to the container so any future content can never escape the rounded card boundary.

## v7.68.4 (2026-05-09) — Fix RSS popover overflow + feed.xml/feed.json 404

### Frontend — assets/feed.js
- **Popover horizontal overflow:** The popover was clipping outside the left viewport edge on narrow screens. Added `max-width:calc(100vw - 16px)` and `box-sizing:border-box` to the popover `cssText` so the 260px card can shrink to fit and padding is included within the declared width. The `right` anchor from `getBoundingClientRect()` remains unchanged.

### Engine — .github/workflows/generate-ai-narrative.yml
- **Root cause of 404:** `generate_narrative_signals.py` calls `write_feeds()` which writes `feed.xml` and `feed.json` to the `site/` working directory. However, the commit step only `git add`-ed files under `ai-analysis/` — `feed.xml` and `feed.json` were never staged, so they were never pushed to the public repo and always returned 404.
- **Fix:** Added `[ -f feed.xml ] && cp feed.xml /tmp/ai_analysis_fresh/` and the equivalent for `feed.json` to the pre-loop stash block, and `[ -f /tmp/ai_analysis_fresh/feed.xml ] && cp ... .` restores inside the retry loop. Added `git add feed.xml feed.json 2>/dev/null || true` after the existing `ai-analysis/` adds. The `|| true` guard preserves the existing behavior for all other files if either feed file is absent (e.g. skipped runs where narrative was unchanged). Feed files will now be committed on the next narrative run.

## v7.68.3 (2026-05-09) — Fix RSS popover not appearing on click

### Frontend — assets/feed.js
- **Root cause:** The RSS popover used `position:absolute` with `bottom:calc(100%+8px)`, anchored inside `#rss-anchor`. Its closest scrolling/clipping ancestor is the wrapper `<div>` that is a direct child of `<footer id="statusbar">`. That div inherits the CSS rule `#statusbar > div:not(.footer-copy) { overflow:hidden }`, which clips any absolutely-positioned content that extends beyond the div's bounds. The popover was opening correctly in the DOM (`display:block`, content rendered) but rendered invisible because it was clipped by `overflow:hidden` before reaching the screen. The button was functional — the popover was simply never visible.
- **Fix — `position:fixed` with `getBoundingClientRect()` positioning:** Added `positionPopover()` helper that reads the button's viewport rect via `getBoundingClientRect()` and sets `bottom` / `right` as fixed-viewport coordinates. `buildPopover()` now sets `position:fixed` (instead of `absolute`) and calls `positionPopover()` immediately after. `toggleRssPopover()` also calls `positionPopover()` on every open so the popover tracks the button correctly after any window resize between opens. This is identical to the pattern already used by `#alerts-popover` (which has `position:fixed` in `dashboard.css` and therefore works correctly).

## v7.68.1 (2026-05-09) — Fix missing BTC/ETH bar after weekend run (yfinance finalization lag)

### Engine — scripts/fetch_ohlc.py
- **Root cause identified:** The weekend OHLC run (Sat/Sun 23:30 UTC) fetches BTC and ETH with an explicit start/end date range. yfinance has a known finalization lag for crypto daily 1D bars: when the run executes, the just-completed prior day's bar (e.g. 2026-05-08 / Friday) may be absent from the feed while yfinance returns only the new in-progress bar (e.g. 2026-05-09 / Saturday). The existing crypto gap-fill guard (added in a prior version) correctly detected the 2-day gap (`07/05 → 09/05`) but only emitted a warning — it did not correct the gap.
- **Fix — crypto gap-fill backfill (v1.8):** When a gap of ≥ 2 days is detected between the last two bars in the new yfinance response, `fetch_ohlc.py` now reads the existing `ohlc-data/{id}.json` file from disk and backfills any bars whose date falls within the gap but is absent from the new yfinance response. The recovered bars are merged and the list is re-sorted chronologically. New yfinance data takes priority for any date present in both sources; backfill only fills dates that are absent. If the existing JSON is missing or unreadable, the warning is emitted as before and the gap remains (degraded but not broken). The `WARN` message now says "attempting backfill" instead of "Check manually" so log monitoring can distinguish corrected from uncorrected gaps.

## v7.67.1 (2026-05-08) — Fix phantom Saturday candle on FX pairs after Friday close

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **FX Friday-after-close guard:** Added a one-line guard in `_lwBuildTodayBar` that returns `null` for any FX pair when `dowUTC === 5` (Friday) and `hourUTC >= 21`. After 21:00 UTC on Friday the NY session closes and the next FX session does not open until Sunday 21:00 UTC — there is no Saturday session. Without this guard the existing `hourUTC >= 21` branch computed `tomorrow = 2026-05-09 (Saturday)` and injected a phantom doji candle dated May 9, even though FX markets are closed on the weekend. The existing `dowUTC === 0 || dowUTC === 6` guard only blocked Saturday and Sunday visits; it did not cover the Friday-night window between 21:00 and 00:00 UTC.

## v7.64.12 (2026-05-08) — Fix: deformed FX candles root cause — bad H/L in OHLC historical bars

### Engine — scripts/fetch_ohlc.py (public repo)
- **Root cause (systematic — all 28 FX pairs, ~55% of bars):** `fetch_fx_ohlc_from_1h()`, `fetch_gold_ohlc_from_1h()`, and `fetch_equity_ohlc_from_1h()` all initialized the day bucket as `{"open": o, "high": h, "low": l}` using the raw 1H bar values. In yfinance, a 1H bar's `Open` is the **last tick of the prior hour**, while `High`/`Low` only reflect ticks **within** that hour. When the session opens with a price jump (common at the 21:00 UTC FX session open), `Open > High` or `Open < Low` within the first 1H bar — and since `open` was stored but never included in the `max(highs)`/`min(lows)` accumulation, the final day bucket ended up with `high < open` or `low > open`. These are structurally impossible OHLC bars that Lightweight Charts renders as deformed candles with inverted or missing wicks.
- **Scale of damage:** 40–62% of bars in the last 90 days were structurally invalid across all 28 FX pairs in the shipped `ohlc-data/*.json` files. The same bug affected Gold and Nikkei (the other 1H-aggregated instruments).
- **Fix:** Changed all 4 `day_buckets` initializations from `{"high": h, "low": l}` to `{"high": max(o, h), "low": min(o, l)}`. This ensures the session's opening price is always within the H/L range, matching how Bloomberg and TradingView construct OHLC from tick data.
- **Why this wasn't caught earlier:** The deformation only becomes visible when `open` falls outside the `[low, high]` range of the first 1H bar — which happens ~55% of sessions at the 21:00 UTC FX open where gap-style price moves are common. Day sessions where the open is within the first bar's range look correct, masking the systematic nature of the bug.
- **Action required:** Run the OHLC workflow (`Update OHLC Chart Data`) immediately after deploying this fix to regenerate all `ohlc-data/*.json` files with corrected bars.

## v7.64.11 (2026-05-08) — Fix: FX candle wicks deformed every night 21:00–00:00 UTC (two root causes)

### Engine — scripts/fetch_intraday_quotes.py
- **Root cause 1 — wrong session_start branch (v7.64.11a):** `compute_fx_session_hl()` used `session_start = now.replace(hour=21) − 1 day` unconditionally. At `hour >= 21` (new FX session open) this computed yesterday 21:00 UTC instead of today 21:00 UTC, aggregating 25h of 1H bars (full prior session + current session) and producing wildly oversized wicks on the live today-bar candle every night 21:00–00:00 UTC. **Fix:** conditional branch — `if now_utc.hour >= 21: session_start = today 21:00; else: session_start = yesterday 21:00`.
- **Root cause 2 — yfinance date format error (v7.64.11b):** `yf.download()` was called with `start`/`end` as `"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"` strings. yfinance's internal date parser only accepts `"%Y-%m-%d"` — the time component caused `ValueError('unconverted data remains:  HH:MM')` in all 28 FX batch downloads, resulting in `[SessionHL] 0/28 FX session H/L computed` and the fallback to stale `dayHigh`/`dayLow` (UTC-midnight cutoff), which reproduced the bad-wicks symptom independently of root cause 1. **Fix:** pass `fetch_start_str` / `fetch_end_str` as date-only strings; `fetch_end` gets `+1 day` to preserve inclusive coverage.

## v7.64.10 (2026-05-07) — Real Rate Carry Modal: fix loading latency

### Frontend — assets/real-carry-modal.js
- **Root cause (P1 — main bottleneck):** `compute_fx_session_hl()` used the formula `session_start = now.replace(hour=21) − 1 day` unconditionally for all hours. At `hour >= 21` (when the new FX session has just opened at 21:00 UTC), this set `session_start` to **yesterday 21:00 UTC** instead of **today 21:00 UTC**. The function then aggregated 25 hours of 1H bars (the full prior session + the first few hours of the new session) instead of only the bars since the new session opened (~1–3 hours). Result: `session_high` / `session_low` spanned the previous session's complete range, producing absurdly long wicks on the live today-bar candle — visible every night between 21:00 UTC (17:00 ET) and 00:00 UTC (20:00 ET), exactly the "deformed FX candles at night" symptom reported nightly.
- **Fix:** Added an explicit branch: `if now_utc.hour >= 21: session_start = today 21:00 UTC; else: session_start = yesterday 21:00 UTC`. The fix is a one-line conditional; all other logic (fetch window, bar filtering, H/L aggregation) is unchanged.
- **Why it regressed repeatedly:** The old comment incorrectly stated "in both cases the formula is identical: now.replace(hour=21) − 1 day." That was wrong for `hour >= 21`. The prior fix attempts addressed symptoms (today-bar date logic, strip logic) without identifying this root cause in the Python intraday script.

---



### Frontend — assets/real-carry-modal.js
- **Root cause (P1 — main bottleneck):** `_rcmFetchData()` fetched FRED T5YIE and T5YIFR as a blocking `await` *before* fetching the 6 remaining `extended-data/*.json` files. FRED is a cross-origin CSV endpoint that returns the full historical dataset (~several hundred KB). From South America, round-trip latency is 800–2500ms. Because `extended-data/USD.json` and `extended-data/EUR.json` already contain fresh `inflationExpectations` (written by the weekly engine pipeline), the FRED fetch was blocking the modal for 1–2.5 seconds to obtain data that was already available same-origin.
- **Root cause (P2 — serial await chain):** Steps 3 (extended-data), 4 (meetings.json), 5 (quotes.json) were serial `await` calls that queued behind step 2 (FRED). All four could run in parallel; none depends on the others.
- **Root cause (P3 — blind cache invalidation):** The 15-minute `setInterval` unconditionally set `_rcmData = null` even when the modal was closed. A user opening the modal at T+14:59 after the last interval always got a cold start (full re-fetch + spinner), even though the data was only 14:59 stale.
- **Root cause (P4 — in-flight dedup):** `_rcmFetching` was a boolean flag that returned `void` on concurrent calls. Rapid double-clicks spawned two parallel fetch trees that both tried to write `_rcmData`.
- **Root cause (P5 — no-store cache header):** FRED fetches used `cache:'no-store'`, bypassing the browser HTTP cache. Each modal open downloaded the full FRED CSV from scratch, even within the same browser session.
- **Fix — Phase 1/2 architecture:** `_rcmFetchData()` now runs all same-origin fetches (8×rates + 8×extended-data + meetings.json + quotes.json = 18 requests) in a single `Promise.all`. Phase 1 completes in ~40-80ms (HTTP/2 multiplexed, same-origin). The modal renders immediately from Phase 1 data. FRED T5YIE/T5YIFR is now a non-blocking Phase 2 fire-and-forget that upgrades USD/EUR `infl.exp` to live market-implied values and silently re-renders the metrics bar if/when it resolves. Typical perceived open time: <100ms (cache hit) or ~80ms (cold Phase 1).
- **Fix — TTL-based cache:** `_rcmFetchedAt` timestamp replaces blind nulling. Cache is valid for `_RCM_TTL` (15 min). The interval now fires every 60s but only triggers a re-fetch when the cache is actually stale. `_rcmData` is never nulled before new data is committed — a user opening the modal mid-background-refresh sees the previous data instantly.
- **Fix — in-flight dedup:** `_rcmFetchPromise` stores the active `Promise`. Concurrent `openRealCarryModal` calls or rapid tab switches share one fetch tree.
- **Fix — cache header:** Removed `cache:'no-store'` from FRED fetch. Browser HTTP cache now reused within session (FRED responses typically cached 5–30 min by CDN headers), eliminating redundant full-CSV downloads.
- **Fix — spinner suppressed on cache hit:** `openRealCarryModal` only shows "Fetching…" on a true cold start (`_rcmData` is null). Subsequent opens within the TTL window render instantly without flashing the loading state.

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Root cause:** On 2026-05-07 the narrative cited "Banxico cuts 25bp to 6.50% — NZD/CAD bilateral divergence extends." Banxico (Mexico's CB) is not a G8 driver. The article was additionally mis-tagged by the publisher as `cur=NZD`, bypassing a simple currency-tag filter.

- **Fix — Layer 2 (title keywords):** Both functions additionally reject articles whose title contains any known non-G8 CB name: Banxico, Banco de Mexico, BCB, PBOC, RBI, SARB, Norges Bank, Riksbank, NBP, CBRT, Banco Central de Chile/Colombia. This layer catches publisher mis-tags regardless of the `cur` field.
- **Fix — NARRATIVE_SYSTEM Rule 13 (G8 SCOPE):** New mandatory rule inserted before Rule 14 (was 13). Explicitly forbids the model from mentioning non-G8 central banks in the narrative body or the forward-looking close — even if a headline slips through the Python filter. Two-line example block: correct (WTI/CAD framing) vs wrong (Banxico in narrative).

BoJ passivity keeps cross bid CLOSED" — grammatically broken and hard to scan.

### Site — assets/heatmap-modal.js
- **Problem:** The Session tab rendered all four session notes (Sydney, Tokyo, London, New York) with identical visual weight regardless of whether each session had already occurred, was currently open, or had not yet started. AI-generated outlook notes for Tokyo/London/New York (e.g. "GBP/USD -0.33% session") were displayed at full brightness at 22:44 UTC when only Sydney was open, making future projections read as accomplished facts — a materially misleading presentation on a professional terminal.
- **Fix:** Added `getSessionState(sName)` — a pure front-end classification function that maps each session to one of three states at render time based on the current UTC hour and the industry-standard session close boundaries (Sydney 06:00, Tokyo 09:00, London 16:00, New York 21:00). No change to `session-context.json` schema or the Gemini prompt.
- **Rendering per state (Bloomberg/Eikon convention):**
  - `active` — blue label + `●` dot + full-brightness text. Session is open; note describes the live move.
  - `past` — muted gray label + muted gray text. Session closed; result is historical fact (same dimming Bloomberg uses for closed sessions).
  - `upcoming` — amber label + `○` dot + slightly muted text + 8px `UPCOMING` badge. Session has not opened; note is an outlook/watch, not a result.
- **Zero token impact:** Classification runs entirely in JS at render time. Gemini continues to generate all four session notes per currency in a single call; the front end decides how to style them. No prompt changes, no extra API calls.
