## v7.64.3 (2026-05-07) — generate_narrative_signals.py: fix UnboundLocalError crashing --mode structural

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Root cause:** `narrative_prompt` and `signals_prompt` were initialised inside `if RUN_INTRADAY:` (line 7981) but referenced unconditionally at lines 7991 and 8004. In `--mode structural` (`RUN_INTRADAY=False`) the assignment block was skipped, so any code path that reached those references raised `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'narrative_prompt' where it is not associated with a value`. This caused every run of `generate-structural-context.yml` to crash with exit code 1 after the change-detection pass, before writing `session-context.json` or `currency-drivers.json`. The workflow had been silently failing since at least 2026-05-06 — confirmed by the `session-context.json` timestamp stuck at 2026-05-05T08:00:08Z.
- **Fix:** Hoisted `narrative_prompt` and `signals_prompt` initialisation to unconditional scope (before the `if RUN_INTRADAY:` guard), so both variables are always bound regardless of run mode. Wrapped the entire narrative + signals execution block (Gemini call, Groq fallback, file writes) inside `if RUN_INTRADAY:` so it is genuinely skipped in structural mode — not just partially guarded. This also prevents the signals `time.sleep()` and `_write_signals()` closure from executing unnecessarily in structural-only runs.
- **Regression note:** `currency-drivers.json` being dated 2026-05-05 is **not** a bug — structural change detection correctly found no change (COT weekEnding still 2026-04-28, biasUpdated still 2026-05-04). It will auto-update when the CFTC publishes the May 5 week report (Friday 2026-05-09).

The workflow runs at 22:30 UTC, which is already the next calendar day in CEST (UTC+2). yfinance was excluding the current UTC-date's bar for European exchanges even when the session had completed hours earlier (Euronext closes ~15:30 UTC), causing `stoxx.json` to end at 2026-05-05 instead of 2026-05-06 after the May 6 run. 1H bars do not share this lag — they are available immediately after each hourly candle closes.

- **`NON_FX_SYMBOLS` unchanged:** `stoxx` remains in this set to keep it out of `FX_SYMBOLS`. The `EQUITY_1H_SYMBOLS` check runs after the FX/CME checks in `fetch_ohlc()` — routing is unambiguous.

## v7.64.0 (2026-05-07) — Inflation fetch v4.3: IMF SDMX 3.0 as G6 primary + quarterly date parser fix

### Site — scripts/fetch_inflation_expectations.py
- **New G6 primary: IMF SDMX 3.0 API** (`api.imf.org/external/sdmx/3.0`). Endpoint: `dataflow/IMF.STA/CPI/~/{ISO3}.CPI._T.IX.M`. Returns monthly CPI index for all G6 countries including Japan (which is absent from OECD DF_PRICES_ALL). YoY computed as 12-month pct change on the index series. No API key required. Lag ~4-6 weeks.
- **Root cause: JPY HTTP 404** — Japan migrated to COICOP 2018 and is only available in `DF_PRICES_N_CP01_*` dataflows, not in `DF_PRICES_ALL` (COICOP 1999). The IMF API has JPN in its CPI dataset. Fixed.
- **Root cause: AUD/NZD "no parseable rows"** — OECD returns quarterly time periods as `2024-Q4`. The v4.2 `_parse_date()` added `-01` suffix producing `2024-Q4-01`, which fails `fromisoformat`. Fixed: parser now detects `Q` in 7-char strings and converts to last month of quarter (Q1→Mar, Q2→Jun, Q3→Sep, Q4→Dec).
- **Root cause: CHF stale** — OECD last obs Dec 2025, today May 2026 = 157 days > 120d threshold. IMF monthly index resolves this since it has CHF through ~Mar 2026.
- **Source cascade updated**: IMF → OECD Explorer (with fixed parser) → FRED MEI → World Bank.

## v7.63.0 (2026-05-07) — Inflation fetch v4.2: OECD Data Explorer as G6 primary source

### Engine — scripts/fetch_inflation_expectations.py
- **Root cause of all G6 failures identified:** FRED OECD MEI series (GBRCPIALLMINMEI,
  CANCPIALLMINMEI, CHECPIALLMINMEI etc.) have a **structural ~12–14 month lag** as of 2026.
  They are updated ~annually by OECD MEI publications; FRED mirrors them without a faster
  update cycle. These series will always fail the 120-day stale guard and are not a viable
  primary source. This is not a network or parsing issue — the data simply does not exist
  beyond ~Mar/Apr 2025 in those series.
- **New G6 primary: OECD Data Explorer SDMX REST API** (`sdmx.oecd.org`). This is the
  official OECD API that replaced `stats.oecd.org` and publishes the same CPI data with
  only ~4–6 weeks lag. Dataflow: `OECD.SDD.TPS,DSD_PRICES@DF_PRICES_ALL,1.0`.
  Key pattern: `{country}.{M|Q}.N.CPI.PA._T.N.GY` (TRANSFORMATION=GY = annual % change).
  Format: `csvfilewithlabels`. No API key required.
- **AUD/NZD frequency:** quarterly (Q), all others monthly (M). Stale threshold for
  quarterly raised from 200d → 210d (one extra quarter buffer for release cycle).
- **All v4.0/v4.1 national-office API code removed** (ONS, e-Stat, ABS, StatsCan, SNB,
  Stats NZ). OECD Data Explorer covers all 6 G6 currencies from a single endpoint pattern
  with consistent parsing, eliminating per-currency brittle scrapers.
- **Output format unchanged:** patches `extended-data/{CCY}.json` updating only
  `data.inflationExpectations` and `dates.inflationExpectations`; all other fields preserved.
- **Site root argument:** script now accepts optional `argv[1]` as site root path

## v7.62.1 (2026-05-07) — Inflation fetch v4.1: fix 6 bugs from first v4.0 GHA run

### Engine — scripts/fetch_inflation_expectations.py
- **Bug 1 — headers TypeError (ABS, Stats NZ):** `_get()` hardcoded `headers=BASE_HEADERS`
  in `requests.get()`, so callers passing `headers=custom_headers` via `**kwargs` triggered
  `TypeError: got multiple values for keyword argument 'headers'`. Fixed: `_get()` now accepts
  a `custom_headers` kwarg and merges it with `BASE_HEADERS` internally; `**kwargs` no longer
  includes `headers`.
- **Bug 2 — ONS URL wrong path:** `api.ons.gov.uk/v1/datasets/mm23/timeseries/D7G7/data`
  returns 404. Correct v1 path is `/v1/timeseries/D7G7/dataset/mm23/data` (series before
  dataset). Now tries both paths sequentially.
- **Bug 3 — SNB cube ID discontinued:** `pkcpival` is no longer a valid cube.
  Correct cube: `plkopr` ("Consumer prices – total"). Switched to CSV format
  (`/api/cube/plkopr/data/csv/en`) which is more stable than the JSON endpoint.
- **Bug 4 — JPY -1.5% wrong value:** e-Stat CSV (`cpim.csv`) parser matched the first
  `総合` row in the file, which belongs to the index section (not the 前年同月比/YoY section).
  Fixed by: (a) switching primary to e-Stat REST API (statsDataId 0003427113) which returns
  structured JSON; (b) rewriting CSV fallback to first locate the `前年同月比` section header,
  then find the `総合` row within that block only; (c) adding a validity guard: `-3.0% < val < 8.0%`
  (Japan's modern CPI range — deflation floor prevents accepting implausible values).
- **Bug 5 — StatsCan WDS connection failure:** `getDataFromCubePidCoordAndLatestNPeriods` endpoint
  silently fails (likely GHA network timeout). No change to cascade position — FRED
  `CANCPIALLMINMEI` remains the immediate fallback; stale guard will skip it if >120d old.
- **Bug 6 — Stats NZ headers TypeError:** same root cause as Bug 1, fixed by same change.

## v7.61.5 (2026-05-07) — Fix OECD SDMX 422: CPALTT01.GY → CPALTT01.ST + index-to-YoY; per-currency stale thresholds

### Root cause (v2.0 regression)
`fetch_inflation_expectations.py` v2.0 used OECD SDMX key `CPALTT01.GY` — but `GY`
(growth year) is a *transformation* code, not a *MEASURE* code. The `DSD_KEI@DF_KEI,4.0`
dataflow uses a `MEASURE` dimension, not a `TRANSFORMATION` dimension. The valid measure
for the CPI series is `ST` (standardised), identical to the `IRLTLT01.ST` bond yield key
that fetch_bond_yields.py has used successfully in GHA. This mismatch caused HTTP 422
for all six G6 currencies, falling through to stale/404 FRED fallbacks.

Additionally, `CPALTT01AUM659N` and `CPALTT01NZM659N` do not exist on FRED (404), and
the other `CPALTT01*M659N` YoY-direct series ended in 2021 (stale data). The 120-day
stale guard was also too strict for AUD/NZD, whose quarterly CPI can legitimately produce
~120-day-old observations in May (Q4 data released in January).

### Site — scripts/fetch_inflation_expectations.py → v3.0
- **OECD SDMX key: `CPALTT01.GY` → `CPALTT01.ST`** — correct MEASURE code for the
  standardised CPI index series (base 2015=100). Fetches last 16 observations.
- **Added `index_to_yoy(obs)`:** Computes YoY % from index observations by finding the
  reading closest to 12 months prior (75-day tolerance, covers both monthly and quarterly).
  Identical approach to `update_extended_data.py` v13.0's `_index_to_yoy()`.
- **Added FRED MINMEI/QINMEI as cascade step 2** for G6 currencies:
  GBP→`GBRCPIALLMINMEI`, AUD→`AUSCPIALLQINMEI`, CAD→`CANCPIALLMINMEI`,
  CHF→`CHECPIALLMINMEI`, NZD→`NZLCPIALLQINMEI`. These are the active OECD MEI index
  series; `CPALTT01*M659N` YoY-direct series all ended 2021.
- **Removed non-existent FRED series:** `CPALTT01AUM659N` and `CPALTT01NZM659N` (404 —
  never existed). Replaced with `AUSCPIALLQINMEI` / `NZLCPIALLQINMEI` → index-to-YoY.
- **Per-currency stale thresholds (`MAX_AGE`):**
  - AUD/NZD: 120d → **200d** (quarterly CPI; Q4 released Jan → May run sees ~120d data,
    years with Feb release would exceed old guard).
  - GBP/JPY/CAD/CHF: unchanged at 120d.
  - USD/EUR: set to 10d (market-implied daily series; staleness here is a signal problem).
- **JPY fallback simplified:** `JPNCPIALLMINMEI` ended Jun-2021 and is not usable.
  Cascade is now: OECD SDMX → World Bank (direct, no dead FRED series).

### Site — .github/workflows/update-inflation-expectations.yml
- Updated source cascade comment to reflect v3.0 key (`CPALTT01.ST`) and MINMEI/QINMEI fallbacks.
- Commit message: `… — G8 (FRED/OECD-SDMX-ST/ECB/WB)`.

### Site — assets/real-carry-modal.js → v1.4
- Header and source comments updated: `CPALTT01 YoY` → `CPALTT01.ST index → YoY`.
  Source labels in `_RCM_IE_SRC` and `liveNote` unchanged (OECD SDMX remains accurate).

### Site — index.html
- Cache-bust: `real-carry-modal.js?v=1.3.0` → `?v=1.4.0`.

## v7.58.4 (2026-05-04) — Fix phantom candle for EuroStoxx and other non-FX indices at week open (PREPRE state not recognised as closed)

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Root cause:** `_lwBuildTodayBar()` had a non-FX phantom-bar guard that only suppressed today-bar injection when `market_state` was `'CLOSED'` or `'POSTPOST'`. Yahoo Finance returns `'PREPRE'` for European indices (EuroStoxx, FTSE, etc.) during the Sunday-night / Monday early-morning window — before their pre-market session begins. `PREPRE` was not in the allowed-closed list, so the guard was bypassed and a today-bar dated `2026-05-04` was injected using Friday's stale close/H/L, producing an extra phantom candle after the last real Friday bar.
- **Fix:** Replaced the explicit `CLOSED | POSTPOST` allowlist with a positive check: the guard now applies to **any** `market_state` that is not `'REGULAR'`. If the exchange is in an active trading session (`REGULAR`), the bar is always allowed through. For all other states (`CLOSED`, `POSTPOST`, `PREPRE`, `PRE`, `POST`, or any future undocumented state), the `lastTradeDate < dateStr` check is applied — if the last trade was on a prior date, the today-bar is suppressed. `PRE`/`POST` states are safe because their `market_time` is same-day, so the date comparison resolves to `false` and the bar is correctly shown.

## v7.58.3 (2026-05-04) — Fix FX phantom candle at Sunday-night session open (stale Yahoo dayHigh/dayLow)

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Root cause (complete diagnosis):** At the start of the FX week, `_lwBuildTodayBar()` built the today-bar using `q.high` / `q.low` from `STOOQ_RT_CACHE`, which are Yahoo's `dayHigh` / `dayLow` fields. Yahoo does **not** clear these fields at the 21:00 UTC FX session open — it keeps serving the prior Friday session's H/L range until enough intraday ticks accumulate (typically 2–4 hours into Monday). The result was a Monday today-bar with `O:157.033 H:157.326 L:155.453 C:157.033` — identical wicks to the last Friday bar (`O:156.561 H:157.326 L:155.453 C:157.033`), visually indistinguishable from a duplicate candle.
- **Fix 1 — STOOQ_RT_CACHE now stores `session_high` / `session_low`:** Added `session_high` and `session_low` from `quotes.json` to the cache object populated in `fetchQuoteBarRT()`. These fields are computed by `fetch_intraday_quotes.py` using 1H bar aggregation over the real 21:00 UTC FX session boundary, and are only present when real session activity has been recorded.
- **Fix 2 — FX today-bar H/L sourced from session data, never from stale dayH/dayL:** In `_lwBuildTodayBar()`, FX bars now use `session_high` / `session_low` when available. When session H/L are absent (as is normal at the very start of the session before 1H bars accumulate), the bar falls back to `Math.max(o, c)` / `Math.min(o, c)` — giving a narrow o/c body with no phantom wicks. Combined with the doji guard (`o===h&&h===l&&l===c`) added in the same fix, a zero-movement early-Monday bar is suppressed entirely until real price action exists.
- **Non-FX unaffected:** Non-FX instruments continue to use `q.high` / `q.low` (Yahoo `dayHigh`/`dayLow`), which are reliable for exchange-traded instruments that have a real session open broadcast.

## v7.58.2 (2026-05-03) — Fix narrative placeholders shown verbatim in frontend (Gemini path missing token resolution)

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Root cause:** `_apply_narrative_guards()` — the post-processing step for the Gemini-primary narrative path (v7.54.0) — applied safe-haven, modal verb, carry-bp, and TIER-1/2 guards but never called `resolve_tokens()` or `fix_direction_mismatch()`. The Groq path resolves tokens inside `_parse_and_process()`, but this function is not called for Gemini output. As a result, `{{gold_pct}}`, `{{spx_pct}}`, `{{dxy_pct}}`, and `{{vix}}` were written verbatim into `ai-analysis/index.json` and displayed as literal placeholder strings in the frontend narrative panel.
- **Fix:** Added Guard 4 (token resolution) to `_apply_narrative_guards()`: calls `extract_tokens_from_intraday()` (or accepts a pre-computed `tokens` dict via new optional parameter), then runs `resolve_tokens()` followed by `fix_direction_mismatch()` on the narrative string before returning. The function signature is backwards-compatible — existing call sites with no `tokens` argument are unaffected.
- **No change to Groq fallback path:** `generate_narrative()` still resolves tokens inside `_parse_and_process()` as before. The fix is scoped entirely to the Gemini path.

## v7.58.1 (2026-05-03) — Fix BTC/ETH weekend candle bugs (partial today-bar + open mismatch + weekend schedule)

### Engine — scripts/fetch_ohlc.py
- **Bug 1 — partial today-bar written for crypto on weekends:** The workflow runs Mon–Fri only (`cron: '30 22 * * 1-5'`). The crypto path used an explicit `start/end` date range with `end = tomorrow`, causing yfinance to return an in-progress bar for the current UTC day (only ~22.5h of data at the 22:30 UTC run). This partial bar was written to `btc.json` / `eth.json` and persisted all weekend with artificially truncated H/L wicks. **Fix:** strip any bar whose `time >= today_utc` before writing. dashboard.js injects the live today-bar from `quotes.json` as usual.
- **Bug 2 — candle body colour could contradict net daily direction for crypto:** The native yfinance 1D open field for crypto is the first tick of the UTC day, which sometimes diverges slightly from the previous bar's close due to exchange aggregation. This produced candle bodies where green/red did not match the actual daily pct sign. **Fix:** apply `prev_close` open correction to the crypto series (same convention already used for FX pairs and legacy 1D FX bars), with H/L clamped to maintain OHLC integrity after the open override.

### Frontend — .github/workflows/update-ohlc.yml
- **Added Sat–Sun schedule:** `30 23 * * 0,6` (23:30 UTC). BTC and ETH trade 24/7 — without a weekend run the partial Friday bar persisted all weekend. The 23:30 UTC timing ensures the UTC calendar day is nearly complete (23.5h) before `fetch_ohlc.py` strips the in-progress today-bar and writes the final JSON. All non-crypto symbols are also refreshed on each run (no additional cost — same script, same public-repo unlimited minutes).

## v7.56.0 (2026-05-02) — Add RSI, Stochastic, MACD oscillators to LW chart

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **RSI(14) sub-pane:** Relative Strength Index calculated with Wilder smoothing on close prices. Renders in a dedicated pane below the main chart with 30/50/70 reference lines. State persists across symbol switches via `window._lwOscState`.
- **Stochastic(14,3,3) sub-pane:** Fast %K smoothed to slow %K and %D. Blue line = %K, orange = %D. 20/50/80 reference lines. Standard Bloomberg/Eikon stochastic configuration.
- **MACD(12,26,9) sub-pane:** Histogram (green above / red below zero), MACD line (blue), Signal line (orange). EMA-based calculation on close prices.
- **Calculation helpers added:** `_calcRSI()`, `_calcEMA()`, `_calcMACD()`, `_calcStochastic()` — all deterministic, no `Math.random()`, mirroring standard institutional conventions.
- **Pane management:** `_buildRSIPane()`, `_buildStochPane()`, `_buildMACDPane()` cleanly remove and recreate panes on toggle. No pane leaks on symbol switch.

## v7.55.4 (2026-05-02) — Fix fetch_rates.py gap-fill: CB hold periods no longer produce stale history

### Engine — scripts/fetch_rates.py
- **Root cause identified and fixed:** `merge_observations()` used the CB source's last *decision* date as the month key. When a central bank holds its rate, the source returns the decision date (e.g. ECB SDMX returned `2025-06-11` every day for 10 months), so every daily run of `update-rates.yml` overwrote the same `2025-06` slot. Months `2025-07` through `2026-04` were never populated despite the workflow running and reporting `overallStatus: ok`. Identical issue for JPY, CHF, NZD via BIS-CBPOL (missing Apr–May 2026).
- **Fix — gap-fill in `merge_observations()`:** After building the month map, the function now walks forward from the latest populated month to today's month, filling any missing slots with the current rate. This is correct by definition: a "hold" decision means the rate was unchanged throughout. Uses stdlib date arithmetic only (`date`, integer month increment) — no `dateutil` dependency added.
- **Currencies affected:** EUR (10 months behind, most severe), JPY/CHF/NZD (1–2 months behind). USD, GBP, CAD, AUD were unaffected — their sources (NYFed-EFFR, BoE-CSV, BoC-Valet, RBA-HTML) return the current or near-current date rather than the last decision date.
- **No workflow changes needed:** `update-rates.yml` pip install line (`requests beautifulsoup4 lxml`) is sufficient — fix is stdlib-only.
- **Silent failure by design:** The workflow correctly reported `ok` because it was successfully fetching and storing the current rate — the gap was in the *history accumulation*, not the current value. No alerting change required.

## v7.54.6 (2026-05-02) — fetch_ohlc: clamp H/L after prev_close open correction

### Engine — scripts/fetch_ohlc.py (also site/scripts/fetch_ohlc.py)
- **Root cause — gap sessions produce H < O or L > O:** The FX daily bar pipeline applies a `prev_close open correction` to the full series after 1H aggregation (Bloomberg/TradingView convention: open = prior session's close). This override is correct for body color consistency but it was NOT followed by an H/L clamp. On large-gap sessions — e.g. USD/JPY on 2026-05-01 where the 21:00 UTC session opened at ~157.x but prev_close was 160.184 — the imposed open (160.184) becomes larger than the 1H session high (157.326), producing `H=157.326 < O=160.184`: an impossible candle that Lightweight Charts renders as a zero-body or inverted candle. Audit confirmed: **all 27 FX pairs affected** with multiple invalid candles in the last 10 bars each.
- **Fix applied (two locations):**
  1. `fetch_fx_ohlc_from_1h()` — full series correction loop (line ~401): after `deduped[i]["open"] = deduped[i-1]["close"]`, now adds `high = max(high, new_o)` and `low = min(low, new_o)`.
  2. `fetch_fx_ohlc_from_1h()` — legacy 1D bars correction loop (line ~378): same clamp applied.
- **Semantics — gap candle:** When FX gaps down at the 21:00 UTC session boundary (open > 1H session high), `H = open` means the candle opens at the top and closes lower — a bearish marubozu without an upper wick. When FX gaps up (open < 1H session low), `L = open` gives a bullish marubozu without a lower wick. This is the correct industry representation and matches TradingView/Bloomberg candle rendering for gapped FX sessions.
- **Double-run (21:35 + 22:30 UTC) — not the cause:** The two workflow runs are idempotent (both produce valid data; second overwrites first). The double-run did not cause the H/L violation. The bug existed in both runs identically.

---

## v7.54.4 (2026-05-02) — Squeeze guard: broaden squeeze/replace patterns + carry bp diagnosis

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Squeeze guard fix — `_sq_squeeze_re` too narrow:** Pattern only matched `"squeeze risk"` (with space + "risk"). Gemini wrote `"massive short-squeeze if..."` — hyphenated, no trailing "risk" word — causing the guard to never fire. Broadened to `r'short[- ]squeeze|squeeze\s+risk|squeeze\s+potential'` which catches all three Gemini forms. Verified: exact run text `"leaving the pair vulnerable to a massive short-squeeze if..."` now triggers correctly.
- **Squeeze guard fix — `_sq_replace_re` too narrow:** Replace pattern required trailing `"risk"` word (`short.squeeze\s+risk`). Since `_sq_squeeze_re` now matches `"short-squeeze"` without "risk", the replace pattern must also match without it. Updated to `r'(?:a\s+)?(?:massive\s+|significant\s+)?short[- ]squeeze(?:\s+risk)?'` — `(?:\s+risk)?` makes "risk" optional. Replacement: `"short-squeeze (USD/JPY downside if shorts cover)"`.
- **Carry bp 175bp — root cause confirmed (not a bug):** The `+175bp Fed-ECB` value in narrative is correct per the data files: `rates/USD.json` shows Fed=3.75% and `rates/EUR.json` shows ECB=2.00% → spread = +175bp. The guard correctly does not override it because `abs(175 - 175) = 0 < 20`. Gemini is reading the context block accurately. No fix needed — the guard is working as designed. If the carry value is stale, the fix is to update `rates/USD.json`, not the guard.
- **OIS `mkt: 0% hike priced` for RBA — deployment lag:** The Fix 2 bias/prob guard (v7.54.3) was not yet deployed when this run executed. Once v7.54.3 is deployed, `bias="hike" AND hikeProb=0` will correctly fall through to `"mkt: 100% hold priced"`.

## v7.54.3 (2026-05-02) — 3 guard fixes: carry bp pair-anchor, OIS bias/prob mismatch, squeeze crowd pattern

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Fix 1 — Carry bp guard: pair-anchor pass (narrative guard):** The v7.54.2 carry bp guard only matched hardcoded bp values when Gemini included explicit CB pair names (`Fed-ECB`, `BoE-Fed`, etc.) in the surrounding text. The failing run showed `"+175bp carry disadvantage"` near `"EUR/USD"` with no CB names — the guard silently skipped it. Added a second pass (Pass B) that detects `"[+]Nbp carry [dis]advantage"` within ±150 chars of a pair name (`EUR/USD`, `GBP/USD`, etc.) and replaces with the exact bp from `rates/*.json`. The `dis` prefix is preserved so `"175bp carry disadvantage"` becomes `"+233bp carry disadvantage"` (not `"+233bp carry advantage"`). Expected log: `INFO _apply_narrative_guards: carry bp 175bp → +233bp via pair anchor (EUR/USD)`.
- **Fix 2 — OIS injection: bias/probability mismatch guard:** `meetings.json` can have `bias="hike"` with `hikeProb=0` when market pricing has repriced away from a hike but the bias tag wasn't updated (e.g. RBA after a data miss). Previous code: `if bias == "hike": show "{hikeProb}% hike priced"` → produced `"mkt: 0% hike priced"` (misleading — implies hike is priced but at 0%). Fix: added probability check to all three bias branches. New logic: `if bias=="hike" AND hikeProb > 0` → hike label; `elif bias=="cut" AND cutProb > 0` → cut label; else → hold label. Verified: `bias=hike, hikeProb=0` → `"mkt: 100% hold priced"`.
- **Fix 3 — Squeeze direction guard: crowd pattern + dir pattern + replacement rewrite:** Three sub-fixes. (a) `_sq_crowd_re` expanded from `"crowded short"` only to also match `"net short of -NNN,NNN"` and `"massive short"` — Gemini writes `"COT net short of -88,543"` without the word "crowded", causing the guard to silently skip JPY signals. (b) `_sq_dir_re` was self-matching `"short-squeeze risk"` (the trigger phrase) as a direction hit, preventing the guard from ever firing on Gemini output. Rewrote to only match explicit direction statements: `"USD/JPY downside"`, `"downside if shorts cover"`, `"shorts cover"`. (c) `_sq_replace_re` updated to match `"a massive short-squeeze risk"` / `"significant short-squeeze risk"` / `"short-squeeze risk"` (full phrase), with replacement `"short-squeeze risk (USD/JPY downside if shorts cover)"`. Also fixed: compiled pattern + `flags=` kwarg raises `TypeError` at runtime — removed `flags=_rg.IGNORECASE` from `.sub()` call (flags already set at compile time). Expected log: `INFO _apply_signal_guards squeeze: disambiguated in 'USD/JPY — G8 Bilateral Theme +'`.

## v7.54.2 (2026-05-02) — Bug fixes: OIS NoneType crash + narrative carry bp guard

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Critical crash fix — OIS probability `NoneType` subtraction (line 1447):** `_apply_signal_guards` Guard 5 (OIS injection) read `hikeProb` and `cutProb` from `meetings.json` using `.get("hikeProb", 0)` / `.get("cutProb", 0)`. When the meetings.json for a currency has an explicit `null` JSON value (e.g. `"hikeProb": null`), Python's `.get()` returns `None` — not the `0` default — because the key is present. The subsequent `100 - _hike_prob - _cut_prob` raised `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'int' and 'NoneType'`, crashing the entire run at the signals write step. Fix: changed to `_meet.get("hikeProb") or 0` / `_meet.get("cutProb") or 0` — `or 0` coerces both `None` and falsy values to `0`. Confirmed by run log: `"mkt: 100% hold priced"` for ECB and `"mkt: 40% hike priced"` for BoJ were injected correctly before the crash, so the logic itself is correct — only the None guard was missing.
- **Narrative carry bp guard (Guard 4 in `_apply_narrative_guards`):** Added deterministic post-processing to correct stale bp values in Gemini narrative output. When Gemini writes a hardcoded carry bp value (e.g. `+175bp`) near a CB pair mention (`Fed-ECB`, `Fed-BoE`, etc.) that differs from the actual computed value by ≥20bp, the guard replaces it with the exact bp from `rates/*.json` — the same source as the `CROSS_CARRY` context block. Trigger: run v7.54.0 showed `"a +175bp Fed-ECB carry advantage"` in the narrative despite the context block containing the correct `+233bp` value. Root cause: Gemini reads the context block for signals (which has per-signal rate guards) but narrative generation appears to prioritise training-memory values when the carry block is present but not referenced in a concrete example. The guard fires post-generation and corrects the value before write, logging `INFO _apply_narrative_guards: carry bp +175bp → +233bp (USD/EUR)`.

## v7.54.1 (2026-05-02) — Bug fix: _apply_narrative_guards modal regex + guard wiring audit

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Modal regex bug fix in `_apply_narrative_guards`:** `_VB` pattern used a non-capturing group `(?:...)` but replacement strings used `` backreference — this raised `re.error: invalid group reference` at runtime, silently breaking Guard 2 (modal verb sanitizer) for all Gemini-primary narrative output. Fix: changed `_VB` to a capturing group `(...)` and introduced a `_adv_vb_repl` lambda for the ADV+VB case (where the verb is `m.lastindex`, not ``). ## v7.53.8 (2026-05-02) — 5 institutional-quality guards: carry bp, adverb-bridged modals, OIS probability injection, squeeze direction

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Fix 1+2 — USD major pair carry pre-computed (eliminates hallucinated 175bp):** `CROSS_CARRY` block extended to include all USD major pairs (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, AUD/USD, NZD/USD, USD/CAD, USD/CHF, USD/JPY) listed first, so the LLM always receives the exact bp spread from rates/*.json before seeing any example. Root cause: `CROSS_CARRY` previously only covered JPY and CHF crosses — Groq had no pre-computed carry for EUR/USD and copied the hardcoded `175bp` from the prompt example. With Fed 4.33% vs ECB 2.00%, the actual spread is +233bp; the LLM now reads that number directly from the context block. The carry block note explicitly instructs: `"Never use training-memory rates to compute carry spreads — always use values above."` The prompt example was also changed to remove the hardcoded `175bp` value and reference the data block instead.
- **Fix 3 — Adverb-bridged modal patterns (`may further impact`, `may also influence`):** `_MODAL_SUBS` (pre-Groq) and Guard G (post-Gemini) only matched `may [verb]` with the verb immediately adjacent. The adverb `further`, `also`, `still`, `now`, `soon`, `yet`, `already`, `again`, `ultimately`, `additionally`, `potentially` between `may` and the verb caused the pattern to miss. Added adverb-bridging regex group to all three modal guard locations (pre-Groq narrative, pre-Groq signals, post-Gemini Guard G). Pattern: `may\s+(?:further|also|...)\s+[verb]` → `is likely to [verb]`. Verified: `"may further impact USD direction"` → `"is likely to impact USD direction"`.
- **Fix 4 — OIS probability injection guard:** New post-processing pass that detects signal text containing `"next [CB] meeting"` without an adjacent market-implied probability (e.g., `mkt: 88%`), then injects the OIS probability from `meetings.json`. Result: `"next BoE meeting"` → `"next BoE meeting (mkt: 88% hold priced)"`, `"next BoJ meeting"` → `"next BoJ meeting (mkt: 30% hike priced)"`. Without this, the meeting reference was editorial rather than institutional — Bloomberg always includes the OIS-implied probability alongside a CB meeting reference.
- **Fix 5 — Squeeze direction disambiguation for USD/JPY:** `"crowded short -88.5k sets up squeeze risk"` was directionally ambiguous — a crowded JPY short implies a short-squeeze would rally JPY = USD/JPY downside, but the original signal framed it as a USD/JPY upside thesis. Guard added: when a signal contains both `"crowded short"` and `"squeeze risk"` without an explicit direction note, replaces `"sets up squeeze risk"` with `"sets up short-squeeze risk (USD/JPY downside if shorts cover)"`. Mirrors Bloomberg's standard for disambiguating COT crowding signals.

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

Gemini now corrects ONLY: (1) COT direction inverted, (2) yield advantage wrong, (3) CB rate/probability confused, (4) directional incoherence. Positive examples in the prompt are more effective at preventing errors than Python regex guards applied after the fact.
- **Fix 3 — Stale-date regex now catches "and next meeting on [date]":** Guards D (pre-Gemini) and Guard D-post (post-Gemini) used a pattern requiring a CB name immediately before "meeting" — e.g. `BoE meeting on 30 Apr`. - **Fix 4 — Modal whitelists extended with 10 missing verbs:** `keep`, `introduce`, `stabilize`, `prevent`, `accelerate`, `delay`, `reinforce`, `amplify`, `reduce`, `increase`, `narrow`, `widen`, `close` added to `_NARR_MODAL_FX_VERBS` (narrative), `_MODAL_SUBS` (pre-Gemini signals), and `_PGG_VERBS` (Guard G post-Gemini). ## v7.53.0 (2026-05-01) — Gemini audit: data quarantine + hallucination guard

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Root cause (hallucinated values):** `audit_signals_with_gemini()` passed the full 11k-char context to Gemini. Gemini would "find" numbers anywhere in the block (G8 correlations, cross-asset data, headlines) and introduce them into signal text, or fall back to training memory when confused (e.g. "JGB 2.42%", "GBP/FTSE +0.327"). The previous "DO NOT ADD" instruction was insufficient.
- **Fix 1 — `_build_gemini_fact_block()`:** New function that builds a compact (~40-line), structured fact-check block containing only the values Gemini needs: CB rates + next meeting date + hike/cut probabilities, bond yields, COT net positions + direction flags, and FX spot levels. Gemini receives this instead of the full context. Context shrinks from 11k to ~1.5k chars, dramatically reducing the search space for hallucination.
- **Fix 2 — Strengthened `_GEMINI_AUDIT_SYSTEM` prompt:** Replaced generic "NEVER introduce data" rule with a STRICT DATA QUARANTINE section listing 6 explicit prohibitions. Added CLASS 4 — DIRECTIONAL INCOHERENCE: detects signals that state two opposite directions (e.g. "yield gap limits JPY upside … sustained JPY bid") and instructs Gemini to keep the dominant driver and delete the contradiction without adding content. Added explicit past-date handling: if a CB meeting date in the block is before CURRENT UTC DATE, write "next [CB] meeting" without a date.
- **Fix 3 — Post-audit hallucination guard:** After Gemini returns corrected signals, a Python validator checks every X.XX% value introduced by Gemini against an authoritative set built from `rates/*.json`, `extended-data/*.json`, and `meetings-data/meetings.json`. Any value not in the set and not present in the original signal is flagged; that signal is reverted to the Groq original with a WARNING log. Prevents hallucinated yields/correlations from reaching production regardless of prompt compliance.

Root cause: the second branch of the alternation had no CB name anchor. Effect: `BoC 40% → 0%`, `BoJ 0% → 40%`, `Fed 40% → 0%` all firing on the AUD/USD signal. Tested: `BoC`/`BoJ` no longer match an RBA signal; `RBA` correctly matches `RBA hike bias (40% priced)`.
- **Advisory stripper — duplicate phrase guard (new patterns):** Added three patterns to collapse adjacent duplicate phrases produced when `for this trade → as the key catalyst` replacement runs on a sentence that already contains `as the key catalyst`. Catches `"as the key catalyst as the key catalyst"` → `"as the key catalyst"`.
- **Empty title guard (new):** Signals with `title: ""` are now caught before appending to results. Fallback derives the title from the first FX pair found in the signal text (e.g. `"EUR/USD — Market Update"`), or `"FX Market Update"` if no pair is found. Logs a WARNING. Prevents blank signal cards in the frontend.

### .github/workflows/generate-ai-narrative.yml
- Added `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY_2`, `GEMINI_API_KEY_5` to the `env:` block of the run step — required for `load_gemini_keys()` to pick up secrets. Updated the secrets documentation comment at the top of the file.

## v7.52.0 (2026-05-02) — Gemini 2.5 Flash as institutional auditor (second-pass corrector)

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Architecture:** Groq (llama-3.3-70b) remains the primary signal generator. Gemini 2.5 Flash is added as a second-pass auditor that receives the Groq-generated signals and corrects specific error classes — it does not regenerate from scratch.
- **`GEMINI_URL` / `GEMINI_MODEL` constants:** `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-04-17` via `generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta` (free tier: 10 RPM, 250 RPD, 250k TPM).
- **`load_gemini_keys()`:** Reads `GEMINI_API_KEY` … `GEMINI_API_KEY_5` from env vars — same pool pattern as `load_groq_keys()`. Add keys to GitHub Actions secrets.
- **`call_gemini()`:** `generateContent` endpoint wrapper. Mirrors `call_groq` error-tag convention (`DAILY_LIMIT` / `RATE_LIMIT` / `INVALID_KEY`) for uniform handling. Temperature 0.15 (conservative — auditor must not drift). Retries on 429 with `retry-after` header or 30s default.
- **`_GEMINI_AUDIT_SYSTEM`:** Focused audit prompt (~600 tokens vs 2,400 for SIGNALS_SYSTEM_CLOSED). Two correction classes only: (1) factual errors — COT direction inversion, yield advantage inversion, carry spread wrong currency, CB rate vs hike probability confusion, directional incoherence; (2) substandard institutional language — CB bias terminology, vague editorial, first person. Explicit DO NOT CHANGE list preserves signal structure and correct theses.
- **`audit_signals_with_gemini()`:** Runs after `call_with_key_rotation` returns Groq signals. Merges corrected fields (text, title, evidence, priority) back onto original signal objects, preserving all metadata. Validates priority field against `{critical, warning, info}`. Logs count of revised signals. Full fallback on any error — audit layer never blocks publication.
- **Pipeline wiring:** Audit runs **only in `market_closed=True` mode** (pre-open weekend setups — highest hallucination risk, no live prices to anchor the LLM). Skipped in live-market mode to conserve the 250 RPD free-tier quota.
- **Failure handling:** Per-key rotation on `DAILY_LIMIT`/`RATE_LIMIT`. Non-retryable errors (400, parse failure, invalid JSON) fall back to Groq output immediately without consuming additional keys.

### Setup required
- Obtain one or more Gemini API keys from [aistudio.google.com](https://aistudio.google.com)
- Add to GitHub Actions secrets: `GEMINI_API_KEY`, optionally `GEMINI_API_KEY_2` … `GEMINI_API_KEY_5`
- No workflow YAML changes needed — keys are read at runtime

## v7.51.0 (2026-05-02) — Architecture: prompt compression + expanded Python post-processors

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Root cause diagnosed:** `SIGNALS_SYSTEM_CLOSED` contained 17,394 chars (~4,350 tokens) with 28 constraints and 12 WRONG/CORRECT example pairs. At a 7.5:1 instruction-to-output token ratio, llama-3.3-70b was experiencing attention diffusion — later rules received less attention weight, causing inconsistent compliance. The fix is architectural: rules enforceable deterministically in Python belong in Python, not in the system prompt.
- **Prompt compression:** `SIGNALS_SYSTEM_CLOSED` reduced from 17,394 → 9,622 chars (−45%). Removed all mechanical text-transformation rules. Retained only 5 rules requiring LLM judgment: directional coherence, COT direction logic, yield advantage accuracy, carry pair accuracy, CB rate vs hike probability.
- **Expanded advisory/style stripper (Python, zero tokens):** Added 35 deterministic patterns covering the full rule set removed from the prompt: CB terminology (neutral/closed/on-hold bias → Hold bias for all 9 CB names), pair convention (JPY/EUR, JPY/GBP, JPY/AUD), investment advice (go long/short, buy the dip, sell the rally, entry point, take profit, stop loss, reduce exposure, add risk, cut positions), vague editorial (will be crucial, worth watching closely, setup is compelling), first person (we see, we view, our view).
- **Principle:** Python enforces format; LLM generates substance. This reduces Groq attention load and improves compliance on rules that require reasoning.

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

  institutional quality standards due to three prompt deficiencies:
  (1) STYLE section provided "USD/JPY Watch" and "EUR Setup" as title examples — the LLM copied

- **Fix B — COT EXTREME MANDATORY RULE:** Any G8 currency with |COT LF net| ≥ 30,000 contracts

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Fix 1 — SIGNALS_SYSTEM_CLOSED — "for this trade" and investment advice language:**
  Added explicit FORBIDDEN phrases list covering all prescriptive/advisory language: `"for this trade"`,

## v7.50.10 (2026-05-01) — Fix: signals always return [] due to missing result.append in post-processing loop

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Root cause:** `generate_signals()` builds a `result = []` list and runs every signal through a post-processing loop (`for i, s in enumerate(signals)`) that applies the VIX safety net, weekend verb sanitizer, CB rate stale-training guard, and hike/cut probability guard. The loop had no `result.append(s)` at its end — it processed and discarded every signal, leaving `result` permanently empty. `generate_signals()` therefore always returned `[]` regardless of how many signals Groq produced or how many COT-OIS enforcement signals were added. This caused the entire signals path to fall into the "degenerate response" retry loop on every single run, burning through all pool keys before ultimately preserving the previous signals.json unchanged.
- **Fix:** Added `result.append({**s, "time": time_str, "text": signal_text, "title": ..., "evidence": evidence, "priority": priority})` at the end of the processing loop. The append merges all post-processed field values (sanitized text, corrected time, validated evidence, normalized priority) into the final dict. This is the pattern the loop was clearly designed to implement — the append was missing from an earlier refactor.

## v7.50.9 (2026-05-01) — Fix: workflow crash from invalid nonlocal + commit step abort on missing structural files

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Root cause (SyntaxError):** The previous fix in v7.50.7 used `nonlocal _signals_tokens_used` inside `_tracked_call_groq()`. `nonlocal` requires a binding in an immediately enclosing *function* scope — but `_signals_tokens_used` is a module-level global, not a local variable of `generate_signals()`. Python raises `SyntaxError: no binding for nonlocal '_signals_tokens_used' found` at import time, crashing the entire script before any code runs. This caused every scheduled run to fail with exit code 1.
- **Fix:** Changed `nonlocal _signals_tokens_used` → `global _signals_tokens_used` in `_tracked_call_groq()`. The variable lives at module scope; `global` is the correct declaration for a nested function to write to it. The two other `nonlocal _cur_key_idx` usages elsewhere in the file remain correct because `_cur_key_idx` is defined as a local variable of its enclosing function.

### Engine — .github/workflows/generate-ai-narrative.yml
- **Root cause (commit step abort):** The "Commit and push" step unconditionally `cp`-ed five files — including `currency-drivers.json` and `session-context.json` — into `/tmp/ai_analysis_fresh/`. Those two files are written exclusively by `mode=structural` (i.e. `generate-structural-context.yml`, 1×/day). Since this workflow runs `mode=intraday`, those files are never written by this run. If they were absent from the checked-out public repo (first run ever, or after repo reset), `cp` exits with code 1 and the entire commit step fails — the freshly generated `index.json` and `signals.json` are never pushed.
- **Fix:** Guarded the `cp` and restore of `currency-drivers.json` and `session-context.json` with `[ -f ... ] &&` existence checks in both the initial save to `/tmp` and the per-retry restore inside the push loop. The `git add` for those two files also uses `2>/dev/null || true` so a not-yet-existing file doesn't abort staging. The three intraday-owned files (`index.json`, `signals.json`, `context_snapshot.json`) remain unconditional.

## v7.50.7 (2026-05-01) — Fix: signals crash with UnboundLocalError on _signals_tokens_used

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Root cause:** `_tracked_call_groq()` is a nested function inside `generate_signals()`. The outer function declares `global _signals_tokens_used`, but Python's scoping rules do not propagate `global` declarations into nested functions. Because `_tracked_call_groq` contains `_signals_tokens_used += ...` (an augmented assignment), Python treats `_signals_tokens_used` as a local variable of the nested function. Reading it before the assignment completes raises `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable '_signals_tokens_used' where it is not associated with a value`. This caused the entire signals generation path to throw an exception on the very first `_tracked_call_groq` call, falling back to the 5 preserved previous signals every run.
- **Fix:** Added `nonlocal _signals_tokens_used` as the first line of `_tracked_call_groq`. This correctly binds the nested function's reference to the enclosing `generate_signals` scope where the variable lives, matching the pattern already used elsewhere in the file (`nonlocal _cur_key_idx` in lines 1850 and 2879).

## v7.50.3 (2026-05-01) — Fix: DXY, WTI, Gold Apr 30 bar mislabeled as Apr 29 (session-open-date shift) + OHLC cache strategy fix

### Engine — scripts/fetch_ohlc.py
- **Root cause:** yfinance native 1D bars for futures that open before UTC midnight (ICE DXY at 22:00 UTC, CME WTI/Gold at 23:00 UTC) are timestamped by session **open** date, not session **close** date. The Apr 30 trading session (opened Apr 29 evening, closed Apr 30) was stored as `"2026-04-29"` in the JSON. The chart displayed it one day early. Meanwhile the `"2026-04-30"` slot contained the partial May 1 in-progress session (~30 min of data), resulting in a tiny-range stub bar on Apr 30 in the chart.
- **Fix — `SESSION_OPEN_DATE_SYMBOLS = {'dxy', 'wti', 'gold'}`:** New constant identifying symbols where yfinance uses session open date as the bar label. In the non-FX fetch loop, dates for these symbols are shifted forward by one business day via the new `_next_bday()` helper (`date + 1 day`, skipping Saturday → Monday). This maps each bar to its correct trading/close date. The last bar (partial in-progress session) is now correctly dated tomorrow, so `dashboard.js`'s strip-last-bar removes it and replaces it with live data from `quotes.json` — the existing intended design unchanged.
- **`_next_bday(d)` helper:** Added. Adds 1 calendar day, then adds 2 more if the result is Saturday (Friday session → Monday label). Sunday inputs cannot occur (futures only trade Mon–Fri).
- **Dedup comment updated:** Prior comment incorrectly described a duplicate-date scenario for DXY/WTI/Gold. After the date shift, no duplicate dates occur — dedup comment updated to reflect the actual behaviour.
- **Version bump:** script header updated to `v1.6`.

### Frontend — sw.js
- **Root cause of "no visual change" after JSON update:** `/ohlc-data/` was missing from `DATA_PATH_PREFIXES`. The service worker treated OHLC JSON files as static shell assets (cache-first strategy), so updated JSONs were never fetched from the network — the browser served stale cached versions indefinitely.
- **Fix:** `/ohlc-data/` added to `DATA_PATH_PREFIXES`. OHLC JSON files now use the network-first strategy (fresh data preferred, cache as offline fallback) — identical to all other data endpoints.
- **`CACHE_VERSION` bumped to `gi-v7.50.5`:** Forces the activate event to delete the old `gi-v7.50.4` caches across all active clients, ensuring no user is left with stale OHLC data from the incorrect cache bucket.

### Frontend — index.html
- **Version query param updated:** `dashboard.js?v=7.50.4` → `?v=7.50.5` to stay in sync with the new service worker cache version.

## v7.50.2 (2026-04-29) — Fix: Gold chart stub bars eliminated via CME 1H session reconstruction

### Site — scripts/fetch_ohlc.py
- **Root cause audit:** yfinance native 1D bars for `GC=F` (Gold front-month futures) had a 46% stub-bar rate — bars where `O==H` or `O==L` because Yahoo constructs them from CME settlement ticks, not from the full COMEX electronic session. This caused the Gold LW chart to render with flat candle bodies and distorted wicks, matching the appearance in the screenshot reported.
- **New function `fetch_gold_ohlc_from_1h()`:** Same hybrid 1H-aggregation pattern as `fetch_fx_ohlc_from_1h()` but with the CME COMEX session boundary: **22:00 UTC → 22:00 UTC** (17:00 ET fixed, EST/winter convention, matching Bloomberg, CME Group charts, and TradingView Gold daily candles). Hours 00–21 UTC belong to the session closing today; hours 22–23 UTC open the next session (closes tomorrow). Saturdays are dropped (CME Gold closes Friday 17:00 ET, reopens Sunday 18:00 ET). No `prev_close` open correction — Gold futures have a genuine electronic open at 18:00 ET, not a continuous market. No back-adjustment — roll gaps appear as-is (institutional front-month standard).
- **`GOLD_SYMBOLS = {'gold'}`** added as a separate routing set. `NON_FX_SYMBOLS` no longer contains `'gold'`. `FX_SYMBOLS` computed as `SYMBOLS - NON_FX_SYMBOLS - GOLD_SYMBOLS`. `fetch_ohlc()` dispatch: FX → `fetch_fx_ohlc_from_1h`, Gold → `fetch_gold_ohlc_from_1h`, everything else → native 1D.
- **WTI unaffected:** audit found only 2% stub-bar rate for `CL=F` (WTI has a cleaner Yahoo 1D feed). No change to WTI fetch path.
- **Version bump:** script header updated to `v1.4`.

## v7.50.1 (2026-04-29) — Fix: narrative hidden on page load due to chart scrollIntoView on boot

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Root cause:** `loadTVChart()` called `scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' })` on `#section-fxpairs` after rendering the chart. On page load, this call is triggered by the `IntersectionObserver` in `initTVWidgets` when `#tv-chart-wrap` enters the viewport — which it does immediately in split layout. The result: `#split-upper` was always scrolled down to the chart on reload, hiding the narrative.
- **Fix 1 — `_chartAutoLoad` flag:** Added a module-level `let _chartAutoLoad = true` flag. `loadTVChart()` reads it, stores it locally as `skipScroll`, then immediately clears it to `false`. The initial auto-load skips all three `scrollIntoView` branches. All subsequent user-initiated loads (tab click, quote bar, keyboard navigation) have `_chartAutoLoad = false` and scroll normally.
- **Fix 2 — `resetSplitUpperScroll` safety net:** After `applyState()` runs in `initSplitLayout`, an IIFE explicitly sets `upper.scrollTop = 0` and repeats after 400 ms to catch any async layout shifts from the TradingView iframe loading. Ensures narrative is visible even if the browser restores scroll position from session history.

### Engine — .github/workflows/update-ff-calendar.yml

Exits 0 on success or exhaustion — push collision is not a real failure; next run delivers fresh data.

### Engine — .github/workflows/update-frankfurter-cache.yml

### Engine — .github/workflows/update-saxo-rr.yml
- **Full rewrite of push step:** Previous implementation used bare `git pull --rebase && git push` with no retry loop and no exit handling — a push failure would silently exit 1 (or 0 on success with no retry). Replaced with canonical 5-attempt hard-reset loop. Added timestamp to commit message for auditability.

### Engine — .github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml
- **Canonical retry loop:** Replaced 3-attempt `git pull --rebase` loop (no sleep, exit 0 on exhaustion) with the standard 5-attempt hard-reset pattern with linear backoff. Timestamp extracted pre-loop for consistent commit messages.

Rule is additive (not a required token) — fires only at threshold levels.

Includes CORRECT/WRONG examples with the USD Sydney note from the failing run (the headline "Dollar Gains on Weak Stocks and Soaring Crude Prices" was the driver — the note "USD/JPY +0.11%. Fed on hold." contained zero of that information).
- **`DRIVERS_SYSTEM` Rule 4b — COT DATA FIDELITY:** New rule explicitly prohibiting the use of training-memory COT values. The failure mode was the model writing "JPY COT LF short -65.3k" (stale training value) when the CFTC data block showed lev_net=-80,578. Rule names the failure mode, gives the process (re-read the CFTC block before writing any COT reference), and includes a CORRECT/WRONG example anchored to the exact JPY values from the failing run.

Chained after `_sanitize_driver_notes()` in the drivers generation flow. Logs corrections with old → new value for auditability.

Bond vol above 100 signals elevated rate uncertainty that compounds carry unwind risk — a layer that institutional desks (Goldman, JPM) routinely include in signals but was absent from the system.

## v7.48.5 (2026-04-27) — Fix FX daily OHLC: build daily bars from 1H aggregation over NY session boundary

### Engine — scripts/fetch_ohlc.py (site repo)
- **Root cause of incorrect FX candle wicks:** Yahoo Finance's native `interval="1d"` FX bars use a UTC midnight (00:00–24:00 UTC) cutoff — not a real FX session boundary. This causes the reported High/Low values to be materially wrong: intraday price extremes that occur between 17:00 NY (≈21:00 UTC) and 00:00 UTC appear in the prior day's bar, while extremes between 00:00 UTC and 17:00 NY appear in the following day's bar. The result is that candle wicks are systematically too short or too long — visible when comparing the terminal's FX daily chart against Yahoo Finance's own 4H chart (which correctly reflects intraday session ranges) or against TradingView and Bloomberg FX daily candles.
- **Industry-standard fix — 1H bar aggregation:** Added `fetch_fx_ohlc_from_1h()` which downloads 1H bars (yfinance supports up to 730 days of 1H data) and aggregates them over the correct FX session boundary: **21:00 UTC → 21:00 UTC** (≈ 17:00 New York → 17:00 New York). This is the session boundary used by Bloomberg, TradingView, and Reuters for all FX daily bar construction. The aggregated Open = first 1H bar's open, High = max of all intraday 1H highs, Low = min of all intraday 1H lows, Close = last 1H bar's close. The resulting daily bars exactly match what Yahoo Finance shows on its own 4H/1H charts.
- **Hybrid history:** yfinance caps 1H data at 730 days. For history older than 730 days, native 1D bars are used with the existing `prev_close` open correction (unchanged). The crossover is seamless — only H/L differ between the two methods, and the 1H-aggregated portion (the most recent ~2 years, which users predominantly view) is always faithful to real session ranges.
- **`fetch_ohlc()` now delegates:** All FX symbols (majors and crosses) route through `fetch_fx_ohlc_from_1h()`. Non-FX symbols (Gold, WTI, BTC, SPX, Nikkei, DXY, etc.) continue using native 1D bars, which are correct for exchange-listed assets with fixed session hours.
- **Candle open convention preserved:** After aggregation, each bar's open is set to the prior bar's close (`prev_close` convention). This guarantees candle body color always matches the daily pct sign — consistent with Bloomberg and TradingView FX daily rendering, and with the `_lwBuildTodayBar()` convention in `dashboard.js`.
- **Performance note:** Each FX symbol now makes 2 yfinance calls (1H + 1D) instead of 1. The polite `sleep(0.4)` between symbols is unchanged. Total runtime increase is bounded by the number of FX symbols (~28) × 0.4s ≈ 11s — acceptable within the workflow timeout.

## v7.48.0 (2026-04-27) — Frontend audit: disclosure, data integrity, and NZD IV dynamic ratio

### Frontend — index.html
- **Reference Spreads panel — methodology tooltip added:** The panel title now carries a `title=` attribute explaining that values are model-derived indicative estimates (ECN floor + HV30 × vol coefficient × VIX stress multiplier), calibrated against published ECN averages, and that they are not tradeable quotes. ### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Myfxbook avg deposit tooltip: removed hardcoded `$96K` claim.** The tooltip for the "Average deposit" stat in the Myfxbook sentiment panel contained the literal string `'$96K average suggests the sample skews toward serious traders…'`. The displayed `avgDep` value is live from the Myfxbook API and changes over time; the tooltip comment was a snapshot that would silently become stale. Replaced with a framing-neutral statement: `'Higher average deposit values indicate more experienced or semi-professional traders — data from larger accounts carries more statistical weight.'` Addresses audit finding #2.
- **NZD/USD ATM IV proxy: replaced hardcoded `× 1.08` with dynamic HV30-derived ratio.** Both occurrences (`fetchOptionSkew` and `updatePairDetail`) previously used a fixed scalar `1.08` (NZD/AUD long-run realised-vol ratio, computed once and never updated). This ratio drifts after RBNZ or RBA rate cycles shift the relative volatility regime — e.g. the 2024–2025 RBNZ aggressive cut cycle compressed NZD realized vol relative to AUD, making 1.08 stale. The fix replaces the constant with `Math.min(1.30, Math.max(0.90, HV30['nzdusd'] / HV30['audusd']))` from `quotes.json`, updated with every intraday refresh (~5 min). This is the standard sell-side methodology (Bloomberg BVOL NZD/AUD realized vol ratio). The clamp `[0.90, 1.30]` prevents outlier distortion during flash-crash episodes. Falls back to `1.08` if `quotes.json` HV30 data is unavailable. Tooltip updated to describe the dynamic ratio methodology. Addresses audit finding #3.

### Engine — scripts/fetch_ohlc.py (site repo)
- **Panama back-adjustment removed:** The previous session had added a proportional backward-pass adjustment (Panama method) to eliminate contract roll gaps in GC=F and CL=F. This was incorrect for a market monitoring terminal: Panama produces synthetic price levels that were never actually traded. Bloomberg `CL1 Comdty` and TradingView `CL1!` use back-adjustment only for their continuous-contract analytical instruments, explicitly documenting that prices are artificial. A monitoring terminal must show real front-month traded prices — the actual settlement price each day — exactly as Reuters Eikon, CNBC, Barchart, and Investing.com do. Concretely: WTI traded above $100 in early April 2026; Panama had rewritten those levels downward to ~$96 to make the series artificially continuous. Removed entirely.
- **HL_MAX_SPREAD guard removed for gold and wti:** The guard (`gold: 4%`, `wti: 8%`) was designed to drop dual-contract artifact bars where yfinance blends two front-month contracts into one bar with an impossible H/L range. However, during the Strait of Hormuz crisis WTI legitimately traded with 8–15% daily ranges and Gold with 4–6% daily ranges. The guard was silently dropping real trading sessions — March 2026 alone had 14 of 22 WTI bars dropped; Jan–Feb 2026 had 13 Gold bars dropped — leaving multi-day gaps in the chart. With Panama removed, any genuine artifact bar would appear as a spike, which matches how Bloomberg and TradingView handle the raw front-month series. The `dxy: 5%` guard is retained since DXY has no roll artifact pattern of this kind and genuinely cannot move 5% intraday.
- **Net result:** `fetch_ohlc.py` now delivers real, unmodified front-month OHLC prices for WTI and Gold, matching the standard of institutional data terminals. Roll gaps appear as market events (contract switch), not as data errors.

## v7.47.13 (2026-04-27) — Fix fetch_ohlc.py: end date off-by-one excludes today's and weekend bars

### Engine — scripts/fetch_ohlc.py (site repo)
- **Root cause:** yfinance's `ticker.history(start=..., end=...)` treats `end` as **exclusive** — the date passed as `end` is not included in the result. `_end = datetime.now(timezone.utc)` resolves to `2026-04-27`, so the download range was effectively `[2023-04-26, 2026-04-27)` — stopping at `2026-04-26`. Because `2026-04-26` is a Sunday and yfinance appears to require a complete UTC day to close before including it, the last bar returned was `2026-04-25` (Friday). Saturday Apr 26 and Sunday Apr 27 were both missing.
- **Fix:** Changed `_end = datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(days=1)`. With `end=2026-04-28`, the exclusive range becomes `[start, 2026-04-28)`, which includes today (Apr 27) and yesterday (Apr 26 — Saturday). The daily workflow will now deliver a complete JSON including the current partial-day bar and the prior weekend bars.
- **`dashboard.js` gap-fill (v7.47.12) remains as defense-in-depth:** Even with the corrected `end` date, there will always be a window between the last workflow run and the user's page load. The gap-fill ensures the chart shows no whitespace during that window.

## v7.47.11 (2026-04-27) — Fix BTC/ETH OHLC missing weekend bars (root cause of chart gap)

### Engine — scripts/fetch_ohlc.py
- **Root cause:** `ticker.history(period="3y", interval="1d")` applies yfinance's default NYSE/NASDAQ business-day calendar filter, which silently drops all Saturday and Sunday bars for every symbol — including BTC and ETH, which trade 24/7. The OHLC JSON files therefore had no bars for the weekend (e.g. Apr 25–26), causing the visual jump from Friday's close directly to Monday's open that appeared as a gap on the chart. The v7.47.9 LWC timestamp fix was correct (prevents LWC from collapsing weekends visually) but had nothing to render because the data was missing.
- **Fix:** Added `CRYPTO_SYMBOLS = {'btc', 'eth'}` constant. For crypto symbols, `fetch_ohlc()` now calls `ticker.history(start=..., end=..., ...)` with an explicit 3-year date range instead of `period="3y"`. yfinance only applies the business-day calendar when `period=` is used; explicit `start`/`end` passes dates directly to the Yahoo Finance API and returns all calendar days including Saturday and Sunday.
- **Non-crypto unchanged:** All FX pairs, Gold, WTI, SPX, indices continue to use `period="3y"` — weekends have no meaningful price data for those instruments.

## v7.47.10 (2026-04-27) — Fix drivers multi-key exhaustion and signals RPM recovery

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

**Bug 1 — Drivers: single rotation on DAILY_LIMIT caused EUR/GBP/JPY to always be dropped when early keys are exhausted.**
- **Root cause:** When a driver call hit `DAILY_LIMIT`, the exception handler called `_rotate_drivers_key()` once and tried the new key in a nested `try/except Exception`. If that key was *also* at the daily limit, the `RuntimeError("DAILY_LIMIT")` was caught as a generic `Exception`, printed as `"rotated-key call failed"`, and the currency was immediately skipped — even though Keys 5 and 6 were still available. In the observed log: EUR→Key2→daily, GBP→Key3→daily, JPY→Key4→daily — all three dropped because each rotated only once.
- **Fix:** Replaced the single-rotation `if rotated:` block with a `while True` loop that keeps calling `_rotate_drivers_key()` until either a key succeeds or the pool is exhausted. The inner exception handler now explicitly re-checks for `DAILY_LIMIT` in `RuntimeError` and continues the loop rather than breaking.

**Bug 2 — Signals: RPM recovery retried only the last key once after 45s.**
- **Root cause:** When all 6 keys returned `[]` (degenerate / silent RPM exhaustion), the recovery block waited 45s and retried only the very last key (`keys[-1]`). In the observed log, Key 6 was itself under RPM pressure — retrying it once with only 8s of internal `call_groq` retry produced `[]` again.
- **Fix:** Recovery now waits 60s (full RPM window) then iterates through **all** keys from Key 1 to Key 6. Earlier keys (1–4 at daily limit) are skipped cleanly via the `DAILY_LIMIT` branch; keys under RPM pressure (5–6) get a fresh attempt after the 60s window. First key that returns a non-empty result is used and returned immediately.

## v7.47.6 (2026-04-27) — Per-currency scoped context for driver calls (~75% token reduction per call)

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Root cause:** Each of the 8 per-currency driver calls received the full `slim_ctx` (~2,800 tokens), which includes CB rates and COT data for all 8 G8 currencies. Each call only needs data for the 2-3 currencies involved in its 7 pairs — the remaining 5-6 currencies' CB/COT lines were pure token waste.

- **Token reduction:** CB rates section: 8 lines → ~3 lines per call. COT section: 8 lines → ~3 lines per call. Estimated per-call saving: ~250 tokens. Across 8 currencies: ~2,000 tokens/run. Across 8 active runs/day: ~16,000 tokens/day freed. This is additive to the structural change detection savings from v7.47.4.

## v7.47.4 (2026-04-27) — Structural change detection for currency drivers

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Root cause:** Currency drivers (8 Groq calls × ~4,400 tokens each = ~35k tokens/run) were being regenerated on every run where any intraday price moved, even when their actual inputs — COT positioning, CB rates, OIS bias — had not changed. This consumed the majority of the daily token budget and left insufficient RPM headroom for signals, directly contributing to the 0-signal failures seen today.
- **Change:** Implemented structural change detection for drivers, mirroring how Bloomberg/Eikon handle currency driver panels — notes update on structural events, not on intraday pip moves. Drivers are now regenerated only when at least one of the following changes across any G8 currency: COT `weekEnding` (CFTC weekly, Fridays), CB rate `lastUpdate` (meeting decisions), OIS `bias` or `biasUpdated` (weekly via workflow_meetings.yml).
- **Implementation:** `_build_drivers_snapshot()` reads COT, rates, and meetings files and builds a per-currency fingerprint. `_drivers_inputs_changed()` compares the current fingerprint against the one stored in the previous `currency-drivers.json` payload (field `_inputs_snap`). If unchanged and existing drivers are present: `⏭ Currency drivers unchanged — preserving existing notes`. If changed: `✅ Driver inputs changed: {reason} — regenerating`. The `--force` flag bypasses the check and always regenerates.
- **Expected impact:** On typical trading days (COT static Mon–Thu, no CB meetings), drivers regenerate at most once per week (Friday after CFTC publish) plus on meeting days. This reduces driver token consumption from ~35k/run to near-zero on most runs, freeing ~280k tokens/day for narrative and signals across 8 active runs.

Key 4 received the rotation but was also rate-limited — it responded without error but returned []. The empty-list guard had no extra keys left, so it returned [] immediately without any recovery wait.

- **Fix 3 — RPM wait in degenerate-response guard inside `generate_signals()`:** Before retrying with each extra key on an empty-array response, the guard now waits 30s (first extra key) to allow the RPM window to clear. Previously it used KEY_SWITCH_PAUSE_DAILY (1s) which was insufficient under simultaneous pressure.

## v7.47.1 (2026-04-27) — Fix 0-signal output when rotated key returns degenerate empty array

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Root cause:** When Key 1 hits its daily limit during the signals call and Key 2 silently returns `[]` (without raising a DAILY_LIMIT exception), the code treated the empty array as a valid response. `dropped_reasons` was also empty, so the MIN_SIGNALS retry condition (`len(filtered) < 4 and dropped_reasons`) was never satisfied, and the COT-OIS enforcement had no base signals to augment. Result: `signals.json` written with 0 alerts even when clear divergences existed (e.g. NZD/USD bilateral spread 0.926%).
- **Fix 1 — `generate_signals()` degenerate-response guard:** After `json.loads`, if `signals == []` and `_extra_keys` is non-empty, the function iterates through each extra key, re-issues the full prompt, and adopts the first non-empty result. Logs `WARNING LLM returned empty signals array — retrying with extra key N` per attempt.
- **Fix 2 — `call_with_key_rotation()` empty-list rotation:** The `generate_signals` branch now checks if the returned list is empty after a successful call. If so, it increments `key_idx`, logs `WARNING generate_signals returned [] — degenerate response. Rotating to Key N`, and loops — effectively rotating to the next key at the `call_with_key_rotation` level as a second safety net. Both fixes are needed: Fix 1 handles the case where `_extra_keys` is available inside `generate_signals`; Fix 2 catches the outer rotation if Fix 1 was not reached (e.g. during the first `call_groq` attempt before any retry logic).

## v7.45.0 (2026-04-26) — Model: llama-4-maverick; hallucination guard extended to CB speakers in all sessions

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Model changed to `llama-4-maverick-17b-128e-instruct`.** Replaces `llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct`. Maverick is the same parameter count as Scout but trained with stronger multi-step reasoning, which directly addresses the failure modes observed in audit: incorrect causal attribution (CAD strength ascribed to 25bp carry instead of WTI/energy shock), safe-haven framing persisting through retries in MIXED regime, and GBP/USD direction misattributed to a cargo ship attack. Token usage per run is unchanged.
- **Hallucination guard: two-tier architecture.** Replaces the prior single-tier UPCOMING-only guard:
  - **TIER A — rate decisions (UPCOMING only):** Unchanged in scope. A rate decision in a CLOSED/ACTIVE note is a legitimate factual recap; only UPCOMING notes can hallucinate a future decision.
  - **TIER B — CB speaker names (ALL sessions, new):** Detects hallucinated CB official names in CLOSED, ACTIVE, and UPCOMING notes. Pattern list covers 20+ names across all G8 CBs: Powell, Waller, Jefferson, Kugler, Warsh (Fed); Lagarde, Knot, Lane, Schnabel, Nagel (ECB); Ueda, Himino, Nakamura (BoJ); Bailey, Pill, Breeden, Haskel, Ramsden (BoE); Bullock (RBA); Macklem (BoC); Schlegel (SNB); Orr, Breman (RBNZ). Each pattern requires the word "speaks" or "speak" — CB official names used in direct citation style ("ECB's Knot: June cut not ruled out") are intentionally not caught.
  - **Root cause fixed:** JPY/London "BOJ's Ueda speaks" and GBP/New York "BoE's Pill speaks" were CLOSED/ACTIVE notes — invisible to the prior UPCOMING-only guard. Both are now caught and replaced with a carry/CB-stance fallback derived from live rates data.
- **`SESSION_CONTEXT_SYSTEM` updated:** PROHIBITED INVENTIONS list extended to include Pill, Bailey, and Schlegel with explicit note that the speaker prohibition applies to CLOSED and ACTIVE session notes, not just UPCOMING.

## v7.44.0 (2026-04-26) — TIER-1 tagger: topic clustering replaces region-specific hardcodes; inflected-verb fix; expand-field inspection

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **TIER-1 detection: dual-method architecture.** The tagger now uses two complementary methods whose results are unioned:
  - **Method 1 — Keyword matching** (unchanged scope): covers single-article high-confidence events where frequency cannot be used — BoJ/FinMin FX intervention warnings, NFP/CPI/FOMC surprises, bank failures, systemic contagion. Region-specific location names intentionally excluded from this method (see below).
  - **Method 2 — Topic clustering (new)**: tokenises each of the 8 high-impact articles sent to the LLM (title + expand[:150]) and builds an inverted index. Tokens present in ≥ 2 of 8 articles (≥ 25% convergence) are classified as "dominant". Any article containing a dominant token is elevated to TIER-1. This detects any emerging shock — geopolitical, commodity, macro — purely from convergent coverage, with zero keyword maintenance required. A new conflict in any region, with any name, self-elevates if it drives ≥ 2 of the 8 top headlines. Validated against a simulated Taiwan Strait crisis: `taiwan`, `strait`, `carrier`, `forces` emerged as dominant tokens and correctly elevated all relevant articles.
- **Region-specific hardcodes removed from keyword patterns.** `hormuz`, `bab al-mandab`, `strait of hormuz`, `energy shock`, `oil shock`, `crude shock`, `blockade` removed from Pattern A and Pattern C. These location/event-specific terms are now covered by clustering — hardcoding them created uneven treatment across regions (Hormuz is listed, South China Sea is not) and required manual updates after each new crisis. The keyword list now contains only durable, event-type patterns (military verbs, intervention language, macro surprise categories) that are stable across geographies.
- **Regex inflected-verb fix (retained from audit).** Pattern A uses `\w{0,3}` suffix on root forms (`attack\w{0,3}`, `escalat\w{0,3}`, `strike\w{0,1}`, etc.) so past-tense and plural forms (`attacked`, `strikes`, `escalating`, `invasions`) are captured. The prior bare `` boundary produced false negatives on the headline "cargo ship has been **attacked** in Bab al-Mandab Strait".
- **Expand-field inspection (retained from audit).** `_is_tier1_keyword()` inspects `title + expand[:150]`. Geopolitical/commodity context buried in the expand body is captured even when the headline title is neutral/generic.
- **Enriched stopword list for clustering.** Added ~25 generic finance/calendar terms (`policy`, `inflation`, `outlook`, `confidence`, `forecasts`, `banks`, `decisions`, etc.) to prevent high-frequency but topic-neutral words from creating spurious dominant tokens when operating on the 8-article window.
- **NARRATIVE_SYSTEM Rule 1 Category A updated.** Removed Bab al-Mandab and Hormuz from the enumerated list; replaced with "any active geopolitical shock or maritime corridor disruption in any region" — consistent with the region-agnostic clustering approach.
- **NARRATIVE_SYSTEM Rule 1 Category C updated.** Replaced "Hormuz blockade, energy shock" with "maritime corridor blockade — any event repricing the energy complex by >2% or disrupting a major oil/gas transit route".
- **SIGNALS_SYSTEM Rule 8 updated.** "Maritime corridor disruption" and "commodity supply shock (OPEC cut, oil embargo, blockade of any transit route)" added as explicit TIER-1 signal triggers, replacing the prior Hormuz-specific language.

## v7.43.0 (2026-04-26) — Myfxbook: self-hosted runner token renewal + pre-auth session architecture

### Cloudflare Worker — myfxbook-proxy-worker.js
- **v3.0 — pre-authenticated session**: Worker no longer performs login. Accepts `{ secret, session }` POST and calls the Myfxbook outlook endpoint directly with the provided token. Returns `tokenExpired: true` (HTTP 401) when the session is invalid, allowing the hourly workflow to trigger automatic renewal.

### Engine — scripts/fetch_myfxbook_sentiment.py
- **v7.0 — session token architecture**: Script sends the pre-authenticated `MYFXBOOK_SESSION` secret to the Worker instead of email/password credentials. On `tokenExpired: true` response, writes `tokenExpired: true` to the JSON output so the workflow can detect and trigger the renewal workflow automatically.

### Engine — .github/workflows/update-myfxbook-sentiment.yml
- **v2.0 — token expiry detection + auto-renewal trigger**: Added `token_expired` output from the fetch step. New `trigger-renewal` job dispatches `renew-myfxbook-token.yml` via `workflow_dispatch` when the token is detected as expired. Notification email updated to describe the auto-renewal flow.

### Engine — .github/workflows/renew-myfxbook-token.yml (new)
- **New workflow — self-hosted runner token renewal**: Runs on `self-hosted` label (user's Windows PC with residential IP). Scheduled every 20 days (`0 6 */20 * *`). Also triggered on-demand by the hourly workflow on token expiry. Steps: (1) PowerShell login to `myfxbook.com/api/login.json` from residential IP; (2) `gh secret set MYFXBOOK_SESSION` via GitHub CLI to update the secret automatically; (3) dispatches `update-myfxbook-sentiment.yml` to verify the new token. Sends failure email if any step fails.

## v7.42.0 (2026-04-26) — Myfxbook proxy redesigned: single-call Worker v2.0 + email alert guard

### Engine — scripts/fetch_myfxbook_sentiment.py
- **v6.0 — single POST architecture**: Script now sends one POST to the CF Worker with credentials. The Worker handles the full login → outlook → logout flow internally and returns normalized pair data. The session token never leaves Cloudflare's network, eliminating the multi-call pattern that Myfxbook's anti-bot layer detected and blocked with a misleading "Wrong email/password" response.
- **Simplified retry logic**: Three retries on network/timeout errors; immediate non-retryable exit on 401/500 from the Worker (auth or config errors).

### Engine — .github/workflows/update-myfxbook-sentiment.yml
- **v1.5 — email alert guard**: The `dawidd6/action-send-mail` step now checks that `NOTIFY_EMAIL_TO`, `NOTIFY_EMAIL_FROM`, and `NOTIFY_EMAIL_PASSWORD` secrets are all non-empty before running. Previously, an unconfigured `NOTIFY_EMAIL_TO` caused the action to fail with "At least one of 'to', 'cc' or 'bcc' must be specified".
- **Workflow renamed to v1.5** to match the architectural change.

### Cloudflare Worker — myfxbook-proxy-worker.js
- **v2.0 — all-in-one flow**: Worker now accepts a single `POST` with `{email, password}` in the JSON body and handles login + outlook + logout in sequence before responding. Normalization moved from Python script to Worker. Response shape: `{ok, pairs, general}`. The `action` query-param routing of v1.0 is removed.
- **Silent logout**: logout is always attempted after outlook, but its failure is non-fatal and never blocks the response.

The X-axis tick marks show "Mon YY" labels and the crosshair tooltip shows the full date (e.g., "Apr 25, 2026") for each point in the 252-day history — making it possible to identify exactly when a correlation peak or trough occurred.

## v7.41.5 (2026-04-25) — Correlations module: data consistency + industry-standard thresholds

### Engine — scripts/fetch_intraday_quotes.py
- **z_score formula corrected to apples-to-apples:**
  - Before: `z_score = (corr60 - norm30) / std` — 60d snapshot vs 30d-rolling norm (inconsistent windows)
  - After: `z_score = (corr30 - norm30) / std` — 30d snapshot vs 30d-rolling norm (same window)
  - The last point of the `history` sparkline is always the most recent rolling-30d value (≈ corr30), so the chart endpoint, the strip Z-score metric, and the signal banner now all refer to the same 30d window. No additional runtime cost.

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Correlation table "vs norm" badge thresholds aligned to Bloomberg/Reuters industry standard:**
  - Removed the non-standard `|z| >= 1.0` "stretched" tier (no institutional equivalent)
  - `|z| >= 2.5` → `↯ break` (class: `down` / red) — confirmed regime change signal
  - `|z| >= 1.5` → `~ stretched` (class: `warning` / orange) — relationship under stress
  - `|z| < 1.5` → `● normal` (class: `flat`) — within historical norm
  - Changed `⚠ broken` label at 2.5 tier to `↯ break` (removes emoji per GUIDELINES.md)

### Frontend — assets/corr-modal.js (v2.1 → v2.2)
- **Background fixed:** Chart background set to `#070a10` (solid, non-transparent). Eliminates the LWC crosshair hover-lighten artifact that was visible when mousing over the chart canvas.
- **Design aligned with dashboard palette:** Modal background `#0e1118`, strip `#0b0e15`, green `#26a69a` (--up), red `#ef5350` (--down), amber `#e07f00` (muted --orange for z-score warn). Border radius `4px` (matches dashboard panel style). All color tokens match CSS variables in dashboard.css.
- **Signal banner: three tiers only** (break / stretched / stable) — removed the non-standard `|z| >= 1.0` mild-deviation tier. Matches dashboard badge thresholds exactly.
- **Z-score CSS class updated:** `.warn` (orange, `#e07f00`) for 1.5–2.5σ; `.down` (red) only for ≥ 2.5σ. Matches table badge colors.
- **Regime card — "30d vs 252d norm"** row now uses `corr30 - norm` instead of `corr - norm` (apples-to-apples, consistent with the corrected z_score formula).
- **Vertical day markers added to chart:** Dashed vertical lines at the 30d / 60d / 90d positions from the right edge of the sparkline. Visually connects the strip metrics to the corresponding point in the 252-day history. Decreasing opacity (38% / 22% / 15%) so 30d marker is most prominent.
- **Crosshair tooltip:** Now shows "Nd ago" / "today" instead of raw index. More legible for temporal orientation.
- **Subtitle** clarifies: "z-score = 30d vs 30d-rolling norm" — removes prior ambiguity about which window was used.
