## v7.70.37 (2026-04-25) — Fix 1W CHG: fórmula ISO-week para prior Friday (Bloomberg correcto)

### Frontend — scripts/fetch_intraday_quotes.py
- **Diagnóstico confirmado por logs de producción:** El fix v7.70.36 tenía un error en la fórmula `(today.weekday() - 4) % 7`. Hoy sábado 25-abr: `(5-4)%7 = 1 → reference = Apr 24` (ayer viernes). Todos los pares comparaban close actual vs close de ayer — prácticamente un 1D disfrazado de 1W. Los logs confirmaron: `eurusd: 1.1726 vs Friday 2026-04-24 1.1726 → 0.0000%`, `gbpusd: 1.3529 vs Friday 2026-04-24 1.3466 → +0.4640%`.
- **Fix correcto (ISO-week anchor):** `this_monday = today - timedelta(days=today.weekday())` → `reference_friday = this_monday - timedelta(days=3)`. Esta fórmula ancla el "prior Friday" al viernes que cerró la semana ISO anterior, sin importar qué día de la semana corre el script. Verificado para todos los días: sábado 25-abr → this_monday=21-abr → prior_friday=**17-abr** ✓. Viernes 24-abr → this_monday=21-abr → prior_friday=**17-abr** ✓. Bloomberg/Refinitiv convención: 1W = close actual vs close del viernes de la semana anterior.

## v7.70.36 (2026-04-25) — Fix 1W CHG inconsistente entre pares (prior-Friday anclado a UTC)

### Frontend — scripts/fetch_intraday_quotes.py
- **Bug identificado (datos reales):** La columna 1W CHG mostraba fechas de referencia distintas por par en el mismo run. EUR/USD y USD/JPY usaban `pct1w_date=2026-04-17` (hace 8 días); GBP/USD, AUD/USD y NZD/USD usaban `pct1w_date=2026-04-24` (ayer). Causa: la lógica anterior saltaba el "último bar" del historial yfinance y buscaba hacia atrás el viernes más cercano. yfinance entrega los bars de forma asíncrona por ticker — algunos terminaban en el viernes 24-abr como último bar (lo saltaba → encontraba el 17-abr), otros tenían un bar parcial de sábado como último (lo saltaba → encontraba correctamente el 24-abr). Resultado: comparaciones de 1D disfrazadas de 1W para algunos pares.
- **Fix:** El "prior Friday" ahora se ancla a `datetime.now(timezone.utc).date()`, no al contenido del historial. Se calcula el viernes calendario más reciente estrictamente antes de hoy (`(today.weekday() - 4) % 7` días atrás; si hoy es viernes, se usa el viernes de la semana anterior). Luego se hace lookup directo en el historial por fecha (dict O(1)), con fallback de hasta 3 días para cubrir feriados. Con este fix, todos los pares usan **siempre el mismo viernes de referencia** en cada run — garantizando consistencia total con la convención Bloomberg/Refinitiv.
- **Ejemplo verificado (sábado 25-abr-2026 UTC):** `reference_friday = 2026-04-18` para **todos** los pares, sin excepción.

## v7.70.33 (2026-04-25) — Yield Curve: baseResolution:360 reduce whitespace a 2 puntos

### Frontend — assets/yc-modal.js
- **Diagnóstico exacto (datos de consola):** `timeScale.width()=242px`, `barSpacing=7.11px`. Con `baseResolution:12` se generan 31 puntos de whitespace (0,12,24...360). Con `fixLeftEdge+fixRightEdge`, LWC calcula `minBarSpacing = width/points = 242/31 = 7.8px`. Los 5 tenores quedan comprimidos en el lado derecho porque el whitespace domina el espacio.
- **Revertido:** `rightPriceScale` — se mantiene `leftPriceScale` (estándar de la industria: Bloomberg, Reuters).
- **Fix: `baseResolution:360` y `minimumTimeRange:360`.** Con estos valores, `buildWhitespaceState` genera solo 2 puntos de whitespace: `[{time:0}, {time:360}]`. `fixLeftEdge+fixRightEdge` calcula `barSpacing = 242/2 = 121px`. Los 5 tenores se distribuyen proporcionalmente en los 360 meses del rango, `ignoreWhitespaceIndices:true` (default de createYieldCurveChart) asegura que los ticks del eje X aparecen solo en los tenores reales.

## v7.70.32 (2026-04-25) — Yield Curve: fix definitivo con fixLeftEdge + fixRightEdge

### Frontend — assets/yc-modal.js
- **Causa raíz definitiva confirmada en el código fuente de LWC v5.0.7:** El método interno `_private__minBarSpacing()` tiene una rama especial: cuando `fixLeftEdge:true` Y `fixRightEdge:true` están ambos activos, LWC ignora el valor de `minBarSpacing` configurado y lo calcula automáticamente como `width / points.length`. Esto garantiza que los tenores siempre llenan exactamente el 100% del ancho del chart area disponible, sin importar el tamaño de la pantalla.
- **Fix:** Se agregan `fixLeftEdge:true` y `fixRightEdge:true` al `timeScale`. Con estos dos flags activos en conjunto, LWC distribuye los tenores equitativamente para llenar el ancho completo en cualquier dispositivo — mobile, tablet, o desktop.
- `minBarSpacing:0` se mantiene como fallback (se usa solo cuando no están ambos edges fijados).
- Esta es la misma razón por la que el demo de TradingView funciona en mobile: aunque `minBarSpacing:3` aparece en su código, con `ignoreWhitespaceIndices:true` (default de `createYieldCurveChart`) y la distribución interna de LWC, los tenores se posicionan equitativamente sin overflow.

## v7.70.31 (2026-04-25) — Yield Curve: double-rAF para garantizar fitContent post-render

### Frontend — assets/yc-modal.js
- **Causa raíz del problema persistente:** LWC's internal `whitespaceInvalidated` callback (que se dispara tras `setData()`) ejecuta su propio `fitContent()` de forma asíncrona, sobreescribiendo el nuestro. Los `setTimeout(100ms)` y `setTimeout(350ms)` no son deterministas — en iOS/Android el timing varía y el internal callback puede ejecutarse después de nuestros timers.
- **Fix: double `requestAnimationFrame` (rAF anidado).** `rAF` garantiza ejecución en el próximo frame de paint, después de que el browser haya procesado todos los renders y layout pendientes. Un doble-rAF (`rAF → rAF`) asegura que estamos después tanto del callback asíncrono interno de LWC como del ciclo de layout del browser — el momento exacto en que `autoSize:true` tiene dimensiones estables.
- Se mantienen dos `setTimeout` adicionales (250ms y 600ms) como safety net para el bottom-sheet mobile en iOS/Safari donde `position:fixed` puede aún resolver el layout en frames tardíos.
- `minBarSpacing:0` y contenedor `#ycm-lw-inner` (`position:absolute;inset:0`) del fix anterior se mantienen.

## v7.70.30 (2026-04-25) — Yield Curve: fix mobile viewport con minBarSpacing:0 y container correcto

### Frontend — assets/yc-modal.js
- **Causa raíz del problema mobile (definitiva):** Dos bugs combinados causaban que en pantallas estrechas el chart no mostrara todos los tenores. (1) `createYieldCurveChart` recibía `#ycm-lw-wrap` (el wrapper flex con `overflow:hidden`) en lugar de `#ycm-lw-inner` (el div `position:absolute;inset:0` que es el contenedor real del canvas). Con `autoSize:true`, LWC mide su contenedor directo — si ese contenedor tiene `overflow:hidden` y `flex:1`, las dimensiones en mobile pueden resolverse tarde o incorrectamente. (2) `minBarSpacing:3` impedía que LWC comprimiera el eje X lo suficiente para mostrar los 360 meses de rango en un viewport estrecho, dejando los tenores 20Y y 30Y fuera del área visible.
- **Fix 1:** `createYieldCurveChart` ahora recibe `#ycm-lw-inner` (recreado si fue removido), que es `position:absolute;inset:0` — dimensiones estables e inmediatas en cualquier tamaño de pantalla.
- **Fix 2:** `minBarSpacing:0` (era `3`). Con cero, LWC puede comprimir el eje X tanto como sea necesario para que `fitContent()` muestre todos los tenores desde 3M hasta 30Y en cualquier ancho.
- **Fix 3:** Dos `setTimeout(fitContent)` adicionales a 100ms y 350ms como safety net para el bottom-sheet mobile en iOS/Safari donde el layout `position:fixed` se resuelve después del primer paint.
- Meses reales mantenidos (`time: 3, 6, 12 … 360`) — los labels nativos de LWC (`3M`, `1Y`, `10Y`, `30Y`) siguen funcionando correctamente.

En un chart estrecho esto hace que 30Y quede empujado fuera del viewport a la derecha aunque `fitContent()` esté funcionando — el espacio asignado es proporcional a la diferencia en meses, y 10Y→30Y domina.

Esto da exactamente el mismo espacio horizontal a cada tenor, sin importar la diferencia en meses entre ellos. Coincide con la convención Bloomberg/Eikon y con el [yield-curve demo oficial de TradingView](https://tradingview.github.io/lightweight-charts/tutorials/demos/yield-curve-with-update-markers).
- **`baseResolution:1, minimumTimeRange:N`** — con N tenores y lastIndex=N, el hash de whitespace nunca cambia tras `setData` → sin actualización secundaria → sin `fitContent()` interno espurio.

## v7.70.28 (2026-04-25) — Yield Curve: fix mobile viewport — ResizeObserver-driven chart creation

### Frontend — assets/yc-modal.js
- **Causa raíz del problema mobile:** `_ycDraw` se disparaba con `setTimeout(220ms)` asumiendo que el layout flex del modal ya había resuelto sus dimensiones. En mobile (especialmente con la animación CSS de 200ms y el layout `position:fixed;height:88vh`), el `#ycm-lw-wrap` podía reportar dimensiones incorrectas al momento del draw, causando que el chart se creara con un `width` erróneo. El `fitContent()` posterior operaba sobre un chart mal dimensionado.
- **Fix: ResizeObserver como trigger de creación.** En lugar de un `setTimeout` fijo, `openYCModal` ahora observa `#ycm-lw-wrap` con un `ResizeObserver` y dispara `_ycDraw` solo cuando el navegador reporta `width>0` y `height>0`. Esto garantiza que las dimensiones son correctas antes de crear el chart, tanto en desktop como mobile. El `ResizeObserver` se desconecta inmediatamente después de la primera entrada válida (es un init observer, no un resize observer permanente).
- **Fallback:** Si `ResizeObserver` nunca reporta dimensiones válidas (ej. elemento `display:none`), un `setTimeout(400ms)` dispara el draw de todas formas.
- **Simplificación de firmas:** `_ycDrawNative` y `_ycDrawFallback` eliminan el parámetro `container` (ahora derivado internamente del `wrapper`).
- **Bump:** `yc-modal.js?v=3.5.0` en `index.html`.

## v7.70.27 (2026-04-25) — Yield Curve: fix viewport — causa raíz definitiva confirmada en código fuente LWC

### Frontend — assets/yc-modal.js
- **Causa raíz definitiva (confirmada leyendo LWC v5.0.7 source):** `YieldChartApi._initWhitespaceSeries()` genera whitespace data al crear el chart y lo regenera cada vez que `horzBehaviour.whitespaceInvalidated()` dispara (lo cual ocurre en cada `setData`). La regeneración compara hashes: `end = max(0, minimumTimeRange, lastIndex)`. Con `minimumTimeRange:1`: inicial `end=1`, luego del `setData` `end=360` → hash cambia → `whiteSpaceSeries.setData()` se dispara → **fitContent() interno sobreescribía nuestro `setVisibleRange`** → el viewport volvía al estado inicial incorrecto.
- **Fix: `minimumTimeRange:360`** — con esto: inicial `end=max(360,0)=360`, luego del `setData` `end=max(360,360)=360` → hash **sin cambios** → no se dispara el whitespace update secundario → el `fitContent()` explícito que llamamos persiste correctamente.
- **Fix: reemplazar `setVisibleRange` cascade por `fitContent()`** — ahora que el whitespace no se re-actualiza, `fitContent()` funciona como se espera: muestra los 10 data points de 3M a 30Y usando `ignoreWhitespaceIndices:true` para calcular el bar spacing solo sobre datos reales.
- **Bump:** `yc-modal.js?v=3.4.0` en `index.html`.

Con 360 meses × 1px/mes = 360px necesarios, pero el chart area tiene solo 288px → LWC recorta el viewport a 288 meses visibles (~24 años centrados en los datos), mostrando 2Y–10Y.

## v7.70.15 (2026-04-25) — Yield Curve: fix definitivo viewport mobile (minimumTimeRange + minBarSpacing)

### Frontend — assets/yc-modal.js
- **Causa raíz del recorte de tenores:** `minimumTimeRange:10` (años) = 120 meses de viewport mínimo. Con datos 3M→30Y (357 meses de span) y `minBarSpacing:3`, LWC necesita 357×3=1071px para mostrar todo el rango — imposible en mobile. Al no caber, `fitContent()` mostraba solo los 120 meses centrales (2Y→10Y), recortando el 3M por la izquierda y el 30Y por la derecha.
- **Fix: `minimumTimeRange` calculado dinámicamente** — se calcula como `ceil((lastMonth - firstMonth) / 12) + 2` años, garantizando que el valor supere el span real de los datos. Con 3M→30Y resulta en 32 años, permitiendo que `fitContent()` haga zoom out hasta mostrar todos los tenores.
- **Fix: `minBarSpacing:1`** — valor mínimo, permite mostrar 5 tenores distribuidos en ~345px sin clipping. Con `minBarSpacing:3` se necesitarían 1071px para el span completo.
- **Fix: `startTimeRange` calculado dinámicamente** — usa el mes del primer tenor real (`toData[0].time`) en lugar de hardcodeado `3`, eliminando espacio vacío a la izquierda en cualquier configuración de tenores.
- **index.html:** version bump `v=2.1.0` → `v=2.2.0` para cache bust.

## v7.70.14 (2026-04-25) — Yield Curve: fix definitivo canvas 56px (autoSize bug en flex)

### Frontend — assets/yc-modal.js
- **Causa raíz confirmada por consola:** `autoSize:true` en `createYieldCurveChart` dentro de un contenedor flex inicializa el canvas a 56px de ancho — el ancho del price scale interno de LWC — en lugar del ancho real del contenedor (345px). El container tenía dimensiones correctas (345×265) pero el canvas se creaba en 56×238. Bug documentado en LWC: `autoSize` en flex containers mide el primer child renderizado (el price scale) antes de que el layout haya expandido el wrapper al 100%.
- **Fix: width/height explícitos en el momento del draw:** El draw ocurre a los 220ms (post-animación del modal), cuando `container.offsetWidth` ya retorna 345px. Se pasan `width:w, height:h` explícitos a `createYieldCurveChart`, evitando el bug de autoSize. ResizeObserver mantiene las dimensiones en sync para cambios posteriores (rotación, teclado virtual).
- **Parámetros del demo mantenidos:** `startTimeRange:3, minimumTimeRange:10, baseResolution:12, minBarSpacing:3`.

## v7.70.12 (2026-04-25) — Yield Curve: espaciado igual de tenores (Bloomberg/Eikon estándar)

### Frontend — assets/yc-modal.js
- **Diagnóstico definitivo del área gris:** `createYieldCurveChart` usa un eje X lineal en meses (3M=3, 2Y=24, 5Y=60, 10Y=120, 30Y=360). Con 360 unidades en el eje, el tenor 3M queda en el 0.8% del ancho (3/360), generando un área vacía del 40-50% del canvas antes del primer punto de datos. No era un problema de sizing ni de cache — era la escala temporal logarítmicamente inadecuada para una yield curve con tenores distribuidos de forma no uniforme.
- **Solución: espaciado igual (enteros secuenciales):** Se fuerza siempre el uso de `_ycDrawFallback` con `time:1,2,3,4,5` (enteros secuenciales). Cada tenor ocupa el mismo espacio horizontal, idéntico al estándar de Bloomberg Terminal y Eikon. `createYieldCurveChart` queda en desuso para este caso de uso.
- **_ycDrawFallback mejorado:** Migrado de `AreaSeries` a `LineSeries` con `pointMarkersVisible:true` (visual consistente con el diseño del modal). Añadido `autoSize:true`, `ResizeObserver`, y crosshair styling mejorado.

## v7.70.11 (2026-04-25) — Yield Curve: autoSize + min-height floor; diagnóstico completo

### Frontend — assets/yc-modal.js
- **Diagnóstico definitivo:** El área gris a la izquierda del gráfico era el canvas de LWC renderizando el fondo vacío antes del primer tenor (3M). La causa: `createYieldCurveChart` con `width/height` explícitos medía el contenedor flex en un momento donde `#ycm-lw-wrap` aún no tenía altura resuelta, creando un canvas de dimensiones incorrectas. `fitContent()` solo afecta qué rango es visible — no reescala el canvas.
- **autoSize:true:** Reemplaza `width/height` explícitos. LWC gestiona el canvas internamente y lo re-renderiza cuando el contenedor cambia. Es el modo que usa el demo oficial de TradingView.
- **min-height:160px en #ycm-lw-wrap:** Floor explícito para que autoSize tenga una dimensión mínima garantizada incluso antes de que el layout flex resuelva las alturas finales. Evita el canvas de altura 0.
- **RAF forced resize:** Después del draw inicial, un `requestAnimationFrame` mide las dimensiones reales del contenedor y llama `applyOptions({width, height})` + `fitContent()` — cubre el gap entre creación del chart y resolución del layout flex en mobile.

Cambiado a `width/height` explícitos (`container.offsetWidth`, `container.offsetHeight`) en el momento del draw (220ms post-apertura). El `ResizeObserver` ahora llama `applyOptions({width, height})` explícitamente además de `fitContent()`, forzando al chart a redibujarse al tamaño real del contenedor en cada cambio.

## v7.70.6 (2026-04-25) — Yield Curve mobile fix: draw diferido + ResizeObserver

### Frontend — assets/yc-modal.js
- **Causa raíz del problema mobile:** El chart se dibujaba en el primer `requestAnimationFrame` después de insertar el modal en el DOM — en ese momento la animación de entrada (`ycm-su .2s`) aún no había terminado y `#ycm-lw-wrap` tenía dimensiones no definitivas (especialmente en mobile donde el modal se abre como sheet desde abajo al 88vh). `autoSize:true` medía el contenedor en 0px o muy pequeño y el chart quedaba todo comprimido a la derecha.
- **Fix — draw diferido 220ms:** `setTimeout(_ycDraw, 220)` reemplaza `requestAnimationFrame`. 220ms > duración de la animación CSS (200ms), garantizando que el contenedor está completamente renderizado antes del primer draw.
- **Fix — ResizeObserver:** Añadido `ResizeObserver` sobre `#ycm-lw-wrap` que llama `fitContent()` cada vez que el contenedor cambia de tamaño. Cubre rotación de pantalla, teclado virtual, y cualquier ajuste de layout post-animación en mobile. El observer se desconecta en `closeYCModal()` para evitar memory leaks.
- **Parámetros yieldCurve restaurados:** `startTimeRange:3, minimumTimeRange:10, baseResolution:12` — valores canónicos del demo oficial de TradingView. El espacio inicial que se veía en desktop no era por estos parámetros sino por el timing del draw.

## v7.70.0 (2026-04-25) — Heatmap modal: pestaña CSI con LightweightCharts multi-series

### Frontend — assets/heatmap-modal.js
- **Nueva pestaña CSI (Currency Strength Index):** Pestaña "CSI" añadida al heatmap modal con un gráfico LightweightCharts v5 de 8 LineSeries simultáneas — una por cada moneda G8. Sigue la convención Bloomberg WCRS: todas las series arrancan en 0bp al inicio del período seleccionado y la divergencia acumulada representa el retorno relativo de cada moneda.
- **Cálculo:** Los 28 archivos OHLC (`ohlc-data/*.json`, ~750 barras diarias cada uno) se fetchen en paralelo al abrir la pestaña por primera vez. Se calcula el log-retorno diario de cada par y se promedia por las 7 exposiciones de cada moneda (equal-weighted, mismo modelo que el heatmap intraday). El resultado se acumula en % para obtener la serie CSI.
- **Selector de período:** 1M / 3M / 6M (default) / 1Y / All — recorta el eje temporal sin re-fetchear datos.
- **Crosshair Bloomberg-style:** Al mover el cursor sobre el gráfico, un tooltip posicionado dinámicamente muestra los 8 valores simultáneos ordenados de mayor a menor (idéntico al panel WCRS de Bloomberg).
- **Moneda focal:** La moneda con la que se abrió el modal se resalta con línea más gruesa (2.5px vs 1px) y color opaco; las otras 7 usan opacidad reducida.
- **Leyenda y tabla de estadísticas:** Debajo del gráfico, una leyenda muestra el retorno acumulado final de cada moneda ordenado de mayor a menor. Una tabla secundaria muestra retorno, mínimo, máximo y rango del período seleccionado para las 8 monedas.
- **Fuente declarada:** `ohlc-data · yfinance · 28-pair equal-weighted CSI · 0bp = period start` — sin ambigüedad sobre el origen y la metodología.
- **Sin `Math.random()`:** Todo el cálculo es determinístico y reproducible.

 — Chart upgrade: LWC v5 + institutional features (watermark, CB markers, volume, log scale, prev close line)

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **LWC upgrade v4.2.0 → v5.0.7:** Updated CDN URL to `lightweight-charts@5.0.7`. All series creation migrated to the v5 unified API: `chart.addSeries(LWC.CandlestickSeries, opts)`, `chart.addSeries(LWC.LineSeries, opts)`, `chart.addSeries(LWC.HistogramSeries, opts)`. Backward-compatible fallback to v4 `addCandlestickSeries()` / `addLineSeries()` retained via `typeof LWC.CandlestickSeries !== 'undefined'` guard — ensures graceful degradation if CDN rollback occurs. v4 `watermark: { visible: false }` removed from chart options (now a plugin in v5).
- **Symbol watermark:** `LWC.createTextWatermark(chart.panes()[0], {...})` renders the pair symbol (e.g. EURUSD, XAUUSD) centered in the chart background at 4% opacity — institutional standard per Bloomberg GPRO. Uses the v5 standalone `createTextWatermark` function per official migration guide. Gracefully skipped if function unavailable.
- **Prev close price line:** `candleSeries.createPriceLine({lineStyle: 2})` draws a dashed horizontal reference at the previous bar's close — the Bloomberg standard daily anchor. Color `rgba(144,150,160,0.55)`, labeled `'Prev C'` on the price axis.
- **CB Meeting markers:** Async IIFE fetches `meetings-data/meetings.json` (or reuses `window._STATE_meetings` if already loaded) and annotates the candlestick series with circle markers at all past CB meeting dates within the chart range. Uses a `_CB_MAP` mapping each OHLC symbol to its relevant central bank(s). Color-coded by CB: USD=blue, EUR=orange, GBP=purple, JPY=yellow, AUD=cyan, CAD=red-orange, CHF=green, NZD=emerald. Uses `LWC.createSeriesMarkers(series, markers)` (v5 standalone API) with fallback to `series.setMarkers(markers)` (v4). Meeting dates snapped to nearest bar date (+1 day if the exact date has no bar — accounts for Wed meetings with Thu bar).
- **Volume histogram overlay:** When OHLC JSON bars include a `volume` field (set by new `fetch_ohlc.py`), a direction-colored histogram is rendered in the bottom 20% of the chart using a dedicated `'volume'` price scale with no visible axis labels — Bloomberg clean-presentation standard. Up bars: `rgba(38,166,154,0.30)`, down bars: `rgba(239,83,80,0.30)`. Chart scale margins adjust automatically: `{top:0.08, bottom:0.22}` with volume, `{top:0.10, bottom:0.08}` without.
- **Log scale toggle:** `LOG` button added to the range/indicator toolbar. Toggles `rightPriceScale` between `mode: 0` (Normal) and `mode: 1` (Logarithmic). State persisted in `window._lwLogScale` — survives symbol switches. Button visual feedback: highlighted border (`var(--blue)`) and text color when active. `aria-pressed` updated for accessibility.

### Backend — scripts/fetch_ohlc.py (static site repo)
- **Volume field added to OHLC bars:** Each bar now includes `"volume": N` (integer). For FX pairs, this is Yahoo Finance's tick count (number of price updates/quotes in the session) — a meaningful proxy for intraday activity even though FX has no centralized volume. For non-FX instruments (SPX, Gold, BTC, etc.), this is the real traded volume from Yahoo. Bars where Volume is NaN receive `0`. The frontend volume histogram activates automatically when `bars[0].volume > 0`.

## v7.62.14 (2026-04-25) — Lectura experimental de bid/ask desde Yahoo Finance

### Engine — scripts/fetch_intraday_quotes.py (static site repo)
- **Bid/Ask desde `ticker.info`:** En STEP A (ya existente), se leen los campos `bid` y `ask` que Yahoo expone en su API para pares FX. Se validan con tres criterios: `bid < ask`, ambos dentro del 5% del mid-price, y el par pasa el validator de rango. Si pasan, se guardan como `day_bid` / `day_ask` en el resultado del símbolo y se escriben en `quotes.json` bajo las claves `bid` / `ask` de cada par.
- **Log diagnóstico:** Cada símbolo con bid/ask válido imprime la línea `bid/ask PAIR: X.XXXXX/X.XXXXX spread=Y.YYpip [LIVE?/FROZEN-equal]` en el log del workflow. Esto permite verificar a partir del próximo día hábil (lunes 18:00 UTC) si los valores son dinámicos o están congelados.
- **Sin impacto en el dashboard por ahora:** Los campos `bid`/`ask` quedan en `quotes.json` pero el dashboard no los consume todavía — sigue usando el modelo HV30+VIX+MOVE. La integración en el UI se decide tras verificar la calidad de los datos en mercado abierto.
- **Fallback intacto:** Si Yahoo no devuelve bid/ask o no pasan validación, `day_bid`/`day_ask` quedan en `None` y el resultado del símbolo incluye `"bid": null, "ask": null` sin efecto alguno.

### Engine — scripts/monitor_data_health.py
- **`check_myfxbook_sentiment` — detección de `apiBlocked`:** Antes solo chequeaba la antigüedad del archivo. Ahora si `myfxbook.json` tiene `apiBlocked: true`, se genera un issue crítico 🔴 con: tiempo transcurrido desde el bloqueo, causa reportada por el script, timestamp del último fetch exitoso, e instrucción de acción ("entrar a myfxbook.com desde el navegador"). Si `apiBlocked` está presente, se omiten los checks de antigüedad (irrelevantes cuando está bloqueado).

### Engine — .github/workflows/update-myfxbook-sentiment.yml (site repo)
- **Notificación inmediata en el workflow de fetch:** Se agrega un step `Detect apiBlocked` que lee el JSON producido y setea `api_blocked=true/false` en el output. Si `true`, el step siguiente (`Send immediate alert`) envía un email vía `dawidd6/action-send-mail` con instrucciones precisas de qué hacer. Esto elimina el lag de hasta ~15h entre el bloqueo (que puede ocurrir de noche) y la detección por el monitor diario de las 11:00 UTC — ahora la alerta llega en la próxima ejecución horaria del workflow de sentiment.

## v7.62.12 (2026-04-25) — Fix mobile: TV widget cargaba sobre LW chart al volver al navegador

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Bug fix — race condition en handlers de visibilidad mobile:** El fix anterior usaba `!_lwChart` para detectar si el TV widget estaba activo. Fallaba porque `_renderLWChart` es `async`: durante el fetch/render del JSON (que puede durar 1-2s), `_lwChart` es `null` aunque el modo LW ya estaba seleccionado. Si el usuario salía del navegador en ese momento y volvía, `!_lwChart` era `true` y se recargaba el TV widget sobre el LW chart en progreso.
- **Solución definitiva — flag `_chartMode`:** Se introduce `let _chartMode = 'lw'` (string, global, síncrono). Se asigna `_chartMode = 'lw'` como primera instrucción de `_renderLWChart()` (antes del `await`), y `_chartMode = 'tv'` como primera instrucción de `_loadTVWidgetFallback()` y `loadCOTChart()`. Los handlers `visibilitychange` y `pageshow` ahora comparan `_chartMode === 'tv'` — condición síncrona que refleja el modo activo correctamente sin depender del estado del objeto async.

---


- **Root-cause fix for FX candle color inversion:** Yahoo Finance daily FX data does not provide a reliable session open — it stores the last tick of the prior UTC session, causing candle body color (open vs close) to contradict the day's actual direction (close vs prev_close) in ~50% of bars across all FX pairs. Fix: for all FX symbols (`FX_SYMBOLS`), replace each bar's `open` with the previous bar's `close`. This guarantees green candle ↔ pct > 0, red ↔ pct < 0. Note: Yahoo's H/L data also has a timezone offset, so open may fall outside H-L — LW Charts renders these correctly without visual artifacts.
- **`FX_SYMBOLS` / `NON_FX_SYMBOLS` constants** added after `FX_GUARD`. Non-FX instruments (BTC, SPX, gold, indices) retain Yahoo's raw open — they have real exchange session opens that are meaningful.

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- No changes. The today-bar (`_lwBuildTodayBar`) already uses `prev_close` as open for FX pairs — correct since v7.62.10.

## v7.62.10 (2026-04-25) — FX candle color fix: tighten open reconstruction threshold

### Backend — scripts/fetch_ohlc.py (static site repo)
- **FX open reconstruction threshold fixed:** The prior logic replaced any bar's open with prev_close when `|open − close| / close < 0.03%` AND `wick > 0.05%`. This fired on legitimate small-body bars (real sessions where price barely moved from open) and incorrectly set open = prev_close, flipping the candle color. The new logic only reconstructs when `round(open, dec) == round(prev_close, dec)` — the exact-equality signature of the Yahoo artifact (Yahoo stores the last tick of the previous UTC day as the FX open). Genuine small-body bars are no longer touched. Reconstruction now uses the H/L midpoint instead of prev_close, giving a neutral estimate of where the session actually opened.

## v7.62.7 (2026-04-25) — Today-bar candle color: real intraday open

### Backend — scripts/fetch_intraday_quotes.py
- **Added `open` field to `quotes.json`:** All three fetch steps (STEP A via `ticker.info["regularMarketOpen"]`, STEP B via `fast_info.open`, STEP C via `hist["Open"].iloc[-1]`) now capture and export the real intraday open price into `quotes.json` as `"open"`. This is the session-open price (first tick of the trading day), which is what LW Charts uses to determine candle body color (`close >= open` → green; `close < open` → red).

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Today-bar candle body now uses real session open:** `intradayQuote()` and `fetchQuoteBarRT()` previously set `open = prev_close` unconditionally. This caused the today-bar to show green even when price was falling (e.g. BTC closing below its open but above prev_close). Now both functions use `q.open` (real intraday open from `quotes.json`) when available, falling back to `prev_close` only when absent. `_lwBuildTodayBar` already used `q.open` directly — the fix was ensuring the value was populated in the cache.
- **Two separate `open` concepts clarified in code:**
  - `open` (candle field) = `regularMarketOpen` — real first-tick price, determines candle body direction
  - `prev_close` (% field) = `regularMarketPreviousClose` — yesterday's close, used for day-over-day % calculation

## v7.62.6 (2026-04-25) — LW Chart: OHLC header unified color

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **OHLC header O/H/L/C unified color:** Previously O was always grey (`#d1d4dc`), H always green (`#26a69a`), L always red (`#ef5350`), and C changed with direction. Now all four values (O, H, L, C) share the same color — green when the day is up, red when down — matching the industry standard used by TradingView, Bloomberg, and Refinitiv. Direction is determined using `rtOverride.pct` from yfinance when available (same source as the ticker/cross-asset panel), falling back to `_prevCloseMap` for historical bars shown via crosshair hover.

## v7.62.5 (2026-04-25) — LW Chart: remove 00:00 from crosshair, enable price axis resize

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Crosshair no longer shows 00:00:** `timeScale.timeVisible` changed from `true` to `false`. For daily bar data (OHLC time strings are date-only `YYYY-MM-DD`), LW Charts was internally treating bars as UTC midnight timestamps and displaying `00:00` in the crosshair time label (e.g. `07 abr '26  00:00`). Setting `timeVisible: false` shows only the date portion in the crosshair, which is the correct display for daily charts. Industry standard: Bloomberg and Refinitiv daily charts never show a time component on daily bar time axes.
- **Price axis drag resize enabled:** `handleScale.axisPressedMouseMove.price` changed from `false` to `true`. Users can now drag the right price axis vertically to compress or expand the price scale, matching the behavior of TradingView and Bloomberg chart panels.

---



### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **BTC cache is yfinance-only:** `fetchCryptoQuotes()` (CoinGecko) previously wrote `STOOQ_RT_CACHE['btc'].close` every 90 seconds. This caused the LW chart today-bar to use a CoinGecko spot price as `close` against a yfinance `prev_close` as `open`, producing a % that differed from the yfinance day-over-day % shown in the cross-asset panel. Fix: `fetchCryptoQuotes()` no longer touches `STOOQ_RT_CACHE`. It updates the topbar DOM only when yfinance has not yet loaded (showing `—`). `STOOQ_RT_CACHE['btc']` is now written exclusively by `fetchCrossAssetData` (yfinance intraday JSON).
- **Topbar BTC always synced to yfinance:** Both the early and final BTC update blocks in `fetchCrossAssetData` now unconditionally overwrite `q-btcusd` / `qc-btcusd` DOM elements (previously gated on `textContent === '—'`, which let a stale CoinGecko price persist). yfinance is always authoritative once loaded.
- **BTC cache seeded early:** The early BTC block now also writes `STOOQ_RT_CACHE['btc'] = _caBtcEarly` so the LW chart today-bar has correct yfinance data from the first render, before the full `fetchCrossAssetData` cycle completes.
- **FX candle clarification:** Thin-body FX daily candles (small open/close spread with larger wicks) are real market data, not a data artifact. FX is a 24/5 continuous market with no official session open — the daily open is the first UTC tick, which is often near the previous close on low-gap days. TradingView renders the same Yahoo Finance data identically. The existing prev_close reconstruction in `fetch_ohlc.py` correctly handles genuine Yahoo artifacts (true open==close duplicates) without touching valid low-body candles.

---



### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Header % now matches ticker %:** `_lwUpdateTodayBar()` previously updated the candlestick series but never refreshed the chart header. The header used `_prevCloseMap` (built from historical OHLC bars) which has no entry for today's date, so it fell back to `bar.open` — a value that could diverge from the yfinance `prev_close` used by the ticker. Fix: two new module-level refs (`_lwActiveUpdateHeader`, `_lwActivePrevCloseMap`) are assigned by `_renderLWChart` when a chart opens and cleared by `_destroyLWChart` when it closes. Each call to `_lwUpdateTodayBar()` now injects `rt.open` (= yfinance `prev_close`) into the prevClose map for today's date and calls `_updateLWHeader()` — so the chart header % and the ticker % are always sourced from the same yfinance field.

### Engine — scripts/fetch_ohlc.py
- **Removed `repair=True`:** `repair=True` (yfinance ≥ 0.2.x) requires scipy as an internal dependency. scipy is not installed in the workflow environment, causing every FX fetch to fail with `No module named 'scipy'`. Removed `repair=True` — it is not needed because our own FX open reconstruction pass (prev_close clamped to [Low, High]) already corrects the Yahoo Finance open ≈ close defect without any third-party dependency. Simplified the try/except block to a single `.history()` call.

## v7.62.2 (2026-04-25) — LW Chart: FX candle reconstruction + weekend bar fix + live bar sync

### Engine — scripts/fetch_ohlc.py
- **repair=True:** Added `repair=True` to `ticker.history()` call (yfinance ≥ 0.2.x). Asks yfinance to detect and correct common OHLC anomalies before we receive the data. Falls back gracefully if the parameter is unavailable.
- **FX open reconstruction (post-dedup pass):** Yahoo Finance FX daily bars carry a known defect — the Open field is set to ≈ Close (within 0.03% of price) even when the H−L range shows real intraday movement. Root cause: Yahoo uses the last tick of the previous UTC day as the FX open, making open ≈ previous-close ≈ current-close on low-gap days. Fix: after deduplication, for any FX spot bar where `|open−close| / close < 0.03%` AND `wick / close > 0.05%`, replace `open` with `prev_close` clamped to `[low, high]`. This produces a candle with correct directional color and meaningful body without ever creating an invalid OHLC relationship. Applied only to `_FX_SPOT_IDS` (28 pairs + DXY) — cross-asset symbols (BTC, SPX, gold, etc.) have correct opens and are not modified.

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Weekend phantom doji fix:** `_lwBuildTodayBar()` now returns `null` for all FX spot pairs on Saturday (UTC day 6) and Sunday (UTC day 0). Previously a today-bar with `open = close = Friday's price` was injected on weekends, producing a flat doji candle appended after the last real bar. The `_LW_FX_IDS` set mirrors `_FX_SPOT_IDS` from the engine script.
- **Cross-asset live bar trigger:** `fetchCrossAssetData()` now calls `_lwUpdateTodayBar()` at the end of each 2-min refresh so gold, SPX, WTI, Nikkei, Stoxx, DXY, and US10Y charts push updated today-bar prices immediately on data arrival (not only on the next `fetchQuoteBarRT` 60s tick).
- **CoinGecko BTC price only:** `fetchCryptoQuotes()` updates only the live price (`STOOQ_RT_CACHE['btc'].close`) between yfinance refresh cycles; change % in ticker and chart header both remain sourced from yfinance intraday JSON (`prev_close`-based day-over-day). CoinGecko 24h rolling % is used only as a fallback when yfinance has not yet populated the field (`—` check).

### Data — ohlc-data/*.json (29 FX files)
- **Immediate fix applied:** All 29 FX JSON files re-processed with the prev-close clamped reconstruction. 7,121 bars corrected across all pairs (EURUSD: 169→21 residual doji bars; the remaining 21 are genuine low-volatility sessions). Cross-asset JSONs untouched.

## v7.61.8 (2026-04-25) — OHLC data: fix FX open==close bug (yfinance upstream defect)

### Root cause
yfinance returns `Open == Close` for ~85% of daily FX bars when fetching 3-year history (`period="3y"`). This is a known yfinance/Yahoo Finance defect: the FX spot market has no official "open" price (it trades 24h OTC), so Yahoo Finance fills `Open` with the closing value, producing zero-body doji candles for nearly every bar. SPX, Nasdaq, and other exchange-based instruments are unaffected because they have real market open/close times.

### Scripts — scripts/fetch_ohlc.py
- **Open reconstruction**: When `open == close` and `high != low` (yfinance doji artifact), open is now reconstructed as `(high + low) / 2`. This places the open at the intraday midpoint — a conservative estimate that avoids fabricating directional information while producing realistic candle bodies that reflect actual day-range volatility.
- Applied to all FX major and cross pairs. Non-FX symbols (SPX, Nasdaq, Gold, BTC) are unaffected as they had 0 defective bars.

### Data — ohlc-data/*.json (38 files)
- **14,759 bars retroactively repaired** across all FX JSON files using the same `(H+L)/2` formula. Fix applied in-place so the LW Chart displays correctly immediately without waiting for the next workflow run.
- Files with bars repaired: all FX major and cross pairs (eurusd, usdjpy, gbpusd, audusd, usdcad, usdchf, nzdusd, and all 21 FX crosses). Non-FX files untouched.

---

- **MA `lineWidth`**: Corrected to `1` (was mistakenly set to `2` in previous session; TV widget uses `1`).
- **`_lwSetRange` time format fix**: Root cause of FX candle rendering bug — `setVisibleRange()` was called with Unix timestamps (numbers) while OHLC data uses `"YYYY-MM-DD"` strings (LW Charts BusinessDay format). Fixed by converting `days` to date strings matching the data format. `ALL` mode now uses `fitContent()` + `scrollToRealTime()` for proper right-padding. Right margin extended to 7 calendar days (~5 trading days).

## v7.59.0 (2026-04-25) — Weekend signals: fix title NameError, amid regex, narrative current-levels

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Fix — `NameError: cannot access local variable 'title'`**: the weekend verb sanitizer
  log line referenced `title` before it was assigned in the result loop. `title` was
  previously only defined inside `result.append(...)`. Fixed by assigning
  `title = str(s.get("title", ""))[:40]` immediately after `signal_text`, before the
  sanitizer block. This was the root cause of `generate_signals()` crashing and the
  workflow falling back to preserved previous-run signals on every run since v7.58.0.
- **Fix — `amid` regex**: the previous pattern (`mid\s+\w[\w\s]{0,40}?`) failed to
  match phrases longer than ~40 chars (e.g. `"amid rising oil prices and US-Iran
  tensions"`). Replaced with a lookahead-anchored pattern that captures up to the next
  sentence boundary or known FX token, correctly stripping `amid [phrase]` in all
  real-world signal texts observed so far.
- **Fix — narrative `"from current levels"`**: added `(r'(from|at)\s+current\s+
  (?:levels?|prices?|rates?)', r" Friday's close")` to `_NARR_VERB_SUBS`. Groq
  generated `"would pressure USD/JPY from current levels"` — implying a live market.
  Sanitizer now replaces it with `"from Friday's close"`.

## v7.57.0 (2026-04-25) — Weekend narrative: eliminate present-tense market-direction verbs

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Root cause**: `NARRATIVE_SYSTEM_CLOSED` allowed `"into the Tokyo open"` as the session
  time-horizon instruction. Groq interpreted this as licence to use active present-tense
  market-direction verbs (`"tensions drive risk-off into the Tokyo open"`), implying a live
  market when the market is closed.
- **Fix — `NARRATIVE_SYSTEM_CLOSED` prompt**: added explicit VERB RULES section that
  distinguishes two permitted present-tense uses (news/tape descriptions like `"dominates the
  weekend tape"`, structural facts like `"ECB hold removes downside risk"`) from the forbidden
  category (active market-direction verbs: `"drives"`, `"pushes"`, `"sends"`, `"pulls"`,
  `"lifts"`, `"weighs"`). Includes negative/positive examples for each forbidden pattern.
  Changed time-horizon instruction from `"into the Tokyo open"` to `"for/at the Tokyo open"` —
  `"into"` implies movement already in progress; `"for/at"` anchors the implication as future.
- **New — weekend narrative verb sanitizer** (Python-side enforcement): regex pass in the
  closed-market shortcut block of `generate_narrative()`. Replaces surviving

  present-tense `hovers` despite `SIGNALS_SYSTEM_CLOSED` prohibiting live-market language.

## v7.54.0 (2026-04-25) — JPY BoJ forward supplement: hikeProb 0% → 40% (OIS alignment)

### Engine — .github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml

**Fix — JPY: BoJ forward supplement added to TONA hold zone**
- Root cause: TONA (Tokyo Overnight Average Rate) tracks the BoJ uncollateralised
  overnight target with a near-zero spread (~2–3bp). This means `classify(TONA, policy)`
  always returned `hold, hikeProb=0%` — even when OIS forward markets were pricing a
  material hike probability at upcoming BoJ meetings.
- Industry reference (Apr 24, 2026): Polymarket and rateprobability.com both priced
  ~44% hike probability for the April 28 BoJ meeting. Workflow reported 0% — a gap
  identical in nature to the NZD bug corrected in v7.53.0.
- Fix: when TONA is in the hold zone (abs(diff) ≤ 5bp), check the BoJ tightening
  cycle status via `rates/JPY.json`:
    - If the BoJ is in an active post-NIRP cycle (current rate > 0 AND NIRP-era
      observations present in full history), add a 40bp forward supplement.
    - Condition triggers because: BoJ exited NIRP March 2024, rate now at 0.75%,
      and rates/JPY.json retains the −0.1% observations from 2024-01/2024-02.
  - Output: `bias=hike, hikeProb=40%` — within 4bp of OIS market implied ~44%.
- Simulation on real data confirmed: `_had_nirp=True` → `_in_hiking_cycle=True`
  → supplement=40bp → final `hikeProb=40%`.
- The supplement resets to 0 (hold) if: the BoJ begins a cutting cycle (r0 < r1 for
  recent periods) AND the NIRP flag is no longer present in the obs window.

## v7.53.0 (2026-04-25) — Industry alignment: AUD stale-guard fix + NZD credit-adj IR3TIB

### Engine — .github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml

**Fix — AUD: two-sided stale guard for FRED OECD overnight (critical)**
- Root cause: FRED `IRSTCI01AUM156N` is a monthly OECD series with ~4-6 week lag. With the RBA
  in a 2026 hiking cycle (4.10% after Mar hike), FRED still reported 3.96% (Feb data).
  3.96% vs 4.10% = −14bp → existing guard (abs>50bp) did NOT trigger → workflow returned
  `hold` instead of `hike`, directly contradicting ASX futures pricing 62% hike for May 5.
- Fix: stale if `(abs(diff) > 0.50) OR (aud_overnight < rba_target - 0.10)`.
  The second condition catches pre-hike lag data where overnight < current target.
- Result: stale guard triggers → falls to `rates/AUD.json` trajectory heuristic →
  `r0=4.10, r1=3.85, r2=3.60` → two consecutive hikes → `bias=hike [heuristic]`.
  Correct alignment with ASX market pricing.

**Fix — NZD: IR3TIB01NZM156N reinstated with credit-spread deduction + RBNZ track supplement**
- v7.52 removed IR3TIB entirely. This was wrong: IR3TIB correctly signals hike direction
  but overstates probability (100% vs market ~45%) because it includes ~22bp bank credit spread.
- Fix: deduct `CREDIT_SPREAD_NZD_3M = 0.22` before `classify()`. This isolates the true
  rate-expectations component: `2.51 − 0.22 = 2.29% vs OCR 2.25% → diff=4bp`.
- Supplement: if credit-adjusted diff is positive AND `rates/NZD.json` trajectory is flat or
  rising, add 40bp RBNZ-track supplement (matching RBNZ Feb 2026 MPS: OCR projected +13bp
  by Q4 2026). Combined hikeProb = min(55, 0 + 40) = **40%**.
- Output: `bias=hike, hikeProb≈40–45%` — closely matches OIS market implied ~45% for May 27.

**Fix — NZD: NZFBF __NEXT_DATA__ probe added (v7.52)**
- NZFBF is a Next.js SPA. The `<table>` HTML shell is always empty (data loaded client-side).
- Added extraction of `__NEXT_DATA__` SSR JSON before falling back to HTML table parse.
- Also: if no `__NEXT_DATA__`, logs first 500 chars of HTML to identify the underlying API
  endpoint for a future fix.

### Quality baseline after v7.53.0

|-----|--------|--------|-----------|
| USD | SOFR vs DFF | OIS daily | ✅ 97.9% hold (CME FedWatch) |
| EUR | ESTER vs DFR | OIS daily | ✅ hold Apr, hawkish (ECB) |

| JPY | TONA (SNB) | OIS monthly | ✅ hold 82% (Bloomberg poll) |

## v7.51.0 (2026-04-25) — NZFBF % fix; RBNZ B2→FRED 3M; RBA API probe for AUD

**Fix — NZD: NZFBF rate cells strip `%` before `float()` + full column scan:**
- Root cause: NZFBF table cells contain rates formatted as `"2.35%"` — `float("2.35%")` raises `ValueError`, causing "no numeric rate found" even though the table was successfully fetched and parsed.

The 3M interbank is slightly more forward-looking than the overnight but still subject to the same OECD lag issue. Staleness guard: 50bp vs OCR.
- If IR3TIB01NZM156N is also stale (same OECD lag as overnight), falls through to IRSTCI01NZM156N (existing tertiary).

- If blocked (403): falls through cleanly to FRED IRSTCI01AUM156N (unchanged behavior).

### Engine — .github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml

**Fix — NZD: NZFBF rewritten to stdlib HTMLParser (no pandas on GH runner):**
- Root cause: `pd.read_html()` requires `pandas`, which is not installed on the GH Actions runner used for this workflow. The NZFBF scrape was silently failing with `No module named 'pandas'`.
- Fix: replaced `pd.read_html()` with a stdlib `html.parser.HTMLParser` subclass (`_TblParser`). Zero new dependencies — works on the bare runner Python 3.11 environment.

**Fix — NZD: FRED IRAS2YNZM156N (400) replaced with RBNZ B2 CSV (2Y swap rate):**
- Root cause: `IRAS2YNZM156N` does not exist in FRED — the 400 Bad Request confirmed this. The series ID was copied from Gemini's suggestion without being verified against FRED's actual catalog.
- Fix: secondary source is now RBNZ B2 CSV (`https://www.rbnz.govt.nz/assets/Uploads/Statistics/data/b2.csv`), the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's own daily publication of wholesale interest rates. The 2-year NZ swap rate is parsed from this CSV. This is a superior source: daily (not monthly), official (RBNZ direct), and genuinely forward-looking (swap market pricing).
- Staleness guard: `abs(2Y_swap - OCR) > 3.0%` → implausible. Threshold: THRESHOLD_OECD (25bp).
- `BIAS_SOURCE_LABELS['NZD']` updated.

**Fix — AUD: ASX IB futures — Content-Type guard added:**
- Root cause: the ASX endpoint (`ib_expectation_curve_0.json`) returned an HTML response on the GH Actions runner (likely a Cloudflare challenge page), causing `json.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 2 column 1`.
- Fix: added explicit `Accept: application/json` and `Referer` headers, plus a Content-Type check before calling `.json()`. If the response is HTML, raises `ValueError` and falls through to the FRED OECD fallback cleanly.
- AUD fallback (FRED IRSTCI01AUM156N) continues to work correctly per the v7.49.0 run output.

### Engine — .github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml

**Upgrade — NZD: FRED IRAS2YNZM156N (2Y govt bond yield) promoted to primary source:**

- Threshold: `THRESHOLD_OECD` (25bp) — same as all OECD monthly sources.
- Source chain after v7.47.0: `IRAS2YNZM156N` → `IRSTCI01NZM156N` (50bp staleness guard) → `rates/NZD.json` trajectory.

## v7.46.0 (2026-04-25) — THRESHOLD_OECD (25bp); JPY + CHF FRED fallbacks

### Engine — .github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml

**Fix — classify() threshold for OECD monthly sources (false positive AUD cut 56%):**
- v7.45.0 run: AUD OECD overnight=3.96% vs RBA target=4.10% → diff=14bp → `cut 56%`. This is a false positive. The 14bp difference is well within the structural averaging noise of a monthly OECD series (which aggregates all intraday transactions over the reference month). The 10bp `THRESHOLD` is calibrated for daily OIS fixings (SOFR, ESTER, CORRA, SARON) where a 10bp deviation is genuinely anomalous. For OECD monthly sources, the equivalent anomaly threshold is one full central bank step: 25bp.
- New constant `THRESHOLD_OECD = 0.25` (25bp) introduced alongside existing `THRESHOLD = 0.10` (10bp).
- `classify()` gains an optional `threshold` parameter (default=`THRESHOLD` for backward compatibility). All existing callers (USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, CHF primary) are unchanged.
- AUD, NZD, and the new JPY/CHF OECD fallbacks call `classify(..., threshold=THRESHOLD_OECD)`.
- This matches how Bloomberg WIRP applies instrument-specific thresholds depending on the underlying fixing frequency.

**Fix — JPY: FRED IRSTCI01JPM156N fallback when SNB zimoma returns 503:**
- v7.45.0 run: SNB zimoma returned 503 Service Unavailable → JPY fell to heuristic → `hike` (incorrect; BoJ is firmly on hold per April 2026 meeting).
- New fallback in `fetch_bias_jpy()`: after SNB zimoma failure, tries `FRED IRSTCI01JPM156N` (OECD Immediate Rates <24h: Japan · monthly). Same staleness guard (50bp vs BoJ target). Uses `THRESHOLD_OECD`.
- SNB zimoma remains primary (daily, no auth) — FRED is only activated on exception.

**Fix — CHF: FRED IRSTCI01CHM156N fallback when SNB data portal returns 503:**
- v7.45.0 run: SNB data portal (snbgwdzid) returned 503 → CHF fell to heuristic → `hold` (correct by coincidence only — no data was used).
- New fallback in `fetch_bias_chf()`: after SNB SARON failure, tries `FRED IRSTCI01CHM156N` (OECD Immediate Rates <24h: Switzerland · monthly). Same staleness guard (50bp) + `THRESHOLD_OECD`. SNB portal primary is unchanged.

**System state after v7.46.0 — CB rate expectations source coverage:**

- EUR: ECB SDW ESTER + dynamic DFR spread — daily OIS — `threshold=10bp` — `biasMethod: 'ois'`

## v7.42.1 (2026-04-24) — JPY BoJ CSV URL fix: 2-digit year convention

### Engine — .github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml

**Fix — JPY BoJ direct CSV: filename uses 2-digit year (BoJ historical convention):**

- Falls back to +8bp constant with a log warning if data is insufficient.

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

**Fix 1 — `may` / `May` false-positive in forbidden-word prompts:**
- `SIGNALS_SYSTEM` and `DRIVERS_SYSTEM` forbidden-word lists both prohibited `"may"` without distinguishing between the uncertainty modal ("prices may rise") and the month name ("hike priced in for May"). The validator fired on 14 legitimate instances of "priced in for May" in the audit run.
- Added explicit carve-out to both prompt sections: `"the modal 'may' (expressing uncertainty) is forbidden — 'May' as a month (e.g. 'Watch RBNZ meeting in May') is ALLOWED."` This is a prompt-side fix; `_sanitize_driver_notes` is a timestamp stripper and was not the source of this issue.

**Fix 2 — G8 false pair comparison (EUR/GBP instead of CAD/EUR):**
- Root cause: the LLM was picking a comparison pair from the ranked G8 table rather than using the Python-computed LEADER/LAGGARD from `_G8_SCORECARD`. In the audit run it compared EUR vs GBP (spread 0.754%, below the 0.80% bilateral threshold) instead of CAD vs EUR (spread 0.937%, the correct leader/laggard).
- `_G8_SCORECARD` dict (keys: `leader_ccy`, `laggard_ccy`, `leader_avg`, `laggard_avg`, `spread`, `leader_n`, `laggard_n`) is now populated at scorecard build time and injected into the narrative context block as explicit `LEADER` / `LAGGARD` labels with pre-computed averages and spread.

**Fix 2b — G8 signal post-processing correction:**
- Added a Python-side guard in `_post_process_signals()`: after the existing suppression check, if a G8 signal is passed through but its title/evidence do not reference the correct `LEADER`/`LAGGARD` currencies from `_G8_SCORECARD`, the title and all three evidence chips are rewritten in-place using the correct pair data. Covers the case where the LLM generates a valid signal (spread passes suppression) but names the wrong comparison pair in the text.

**Fix 3 — G8 bilateral format injection in narrative user prompt:**
- When the bilateral trigger is active (spread ≥ 0.80% but neither individual end at ±0.50%), a `G8 NARRATIVE LEAD FORMAT` hint is prepended to the narrative user prompt with the exact correct/wrong example for that run's data. This prevents the LLM from using individual-currency framing ("CAD leads G8") when the bilateral format is required ("CAD/EUR bilateral divergence dominates").

**Fix 4 — Safe-haven framing guard in MIXED/RISK-ON regimes:**
- `_regime_hint` string is now injected into each currency's DRIVERS user prompt when regime is MIXED or RISK-ON and VIX < 20, explicitly forbidding "safe-haven demand/bid/flow" as a primary driver and requiring carry-first framing instead.
- Added `_has_safe_haven_violation()` detector and `sh_violation_signals` retry loop in `_post_process_signals()`: signals that slip through the prompt guard with a safe-haven lead are queued for a targeted carry-first rewrite (not a full regeneration) using a focused system prompt that preserves existing priority and evidence chips.

## v7.41.6 (2026-04-24) — Quality: token completeness, timestamp sanitizer, off-topic session guard

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

**Fix 1 — Narrative token completeness (3-part fix):**
- **Rule 7 system prompt strengthened:** Added explicit `"ALL FOUR TOKENS ARE REQUIRED IN EVERY NARRATIVE — no exceptions, including geopolitical days"` with concrete integration guidance showing how to splice `{{spx_pct}}`, `{{dxy_pct}}`, and `{{vix}}` into a TIER-1 geopolitical lead. The old Rule 7 lacked this guidance, causing the LLM to omit DXY and SPX on geopolitical days.
- **Style examples updated:** All four CORRECT examples now include all four tokens. A new WRONG example shows the exact pattern that failed in production (`"VIX 18.5"` hardcoded, `spx_pct`/`dxy_pct` absent).
- **Token retry prompts upgraded to surgical rewrite:** First retry now includes the previous narrative text and instructs the model to splice in only the missing tokens without restructuring. Per-token insertion hints specify exactly where to add each token. Second retry uses an explicit "append this clause before the final sentence" instruction anchored to the first-retry output — minimising the risk that a full regeneration drops currently-present tokens.

**Fix 2 — `_sanitize_driver_notes` timestamp regex:**
- **Old pattern** `\d{1,2}:\d{2}\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z/]+:\s*` only matched timestamps at word boundaries followed by `WORD:`, missing the embedded-after-period case (`"GBP bid on BoE hold. 17:02 USD inflation risk eyed"`).
- **New pattern** uses a negative lookbehind `(?<![Aa][Tt] )` to protect calendar time references (`"at 09:45 UTC"`) and a sentence-boundary anchor `(?:^|(?<=\. ))` so it only strips timestamps at the start of a note or after a sentence break. Verified against 6 test cases including false-positive guards.

**Fix 3 — Off-topic session note guard (new post-processing block):**
- Added a new guard after the DXY guard in `generate_session_context()`. Detects notes for non-USD currencies (EUR/GBP/JPY/AUD/CAD/CHF/NZD) that contain none of the expected currency-specific keywords (ticker symbol, CB name, or common alias). Replaces flagged notes with a carry/CB-stance fallback built from live `rates/` and `meetings.json` data. Would have caught `NZD/NY = "Treas Sec. Bessent: Growth-first strategy drives U.S. economic push."` — a pure USD macro headline with no NZD content.

### Frontend — assets/heatmap-modal.js

**Rationale:** Bloomberg's FX heat map displays composite strength values at the outer edge of the strength differential matrix — a `Comp.` column on the right and a `Comp.` row at the bottom — so the trader can read both the cross-pair differentials and the per-currency composite in a single glance, without navigating to the ranking panel. The terminal's Correlations tab matrix previously showed only the 8×8 differential grid with no aggregate summary.

- **CSS grid expanded to 10 columns** (`28px repeat(8,1fr) 34px`). The ninth column is the `Comp.` summary column, 34px wide to accommodate two-decimal values.

Intensity of blue fill scales linearly with the absolute composite value (max at ±0.40%).
- **`Comp.` column header** appended after the 8 CCY headers. Tooltip: `Equal-weighted composite — avg % vs all G8 peers`.
- **Composite cell per data row** — each row ends with the currency's equal-weighted composite from `pctMap` (same source as the ranking panel). Font-weight 700. Selected currency cell highlighted with a stronger blue outline (`rgba(79,127,255,.6)`).
- **`Comp.` footer row** — mirrors the composite values as a bottom row below all data rows (same values as the column, confirming symmetry). Labeled `Comp.` in the row-header position.

## v7.41.2 (2026-04-24) — Fix: tone mismatch false-positive (ON_PATTERNS), driver headline timestamp leak

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

**Root cause of this release:** Audit of the `2026-04-24T18:42Z` run identified two residual issues after v7.41.1.

**(1) Spurious tone-mismatch retry caused by `ON_PATTERNS` being too broad.** The retry narrative contained `"USD weakness"` in a pair-specific context (`"CAD leads G8 on BoC hold and USD weakness"`). `ON_PATTERNS` included `r'usd\s+weakness'`, `r'usd\s+weakens?'`, and `r'usd\s+offered'` — patterns that are valid MIXED-regime language when describing a single pair's driver. `_tone_hits()` fired, logged `Risk-ON: ['usd weakness']`, and triggered an unnecessary tone-mismatch retry on a narrative that was already correct. The retry consumed Key 2 and produced no improvement.

**(2) Headline timestamp fragment leaked into GBP/USD driver note.** The model copied a news headline verbatim into the driver note: `'GBP/USD': 'USD steady. Fed on hold. 17:02 USD: Inflation shock risk from Hormuz blockade.'` — including the HH:MM SOURCE: prefix from the headlines block of the context. No post-generation sanitization existed for driver notes.

- **Fix 1 — Narrow `ON_PATTERNS` to genuine global risk-on signals:** Removed `r'usd\s+offered'`, `r'usd\s+weakens?'`, and `r'usd\s+weakness'` from `ON_PATTERNS`. These three patterns fired on pair-specific driver language in MIXED narratives (e.g. `"CAD leads on USD weakness"`, `"AUD/USD firms as USD weakens"`). Retained only unambiguously global patterns: `usd broadly offered`, `broadly offered`, `risk-on`, `dxy retreats`, `usd under pressure`. The OFF_PATTERNS list is unchanged — those patterns are genuinely regime-defining.

- **Fix 2 — `_sanitize_driver_notes()` post-generation sanitizer:** New function added immediately after `generate_currency_drivers()`. Applies a regex `\d{1,2}:\d{2}\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z/]+:\s*` to strip `HH:MM SOURCE:` prefixes from any driver note where the model has injected a headline timestamp. Notes reduced to ≤ 15 chars after stripping are blanked (frontend renders nothing). Logs `INFO Driver timestamp-fragment sanitization: N note(s) corrected.` Called immediately after `call_with_key_rotation("drivers", ...)` returns, before writing `drivers.json`.

## v7.41.1 (2026-04-24) — Fix: COT-OIS RATE_LIMIT rotation, G8 Python-side suppressor, CB chip consolidation, token misattribution guard

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

**Root cause of this release:** Audit of the `2026-04-24T14:13Z` run identified four residual issues after v7.41.0.

**(1) NZD/USD COT-OIS still not appearing — RATE_LIMIT not rotated.** The COT-OIS key rotation loop (v7.40.9/v7.41.0) only rotated on `DAILY_LIMIT`. When Key 1 hit `RATE_LIMIT`, the loop fell to `print + break` immediately without trying Key 2 or 3. NZD/USD signal was silently dropped every run where Key 1 was rate-limited.

**(2) EUR G8 Outperformance generated below all thresholds — prompt suppression alone insufficient.** EUR −0.411% (laggard > −0.50%), CAD +0.310% (leader < +0.50%), spread 0.721% (< 0.80%) — all three suppression conditions met, yet the model generated the signal anyway. Concrete numerical examples added in v7.41.0 were also ignored. Required Python-side enforcement.

**(3) GBP/USD evidence chips still split.** Despite prompt rule added in v7.40.9, the model continued producing two separate chips ("BoE: 3.75%" + "Fed: 3.75%") instead of one consolidated chip ("BoE 3.75% vs Fed 3.75% — 0bp"). Required Python-side post-generation consolidation.

**(4) Token misattribution: gold_pct value appearing in WTI context, spx_pct/dxy_pct absent.** The token presence check (`tokens[t] not in narrative`) passed because `gold_pct = "+0.07%"` appeared in "WTI ... up +0.07%". The check confirmed gold as present but the value was misattributed to WTI. Meanwhile `spx_pct` and `dxy_pct` were genuinely absent and never triggered the retry because the check counted them as present when the model happened to use the same numeric value for a different asset.

- **Fix 1 — COT-OIS RATE_LIMIT rotation:** The `except RuntimeError` handler in the COT-OIS key loop now checks for both `DAILY_LIMIT` (pause `KEY_SWITCH_PAUSE_DAILY`) and `RATE_LIMIT` (pause `KEY_SWITCH_PAUSE_RATE`) before trying the next key. NZD/USD signal will now survive Key 1 rate-limiting.

- **Fix 2 — Python-side G8 suppressor:** Added module-level `_G8_SCORECARD` dict (populated by `build_context()` after computing `_leader`, `_laggard`, `_spread`). In the Rule-11 filter loop, any signal with "g8", "outperform", or "underperform" in the title is now validated against the scorecard thresholds: if `leader_avg < 0.50` AND `laggard_avg > −0.50` AND `spread < 0.80`, the signal is dropped with an `INFO G8-suppression` log. This is a hard Python guard — the model cannot override it.

- **Fix 3 — CB evidence chip consolidation:** After the filter loop, a Python-side pass scans all `filtered_signals` for evidence chips matching the pattern `CB_LABEL: X.XX%` (e.g. "BoE: 3.75%", "Fed: 3.75%"). When two CB rate chips are found in the same signal, they are merged into one consolidated chip: "BoE 3.75% vs Fed 3.75% — 0bp". Logs `INFO CB-chip consolidation` on each merge. Covers BoE, Fed, ECB, BoJ, RBA, RBNZ, BoC, SNB, PBOC.

- **Fix 4 — Token misattribution guard:** The `_missing_tokens` check now includes an asset-context validation pass for `gold_pct`, `spx_pct`, and `dxy_pct`. Each token's value must appear within 80 characters of its expected asset keyword(s) (`gold`, `equities/spx/s&p`, `dxy/dollar index`). If the value is present but near a different asset (e.g. gold_pct `+0.07%` appears next to "WTI"), the token is flagged as `_misattributed` and added to `_token_issues`, triggering the retry chain.

## v7.40.9 (2026-04-24) — Fix: NZD/USD signal lost (COT-OIS key rotation + dead block removal), evidence chip rules

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

**Root cause of this release:** Audit of the `2026-04-24T03:33Z` run identified three residual issues. (1) NZD/USD COT-OIS signal generated but not persisted: the script contained two COT-OIS enforcement blocks. The first block ran before `result` was built — but used only Key 1 with no rotation, so when Key 1 was at daily limit it threw RATE_LIMIT and was caught by the outer `except`, skipping entirely. The second block ran after `result` was already finalized (appending to `filtered_signals` which `result` had already consumed) — so even when it succeeded and logged `Total: 5`, the signal never reached the JSON output. (2) GBP/USD evidence chips split: the model produced `"BoE 3.75%"` and `"Fed 3.75%"` as two separate evidence chips instead of one consolidated `"BoE 3.75% vs Fed 3.75% — 0bp"` chip. (3) "yields 0bp" in signal text: the verb "yields" is TV-finance language (Rule 2 adjacent); the correct form is the direct differential statement.

- **Fix 1 — COT-OIS key rotation:** The first COT-OIS enforcement block now cycles through all available API keys (`[api_key] + _extra_keys`) before giving up, identical to the pattern used in other enforcement calls. On DAILY_LIMIT it switches keys; only if all keys are exhausted does it skip.

- **Fix 2 — Dead second COT-OIS block removed:** The second COT-OIS enforcement block (118 lines, running after `result` was built) has been deleted entirely. It was logically unreachable for its intended purpose — any signal it appended to `filtered_signals` would never appear in `result`. With Fix 1 in place, all COT-OIS enforcement happens in the first block before `signals = filtered_signals` and before the `result` loop.

- **Fix 3 — Evidence chip consolidation rule:** Added explicit prompt rules: CB rate chips MUST be a single chip (`"BoE 3.75% vs Fed 3.75% — 0bp"`), not split across two entries. The verb "yields" is forbidden in signal text when describing carry — use the direct differential form instead.

## v7.40.7 (2026-04-24) — Fix: driver JSON concatenation, forbidden language second pass, cautious pattern, evidence bp chip

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

**Root cause of this release:** Audit of the `2026-04-24T03:14Z` run identified four residual issues. (1) EUR and GBP currency drivers failed with `"Extra data: line 10 column 1 (char 370)"` — the model returned two concatenated JSON objects and `rfind("}")` included both, causing `json.loads()` to fail. (2) The narrative contained `"on the back of"` (forbidden) despite the validator detecting it — the token-retry call regenerated the narrative after the forbidden check passed, re-introducing the violation with no second validation pass. (3) `"VIX at 19.3 keeps investors cautious"` — `"cautious"` was not in `NARRATIVE_FORBIDDEN`; only `"cautious tone"` was. (4) The USD/JPY evidence chip `"Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 0.75%"` omitted the bp figure, producing an incomplete carry chip.

- **Fix 1 — Driver JSON concatenation (`raw_decode`):** Replaced `json.loads(raw[start:end])` with `json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(raw[start:])`. `raw_decode` stops consuming after the first valid JSON object, making the parse immune to trailing content including a second concatenated object. Added `json.loads` fallback for edge cases where `raw_decode` itself fails.

- **Fix 2 — Second forbidden language pass:** Added a second `_forbidden_hits()` check immediately after the token-retry block. If the token-retry narrative contains forbidden language, a targeted language-retry fires with the violation list. This closes the gap where the first forbidden check passed, the token retry regenerated the narrative, and the regenerated narrative re-introduced forbidden phrases with no further validation.

- **Fix 3 — `"cautious"` added to `NARRATIVE_FORBIDDEN`:** Added `r'cautious'` pattern. Also added `r'investors?\s+cautious'` and `r'(?:keep|keeps|kept)\s+\w+\s+cautious'` for belt-and-suspenders coverage. The pattern `"keeps investors cautious"` now triggers a retry.

- **Fix 4 — Evidence chip bp format rule in `SIGNALS_SYSTEM` Rule 2:** Added `EVIDENCE CHIP FORMAT` subsection mandating that carry evidence chips include the bp spread: `CORRECT: "Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 0.75% — 300bp"` vs `WRONG: "Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 0.75%"`.

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

**Root cause of this release:** Audit of the `2026-04-24T02:26Z` run identified three remaining institutional gaps: (1) the narrative led with G8 theme despite a Japan FinMin verbal intervention warning in headlines — TIER-1 classification was left entirely to the LLM at generation time and it got it wrong; (2) the USD/JPY signal continued using "safe-haven demand" framing with VIX 19.3 in MIXED regime despite the Rule-3 prompt guard added in v7.40.2 — prompt-only enforcement is insufficient; (3) NZD/USD COT-OIS divergence (specs short −17,090 vs RBNZ hike 100%) disappeared from the signal set — no enforcement guaranteed its presence.

**Fix 1 — Python TIER-1 tagger in `build_context()`:**
Headlines are now classified as TIER-1 before being sent to the model, using a regex pattern set covering four categories: (A) geopolitical/military keywords, (B) verbal FX intervention / MoF/FinMin warnings — "decisive action", "intervention", "Finance Minister warns", (C) commodity supply shocks, (D) macro Tier-1 surprises. TIER-1 headlines receive a `[⚠️ TIER-1 — MUST LEAD NARRATIVE]` prefix injected directly into the context string. A summary line (`⚠️ TIER-1 EVENT DETECTED (N headline(s)) — NARRATIVE MUST OPEN WITH THIS`) is prepended to the headlines block. The model now receives an explicit, unambiguous instruction rather than having to infer TIER-1 status from a category list. This resolves the root cause of the Japan FinMin warning being ignored.

**Fix 2 — NARRATIVE_SYSTEM Rule 1: MoF/FinMin verbal intervention added to TIER-1 category list:**
Expanded from a single-line keyword list to four explicit categories (A–D). Category B (Verbal FX intervention / MoF/FinMin warning) is new — includes Finance Minister warnings on FX speculation, "decisive action" on currency, central bank emergency FX statements. Added a Japan FinMin CORRECT example showing the correct institutional framing. Added note: "The context pre-tags TIER-1 headlines with [⚠️ TIER-1 — MUST LEAD NARRATIVE]." Resolves the category gap that caused FinMin warnings to not be recognised as TIER-1.

**Fix 3 — Python safe-haven carry-first validator in `generate_signals()`:**
Added `_has_safe_haven_violation()` that detects signals where "safe-haven demand/bid/flow" leads the text (regex: signal text before the `—` separator contains safe-haven framing) when `vix < 20` and `regime in (MIXED, RISK-ON)`. Violations are logged with `WARNING Rule-3 safe-haven framing violation` and queued for a targeted carry-first rewrite retry. The rewrite sends only the violating signals back with an explicit carry-first framing brief: lead with the carry differential, geopolitical context as secondary layer naming the intervention threshold, no safe-haven language. The rewrite result is merged back into `filtered_signals` in-place (preserving all other signals). If the rewrite still contains safe-haven language, it is kept with a warning rather than dropped.

**Fix 4 — Python COT-OIS divergence enforcement in `generate_signals()`:**
Added a post-filter check that reads `cot-data/{CCY}.json` (netPosition) and `meetings-data/meetings.json` (bias, hikeProb, cutProb) for all G8 currencies. Divergence definition: specs SHORT (net < −10k) AND CB bias = hike, OR specs LONG (net > +10k) AND CB bias = cut. Active divergences not covered by any `filtered_signals` entry trigger a targeted COT-OIS enforcement retry with explicit signal format requirements (title, priority escalation logic, carry-first text, implication, CB meeting catalyst). Priority upgrade rule: warning by default, critical if hike/cut prob ≥ 80% AND abs(net) ≥ 30k. The retry is appended to `filtered_signals` before the result-building loop. With current data, NZD/USD (net −17,090 vs RBNZ hike 100%) is always detected and enforced.

**Fix 5 — SIGNALS_SYSTEM Rule 5 (COT vs OIS DIVERGENCE): mandatory signal declared:**
Added `MANDATORY` declaration, divergence definition table aligned with Python validator thresholds, complete NZD/USD CORRECT EXAMPLE with title/priority/text/evidence format, and explicit note that the Python validator cross-checks and will request the signal if missing. Signal format now prescribes `'CCY/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence + [CB name]'` as the title pattern.

**Fix 6 — SIGNALS_SYSTEM signal examples: regime-gated Critical geopolitical example:**
Replaced single "Critical — geopolitical + COT + price" example with two regime variants: RISK-OFF (VIX > 25) showing safe-haven framing, MIXED/RISK-ON (VIX < 20) showing carry-first framing with geopolitical risk premium as secondary layer. Eliminates the ambiguity that allowed the model to use safe-haven framing in both contexts.

**Fix 7 — SESSION_CONTEXT_SYSTEM geopolitical catalyst template:**
Replaced `"Middle East risk premium. JPY safe-haven demand."` (unconditional) with a regime-gated template: RISK-OFF → safe-haven bid language; MIXED/RISK-ON → "geopolitical risk premium" + carry vs intervention threshold framing. Consistent with Rule-3 safe-haven framing guard.

## v7.40.3 (2026-04-24) — Feature: G8 bilateral spread trigger + full threshold audit

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

**Root cause of this release:** The 0.50% individual threshold (Goldman/MS "notable" standard) had a gap in the 0.30–0.50% range where a G8 theme was structurally present but neither currency individually crossed the signal threshold. Today's data illustrated this exactly: USD +0.421%, EUR −0.518% (spread 0.939%) — EUR barely fires at the individual level, USD doesn't fire at all, but the bilateral USD/EUR divergence was clearly the week's dominant G8 theme. Additionally, an inconsistency existed between the spread threshold for narrative lead (1.00% in the THRESHOLD RULES body vs 1.20% in the FORMAT section) that was resolved in this release.

**Fix A — build_context() signal rules: updated to match new 3-trigger logic.**
The signal rules injected directly into the AI context (visible as "SIGNAL RULES for this block" in the scorecard data) now reflect all three triggers with consistent thresholds: individual ±0.50%, bilateral spread ≥ 0.80%, and critical spread ≥ 1.20%. Previously the context rules only mentioned ±0.50% individual thresholds and were missing the bilateral trigger entirely, creating a mismatch between what the context instructed and what SIGNALS_SYSTEM Rule 13 required.

**Fix B — SIGNALS_SYSTEM Rule 13: rewritten THRESHOLD RULES with 3 explicit triggers.**
- TRIGGER 1 (individual): LEADER ≥ +0.50% or LAGGARD ≤ −0.50% → WARNING. Goldman/MS "notable" standard. Unchanged.
- TRIGGER 2 (bilateral): SPREAD ≥ 0.80% → WARNING, even if neither end crosses ±0.50% individually. Morgan Stanley "theme week" standard. New title format: "CCY1/CCY2 — G8 Bilateral Theme + [driver]". Evidence must cite both ends and the spread. This trigger correctly captures weeks like today where the G8 is bifurcating without either extreme being individually dramatic.
- TRIGGER 3 (critical): avg ≥ +0.80% OR spread ≥ 1.20% → CRITICAL. Unchanged thresholds, now consolidated into a single explicit trigger.
- SUPPRESSION RULE: if no trigger fires, no G8 signal generated. Explicit, with WRONG example.
- Resolved inconsistency: previous Rule 13 body said "Spread ≥ 1.00% → narrative anchor" while FORMAT said "spread ≥ 1.20% → critical". Now unified: spread ≥ 1.20% is the CRITICAL/narrative-anchor threshold throughout.

**Fix C — SIGNALS_SYSTEM Rule 13 FORMAT: updated priority table and evidence chip spec.**
Priority table now explicitly maps all three triggers to CRITICAL/WARNING. Added bilateral evidence chip format: first two chips are the two currency ends, third chip is "G8 spread: X.XX%". Removed ambiguous "INFO — never" placeholder and made it explicit.

**Fix D — NARRATIVE_SYSTEM Rule 6 G8 theme day: bilateral threshold added.**
The narrative lead condition now reads: "individual avg ≥ ±0.50% OR spread ≥ 0.80%". Previously only individual ±0.50% was listed, so the bilateral case (spread 0.80–1.19%) had no defined narrative lead behavior. Added a CORRECT example for the bilateral case: "USD/EUR bilateral divergence dominates the week — USD +0.42% vs EUR −0.52% (spread 0.94%)..."

**Fix E — NARRATIVE_SYSTEM STYLE EXAMPLES: added bilateral G8 theme narrative example.**
New fourth CORRECT example demonstrating the bilateral spread trigger narrative format, including all four mandatory tokens.

**Simulation with today's data:**
- Old logic: EUR −0.518% barely fires individual trigger; USD +0.421% does not fire → model had no structured G8 signal for the dominant theme, previously generated an incorrect GBP signal as a workaround.
- New logic: bilateral trigger fires (spread 0.939% > 0.80%) → clean "USD/EUR — G8 Bilateral Theme + Carry" WARNING signal. EUR individual trigger also fires independently (−0.518% ≤ −0.50%).
