## v7.23.9 (2026-04-13) — Negated risk-off false positive fix in tone detector

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

**Bug — "risk-off sentiment wanes" triggered spurious retry:**
The phrase "risk-off sentiment wanes" was firing `OFF_PATTERNS` as a genuine risk-off signal,
causing the retry to report "did not fully resolve tone mismatch" even though the narrative
was correctly written in MIXED tone. "Risk-off wanes/eases/fades" is standard MIXED/transitional
language — it means risk aversion is receding, which is the opposite of a risk-off signal.

Extended `_tone_hits()` with the same negation-aware logic already applied to `safe-haven bid`
in v7.23.7, now also covering `risk[\s-]off` patterns. Checks 30 chars after and 15 before
the match for waning/easing words: `wanes`, `fades`, `easing`, `diminishes`, `recedes`,
`subsides`, `abates`, `declining`, `reduced`, `limited`.

Validated with the exact retry narrative from the v7.23.8 run:
"...risk-off sentiment wanes, while DXY steady" → OFF hits: [] ✅
True risk-off narrative ("risk-off tone dominates") → fires correctly ✅

With this fix, a correctly-written MIXED retry narrative that uses "risk-off sentiment wanes"
will no longer generate a spurious "did not fully resolve" warning or waste a second retry.

## v7.23.7 (2026-04-13) — Safe-haven bid false positive fix; retry narrative quality

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

**Bug — `safe-haven bid` triggered risk-off detection incorrectly:**
The phrase "JPY safe-haven bid absent/muted" was firing `OFF_PATTERNS` as a risk-off signal,
causing an unnecessary retry even when the narrative was correctly written as MIXED.
"Safe-haven bid absent" is the standard institutional phrasing for a MIXED/NEUTRAL regime
where JPY is not performing its safe-haven role — it is NOT a risk-off indicator.
`_tone_hits()` now uses context-aware detection for this pattern: inspects the 35 chars
after and 15 chars before each match for negation words (`absent`, `muted`, `limited`,
`fading`, `reduced`, `suppressed`, `compromised`, `weakened`). Only fires if no negation
is present. 7/7 test cases pass including all edge cases.

**Retry prompt — narrative quality improvement:**
Previous retry prompt suppressed RISK-ON language but gave no guidance on content quality,
allowing Groq to fall back to pure level-listing (e.g. "EUR/USD trading at 1.1766, GBP/USD
at 1.3508") with no catalyst. Added mandatory instruction to the retry prompt: "mention at
least one CB or yield catalyst to explain EUR/USD or USD/JPY direction — do not just list
price levels." This targets the quality regression seen in the v7.23.6 run where the retry
narrative omitted the 175bp Fed/ECB differential that was explicit in the context.

## v7.23.6 (2026-04-13) — Retry key rotation; tone log readability; DXY steady sanitizer

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

**Bug A — `_tone_hits` logged regex patterns instead of matched strings:**
`_tone_hits()` returned the list of patterns that matched, not the actual substrings found in the
narrative. Log showed `['usd\s+broadly\s+offered', ...]` instead of `['usd broadly offered', ...]`.
Fixed: now calls `m.group(0)` for each match and returns the matched text.

**Bug B — DXY sanitizer missed `"DXY steady with -0.27%"` pattern:**
The retry prompt correctly suppressed "DXY retreats" but Groq substituted "DXY steady with -0.27%",
which is incoherent (neutral label + numeric move). The DXY regex in `sanitize_hardcoded_tokens()`
did not include `steady|consolidating` or the connectors `with|at`. Extended the pattern to cover
all DXY neutral-label constructions followed by a percentage. Also added explicit instruction to
the retry prompt: "DXY steady must never be followed by a numeric value".

**Bug C — Retry consumed key budget when `api_key` hit daily limit mid-session:**
When Key 1 was already at its daily limit, the retry call immediately raised `DAILY_LIMIT`,
which propagated up to `call_with_key_rotation` as a full function failure — triggering a second
normal (non-retry) call on Key 2 instead of a retry call. Fixed by:
  1. `generate_narrative(api_key, context, _extra_keys=None)` — new optional parameter
  2. `call_with_key_rotation` passes `keys[key_idx+1:]` as `_extra_keys` when calling
     `generate_narrative`, so the retry has a list of fallback keys to try internally
  3. Retry loop in `generate_narrative` iterates `[api_key] + _extra_keys`, rotating
     on `DAILY_LIMIT` without re-running the first call or losing the retry prompt

## v7.23.5 (2026-04-13) — Tone detector false positive fix; validate_regime logging cleanup

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

**False positive in tone mismatch detector fixed:**
Substring match `"usd firms" in narrative.lower()` was triggering on `"AUD/USD firms to 0.7096"`,
causing an unnecessary retry even when the narrative was correctly written as MIXED.
Replaced all tone-detection logic with word-boundary regex patterns. The critical fix is
`(?<![/\w])usd\s+firms?` — negative lookbehind ensures "USD firms" only matches when USD
itself is the subject, not when it appears as the quote currency in a pair (EUR/USD, AUD/USD, etc.).
Validated against 5 test cases covering the false-positive scenario and all true-positive cases.

**Hormuz headline confirmed not a hallucination:** The catalyst "US blockade of Strait of Hormuz"
was present in `news-data/news.json` — Groq read it correctly from context. CAUSALITY REQUIRED
is working as intended.

**`validate_regime()` print statements removed:** Function now returns silently.
All regime override logging is handled by `generate_narrative()` which has the full
narrative context needed to report override + tone mismatch in one coherent log line.
Previously this printed a duplicate WARNING before `generate_narrative()` could assess tone.

## v7.23.3 (2026-04-13) — Python-side sanitizers for token/VIX/regime bugs

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

Three Python-side post-processors added. These bugs cannot be solved by prompt instructions —
Groq violates token rules consistently regardless of how the instructions are written.

**Bug 1 — Hardcoded token values (`sanitize_hardcoded_tokens()`):**
Groq was writing `"DXY retreats -0.23%"` and `"gold lower -0.56%"` with literal numbers instead
of `{{dxy_pct}}` / `{{gold_pct}}` placeholders.

Root cause found in v7.23.3 second pass: previous fix was architecturally wrong — it ran
*after* `resolve_tokens()`, so when hardcoded value == token value (same execution cycle),
`narrative_before == narrative` and the change was silently a no-op.

Correct architecture: `sanitize_hardcoded_tokens()` now runs **BEFORE** `resolve_tokens()`.
It replaces hardcoded numbers with `{{placeholder}}` tokens. `resolve_tokens()` then
substitutes live values as normal. This also fixes JS live-refresh on the frontend
(index.json previously stored hardcoded numbers that the JS refresh couldn't update).

Equity keyword list also expanded: `"equity gains +0.65%"` was not caught because pattern
only matched `equities rise/slide/higher/lower` — added `gains?`, `rises?`, `stocks?`.

**Bug 2 — VIX label mismatch in signals (`_correct_vix_label()`):**
Groq called VIX=19.4 "low volatility". Previous fix had a logic error: the `_fix()` function
was used as a `re.sub()` replacement callback but returned the full corrected string instead of
just the matched portion, causing `re.sub()` to replace `"VIX at 19.4"` with the entire
sentence — producing the same output as input.

Correct implementation: two-pass approach. Pass 1 finds VIX numeric value via `re.search()`.
Pass 2 does a standalone `re.sub()` on the volatility label in the full text. Validated
against all 4 bands: <15 low, 15–20 normal, 20–28 elevated, >28 high/fear.

**Bug 3 — Narrative tone mismatch after regime override (monitoring):**
When `validate_regime()` overrides LLM regime (e.g. RISK-ON → MIXED), narrative tone
still reflects RISK-ON language. Python logs a targeted warning with offending phrases.
A full fix would require a conditional Groq retry — deferred until frequency data available.

---



### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

Three Python-side post-processors added — these bugs cannot be solved by prompt instructions alone
because Groq ignores token rules under certain conditions:

**Bug 1 — Hardcoded token values (`sanitize_hardcoded_tokens()`):**
Groq was writing `"DXY retreats -0.24%"` instead of `"DXY retreats {{dxy_pct}}"`.
`resolve_tokens()` couldn't fix this because there was no placeholder to replace.
New `sanitize_hardcoded_tokens()` runs after `resolve_tokens()` and detects bare numeric
values in the 4 live-metric positions (DXY/gold/equities pct, VIX level) using keyword-anchored
regex patterns. Replaces them with the canonical `tokens{}` values. Logs `INFO Hardcoded token
values sanitized` when triggered.

**Bug 2 — VIX label mismatch in signals (`_correct_vix_label()`):**
Groq was calling VIX=19.4 "low volatility" when the rule is VIX 15–20 = "normal volatility".
A per-signal corrector now parses the VIX numeric value from signal text, computes the correct
label, and substitutes it. Enforces all 4 bands: <15 low, 15–20 normal, 20–28 elevated, >28
high/fear. Logs `INFO VIX label corrected` when triggered.

**Bug 3 — Narrative tone mismatch after regime override:**
When `validate_regime()` overrides LLM regime (e.g. RISK-ON → MIXED), the narrative written
by Groq still used RISK-ON language ("USD broadly offered"). Python cannot rewrite the narrative
without a second Groq call, so instead a targeted warning is logged:
`WARNING Narrative tone may not match overridden regime=MIXED` with the specific offending
phrases listed. This makes the mismatch visible in CI logs for monitoring.

---

 — Narrative prompt: CAUSALITY REQUIRED + DXY materiality hardening

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py

**Problem addressed:** Narrative was producing screen-reads ("EUR/USD firms at 1.1732") without
naming the driver, and violating the DXY materiality threshold by describing sub-0.10% moves as
"retreats" and hardcoding the numeric value instead of using `{{dxy_pct}}`.

**Changes to `NARRATIVE_SYSTEM` prompt:**

- **CAUSALITY REQUIRED rule added** (new mandatory CRITICAL RULE): Every directional statement about
  a pair or asset must name a specific driver from the context data (CB stance/divergence, yield
  differential, macro data, COT extreme, cross-asset flow, VIX/MOVE regime, or news headline).
  Three explicit VIOLATION/CORRECT pairs included to teach by contrast.
  "Profit-taking" is now explicitly flagged as a tautology, not a valid catalyst.

- **DXY materiality threshold hardened:** Sub-threshold DXY moves must now use "DXY steady" or
  "DXY consolidating" — explicitly forbidden to write the numeric value. Added a VIOLATION/CORRECT
  example using the exact real-world failure case ("DXY retreats -0.05%").

- **BAD EXAMPLE section added to STYLE GUIDE:** The exact narrative from the live session
  ("USD broadly offered — DXY retreats -0.05%...") is annotated line-by-line with 5 numbered
  failure reasons. This teaches Groq by negative contrast alongside the existing good examples.

## v7.23.0 (2026-04-13) — pct1m added to quotes.json; narrative migrated off fx-performance

### Engine — scripts/fetch_intraday_quotes.py (site repo)
- **New field `pct1m`:** Added 1-month % change calculation inside `fetch_hv30_fx()`, which already downloads 3-month daily history for HV30 — no extra API call. For each of the 7 FX majors, finds the first available close in the window `[today-32d, today-28d]` (±2-day tolerance absorbs weekends and holidays without jumping to a different month) and computes `pct1m = (close / ref_close − 1) × 100`. Stores `pct1m` and `pct1m_date` in each pair's `quotes.json` entry alongside the existing `pct1w` and `hv30` fields.

The section header changes from `Live FX Spot Rates (ECB/Frankfurter)` to `Live FX Spot Rates (yfinance · ~5 min delay)`.

## v7.22.6 (2026-04-13) — 1W CHG migrated to intraday quotes (5-min refresh)

### Engine — scripts/fetch_intraday_quotes.py
- **Period expanded:** `ticker.history(period="5d")` → `period="10d"` to guarantee the prior Friday close is always available (on Monday post-holiday, 5d history could land in the prior week before the Friday).

Uses the daily history already downloaded — no extra API call. ## v7.22.5 (2026-04-13) — Fix 1W CHG: prior Friday close convention (Bloomberg/TradingView)

### Engine — .github/workflows/update-fx-performance.yml
- **Bug fix:** `fxPerformance1W` was calculated as `ref_date - 7 calendar days`, which produces an inconsistent window depending on the day of the week (e.g. on Tuesday, it compared against last Monday = 10 market days back instead of ~5). Bloomberg and TradingView define "1W change" as the current price vs the **prior Friday close**.
- **Fix:** Replaced `date_7d = ref_date - timedelta(days=7)` with a formula that always resolves to the **Friday of the prior week** regardless of today's weekday: `days_to_prev_friday = (ref_date.weekday() - 4) % 7 or 7`. This matches the institutional convention and eliminates the divergence vs TradingView observed in the terminal.

## v7.22.0 (2026-04-13) — OIS bias automation, 12× narrative cadence, IV proxy labelling

### Engine — .github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml
- **OIS-implied bias automation:** Replaced the trajectory heuristic with real overnight/OIS rate fetchers for all G8 central banks. Each CB now has a dedicated source: USD → CME FedWatch SOFR futures (fixed endpoint); EUR → ECB Statistical Data Warehouse (ESTER overnight rate, +7bp DFR spread normalisation); GBP → BoE public database (SONIA series IUDSOIA); JPY → BoJ TONA daily CSV; AUD → ASX 30-Day Interbank Cash Rate Futures (same source as Bloomberg AUS); CAD → BoC Valet API (CORRA overnight, replacing CDOR); CHF → SNB data portal (SARON overnight); NZD → RBNZ OCR interbank daily CSV (series HB2). All fetchers return `(bias, cut_prob_pct)` — if a source is temporarily unavailable, the workflow falls back to rate-trajectory heuristic and preserves any prior OIS directional signal rather than silently flipping to 'hold'.
- **New fields in `meetings.json`:** `biasMethod` ('ois' | 'ois-preserved' | 'heuristic'), `biasSource` (human-readable source label), `biasUpdated` (ISO date the bias was last computed). These are consumed by `dashboard.js` to build per-cell tooltips showing method, source, and freshness.
- **CME FedWatch endpoint fixed:** Previous URL (`MeetingTargetOptionsDataByDate.do`) was incorrect and returning null. Corrected to `getMeetingTargetRateProbs.do?exchange=CME&asset=ZQ` — the stable public endpoint. Probability parser now handles all observed response shapes (`probs`, `targetProbs`, `probabilities`, `meetingProbs`).
- **Preserve logic hardened:** When OIS source is down and heuristic says 'hold' but previous method was 'ois'/'ois-preserved' with a directional signal, the prior bias is preserved with `biasMethod: 'ois-preserved'` rather than silently reverting to 'hold'. Prevents false regime flips during transient API outages.

### Engine — .github/workflows/generate-ai-narrative.yml
- **Frequency increased from 8× to 12× daily.** New schedule adds four runs: 02:00 UTC (Tokyo mid), 04:00 UTC (Tokyo close / pre-London), 10:30 UTC (London mid), 14:30 UTC (NY open peak), 16:00 UTC (NY afternoon), 20:00 UTC (post-NY / pre-Asia data). Narrative TTL effectively halved from ~3h to ~2h between updates.
- **Resource verification:** GitHub Actions usage rises from ~600 to ~900 min/month (45% of 2,000 min free tier). Groq token usage rises from ~29k to ~43k tokens/day across 3 keys (~14,400/key — well within 500k/day free limit). Both within safe operating margins.

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Bias column tooltips now show source + method + freshness.** Hovering any Bias cell in the CB Rate Expectations panel displays: the OIS source (e.g. "CME FedWatch (SOFR futures)"), the `biasUpdated` date, and a note if the value is heuristic-estimated or OIS-preserved. Cells with `biasMethod: 'heuristic'` show "estimated from rate trajectory · OIS source unavailable"; `biasMethod: 'ois-preserved'` shows the preservation notice.
- **`probSuffix` tooltip updated:** Cut probability chip title now shows the specific OIS source per currency (e.g. "ASX Rate Indicator (IB futures)") instead of the hardcoded "CME FedWatch / ASX Rate Indicator" string.
- **IV proxy labelling improved.** Panel subtitle updated from "ETF options IV · CBOE" to "ETF options IV · CBOE (proxy)" to signal clearly that these are not OTC interbank rates. ## v7.21.10 (2026-04-12) — FX Liquidity canvas: fix now-line position on Sunday market open

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Root cause:** `drawLiquidityChart()` and `fetchLiquidityData()` used `utcHour < 21` as the Sunday weekend threshold. The canvas `OFFSET=44` anchors the left edge at 22:00 UTC. At 21:xx UTC Sunday (market opens at 21:00 UTC), `isWeekend` evaluated to `false`, but `nowArraySlot` (42–43) mapped to `nowCanvasSlot` 46–47 — the far-right edge of the canvas. This caused the solid past-area to fill the entire chart and the dotted future line to appear pinned at the far right, even though the FX week had just started.
- **Fix:** Changed the Sunday threshold in both `fetchLiquidityData()` and `drawLiquidityChart()` from `utcHour < 21` to `utcHour < 22`. The canvas stays in weekend (flat/grey) mode until 22:00 UTC Sunday, the moment `nowCanvasSlot` correctly resolves to 0 (far left). The session indicator and other panels retain the original `< 21` threshold — only the canvas functions are affected.

### Frontend — assets/cot-modal-chart.js
- **Plugin declaration order bug fixed:** `_gradFillPlugin` was declared with `const` *after* `Chart.register(_crosshairPlugin, _priceBadgePlugin, _gradFillPlugin)` — `const` is not hoisted, so `_gradFillPlugin` was `undefined` at registration time. The gradient plugin was never actually registered. Fixed by declaring both plugins before the `Chart.register()` call.
- **Gradient rewritten as manual canvas draw:** Instead of mutating `ds.backgroundColor`, `_gradFillPlugin` now draws the gradient fill manually in `afterDatasetsDraw` by retracing the rendered line path (`meta.data` points), closing to the baseline (y=0 or chartArea.bottom), and filling with a `createLinearGradient` built from `chartArea.top/bottom` (CSS coordinates, always correct). Clipped to chartArea so fill doesn't bleed into axes.
- **Badge X coordinate corrected:** With `scales.y` at `position: 'right'`, `chartArea.right` is the left edge of the Y axis tick area — not the canvas edge. Badge now draws at `chartArea.right + 2`, overlapping the Y axis area where there's already space. No extra `layout.padding.right` needed.

## v7.21.7 (2026-04-12) — COT modal: switch Net/Long-Short to responsive:true, fix mobile DPR scaling

### Frontend — assets/cot-modal-chart.js
- **Root cause of mobile tiny content:** Net Position and Long/Short were using `responsive: false` with manual canvas sizing (`cv.width = r.width * DPR`). Chart.js with `responsive: false` does not apply `devicePixelRatio` scaling to fonts, ticks, tooltips, or plugins — all text rendered at 1× while the canvas was 2–3× larger, making everything appear half/third size on Retina/mobile screens. Participants used `responsive: true` (Chart.js default) and had no issue.
- **Fix:** Switched Net Position and Long/Short to `responsive: true` + `maintainAspectRatio: false`. Removed all manual `cv.width/height/style` assignments from `buildChart`.
- **CSS fix:** Added `flex:1; min-height:0; height:100%` to `#p-net.on .cot-cw > .cot-chart-area` and `#p-split.on .cot-cw > .cot-chart-area` so Chart.js can measure the container correctly in responsive mode.
- **Removed manual height computation from `cotTab`:** The `rAF` block that measured siblings and set `chartArea.style.height` in px was designed for `responsive: false`. With `responsive: true` it conflicts with the CSS flex layout. Removed — `rAF x2` is kept only to ensure the panel is painted before `buildChart` runs.
- **Removed redundant mobile fixed heights:** `#p-net .cot-chart-area` and `#p-split .cot-chart-area` no longer need explicit pixel heights on mobile — flex fill handles it correctly at any screen size.

On Retina/mobile screens with DPR=2–3, the gradient compressed into the top third of the chart. Fixed to use `canvas.height` (physical pixels), which matches the 2D context coordinate system correctly.

## v7.21.5 (2026-04-12) — COT modal: canonical Chart.js config, grid/axis parity across all tabs

### Frontend — assets/cot-modal-chart.js
- **Root cause fixed — flat config vs canonical config:** Previous `_lineChart` and `_barChart` merged `type` and `data` directly into the `_chartDefaults` object, producing a flat config (`{ type, data, responsive, scales, ... }`). Chart.js accepts this for `responsive: true` but silently ignores top-level `scales` (including `position: 'right'`) when `responsive: false` is set with a manually-sized canvas. All wrappers now use the canonical form `{ type, data, options: { ... } }`, which Chart.js always applies correctly regardless of responsive mode.
- **`_buildOptions()` helper introduced:** Centralises deep-clone, plugin re-attachment, border suppression (`drawBorder: false`, `border.display: false`), and deep-merge of overrides for `layout` and `plugins`. All three chart builders (`_lineChart`, `_barChart`, Participants) now call `_buildOptions()` — eliminating three separate JSON round-trip clones with partial, inconsistent property restoration.
- **Eje Y derecho en Net y Long/Short:** With the flat-config bug fixed, `scales.y.position: 'right'` now applies correctly on all tabs — matching Participants.
- **Grid parity:** Grid color `rgba(242,242,242,0.06)` and no-border settings now consistently applied across all chart types.
- **Cleanup:** Removed redundant `borderRadius: 2` from the `_barChart` dataset call in `buildChart` (wrapper already enforces `0`).

## v7.21.4 (2026-04-12) — COT modal: gradient fix, grid consistency, bar radius removal

### Frontend — assets/cot-modal-chart.js
- **Gradient fix (Long/Short):** Moved gradient creation inside `_lineChart` via new `_tvGradFromCanvas()` helper. Previous implementation built the gradient using `cv.height` (DPR-scaled physical pixels), causing the gradient to compress into the top fraction of the chart. `_tvGradFromCanvas` uses the logical CSS height (`style.height`) instead, so the fade-to-transparent spans the full visible chart area correctly.
- **Grid consistency (Net / Long-Short):** Both `_lineChart` and `_barChart` now explicitly set `grid.drawBorder = false` and `border.display = false` on both axes after the JSON deep-copy — these properties were being silently dropped when Chart.js applied `responsive: false`, causing a visible chart-area border on Net/Long-Short that was absent from Participants.
- **Bar radius removed:** `borderRadius` changed from `2` to `0` in `_barChart`. Chart.js applies radius on the edge away from zero: positive bars get rounded tops, negative bars get rounded bottoms. This creates an asymmetric look inconsistent with TradingView and Bloomberg histograms.

The `--no-edit` flag is not a valid option for `git rebase --continue` (only for `git commit` / `git merge`); it caused a `fatal: unknown option` exit 128 on every push collision, bypassing the intended `exit 0` and triggering GitHub failure-notification emails on each concurrent run. `GIT_EDITOR=true` suppresses the interactive editor prompt, replicating the desired no-edit behavior correctly.

## v7.20.0 (2026-04-12) — Meetings workflow: static calendar replaces scraping; all dates verified

### Engine — .github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml

**Architecture change:** Replaced HTML/API scraping with a static curated calendar dict in the workflow script.

Root cause of persistent scraping failures: GitHub Actions runs on known AWS/Azure IP ranges that central bank websites actively block or rate-limit. Additionally, CB sites change URL structures without notice and use JS-rendered content. After two iterations of scraper fixes (v7.18.0, v7.19.0), 7 of 8 currencies still fell back to cbrates.com on every production run. This is a structural problem, not a fixable code problem.

**Static calendar approach:**
- Meeting dates are stored as a `CALENDAR_2026` dict directly in the workflow script.
- Dates are verified manually against official CB publications and updated once per year (typically January, when CBs publish their annual schedule).
- Bias detection (`detect_bias()`) continues to run weekly and reads from `rates/*.json` — this part remains fully automated.
- The workflow still commits to the repo weekly; if bias changes (e.g. a CB hikes), the JSON is updated automatically. Meeting dates only change if the workflow script is manually updated.

**Verified 2026 dates (cross-referenced April 2026):**
- USD: Apr 29, Jun 17, Jul 29, Sep 16, Oct 28, Dec 9 — `federalreserve.gov`
  - Corrected from broken 2028-01-26 (stale scraper artifact)
- EUR: Apr 30, Jun 11, Jul 23, Sep 10, Oct 29, Dec 17 — `ecb.europa.eu` (unchanged)
- GBP: Apr 30, Jun 18, Jul 30, Sep 17, Nov 5, Dec 17 — `bankofengland.co.uk` (unchanged)
- JPY: Apr 28, Jun 16, Jul 31, Sep 18, Oct 30, **Dec 18** — `boj.or.jp` (added Dec)
- AUD: May 5, Jun 16, Aug 11, Sep 29, Nov 3, Dec 8 — `rba.gov.au` (unchanged)
- CAD: Apr 29, Jun 10, Jul 15, **Sep 9**, Oct 28, Dec 9 — `bankofcanada.ca` (Sep corrected: was Sep 2)
- CHF: Jun 18, Sep 24, Dec 10 — `snb.ch` (unchanged)
- NZD: **May 27**, Jul 8, Sep 2, Oct 28, Dec 9 — `rbnz.govt.nz` (May corrected: was May 26)

**Source field:** Each currency now shows the official CB domain as source (no more `cbrates.com (fallback)` labels).

**Update procedure** (documented in script header):
1. Each January, CBs publish their full annual schedule.
2. Update `CALENDAR_YYYY` dict in the workflow.
3. Commit with `"CB calendar update YYYY - manual verification"`.

### Data — meetings-data/meetings.json
Updated in-place with verified 2026 dates. All 8 currencies now show official CB source labels.

## v7.19.0 (2026-04-12) — Meetings workflow: fix all 7 CB scraper failures from first production run

### Engine — .github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml

Production run on 2026-04-12 revealed that 7 of 8 CB scrapers fell back to cbrates.com.
Root cause analysis per currency:

- **Fed/USD — Parse failure (Tipo B):** URL correct (200 OK), but returned only 1 date (2028-01-26).
  The Fed page groups meetings under `<h4>2026</h4>` year headers with dates listed as
  "January 27-28" (no year in the same line). The generic `PAT_MULTI` regex requires the year
  in the match, so it skipped 2026 meetings entirely and only captured one distant 2028 entry
  where the year happened to appear inline. **Fix:** Dedicated structured scraper that walks
  the DOM tracking `<h4>` year headers and extracts dates from adjacent content without
  requiring the year in each date string. Falls back to full-text generic parse if no dates found.

- **ECB/EUR — Parse failure (Tipo B):** URL correct (200 OK), returned 0 dates. The previous
  scraper filtered lines to those containing "monetary policy" or "governing council". The ECB
  calendar layout places the event label and the date in separate DOM elements — date lines
  contain no keyword match and were silently discarded. **Fix:** Removed keyword filter; parse
  full page text. The date regex is specific enough to avoid false positives.

- **BoE/GBP — URL 404 (Tipo A):** `/monetary-policy-committee/mpc-meeting-dates` no longer
  exists. BoE restructured their site. **Fix:** Try `/monetary-policy/calendar` first, fall back
  to `/monetary-policy/monetary-policy-committee` (both tried sequentially).

- **BoJ/JPY — URL 404 (Tipo A):** `/en/mopo/mpmdates/index.htm` returned 404. **Fix:**
  Corrected to `/en/mopo/mpmdates/` (trailing slash, no index.htm). Cross-month pattern
  preserved ("April 30 - May 1" → May 1).

- **RBA/AUD — URL 404 (Tipo A):** `/monetary-policy/rba-board-meetings/` no longer exists.
  **Fix:** Try `/monetary-policy/` first, then `/monetary-policy/about/`. Using `HEADERS_RELAXED`
  (more browser-like Accept headers) for improved compatibility.

- **BoC/CAD — Parse failure (Tipo B):** URL correct (200 OK), returned 0 dates. The HTML
  page no longer contains parseable date strings in the expected format. **Fix:** Switch primary
  source to the **Bank of Canada Valet REST API** (`/valet/announcements/bank-rate`) which
  returns scheduled announcement dates as structured JSON (`YYYY-MM-DD`). HTML page remains
  as in-scraper fallback if the API is unavailable.

- **SNB/CHF — URL 404 (Tipo A):** `/the-snb/mandates-goals/monetary-policy/monetary-policy-assessment`
  returned 404. **Fix:** Try `/monetary-policy/interest-rates-and-current-account`, then
  `/the-snb/mandates-goals/monetary-policy`, then `/monetary-policy` (three-URL cascade).

- **RBNZ/NZD — Bot block 403 (Tipo C):** `/monetary-policy-committee/mpc-meeting-dates`
  returned 403. **Fix:** Try parent pages `/monetary-policy/monetary-policy-committee`,
  `/monetary-policy`, `/monetary-policy/monetary-policy-statement` with `HEADERS_RELAXED`
  (Windows Chrome UA + browser-like Accept headers).

**Architecture additions:**
- `HEADERS_RELAXED`: New header set with Windows Chrome UA and full browser-like Accept string.
  Used for RBA and RBNZ which apply stricter bot filtering.
- All scrapers now use multi-URL cascades (try list) so a single URL change doesn't kill a scraper.
- BoC now uses JSON API as primary — the only CB with a documented public REST endpoint.

## v7.18.0 (2026-04-11) — Meetings source migration: cbrates.com → official central bank publications

### Engine — .github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml
- **Root cause:** The meetings workflow scraped cbrates.com, a third-party aggregator with no direct CB affiliation, non-institutional reliability, and no published data sourcing methodology. Bloomberg and Refinitiv Eikon feed directly from CB press releases and official meeting calendars. Using cbrates.com as primary source placed the terminal below institutional standard for data provenance.
- **Architecture change:** Each CB now has a dedicated scraper targeting its official publication:
  - USD → `federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm`
  - EUR → `ecb.europa.eu/press/calendars/mgcgc/html/index.en.html`
  - GBP → `bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/monetary-policy-committee/mpc-meeting-dates`
  - JPY → `boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmdates/index.htm`
  - AUD → `rba.gov.au/monetary-policy/rba-board-meetings/`
  - CAD → `bankofcanada.ca/core-functions/monetary-policy/key-interest-rate/`
  - CHF → `snb.ch/en/the-snb/mandates-goals/monetary-policy/monetary-policy-assessment`
  - NZD → `rbnz.govt.nz/monetary-policy/monetary-policy-committee/mpc-meeting-dates`
- **Fallback chain:** If a primary scrape fails (0 dates returned or HTTP error), cbrates.com is queried as last-resort fallback for that specific currency only. When used, the output carries `source: "cbrates.com (fallback)"` for full transparency.
- **Decision date extraction:** Multi-day meetings are handled correctly per CB convention. BoJ cross-month meetings ("April 30 - May 1") use a dedicated pattern that extracts the last day as the decision date. Fed and BoE 2-day meetings ("April 28-29") also resolve to the decision day.
- **Per-currency source field:** Each entry in `meetings.json` now carries a `source` field naming the actual origin used (e.g. `"federalreserve.gov"` or `"bankofcanada.ca"`). The top-level `source` and `sourceUrl` fields pointing to cbrates.com have been removed.
- **Error resilience:** Script exits with error code 1 only if more than 3 currencies are missing dates (threshold for "something is structurally broken"). Individual CB scrape failures fall through to fallback gracefully.

### Data — meetings-data/meetings.json
- Removed top-level `source: "cbrates.com (International Central Banks)"` and `sourceUrl` fields.
- Added per-currency `source` field. Current data is labeled `"(pending next run)"` — will be replaced with the official CB source name on the next Monday workflow execution.

## v7.17.1 (2026-04-11) — Fix: Meetings dates in English + AUD/USD collapsed H/L bar invalidation + IV Rank context

### Engine — .github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml
- **Root cause:** `format_meeting_date()` used `MONTHS_ES` (Spanish: Ene, Feb, Mar, Abr…) to format display dates. The platform is English-only per GUIDELINES.md. The resulting strings ("29 Abr", "30 Abr", "5 May") were visible in the CB Rate Expectations panel next meeting column and would immediately flag the site as non-institutional to any Bloomberg/Eikon user.
- **Fix:** Replaced `MONTHS_ES` dict with `MONTHS_EN` (Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr…). Replaced the hardcoded Spanish fallback "Por definir" with "TBD". All future `workflow_meetings.yml` runs will produce English dates.
- **Immediate fix:** Translated existing `meetings-data/meetings.json` in-place via a one-shot script — all 8 currencies now show English month abbreviations without waiting for the next Monday workflow run.

### Engine — scripts/fetch_intraday_quotes.py (site repo)
- **Root cause:** When `ticker.info` returns `dayHigh`/`dayLow` as `None` (common for FX pairs outside active trading hours or after a stale yfinance tick), the script falls through to STEP C (daily history fallback) where `hist["High"].iloc[-1]` and `hist["Low"].iloc[-1]` may both equal the same close price. This produces `high == low == close` — a collapsed intraday bar that Bloomberg would never show during active trading hours. Detected in AUD/USD: `high: 0.7062, low: 0.7062`.
- **Fix:** Added a post-fetch sanity check: if `high == low` after all three steps (A/B/C), both values are set to `None` and a warning is logged. The frontend already renders `None` high/low as `'—'` (dash), which is the correct behaviour — showing an empty range is more honest than showing a collapsed bar.

### Context — IV Rank status (no code change)
- IV Rank is `null` for all pairs (`iv_hist_n: 1`) because the iv_history accumulator was initialised this week. This is expected and correct. The dashboard already handles this transparently: when `iv_rank == null`, the Positioning Bias panel falls back to the COT skew column and the tooltip reads "IV Rank building (need ≥4 weekly snapshots)". No frontend change needed — the existing fallback is honest and institutionally appropriate. IV Rank will become active automatically once 4 weekly snapshots have been accumulated (est. ~3 weeks).

## v7.17.0 (2026-04-11) — Fix: AI signal accuracy — CB trend pause detection + carry causality + meetings bias in context

### Engine — scripts/generate_narrative_signals.py
- **Root cause 1 — ECB trend computed as CUTTING:** `build_context()` determined CB trend by comparing `obs[0]` vs `obs[2]` in the rates array. For ECB, `obs[0]` = 2.00% (Jun-2025) vs `obs[2]` = 2.25% (Apr-2025) → labeled CUTTING. But the ECB has been on hold for ~346 days. The LLM received "ECB [CUTTING]" and generated a signal saying "ECB cutting rates" — contradicting meetings.json which correctly records `bias: hold`.
- **Fix 1 — Pause detection:** Replaced naive 3-point comparison with a proper last-change-date scan. The script now finds the most recent observation where the rate actually changed, computes days elapsed since that date, and forces `ON HOLD` when ≥90 days have passed — mirroring Bloomberg's pause detection behaviour. ECB now correctly shows `[ON HOLD]` (346d). Fed: `[ON HOLD]` (162d). BoJ: `[ON HOLD]` (315d) with `Bias: ↑ Hike` from meetings.json (intentional divergence — markets price hike while BoJ holds).
- **Fix 2 — meetings.json forward bias in LLM context:** The `bias` field from `meetings-data/meetings.json` (OIS/futures consensus for the next meeting) was not included in the context passed to the LLM. Added it to the CB rates section as "Market bias: ↓ Cut / → Hold / ↑ Hike" alongside the next meeting date. The LLM now sees both the historical trend (what the CB has done) and the forward expectation (what the market prices next) — and can correctly distinguish them.
- **Fix 3 — Carry causality rule in SIGNALS_SYSTEM:** Added explicit rule prohibiting inverted carry logic. "RBA hiking rates, AUD/USD may decline further" is a carry-logic inversion (hiking → better carry → currency supported, not weakened). New rule requires naming a countervailing factor (fully-priced hike, risk-off, cross-asset flow) when a hiking currency is discussed as bearish.
- **Fix 4 — USD/JPY intervention threshold clarity:** Tightened the intervention rule wording. The forbidden pattern "BoJ intervention risk elevated as USD/JPY trades above 159.00" implied 159.00 is the intervention level. Rule now explicitly states 160.00 is the watch level, and requires the signal to frame current price as "approaching" 160.00 rather than having already triggered the threshold.

## v7.16.23 (2026-04-11) — Fix: Carry Trade bar width uses percentage, not fixed px

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Root cause:** Bar width was calculated as `Math.round(barVal * 60)` — a fixed pixel value (max 60px). After the CSS redesign made `cr-bar-wrap` a `1fr` flexible column (variable width ~20–30px in the 180px sidebar), a 60px bar always overflowed and filled the container 100%, making every bar appear identically full.
- **Fix:** Changed to `Math.round(barVal * 100)` rendered as `width:${barPct}%`. Percentage is always relative to the bar-wrap container regardless of its rendered width, so bars now correctly scale proportionally — #1 at 100%, subsequent pairs at their ratio vs the top pair.

## v7.16.15 (2026-04-11) — Fix: CSS !important overrides Chart.js inline canvas styles

### Frontend — assets/cot-modal-chart.js
- **Root cause confirmed:** Chart.js sets `style="height:167px;width:335px"` directly on the `<canvas>` element after construction, locking it at the initial (wrong) size regardless of the container height. The JS height calculation was correct (367px on the container) but Chart.js inline styles won. Fix: CSS rule `#c-net, #c-split { width:100% !important; height:100% !important }` overrides the Chart.js inline style, forcing the canvas to fill the `.cot-chart-area` container at its correct JS-computed height.

### Frontend — index.html
- Bumped `cot-modal-chart.js` query version to `v=7.16.15` to bust browser cache.

## v7.16.14 (2026-04-11) — Fix: replace canvas element on rebuild to clear stale dimensions

### Frontend — assets/cot-modal-chart.js
- **Root cause:** After `chart.destroy()`, Chart.js leaves stale `width`/`height` attributes on the `<canvas>` element. When a new Chart instance is created on the same canvas, it inherits those stale pixel dimensions instead of measuring the container. Fix: after destroying the old chart, replace the `<canvas>` with a fresh `document.createElement('canvas')` with the same `id`. The new canvas has no attributes, so Chart.js measures the container cleanly and renders at the correct height.
- **Also removed:** The `chart.resize()` shortcut added in v7.16.13 — no longer needed since the canvas is always fresh on rebuild.

---

## v7.16.13 (2026-04-11) — Fix: chart.resize() after height set — replaces rebuild

### Frontend — assets/cot-modal-chart.js
- **Root cause confirmed via DevTools:** Chart.js built the canvas at 167px (default 2:1 aspect ratio) when the container had no height yet. After that, `built[tabId]=true` prevented rebuilding, so the chart stayed at 167px regardless of the container growing to 367px. Fix: after setting `chartArea.style.height`, call `Chart.getChart(canvas).resize(w, h)` directly if a chart instance already exists — this forces an immediate re-render at the correct dimensions without destroying and recreating the chart.

## v7.16.12 (2026-04-11) — Fix: dynamic DOM height measurement for Net/Long-Short charts on mobile

### Frontend — assets/cot-modal-chart.js
- **Chart fill on mobile:** Replaced hardcoded `used` height calculation (which assumed desktop padding values) with a fully dynamic DOM measurement. `cotTab()` now sums the actual `paddingTop + paddingBottom + borderTopWidth + borderBottomWidth` of `.cot-cw` via `getComputedStyle`, plus the measured height of all sibling elements (e.g. `.cot-ct` label) and the body's own padding. This means the calculation is correct at all screen sizes — desktop, mobile, and any custom breakpoint — without hardcoded pixel offsets.
- **CSS cleanup:** Removed `flex:1;min-height:0` from `#p-net.on .cot-cw > .cot-chart-area` and `#p-split.on` equivalent. These CSS rules conflicted with the JS-set `style.height` in px; now the chart-area has only `position:relative` and is sized exclusively by JS.

### Engine — scripts/cot_backfill_52w.py (site repo root)
- **Fix: parser completely rewritten from HTML block parser to CSV parser** — the previous version used `extract_tff_block()` which searched for a `Positions` keyword line, the format used by the CFTC weekly HTML page (`financial_lof.htm`). The annual ZIP files (`com_fin_txt_YYYY.zip`) are comma-separated text files with a completely different column layout. ### Engine — .github/workflows/update-cot-cftc-all.yml

Primary momentum signal in institutional COT analysis. `null` on first run (no prior week). Stored in both the root JSON and each history snapshot.
- **New: `levNetPctOI`** — LF net as a percentage of total market Open Interest (`net / totalOpenInterest × 100`). Bloomberg equivalent: "Net % OI". Normalises positioning across currencies with different contract sizes (EUR = 125k, JPY = 12.5M contracts). Stored in root JSON.

## v7.14.5 (2026-04-10) — Fix: suppress push-failure emails from intraday quotes workflow

### Site — .github/workflows/update-intraday-quotes.yml

- **Fix: changed `exit 1` to `exit 0` in the "all push attempts failed" branch** — when
  the 4-attempt rebase retry loop exhausts (e.g. due to concurrent runs queued by
  cron-job.org), the step now exits cleanly instead of with an error code. A push failure
  is not a data loss event: the next cron-job.org dispatch (≤5 min) will fetch and push
  fresh data. Exiting with 1 triggered GitHub's failure notification email on every
  collision; exiting with 0 is silent. No impact on data freshness or terminal behavior.

---



### Site — .github/workflows/update-intraday-quotes.yml

- **Fix: removed `schedule` trigger** — the GitHub Actions schedule (every 15 min) was running
  concurrently with cron-job.org dispatches (every 5 min). At 15-minute marks both triggered
  simultaneously, creating two parallel runs each trying to `git push` the same `quotes.json`.
  The 4-attempt rebase retry loop exhausted and exited with code 1, triggering GitHub's
  failure notification email on every collision (~4-6 times per hour during market hours).
  Resolution: `schedule` block removed entirely. cron-job.org is the sole clock.
  If cron-job.org goes down, the maximum data gap equals its configured interval (5 min) —
  acceptable for a ~5-minute delayed terminal. Manual trigger via `workflow_dispatch` preserved.

## v7.13.46 (2026-04-10) — Fix CB Rates trend arrow: apply recency + pause detection

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Rewrote `computeCBTrend()`** to use the same two-layer logic as the workflow bias detection, fixing trend arrows that diverged from the `meetings.json` bias field:
  - **Layer 1 — Recent momentum (`PAUSE_DAYS = 90`):** directional signal (up/down) is only applied when `obs[0]` is less than 90 days old. Previously, the ECB's last cut (Jun 2025, ~10 months old) kept showing ↓ because the old code only checked the 180-day data-gap guard without verifying how recent the *move itself* was.
  - **Layer 2 — Pause detection:** computes `effectiveFlat = max(consecutiveFlatMonths, dataAgeMonths − 1)`. If ≥ 3 → `'flat'`. This catches both banks with genuinely flat rates (Fed, BoE, BoC, SNB, RBNZ) and banks whose `rates/*.json` is stale because the rate hasn't changed (ECB at 2.00% since Jun 2025).
  - **BoJ special case:** BoJ is correctly shown as `—` (flat) in the *rates* panel — the rate has been at 0.75% for 8 months. This is intentional: the trend arrow shows **historical rate direction** (what has happened), while the bias in the *Expectations* panel shows **forward direction** (what markets expect next). These are different signals and should differ when a CB pauses between hikes.
- **Cache buster:** `dashboard.js?v=7.13.43` → `?v=7.13.46`.
- **Validated 8/8** correct against current `rates/*.json` data before deployment.

### Industry standard note
Bloomberg Terminal and Refinitiv Eikon display the CB rate trend arrow based on the **direction of the most recent policy decision**, resetting to neutral (—) after 3+ months without a move. The new `computeCBTrend()` matches this behaviour.

### GUIDELINES.md
- **Added "Industry standard compliance — non-negotiable" section** (after Product identity): mandates that every change to the terminal must meet Bloomberg / Refinitiv Eikon conventions. Covers CB trend arrows, rate bias labels, color coding, forward rate methodology, signal separation (retrospective vs prospective), and the mandatory pre-change question ("How does Bloomberg handle this?"). Lists authoritative reference sources (Bloomberg, Eikon, CME FedWatch, ASX Rate Tracker, OIS pricing).
- **Added industry standard check to both deployment checklists**: first item in "Checklist — before adding or modifying any data panel" and "Checklist — before any frontend deployment". Confirms the check is required even when the change seems purely cosmetic.
- **Version footer bumped** to v7.13.46.

## v7.13.45 (2026-04-09) — Fix CB Rate Expectations bias: correct 5 stale values, automate detection

### Data — meetings-data/meetings.json
- **Fixed 5 incorrect bias fields** that had not been updated to reflect post-Middle-East-war central bank reality:
  - `USD` (Fed): `cut` → `hold` — Fed on hold since Dec 2024; CME FedWatch 94-98% probability of no change at Apr 29 FOMC.
  - `EUR` (ECB): `cut` → `hold` — ECB held at last meeting; cutting cycle considered complete; inflation converging to 2% target.
  - `GBP` (BoE): `cut` → `hold` — BoE held unanimously in March 2026; Middle East energy shock raised near-term CPI above 3%; 90% of surveyed economists expect hold at Apr 30.
  - `AUD` (RBA): `cut` → `hike` — RBA raised in both February and March 2026 (cash rate now 4.1%); Westpac forecasts peak at 4.85%; UBS labels RBA a "hawkish outlier".
  - `JPY` (BoJ): `hold` → `hike` — BoJ in active hiking cycle; multiple board members support further increases; near-2% inflation and negative real rates underpin the case.
- **Unchanged (already correct):** `CAD` hold, `CHF` hold, `NZD` hold.

### Engine — .github/workflows/workflow_meetings.yml
- **Replaced static bias preservation with automatic two-layer trajectory detection.** The previous logic copied `bias` from the prior file unchanged every Monday, meaning stale values were never corrected automatically. New system:
  - **Layer 1 — Recent momentum:** checks whether the rate moved within the last `PAUSE_MONTHS` (3) months. If it rose → `hike`; fell → `cut`. Critically, this layer is skipped if the latest data point is older than 3 months — this prevents old ECB cuts (Jun 2025) from being misread as current momentum.
  - **Layer 2 — Pause detection:** computes `effective_flat = max(consecutive_flat_months, data_age_months − 1)`. If ≥ 3 → `hold`. This correctly catches both paused-hiking banks (BoC, RBNZ at 2.25% flat) and banks whose rate JSON is stale because the rate hasn't moved (ECB at 2.00% since Jun 2025 → 10 months → `hold`).
  - **Per-bank hawkish override:** `HAWKISH_OVERRIDE = {'JPY': 'hike'}` corrects BoJ, which is in an active hiking cycle but shows a flat plateau in the monthly rate series (0.75% for 8 months). The override fires when Layer 2 would otherwise return `hold`.
  - Falls back to prior file bias on any exception — no data loss on transient failures.
  - Logs `data_age`, `flat_months`, and `eff_flat` diagnostics in Actions output for auditability.
  - Validated 8/8 correct against current real rate data before deployment.

## v7.13.44 (2026-04-09) — Fix EUR rate: remove fabricated estimate, strengthen fetch_eur_ecb

### Engine — scripts/fetch_rates.py
- **Removed incorrect EUR MANUAL_OVERRIDE (1.75%):** The 1.75% value added in v7.13.42 was a fabricated estimate with no verified source. The last confirmed ECB DFR in EUR.json (2.00%, Jun 2025) is more accurate and honest than a made-up number labeled `manual-override`. Rule added to GUIDELINES: never add EUR to MANUAL_OVERRIDES.
- **Rewrote `fetch_eur_ecb()` with 4 sources:** The function previously had only the ECB SDMX API (1 source, 4 format variants). When the SDMX endpoint fails in CI (connection issues or API changes), EUR falls through all the way to stale cache. New source chain: (1) ECB SDMX API — unchanged, (2) ECB website HTML key-rates page — scrapes `ecb.europa.eu/mopo/implement/sf/html/index.en.html` for "Deposit facility X.XX%", (3) BIS CBPOL `stats.bis.org` for eurozone (XM), (4) global-rates.com. This makes EUR as resilient as AUD, CAD, and GBP.
- **MANUAL_OVERRIDES comment updated:** Documents that EUR must never be added here and why.

### Site — rates/EUR.json
- **Reverted to last confirmed value (2.00%, 2025-06-01):** Removed the 6 fabricated `manual-estimate` observations (1.75% and 2.00% entries from Jul 2025 onward). The ECB DFR as of June 2025 was confirmed at 2.00% by the ECB decision data already in the file. Subsequent entries were unverified estimates.

### GUIDELINES.md
- **Added EUR rate — authoritative sources and staleness rule section:** Documents DFR vs MRO distinction, 4-source fetch priority, and the non-negotiable rule against fabricated MANUAL_OVERRIDES for EUR.
- **Version bumped** to v7.13.44.

## v7.13.41 (2026-04-09) — Stress scoring thresholds aligned to industry standards

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **MOVE index threshold:** `> 120` → `> 100`. BofA/ICE define MOVE >100 as "elevated" bond market stress. The previous threshold of 120 only activated during late-stage crisis (SVB, Oct 2023 peaks), missing the early stress signal window. The MOVE display logic already used 100 as the "Elevated" label boundary — the scoring now matches.
- **Gold intraday threshold:** `> 1.0%` → `> 2.0%`. A 1% gold move occurs on routine inflation prints and USD weakness days with no systemic stress. Institutional risk models (BlackRock RAI, MSCI) use rolling ratio metrics rather than intraday; the closest equivalent for an intraday signal is a 2%+ safe-haven surge.
- **SPX intraday threshold:** `< -0.5%` → `< -1.5%`. A -0.5% SPX dip is a normal intraday fluctuation. -1.5% represents a statistically meaningful risk-off session (roughly 1σ for a typical low-vol day).
- **Regime tooltip updated** to reflect new thresholds and boundary rationale.

### GUIDELINES.md
- **Added stress scoring canonical thresholds table** under the Regime badge architecture section. Documents all boundary values, point weights, and rationale for each factor. Future changes to scoring must update this table and the test suite.
- **Version bumped** to v7.13.41.

## v7.13.39 (2026-04-09) — Fix export download: replace blob: URL with data: URL for Edge compatibility

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Root cause identified:** Edge Enhanced Tracking Prevention silently blocks programmatic `blob:` URL downloads triggered by `a.click()` — no error is thrown, no console output, the click is simply discarded. This caused CSV/JSON exports to appear completely non-functional despite `exportPanel()` running correctly and generating the file content.
- **Fix:** Replaced `URL.createObjectURL(blob)` + `a.click()` with a `data:` URI (`data:text/csv;charset=utf-8,...`). Edge does not restrict `data:` URL downloads under Tracking Prevention, and the approach is compatible with all modern browsers.

## v7.13.37 (2026-04-09) — Fix loadIntradayQuotes race condition and sentiment interval

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Fixed race condition in `loadIntradayQuotes()`:** Multiple async callers (fetchSentiment, fetchRiskData, fetchCrossAssetData, fetchQuoteBarRT, etc.) were firing simultaneously on page load and at each refresh cycle. Because they all passed the cache guard before any single call had completed and set `_intradayCacheTime`, each fired an independent fetch — producing hundreds of duplicate `[Intraday] ✓ Loaded` log entries and saturating the browser's network/event loop, which prevented click handlers (including CSV/JSON export buttons) from responding. Fix: added `_intradayInFlight` promise deduplication — if a fetch is already in progress, subsequent callers await the same promise instead of starting a new one.
- **Fixed `fetchSentiment` poll interval:** Was running every 30 seconds despite the underlying data source (Myfxbook via GitHub Action) only updating every 30 minutes. Interval changed to 10 minutes, eliminating 18 of every 20 redundant calls per half-hour.

## v7.13.16 (2026-04-06) — fix: 1D % change FX aún incorrecto — usar regularMarketChangePercent de Yahoo

### Engine — scripts/fetch_intraday_quotes.py
- **Causa raíz definitiva del bug +0.00%:** `fast_info["last_price"]` y `closes.iloc[-1]` pueden coincidir en FX porque yfinance incluye la barra de reapertura del domingo 22:00 UTC (con el precio del viernes) en el historial del lunes. Tanto `last_price` como `closes.iloc[-1]` devuelven ese mismo precio → chg = 0.
- **Fix v2.7 — cascade de 3 estrategias:** (A) `ticker.info["regularMarketChangePercent"]` + `regularMarketPrice` + `regularMarketPreviousClose` — idéntico al porcentaje que muestra Yahoo Finance en su sitio; (B) `fast_info.previous_close` (campo oficial de Yahoo, no el bar de la historia) vs `fast_info.last_price`; (C) `closes.iloc[-1]` vs `closes.iloc[-2]` como último recurso.
- **Fuente primaria ahora es `ticker.info`**, el mismo endpoint que usa finance.yahoo.com para mostrar el % de cambio — elimina toda discrepancia con lo que el usuario ve en Yahoo Finance o TradingView (que también usa Yahoo como fallback).

## v7.13.15 (2026-04-06) — fix: 1D % change still 0.00% — replace intraday bars with fast_info

### Engine — scripts/fetch_intraday_quotes.py
- **Bug fix (definitive):** Even with UTC-date filtering (v2.5), intraday intervals (`period="1d"/"2d"`) for FX pairs include a Sunday 22:00 UTC reopening bar carrying Friday's price. That bar passes the "today" date filter on Monday, making `close ≈ prev_close` → `+0.00%`. Replaced the entire intraday-bar approach with `ticker.fast_info["last_price"]` — a lightweight real-time field yfinance always populates without bar alignment, available for all symbols including FX. `prev_close` remains `closes.iloc[-1]` from the daily `period="5d"` bars (last completed session). `day_high`/`day_low` come from `fast_info["day_high"]`/`["day_low"]`. Fallback to `iloc[-1]` vs `iloc[-2]` (prev vs prior session) if `fast_info` throws.
- **Script version bumped:** v2.5 → v2.6.

---



### Engine — scripts/fetch_intraday_quotes.py
- **Bug fix (root cause):** `_date.today().isoformat()` returned the **server's local date**, not UTC. On GitHub Actions runners in non-UTC timezones, this caused `hist_today` to filter to an incorrect date (e.g. "2026-04-05" instead of "2026-04-06"), leaving it empty. Fixed by replacing with `datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")` — always UTC.
- **Bug fix (secondary):** The single `period="2d", interval="1h"` fetch is unreliable for FX pairs in CI — hourly bars for the current UTC day may not yet exist. Replaced with a cascade: try `period="1d", interval="5m"` first (more granular, better FX intraday coverage), then `period="2d", interval="1h"` as fallback. Both paths use the new `_extract_today()` helper for consistent UTC-date filtering.
- **Script version bumped:** v2.4 → v2.5.

---



### Engine — scripts/fetch_intraday_quotes.py
- **Bug fix:** `fetch_yfinance_all()` used `period="5d", interval="1d"` and took `closes.iloc[-1]` as current price and `closes.iloc[-2]` as prev_close. On Mondays (and any post-holiday open), `iloc[-1]` is the **prior Friday close** and `iloc[-2]` is Thursday — producing a Thu→Fri change instead of today vs Friday. Fixed by: (1) using `iloc[-1]` from the daily bars as `prev_close` (last completed session), and (2) fetching `period="1d", interval="1m"` for the true current intraday price and today's real high/low. Falls back to the old daily-only logic when intraday data is unavailable (weekend, holiday).

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Fix carry sign for USD/CCY pairs:** `USD/JPY`, `USD/CHF`, `USD/CAD` were showing negative carry (e.g. −3.00% for USD/JPY). Root cause: the formula used `cbBase − cbQuote` for `invert:false` pairs, but `base='JPY'` in those pairs — so it computed JPY rate − USD rate. Fix: `invert:true` (CCY/USD) → `cbBase − cbQuote`; `invert:false` (USD/CCY) → `cbQuote − cbBase`. USD/JPY now correctly shows ~+4.00%.

### Engine — scripts/fetch_fx_liquidity.py
- **Bug:** `today_profile` se normalizaba con su propio máximo (`normalize_to_100`). Con 1 sola hora de datos reales, esa hora se convertía en 100.0 — produciendo un spike artificial al inicio del día.
- **Fix:** `today_profile` ahora se normaliza con el mismo denominador (`baseline_max`) que `baseline_30d`. Los valores de `today` y `baseline_30d` quedan en la misma escala y son directamente comparables.
- **Cleanup:** Función `normalize_to_100` eliminada (ya no se usa).

## v7.12.32 (2026-04-05) — FX Liquidity: enriquecimiento con datos reales vía yfinance

### Engine — scripts/fetch_fx_liquidity.py (nuevo — repo público)
- **Nuevo script:** produce `fx-data/fx-liquidity.json` con dos arrays de 24h UTC: `today` (rango H-L realizado del día actual, hora a hora) y `baseline_30d` (promedio rolling 30 días del mismo índice).
- **Metodología:** mediana del rango H-L por hora entre 5 pares (EURUSD=X, GBPUSD=X, USDJPY=X, USDCHF=X, AUDUSD=X) vía yfinance `1h`, 35 días de historia. El rango H-L es el proxy de actividad FX más robusto disponible en fuentes públicas (referencia: IEEE 2013 — el tiempo del día es el factor que más influye en la liquidez FX).
- **Fallback en cadena:** fx-liquidity.json → frankfurter.json vol-scalar (legado) → LIQ_BASE hardcodeado. El campo `fallback: true` señala cuando no hay datos reales.
- **No requiere API keys.** yfinance, sin ventaja competitiva → repo público.

### Engine — .github/workflows/update-fx-liquidity.yml (nuevo — repo público)
- Corre cada hora, todos los días (`0 * * * *`). Sin secrets. Minutos ilimitados en repo público.
- Timeout: 10 min. Concurrency group para evitar solapamientos.

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **`fetchLiquidityData()` reescrita** con tres capas de fallback: (1) `fx-liquidity.json` primario, (2) `frankfurter.json` legado, (3) LIQ_BASE puro.
- **`_liqBaseline`** (nuevo): array de 48 slots con el promedio 30d, dibujado como línea de referencia gris punteada sobre el área del día actual.
- **`_liqSource`** (nuevo): string de atribución actualizado dinámicamente en `#liq-source-label` después de cada fetch.
- **Helper `_liqTo48()`**: interpola un array de 24h a 48 half-hour slots, evitando duplicación de lógica.
- Cache bust: `dashboard.js?v=7.12.32`.

### Frontend — index.html
- Leyenda "30d avg" con línea punteada gris agregada al pie del panel FX Liquidity.
- `<span id="liq-source-label">` agregado debajo de la leyenda — muestra la fuente activa en 7.5px.
- Cache bust: `dashboard.css?v=7.12.32`.

### GUIDELINES.md
- Regla de label del panel FX Liquidity actualizada: `yfinance · H-L range proxy · 30d avg` cuando el JSON está disponible; `Historical avg · fixed reference` como fallback. Versión bumpeada a v7.12.32.

## v7.12.30 (2026-04-05) — Fix: FX Liquidity no reacciona al abrir el mercado el domingo

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **Bug:** `drawLiquidityChart()` y los dos generadores de `_liqData` en `fetchLiquidityData()` usaban `utcDay === 0 || utcDay === 6` para detectar fin de semana. Esta definición trata **todo el domingo UTC como mercado cerrado**, incluso después de las 21:00 UTC cuando Sydney ya abrió. El canvas permanecía con la curva plana y el texto "MARKET CLOSED — WEEKEND" hasta las 00:00 UTC del lunes.
- **Fix:** Los tres `isWeekend` corregidos a la definición canónica ya usada en el resto del archivo: `utcDay === 6 || (utcDay === 0 && utcHour < 21) || (utcDay === 5 && utcHour >= 21)`. El mercado FX cierra viernes 21:00 UTC y reabre domingo 21:00 UTC (Sydney open).
- Cache bust: `dashboard.css?v=7.12.30`.

## v7.12.28 (2026-04-05) — Fix: Google Fonts carga bloqueante — Inter + JetBrains Mono garantizados

### Frontend — index.html
- **Fuente raíz del problema:** `display=optional` + carga no-bloqueante (`media=print/onload`) hacía que el browser comprometiera el fallback (Courier New / sistema) antes de que llegara el CSS de Google Fonts. JetBrains Mono nunca se aplicaba en ninguna sesión, independientemente de la velocidad de red.
- **Fix:** Google Fonts ahora carga como stylesheet bloqueante (`<link rel="stylesheet">` directo). Con carga bloqueante, Inter y JetBrains Mono están definidas antes del primer paint → ningún swap ocurre → CLS de fuentes = 0. El costo en FCP (~50ms) es aceptable y ya estaba presente en el repo de referencia.
- **`display=swap` mantenido:** Con carga bloqueante, `swap` nunca dispara un intercambio visible porque las fuentes ya están disponibles en el momento del paint.
- Cache bust: `dashboard.css?v=7.12.28`.

### GUIDELINES.md
- Sección Font loading reescrita: documenta la estrategia correcta (bloqueante + swap) y prohíbe explícitamente `display=optional` con carga no-bloqueante.

## v7.12.21 (2026-04-05) — CLS fix: skeleton rows para CB Rates y Key Correlations tables

### Frontend — index.html

#### Diagnóstico del CLS desktop residual 0.129 (v7.12.20)
La tabla CB Rate Expectations seguía siendo el culpable, pero el mecanismo de CLS era diferente al previsto. El elemento NO estaba creciendo — estaba siendo EMPUJADO HACIA ABAJO por las tablas que están encima de él en el `#rightpanel`, las cuales aún no tenían skeleton rows:

1. **`#cbrates-tbody`** (Central Bank Rates): 1 fila "Loading…" → 8 filas reales (una por banco central). Crecimiento: ~7 filas × ~22px = ~154px. Posición en DOM: inmediatamente encima de las correlaciones y CB Expectations.
2. **`#correlations-tbody`** (Key FX Correlations): 1 fila → 10 filas reales (pares de correlación de 60 días). Crecimiento: ~9 filas × ~22px = ~198px. Posición: entre CB Rates y CB Expectations.

El crecimiento combinado de ~352px empujaba la tabla CB Expectations hacia abajo, generando el CLS 0.109 + 0.015 = 0.124.

Las versiones v7.12.18–v7.12.20 habían corregido los skeleton rows de la tabla CB Expectations en sí, pero la causa real era el crecimiento de las tablas SUPERIORES en el panel.

#### Fix: skeleton rows en ambas tablas superiores
- **`#cbrates-tbody`**: 8 skeleton rows con estructura idéntica al JS (`<span class="fi fi-XX">` + bank name en font-size:10px, columnas Rate y Trend). Las filas usan `class="up"` para Rate y `<span class="flat">—</span>` para Trend, replicando exactamente la altura de las filas reales.
- **`#correlations-tbody`**: 10 skeleton rows con los pares exactos que sirve `intraday-data/quotes.json` (EUR/USD·DXY, AUD/USD·Gold, USD/JPY·US 10Y, USD/JPY·VIX, USD/CAD·WTI Oil, GBP/USD·FTSE 100, AUD/USD·ASX 200, NZD/USD·NZX 50, EUR/USD·EuroStoxx, GBP/USD·Gold). Los nombres de los pares son idénticos a los del JSON → sin cambio de ancho de columna al reemplazar.

#### CLS esperado post-v7.12.21
- CB Rates + Correlations empujando CB Expectations: 0.124 → ~0
- Residual conocido: `sb-section` crosses 0.003 + risk panel-sub 0.001 + topbar 0.000 = CLS total esperado ≤ 0.005 desktop ✅
- Móvil: sin cambio (CLS 0 mantenido desde v7.12.20 ✓)

## v7.12.20 (2026-04-05) — CLS fix: flag-icons bloqueante + skeleton rows exactos en CB Rate Expectations

### Frontend — index.html

#### Diagnóstico del CLS desktop residual 0.130 (v7.12.19)
El análisis de los skeleton rows de v7.12.18 confirmó que el mecanismo esqueleto era correcto en concepto pero fallaba por dos razones:
1. **flag-icons.min.css cargaba en modo non-blocking** (`rel="preload" onload`): la hoja de estilos se aplicaba tarde (post-render), causando que cada `.fi` span recibiera su `background-image` después del primer paint → reflow de toda la tabla CB Rate Expectations → CLS 0.109 + 0.017 = 0.126.
2. **Los skeleton rows no replicaban la estructura HTML real**: carecían de los spans de flag (`<span class="fi fi-xx">`), el nombre del banco en `font-size:10px` y el placeholder de fecha en `font-size:9px`, lo que hacía que la altura inicial de la fila fuera diferente a la final.

#### Fix 1: flag-icons bloqueante
- **Cambio:** Reemplazado `<link rel="preload" as="style" ... onload="this.rel='stylesheet'">` + `<noscript>` por un único `<link rel="stylesheet">` bloqueante.
- **Efecto:** flag-icons.min.css se aplica antes del primer paint → las `.fi` spans tienen su `background-image` desde el inicio → sin reflow tardío de la tabla.
- **Costo:** flag-icons.min.css es ~11 KiB comprimido, se sirve desde jsDelivr CDN con caché larga. El bloqueo de render es mínimo (ya era un preconnect existente a cdn.jsdelivr.net).

#### Fix 2: skeleton rows con estructura exacta
- **Cambio:** Los 8 skeleton rows del `#fed-exp-tbody` ahora replican exactamente la estructura HTML que produce el JS: `<span class="fi fi-XX">` + `<span style="font-size:10px;">` (banco) + `<span style="color:var(--text3);font-size:9px;">` (fecha placeholder «—»), más la celda de bias con `<span class="flat">→ —</span>` y la celda de fwd rate con las mismas clases de color y font-family que el JS genera.
- **Efecto:** La altura de cada fila skeleton es idéntica a la fila real → sin cambio de altura al reemplazar innerHTML.

#### CLS esperado post-v7.12.20
- CB Rates table: 0.126 → ~0 (ambas causas eliminadas)
- Residual: `sb-section` crosses 0.003 + risk panel-sub 0.001 + topbar 0.000 = CLS total esperado ≤ 0.005 desktop
- Móvil: sin cambio respecto a v7.12.19 (0.055, pasa threshold de 0.1 ✓)

## v7.12.19 (2026-04-05) — Frankfurter CORS fix: mover fetches al engine workflow

### Engine — .github/workflows/update-frankfurter-cache.yml (nuevo)
- **Nuevo workflow:** Fetcha los datos de Frankfurter/ECB server-side (sin CORS) cada 4h en días de semana y una vez en fin de semana, y los deposita en `/fx-data/frankfurter.json` del repo público. Estructura: `today` (tasas USD-base del día), `prev` (día hábil anterior), `series` (timeseries 7 días EUR-base→USD,GBP,JPY para el liquidity canvas).

- **Nuevo script:** Realiza las 3 llamadas a `api.frankfurter.app` en Python (server-side, sin restricción CORS) y escribe `site/fx-data/frankfurter.json`. Incluye validación de respuesta y exit(1) ante error para notificación por email desde GitHub Actions.

### Frontend — assets/dashboard.js
- **`fetchFrankfurter()`:** Eliminadas las dos llamadas directas a `api.frankfurter.app/{date}?from=USD`. Ahora lee `fetch('/fx-data/frankfurter.json')` y extrae `data.today.rates` / `data.prev.rates`. Comportamiento idéntico al anterior pero sin CORS.
- **`fetchLiquidityData()`:** Eliminada la llamada a `api.frankfurter.app/{start}..{end}?from=EUR&to=USD,GBP,JPY`. Ahora lee la misma caché y extrae `cacheData.series.rates`. El cálculo del `volScalar` y la generación de los 48 buckets de liquidez es idéntico.
- **Efecto en consola:** Los 3 errores de CORS de Frankfurter desaparecen de la consola → Best Practices desktop/móvil debería subir de 77 a ~92 (solo quedan el unload handler de TradingView y los WebSocket ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED, ambos de terceros e irresolubles).

## v7.12.17 (2026-04-05) — CLS fix: skeleton rows para FX table y Heatmap

### Performance — index.html

#### Causa raíz del CLS desktop residual identificada: crecimiento de paneles sobre el viewport
- **Diagnóstico:** El CLS desktop de 0.262 (Cross-Asset grids: 0.145 + 0.112) no era causado por fuentes — era causado por dos paneles que crecen cuando JS carga datos, empujando el panel Cross-Asset (visible en viewport) hacia abajo.
  - **FX Pairs table:** El tbody arrancaba con 1 fila genérica "Loading…" (~24px). Al cargar datos, JS la reemplaza por 7 filas reales de pares (~168px). Crecimiento: ~144px → shift del panel Cross-Asset.
  - **Currency Strength Heatmap:** El `#heatmap-grid` arrancaba vacío (0px). Al cargar, JS inserta 8 celdas `hm-cell` (~58px de contenido). Crecimiento: ~58px → otro shift acumulado.
  - Ambos paneles están posicionados SOBRE el panel Cross-Asset en el flujo vertical de `#main`. Como `#main` es `overflow-y:auto`, el Cross-Asset (abajo) se desplaza cuando los paneles de arriba crecen. Lighthouse detectó el desplazamiento en el elemento visible (Cross-Asset) y lo atribuyó a ese div, cuando la causa real era el crecimiento de los paneles superiores.

#### Fix: skeleton rows en FX Pairs tbody (7 filas)
- **Cambio:** Reemplazado el `<tr><td colspan="9">Loading…</td></tr>` por 7 filas skeleton — una por cada par no-cruzado del array `PAIRS` (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, USD/JPY, AUD/USD, USD/CHF, USD/CAD, NZD/USD). Cada fila tiene `<td class="sym">PAR</td>` + 8 celdas con "—". Altura resultante idéntica a los datos reales.
- **Efecto:** El tbody ya ocupa el espacio final desde el primer paint. Cuando JS llama a `populateFxPairsTable()` y reemplaza el innerHTML, el panel no crece → sin shift.

#### Fix: skeleton cells en Currency Strength Heatmap (8 celdas)
- **Cambio:** Añadidas 8 celdas skeleton `<div class="hm-cell h-flat">` con `<span class="hm-sym">CCY</span>` + `<span class="hm-val flat">—</span>` directamente en el HTML. Una por cada divisa (EUR, USD, GBP, JPY, AUD, CAD, CHF, NZD). Usa la misma clase `h-flat` que aplica el JS para el estado neutral.

## v7.12.16 (2026-04-05) — Fix JetBrains Mono 404 preload; add Core Web Vitals guidelines

### Performance — index.html

#### JetBrains Mono WOFF2 preload removed (was returning 404)
- **Problema:** El tag `<link rel="preload" as="font">` apuntaba a `tDbv2o-flEEny0FZhsfKu5WU4xD-IQ.woff2`, que devolvía HTTP 404. Google Fonts sirve WOFF2 con hashes específicos por combinación de navegador/OS (User-Agent negotiation); hardcodear una URL sin verificarla en el navegador destino produce el 404. El error aparecía en la consola de PageSpeed degradando el score de Best Practices. Además, un preload que devuelve 404 no cumple ningún propósito útil: el browser lo descarta y la fuente sigue cargando vía la regla `@font-face` del CSS de Google Fonts, que sí usa la URL correcta para cada UA.
- **Fix:** Eliminado el preload de JetBrains Mono. Se mantiene únicamente el preload de Inter v13 (URL verificada y estable). JetBrains Mono sigue cargando correctamente vía `@font-face` con `display=optional`; sin el preload no garantizamos que llegue en los 100 ms del período optional, pero tampoco causamos un 404 en consola.
- **Efecto esperado:** Eliminación del error `Failed to load resource: 404` de JetBrains Mono en consola → mejora de Best Practices score. El CLS residual de 0.306 en desktop (Cross-Asset grids) debería reducirse al eliminar el 404 que impedía que el período optional funcionara correctamente.

### GUIDELINES.md

#### Nueva sección: Core Web Vitals — non-negotiable performance standards
- **Motivo:** Tras múltiples iteraciones de optimización (v7.12.12–v7.12.15), documentamos formalmente las reglas que garantizan CLS ≤ 0.1, LCP ≤ 2.5 s y TBT ≤ 200 ms. Sin estas reglas escritas, cambios futuros que parezcan inocuos (cargar CSS en forma no-bloqueante, añadir `display=swap`, quitar `min-height` de paneles) pueden reintroducir el CLS de 1.2+ que se tardó varias sesiones en diagnosticar y corregir.
- **Contenido añadido:** Tabla de thresholds por métrica; reglas obligatorias para CSS loading, font loading, layout shifts y blocking resources; lista de errores de consola no corregibles (Frankfurter CORS, TradingView WebSocket, TradingView deprecation warning); `min-height` requeridas por panel.
- **Checklist de deployment actualizado:** Nueva línea: Core Web Vitals verificados (CLS ≤ 0.1 en desktop y mobile) antes de cerrar sesión.

## v7.12.15 (2026-04-05) — CLS fix: blocking CSS + font-display:optional + JetBrains Mono preload

### Performance — index.html

#### dashboard.css cambiado a carga bloqueante
- **Problema:** El patrón `<link rel="preload" as="style" onload="this.rel='stylesheet'">` (CSS no-bloqueante) mejora el FCP pero causa CLS porque la página pinta primero con el CSS inline (2.7 KB) y luego aplica las ~48 KB de reglas restantes de `dashboard.css`. Cada regla nueva que cambia dimensiones, márgenes o tipografía después del primer paint es un layout shift medible. PageSpeed Desktop reportó CLS=1.226, con `#tv-chart-wrap` acumulando 0.913 de ese total.
- **Fix:** Cambiado a `<link rel="stylesheet" href="assets/dashboard.css?v=7.12.15">` (carga bloqueante estándar). El browser espera que `dashboard.css` cargue antes del primer paint → el DOM se pinta ya estilado → CLS=0 por este concepto. El FCP aumenta ~200–400 ms en desktop (GitHub Pages sirve desde CDN con latencia baja), pero la mejora de CLS vale muchos más puntos en el score.

#### `font-display:swap` → `font-display:optional` en Google Fonts
- **Problema:** Google Fonts con `display=swap` hace que el browser pinte primero con la fuente del sistema (system fallback) y luego intercambie a Inter y JetBrains Mono cuando cargan. Ese intercambio ("swap") cambia las métricas tipográficas de todos los elementos de texto visible — alto de línea, ancho de caracteres, dimensiones del contenedor — generando layout shifts en cadena. PageSpeed identificó explícitamente las dos fuentes WOFF2 de `fonts.gstatic.com` como causantes del CLS de `#tv-chart-wrap` (0.913) y de los dos grids de Cross-Asset (0.160 + 0.146).
- **Fix:** URL de Google Fonts cambiada a `display=optional`. Con `optional`, el browser tiene exactamente 100 ms para cargar la fuente antes del primer paint. Si carga (ver preloads a continuación): se usa sin swap. Si no carga: el sistema usa la fuente fallback **permanentemente** para esa sesión, sin ningún intercambio posterior → CLS=0 por fuentes.

#### Preload de JetBrains Mono WOFF2 añadido
- **Problema:** Solo existía un `<link rel="preload" as="font">` para Inter Regular (400). JetBrains Mono (usada en `.ca-val` a 16px font-weight:700, en el quotebar, y en los tooltips) no tenía preload — el browser no iniciaba su descarga hasta que el parser encontraba la referencia en el Google Fonts CSS, ya demasiado tarde para el período de 100 ms de `display:optional`.
- **Fix:** Añadido `<link rel="preload" as="font" type="font/woff2" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/jetbrainsmono/v24/tDbv2o-flEEny0FZhsfKu5WU4xD-IQ.woff2" crossorigin>` inmediatamente después del preload de Inter. Con ambas fuentes preloadeadas, el navegador las descarga en paralelo desde el inicio de la navegación y ambas están disponibles dentro de los 100 ms del período `optional`.

#### `#narrative` en mobile: `min-height:84px` añadido
- **Problema:** En mobile (`max-width:900px`) el panel `#narrative` tenía `height:auto` sin `min-height`. Al cargar el texto AI (~226 caracteres), el panel crecía de ~40 px (placeholder "Loading…") a ~84 px (texto real en 3 líneas a 11px × 1.5), empujando `#tv-chart-wrap` hacia abajo.
- **Fix:** Añadido `min-height:84px` al `#narrative` en el bloque `@media(max-width:900px)` del CSS inline crítico. El panel ya tiene su altura correcta en el primer paint → sin shift cuando el texto AI carga.

## v7.12.13 (2026-04-05) — Core Web Vitals: minificación habilitada, logo optimizado, fetchpriority

### Performance — netlify.toml

#### Minificación JS y CSS habilitada
- **Problema:** `[build.processing.js]` y `[build.processing.css]` tenían `minify = false`. Netlify no comprimía los assets en cada deploy, sirviendo `dashboard.js` (238 KB) y `dashboard.css` (48 KB) sin minificar.
- **Fix:** `minify = true` en ambas secciones. Netlify aplicará su pipeline de minificación en cada deploy: `dashboard.js` ~238 KB → ~150 KB, `dashboard.css` ~48 KB → ~30 KB. Compatible con el cache-busting `?v=` existente.

### Performance — index.html + todas las páginas

#### Logo del topbar: imagen correctamente dimensionada
- **Problema:** `apple-touch-icon.png` (180×180 px, 45 KB) se usaba en el topbar con display de 28×28 px. PageSpeed lo marcaba como "Properly size images" — se transfieren 45 KB para mostrar ~0.5 KB de datos visuales.
- **Fix `index.html`:** Creado `logo-56.png` (56×56 px a 2× retina, 7.6 KB) mediante resize LANCZOS desde el original. El topbar ahora referencia `logo-56.png` en lugar de `apple-touch-icon.png`. Ahorro: ~37 KB por visita en desktop.
- **Fix páginas secundarias:** `apple-touch-icon.png` se mantiene en las páginas secundarias (el archivo 180×180 es correcto para iOS), pero se añadieron atributos `width="28" height="28"` explícitos donde faltaban para evitar reflow.

#### `fetchpriority="high"` en logo del topbar
- Añadido `fetchpriority="high"` al `<img>` del logo en todas las páginas. El logo es el primer elemento visual above-the-fold; esta pista HTTP Priority Hints instruye al browser a priorizarlo en la fase de preload scan, mejorando el LCP en casos donde la imagen compite con otros recursos.

### Archivo nuevo — logo-56.png
- Imagen de 56×56 px (2× retina) generada desde `apple-touch-icon.png` con filtro LANCZOS. Uso exclusivo del topbar. No reemplaza `apple-touch-icon.png` (que sigue siendo la referencia estándar iOS 180×180 en el `<link rel="apple-touch-icon">`).
